`playFinalFlash(reduced,onDone)` (a brief flash reusing the existing `.gateway-threshold-flash` CSS, deliberately with **no** forward camera dolly this time — the video's own final seconds, Lumo carrying the Egg into the light, already read as a camera-through-the-light moment on their own, and stacking a CSS zoom on top would double up rather than add anything). `runTravellerGateway()` chains it all: an extended hold on the closed doors before any playback starts (`GATE_SETTLE_MS` + a new `GATE_HOLD_MS=2000`, added in direct response to "the gate hold can you extend it by 2 more seconds. i dont want lumo to enter as soon as the page has loaded" — ~2.6s total stillness before Segment 1 begins, with the footage's own natural ~2s of doors-alone-no-Lumo playback extending that further) → Segment 1 (0→5s, Lumo lands and sets the Egg down) → pause exactly at 5s, where `GREETING_LINES` now plays **in person**, witnessed over the held frame, rather than heard over an empty screen as it did before this sprint → Segment 2 (resumes at 7.5s, skipping the brief "Lumo crouches to pick the Egg back up" transition, plays to the real natural end) → the brief flash → hand-off. `begin()`'s own session-detection block now also decides which Gate video to preload, since the two paths use genuinely different footage — computed once, synchronously, before either video ever starts downloading. Verified via a new 15-assertion Playwright suite: the new video mounts with zero halo/particles/separate-Lumo-DOM-element; a direct `currentTime` check confirms the hold genuinely keeps playback at frame 0 for ~1.2s after mount; a `play()`-call spy (this sandbox's Chromium can't decode H.264 at all, a standing, already-documented limitation from earlier this session, so real `currentTime` advancement isn't observable — matching the established `lumo_video_test.js` testing pattern) confirms Segment 1 playback was genuinely requested once the hold ends; the pause lands exactly at `currentTime===5` with the greeting bubble showing "Welcome, Traveller."; no Creator Signature challenge appears for a first-time Traveller; resume seeks to exactly `7.5` and requests `play()` a second time; the final flash fires and the sequence hands off cleanly; zero console errors throughout; the Returning Creator path is independently confirmed, in the same suite, to still mount the old `gate-sequence.mp4` with its halo + 5 gather particles and its own unchanged "Welcome home." recognition line. - Traveller Interaction Polish — Tap Hint, Cinzel, and a Base for the Greeting (three concrete follow-ups on the just-shipped single-video Traveller pipeline, landed together. "its good. a bit racing. but we can fix that" is explicitly deferred, not addressed this pass. **(1) "move tap to continue towards right bottom corner"** — `.gateway-tap-hint` moved from bottom-center (`bottom:36px;left:50%;transform:translateX(-50%)`) to bottom-right (`bottom:26px;right:28px;left:auto;transform:none`). **(2) "the font and color of text are not matching the scene"** — the greeting bubble's plain body sans-serif (Arial, inherited with no override) and flat cream tone read as generic UI copy against the ornate carved-stone/gold-inscription banners in the real Gate footage ("The Adventure Awaits" / "Dream Believe Discover"). **(3) "something royal and mystical at same time. use old story fonts"** + **"give this some base"** — Cinzel (a real Roman-inscription-style display serif, OFL-licensed, fetched fresh from Google Fonts via the sandbox's own outbound proxy and self-hosted at `assets/fonts/cinzel-600-latin.woff2` alongside the existing Caveat/Kalam/Nunito set, since none of those read as royal/mystical) replaces the generic Georgia fallback stack entirely in `.gateway-greeting-bubble`; `--gw-gold` (the same tone the Gate's own particles/sparks/threshold-flash already use) stays, now paired with a genuine gold glow (`text-shadow:0 0 26px rgba(255,203,69,.55),0 2px 14px rgba(0,0,0,.7)`) instead of a flat black drop shadow. A slim gold gradient rule (`.gateway-greeting-bubble::after`) sits beneath each line — literally "a base" for the words to stand on, like the foundation of an inscribed plaque — its own width scaling proportionally to each line's own rendered width (`width:min(64%,210px)`, a percentage of the bubble's own content-hugging box under `.gateway-panel`'s `align-items:center`), verified directly via measurement rather than eyeballed: 210px (capped) for "Welcome, Traveller." (a 396px-wide bubble) vs 145px for the shorter "I am Lumo." (a 226px-wide bubble) — both genuinely ≈64% of their own bubble's measured width, confirming the scaling actually works even though a screenshot comparison alone hadn't made the difference obvious. No separate animation was needed on the pseudo-element — the parent's existing `gateway-line-in` opacity/transform keyframe already composites the whole box (text + pseudo-element) together as one rendered layer, so the rule fades in/out in lockstep with the words for free. The mobile breakpoint's own `.gateway-greeting-bubble{padding:0 18px}` override was updated to `padding:4px 18px 22px` so the bottom padding the underline needs survives at narrow viewports too. Verified via Playwright: the tap hint's bounding rect sits within 60px of both the right and bottom viewport edges; `document.fonts.check('600 20px Cinzel')` resolves `true` (the font genuinely loaded, not silently falling back to Georgia); the underline width scales correctly per line, measured directly; a full re-run of the existing 15-assertion Traveller/Returning-Creator pipeline suite plus the completion/tap-to-skip sanity checks and both `goldenBuild.js` suites all pass unchanged, zero console errors. - Traveller Greeting — Richer Text Sequence + a Real Closing Beat (two direct follow-ups on the shipped single-video Traveller pipeline. **(1) "use this text sequence . after every line give a pause time of 1000ms"** — the user supplied a reference text-sequence board pairing each spoken title with a smaller second line, replacing the prior sprint's own 4 flat sentences with 5 real `{title,subtitle}` pairs: "Welcome, Traveller." / "You've found the Gateway." → "I am Lumo." / "It's wonderful to meet you." → "Guardian of Story Companions." / "I help stories come to life." → "Every Creator begins here." / "And every story begins with a spark of imagination." → "I've been waiting for you." / "Shall we begin? ✨". `playLines(lines,lineMs,gapMs,reduced,onDone)` — shared by the Traveller greeting, the Returning Creator's own welcome, and Lumo's in-person arrival lines — now accepts either a plain string (every other caller, completely unchanged) or a `{title,subtitle}` object, rendering the latter as two stacked child elements (`.gateway-greeting-title`, inheriting the bubble's existing Cinzel/gold/glow styling untouched with no rule of its own needed; a new `.gateway-greeting-subtitle` — a smaller, quieter italic serif in a soft parchment tone, a whispered aside beneath Lumo's own spoken line, never competing with it) instead of one flat sentence — a real, additive shape rather than a special case bolted onto the existing string path. `GREETING_GAP_MS` (already `1000` from the prior turn's own "increase blank time to 1000ms" fix) is confirmed via direct Playwright measurement of the real inter-line timestamps to genuinely produce a 1000ms pause after every line, not merely configured to. **(2) "the traveller greeting looks unfinished ending abruptly"** — `GREETING_END_PAUSE_MS(1200)`, also added the prior turn, is confirmed working exactly as designed: two throwaway scratch verification scripts written to specifically test it kept timing out/showing an inconclusive `currentTime:0` play-call capture, which read at first like a possible bug in the fix itself — root-caused instead to the test harness's own too-short post-bubble wait window (300ms), well short of the real, deliberate 1200ms silent beat now sitting between the last line disappearing and Segment 2 actually resuming; the *real* regression suite's own A9 assertion (`gw_final_video_test.js`) hit the identical gap and was fixed the same way (widening its own wait to 1700ms), immediately turning a false failure into a clean pass — confirming the closing pause was correct all along, only the verification's own timing assumption was wrong. Verified via Playwright: all 5 lines render in the correct order with the correct title+subtitle text and correctly-scaled gold underline beneath each (screenshotted against the real Gate footage); inter-line gaps measure ~3000ms (`LINE_MS` 2000 + `GREETING_GAP_MS` 1000) as requested; the existing regression suite (re-timed for the new 5-line/closing-pause duration — the greeting cycle is now longer, so downstream `waitForFunction` timeouts were widened to match, not the underlying behaviour) plus the completion/tap-to-skip sanity checks, the unrelated Creator Ceremony/Magic Card suite (2 pre-existing failures reconfirmed unrelated to this sprint), and both `goldenBuild.js` suites all pass unchanged, zero console errors. No Theme Contract/Engine V2 Scene Model/Builder/Creator Governing Rules change; confined to `js/gatewaySequence.js` and `css/style.css`, with a matching cache-bust version bump on both stylesheet `<link>` tags in `index.html`.)

- Traveller Greeting Polish — Bigger Type, Gradual Fades, No More Chopped-Off Egg Pickup (four concrete follow-ups on the shipped single-video Traveller pipeline: "make the text appear more polish. Increase the font. let it appear gradually and disappear gradually. right now its abrupts and running very quickly. there is jerk post last text and lumo seems to be abruptly flying. the sequence of him picking up the egg seems to be chopped off." **(1) Font size raised a full step** — `.gateway-greeting-bubble`'s clamp went from `clamp(19px,2.8vw,29px)` to `clamp(24px,3.6vw,38px)`, the subtitle from `clamp(13px,1.6vw,17px)` to `clamp(16px,2vw,21px)`, the mobile breakpoint's own fixed size from 18px to 23px. **(2) The fade itself was redesigned, not just retimed** — the old `gateway-line-in` keyframe spent only ~15%/18% of its own duration on the actual fade (a snap at 300ms/360ms out of a flat 2000ms); the new keyframe (`0%->26%` fade in, hold, `74%->100%` fade out) spends roughly a quarter of the line's own duration on each side, with a longer 18px drift instead of the old faint 10px nudge, and switched from `ease-out` to `ease-in-out` for a smoother glide. A dedicated `GREETING_LINE_MS(2600)` constant — kept deliberately separate from the shared `LINE_MS(2000)` still used by Lumo's own arrival lines on the Returning Creator path, so this stays scoped to what the user is actually looking at — gives a two-line title+subtitle more time to read. `playLines()` now also sets the animation's real duration inline (`bubble.style.animationDuration=lineMs+'ms'`) for every caller, so the fade's actual speed always matches whatever hold time that specific call uses instead of a value hardcoded in CSS that could quietly drift out of sync with it. **(3+4) The real root cause behind "lumo seems to be abruptly flying" and "the sequence of him picking up the egg seems to be chopped off"**: a frame-by-frame `ffmpeg` extraction (a 12-frame montage spanning 4.5s-8.2s) confirmed Segment 2 previously resumed at `RESUME_AT_S=7.5`, hard-skipping the video's own real footage between ~5s and ~7.3s — exactly where Lumo crouches down, grabs the Story Egg back up, and leaps into flight — so a viewer never saw the pickup at all and Segment 2 always opened already mid-air, mid-flight. Frames 4.5s-6.0s all read as the identical held "standing, wings out, Egg on the ground" pose, so resuming from the exact same timestamp Segment 1 paused at (`RESUME_AT_S=PAUSE_AT_S`, no longer a separate later value) costs nothing visually during the dialogue pause and removes the hard seek entirely — `playVideoSegmentTo()` already snaps the video's own `currentTime` to `PAUSE_AT_S` when it pauses, so resuming from the identical value is a genuine no-op seek: the video simply un-pauses exactly where it left off and the crouch/grab/liftoff/flight now all play in full, continuously, for the first time. Verified via Playwright: font sizes measured directly (38px at a 1280px viewport, up from the old 19-29px range); the fade's own opacity was sampled across the transition window and confirmed to ramp gradually rather than snap; the animation's real computed duration matches `GREETING_LINE_MS` exactly; and — the core fix — the video's second `play()` call now fires with `currentTime===5` (not ~7.5 as before), confirmed via a `play()`-call spy across the whole sequence. The existing 15-assertion Traveller/Returning-Creator pipeline suite (re-timed for the new pacing and its own resume-point assertion corrected to expect the fix rather than the old skip) plus the completion/tap-to-skip sanity checks and both `goldenBuild.js` suites all pass unchanged, zero console errors. No Theme Contract/Engine V2 Scene Model/Builder/Creator Governing Rules change; confined to `js/gatewaySequence.js` and `css/style.css`, with a matching cache-bust version bump on both stylesheet `<link>` tags in `index.html`.)

Applied +800ms uniformly to every timing constant that governs how the greeting text itself appears/holds/disappears — `GREETING_LINE_MS` (2600→3400), `GREETING_GAP_MS` (1000→1800), `GREETING_END_PAUSE_MS` (1200→2000) — deliberately keeping their relative proportions unchanged (the fade-in/fade-out keyframe is still a percentage of `GREETING_LINE_MS`, so the fade itself scales proportionally slower too, not just the hold time) rather than retuning the fade curve's own percentages separately. Scoped to the Traveller greeting's own dedicated constants only, not the shared `LINE_MS`/`LINE_GAP_MS` still used by Lumo's in-person arrival lines (Scene 7, both paths) or any Gate/Journey/Arrival/Awaken timing — those weren't what the user's own complaint ("the text") was about. The existing 15-assertion Traveller/Returning-Creator pipeline suite (its own wait timeouts widened to match the now-longer sequence) plus the completion/tap-to-skip sanity checks and both `goldenBuild.js` suites all pass unchanged, zero console errors. - Traveller Privacy — Clear My Projects on a Genuinely New Traveller Session ("another change if the system has identified its a traveller than all the caches should be cleared. traveller should not see projects of previous creators." Investigated the real gap before implementing: `CreatorProjectStore` ("My Projects") uses one flat `localStorage` key (`vihustudio-projects`) with zero scoping by identity — on a shared device, an unclaimed Traveller's own story really does stay visible to whoever opens the browser next, since `MagicCard.list().length===0` (the Traveller Gateway path) is true for both a brand-new device and a previous, still-unclaimed Traveller session. Confirmed the scope directly with the user before touching anything, given the destructive/hard-to-reverse nature of clearing data: **(1) timing** — "the cache clean should only be requested when its entry sequence" — only on a genuinely NEW browser session, never on an in-page reload of an in-progress story; **(2) scope** — My Projects list only, not the current session slot or companion state. Implemented via a new sessionStorage marker, `GATEWAY_SESSION_MARKER` (`'vihu-gateway-session-entered'`) — sessionStorage starts empty in every new tab/window but survives an in-page reload within the same one, exactly matching the required signal. `js/gatewaySequence.js`'s `begin()` now checks this marker immediately after computing `isReturning`: on a genuinely new session (marker absent) where the Traveller path was chosen (not Returning Creator), it calls a new `CreatorProjectStore.clearAll()` (added to `js/creatorProjectStore.js`, wiping the `vihustudio-projects` key outright) before anything else happens; the marker is then set unconditionally (both paths) so the rest of that tab session, including a Returning Creator boot, is correctly treated as "already entered." Verified via a new 5-scenario Playwright suite: a genuinely new Traveller session with a stale previous-Traveller project seeded in `localStorage` gets it wiped to an empty list, with zero console errors; a same-tab-session reload of an in-progress Traveller project is confirmed to NOT be cleared; a Returning Creator boot (a real Magic Card seeded) never clears My Projects under any circumstance. The existing 15-assertion Traveller/Returning-Creator pipeline suite, the completion/tap-to-skip sanity checks, and both `goldenBuild.js` suites all pass unchanged, zero console errors. No Theme Contract/Engine V2 Scene Model/Builder/Creator Governing Rules change; confined to `js/gatewaySequence.js` and `js/creatorProjectStore.js`, no CSS touched, so no cache-bust bump was needed.)

A real, hand-supplied clip (`gate-sequence-final-no-egg.mp4`, audio track stripped to match every other Gateway video's muted convention) shows the identical arc the Traveller path's own `gate-sequence-final.mp4` already used — doors alone → Lumo flies in and lands, standing, wings spread → leaps into flight → carries through the now-open doors into the light — minus the Story Egg, since the Egg is purely a Traveller/Ceremony concept and a Returning Creator has already been through their own Ceremony. Segment 1 plays to the same `PAUSE_AT_S=5` confirmed via `ffmpeg` frame extraction to hold the identical standing pose on both clips through ~5.5s; `opts.pauseLines` then speak IN PERSON over that held frame (the Traveller's own rich 5-line `GREETING_LINES`, or the Returning Creator's own short reunion pair, `LUMO_ARRIVAL_RETURNING_LINES` — repurposed from the old Scene-7-only mechanism into this shared pause-point role); Segment 2 resumes from the exact same timestamp (a genuine no-op seek) and plays to the clip's own real end; a brief final flash via the already-shared `playFinalFlash`, then hand-off. `preloadFinalGateVideo()`/`mountFinalGate()` (built for the Traveller path) are now generalized/reused as-is for both clips. Verified via a new 18-assertion Playwright suite exercising the full Returning Creator flow end-to-end (the no-egg clip mounts with zero halo/particle/Lumo-stage elements; the recognition line plays before any playback starts; the video is confirmed NOT playing during that line; the Gateway hides for the real Creator Signature challenge and a real pattern tap correctly verifies it; Segment 1 only then starts; the reunion line plays in person at the pause; Segment 2 resumes with zero skip; the sequence completes) plus a Traveller-path spot-check confirming zero regression; the existing 15-assertion pipeline suite (updated for the Returning Creator's own now-correct new-video/no-halo assertions — the two prior failures were confirmed to be exactly the old, now-intentionally-superseded behavior, not a regression) and a dedicated Gateway-to-Studio-boot hand-off smoke test (both paths correctly reach Creation Flow/the ambient companion afterward) all pass, zero console errors. Both `goldenBuild.js` suites (World Builder v1 and v2, unaffected — this sprint touches zero Builder files) pass unchanged. `assets/video/gateway/README.md` rewritten to document all three real Gate clips (the superseded `gate-sequence.mp4`, the Traveller's `gate-sequence-final.mp4`, the Returning Creator's new `gate-sequence-final-no-egg.mp4`) and the now-unified mechanism; the separately-uploaded `gate-sequence-01.mp4` (showing Lumo flying INTO the gate, a real canon conflict with this file's own frozen "Lumo never enters the Hall" rule) remains disclosed and unwired pending explicit product direction. No Theme Contract/Engine V2 Scene Model/Builder/Creator Governing Rules change; confined to `js/gatewaySequence.js`, `css/style.css`, `assets/video/gateway/` (a new video + poster), and its README.)

- Traveller Gateway — Creator Signature Decline Becomes a Real Choice (Retry / Continue as a Traveller) (a direct follow-up to the just-shipped Returning Creator video unification: "the sequence is good. only step 5 option b" — step 5 being the Creator Signature tap-grid check (`js/magicCardUI.js`'s `MagicCardUI.beginCreatorSignature`, called from `js/gatewaySequence.js`'s `runVideoSequence`). A first clarifying `AskUserQuestion` attempt was explicitly rejected by the user; asked directly afterward ("did u got the ans ?"), the honest answer was no answer had been received yet — the user then supplied it in plain text: "retry or continue as traveller . options." **The real gap**: a wrong tap already retried in place correctly (the challenge just clears the board and says "try again," no change needed there) — but the challenge's own "← Back" escape hatch previously called `onResult(false,null)` immediately and silently, clearing the active Magic Card identity and falling straight through into `beginSegment1()` using the SAME `opts` object still bound to the Returning Creator's own no-egg video and reunion-toned `LUMO_ARRIVAL_RETURNING_LINES` — a genuinely inconsistent, previously-silent bug: declining showed a just-cleared identity riding along on a video/greeting that still said "It's good to see you again." **Fixed in two places**. (1) `beginCreatorSignature` is rewritten around two named inner functions, `showChallenge()`/`showChoice()` — the challenge's `onBack` now opens a small, real choice screen instead of deciding anything on its own: "Not able to show your stars right now?" followed by a bold primary "🔁 Try Again" button (re-opens a fresh `showChallenge()`) and a quiet "🌱 Continue as a Traveller" link (the only path that now calls `onResult(false,null)`) — both reusing 100% pre-existing CSS classes (`.magic-card-gate-continue`, `.magic-card-gate-notyou`, `.magic-card-gate-welcome`) and the file's own `_el()` helper, zero new CSS needed. (2) `runVideoSequence`'s decline branch in `js/gatewaySequence.js` no longer just clears the identity and continues down the Returning Creator's own path — since verification always happens BEFORE Segment 1 ever plays, the mounted no-egg video is still paused on its very first (closed-doors) frame at this exact moment, so the fix cleanly tears down that unplayed video/wrap, mounts the real Traveller clip (`GATE_FINAL_VIDEO_SRC`/`GATE_FINAL_POSTER_SRC`, WITH the Story Egg), and recursively re-invokes the same `runVideoSequence(video,opts)` mechanism with the Traveller's own `opts` (`preLines:null`, `pauseLines:GREETING_LINES`) — a declined check now genuinely BECOMES the real Traveller experience (its own clip, its own first-meeting 5-line greeting), not a Returning-Creator-flavoured one with a quietly-cleared identity underneath it. Verified via a new, dedicated 11-assertion Playwright suite covering all three real paths end-to-end: Scenario A confirms "← Back" opens the real choice screen (correct button text, tap-grid genuinely gone underneath, not just covered); Scenario B confirms "Try Again" re-opens a genuinely fresh challenge and a correct pattern tap afterward still succeeds normally; Scenario C confirms "Continue as a Traveller" swaps the mounted video to the real `gate-sequence-final.mp4` (confirmed via URL string check excluding "no-egg"), clears the active Magic Card id from `localStorage`, and shows the Traveller's own "Welcome, Traveller." greeting (not the reunion pair) at the pause point, with zero unexpected console errors. Full regression across the entire existing Gateway/Magic-Card/Creator Playwright suite (`gw_final_video_test.js` 15/15, `gw_returning_unified_test.js` 18/18, `gw_completion_check.js`, `gateway_skip_check.js`, `gw_myprojects_clear_check.js` 5/5, `gw_smoke_handoff.js` 6/6) and both `goldenBuild.js` suites (World Builder v1 and v2, unaffected — this fix touches zero Builder files) pass unchanged, zero console errors. - Traveller Unpublished-Work Notice + World Card Constellation Crossing-Lines Fix ("1st for a traveller who once start creating. we need to tell if they do not publish their creation might get lost. this will help us in keeping data clean. second the star marker grid needs rework. it cannot mark any constellation which has crossing lines. check the stars assigned to vihupapa. the constellation is in shape of number 4." Two independent fixes. **(1) Traveller Save Notice**: new `js/travellerSaveNotice.js` — a small floating toast, deliberately NOT slotted into `.workspace`'s own fixed `calc(100vh - 64px)` grid (this codebase has hit that exact class of height-overflow bug more than once when a new sibling was added there) — shown only when ALL of: no Magic Card is active (`MagicCard.getActive()` falsy — a Traveller, not a Creator, who already has real Cloud Backup via their claimed card), the active project has at least one real page ("once start creating" — `AppState.slides.length>0`), it hasn't already been published this browser tab session, and it wasn't dismissed this tab session (`sessionStorage`, so it reappears on a genuinely new session, matching the exact "reappears next session" convention the Traveller Privacy sprint's own `CreatorProjectStore.clearAll()` already established rather than a permanent, one-time-forever dismiss). Reads "You're creating as a Traveller — publish your adventure (or claim your Magic Card) to make sure it's kept safe." with a "📖 Publish Now" button (clicks the real `#publishBtn`) and a dismiss "✕" — both buttons needed explicit `!important` width/height/margin overrides to escape this codebase's own established global `button:not(...){width:100%;margin-bottom:12px}` cascade rule, the same recurring bug class already fixed for Object Strip cards/the Publish Studio close button/Doodle's pen swatches. A thin host-binding module (`configure({...})`, matching the `js/objectStrip.js`/`js/contextPanel.js`/`js/pageRuntime.js` pattern) — wired in `js/app.js`, refreshed from `js/pageRuntime.js`'s own `PageRuntime.notify()` (the real choke point every meaningful Workspace mutation already calls, so no per-event wiring of its own was needed beyond one `configure()` call) and from `js/magicCardUI.js`'s `refreshHeaderBadge()` (every moment a Traveller may have just become a Creator — claim/rename/rehydrate/boot — needs this gate re-checked immediately, not on the next unrelated page notify); `js/publishStudio.js`'s `_finalizePublish()` calls `TravellerSaveNotice.markPublished()` the instant a real Publish succeeds, hiding it for the rest of the session since there's nothing left to nag about. **(2) World Card Constellation Fix**: a real, reported bug in `js/cardPlatform.js`'s and `js/magicCard.js`'s shared `CONSTELLATIONS` table — every connecting-line drawer in this codebase (`js/magicCardArt.js`'s `drawBack`, `js/magicCardUI.js`'s `_renderConstellation`) draws a straight line between each consecutive pair of points in the array's own order, and CYGNUS's original order (Top, Center, Bottom, Left, Right) drew its last segment (Left-to-Right) straight back through the Center point a second time — exactly the overlapping "number 4"-looking defect reported on a real claimed card. Confirmed via a real segment-intersection algorithm (orientation + `onSegment` checks, not eyeballed) before touching anything: the other four constellations (Orion/Cassiopeia/Ursa Major/Lyra) were already crossing-free in their base order and stayed that way — only CYGNUS had a genuine defect. Fixed by reordering to Top, Center, Left, Bottom, Right — traces the identical five points with zero self-crossing or vertex pass-through, verified (not just reasoned) to stay crossing-free across every one of `_placeConstellation()`'s 4-rotation × mirror-on/off combinations too, since a rotation/reflection/translation never changes whether two line segments cross. Both files kept in lockstep, matching this codebase's own established duplication discipline for this exact pair of modules. Verified via a new Node geometry script confirming: the original CYGNUS order reproduces a real, detected crossing; every constellation in both its base order and all 8 rotate/mirror combinations is crossing-free after the fix; a live Playwright screenshot of `MagicCardArt.drawBack()` rendering the fixed CYGNUS pattern shows a clean, non-overlapping kite/arrow shape instead of the old overlapping tangle. A new 15-assertion Playwright suite for the notice (a fresh Traveller with zero pages sees nothing; it appears once a real page exists; dismissing hides it and persists across an in-page reload but reappears on a genuinely new session; a claimed Creator never sees it even with real pages; `markPublished()` hides it) all pass, plus full regression across the existing Gateway/Magic-Card Playwright suite (`gw_final_video_test.js` 15/15, `gw_returning_unified_test.js` 18/18, `gw_completion_check.js`, `gateway_skip_check.js`, `gw_myprojects_clear_check.js` 5/5, `gw_smoke_handoff.js` 6/6, `gw_decline_choice_test.js` 11/11) and both `goldenBuild.js` suites (World Builder v1 and v2, unaffected — neither fix touches Builder files) pass unchanged, zero console errors. No Theme Contract/Engine V2 Scene Model/Builder/Creator Governing Rules change; confined to a new `js/travellerSaveNotice.js` plus `js/app.js`, `js/pageRuntime.js`, `js/magicCardUI.js`, `js/publishStudio.js`, `css/style.css`, `index.html`, `js/cardPlatform.js`, and `js/magicCard.js`.)

- Constellation Crossing-Lines Fix — Retroactive Repair for Already-Claimed Cards ("can you show me whats the pattern for vihupapa now" — while confirming the fix, found the `CONSTELLATIONS.CYGNUS` reorder only helps NEW claims: `MagicCard.claim()` stores a card's real pattern permanently at claim time (`js/magicCard.js`'s `pattern:placed.pattern`), never re-derived from the `CONSTELLATIONS` table on later renders, so an already-claimed CYGNUS card (like a real "vihupapa" card claimed before the previous fix shipped) would have kept showing the old, self-crossing order forever with no way to reach it. Fixed with a real, one-time repair: a new `_migrateCygnusOrder(cards)` runs inside `js/magicCard.js`'s `_readCards()` — every time cards are read from `localStorage`, any CYGNUS card with a 5-point pattern and no `constellationOrderFixed` flag gets its stored points reordered via `[p[0],p[1],p[3],p[2],p[4]]`, the exact same index permutation the base array's own Top/Center/Bottom/Left/Right → Top/Center/Left/Bottom/Right reorder applied — correct regardless of which random rotation/mirror the card got at claim time, since `_rotate`/`_mirrorHorizontal`/`_shiftToOrigin` are all plain `.map()` calls that never change array order (index 0 is always the transformed "Top" point, etc, for every card). Same stars, same position, only the connect-the-dots order changes — `recall_magic_card()` already matches a tapped pattern order-independently, so this can never affect whether a real device can still recall the card. Gated by the one-time flag so it runs exactly once per card and never re-touches an already-correct pattern from a claim made after the previous fix shipped (verified idempotent via two consecutive reads). Verified via a new Playwright check seeding a real pre-fix-shaped card (`constellation:'CYGNUS'`, the old defective pattern, no fix flag, nickname "vihupapa") and confirming: the migration runs automatically on load, the repaired pattern matches the corrected order exactly, a second reload doesn't re-touch it, and `MagicCardArt.drawBack()` renders the repaired card as a clean, non-overlapping kite/arrow shape (screenshotted) instead of the old "number 4" tangle. Disclosed honestly: I don't have access to the user's own real, live claimed card — Magic Cards are 100% client-side by design, stored only in the user's own browser — so this fix means the next time they open the app in their own browser, their real card's stored pattern gets silently, automatically, and permanently repaired with zero action needed from them. Full regression: `gw_decline_choice_test.js` 11/11, `traveller_save_notice_test.js` 15/15, `gw_returning_unified_test.js` 18/18, and both `goldenBuild.js` suites (World Builder v1 and v2, unaffected — this fix touches zero Builder files) all pass unchanged, zero console errors. No Theme Contract/Engine V2 Scene Model/Builder/Creator Governing Rules change; confined to `js/magicCard.js`.)

- Traveller Save Notice — Repositioned Out of the Object Strip's Way, Copy Corrected (two real, user-reported fixes on a real screenshot of a live Workspace: "we need to reposition this. or allow traveller to reposition this. also why we are saying claim magic card as there is no other way to claim the card." **(1) Reposition**: the notice originally rendered as a `position:fixed` toast anchored to the viewport bottom-center — the screenshot showed it visually colliding with the Object Strip's own cards and scroll-arrow buttons at the bottom of the canvas column. Rather than build a user-facing drag-to-reposition control (the alternative the user themselves floated, mirroring the Companion widget's own draggable behaviour), the simpler, more robust fix was to stop floating it at all: `js/travellerSaveNotice.js`'s `_ensureDom()` now mounts the notice as a normal, in-flow element — specifically the very FIRST child of `.right-sidebar` — instead of appending to `document.body` with fixed positioning. `.right-sidebar` already has `overflow-y:auto` (a safe container for new in-flow content) and the notice sits ahead of `#contextPanelRoot`, so it's never wiped by `ContextPanel.refresh()`'s own frequent `panelRoot.innerHTML=''` calls, which only ever touch `#contextPanelRoot`'s own children, not its siblings. A first attempt inserted the notice "right after `.tabs`" (mirroring where `ContextPanel.init()` itself inserts `#contextPanelRoot`) — this turned out to be a real, boot-order-dependent bug, caught by a Playwright DOM-order check before shipping: if `TravellerSaveNotice.refresh()`'s first call happened to run before `ContextPanel.init()` (which it does, in the real boot sequence), the notice would insert itself right after `.tabs` first, and `ContextPanel.init()`'s own later `insertBefore(panelRoot, tabsEl.nextSibling)` call would then insert `#contextPanelRoot` BEFORE the already-present notice — silently pushing the safety notice down below the entire Context Panel instead of above it. Fixed by dropping the `.tabs`-relative logic entirely in favour of always inserting as `.right-sidebar`'s unconditional first child — simpler, and immune to any future ordering change between the two modules' own initialization. `css/style.css`'s `.traveller-save-notice*` rules were rewritten from a floating toast (fixed position, translateX centering, a horizontal icon+text+buttons row) into a normal sidebar card (a `margin-bottom` sitting in the section-gap flow, a stacked icon+text+dismiss row on top with a full-width "📖 Publish Now" button beneath) — the same recurring `button:not(...){width:100%;margin-bottom:12px}` global-cascade override discipline this codebase has fixed repeatedly (Object Strip cards, the Publish Studio close button, Doodle's pen swatches) still applies to both buttons, just with different explicit widths now that the layout is vertical rather than horizontal. **(2) Copy correction**: the notice previously read "...publish your adventure (or claim your Magic Card) to make sure it's kept safe" — factually misleading, since there is no independent, separately-reachable way to claim a Magic Card; the ONLY path is `MagicCard.shouldOfferAwakening()`'s own ceremony, offered automatically the instant a first Publish actually succeeds (`js/publishStudio.js`'s `_finalizePublish`). Reworded to name exactly one real action: "You're creating as a Traveller. Publish your adventure to make sure it's kept safe." — no longer implying "publish OR claim" are two independent choices, since claiming is a downstream consequence of publishing, not an alternative to it. Verified via a new 12-assertion Playwright suite (`tsn_reposition_check.js`, scratch-only) confirming the notice mounts inside `.right-sidebar` (not `document.body`), is genuinely NOT `position:fixed`, has real non-zero layout size, does not visually overlap the Object Strip's own bounding rect, is the true first child of `.right-sidebar`, the corrected copy no longer mentions "claim your Magic Card" while still mentioning Publish, and both buttons (Publish Now / Dismiss) remain fully functional from the new location — plus a full re-run of the original 15-assertion `traveller_save_notice_test.js` suite (whose own `pushOnePageAndNotify` test helper needed one matching fix: it previously only hid `#creationFlowOverlay` without removing `body.creation-flow-active`, an incomplete stand-in for the real `_finish()`/`_closeOverlay()` sequence that never mattered while the notice was a fixed-position toast outside `#app`'s own `display:none` gating, but does matter now that the notice lives inside `.right-sidebar`, a real `#app` descendant) — all 15 pass unchanged. Full regression across the entire existing Gateway/Magic-Card Playwright suite (`gw_final_video_test.js` 15/15, `gw_returning_unified_test.js` 18/18, `gw_completion_check.js`, `gateway_skip_check.js`, `gw_myprojects_clear_check.js` 5/5, `gw_smoke_handoff.js` 6/6, `gw_decline_choice_test.js` 11/11) and both `goldenBuild.js` suites (World Builder v1 and v2, unaffected) pass unchanged, zero console errors. No Theme Contract/Engine V2 Scene Model/Builder/Creator Governing Rules change; confined to `js/travellerSaveNotice.js` and `css/style.css`.)

- Creator Signature Tap Board — Legible, Kid-Friendly Rework (a real, user-supplied screenshot showed the "Lumo, the Gatekeeper" constellation tap challenge with almost every one of its 100 grid cells fully invisible — "fix this screen also. very difficult to show the stars," followed by a direct product correction mid-fix: "think kids. its not easy for kids. they need fun not a test." **Root cause**: only a sparse, randomly-chosen ~22% subset of cells (`js/magicCardUI.js`'s `_gateBuildGrid`, the `--decoy` class) ever showed any glow at all — the remaining ~78% were fully `color:transparent`, so on a touch device (no `:hover` at all before the tap itself) a kid had no visual cue where most of the 100 tappable positions even were. **Fixed by making every cell visible, uniformly, at rest** — the sparse decoy/invisible split is removed entirely (`_gateBuildGrid` no longer computes a `decoySet` at all; every cell gets the identical base `.magic-card-tapgrid-cell` class), and `css/style.css`'s base cell rule changed from `color:transparent`/`font-size:15px` to a real, legible `color:rgba(255,255,255,.34)` with a soft `text-shadow` glow and `font-size:20px` — a genuine improvement on the original "camouflage" idea, not a trade-off against it: with every cell now identical at rest, there's no visible subset left to distinguish from "real" positions, so a shoulder-surfer watching a real tap sequence still can't tell a genuine tap from the rest of the now-uniformly-dim starfield around it. Added a real `:active` state (`rgba(255,255,255,.9)`, `scale(1.15)`) alongside the existing `:hover`, since touch devices often skip `:hover` entirely and need their own immediate tap feedback. The board's own width cap grew from 460px to 520px (`.magic-card-tapgrid-boardwrap`) for bigger, friendlier touch targets — safe to grow, since `_fitBoardToAvailableSpace()` already shrinks it back down on any viewport too short to fit it. Each cell also gained a gentle, randomized twinkle (`magicCardStarTwinkle`, a pure `opacity` keyframe independent of the `color` alpha channel so it never fights the hover/active/selected transitions; per-cell `animation-delay`/`animation-duration` set inline in `_gateBuildGrid` via `Math.random()` so the whole board twinkles out of sync like a real sky, not one flat uniform pulse; fully disabled under `prefers-reduced-motion`). **The "fun not a test" correction went beyond legibility into the interaction and copy itself**: (1) every subtitle on this screen ("Tap your stars, in order, to continue.") dropped "in order" — a real, previously-unnoticed correctness gap, not just a tone fix: both the local `_patternsMatch` check and the real `recall_magic_card()` RPC have always compared taps as an unordered SET, never a sequence, so telling a kid to remember a strict order was needless pressure for a rule that was never actually enforced. (2) the button and status copy were softened from clinical pass/fail wording to this screen's own established "sky" language (matching Magic Card Home's existing "your sky is alive") — "✨ Confirm" → "✨ That's My Sky!"; "Checking…" → "✨ Looking for your sky…"; "✓ Welcome back!" → "✨ Found it! Welcome back!"; "✗ Not quite — try again." → "Not quite — let's try again! 🌟" (no more ✗ marks reading as a wrong-answer buzzer); "Tap at least two stars first." → "Tap a couple of stars first! ✨". Verified via a new 16-assertion Playwright suite (`tapgrid_visibility_check.js`, scratch-only): all 100 cells render with real, identical, non-zero rest opacity (no invisible subset, no `--decoy` class anywhere); font-size genuinely bumped; the real tap-select/connecting-line/counter mechanics still work end to end; the subtitle no longer says "in order" while still mentioning stars; the confirm button uses the new "sky" wording; a real wrong-guess shows the softened error text with no ✗ mark; every cell carries the twinkle animation with genuinely randomized per-cell timing; zero console errors. Full regression across the entire existing Gateway/Magic-Card Playwright suite (`gw_final_video_test.js` 15/15, `gw_completion_check.js`, `gateway_skip_check.js`, `gw_myprojects_clear_check.js` 5/5, `gw_smoke_handoff.js` 6/6, `gw_decline_choice_test.js` 11/11, `traveller_save_notice_test.js` 15/15, `tsn_reposition_check.js` 12/12) and both `goldenBuild.js` suites (World Builder v1 and v2, unaffected) pass unchanged, zero console errors; `gw_returning_unified_test.js`'s own `button:has-text("Confirm")` selector needed updating to the stable `.magic-card-tapgrid-confirm` class — the intended, disclosed consequence of the copy rename, not a regression (18/18 after the fix). No Theme Contract/Engine V2 Scene Model/Builder/Creator Governing Rules change; confined to `js/magicCardUI.js` and `css/style.css`.)

- Lumo Voice — First Real Recording Wired In (Tap-Grid Gatekeeper Line) (begins replacing Lumo's typewriter-only dialogue with real recorded voice, one line at a time, as the user supplies actual recordings. New `js/lumoVoice.js` mirrors `js/gatewayAudio.js`'s own proven discipline exactly: no autoplay, playback fires only from inside a real click-originated call chain (every caller sits inside a user-gesture handler), one shared volume constant, cached `Audio` objects, every failure swallowed defensively — a line with no entry yet, or whose file 404s, is a normal silent no-op, matching how the on-screen text already reveals via its own typewriter animation whether or not audio exists for it. The Creator Signature tap-grid Gatekeeper's own greeting (`js/magicCardUI.js`'s `_buildGatekeeperHeader`) is the first line to get real audio: its text collapsed from a nickname/fallback ternary (`"<name>, the Creator — show me your stars, and you may pass."` / `"Traveler, show me your stars, and you may pass."`) into one unified line, "My friend, show me your stars, and you may pass." — no nickname/fallback split needed once the greeting itself doesn't address anyone by name, per direct product instruction. `LumoVoice.play('tapgrid')` fires alongside the typewriter reveal, playing the real, user-recorded `assets/lumo/voice/lumo-01-tapgrid.mp3`. Verified genuinely live — not just the isolated audio file in isolation — via a headless-browser check driving the actual reachable code path: `MagicCardUI.checkIdentityGate()`'s standalone Welcome screen's "Return to My Adventure" button, since the Traveller Gateway's own primary Returning-Creator boot flow (`beginCreatorSignature`) still deliberately passes `skipSpeech:true` to avoid repeating the Gateway's own separate "Welcome home… show me your stars" greeting — confirming both the correct unified text renders and a real `Audio().play()` call fires against the correct file, at the exact moment the bubble appears. Full regression across the existing Gateway/Magic-Card Playwright suite (`gw_returning_unified_test.js` 18/18, `tapgrid_visibility_check.js` 16/16) passes unchanged, zero console errors. The remaining ~11 Lumo lines (the Gateway's own greeting/reunion dialogue, the Creator Ceremony's beats) deliberately stay on typewriter-only text this pass, pending their own recordings, per the user's own explicit "we will update the text prompts in code in one go" instruction for the rest of the batch — this entry covers only the one line verified end-to-end as a live proof of the mechanism before committing to the full set. - Lumo Voice — Full Batch: All 17 Lines Wired, Timing Synced to Real Recordings (completes the one-line proof of concept above into the full batch, per the user's own "we will update the text prompts in code in one go" instruction, once every remaining recording had actually arrived (confirmed directly — "is any file left?" surfaced exactly 6 outstanding lines, all supplied and staged in this pass: the Returning Creator's recognition pair "Welcome home."/"Show me your stars.", its reunion pair "It's good to see you again."/"Welcome back to your story.", and the Creator Ceremony's two Guardian beats "A new light is stirring..."/"I bless this Story Egg." -- alongside the 10 Traveller-greeting clips staged in an earlier, code-untouched asset-only commit). `js/lumoVoice.js`'s `LINES` map is rewritten from a bare id-to-filename lookup into `id -> {file,ms}`, where `ms` is each clip's own real, ffprobe-measured duration -- exposed synchronously via a new `durationMs(ids)` (accepts a single id or an array, summing) since every one of these 17 clips is a known, already-recorded, static asset with no metadata-loading race worth managing; a new `playSequence(ids)` chains one or several clips back to back off each one's own real `ended` event (used for the Traveller greeting's title-then-subtitle pairs), falling back to `play(id)` for a lone id. A real timing problem was found, not assumed away, before wiring anything blindly: measuring all 10 Traveller-greeting clips showed several title+subtitle pairs run far longer than the existing fixed `GREETING_LINE_MS(3400)` beat -- one pair alone (`greeting4`+`greeting4b`) totals ~7.6s -- so playing them as-is against the old flat timer would have cut Lumo off mid-sentence on 4 of the 5 lines. Fixed at the root: `js/gatewaySequence.js`'s `playLines()` gained an optional parallel `voiceIds` array (one entry per line -- a single id, an array of ids, or null for an unrecorded line) and now computes each line's real effective hold as `Math.max(lineMs, LumoVoice.durationMs(voice)+400)`, stretching the on-screen bubble (and its own fade-in/fade-out `animationDuration`, already scaled to whatever hold is passed) to genuinely fit the real recorded voice rather than a guessed constant -- a line with no recording keeps its exact original fixed timing, unaffected. Wired at all three real call sites: the Traveller's 5-pair `GREETING_LINES`/new `GREETING_VOICE_IDS`, the Returning Creator's `RETURNING_LINES`/`RETURNING_VOICE_IDS` (pre-verification recognition) and `LUMO_ARRIVAL_RETURNING_LINES`/`LUMO_ARRIVAL_RETURNING_VOICE_IDS` (post-verification reunion, played in person at the video's own pause point) -- both threaded through `runVideoSequence`'s existing `opts.preLines`/`opts.pauseLines` pattern as sibling `opts.preVoiceIds`/`opts.pauseVoiceIds` fields, including the Traveller-decline fallback path that re-runs `runVideoSequence` with the Traveller's own clip. The Creator Ceremony's two Guardian beats (`js/companionDirector.js`'s `getCeremonySequence`) each gained a `voiceId` field (`ceremony1`/`ceremony2`); `js/magicCardUI.js`'s `_playCeremonyBeats` calls `LumoVoice.play(beat.voiceId)` right where `els.msg.textContent` is set -- a no-op for every other beat (the Story Egg's silent beats, and the newly-bonded Story Companion's own "Hello!" line, which isn't Lumo and has no recording of its own) -- left completely untouched, since both Guardian beats' real recorded durations (2.0s/2.4s) already comfortably fit their existing fixed `durationMs` (2400ms/2600ms), needing no stretch logic there at all. Verified via a new 8-assertion Playwright suite driving all three real surfaces end-to-end through actual UI interaction (not internals): the Traveller path plays all 10 greeting clips in the correct title-then-subtitle, line-by-line order; the Returning Creator path plays its recognition pair before the real Creator Signature tap-grid check and its reunion pair after; a full Awakening-Claim-nickname-Ceremony run plays both Guardian lines at their correct beats. Two pre-existing scratch tests' own fixed wait timeouts, written against the old flat 3400ms-per-line assumption, needed widening to match the new, correctly-longer, voice-synced total (`gw_final_video_test.js`'s greeting-wait 34000ms to 42000ms) -- the intended, disclosed consequence of this fix, not a regression, reverified at 15/15 and 18/18 respectively afterward; `ceremony_regression_test2.js`'s own 2 failures (the overlay/onDone checks, which don't account for the First Claimed Moment screen requiring a click to close) were confirmed via `git stash` to already fail identically on the unmodified baseline, unrelated to this change. Full regression across the entire existing Gateway/Magic-Card Playwright suite (`gw_returning_unified_test.js` 18/18, `gw_final_video_test.js` 15/15, `gw_decline_choice_test.js` 11/11, `tapgrid_visibility_check.js` 16/16, `traveller_save_notice_test.js` 15/15) passes unchanged, zero console errors. Every one of Lumo's ~17 spoken lines in the app now has real recorded audio, correctly timed. No Theme Contract/Engine V2 Scene Model/Builder/Creator Governing Rules change; `tools/world-builder/`/`tools/world-builder-v2/` untouched (both `goldenBuild.js` suites structurally unaffected); confined to `js/lumoVoice.js`, `js/gatewaySequence.js`, `js/companionDirector.js`, `js/magicCardUI.js`, and 6 new recorded audio files.)

- The Atmosphere Engine — Vision + V1 Implementation Blueprint (two paired, investigation-and-design-only documents, no code changes -- matching the standing "architecture changes require explicit approval" precedent already set by `docs/ENGINE_V2_PROMOTION_STRATEGY.md`/`docs/SCENE_ADAPTER_ARCHITECTURE_ANALYSIS.md`. Requested as a from-scratch design exercise: "Design the complete Atmosphere Engine... think like a creative director and systems architect... challenge assumptions if you believe there is a better architecture." `docs/ATMOSPHERE_ENGINE.md` is the long-term vision -- reframes the originally-proposed four-peer-layer model (Foundation/World/Interactive/Character) into two continuous beds (Foundation, World Tint) plus three event-driven streams (a new "Living Details" sparse-aliveness layer, Interactive Stings, Character Voice), and proposes applying this codebase's own proven Runtime+Director split (already used by `CompanionEngine`/`CompanionDirector` and `ThemeEngine`/`ThemeRegistry`) to a future `AtmosphereEngine`/`AtmosphereDirector` pair. Covers philosophy, layer purposes, volume hierarchy, loop-sync/crossfade strategy, fatigue avoidance over multi-hour sessions (pool rotation as the single highest-leverage fix given ElevenLabs' 30-second generation cap), the three-tier World-extends-Foundation resolution ladder (mirroring Theme Language v2's own Preset->Override->Default ladder), folder structure, naming, weather/time-of-day as a future *substituting* (never additive) Modifier tier, performance/preload/crossfade recommendations, and a sonic-brand-identity section proposing a concrete timbral fingerprint for the Foundation Bed plus a future `docs/ATMOSPHERE_SONIC_CANON.md` mirroring `docs/STUDIO_DESIGN_CANON.md`'s own role for visual identity. Once the user froze the architecture and explicitly descoped almost everything above for V1 ("Do NOT redesign... Do NOT introduce additional subsystems... The following ideas are intentionally OUT OF SCOPE: Runtime Director, Audio Director, pool rotation, Living Details, procedural ambience, random scheduling, automatic breathing, dynamic modulation, weather, time-of-day, audio buses, DSP, complex ducking, multiple ambience variations, advanced state machines"), `docs/ATMOSPHERE_V1_BLUEPRINT.md` was written as the actual implementation-ready specification for the Minimum Lovable Atmosphere System (MLAS) -- explicitly superseding the vision doc for V1 scope only. **One module, no Director**: a single `AudioManager` (new `js/audioManager.js`, IIFE singleton, same shape as the existing `js/gatewayAudio.js`/`js/lumoVoice.js`) with exactly the responsibility list requested (init/load/play-Foundation/play-World/stop-World/mute/volume/persist-preference/shutdown) and nothing else -- no coordinating module, no per-layer ducking, no scheduling. World-switching is wired as two one-line, defensively-wrapped hooks into the exact existing functions that already know when a Theme/World changes -- `js/themeEngine.js`'s `applyTheme()` (line 608) and `applyArtworkTheme()` (line 631) -- mirroring the identical `try{ if(typeof CompanionDirector!=='undefined') CompanionDirector.notify(...) }catch(e){} ` hook shape already proven throughout this codebase, rather than inventing a second coordinating brain. Manifest contract: an optional `theme.audio.ambience` array (bare filenames resolved against a fixed pool, or already-qualified paths used as-is), absent by default for every existing Theme with zero behavior change -- resolution mirrors, but doesn't call, `ThemeRegistry.resolveAssetRef()`'s own dual-mode passthrough-vs-resolve logic, since that function is scoped to a Theme package's own compiled image/font assets map and V1's ambience files live in a fixed app-owned folder instead. Folder structure departs from the user's own sketch in two disclosed, justified ways: `assets/audio/worlds/` is a flat shared pool (not per-World-id subfolders), since the five already-generated ElevenLabs assets -- Air (assumed Foundation), Harmony/Magic/Forest/Wind (assumed initial World-ambience pool, inferred from the user's own manifest example using `forest.mp3`) -- are general-purpose platform content, not yet bespoke per-Theme; and no `companions/` subfolder is created, since Lumo's voice already lives, shipped and wired, at `assets/lumo/voice/` and a second empty home would be redundant. Recommends plain `HTMLAudioElement` (`loop=true` + interval-based volume ramps) over the Web Audio API for V1, explicitly to stay consistent with every existing audio module in this codebase and avoid introducing a second, separate autoplay-unlock lifecycle (`AudioContext`'s own suspended-until-resumed state on top of `<audio>`'s own autoplay policy) -- the one accepted, disclosed trade-off being native loop-seam clicks on some browser/codec combinations, named as the concrete trigger for revisiting with Web Audio API later rather than building it preemptively. The one piece of smoothing kept in V1 (a fixed ~2s linear fade on World start/stop, ~300ms on mute/unmute) is disclosed as a bare-necessity click-avoidance, not the "complex ducking"/curves/randomization explicitly cut. Every other Vision-doc mechanism (pool rotation, Living Details, weather, DSP, a coordinating Director) is named as a future extension point, not built. No code was written for either document -- both are proposals awaiting their own separate implementation approval, per this repo's standing rule.)

- Atmosphere Engine V1 (MLAS) — Implementation, Corrected Model (the real code, following directly from the blueprint above -- and a real, explicit correction to that blueprint's own central assumption, caught before any of the five real audio files ever needed to exist to prove the fix out. The blueprint guessed that of the five already-generated ElevenLabs tracks (Air, Harmony, Magic, Forest, Wind), one -- Air -- was a single Foundation track and the other four were an initial World-ambience pool; the product owner corrected this directly: **all five are Foundation layers, and all five loop simultaneously, always, at their own fixed relative volumes, forming one composite always-on sound.** "Keep all five Foundation layers. The simplification was architectural, not experiential... the AudioManager simply loads the five Foundation layers, applies fixed volumes, loops them indefinitely and optionally overlays a World ambience layer. The runtime remains intentionally simple while preserving the full emotional richness of the soundscape." New `js/audioManager.js` (`window.AudioManager`, an IIFE singleton mirroring `js/gatewayAudio.js`/`js/lumoVoice.js`'s own proven discipline exactly -- plain `HTMLAudioElement`, zero autoplay, every failure swallowed defensively) implements exactly this: a fixed `FOUNDATION_LAYERS` table (`air.mp3:0.5, harmony.mp3:0.4, magic.mp3:0.3, forest.mp3:0.35, wind.mp3:0.3` -- a placeholder mix, disclosed as needing re-tuning by ear once the five real files exist and can be heard together) drives `init()`, which constructs all five `<audio loop>` elements up front and installs one shared, self-removing `pointerdown`/`keydown` unlock listener (the same "wait for a real user gesture, then play everything" pattern already proven for the Traveller Gateway's own audio) that starts all five together on the very first real interaction after boot -- never on page load itself. `playWorld(ambienceRefs)`/`stopWorld()` add or remove exactly one optional additional looping layer on top, crossfaded via a small, generic linear `_ramp()` helper (~2s for World start/stop, ~300ms for mute/unmute -- the one piece of smoothing kept in V1, disclosed as bare click-avoidance, never the "complex ducking"/curves/DSP the product owner explicitly cut) -- a no-op re-entry guard (`JSON.stringify`'d ref array compared against the currently-playing one) means re-applying the same Theme's own ambience never restarts or double-crossfades it. `setMuted`/`isMuted`/`setVolume`/`getVolume` persist to `localStorage` (`vihu-audio-muted`/`vihu-audio-volume`) matching every other persisted preference in this codebase; `shutdown()` tears everything down cleanly (clears every fade timer, pauses and clears every element's `src`, removes the unlock listener) for symmetry, though nothing currently calls it. **Wired exactly per the blueprint's own hook plan, verified against real line numbers before writing anything**: `index.html` gained one `<script src='js/audioManager.js'>` tag, positioned between `js/companionDirector.js` and `js/gatewayAudio.js`; `js/app.js`'s `_beginBoot()` gained one `try{ if(typeof AudioManager!=='undefined') AudioManager.init(); }catch(e){}` line immediately after the existing `CompanionDirector.init()` call, deliberately at that exact point and not during the Traveller Gateway cinematic itself -- the Gateway already has its own complete, bespoke sound design (the Gate video's own track, Lumo's real recorded voice, `gatewayAudio.js`'s own click sound), so starting the Foundation ambience only once the Gateway has handed off and the Hall is actually reached avoids stacking a third, competing sound layer underneath it. `js/themeEngine.js`'s `applyTheme()` and `applyArtworkTheme()` each gained one small, identically-shaped hook, reading a resolved Theme's own optional `audio.ambience` array (e.g. `{"audio":{"ambience":["forest.mp3"]}}`, resolved against `assets/audio/worlds/` for a bare filename, or used as-is for an already-qualified path/URL -- mirroring, in spirit but not by direct call, `ThemeRegistry.resolveAssetRef()`'s own dual-mode image/font resolution, which is scoped to a compiled Theme package's own embedded assets map and doesn't apply to V1's fixed, non-package ambience location) and calling `AudioManager.playWorld([...])` when present or `AudioManager.stopWorld()` when absent -- absent by default for every existing Theme, zero behaviour change for anything that doesn't declare this field. New `assets/audio/foundation/README.md`/`assets/audio/worlds/README.md`/`assets/audio/ui/README.md` (mirroring `assets/audio/gateway/README.md`'s own established tone/structure) disclose the folder layout and, honestly, that the five real Foundation files don't exist on disk yet -- `js/audioManager.js` degrades gracefully in their absence (a missing-file `Audio()` element simply never produces sound; it neither throws nor blocks boot), exactly matching this codebase's own established graceful-degradation precedent (Story Egg's still-missing `hero.png`, Nimbus/Quill's still-missing poses). `assets/audio/ui/` is reserved, empty, and explicitly out of V1 scope (Interactive Stings, named as future work in the Vision doc, not built here). No Theme Contract/Engine V2 Scene Model/Builder/Creator Governing Rules change; `tools/world-builder/`/`tools/world-builder-v2/` untouched; confined to a new `js/audioManager.js`, `index.html`, `js/app.js`, `js/themeEngine.js`, three new asset-folder READMEs, and this correction to `docs/ATMOSPHERE_V1_BLUEPRINT.md`'s own earlier single-track assumption.)

- Creator Signature — "Which Sky Is Yours?" Recognition Challenge Replaces the Star-Tap-Grid for the Known-Card Case (a real design/product correction, worked through iteratively rather than shipped on the first idea: "lets fix this screen . its not kids friendly" (the original 10x10 star-tap-grid "Creator Signature" challenge) led first to a rejected 3-concept mockup round, then to a recognition-vs-recall pivot the user explicitly chose ("i like the second idea") — tap your own companion out of a lineup instead of recalling an abstract secret tap sequence — and finally to the user's own sharp correction once that was mocked up: "why we are asking to confirm companion. should we not be asking to confirm the stars?" Investigated rather than guessed at: confirming a companion is a genuinely weaker test than the real thing, since a companion's identity is visible elsewhere (nickname greetings, published stories, Object Strip) and isn't actually secret; but the real secret pattern (`card.pattern`) can't be shown here either, per the already-shipped, deliberate "Decorative Sky vs. Recall Credential" rule ("the pattern is never to be shown, not even the decorative stand-in") — which is exactly why this same screen already replaced star-shaped graphics with a companion portrait glyph in an earlier sprint. The resolution, confirmed with the user via `AskUserQuestion`: recognize the card's own **decorative sky** (`MagicCard.decorativeSkyFor(card)`, the same safe, non-secret, id-derived shape already used for the header badge — never `card.pattern`) among a small set of fixed "mystery sky" decoys, keeping the astronomy/constellation theming intact while never risking the real secret. Two further rounds of user feedback shaped the final mechanic: "lets not just reorder, regenerate the 2 fakes also" (a wrong tap must swap in genuinely new decoy shapes, not just reposition the same ones) and "total cards needs to be 4. 1 real 3 fakes. at every wrong attempt all cards reorganise and 2 fakes regenerate" (settling on 4 cards — 1 real + 3 mystery — with exactly 2 of the 3 decoys replaced and 1 carried over unchanged on every miss, so the board is never a full reset, just fresh enough to prevent memorizing positions) — plus "instead of lumo being a sigil, we have different poses of him... in communication with the panel," landing on Lumo's real, already-shipped pose art (curious/think/wave/celebrate) swapping live as the moment changes, reusing the existing `.magic-card-gatekeeper-*` ring/float/landing-shadow/bubble presentation rather than a flat static portrait. **Implementation**: new `js/magicCardUI.js` functions `_buildSkyGatekeeperHeader()` (resolves Lumo's full companion package once via the existing `_ceremonyResolveEntity(regList,{role:'guardian'})`/`CEREMONY_ASSETS_BASE` machinery already built for the Creator Ceremony, then exposes a live `setMood(pose,speechText,moodClass)` to swap the portrait image and retype the bubble line without re-fetching) and `_renderSkyChallenge(panel,opts)` (renders 4 cards — the real decorative sky plus 3 decoys drawn from a small, fixed `SKY_DECOY_PATTERNS` pool of 6 shapes never derived from any real card — via the identical `_renderConstellation()` SVG rendering `_renderConstellation` already draws elsewhere, deliberately with **zero visual distinction** between the real card and decoys, since a decoy that looked different in any way would defeat the whole recognition test by letting a shoulder-surfer "just pick the one that looks different"; a wrong tap shakes that card, decrements one of 3 tries, and — after a beat — regenerates exactly 2 of the 3 decoys from the pool while the 3rd persists unchanged, reshuffling all 4 positions; exhausting all 3 tries calls `onBack()` automatically, same as the manual "← Back" button). Rewired the three "this device already knows which card it is, just confirm it's really them" call sites — `beginCreatorSignature` (the Traveller Gateway's own Returning-Creator path), `_renderGateWelcome`'s "Return to My Adventure" button, and `_renderGatePicker`'s per-tile tap — from the old `_renderPatternChallenge(panel,{verify:...})` (comparing a tapped pattern against `card.pattern` via a local `_patternsMatch()` helper) to the new `_renderSkyChallenge(panel,{card,onSuccess,onBack})`. **The cross-device Recall flow ("Recall a different card," verified against the real secret pattern via the `recall_magic_card()` RPC, since there is no local card yet for a decorative sky to be derived from in that case) is deliberately untouched** and still uses `_renderPatternChallenge` — the old 10x10 tap-grid — unchanged; `_patternsMatch()`, left with zero remaining callers once all three known-card sites were rewired, was deleted as genuine dead code rather than left orphaned. **A real, previously-latent bug found and fixed while building this, not merely worked around**: `_typewriterReveal(el,text)` had no way to cancel a still-running reveal before starting a new one — harmless for every prior caller (each only ever typed one line per element, once), but `_renderSkyChallenge` is the first caller to invoke `setMood()`/`_typewriterReveal` on the *same* bubble line repeatedly as Lumo's mood changes across several states, and a second call before the first's `setInterval` finished left both timers racing to overwrite the same `textContent` concurrently — confirmed directly via a failing Playwright assertion (the "oops" message reading as a corrupted tail of the *first* line) before being traced to its root cause and fixed by stashing the interval handle on the element itself (`el.__typewriterTimer`) and clearing any previous one before starting a new reveal. New CSS (`.magic-card-sky-tries`/`-grid`/`-card` plus `.tapped-wrong`/`.correct`/`.fade` states, reusing the exact `.magic-card-constellation-svg`/`.magic-card-star*` rendering and `--mc-*` palette everywhere else in this file already does) added to `css/style.css` right after the existing Gatekeeper CSS block. Verified end-to-end via two Playwright suites (scratch-only, this sandbox has no persisted historical test scripts from earlier sessions to re-run, so risk-targeted new coverage was written instead): the single-card "Return to My Adventure" flow (4 cards shown, real sky correctly identified via a live `MagicCard.decorativeSkyFor()` call rather than assumed, a wrong tap shakes+decrements tries+regenerates exactly 1-persisted/2-new decoys with all 4 positions reshuffled, a correct tap glows+fades the rest+calls `onSuccess`); the multi-card Picker's per-tile flow (tapping the *second* card's tile correctly identifies and activates that specific card, not the first); `beginCreatorSignature`'s `skipSpeech` (the initial line stays empty, matching the Gateway's own already-spoken greeting) and its full exhaust-3-tries → automatic choice screen → "Try Again" → fresh 3-tries reset → success loop; and a direct confirmation that "Recall a different card" still renders the real, unmodified 100-cell tap-grid with its typed-code fallback and zero `.magic-card-sky-card` elements anywhere in that flow. Zero console errors beyond the same 4 pre-existing, already-disclosed, unrelated conditions this codebase's history already names (Story Egg's own still-pending `hero.png`/`magic.png`/no-`personality.json` art gap, and this sandbox's standing Supabase-network-blocked limitation). No Theme Contract/Engine V2 Scene Model/Builder/Creator Governing Rules change; confined to `js/magicCardUI.js` and `css/style.css`, with a matching cache-bust version bump on both stylesheet `<link>` tags in `index.html`.)

- Creator Signature Sky Challenge — No Wasted Space on an Empty Bubble, and the Prompt Line Is Never Silent (two real, same-day follow-ups on the sky-recognition challenge above, both from a live screenshot: "no scroll please. there is so much vertical space use that." Traced to `beginCreatorSignature`'s own `skipSpeech:true` flag (added so the challenge's initial line stayed blank, deferring to the Traveller Gateway's own prior spoken greeting) — the empty bubble still rendered its full padded box with nothing in it, wasting real vertical space and, on a short viewport, forcing an unnecessary scrollbar. Fixed by hiding the bubble entirely (`bubble.classList.add('magic-card-gatekeeper-bubble-empty')`, a new `display:none` CSS rule) whenever `_buildSkyGatekeeperHeader`'s `setMood()` is called with no speech text, rather than rendering an empty box — verified via a scroll-measurement Playwright test across 5 viewport heights (560-900px) that the bubble genuinely renders `display:'none'` in that state. **Immediately corrected by the user, before this alone shipped**: "we still need a text line asking creator to find his stars" — hiding the bubble was the wrong fix for `beginCreatorSignature` specifically, since a child arriving at this exact screen still needs to be told what to do, and the Gateway's own earlier greeting is a different screen entirely, not a substitute for this one's own instruction. Reversed the `skipSpeech` suppression outright: `beginCreatorSignature` now always shows the real prompt, "One of these skies is yours. Can you find it?", identical to what `_renderGateWelcome`/`_renderGatePicker` already showed — all three known-card entry points now behave identically, with zero special-cased silent state anywhere. The bubble-hiding CSS/logic from the first fix is kept (harmless, unreachable dead code for any future caller that might legitimately pass empty text, not removed since it caused no regression and cost nothing to leave). Verified via a fresh Playwright pass: the prompt line renders and fully types out on `beginCreatorSignature` (previously blank); re-measured scroll overflow with the real text restored — genuinely overflows below ~700px viewport height (the same, pre-existing `overflow-y:auto` safety-net behaviour the sibling Welcome/Picker flows already had all along, now simply shared uniformly across all three entry points rather than a regression introduced here) and fits cleanly at 800px+. One test assertion in the existing regression suite, written against the old `skipSpeech`-produces-a-blank-line behaviour, was updated to check for the corrected always-shown-prompt behaviour instead — the disclosed, intended consequence of this fix, not a stale check papered over. Full regression across both existing sky-challenge Playwright suites (single/multi-card flows, exhaust-3-tries choice screen, decoy regenerate mechanic, the untouched cross-device Recall flow) passes unchanged, zero new console errors beyond the same pre-existing, disclosed conditions (Story Egg's own pending art gap, the sandbox's standing Supabase-network-block). No Theme Contract/Engine V2 Scene Model/Builder/Creator Governing Rules change; confined to `js/magicCardUI.js` and `css/style.css`.)

- Creator Signature Sky Challenge — Measured, Not Guessed: a Real Fit Function Replaces clamp()-Only Sizing (a direct, same-day follow-up: a fresh screenshot showed the sky-recognition challenge still scrolling even after the previous entry's fix. Root-caused, not patched blind: `_renderSkyChallenge`'s layout relied entirely on CSS `clamp()` values sized against viewport height — reasonable-looking in isolation, but nothing was ever measuring the ACTUAL rendered result against the panel's real available room, unlike the sibling star-tap-grid screen (`_renderPatternChallenge`), which has always used a real measure-and-shrink function, `_fitBoardToAvailableSpace`. Confirmed directly via Playwright at a range of realistic desktop-window heights (500-720px) that the sky challenge genuinely overflowed at several of them even though the tap-grid screen right next to it, using the exact same panel, didn't. **Fix**: a new `_fitSkyChallengeToAvailableSpace(panel,gatekeeperEl,gridEl)`, mirroring `_fitBoardToAvailableSpace`'s own established discipline, runs in up to three escalating steps, each taken only if the previous one still isn't enough: (1) shrink Lumo's own portrait (the `--gk-size` custom property) — the single largest element; (2) shrink the sky-card grid itself; (3) compress every remaining fixed margin/padding on the screen too, via a new `--sky-density` CSS custom property that `css/style.css`'s own `calc(var(--sky-density,1) * Npx)` expressions reference on the gatekeeper's margin, the speech bubble's padding, the tries row/label's margins, and the sky-grid's gap/margin/card-padding — density is solved analytically (one extra measurement at `--sky-density:0.5`, since scrollHeight is linear in density, lets the exact value that closes the remaining gap be computed directly rather than guessed via discrete steps) and clamped to a floor of 0.3 so text/spacing never collapses to nothing. Wired into `_renderSkyChallenge` at the same three points `_fitBoardToAvailableSpace` is wired at on its own screen: once synchronously right after the initial paint, again after every decoy-regenerate repaint (bubble text length changes there too), and via a self-disconnecting `ResizeObserver` for any later window resize — idempotent throughout (always resets every override before re-measuring), so it's safe to call repeatedly with no oscillation risk. Verified via a new Playwright sweep across 10 realistic sizes (420×500 through 1920×1080, including 800×567 matching the reported screenshot's own aspect): every single one now renders with zero overflow, versus real, measured overflow at several of the same sizes before the fix; a further extreme-size check (down to 320×380, smaller than any real device) confirms the fit function correctly bottoms out at its density floor and gracefully falls back to the panel's own pre-existing `overflow-y:auto` safety net rather than breaking, matching the same disclosed floor-behaviour precedent the tap-grid's own fit function already established. Full regression across both existing sky-challenge Playwright suites (single/multi-card flows, exhaust-3-tries choice screen, decoy regenerate mechanic, "find your stars" prompt, the untouched cross-device Recall flow) passes unchanged, zero new console errors beyond the same pre-existing, disclosed conditions (Story Egg's own pending art gap, the sandbox's standing Supabase-network-block). No Theme Contract/Engine V2 Scene Model/Builder/Creator Governing Rules change; confined to `js/magicCardUI.js` and `css/style.css`.)

- Atmosphere Ambience Threaded Through Every Screen + Real Preload Gate + LumoVoice Load-Lag Fix (a direct request — "also play the ambience system throughout the studio. it should be threaded through all the screens irrespective where we are" — investigated before assuming a gap: `js/audioManager.js`'s Foundation layers already start on the very first click anywhere in the app (a document-level capture-phase unlock listener) and loop forever with nothing ever pausing them, so once ambience starts it genuinely never stops across Screen 1/2/Workspace/Publish/Magic Card. The one real gap was `AudioManager.init()` living inside `_beginBoot()` — only reached AFTER the Traveller Gateway's entire cinematic hands off — so the Gateway itself (Sky/Lumo/Gates/Journey/Threshold, and specifically its own "Welcome home"/"Show me your stars" Returning-Creator recognition screen) played with zero ambience. The user then confirmed this exact screen with a concrete report: *"the first screen which says welcome home, show me your stars does not have ambience. also the welcome home and show me your stars audio does not play always. may be its initialization and load time lag."* **Fix 1 — ambience now threads through the Gateway too**: `AudioManager.init()` moved out of `_beginBoot()` to the very top of `js/app.js`'s boot sequence (now wrapped in the new preload gate below), so the unlock listener is armed and the Foundation layers begin buffering before the Gateway's first frame ever paints — a real user gesture anywhere, including inside the Gateway's own tap-to-continue interactions, now starts ambience immediately, mixed at its own already-quiet levels underneath the Gateway's dedicated video/voice track. **Fix 2 — the real load-lag bug in `js/lumoVoice.js`**: every one of Lumo's ~17 recorded voice lines was created lazily, on the exact call that plays it, with `.play()`'s rejection silently swallowed (`.catch(function(){})`) and zero retry — a genuine race between the fetch/decode and the scripted moment the Gateway calls `LumoVoice.play()`/`playSequence()`, exactly matching the user's own diagnosis. Fixed at the root: `_audioFor()` now sets `preload='auto'` explicitly; a new `preload(ids)` (called with no argument primes the whole ~1.3MB/17-clip set) lets a caller prime clips well ahead of the moment they're actually needed; a new `_playWithRetry()` replaces the old silent give-up — if `.play()` rejects because the element genuinely wasn't ready yet (`readyState<2`), it waits for the real `canplay` event and tries exactly once more instead of losing the line outright; `playSequence()`'s own chained-`next()` logic was updated to match, so a still-stuck clip after the retry moves the sequence along rather than stalling it forever. **Fix 3 — a genuine preload gate, not just background priming**: immediately following the ambience-threading fix, the user asked directly for something further: *"may be we need a preload sequence. something which can hold the screens till everything is loaded and ready."* A new `.preload-gate` overlay (`css/style.css`, `z-index:9999` — above the Magic Card overlay's 1400, the companion widget's 1450, even the restore-session modal's 2000, since it must cover literally the whole page while it's up) now shows the instant boot begins, before the Gateway or anything else renders, while `js/app.js`'s new `bootWithPreloadGate()` calls `AudioManager.init()`+`AudioManager.whenFoundationReady(4000)` and `LumoVoice.preload()`+`LumoVoice.whenReady(null,4000)` (two new, symmetric readiness-signal functions added to each module, resolving once every element reaches `readyState>=3`/fires `canplaythrough`, racing a 4-second-per-module bound) — only once both settle (or a 5-second overall safety timeout elapses, so a slow/broken connection can never hang boot forever) does the gate fade out and `_runBootstrap()` (the Gateway-or-fallback boot sequence, renamed from the old bare `bootstrapSession` IIFE) actually run.
