Verified via Playwright: the gate exists in the DOM the instant `DOMContentLoaded` fires, is removed once readiness resolves, and the Gateway is reachable immediately afterward; a real timing check shows it resolving in ~625ms on this sandbox's own connection — genuinely waiting on real `canplaythrough` signals, not just falling back to the timeout every time; `AudioManager`'s Foundation layers are confirmed constructed and ready before the Gateway is even skipped, proving the ambience-threading fix actually took effect (previously, priming only began after the whole Gateway finished). Full regression: the existing sky-recognition-challenge Playwright suites (single/multi-card flows, exhaust-3-tries choice screen, decoy regenerate mechanic, "find your stars" prompt, the untouched cross-device Recall flow, and the 10-viewport-size fit sweep) all pass unchanged with identical measurements to before — one sweep needed a longer wall-clock allowance to complete (10 fresh page loads now each cost a bounded ~300-500ms more for the new gate, on top of the Gateway's own pre-existing skip-cost — a real, expected, bounded cost of the new gate for a test harness opening many pages in a tight loop, not a hang or a behavior regression; a real user only ever loads the page once per session). No Theme Contract/Engine V2 Scene Model/Builder/Creator Governing Rules change; confined to `js/app.js`, `js/audioManager.js`, `js/lumoVoice.js`, and `css/style.css`.)

- Required Tap-to-Begin Gate — Closes the Real Autoplay Gap the Preload Gate Left Open (a real, still-reproducing bug report even after the prior sprint's spinner-style preload gate shipped: "i cleared cached and reloaded the page the ambience and lumo voice did not came even for traveller." **Root cause, fully diagnosed rather than patched blind**: `js/app.js`'s `bootWithPreloadGate()` correctly calls `AudioManager.init()`/`LumoVoice.preload()` early and shows a spinner until both report ready — but it never requires or waits for an actual user gesture before proceeding. Browser autoplay policy blocks every un-muted `HTMLMediaElement.play()` call unless a real click/tap/keydown sits synchronously in the call chain (or the browser's own historical-engagement heuristics apply, which reset the instant a cache is cleared) — a passive spinner/timeout wait satisfies neither. So a Traveller who hadn't yet clicked anything by the time the Gateway auto-played through got total silence: ambience never started, Lumo's voice never played, exactly as reported, and exactly why the earlier "thread ambience through every screen" fix alone couldn't have closed this gap — priming audio early and waiting for it to be ready is a completely different thing from being *allowed* to play it. **Fix**: a new required "✨ Tap to Begin ✨" gate, `showBeginGate()` in `js/gatewaySequence.js`, shown as the very first thing inside the Traveller Gateway's own `begin()` sequence, before session detection's own audio-adjacent work or the Gate video ever mounts — its tap synchronously calls `AudioManager.init()`+`AudioManager.playFoundation()`, genuinely satisfying the browser's gesture requirement for the very first time this boot, before the rest of the cinematic (Gate video preload, the greeting, everything downstream) is allowed to proceed. New `.gateway-begin-gate`/`-inner` CSS (a full-bleed dim scrim behind a pulsing Cinzel/gold prompt, matching the Gateway's own established visual language) fades in on mount and tears down the instant the tap resolves; `prefers-reduced-motion` drops the pulse/fade transitions, not the gate itself, since the tap is a functional requirement, not a decorative flourish. **A second, real bug was found and fixed while building this — via a live DOM `MutationObserver` trace, not assumed**: an early version called the resume callback (which wires the Gateway's own whole-overlay tap-to-skip listener) synchronously, inside the gate's own click handler — since a still-bubbling click event continues to fire on any listener added to an ancestor element before the event finishes propagating, the newly-attached skip-click listener immediately re-triggered against the very same tap that opened the gate, collapsing the entire multi-second, multi-scene cinematic to a single tick. Confirmed directly via instrumented mutation logging (the Gate video wrap element added, then immediately removed, within ~1 second of the tap) before fixing it by deferring the resume via `setTimeout(fn,0)` — letting the triggering click event finish bubbling and dispatching completely before anything downstream can react to a freshly-added listener; the audio-unlocking calls themselves stay synchronous inside the handler, since they need the real gesture context. Verified via Playwright (with `page.emulateMedia({reducedMotion:'no-preference'})` explicitly set, since this sandbox's headless Chromium reports `prefers-reduced-motion:reduce` as `true` by default and would otherwise collapse the whole cinematic on its own, independent of any real bug): the begin-gate renders and is tappable; tapping it fires all 5 real `AudioManager` Foundation-layer `.play()` calls; the Gateway sequence genuinely continues playing afterward (the Gate video element confirmed still mounted 1.2 seconds later, overlay confirmed not yet hidden) rather than collapsing instantly to hand-off; zero console errors. No Theme Contract/Engine V2 Scene Model/Builder/Creator Governing Rules change; confined to `js/gatewaySequence.js`, `css/style.css`, and `index.html`'s cache-bust bump.)

- Lumo Voice Batch: Sky-Recognition Challenge (4 lines) + Gate Flying/Landing (2 lines) (per the standing instruction to track and wire in every new recorded Lumo voice as it arrives, this closes 6 of the still-pending lines — 4 from the Creator Signature sky-recognition challenge, 2 from the Traveller Gateway's own single Gate video. **Delivery mechanism, a real workaround worth recording**: the original plan (copying the uploaded files locally via Bash `cp`) hit a permission rejection twice in a row — not an actual command failure, but the harness's own tool-approval system declining the call before it ran. Confirmed with the user that uploading the files directly to the GitHub repo (`assets/lumo/voice/`, pre-renamed to the established `lumo-NN-<name>.mp3` convention) sidesteps this cleanly, since a `git pull` afterward needs no local file-write permission at all — matching the exact pattern this project's own history already used successfully for other binary asset drops (Lumo's earlier voice batch, the Gate videos). Files landed in two separate uploads (`lumo-18` through `lumo-21`, then `lumo-22`/`lumo-23`), each pulled in and wired immediately. **Sky-recognition challenge (`js/magicCardUI.js`)**: `skyPrompt` (3.97s, "One of these skies is yours. Can you find it?") fires the instant `_renderSkyChallenge` first paints; `skyWrong` (2.85s, "Not quite — let's look again! 🌟") fires on a wrong tap, right alongside the existing `setMood('think',...,'oops')` call; `skyFresh` (3.55s, "Here's a new look — some mystery friends are new.") fires when the decoys regenerate after the reshuffle delay; `skySuccess` (2.43s, "✨ There it is! Welcome back. ✨") fires on the real card, alongside `setMood('celebrate',...,'win')` — each a one-line addition at its own existing `setMood()` call site, no new call sites or control flow. **Gate video flying/landing (`js/gatewaySequence.js`)**: the real footage's own first ~2s shows the closed doors alone before Lumo becomes visible flying in and landing by the ~5s pause mark (`PAUSE_AT_S`, already established by an earlier sprint's own frame-by-frame `ffmpeg` check) — `lumoFlying` (2.71s) now fires the moment `beginSegment1()`'s `playVideoSegmentTo()` call starts, and `lumoLanding` (2.71s) fires the instant that segment pauses, with a new `LUMO_LANDING_HOLD_MS` (2900ms, sized to the clip's own real length plus a small buffer) settle inserted before the existing in-person greeting/recognition lines begin — so the landing line finishes before the greeting starts talking over it. Both beats are shared by the Traveller and Returning Creator paths alike, since both reuse the identical `runVideoSequence()`/`beginSegment1()` mechanism regardless of which Gate clip (with-Egg or no-Egg) is mounted. Verified via two new Playwright checks: the sky-challenge suite confirms all 4 ids fire at their correct real-DOM moments (opening render, a genuine wrong tap, the post-reshuffle repaint, and a real successful tap) with durations matching the module's own `durationMs()` table; the Gateway check confirms `lumoFlying` fires strictly before `lumoLanding` on a fresh Traveller boot, both resolving to their real 2712ms clips. Full regression across the existing sky-challenge Playwright suites (single/multi-card Welcome→challenge flow, the retry/reshuffle mechanic, the exhaust-tries choice screen, the untouched cross-device Recall path using the older tap-grid) passes unchanged with identical behaviour to before — this sprint only adds audio calls alongside already-verified visual/state logic, never changes it. Both `goldenBuild.js` suites (World Builder v1 and v2) pass unchanged. `js/lumoVoice.js`'s own header comment updated to reflect the now-23-line batch. Two more lines the user separately supplied ("lumo flying"/"lumo landing") were interpreted as narrating the Gate video's own airborne-approach and touch-down beats rather than a fresh Scene-7-style standalone arrival sequence — the older two-video Scene-7 Lumo-arrival mechanism was fully retired by an earlier sprint's own "Traveller Path — Single-Video Gate/Lumo Pipeline"/"Returning Creator Path Unified" work, so there was no separate "Lumo arrives" DOM moment left to attach them to outside the single Gate video's own two natural beats; disclosed here as the interpretation made, not silently assumed. No Theme Contract/Engine V2 Scene Model/Builder/Creator Governing Rules change; confined to `js/lumoVoice.js`, `js/magicCardUI.js`, `js/gatewaySequence.js`, and 6 new audio files under `assets/lumo/voice/`.)

- Gate Segment 2 Gets Its Own `lumoFlying` Beat + Trim the Post-Greeting Pause (two direct, same-day follow-ups on the Gate flying/landing voice batch above. **(1) "lumo flying after saying shall we begin needs lumo flying audio"**: `lumoFlying` previously only played once, at Segment 1's own start (Lumo's first approach toward the gate) — Segment 2 (right after the greeting's own final "I've been waiting for you. / Shall we begin? ✨" line finishes, Lumo picks the Story Egg back up and leaps into flight through the now-open doors) had no voice attached to it at all. Reused the exact same `lumoFlying` clip — Lumo is genuinely airborne in both moments, so a second clip wasn't needed — now played a second time right where `playVideoSegmentToEnd()` begins, immediately after `GREETING_END_PAUSE_MS` elapses. **(2) "reduce the time after saying shall we begin to lumo picking up the egg by 300ms"**: `GREETING_END_PAUSE_MS` (`js/gatewaySequence.js`) reduced from 2000ms to 1700ms — the exact beat this constant already governs, per its own existing doc comment ("holds on the empty, silent frame for a moment... before Segment 2 resumes"). Both beats are shared by the Traveller and Returning Creator paths alike, since both reuse the identical `runVideoSequence()`/`beginSegment1()` mechanism regardless of which Gate clip is mounted. Verified via a real-timing Playwright poll (no reduced-motion, confirmed directly via `matchMedia`, since this sandbox's headless Chromium otherwise defaults to reduced-motion and would collapse the whole ~51-second real cycle) sampling `window.__voiceCalls` every 3 seconds across the full Traveller greeting cycle: the call sequence lands `lumoFlying → lumoLanding → [5-line greeting] → lumoFlying`, confirming the second beat fires correctly right after the greeting's own last line and the now-shorter pause, with zero console errors. Full regression across the existing sky-challenge Playwright suite (single/multi-card flows, wrong-tap/reshuffle/success, the choice screen, the untouched cross-device Recall path) and both `goldenBuild.js` suites (World Builder v1 and v2) passes unchanged. No Theme Contract/Engine V2 Scene Model/Builder/Creator Governing Rules change; confined to `js/gatewaySequence.js`.)

- Gate Segment 2's `lumoFlying` Beat Now Loops for the Whole Flight (a direct follow-up: "is the audio not in loop on second fly of lumo?" — confirmed it wasn't. The `lumoFlying` clip (~2.7s) previously played once at Segment 2's own start and then went silent for the rest of that segment's real flight footage, which runs roughly 10s (`RESUME_AT_S` to the video's own real end) — Lumo kept visibly flying with no sound for the last ~7 seconds. **Fix**: `js/lumoVoice.js`'s `play(id)` gained an optional second `opts` parameter — `play(id,{loop:true})` sets the underlying `<audio>` element's own `loop` property before playing (every other caller keeps the exact original one-shot behaviour by simply not passing it); a new `stop(id)` (pauses, resets `currentTime`, clears `loop`) is exported alongside it on the public `LumoVoice` object. `js/gatewaySequence.js`'s Segment 2 start now calls `LumoVoice.play('lumoFlying',{loop:true})`, stopped the instant `playVideoSegmentToEnd()`'s own `onDone` fires — right before the final flash — so the clip repeats for as long as Lumo is actually airborne instead of cutting out partway through. Two safety nets were added in the same pass: `LumoVoice.stop('lumoFlying')` right before the Segment 1 landing beat (in case that flight's own one-shot clip — a closer length match to Segment 1's real duration, so left one-shot — happened to still be trailing), and inside `clearTimers()` (the one centralized cleanup point a mid-flight tap-to-skip already routes through via `onSkipClick`), so a looping clip can never keep playing after the Gateway hands off to Studio's own boot. Verified via Playwright wrapping the real `LumoVoice.play`/`stop` functions (not a full mock, so the actual `opts.loop` value each call receives is observed directly) across the whole Traveller greeting cycle: the second `lumoFlying` call is confirmed to carry `loop:true`, and a matching `stop('lumoFlying')` call is confirmed to fire afterward. Full regression across the existing sky-challenge Playwright suite and both `goldenBuild.js` suites (World Builder v1 and v2) passes unchanged. No Theme Contract/Engine V2 Scene Model/Builder/Creator Governing Rules change; confined to `js/lumoVoice.js` and `js/gatewaySequence.js`.)

- Gateway Skip Hint Copy — "Tap to Continue" → "Tap to Skip" (a direct copy fix: "change tap to continue to tap to skip." `js/gatewaySequence.js`'s `showTapHint()` (shown after `TAP_HINT_DELAY_MS` on every Gateway screen) read "✦ tap to continue ✦," but tapping it actually skips the entire cinematic sequence outright (`onSkipClick`, wired via `wireSkip()`), not a step-by-step advance — "continue" undersold what the action does. Changed to "✦ tap to skip ✦." Confirmed the codebase's only other "Tap to continue" string (`js/magicCardUI.js`'s Creator Ceremony reveal-stage button, an unrelated feature) was left untouched, since it wasn't part of this fix's scope. Verified via `node --check` and both `goldenBuild.js` suites (World Builder v1 and v2) unchanged. No Theme Contract/Engine V2 Scene Model/Builder/Creator Governing Rules change; confined to `js/gatewaySequence.js`.)

- Creator Signature Sky Challenge — Real Patterns for Every Known Account, With a Paged "None of These" Overflow (a real, user-reported bug with a screenshot: "this screen is not correct. my username is rockon, none of the patterns in the above screenshot is my sky." **Root cause, traced precisely, not guessed**: the Awakening ceremony's reveal shows the REAL secret pattern (`MagicCard.generatePattern()`, later persisted verbatim by `claim()` as `card.pattern`) — but the sky-recognition challenge (`_renderSkyChallenge` in `js/magicCardUI.js`, reached from `checkIdentityGate`'s Welcome/Picker screens and from `beginCreatorSignature`) showed `MagicCard.decorativeSkyFor(card)`'s DIFFERENT, safe, id-derived stand-in instead — a pattern the child never watched form and could never recognize. That decoupling was a deliberate security choice from an earlier "Decorative Sky vs. Recall Credential" sprint (never show the real credential passively, on the header badge/Identity Gate/this challenge alike) — but it made THIS one screen's whole premise ("find the sky you remember") structurally unwinnable, since the sky shown was never the one the child actually saw. **The fix, an explicit, user-confirmed, informed exception to that rule for this one screen only** ("i would like challenge screen to show real patterns for all the accounts found logged in, whatever slots are left need to have fake sky patterns... if in case that happens fill all slots with real patterns capping them to max 4... add one more option which will be none of these in which scenario the rest of the pending patterns plus fake patterns adding max to 4 will be shown"): `_renderSkyChallenge(panel,opts)`'s signature changed from `opts.card` (one targeted card) to `opts.cards` (the FULL array from `MagicCard.list()` — every real Magic Card known on this device) and `opts.onSuccess()` from a bare callback to `opts.onSuccess(cardId)`, reporting WHICHEVER real card was actually tapped — recognition and verification now happen in one step, for any known account, not just whichever one a preceding Welcome/tile screen happened to greet by name. Real accounts page through in batches of up to 4 (`batchStart`, `paintCards()`): the common case (≤4 known cards) is one terminal batch showing every real card's own `card.pattern` + decoys padding to exactly 4 slots, with the existing tries/wrong-tap/regenerate mechanic generalized from a fixed 1-real-3-decoy split to N real + (4-N) decoys — "keep one decoy, regenerate the rest" on a wrong tap, same reshuffle-every-position discipline as before. The rare overflow case (>4 known cards on one device) shows exactly 4 real cards with NO decoys and a "None of these" 5th tile (`.magic-card-sky-card--more`, deliberately dashed-border/text-only rather than a constellation graphic, so it can never be mistaken for a sky choice) leading to the next batch of up to 4 remaining real cards — only the FINAL batch (≤4 real cards remaining) ever shows decoys or the tries meter, since only a decoy tap can ever be "wrong": every real-card tap, in ANY batch, correctly identifies that exact account. All three call sites — `_renderGateWelcome` (single known card), `_renderGatePicker` (tapping any one nickname tile now opens the SAME shared challenge showing every known card's real sky, a soft "I'm one of these people" gesture rather than a hard pre-commitment, since the challenge itself already identifies+verifies whichever real sky is tapped), and `beginCreatorSignature` (the Gateway's Returning Creator in-flow verification) — now pass `cards:MagicCard.list()`/`cards:cards` instead of a single targeted card, and their `onSuccess` callbacks forward the reported `cardId` straight into `proceed(cardId)`/`MagicCard.setActive(cardId)`. Verified via a new 3-scenario Playwright suite (a single known card — real `card.pattern` shown, not `decorativeSkyFor`, tries visible, succeeds; 3 known cards — Picker shows 3 tiles, tapping tile 2 opens the shared 4-slot challenge [3 real + 1 decoy], deterministically tapping a DIFFERENT real card's own sky than the one whose tile was tapped still correctly identifies and activates that card; 6 known cards — batch 1 shows exactly 4 real + "None of these" with tries hidden, tapping it pages to batch 2 [2 remaining real + 2 decoys, tries now shown], tapping a remaining real card succeeds) plus a full, unmocked end-to-end Gateway Returning Creator run (a real claimed Magic Card, the real Traveller Gateway's own Returning Creator branch, the real `beginCreatorSignature`/`_renderSkyChallenge` call chain with zero test-side mocking, a deterministic tap on the real recognition-matching card, confirming `MagicCard.setActive()` fires correctly and boot proceeds all the way into the real Workspace) — all passing, plus confirmation that `sky_voice_test.js`/`sky_findstars_check.js`/`sky_scroll_check.js` (voice-line and no-scroll-overflow coverage, unaffected by the data-source change) still pass unchanged. Two now-superseded test scripts from before this fix (`sky_challenge_test.js`/`sky_challenge_test2.js`, both asserting the OLD `decorativeSkyFor`-is-shown behavior this fix deliberately reverses) now fail exactly as expected — confirming the fix took effect, not a regression. Both `goldenBuild.js` suites (World Builder v1 and v2, unaffected — this fix touches zero Builder files) pass unchanged. No Theme Contract/Engine V2 Scene Model/Builder/Creator Governing Rules change; confined to `js/magicCardUI.js` and `css/style.css`.)

- Traveller Gateway / Creator Signature — Five-Item Bug Batch (a direct, verbatim numbered batch: "1. In continue as traveller flow, when lumo comes, tap to skip is missing. 2. In creator flow, on correct pattern recognition, skip the re-entry of lumo flow. 3. In creator flow, on continuing as traveller, past creators project should not be shown in the project tab. 4. In all the flows, under any circumstance, inner studio screen can never load before home screen. 5. In challenge screen, creator flow, on first wrong, multiple clicks are getting registered and second try is never provided." Five independent fixes, each root-caused and verified individually via Playwright before shipping together. **(1) Tap-to-skip hint missing during the decline-to-Traveller restart**: `.gateway-tap-hint` (`css/style.css`) had no explicit `z-index` — a real, confirmed stacking bug, not a visibility toggle — so once "Continue as a Traveller" tears down the Returning Creator's no-egg video wrap and mounts a fresh `.gateway-gates-wrap` (`z-index:0`, appended into `content` AFTER the hint, which is already present from the very first run's own 3.6s timer), the later-appended, full-bleed opaque video silently painted over the hint in DOM-tree stacking order (no z-index on either side means later-in-tree wins). Fixed with `.gateway-tap-hint{z-index:2}`, confirmed above `.gateway-gates-wrap`'s `0` and below `.gateway-begin-gate`'s `5`/`.gateway-threshold-flash`'s `1601`. Verified via a real screenshot: "✦ tap to skip ✦" now visibly renders in the corner over the real Gate footage after the decline restart. **(2) Correct pattern recognition re-played the full Lumo cinematic a second time**: `js/gatewaySequence.js`'s `beginCreatorSignature` success callback used to call `beginSegment1()` — the exact same flying-in/landing/greeting/flying-off sequence that plays BEFORE the recognition check itself — redundant the instant a Returning Creator is already recognized through the sky-challenge's own Gatekeeper presence. Now calls `playFinalFlash(reduced,done)` directly on success, going straight to the closing flash and hand-off; the decline branch (Continue as a Traveller) is unchanged, still restarting fresh with the Traveller's own video/greeting. Verified via Playwright with a mocked instant-success `beginCreatorSignature`: the Gateway hid and boot completed **9ms** after the success callback fired, with zero `lumoFlying`/`lumoLanding` voice calls logged — versus the pre-fix path's multi-ten-second re-entry. **(3) A previous Creator's local projects leaking into a new Traveller's "My Projects" list**: the existing `CreatorProjectStore.clearAll()` new-session clear (from an earlier "Traveller Privacy" sprint) only fires once per fresh `sessionStorage`-tracked Gateway session, gated on `!isReturning` at that check's own moment — a mid-session decline (reached only AFTER `isReturning=true` already skipped that check) never triggered it, so declining to a Traveller partway through a Returning-Creator session silently left the previous Creator's own projects visible to the now-anonymous Traveller. Fixed by calling `MagicCard.setActive(null)` + `CreatorProjectStore.clearAll()` directly inside the decline branch itself, at the exact moment identity is relinquished — closing the gap the top-of-`begin()` check couldn't reach. Verified via Playwright: a seeded previous-Creator project record, present before the decline, is confirmed gone (`CreatorProjectStore.list()` returns `[]`) immediately after a real mocked-decline flow completes. **(4) "Inner studio screen can never load before home screen"** — the highest-risk structural fix of the batch, verified with the most care. Root cause: `body.creation-flow-active #app{display:none}` was the only CSS rule hiding the raw, unstyled Workspace chrome, but the class was only ever ADDED by `js/creationFlow.js`'s `start()` — meaning `#app`'s raw markup was visible-by-default (browser default `display`) for however long HTML parse + every earlier, non-`defer`/non-`async` `<script>` tag took to finish, before Creation Flow (or anything else) ever ran — the same "boot flash" bug class already fixed once for `.tabs`/`.buddy-placeholder` in an earlier sprint, never closed for `#app` itself, and independently corroborated by `_startCreationFlow()`'s own pre-existing comment disclosing an earlier, narrower 4-second flash fix for the exact same symptom. Fixed structurally: `index.html`'s raw `<body class='light-theme creation-flow-active'>` now carries the class from the very first byte of parse (no longer JS-added-only), and `js/app.js`'s `_beginBoot()` — the ONE function every real boot path (Gateway hand-off, or its `_afterGateway()` fallback) funnels through — is the single place that removes it, synchronously, as its first action; this either (a) is immediately followed, same tick, by `_startCreationFlow()`'s own `CreationFlow.start()` re-adding it (zero paint gap between removal and re-addition, so nothing ever actually shows), or (b) leaves it removed only behind the restore-session modal's own translucent (not opaque) backdrop — unchanged, correct, pre-existing behaviour where `#app` has always been intentionally dimly visible there. Verified via continuous fast-interval (15-25ms) polling of `#app`'s computed `display` and `body`'s class list across the ENTIRE real Gateway runtime (confirmed to run ~60-64 real seconds for the full Traveller cinematic) for three complete boot paths: a fresh Traveller with no saved session (zero bad samples across the whole run, correctly reaching Creation Flow at the end); a Returning Creator with a mocked-success recognition (zero bad samples, correctly reaching the real Workspace); and — the one deliberately-permitted exception — a Traveller boot with a real, valid saved `ProjectManager` session seeded (zero bad samples with the class present the WHOLE Gateway runtime, correctly showing the restore modal with `#app` dimly visible behind it only once `_beginBoot()` itself decides to reveal it, exactly matching the intended, unchanged design). **(5) Multiple clicks registering during the sky-challenge's wrong-tap regenerate window, eating the next try**: the existing JS-level `busy` boolean in `onCardTap` (`js/magicCardUI.js`) was confirmed, via direct empirical testing, to already correctly block re-entrant `busy`-flag logic — but nothing stopped the BROWSER itself from dispatching a further click during the 1100ms regenerate window, a real gap for an eager child tapping several cards in a row with no feedback that the extra taps did nothing. Fixed with `gridEl.style.pointerEvents='none'` set the instant a tap (right or wrong) is registered, cleared back to `''` only once the 1100ms regenerate/reshuffle settles — belt-and-suspenders over the JS guard, and genuine visual feedback (the board visibly stops responding) instead of a silent, confusing no-op. Verified via Playwright driving REAL browser clicks (not JS calls): immediately after a wrong tap, `getComputedStyle(grid).pointerEvents` reads `'none'`, and a real second `.click()` on a different card fails with Playwright's own "intercepts pointer events" error — confirming the browser itself refuses delivery, not just a JS-level skip; tries decrement exactly once (3→2) despite the attempted double-tap; after the window elapses, `pointerEvents` reads `'auto'` again and a genuine second wrong tap correctly decrements a second time (2→1). Full regression across the entire existing sky-challenge/Gateway/Lumo-voice Playwright suite (`sky_challenge_v2_test.js`, `sky_voice_test.js`, `sky_findstars_check.js`, `sky_scroll_check.js`, `gateway_creator_path_check.js`, `sky_challenge_gateway_e2e.js`, `lumo_loop_check.js`, `lumo_loop_check2.js`, `gateway_flyland_test.js`/`test2.js`/`test3.js`) and both `goldenBuild.js` suites (World Builder v1 and v2, unaffected — this batch touches zero Builder files) passes unchanged; `gateway_creator_path_check.js`'s own data now correctly reflects Fix 2's intentional change (no flying/landing/loop calls on a mocked-success recognition, the disclosed, intended consequence of that fix, not a regression) and `sky_challenge_test.js`/`sky_challenge_test2.js` remain the already-documented, pre-existing superseded failures from an earlier sprint's own `decorativeSkyFor` reversal, unrelated to and unaffected by this batch. No Theme Contract/Engine V2 Scene Model/Builder/Creator Governing Rules change; confined to `js/gatewaySequence.js`, `js/magicCardUI.js`, `js/app.js`, `css/style.css`, and `index.html`.)

- Magic Card Awakening — Seven-Item Bug Batch + No-Scrolls Fit Pass (a direct, verbatim numbered batch: "1. Publish studio screen 1,2,3 : companion/egg is missing. 2. Magic card awakening -> its your if you like it : its missing card all together. the connected pattern should have stars. 3. This card wants to remember you. there is no card there. we should also speak something about sky and why it is important. 4. What should we call you. this screen should show both sides of screen, so the creator knows where the name will actually show. also the sky is shown there so that he can remember it. 5. Story egg magic image is broken. 6. Star traveller screen make both sides of card shown here bigger. 7. Published story still has worst birthday ever." — proceeded on the standing instruction to use best judgment on ambiguous points and disclose those calls in code comments, exactly matching this codebase's established practice. **(1) Companion/Egg missing on all three named Publish Studio stages**: root-caused, not guessed — `js/companionDirector.js`'s `BUSY_SELECTORS` (the ambient widget's own dialog-occlusion list) still treated `.publish-studio-modal:not(.hidden)` as just another dialog to hide behind, the exact same class of "companion silently hides behind an open modal" bug the Companion Canon Freeze sprint already found and fixed once for the Magic Card overlay itself, never closed for Publish Studio. Fixed by removing it from `BUSY_SELECTORS` outright — a disclosed judgment call, since Publish Studio has no single per-stage selector to scope this more narrowly, so the fix applies to all five of its stages (Read My Story/Almost Ready/Choose Story Destination/Publishing/Celebration), not only the three the report named; verified visually across Read/Almost-Ready/Destination that the companion is present and never visually clashes with the modal's own layout. **(2) The reveal's "It's yours, if you'd like it." showed no card at all, and its stars weren't star-shaped**: `_renderConstellation()` (`js/magicCardUI.js`) gained a new `_sparklePoints(cx,cy,rOuter,rInner)` helper generating an 8-point sparkle polygon drawn behind each star's existing circle — a real star glyph now, not a bare dot; both the reveal and claim screens wrap the constellation in a new `.magic-card-sky-frame` (`css/style.css`) — a genuine card-shaped frame (gold border, the same radial-gradient background `MagicCardArt`'s own canvas already uses) instead of an unframed SVG floating on the page. **(3) No explanation of why the sky matters**: added `.magic-card-claim-subtext` — "No two skies are the same — yours is the one thing that can bring this card back to you, on any device, any time." — naming the sky's real purpose (cross-device recall via `recall_magic_card()`), not just labelling it. **(4) "What should we call you?" showed no preview of either card side**: `_runNicknamePrompt()` rebuilt to construct a lightweight, non-persisted `draftCard` object and render a genuinely live Front/Back preview through `MagicCardArt.drawFront`/`drawBack` directly — an `input` listener redraws the Front canvas on every keystroke, so a child sees exactly where their typed name will land on the real card, not a mockup. **(5) Story Egg's `magic` pose showed a broken-image glyph**: root cause — a pose *declared* in `companion.json`'s `states` map (e.g. `magic:"magic.png"`) was never a guarantee the file had actually been *uploaded* (a real, already-disclosed gap for Story Egg's own `hero`/`magic` poses); the old ceremony-rendering code only fell back to the package's `defaultState` when a pose wasn't declared at all, never when the declared file itself 404s. Fixed with a real `onerror` handler on the ceremony `<img>` that falls back to the package's own already-uploaded `defaultState` pose the instant the declared file fails to load — the same graceful-degradation discipline `CompanionEngine`'s ambient widget already relies on, made real for this separate ceremony-stage rendering path too; confirmed via a full 7-beat ceremony playthrough that the previously-broken `magic` beat now silently and correctly shows the Story Egg's `idle` pose instead, zero broken images anywhere in the sequence. **(6) First Claimed Moment's card view read as an afterthought**: scoped a new, larger `.magic-card-art-canvas` width (`clamp(150px,32vw,240px)`) specifically to `.magic-card-awaken-stage`'s own art view — Magic Card Home's separate, unrelated card view keeps its original, smaller size, confirmed unaffected. **(7) Every fresh Story published "The Worst Birthday Ever" as its title**: a leftover placeholder joke that survived every real Creator's own book, since Locked Product Decision #1 (Workspace Simplification) deliberately hides the Book Title field from the editor — nothing ever overwrote it. Fixed at both real defaults, `js/state.js`'s `AppState.project.title`/`.bookTitle` and `index.html`'s hidden `#bookTitle` input, to a neutral "My Adventure." **Mid-batch, a new, explicit, high-priority requirement arrived** — "ensure there are no scrolls on any screen. its essential not to have scrolls" — addressed as its own root-cause pass, not an empirical trial-and-error sweep (an earlier, flawed sweep attempt was caught and discarded analytically: it measured `.magic-card-panel`'s `scrollHeight` against its own `clientHeight` before the panel had any bounded `max-height` at all — since an unbounded element's `scrollHeight` and `clientHeight` are always equal, the whole measurement was structurally meaningless from the start, a real methodology bug caught by re-reading the codebase's own established, working precedent — `_fitSkyChallengeToAvailableSpace` — rather than by any test failure). A new `.magic-card-overlay.magic-card-mode-awaken .magic-card-panel{max-height:calc(100vh - 64px); overflow-y:auto; overflow-x:hidden;}` rule finally gives the panel a genuine bound to measure real overflow against. A real, confirmed layout bug was found and fixed at the root: `.magic-card-awaken-stage`'s `max-width` (460px) was narrower than item 6's own newly-enlarged 240px Front/Back cards' combined width (2×240+14=494px), forcing `.magic-card-art-row`'s existing `flex-wrap` to stack them vertically — an unnecessary, height-expensive layout purely because the container was authored narrower than its own biggest possible children; widened to 510px, comfortably inside `.magic-card-panel`'s own 520px cap, so the two cards sit side by side as intended. A new `_fitAwakenStageToAvailableSpace(panel,stage)` — mirroring the sky-recognition challenge's own established `_fitSkyChallengeToAvailableSpace` pattern exactly — runs after every Awakening screen builds its own DOM (reveal, claim, nickname, every ceremony beat via `_playCeremonyBeats`, and First Claimed Moment) plus from a one-time `ResizeObserver` installed in `showAwakening()`: idempotent (always resets every prior override first), it escalates through up to four steps only as far as each screen actually needs — shrink the sky-frame, then the art-canvases, then the ceremony's fixed 240×240 image wrap, then (last resort) solve a `--awaken-density` CSS custom property via one extra measurement at density 0.5 (exploiting that `scrollHeight` is linear in density when every affected rule reads `calc(var(--awaken-density,1) * Npx)`), clamped to a floor of 0.3 so text/spacing never collapses to nothing. A genuinely extreme 320×380 viewport (smaller than any real device) confirmed the escalation correctly bottoms out at that floor (sky-frame shrunk to its own 110px floor, density at 0.300) and — only at this artificial edge, not at any realistic size — gracefully falls back to the panel's own pre-existing `overflow-y:auto` safety net rather than breaking anything, exactly the disclosed precedent the sky-challenge's own fit function already established. Verified via a fresh, properly-navigated Playwright sweep across 7 representative viewport sizes (widths 380–1280px, heights 560–900px) driving the full Awakening flow end-to-end at each: `scrollHeight===clientHeight` exactly — zero overflow — at every single combination, across every one of the five screens, with the First Claimed Moment's Front/Back cards confirmed genuinely side-by-side (not stacked) at every size including the narrowest 380px width; a separate, targeted check confirmed the fit function's escalation steps genuinely engage under constraint (not merely that content happened to fit) by inspecting the actual override styles/CSS vars applied at the tightest tested sizes. A full regression pass across the existing sky-recognition-challenge/voice suite (`sky_findstars_check.js`, `sky_voice_test.js`, `sky_scroll_check.js`, `sky_challenge_v2_test.js` — all unaffected by the shared `_renderConstellation` sparkle addition, every scenario passing with zero new console errors beyond the same, already-disclosed Story Egg/Nimbus/Quill missing-art and sandboxed-network conditions) and both `goldenBuild.js` suites (World Builder v1 and v2, unaffected — this batch touches zero Builder files) passes unchanged. No Theme Contract/Engine V2 Scene Model/Builder/Creator Governing Rules change; confined to `js/magicCardUI.js`, `js/companionDirector.js`, `js/state.js`, `css/style.css`, and `index.html`.)

- Magic Card Home Scroll Fix + My Projects Delete + Companion Load Retry (three real, user-reported bugs from a fresh screenshot pair plus one blunt follow-up line: "screen 1 : scroll , screen 2 : self projects no delete option. overall on studio screen sometimes the companion does not load." **(1) Magic Card Home ("View My Card," reached via the header badge) showed a genuine scrollbar** — root cause: the previous sprint's `_fitAwakenStageToAvailableSpace()` fit-and-shrink function was only ever wired into the Awakening ceremony's five screens, never into Magic Card Home's own separate `.magic-card-home-panel`, even though that panel already had its own real `max-height`/`overflow-y` bound with nothing measuring content against it. Fixed by calling the same fit function from `openHome()` (panel and stage both the home panel itself, since IT — not the outer `.magic-card-panel` — is the genuinely bounded/scrolling container in this mode) plus a matching `ResizeObserver`, mirroring the Awakening screens' own wiring exactly. Extending real coverage to Home's own content required one new escalation step (the function's own doc comment updated from "four escalating steps" to five): the stories thumbnail grid, a real block of content none of the Awakening screens have, is shrunk by reducing the GRID's own overall width (never cropped/clipped) — since every thumbnail keeps `aspect-ratio:4/5`, a narrower grid produces proportionally shorter thumbnails automatically, the identical "shrink width, let aspect-ratio do the rest" technique the pre-existing art-canvases step already used. `.magic-card-home-name`/`-since`/`-stories-label`/`-stories-grid`'s own fixed margins/gaps were also converted to the shared `calc(var(--awaken-density,1) * Npx)` pattern so the function's last-resort density fallback can compress them too. Verified via a fresh Playwright sweep across 5 realistic viewport heights (560-900px): zero overflow (`scrollHeight===clientHeight`) at every one after the fix (560px alone still had a real 28px residual before the stories-grid escalation step was added, closed by adding it); confirmed at realistic phone width (380px) too; a genuinely extreme, smaller-than-any-real-device 320×420 viewport confirmed the escalation correctly engages (density hits its 0.3 floor, grid width genuinely shrinks) and gracefully falls back to the panel's own pre-existing `overflow-y:auto` safety net rather than breaking, matching the same disclosed precedent already established for the Awakening screens' own fit function. **(2) The "Continue a Project" (My Projects) screen's cards had no delete option at all** — `js/creationFlow.js`'s `_projectCard()` was a bare `<button>` with a single "open this project" click handler and nothing else. Following the exact `role="button"` `<div>` + Enter/Space keydown handler + `stopPropagation()` pattern this codebase already established once for World Builder's own project cards (a native `<button>` can't legally contain a nested clickable action), the card is now a div with a real Delete button inside it — a `window.confirm()` gate, then `CreatorProjectStore.remove(record.id)`, then either re-rendering My Projects (more remain) or returning to Screen 1 (none do, avoiding a dead-end empty grid). The new inner button needed the same `!important` width/height/margin overrides this codebase has fixed repeatedly for a nested button caught by the global `button:not(...){width:100%}` cascade rule (Object Strip cards, the Publish Studio close button, Doodle's pen swatches, and now this). Verified via Playwright: deleting one of three cards removes exactly that one from both the DOM and the real `vihustudio-projects` storage record while staying on My Projects (confirming `stopPropagation` works — a bubbled click would have also fired the card's own "open project" handler and navigated away); deleting the last remaining project correctly returns to Screen 1; declining the `confirm()` dialog leaves the project completely untouched. **(3) "Sometimes the companion does not load"** — traced, not guessed: `js/companionDirector.js`'s `_mountEntity()` called `engine.load(id)` with zero retry, and `CompanionEngine.load()`'s own `fetch(companion.json)` has no retry of its own either; since `CompanionDirector.init()` is called exactly once per boot (`js/app.js`'s `_beginBoot()`) with nothing anywhere re-triggering it, a single transient fetch hiccup (a cold static-host request, a brief connectivity blip — exactly the class of failure real users on real networks hit) permanently left the companion absent for that entire session, with zero visible error. Fixed with one small, bounded retry-with-backoff (`_loadWithRetry`, 2 total attempts, 700ms delay) wrapped around the existing `engine.load(id)` call inside `_mountEntity` — `js/companionEngine.js` itself is untouched (confirmed via `git diff`, matching every prior Companion sprint's own verification discipline). Verified via Playwright route interception: a simulated first-attempt failure (a real aborted fetch, not a mock) on `companion.json` is confirmed recovered by the retry — the companion widget still mounts and is visible, reaching the real Workspace successfully; a separate, persistent-failure simulation (every attempt fails) confirms the retry stays correctly bounded at exactly 2 attempts rather than looping forever, with the companion correctly staying absent and zero page errors, Studio remaining fully functional either way. Full regression across the entire existing seven-item-batch verification suite, the sky-recognition-challenge/voice suite, and both `goldenBuild.js` suites (World Builder v1 and v2, unaffected — this batch touches zero Builder files) passes unchanged. No Theme Contract/Engine V2 Scene Model/Builder/Creator Governing Rules change; confined to `js/magicCardUI.js`, `js/companionDirector.js`, `js/creationFlow.js`, `css/style.css`, and `index.html`.)

- Creator Signature Sky Challenge — Savor the Success (a real, user-reported UX bug: "challenge screen, on correct tile choose screen transition is very fast, its not allowing user to savor the success, neither the voice is completed." Root-caused, not guessed: `js/magicCardUI.js`'s `onCardTap()` (the tap handler inside `_renderSkyChallenge`) fired `opts.onSuccess()` after a flat 900ms delay on a correct tap, regardless of how long the real recorded `skySuccess` voice line actually runs — `LumoVoice.durationMs('skySuccess')` confirms it's 2429ms, so the screen was handing off roughly 1.5 seconds before the line finished, and the celebration state (the `'correct'`/`'fade'` card classes plus the gatekeeper's `'celebrate'` mood and "✨ There it is! Welcome back. ✨" message) was visible for barely a second — exactly matching both halves of the report. Fixed by computing the hold from the clip's own real, measured duration instead of a guessed constant — `Math.max(900, LumoVoice.durationMs('skySuccess') + 900)` — mirroring the identical "stretch the timer to fit the real recording" pattern `js/gatewaySequence.js`'s `playLines()` already established elsewhere in this same feature; falls back to the original flat 900ms if `LumoVoice` is ever unavailable, matching the pre-existing defensive `try/catch` already wrapping the `LumoVoice.play()` call right above it. **Disclosed scope decision**: the wrong-tap path has the identical class of gap (`skyWrong`'s own real clip runs 2847ms against a flat 1100ms regenerate-and-reshuffle delay, so a wrong guess's own voice line can get cut off by `skyFresh` starting right after) — left untouched here since the user's report named the correct-tap transition specifically ("on correct tile choose"), not the wrong-tap flow; recorded in a code comment as a candidate for its own future fix if ever reported. Verified via a new Playwright test driving the real `_renderSkyChallenge`/`beginCreatorSignature` code path (not a reimplementation): identified the one real sky card deterministically by matching its rendered SVG star coordinates against the seeded card's own known pattern (rather than tap-and-see, which risks burning tries on decoys first), tapped it, and confirmed the real elapsed time from tap to `onSuccess` firing is now ~3.3 seconds, comfortably covering the full 2429ms voice line plus a genuine pause afterward — versus the old, confirmed-too-short 900ms. Full regression across the existing sky-recognition-challenge/voice/scroll suites required widening several tests' own fixed post-tap wait timeouts to match the new, correctly longer hold — the intended, disclosed consequence of this fix, not a regression (all three scenarios in the multi-batch challenge suite, the full Gateway-to-Studio-boot end-to-end path, and the voice-call-sequence/no-scroll suites all pass with the widened waits, identical pass/fail shape to before except for timing). Both `goldenBuild.js` suites (World Builder v1 and v2, unaffected — this fix touches zero Builder files) pass unchanged. No Theme Contract/Engine V2 Scene Model/Builder/Creator Governing Rules change; confined to `js/magicCardUI.js`.)

- Creator Signature Sky Challenge — No More Overlapping Voices on a Wrong Tap (a direct, same-day follow-up to the correct-tap savor-the-success fix: "challenge screen. not quite and here some mystery friends are new voices are overlapping." Confirmed this was exactly the disclosed, deliberately-left-out-of-scope gap that fix's own code comment already named: `js/magicCardUI.js`'s `onCardTap()` wrong-tap branch fired `LumoVoice.play('skyWrong')` then, on a flat 1100ms `setTimeout`, regenerated the board and fired `LumoVoice.play('skyFresh')` — but the real `skyWrong` clip runs 2847ms, so "Here's a new look..." always started talking while "Not quite..." was still mid-sentence, exactly matching the report. Fixed identically to the correct-tap case: the regenerate-and-reshuffle delay is now `Math.max(1100, LumoVoice.durationMs('skyWrong') + 400)` — the same "+400ms buffer" convention `js/gatewaySequence.js`'s `playLines()` already established — instead of a guessed constant, so `skyFresh` never starts until `skyWrong` has actually finished; falls back to the original flat 1100ms if `LumoVoice` is unavailable. Verified via a new Playwright test instrumenting `LumoVoice.play()` with real timestamps (not just call order): the real gap between the `skyWrong` and `skyFresh` calls now measures ~3.25 seconds (matching 2847ms duration + 400ms buffer almost exactly), comfortably covering the full clip with zero overlap — versus the old, confirmed-overlapping ~1.1 second gap. Full regression across the existing sky-recognition-challenge/voice suite required widening the voice test's own three wrong-tap-related fixed waits (previously assuming the old flat 1100ms) to match the new, correctly longer duration-driven delay — the intended, disclosed consequence of this fix, not a regression; the multi-batch challenge suite (which never exercises the wrong-tap path) and the scroll/gateway-e2e suites pass unchanged. Both `goldenBuild.js` suites (World Builder v1 and v2, unaffected — this fix touches zero Builder files) pass unchanged. No Theme Contract/Engine V2 Scene Model/Builder/Creator Governing Rules change; confined to `js/magicCardUI.js`.)

- Traveller Decline Reset — My Projects No Longer Leaks, the Ceremony Re-Offers Correctly (a direct, explicit design question that itself pointed at the real gap, immediately followed by a concrete reproduction: "but should these 3 flags should not be removed as soon we start the traveller journey? try this flow. start as traveller become creator than reload the page on challenge screen go back and choose to move forward as traveller. with this flow i have 2 observations. 1. from studio when you click home, you can see previous projects. 2 magic card generation ceremony not showing up." Traced to `js/gatewaySequence.js`'s `runVideoSequence`'s "Continue as a Traveller" decline handler (fired from `js/magicCardUI.js`'s `beginCreatorSignature`'s own choice screen) and to `js/magicCard.js`'s `shouldOfferAwakening()`, and found two real, compounding gaps in exactly the reported sequence — become a Creator, reload onto the Returning Creator's own recognition challenge, decline back to being a Traveller. **Gap 1 — My Projects leak**: the decline handler already called `CreatorProjectStore.clearAll()` (wiping the "My Projects" catalog, `vihustudio-projects`), added by an earlier "Five-Item Bug Batch" fix — but a genuinely SEPARATE key, `js/projectManager.js`'s `vihustudio-session` (the actual in-progress live/loaded project, not the catalog listing of it), was left completely untouched; the very next autosave would silently re-populate the catalog with that same stale, just-declined Creator's project, exactly explaining "from studio when you click home, you can see previous projects." Fixed by calling the pre-existing `ProjectManager.discardSession()` (already used elsewhere for exactly this purpose) at the same decline point, right alongside the catalog clear — a newly-declared Traveller now genuinely starts blank. **Gap 2 — the ceremony never re-offering**: `shouldOfferAwakening()` originally gated on "has *any* Magic Card ever been claimed on this device" (`MagicCard.list().length===0`) rather than "is one currently active right now" — so the very first Creator's claim permanently exhausted this Traveller's own future shot at the ceremony, on every subsequent Publish, for the rest of the device's life, regardless of how many times identity was later relinquished. Compounding it, `awakeningOffered` (set `true` the instant the very first ceremony closed, by ANY outcome — Claim, Maybe Later, or Just Exploring) was never reset by the decline path either, so even fixing the first half alone wouldn't have been enough. Fixed both together: `shouldOfferAwakening()` is rewritten to `!getActive() && !_readFlags().awakeningOffered` (no active card AND not already offered THIS identity-less stretch), and the decline handler now also calls `MagicCard.setActive(null)` + `MagicCard.setFlags({awakeningOffered:false})` — so a genuinely re-declared Traveller gets a real, fresh shot at the ceremony on their very next Publish, exactly matching "magic card generation ceremony not showing up." **A deliberate, disclosed safety boundary, not an oversight**: the real Magic Card record itself (`vihu-magic-cards`) is never wiped by the decline — only `setActive(null)` (the pointer to which card is "on," if any) is cleared — since on a shared device this may be a sibling's own real, recoverable card, and destroying it just because a different person declined to be recognized as it would be genuine data loss; this mirrors the exact reasoning already established for the Shared Device Identity Gate Picker. Verified end-to-end via a comprehensive Playwright reproduction driving the real UI throughout (a real Publish claim ceremony to completion, a real page reload, the real Returning Creator sky-recognition challenge, its real "← Back" → "🌱 Continue as a Traveller" choice, then a second real Publish as the now-reset Traveller): confirmed `activeId:null`/`awakeningOffered:false`/`shouldOffer:true`/`myProjectsCount:0` immediately after the decline while the underlying card record itself stays present (`cardCountStillOnDevice:1`, not destroyed); confirmed no restore-session modal appears and Creation Flow Screen 1 is reached cleanly; confirmed the My Projects screen itself shows zero cards; and confirmed the second Publish genuinely re-offers the Awakening ceremony (`awakenOverlayVisible:true`) with the card record still intact on the device. A separate, targeted regression check confirmed the OTHER, more common path — a Returning Creator who successfully verifies their pattern (`setActive()` firing via the real `_renderSkyChallenge` `onSuccess`, mocked here for speed) — still correctly has `shouldOfferAwakening()` return `false` afterward, i.e. the rewritten gate does not cause the ceremony to wrongly re-offer to an already-recognized Creator. Full regression across the entire existing Gateway/sky-recognition-challenge/companion/My-Projects/pointer-guard Playwright suite (`sky_challenge_v2_test.js`, `sky_findstars_check.js`, `sky_scroll_check.js`, `sky_voice_test.js`, `sky_challenge_gateway_e2e.js`, `gateway_creator_path_check.js`, `gateway_flyland_test.js`/`test2.js`/`test3.js`, `lumo_loop_check.js`/`check2.js`, `ceremony_beats_check.js`, `verify_myprojects_delete.js`/`_cancel.js`, `verify_home_scroll_fix.js`/`_extreme.js`, `verify_companion_retry.js`/`_persistent_fail.js`, the earlier Five-Item Bug Batch's own `fix1`-`fix5` scripts) passes unchanged — a handful of individual runs showed pre-existing, already-disclosed test-script staleness unrelated to this fix (a decoy-vs-real-card tap-order coin-flip in `sky_voice_test.js`'s own retry loop; several older scripts' fixed wait timeouts written before the "+800ms across all timings"/voice-duration-driven-delay changes shipped in earlier sprints, all confirmed to pass cleanly once re-run with a widened wait matching the current, correct behaviour) — none of it caused by this fix, all independently re-verified passing. Both `goldenBuild.js` suites (World Builder v1 and v2, unaffected — this fix touches zero Builder files) pass unchanged, 30/30. No Theme Contract/Engine V2 Scene Model/Builder/Creator Governing Rules change; confined to `js/gatewaySequence.js` and `js/magicCard.js`.)

- World Builder — Mandatory Sign-In + Versioned, Conflict-Aware Cloud Sync + "My Cloud Worlds" (a real, confirmed data-loss incident — traced step by step via the user's own console diagnostics after asking "why am not seeing my forest adventure in builder as am seeing it in studio" — found a genuine architecture gap: "Story-Forest Adventure" (a real World Builder Project with a rich forest artwork Place + a "boy" decoration/character) still rendered correctly in Studio, because Publish snapshots the compiled Theme into Supabase's `themes` table and that snapshot was untouched — but its *editable* Builder Project (Scenes/Places/Experiences) had silently reverted to a near-empty state, both in `localStorage` and in its own Cloud Backup row (`builder_projects`). The compiled Theme cannot be reverse-compiled back into editable authoring data (a confirmed, permanent, one-way-compile limitation already disclosed elsewhere in this codebase — see the earlier Engine V2 Promotion Strategy investigation), so the rich content is genuinely gone and must be re-authored by hand, using Studio's still-correct render as reference — that recovery is the user's own follow-up work, out of scope for this sprint. **Root cause**: `builder_projects`/`tools/world-builder-v2/js/services/projectSync.js` was deliberately built "local-primary, cloud backup only, never a second read path" — every save did an unconditional `ProjectStore.save()` + `ProjectSync.push()` upsert with zero check that the cloud row hadn't moved since this tab last saw it, so two tabs/sessions/devices working on the same Project id could silently stomp each other, exactly as happened here. Three explicit decisions, made by the user in plain text across the investigation, are what this sprint implements: **(1) versioned, conflict-aware sync** ("Option 1") reusing the existing `builder_projects.updated_at` column (no schema migration) to detect a moved cloud row and surface it as an explicit human choice, never a silent overwrite or an automatic merge; **(2) a real "browse my cloud Worlds, pick which to pull down" screen** ("an added way of seeing all my personal repos on a new machine and choosing which i want to sync into local machine to work upon"), distinct from the existing incidental orphan-repo-card mechanism; **(3) mandatory sign-in for World Builder** ("i would go with mandatory sign in. builder is backend, it has to be robust") — scoped explicitly to World Builder only; Studio's own signinless-for-children design (Magic Card Identity Evolution, World Card Platform, `refreshFromRepository()`) still depends on `js/themeRepositoryClient.js`'s `_ensureAuth()` anonymous-session fallback, completely untouched (confirmed via `git diff` — zero lines inside `_ensureAuth()`'s body changed); the user explicitly declined an anonymous→permanent "upgrade" path as an alternative, and explicitly accepted that this does NOT retroactively migrate anything already published under an anonymous session — only Worlds published after this ships become genuinely cross-device browsable under a real identity. `tools/world-builder/` (v1) is untouched — this sprint targets `tools/world-builder-v2/` only. **Part 1 — Mandatory Sign-In**: `js/themeRepositoryClient.js` gained `signUp(email,password)` alongside the existing `signIn()`, mirroring it exactly (calls `client.auth.signUp()`, replaces `_authPromise` on success, never throws — comes back `{ok:false,error}`); a `needsConfirmation:true` branch handles the case where Supabase's own email-confirmation flow means no session comes back yet. `tools/world-builder-v2/index.html` gained a new `#wb-signin-gate` (title/subtitle/`#wb-signin-gate-body`) sitting beside the existing `#wb-welcome-main` (which gained an explicit id); `worldBuilderApp.js`'s old, dismissible `_showSignInModal()` is deleted outright and replaced by a real, non-dismissible gate — `_checkIdentityGate()` (checks `getIdentity()`, toggles which of the two is `wb-hidden`, only calls `renderMyWorlds()`/`_renderCloudWorlds()` once `configured && signedIn`) and `_renderSigninGateBody()` (a real Sign In / Create Account form with a mode-toggle link, calling the new `signUp()`/existing `signIn()`); Sign Out returns to this same gate. A real, confirmed boot-sequence bug was caught and fixed while wiring this up: the IIFE's own tail originally ended with `renderMyWorlds()` directly, bypassing the gate entirely on first page load regardless of identity — fixed to end with `_checkIdentityGate()` instead. If Supabase isn't configured at all, the existing "not configured" disclosed state shows instead of silently falling back to anonymous. **Part 2 — Versioned, Conflict-Aware Cloud Sync**: `projectSync.js`'s `push(project,opts)` gained an optional `opts.expectedUpdatedAt` — when passed, performs a conditional `update().eq('updated_at',opts.expectedUpdatedAt)` (with `.select('id')` chained after, mirroring `themeRepositoryClient.js`'s own established `reset()`/`deleteTheme()` discipline for telling "genuinely wrote" apart from "silently matched nothing") instead of a blind upsert; an empty affected-row result then distinguishes a real conflict (a row exists with a different `updated_at` — someone else's save already moved it, reported as `{ok:false,conflict:true,cloudUpdatedAt}`, the row is NEVER overwritten) from a brand-new Project this device has never pushed before (no row at all yet, handled via a plain insert) — omitting `opts`/`opts.expectedUpdatedAt` keeps the exact original unconditional-upsert behaviour, so every pre-existing caller is unaffected. New `get(projectId)` fetches the current cloud row (`id,data,updated_at`), resolving `null` (never throwing) for an unreachable/nonexistent row — used both for the pre-open freshness check below and for "My Cloud Worlds." In `worldBuilderApp.js`: `openWorkspace(project)` now calls the new `_checkCloudFreshness(project)` right after its existing `_scheduleCloudSync()` call — a non-blocking background check (fails open, matching this function's own established View Mode discipline: never delay opening the Workspace on a network round trip) that, when the cloud row's `updated_at` is newer than what this device last recorded (`project.cloudSyncedAt`), shows an explicit "☁️ Newer Cloud Version Found" prompt (reusing `_showInfoModal()`) with a "Load Cloud Version" button — dismissible with zero forced action, since local work is never silently discarded either way. `_scheduleCloudSync()` now calls `ProjectSync.push(project,{expectedUpdatedAt:project.cloudSyncedAt})`; on success it records the new `updatedAt` onto `project.cloudSyncedAt`; on `{conflict:true}` it shows a new cloud-sync-badge "conflict" state ("Cloud has newer changes," clickable) rather than silently retrying or discarding the local edit — clicking the badge calls the new `_forceOverwriteCloud(project)` (a `window.confirm()` gate, then an unconditional push with no `expectedUpdatedAt`, the disclosed, deliberate escape hatch for the legitimate single-user-multi-tab case), settling back to the ordinary "Backed up" state once that succeeds. **Part 3 — "My Cloud Worlds"**: a new Welcome-screen `<section class="wb-section wb-cloud-worlds">` (right after "My World Projects," before "Browser Storage") lists every real cloud backup this signed-in account owns (`ProjectSync.list()`) via a new `_renderCloudWorlds()`/`_cloudWorldCard()` — comparing each row's real `updated_at` against any matching local Project's own `cloudSyncedAt` to show exactly one of three states: **"Sync to This Device"** (no local copy at all — the actual "new machine" case), **"Update Available — Load It"** (a local copy exists but the cloud is ahead, gated behind `window.confirm()`), or a disabled **"Up to Date"** (nothing to click). This is a new, always-visible, complete listing — deliberately distinct from and in addition to the existing `_annotateProjectBadges`/orphan-repo-card mechanism, which is left completely untouched; `_repoOnlyCard()`'s own restore path was widened to also stamp the restored Project's `cloudSyncedAt` from the row it materialized, so a freshly-synced Project correctly reads "Up to Date" rather than immediately re-flagging a false conflict on its very next save. Verified via three separate Playwright/Node suites: a Node-only unit test loading the real, unmodified `projectSync.js` against a hand-built thenable-based fake Supabase client (13/13 assertions — first-ever push via the insert path, a matching-`expectedUpdatedAt` conditional update genuinely succeeding, a stale `expectedUpdatedAt` correctly reported as a conflict with the row **never** overwritten, the original unconditional-upsert behaviour completely unchanged for a caller passing no `opts`, `get()`'s found/null cases); a full-browser Playwright suite mocking `ThemeRepositoryClient`/`ProjectSync` via route interception (15/15 assertions, zero console errors — the gate blocks the Welcome screen on boot with zero identity, Create Account unlocks it with a real 3-field signup form, a cloud-only World with no local match correctly shows "Sync to This Device" and materializes+opens a real local copy, an already-synced local Project against a newer cloud row correctly shows "Update Available," Sign Out re-locks the gate); and a second full-browser suite specifically covering the remaining conflict-UI paths (8/8 assertions, zero console errors — a caught-up local copy correctly shows a disabled "Up to Date"; opening a genuinely stale local Project shows the "Newer Cloud Version Found" prompt, dismissible with no forced action; a real edit that pushes into a mocked `{conflict:true}` response shows the cloud badge's conflict state, and clicking it force-overwrites and settles back to "Backed up"). Two real Playwright-harness gotchas were found and fixed while writing these tests, not app bugs: `worldBuilderApp.js`'s own private closure variables (`currentNav`, etc.) are unreachable from a separate `page.evaluate()` execution context — poking them directly silently creates an unrelated global instead, so reaching Overview/World Settings for a real edit had to go through the actual reachable `#wb-btn-settings` header control (which correctly opens Overview inside the shared `#wb-modal`/`#wb-modal-body`, not the permanent `#wb-context-panel` — `#wb-global-nav`'s own tab bar is permanently `wb-hidden` and non-functional in the current rebuilt Workspace, per that element's own already-existing code comment, a real dead-DOM-mount-point the test initially, mistakenly, tried to click). Full regression: both `goldenBuild.js` suites (World Builder v1 and v2) pass unchanged, confirming this sprint's real Build/Validate/Publish/Import pipeline is completely untouched; `git diff --stat` confirms zero changes to `tools/world-builder/` (v1) and zero changes to any Studio-side file (`js/app.js`, `js/creationFlow.js`, `js/magicCard*.js`, `js/contextPanel.js`, `js/objectStrip.js`, `js/pageRuntime.js`, `renderer/slideRenderer.js`) — the diff is confined exactly to `js/themeRepositoryClient.js` (additive `signUp` only) plus `tools/world-builder-v2/{index.html,css/world-builder.css,js/worldBuilderApp.js,js/services/projectSync.js}`. No `supabase/schema.sql` change was needed — the existing `updated_at` column already suffices for optimistic concurrency. No Theme Contract/Engine V2 Scene Model/Creator Governing Rules change.)

- My Cloud Worlds — Card Layout Fix (a real, user-supplied screenshot of the just-shipped feature showed every card's World Name crushed down to 1-2 characters ("C..", "M.."), overlapping the "Sync to This Device"/"Up to Date" action. Two real, compounding CSS bugs, both found and fixed. **(1)** `.wb-cloud-world-card` shares its base class with "My World Projects"'s own `.wb-project-card`, whose 112px right padding is reserved purely for that OTHER card's absolutely-positioned Rename/Duplicate/Delete control trio — a Cloud World card has no such controls, so that padding sat entirely empty, wasting real horizontal space; fixed with the exact same `padding-right:18px` override `.wb-project-card-repo-only` already uses for the identical reason. **(2)** Even with that space reclaimed, a Cloud World card's own action is a real text label ("Sync to This Device" / "Update Available — Load It"), not a single glyph like Rename/Duplicate/Delete — it can't share one narrow inline flex row with a long World Name without the name still getting crushed, since the button (flex-shrink:0) refuses to shrink and all the squeeze falls onto the name instead. Fixed by restructuring `_cloudWorldCard()` (`tools/world-builder-v2/js/worldBuilderApp.js`) into a two-row stack — a new `.wb-cloud-world-top` (thumb+info, a nested row) sits on its own line, with the action button now a full-width row beneath it — rather than one cramped inline row. Verified via a direct Playwright measurement against the exact realistic long name from the reported screenshot ("Story-Forest Adventure With A Genuinely Long Real Name"): before the fix, the name's rendered box was 64.6px wide (crushed to a couple characters) with the button crowding right beside it; after, the name box is 224px wide (the full name renders, no crushing) with the button on its own 290px-wide row beneath, zero overlap. Full regression: all three existing Node/Playwright verification suites for this feature (13/13, 15/15 with zero console errors, 8/8 with zero console errors) and both `goldenBuild.js` suites (World Builder v1 and v2) pass unchanged. No Theme Contract/Engine V2 Scene Model/Creator Governing Rules change; confined to `tools/world-builder-v2/css/world-builder.css` and `tools/world-builder-v2/js/worldBuilderApp.js`.)

- World Builder — Cache-Bust Query Params (the layout fix above was correctly shipped and verified, but the user's browser kept showing the old, broken layout after refreshing — pointing at a real, separate gap this codebase had already learned to guard against everywhere else: `index.html` (root Studio) has carried `?v=NNNN` cache-busting query params on its own stylesheet links since the "Stylesheet Cache-Busting" fix earlier in this project's history, precisely because a browser (or an intermediate cache/CDN) can keep serving a stale same-URL asset across deploys indefinitely — but `tools/world-builder-v2/index.html` had never adopted the same convention on ANY of its own tags, CSS or JS, across its entire history. Confirmed via `grep`: every `<link>`/`<script src>` in that file referenced its target with no query string at all. Fixed by appending `?v=0095` (this sprint's own World Builder v2 build number) to the stylesheet link and all 24 `<script src>` tags in `tools/world-builder-v2/index.html` — a plain, global, safe find-and-replace, confirmed beforehand via `grep` that every occurrence of `.js"`/`.css"` in the file is genuinely inside one of these tags (no other quoted string happens to end that way). The going-forward convention: bump this one number on every future World Builder v2 ship that touches CSS/JS, mirroring the root `index.html`'s own established ritual, so a returning browser is guaranteed a real re-fetch rather than risking a silently stale cache. **A real Playwright-harness gotcha found and fixed while re-verifying, not an app bug**: this sprint's own existing test suites' `page.route('**/themeRepositoryClient.js', ...)` mocks stopped matching the instant the real URL gained a query string, since Playwright's glob pattern requires the pattern to match the full URL including its query — widened to `'**/themeRepositoryClient.js*'`/`'**/services/projectSync.js*'` (a trailing wildcard) in both affected scripts, re-verified passing (14/14 and 8/8) afterward. A separate two-`goldenBuild.js`-failure scare during this same verification pass was traced to the shell's own leftover working directory from an earlier `cd` in the fix command, not a regression — re-run from the repo root, both pass (30/30 each) unchanged. Verified via a fresh Playwright screenshot loading the real, versioned URLs end-to-end (zero console errors, the fixed two-row card layout renders correctly). No Theme Contract/Engine V2 Scene Model/Creator Governing Rules change; confined to `tools/world-builder-v2/index.html`.)

- My Cloud Worlds — Real Thumbnails (a direct follow-up: "can we show the thumbnails in the cloud worlds." Until now `_cloudWorldCard()` (`tools/world-builder-v2/js/worldBuilderApp.js`) only ever showed a plain glyph — the World's `themeIcon`/icon, or a generic ☁️ — never a real authored image, unlike "My World Projects"'s own `_projectCard()`, which has always resolved `thumbnail.png` via `window.ProjectModel.getAsset(project,'thumbnail.png')` and rendered a real `<img>` when one exists. Confirmed this gap was purely an oversight in the earlier Cloud Worlds sprint, not a real constraint — `ProjectSync.push()` stores `data: project` verbatim (the exact same raw Project shape `ProjectStore` persists locally, `.files` and all), so a Cloud World row's `row.data` is already a fully valid `ProjectModel`-shaped object with no translation needed. Fixed by reusing the identical `getAsset`/fallback/`onerror`-degrades-to-glyph pattern `_projectCard()` already established: `_cloudWorldCard()` now resolves `window.ProjectModel.getAsset(row.data,'thumbnail.png')` and renders a real `<img>` when present, falling back to the existing glyph only when no thumbnail was ever authored. No CSS change was needed — `.wb-cloud-world-card` already inherits `.wb-project-thumb img{width:100%;height:100%;object-fit:cover}` from the shared base class the two card types share. Verified via a new 8-assertion Playwright suite (mocking `themeRepositoryClient.js`/`services/projectSync.js` via `page.route()` module-body replacement, mirroring this feature's own established test-harness pattern — a bare `addInitScript` overwrite was tried first and found to race against, and lose to, the real modules' own tail `window.X=api` assignment once their script tags actually execute, the identical class of gotcha already documented for this feature's other tests): a row with a real `thumbnail.png` asset renders exactly one `<img>` whose `src` matches the authored data URI with no glyph text alongside it; a row with no thumbnail renders zero `<img>` elements and correctly falls back to its own theme icon glyph. Full regression across the existing 13/15/8-assertion suites for this feature and both `goldenBuild.js` suites (World Builder v1 and v2) passes unchanged. Since this changes `worldBuilderApp.js`'s own content, the cache-bust `?v=` query param on every tag in `tools/world-builder-v2/index.html` was bumped from `0095` to `0097` (matching this ship's build number), mirroring the "bump this one number on every future ship that touches CSS/JS" ritual established by the prior Cache-Bust sprint — skipping this would have reintroduced the exact stale-browser-cache bug that sprint existed to fix. No Theme Contract/Engine V2 Scene Model/Creator Governing Rules change; confined to `tools/world-builder-v2/js/worldBuilderApp.js` and `tools/world-builder-v2/index.html`.)

- My Cloud Worlds — Delete Option (a direct follow-up: "give delete option on cloud worlds also." A Cloud World card previously had no way to remove itself — only "My World Projects"'s local `_projectCard()` and the Personal-repo-only `_repoOnlyCard()` had a Delete button, and My Cloud Worlds lists a genuinely different resource (a `builder_projects` cloud backup row, not a local draft or a Published Theme), so neither existing Delete implementation already covered it. **Scope, deliberately narrow**: Delete on a Cloud World card removes ONLY that cloud backup row (`ProjectSync.remove(row.id)`) — never any local draft on this device, even if one exists with the same id — matching this module's own established "local-primary, cloud backup only" discipline (`js/services/projectSync.js`'s own header comment): "My Cloud Worlds" represents the backup itself, so Delete here means "stop keeping this World backed up in the cloud," not "delete my local work," which already has its own separate Delete affordance on the local card. `_cloudWorldCard()` gained a `.wb-project-card-controls`/`.wb-project-card-btn` (🗑) control reusing the exact same corner-anchored visual language `_repoOnlyCard()`'s own Delete button already established, rather than inventing a second delete-button style — gated behind `window.confirm()`, then re-rendering `_renderCloudWorlds()` so the list always reflects the real, current state (a failed remove simply leaves the row still listed on the next fetch, never a fabricated success). **A real, measured layout bug was found and fixed while verifying, not assumed away**: `.wb-cloud-world-card` inherited `_repoOnlyCard()`'s own `padding-right:18px` override, but that card's absolutely-positioned Delete control never participates in flex layout, so nothing constrained the World Name's available width to leave room for it — a direct bounding-box measurement (nameBox/delBox, the same technique the earlier Card Layout Fix sprint used) confirmed a real ~22px overlap between a long World Name and the new Delete button before the fix; widened to `padding-right:46px` (30px button + 10px inset + a small buffer), re-measured afterward with a clean 6px gap and zero overlap. Verified via a new 8-assertion Playwright suite: exactly one Delete button per card; the layout measurement confirming no overlap with a genuinely long real-world name; clicking Delete calls `ProjectSync.remove()` with exactly the correct row id; the deleted card disappears from the list while the other, undeleted card remains and is confirmed to be the correct one. Full regression across the existing 13/15/8/8-assertion suites for this feature and both `goldenBuild.js` suites (World Builder v1 and v2) passes unchanged. Cache-bust `?v=` bumped from `0097` to `0098` on every tag in `tools/world-builder-v2/index.html` since this changes both `worldBuilderApp.js` and `world-builder.css`. No Theme Contract/Engine V2 Scene Model/Creator Governing Rules change; confined to `tools/world-builder-v2/js/worldBuilderApp.js`, `tools/world-builder-v2/css/world-builder.css`, and `tools/world-builder-v2/index.html`.)

- My Cloud Worlds — Classification Redesign: Linked / Related / Orphan (a direct, explicit request to redesign, not just patch: after shipping Thumbnails and Delete for "My Cloud Worlds," a real screenshot showed "My World Projects" and "My Cloud Worlds" appearing to list duplicate copies of the same World ("My shapes" showing in both, "Story-Forest Adventure" showing as a second, unrelated-looking card) — "i need to understand this. what does this actually mean." The honest explanation, given first without changing anything: a Cloud World card previously matched a local Project only by exact Project *storage* id (`row.id === project.id`), never by World identity (`manifest.id`) or display name — so any Cloud backup left behind by an earlier Duplicate/Clone/rename in that World's own history (Duplicate always mints BOTH a fresh Project id AND a fresh World id, confirmed via direct code read of `_duplicateProject()`) rendered as an apparently unrelated second card, with no way to tell it apart from a genuinely different World on another machine.
