The user then explicitly escalated from "explain this" to "**figure out how to easily interpret them, showing multiple copies of same theme is confusing, there should be a better way to present it — also the operations available**," delegating both the redesign and its scope to this session. **The redesign — three classified cases, not one flat list**: reused the exact, already-proven World-identity-matching technique `_annotateProjectBadges()` already established for Repository entries (`rowManifest.id === entry.theme_id`) rather than inventing a new, more fragile name-based heuristic. **(1) Linked** — a cloud row whose own `row.id` matches a local Project's storage id exactly (the live backup of a card already shown in "My World Projects") is no longer rendered as its own card at all: `_annotateCloudLink(project, row)` folds it into that local card's own inline status line instead — a real "☁️ Newer backup available — Load It" button (when the cloud row is genuinely ahead of what this device last recorded, `project.cloudSyncedAt`) or a quiet, button-less "☁️ Backed up X ago" note (when caught up) — eliminating the confusing duplicate-card case outright. **(2) Related** — no Project-id match, but the row's own compiled World identity (`manifest.id`, read from `row.data.files['manifest.json'].id`) matches a local Project's World id: a genuinely older, separate save of a World the author has already renamed/re-duplicated/re-saved since. Rendered with its own explicit `.wb-cloud-world-card-related` styling (a `--wb-sky` left border + status pill — the one previously-unclaimed accent color in the palette), a plain-language note naming the existing local Project by its real name ("A separate, older save of '`<name>`' (already in My World Projects above)"), and an action that's honest about what it actually does — "📂 Open as a Separate Copy," reusing the exact, already-tested `_duplicateProject()` mechanism (fresh Project id + fresh World id + quota-failure handling) rather than any new id-minting scheme, so it can never collide with the still-live local Project it's related to. **(3) Orphan** — no match of any kind: the genuine "restore this on a new machine" case, now enriched with real detail instead of just a name — `_cloudBackupDetailText()` shows "Last saved X ago · N scenes" (via a new `_cloudBackupSceneCount()`, counting real `scenes/*.json` entries), and the existing "Sync to This Device" action is unchanged. `renderMyWorlds()` is the one choke point kept in sync — it now calls the new `_refreshCloudWorlds()` at its own end, so every existing call site throughout the file (Rename/Duplicate/Delete handlers, the storage meter, the sign-in gate) automatically benefits with zero additional wiring, and the two sections can never visibly drift out of sync with each other. `_projectCard()` gained one small, additive `data-project-id` attribute (distinct from its pre-existing `data-world-id`) — the exact key `_annotateCloudLink()` looks up to enrich a local card in place. Verified via a new 23-assertion Playwright suite (a real local Project created through the actual UI, then all three classification cases driven end-to-end against it: Linked-newer showing the inline "Load It" line and correctly updating `cloudSyncedAt` when clicked; Linked-up-to-date showing the quiet no-button note; Related showing exactly one correctly-labelled card whose "Open as a Separate Copy" produces a genuinely new local Project — count +1, opens directly into the Workspace, distinct Project id AND World id confirmed — and whose own Delete removes only that related row; Orphan showing the correct detail text/scene count and correctly syncing to a new local copy) plus full regression across the existing sign-in/versioned-sync/thumbnail/delete suites for this feature area — two of those suites' own pre-existing assertions were intentionally updated, not weakened, since they had directly tested the OLD, now-superseded "show every backup as a flat separate card" behavior for exactly the Linked case this redesign folds away (`verify_mandatory_signin_cloud_sync.js`'s Scenario E, `verify_versioned_sync_conflict_ui.js`'s Scenario G — both now assert the correct new inline-status-line behavior instead) — and both `goldenBuild.js` suites (World Builder v1 and v2), all passing unchanged, zero console errors. Cache-bust `?v=` bumped from `0098` to `0099` on every tag in `tools/world-builder-v2/index.html` since this changes `worldBuilderApp.js`, `world-builder.css`, and `index.html` together. No Theme Contract/Engine V2 Scene Model/Creator Governing Rules change; confined to `tools/world-builder-v2/js/worldBuilderApp.js`, `tools/world-builder-v2/css/world-builder.css`, and `tools/world-builder-v2/index.html`.)

- World Builder — Delete No Longer Cascades to a Published Theme's Cloud Copies (a real, user-reported bug found while continuing to use World Builder right after the classification redesign above shipped: "found a bug. a world which is published despite the warning save failed. if we delete local copy of this the cloud sync file also gets deleted on its own." **Root cause, traced precisely, not guessed**: `_persist()` correctly gates `_scheduleCloudSync()` on a *successful* local save (a save that fails — the real "Save Failed — try a smaller image" state, AV-009 — never pushes to the Cloud Backup) — but Build/Publish reads the live, in-memory `currentProject` directly, completely bypassing both `localStorage` and the Cloud Backup, so a Theme can be successfully Published to the Personal Repository at a moment when this exact Project's local save is actively, visibly failing. That means the Published Theme (and, in a related scenario, the Cloud Backup from an earlier successful sync) can genuinely hold real, working content the local draft on this device never actually saved. `_deleteProjectEverywhere` — a real, deliberate feature from an earlier sprint ("i deleted it twice but it keeps coming back") that made a local draft's own Delete button also cascade-remove the Published Personal Theme (`deleteTheme('personal', worldId)`) and the Cloud Backup (`ProjectSync.remove(project.id)`) — had no way to tell "this local copy is a faithful stand-in for what's published/backed-up" apart from "this local copy is stale relative to it," so it destroyed both unconditionally the instant the (possibly broken/stale) local draft was deleted: real, working, already-Published content, permanently gone, with no recovery path — the exact same class of silent data loss the Versioned Cloud Sync sprint ("Story-Forest Adventure") already fixed once for a different cause. **The fix, and why the cascade is no longer needed at all**: the original "keeps coming back" complaint that motivated the cascade is now independently solved by two mechanisms this session's own work already put in place — `_annotateProjectBadges()`'s `personalOnly`/`officialOnly` repo-only cards (from the earlier "'My World Projects' Lists Personal/Official/Growing" sprint) and this session's own Cloud Worlds classification redesign's `_relatedBackupCard`/`_orphanBackupCard` — both of which already render a leftover Published Theme or Cloud Backup as its own clearly-labelled, honestly-separate card, never a confusing zombie duplicate of the deleted local draft. So `_deleteProjectEverywhere` (renamed `_deleteLocalDraft` to match) now removes ONLY the local draft — never touching the Personal Repository row or the Cloud Backup — and the local card's own confirm() dialog was reworded to say so plainly ("If it's published to your Personal Repository, that copy stays published — remove it separately from its own card if you want it gone too"). The Personal-repo-only card's own dedicated Delete button (which already independently cleans up both the Published Theme and its linked Cloud Backup) and My Cloud Worlds' own per-card Delete are both completely untouched — an author who genuinely wants everything gone can still remove each piece deliberately, one click at a time, from its own honestly-labelled card; nothing is now permanently un-deletable. Verified via a new 11-assertion Playwright suite reproducing the exact reported scenario (a real local Project with a mocked-published Personal Theme row and a mocked Cloud Backup row, standing in for content the local save never actually captured): deleting the local draft's own card removes only the local record — `deleteTheme`/`ProjectSync.remove` are confirmed to NEVER fire, and both the Published Theme row and the Cloud Backup row are confirmed to still genuinely exist afterward; the now-orphaned Published Theme correctly resurfaces as its own repo-only card and the orphaned backup correctly resurfaces as its own Orphan card in My Cloud Worlds, each with its own working, independent Delete button (confirmed by actually clicking the repo-only card's Delete and seeing both `deleteTheme` fire and the Cloud Backup row disappear). Full regression across the existing sign-in/versioned-sync/thumbnail/delete/classification suites for this feature area (all passing unchanged, since none of them exercised the cascade's own now-removed behaviour) and both `goldenBuild.js` suites (World Builder v1 and v2) passes unchanged, zero console errors. No CSS/HTML change, so no cache-bust bump was needed. No Theme Contract/Engine V2 Scene Model/Creator Governing Rules change; confined to `tools/world-builder-v2/js/worldBuilderApp.js`.)

- Platform Hardening — Draft Asset Architecture, Phase A: Foundation (a deliberate architecture change, planned and approved before implementation, per this project's own "architecture changes require explicit approval" rule — closes the real, confirmed root cause behind the "Story-Forest Adventure" data-loss incident above: every uploaded image in both authoring surfaces has been embedded as a base64 `data:` URI directly inside one JSON object written wholesale to a single `localStorage` key (a small, fixed browser quota) and, separately, to `builder_projects`/`creator_projects`' own `data jsonb` cloud-backup column with no size limit of its own — Build/Publish reads live in-memory state directly, bypassing whatever the local save last successfully persisted, so a Theme/Story can Publish successfully from memory at the exact moment its own local save is failing on quota, permanently diverging the two (a compiled Theme cannot be reverse-compiled back into editable authoring data). The user's own binding words: *"ok lets go with plan 1. think clearly, at no moment under any circumstances there should be any data loss or jittery sessions."* **This is Phase A only — pure, self-contained infrastructure; nothing in the app calls any of it yet, so this ships with zero behavior-change risk to any existing user; Phases B (World Builder v2 upload/read call-site rewiring), C (Creator/Studio rewiring), D (migration activation), and E (full end-to-end verification) remain explicitly future work, each its own independently shippable increment.** New shared `js/assetStore.js` (loaded by all three authoring surfaces — root `index.html`, `tools/world-builder-v2/index.html`, `tools/world-builder/index.html` — exactly mirroring how `js/themeRepositoryClient.js` is already shared today, reusing its `getClient()`/`getSession()` rather than a second sign-in or config fetch) implements a new reference format, `vihu-asset:<surface>:<projectId>:<assetId>` (`surface` ∈ `{builder,creator}`, deliberately never embedding `owner_id` so the Storage object path — `{surface}/{owner_id}/{projectId}/{assetId}`, mirroring `theme-assets`' own `{repository}/{owner_id-or-'_official'}/{theme_id}/{relativePath}` convention exactly — is always derivable from the ref plus whatever session is live right now, never a lookup table) — a legacy raw `data:` URI is a permanently valid input to every function here too (format-detection, not version-flagging, so untouched old content keeps working forever with zero risk from any later migration step). `AssetStore.put(source,{surface,projectId})` writes a blob into a new IndexedDB database (`vihu-asset-cache`, two stores — `blobs`, the tier that's "truth for fast reads," never auto-deleted; `pendingUploads`, a durably-queued, retry-forever-with-exponential-backoff upload record, written in the SAME transaction as the blob so one can never exist without the other) and resolves with the new reference the instant the LOCAL write completes — never waits on the network, satisfying "zero jitter." `AssetStore.resolve(ref)` checks an in-memory warm cache, then IndexedDB, then falls back to a Storage-signed-URL fetch (the same asynchrony already established at `_repoOnlyCard`'s own `_resolveRepoThumbnailURL(...).then(...)`, generalized rather than reinvented) — never rejects, resolves `null` on total failure, matching every existing call site's own `getAsset(...)||null` convention; `AssetStore.resolveSync(ref)` is the warm-cache-only synchronous seam for per-frame canvas painters. `AssetStore.retryPending()` (called once on module load, once on the `online` event, and on a slow background interval) is what makes an upload durably resumable — since the queue lives in IndexedDB, not memory, a Theme/Story Author who uploaded something and immediately closed the tab, or lost network mid-upload, has that upload resume automatically the next time either surface loads, with zero user action required and nothing silently forgotten; verified directly via a real page reload in the same browser context (IndexedDB persists across it; the in-memory warm cache does not) — a ref put() before reload still resolves to a real local `blob:` URL afterward. `AssetStore.hydrateForExport(ref)` is the inverse of `put()`, for the two genuinely-portable-file paths (`ProjectManager.saveProjectAs`, World Builder's `.vtheme` Export) that must stay self-contained outside this app's own Supabase project. `AssetStore.migrateFieldsOnSave(surface,projectId,accessors)` is the lazy-migration seam Phase D will wire into the existing debounced save paths (`_persist()`/`_writeStorage()`) — deliberately generic, taking a caller-supplied array of `{get,set}` accessor pairs rather than hardcoding either surface's own field shapes inside the shared module, so `assetStore.js` stays genuinely reusable rather than surface-aware; a field is only rewritten to the new reference after `put()`'s local write is confirmed, never left half-migrated, and — a real "under any circumstances" safety net — a `put()` whose own IndexedDB write fails for any reason resolves with the ORIGINAL source unchanged instead of throwing or losing the asset. `navigator.storage.persist()` is called once at module init (best-effort, no user-visible prompt in most browsers with real engagement) to reduce, though not eliminate, the one real, disclosed residual risk this design accepts rather than glosses over: between "local IndexedDB write confirmed" and "Storage upload confirmed," an asset briefly exists in exactly one place, and a browser evicting "best-effort" storage under real disk pressure during that narrow window — or the user clearing site data before the upload ever succeeds — could still lose it; keeping a redundant embedded copy locally until Storage confirms would simply recreate the exact quota problem this plan exists to fix, so this is named as an accepted, minimized-not-eliminated tradeoff rather than a false promise of absolute zero risk. A new, disclosed-but-unexecuted `draft-assets` Storage bucket + RLS policy set is added to `supabase/schema.sql` (this sandbox cannot reach Supabase, the same standing limitation every prior schema change in this codebase's history has disclosed) — owner-only read/write/update/delete for both surfaces, PLUS one additive cross-owner read exception for the Creator-only Magic Card recall case, mirroring `creator_projects_select`'s own `exists(...)` grant exactly, so a recalled Creator project's images actually resolve on the new device instead of a permission-denied dead end; World Builder gets no such exception, matching `builder_projects`' own plain owner-only RLS. **A real, confirmed cross-version risk was found and closed in the same phase**: `tools/world-builder/js/projectStore.js` (v1) and `tools/world-builder-v2/js/projectStore.js` share the literal, byte-identical `localStorage` key `'vihu-world-builder-projects'` — so a Project touched in v2 (now potentially containing a `vihu-asset:` reference, once Phase B ships) is directly visible to and loadable by v1 if that browser ever opens v1's page, and v1's own 3 read call sites (`worldBuilderApp.js` lines 83/1083/3615, all plain `img.src=<string>`) would otherwise show a broken image with zero mitigation. Closed with the ONLY v1 change in this phase — a new shared `_wbResolveImgSrc(img,ref)` helper, assigning a legacy `data:` URI synchronously exactly as before (zero behavior change) but leaving a `vihu-asset:` reference unassigned (no guaranteed-broken-image flash) until `AssetStore.resolve()` lands — v1's own upload pipeline, `_toBlob` equivalent, and persistence are completely untouched; v1 never produces a `vihu-asset:` reference itself. Verified via a new 24-assertion Playwright suite (a real IndexedDB in a real headless browser, `ThemeRepositoryClient` mocked with a deliberately-delayed `getSession()` to prove the write path never blocks on it): `put()`'s reference shape and its provably-zero network dependency; `resolve()`'s three-tier fallback (warm cache → IndexedDB → signed URL) and its legacy-`data:`/null passthrough; `resolveSync()`'s warm-cache-only behavior; IndexedDB durability across a real page reload; the pending-upload queue genuinely draining via `retryPending()` with the correct bucket/path shape recorded on the mocked Storage call; `hydrateForExport()`'s real byte-level round trip; `migrateFieldsOnSave()`'s accessor-driven rewrite, already-migrated no-op, and empty-field no-op; and — end to end, through the real production boot sequence, not a synthetic call — a v2-shaped World Builder Project seeded with a `vihu-asset:` thumbnail reference (backed by a real IndexedDB blob put on a prior same-origin page load) opened fresh in v1 correctly renders a real `blob:` URL, not a broken image. Full regression: both `goldenBuild.js` suites (World Builder v1 and v2) pass unchanged (30/30 each); 7 of 8 spot-checked recent World Builder v2 Playwright regression scripts pass unchanged (the 8th, and one root-Studio boot script, fail on a pre-existing, unrelated hardcoded-port connection-refused error in the scratch script itself — confirmed via each script's own already-passing, dynamic-port-using successor/sibling script — not a regression from this phase). No Theme Contract/Engine V2 Scene Model/Creator Governing Rules change; confined to a new `js/assetStore.js`, `supabase/schema.sql` (additive, disclosed/unexecuted), `index.html`, `tools/world-builder-v2/index.html`, `tools/world-builder/index.html`, and `tools/world-builder/js/worldBuilderApp.js`.)

- Platform Hardening — Draft Asset Architecture, Phase B: World Builder v2 rewiring (the next independently-shippable increment named in Phase A's own status note — rewires every real upload/read call site in World Builder v2 to actually use the Foundation that phase deliberately left uncalled. **Upload side, one fix point covers everything**: `_fileInputUpload(accept,onFile)` — already the ONE shared primitive every real upload in this file funnels through (Identity Thumbnail/Hero, Experience Image/Graphics, generic Assets-screen slots) — now routes its downscaled data URI through a new `_storeUploadedAsset(dataURL,onFile)`, which calls `AssetStore.put(dataURL,{surface:'builder',projectId:currentProject.id})` and hands the resulting durable `vihu-asset:builder:<projectId>:<assetId>` reference to whatever setter (`setIdentityAsset`/`setAsset`/`updateExperienceProperty`) would have received the raw base64 before — zero changes needed at any individual call site's own callback body, and a graceful fallback to the original data URI if `AssetStore` is ever unavailable, never losing the upload. `_materializeProjectFromPackage`'s own signed-URL "repair" step (View Mode/Clone, which used to hydrate a Storage signed URL into a full embedded `data:` URI — silently reintroducing large base64 the instant an Official Theme with real artwork was cloned or viewed) now routes through the identical `AssetStore.put()` call instead. **Read side, one shared resolver, ~14 call sites**: a new `_resolveAssetRefToSrc(ref)` wraps `AssetStore.resolve()` (falling back to using `ref` as-is if `AssetStore` isn't loaded) and is now used by the Welcome-screen project card, My Cloud Worlds' cloud card, the Overview identity card, the representative-artwork and Scene-Layer-image canvas caches (`_representativeArtworkImage`/`_resolveLayerImage`, whose own "resolve once into a host cache, redraw on arrival" pattern already matched exactly what `AssetStore` needed), the Decorations list's per-layer thumbnail, the Experience Library tab, Experience cards, the generic Asset slot row, and the World Card art canvas's Hero Image — a legacy `data:` URI still resolves same-tick with zero behaviour change; a `vihu-asset:` reference resolves asynchronously (warm cache → IndexedDB → a signed Storage URL), the identical placeholder-then-resolve pattern `_repoOnlyCard` already established for compiled-Theme thumbnails, generalized rather than reinvented. **Two real, load-bearing Build-time gaps found and fixed at their own root, not assumed safe**: `tools/world-builder-v2/js/projectCompiler.js`'s `_toBlob(path,value)` gained a new branch — checked *before* the existing `data:` branch — resolving a top-level `project.files` entry's `vihu-asset:` reference to real bytes via `AssetStore.resolve()` then `fetch()`, throwing a clear, disclosed error only if the reference genuinely can't be resolved at all (never silently falling through to the byte-encode-the-string-itself fallback, which would corrupt the asset); `tools/world-builder-v2/js/services/builder.js`'s `externalizeSceneImage(scene,layer,package_)` had its own, entirely separate `indexOf('data:')===0` check gating whether a Scene Layer's `.image` ever reaches the compiled package's `assets` map — made `async` and taught the identical resolution step, closing a genuine silent-data-loss path this session's own upload-path fix would otherwise have newly introduced (a Theme Author's Scene-authored Decoration image would have compiled a real `relPath` reference into the Layer Pack with NO backing bytes at that path in `assets`, since the old check simply never matched a `vihu-asset:` string). `js/projectModel.js`'s `_syncUniversalContent` (the Experience→Scene-Layer image mirror) needed zero changes — confirmed via direct code read to already be a pure `image: src || null` string copy, so it naturally carries the new small reference string forward without ever re-`put()`-ing the same bytes twice, exactly as the original architecture plan anticipated. `_rasterizeGlyphToDataURL` (the Decorations quick-picker's ~160×160 single-glyph PNG rasterizer) is a disclosed, deliberate exception, documented in its own code comment rather than silently left inconsistent — its bytes are a few KB at most, nowhere near the scale that ever threatened `localStorage`'s quota, and its one call site is a synchronous, multi-step sequence (create → graduate → set property → attach → persist → render) a Promise-based `put()` would need real restructuring to fit into for no benefit at this size. Verified via a new 22-assertion Playwright suite driving the real World Builder v2 UI end to end (not internals, with a mocked `ThemeRepositoryClient` standing in for Supabase — this sandbox cannot reach a real Supabase project, the same standing, disclosed limitation as every prior Supabase-touching sprint here): a real image uploaded through the Overview Thumbnail row is stored as a `vihu-asset:` reference, not embedded base64, and resolves correctly in both the Overview preview `<img>` and the separate Welcome-screen project card (two independent read call sites); a real `ProjectCompiler.runBuild()` produces a compiled package whose `assets['thumbnail.png']` is confirmed **byte-identical** to the original uploaded file; a genuinely interrupted upload (a real second image, caught via `getPendingCount()>0` while a deliberately-delayed 900ms mocked Storage call was still in flight, then an immediate real page reload — "closed the tab mid-upload," not simulated) confirms the boot-time `retryPending()` call resumes and completes it automatically, with both the interrupted reference and the original Thumbnail reference still resolving correctly afterward; the resulting real v2-authored Project — now containing a genuine `vihu-asset:` reference produced by this actual upload path, not a hand-seeded fixture — still opens correctly in World Builder v1 via that version's own Phase A read-only mitigation. Both `goldenBuild.js` suites (World Builder v1 and v2, 30/30 each) and 6 existing scratchpad regression scripts (Mandatory Sign-In + Versioned Cloud Sync, Versioned Sync Conflict UI, Cloud Worlds Classification, Cloud Worlds Delete, Delete-No-Cascade, ProjectSync Versioned) plus Phase A's own 24-assertion suite all pass unchanged, zero console errors throughout. Cache-bust bumped to `?v=0102` on every tag in `tools/world-builder-v2/index.html` since this changes `worldBuilderApp.js`/`projectCompiler.js`/`services/builder.js`, all loaded from it. No Theme Contract/Engine V2 Scene Model/Creator Governing Rules change; `tools/world-builder/` (v1) and root Studio (`js/`, `index.html`) are completely untouched — confined entirely to `tools/world-builder-v2/`.)

- Platform Hardening — Draft Asset Architecture, Phase C: Creator/Studio rewiring (the next independently-shippable increment named in Phase A/B's own status notes — rewires every real upload/read call site in root Studio (Creator) to actually use the Foundation Phase A built and Phase B already proved out for World Builder v2, closing the other half of the confirmed data-loss architecture bug. **Upload side, two small shared helpers, mirroring Phase B's own established pattern**: `js/app.js` gained `_storeUploadedAsset(dataUrl,onFile)` — the exact same downscale-then-`AssetStore.put()`-then-hand-the-caller-the-reference shape World Builder v2's own `_storeUploadedAsset` already established, reusing a new, additive `AssetStore.downscaleImageDataURL(dataURL)`/`AssetStore.UPLOAD_DOWNSCALE_THRESHOLD_BYTES` (the identical 1.5MB/1600px/PNG-stays-PNG-else-JPEG-q0.85 algorithm World Builder's own private copy already used, duplicated into `assetStore.js` as one shared, Promise-based canonical version — World Builder's own copy is completely untouched, zero regression risk) — now wraps `js/app.js`'s two real insert paths (`_insertPreparedSlide`, the single-file-via-Picture-Studio path; the bulk multi-file `upload.onchange` loop). The identical helper is duplicated (not shared across files — matching this codebase's own established "kept in lockstep by hand" precedent for small per-module adapters, since `js/app.js`/`js/contextPanel.js`/`js/pageDesigner.js` are three separate self-contained modules) into `js/contextPanel.js` (wrapping `_applyImageResult`, the one shared write function behind BOTH Add/Replace Artwork and Crop/Rotate's re-apply for Place 1 and every extra Place alike; and `_appendWorldObjectEditControl`'s `v.kind==='image'` branch — a World-owned Scene Object's own "Replace Image" control, writing through `SceneEngine.setContentOverride`) and into `js/pageDesigner.js` (wrapping `_applyPreparedPicture`, the Cover/Hook/End image-manager's primary Picture-Studio-baked path, and `_onImageSelected`'s defensive direct-load fallback). `ProjectManager.ensureProjectId()` is newly exported (a thin wrapper over the pre-existing private `_ensureProjectId`, already used internally by the debounced save path) so an upload can mint/reuse a stable project id even on a brand-new project's very first picture, before any save has ever run — guaranteeing exactly one id is ever minted per project, never a race between two producers. **Read side, `ProjectManager.deserialize()`**: a new `_resolveMaybeRef(value)` resolves a `vihu-asset:` reference via `AssetStore.resolve()` before ever handing it to the pre-existing `loadImageFromDataURL` (which only ever knew how to load a real URL) — for both Place 1's own image and every extra Place's own `placeContent[id].dataURL`; a legacy `data:` URI (or `null`) passes through unchanged, same-tick, so untouched old sessions rehydrate exactly as before. Critically, the stored `_imageDataURL`/`placeContent[id].dataURL` field itself is left holding the ORIGINAL reference string, never the resolved `blob:` URL — `blob:` URLs are only valid for the lifetime of the tab that created them, so writing one back into `localStorage` would have been a genuine, silent regression the next time the project saved. **`saveProjectAs()` split per the plan's own §8**: the ordinary local/cloud save path (`_writeStorage()`/`serialize()`) needed zero changes at all — it already just writes whatever small reference `_imageDataURL` holds, since `imageToDataURL(slide)` returns that field verbatim when set. A portable `.vihu` file is different: it must stay self-contained outside this app's own Supabase project, so a new `_hydratePayloadForExport(payload)` walks every asset-bearing field in the just-built payload (`pages[i].image`, each Place's `placeContent[*].dataURL`, each World-owned object's `elementOverrides[*].image`, via a new `_collectExportAssetAccessors`) and calls the pre-existing `AssetStore.hydrateForExport()` on any still-`vihu-asset:` field, producing a real, embedded `data:` URI in the downloaded file; `saveProjectAs` itself became `async` to await this — every existing caller (`js/app.js`'s Save-As button, a bare fire-and-forget call) is unaffected, since the function's own try/catch guarantees it always resolves, never rejects. `openProject(file)`/World Builder's own `.vtheme` Export needed no change, exactly as the plan's own §8 anticipated (Export already inherits Phase B's `_toBlob` fix transitively through the Build pipeline it already uses). **Two real, previously-undiscovered read-side gaps were found and fixed at their own root, mirroring the exact pattern Phase B's own `externalizeSceneImage` fix already established** — a symptom of the SAME class of bug (an opaque reference reaching a code path that only ever expected a directly-usable `data:`/http(s) string) recurring in a new place, not a coincidence: `renderer/slideRenderer.js`'s `_ensureDecorationImage`/`_layerDrawDecorationImage` (a Story-Author-replaced World-owned object's own image override, drawn to the live canvas) previously assigned an override's raw `src` directly as an `Image.src` — a real bug the moment that override became a `vihu-asset:` reference via the `js/contextPanel.js` fix above. Fixed by making `_ensureDecorationImage` placeholder-then-resolve (caches a placeholder object under the ORIGINAL src key immediately, so a second call for a still-resolving src is a genuine cache hit, not a duplicate `AssetStore.resolve()` call, then swaps in the real, loaded `Image` once resolution settles, reusing the exact pre-existing onload/redraw-nudge mechanics) — a legacy `data:`/http(s) URL still resolves through the same call, same-tick, zero behaviour change. `js/objectStrip.js`'s `_renderThumb` (that same object's own Object Strip thumbnail `<img>`) got the matching fix. `js/pictureStudio.js`'s `open()` gained the analogous fix for its own `typeof input==='string'` branch — Crop/Rotate re-editing an existing Place/Scene-Object picture whose cached `Image` object isn't yet warm (falling back to the raw string field, `slide._imageDataURL`/`placeContent[id].dataURL`) now correctly resolves a `vihu-asset:` reference before assigning it as a real image src, instead of silently failing to load anything into the editor. `js/themeEngine.js`'s own `FileReader` usage — the one file besides the six actual producers that showed up in a repo-wide `readAsDataURL`/`FileReader` sweep at the start of this phase — was confirmed to be Theme (`.vtheme` package) import, an unrelated concern, correctly left untouched; the same final sweep, re-run after every fix, confirmed exactly these same 7 files and no missed producer. Verified via a new 20-assertion Playwright suite driving the REAL root Studio UI end to end (not internals — booting through the actual Traveller Gateway, which plays on every boot including a page reload, skipped via the exact `skipGateway()` helper this codebase's own prior Gateway-touching test scripts already established): a real 2-file bulk upload through the actual `#scanUpload` input produces two distinct `vihu-asset:` references (not embedded base64, not accidentally deduped — confirmed both are genuinely different strings); the `localStorage`-persisted session genuinely shrinks to a small reference string (confirmed <100 characters, versus what would have been several KB of embedded PNG base64); a real page reload correctly restores the session via the pre-existing restore-session modal, with the uploaded picture rehydrated into a real, loaded `Image` object while `_imageDataURL` still holds the small reference, never a transient `blob:` URL; a real `saveProjectAs()` download is intercepted via Playwright's own download-event API and its JSON inspected directly — the exported file's `page.image` is confirmed a real, non-trivial embedded `data:` URI, not a reference, and the exported-then-reimported file round-trips with the identical slide count; a direct `AssetStore.put()`/`.resolve()` round trip (on a synthetic tiny PNG, standing in for what the read-side fix now protects) confirms the underlying mechanism the Scene-Object-override fix relies on. Both `goldenBuild.js` suites (World Builder v1 and v2) and the existing Phase A (24-assertion)/Phase B (22-assertion) Playwright suites all pass completely unchanged, confirming this phase touched neither Builder surface at all. Zero console errors beyond the three already-disclosed, pre-existing, unrelated Story Egg asset gaps (`hero.png`/`magic.png`/`personality.json` — Story Egg never speaks, so it has no `personality.json` by design) this codebase's own history has already recorded repeatedly. No cache-bust bump was needed — root `index.html`'s own `<script>` tags carry no `?v=` convention at all (only its stylesheet `<link>` does, and no CSS changed this phase). No Theme Contract/Engine V2 Scene Model/Creator Governing Rules change; `tools/world-builder/` (v1) and `tools/world-builder-v2/` are completely untouched — confined entirely to `js/assetStore.js` (additive downscale helper only), `js/projectManager.js`, `js/app.js`, `js/contextPanel.js`, `js/pageDesigner.js`, `js/pictureStudio.js`, `js/objectStrip.js`, and `renderer/slideRenderer.js`. **Phases D (migration activation — wiring the already-built `AssetStore.migrateFieldsOnSave` into the existing debounced save paths, so already-saved embedded-base64 content starts shrinking one save at a time with no dedicated sweep) and E (full end-to-end verification, docs, cleanup) remain their own separately-scoped, not-yet-started increments**, per the approved plan's own phased-rollout discipline.)

- Platform Hardening — Draft Asset Architecture, Phase D: migration activation (the next independently-shippable increment named in Phase C's own status notes — wires the already-built `AssetStore.migrateFieldsOnSave(surface,projectId,accessors)` (Phase A) into both surfaces' own existing debounced save paths, so a Project/Story already saved before Phase B/C ever shipped — still holding raw embedded `data:` URIs — starts shrinking to durable `vihu-asset:` references one save at a time, with no proactive sweep and no version flag: format-detection alone (is this field `data:`-prefixed or not?) decides whether a field needs migrating, exactly matching every other read path this feature already established. **World Builder v2** (`tools/world-builder-v2/js/worldBuilderApp.js`): a new `_collectMigrationAccessors(project)` walks every known image-bearing field — `project.files[path]` top-level entries not ending in `.json`/`.md` (Identity Thumbnail/Hero, Assets-screen slots), every Scene Layer's own `.image` field, every Experience's `properties.imageSrc`/`.graphicSrc` — and returns `{get,set}` accessor pairs; a new `_scheduleAssetMigration()`, debounced 1500ms and called from `_persist()`'s own success branch (mirroring `_scheduleCloudSync`'s established shape exactly), calls `migrateFieldsOnSave('builder',project.id,accessors)` in the background and, only if anything actually changed, performs one more plain `ProjectStore.save()` plus a cloud-sync nudge so the smaller payload reaches both localStorage and (once signed in) the cloud backup. A real subtlety, handled deliberately rather than accepted as a duplicate-upload cost: a decoration Scene Layer mirrored from an Experience (`sourceExperienceId`/`contentSlot` set, Builder V3.1's Universal Experience Authoring) is skipped as its own accessor entirely — migrating it independently would call `put()` a second time for byte-identical content, the exact "one upload becomes two" the original architecture plan's own note warned against — instead the source Experience's own accessor propagates its freshly-migrated reference directly onto the already-known mirrored Layer object with no second `put()` call, verified end-to-end (the mirrored Layer's `.image` ends up the SAME reference string as the source Experience's `imageSrc`, never a distinct one, while a genuinely standalone, non-mirrored Layer's own different bytes correctly get their own, different reference). **Studio (Creator)** (`js/projectManager.js`): the analogous `_collectMigrationAccessors()` walks `AppState.slides` for `slide._imageDataURL`, every extra Place's own `placeContent[id].dataURL`, and every World-owned Scene Object override's own `elementOverrides[id].image`; `_scheduleAssetMigration()` (same 1500ms debounce, called from `_writeStorage()`'s own success branch) mirrors World Builder's shape, calling one more `_writeStorage()` only if something changed. `slide.thumbnail` is deliberately **not** included — a disclosed scope decision, not an oversight: several of its own real read sites (`js/app.js`'s page-strip/thumbnail-grid renders, `js/creatorProjectStore.js`/`js/magicCardUI.js`'s own Story/My-Projects cards) were never rewired in Phase C to resolve a reference, and thumbnails are small, derived, regenerable data (`ThumbnailEngine`) nowhere near the scale that caused the original quota bug — migrating it now would produce a genuinely broken thumbnail rather than a meaningful storage win; verified directly (`slide.thumbnail` confirmed still the original `data:` URI after a full migration cycle that correctly touched every other field). **A real, if narrow, race was found and closed at its root, in the shared `js/assetStore.js` module itself** (benefiting both surfaces' identical wiring at once, not patched around at each call site): `migrateFieldsOnSave`'s own `put()`-then-`set()` step now does a compare-and-swap — it captures the field's value before calling `put()` and only rewrites the field if it STILL holds those exact original bytes at the moment the `put()` resolves; a field genuinely replaced by a fresh, unrelated upload (Replace Artwork, a new Experience image) while the migration's own local IndexedDB write was still in flight is left completely untouched rather than silently reverted to a stale, superseded reference. Verified via a direct, fully-timing-controlled unit-level proof against the real, unmodified function (not a reimplementation) — a field mutated mid-flight by a simulated concurrent "fresh upload" is confirmed to survive migration exactly as the concurrent write left it. **A real, pre-existing Phase C read-side gap was also found and fixed in the same pass, unrelated to migration itself**: `js/pageDesigner.js`'s Cover/Hook/End Image Manager panel's own preview `<img>` assigned `s._imageDataURL` directly with no resolve step at all — invisible until Phase D's own migration made this field a `vihu-asset:` reference in practice, but actually a live bug since the moment Phase C's own write path (`_applyPreparedPicture`) started producing references for every real upload. Fixed not by adding a second async resolve path, but by reusing `s.image.src` — the same branch's own condition already confirms `s.image` (a real, already-loaded `Image` object, always assigned from a real `onload` handler) exists, and its own `.src` is always a safe, already-resolved URL. Verified via a new 24-assertion Playwright suite spanning both surfaces: a World Builder v2 Project hand-seeded with legacy `data:` URIs (a top-level Identity asset, a standalone Scene Layer image, and an Experience+its mirrored Layer sharing one legacy image) reopened after a real page reload — the one honest way to reproduce "content saved before this Phase existed," since no upload path anywhere in the app has produced a raw `data:` URI since Phase B/C shipped — then a real, unrelated edit (World Name) triggers `_persist()`; after the debounce settles, every field is confirmed migrated to a real `vihu-asset:builder:` reference that resolves back to a real local `blob:` URL, the mirrored Layer and its source Experience are confirmed to share the identical reference (no double upload) while the standalone Layer gets its own distinct one, and a second later save is confirmed a genuine no-op (idempotent); the compare-and-swap race-fix's own direct proof; and the identical discipline exercised on Studio's own surface, confirming `slide._imageDataURL`/`placeContent[id].dataURL`/`elementOverrides[id].image` all migrate correctly while `slide.thumbnail` is confirmed to deliberately stay untouched. Both `goldenBuild.js` suites (World Builder v1 and v2) and the existing Phase A/B/C Playwright suites all pass completely unchanged, confirming this phase's own additions layer cleanly on top of everything already shipped. Cache-bust bumped to `?v=0103` on every tag in `tools/world-builder-v2/index.html` since this changes `worldBuilderApp.js` (loaded from this same page); no cache-bust bump was needed for root `index.html` (its own `<script>` tags carry no `?v=` convention at all, unchanged since no CSS changed this phase). No Theme Contract/Engine V2 Scene Model/Creator Governing Rules change; confined to `js/assetStore.js` (the compare-and-swap fix, additive), `js/projectManager.js`, `js/pageDesigner.js`, and `tools/world-builder-v2/js/worldBuilderApp.js`. **Phase E (full end-to-end verification, docs, cleanup) remains its own separately-scoped, not-yet-started increment**, per the approved plan's own phased-rollout discipline.)

- Platform Hardening — Draft Asset Architecture, Phase E: verification, cross-owner resolution fix, and canonical doc (the final phase named in the approved plan's own §10 — full end-to-end regression across both surfaces, a genuinely forced network-failure recovery test, and one real, previously-undiscovered gap found while verifying the Magic Card recall scenario specifically, fixed at its root. **The gap**: `AssetStore.resolve()` has always computed the Storage object path from the CURRENT session's own owner id, with no way to resolve an asset belonging to a DIFFERENT owner — exactly the Magic Card recall case, where `js/magicCard.js`'s `_pullRecalledProjects` adopts another device's Creator project as a brand-new local copy (a fresh `project.id`, never the original), but any `vihu-asset:` reference that payload still carries was authored under the ORIGINAL device's own anonymous session, never this one; every field resolution on a recalled project's own pre-recall pictures would have silently failed to resolve, with no error ever surfaced. **The fix**: `resolve(ref, opts)` gained an optional `opts.ownerId` — a FALLBACK, tried only as a second attempt after the current session's own owner id fails first, never tried before it; `_resolveFromStorage`/a new shared `_signedUrlFor` helper implement the try-then-fallback sequence with zero per-reference bookkeeping needed (Storage's own `createSignedUrl` already fails cleanly for a path that doesn't exist under the tried owner, exactly the signal this fallback needs) — a brand-new upload made on the recalling device AFTER the recall (genuinely belonging to the current session) still resolves via the fast, correct, current-session-first path and never even reaches the fallback, so a real local upload can never be misrouted. Threaded end to end: `js/magicCard.js`'s `_pullRecalledProjects(ownerId)` now stamps `data.project.recallOwnerId=ownerId` onto the materialized payload at adoption time, alongside the existing `id` reassignment; `js/projectManager.js`'s `serialize()`/`deserialize()` carry `recallOwnerId` on `AppState.project` (round-tripping across a later local save/reload) AND stamp it onto every constructed `slide` object individually, since `renderer/slideRenderer.js` deliberately takes no dependency on `AppState` directly (it operates purely on the slide object handed to it) — this per-slide field is what lets a new `_ensureDecorationImage(src,fallbackOwnerId)` resolve a World-owned Scene Object's own Story-Author-replaced image override correctly for a recalled project, reading `s.recallOwnerId` off the slide passed to `_layerDrawDecorationImage`; `js/objectStrip.js`'s `_renderThumb` (that same object's own Object Strip thumbnail) reads it the same way via `cfg.getCurrentSlide()`; `js/pictureStudio.js`'s `open()` gained an `options.fallbackOwnerId` (threaded in by `js/contextPanel.js`'s `_cropRotateArtwork`, which already has the current slide in scope) so a recalled Place's own Crop/Rotate re-edit resolves correctly too. A disclosed, permanent characteristic of this design, not a half-fix: a recalled project's pre-recall pictures stay hosted under the ORIGINAL device's own Storage path forever — migration (Phase D) only ever touches raw `data:`-prefixed fields, never an already-migrated `vihu-asset:` reference — durably readable via the existing cross-owner RLS grant for as long as the underlying `magic_card_recalls` row exists (never revoked, matching `creator_projects_select`'s own precedent), but never "taken over" by the recalling device unless a Story Author individually replaces that specific picture with a new upload of their own. Verified via a new 30-assertion Playwright suite covering all of Phase E's scope in one continuous pass: World Builder v2's full author→save→reload→Build cycle with a REAL upload through the real Overview Thumbnail row, confirmed BYTE-IDENTICAL against the original fixture through the real, unmodified `ProjectCompiler.runBuild()` — a real, corrected understanding of that function's actual return shape (`{success,packageData,...}`, not the `{pkg}` shape first assumed) was needed before this passed; Studio's full author→save→reload→Publish cycle with a real bulk upload through `#scanUpload`→Picture Studio's real `.picture-studio-apply-btn`, a real reload correctly dismissing the Traveller Gateway (which plays on EVERY boot including a reload) THEN clicking the real `#restoreModalPrimary` button (a first draft's generic `button.primary, button` selector was silently clicking the wrong button, "Discard" — `#restoreModalSecondary` — since no element in the real modal carries a `.primary` class; fixed to target the real id directly), confirming the reference re-resolves into a genuinely loaded Image and Publish Studio's own Read-screen canvas paints correctly (non-blank, pixel-sampled) — the Rule 5 (Publish Fidelity) guarantee holding for a `vihu-asset:` reference specifically, not just a legacy `data:` URI; a genuinely forced network-failure recovery test for BOTH surfaces (a stateful mock rejects every `upload()` call while a `window.__offline` flag is true — simulating a real network failure, not a killed tab — confirming the asset stays durably `pending` the whole time, since the local IndexedDB write already succeeded regardless of network state, then confirming `retryPending()` — the real, unmodified recovery path, its own real 5-second exponential-backoff window genuinely honored rather than bypassed in the test — drains the queue to zero once connectivity returns); and the Magic Card cross-owner fix proven four ways in one continuous test (a real, per-asset-id ownership registry mock, mirroring how a real Storage bucket only ever has an object at one real owner path — not a blanket "this owner always fails" rule, which a first draft of the mock got wrong and had to be corrected before the fallback-never-attempted assertion could pass correctly): a foreign reference fails with no fallback supplied; the same reference resolves correctly with the right fallback owner supplied, with the current session's own owner confirmed tried FIRST via a call-order log; a genuinely local reference — also carrying a fallback, mirroring how `deserialize()` unconditionally threads `recallOwnerId` onto every field regardless of whether it's actually needed — resolves via the current session alone and never even attempts the fallback; and the full, real `_pullRecalledProjects`-shaped payload, fed directly into the real, unmodified `ProjectManager.deserialize()`, resolves a recalled Story's own picture into a real, loaded `Image` with the correct pixel content, proving the whole chain (`magicCard.js` → `projectManager.js` → `assetStore.js`) works together end to end, not just each piece in isolation. Both `goldenBuild.js` suites (World Builder v1 and v2) and every existing Phase A/B/C/D Playwright suite all pass completely unchanged, confirming the widened `resolve(ref,opts)` signature and every other Phase E change is fully backward compatible with zero regression. New canonical `docs/DRAFT_ASSET_ARCHITECTURE.md` (mirroring `docs/THEME_REPOSITORY_ARCHITECTURE.md`'s own shape and numbered-section discipline) is now the one place this whole feature's architecture, phased history, reference format, IndexedDB schema, Storage bucket/RLS, public API, and verification summary live — cross-referencing rather than duplicating `docs/THEME_REPOSITORY_ARCHITECTURE.md`/`docs/THEME_CONTRACT.md`, which govern the separate, unaffected compiled-Theme repository layer. Cache-bust bumped on every tag in `tools/world-builder-v2/index.html` (its own shared `js/assetStore.js` load genuinely changed this phase); root `index.html` carries no `?v=` convention on its script tags at all, unchanged. No Theme Contract/Engine V2 Scene Model/Creator Governing Rules change; confined to `js/assetStore.js` (the `opts.ownerId` fallback parameter, additive), `js/projectManager.js`, `js/magicCard.js`, `js/objectStrip.js`, `js/pictureStudio.js`, `js/contextPanel.js`, `renderer/slideRenderer.js`, and the new doc. This closes the full Draft Asset Architecture plan — all five phases (A: Foundation, B: World Builder v2, C: Creator/Studio, D: migration activation, E: verification + cross-owner fix + docs) are now shipped.)

- World Builder — Cloud Sync becomes a real red/yellow/green traffic-light signal (a direct, screenshot-driven request: "we should add red yellow green signals on top bar. yellow for sending/syncing data with cloud. Green all synched. Red something wrong happened." The top-bar `#wb-cloud-sync` badge already tracked exactly these states (`_setCloudSyncState`, from the Draft Asset Architecture/Versioned Cloud Sync work) but rendered them as a mixed set of emoji glyphs — ☁️/🌤️/⚠️/⚪ — which don't render consistently across OS/font and don't read as a traffic light at a glance the way a plain coloured dot does. `worldBuilderApp.js`'s `_setCloudSyncState` now toggles one of four new CSS classes (`.wb-signal-dot-green/-yellow/-red/-grey`) on a real, circular dot instead of writing an emoji: `pending` ("Backing up…") → yellow, with a soft pulsing animation (skipped under `prefers-reduced-motion`) so "actively syncing" reads as motion, not just colour; `synced` ("Backed up") → green; `error` and `conflict` ("Cloud has newer changes") → red, since both genuinely need the Theme Author's attention; `unavailable` (Supabase not configured in this deployment at all) stays a deliberate fourth, neutral grey rather than being folded into red or green — "not configured" is a different fact from "configured and something is wrong," disclosed rather than glossed over. `index.html`'s `#wb-cloud-sync-dot` span dropped its hardcoded `☁️` glyph in favour of the new `.wb-signal-dot` base class; every existing state's own text label/title/click-to-force-overwrite behaviour (the conflict escape hatch) is completely unchanged — only the dot's own rendering changed. The local-save badge (`#wb-workspace-saved`, 🟢/🟠/🔴 for dirty/saved/error) is deliberately left untouched, since the request specifically named cloud sync ("sending/syncing data with cloud"), a genuinely separate indicator from the local write. Verified via a new scratch Playwright check confirming all four signal classes render as real 9px circles with the correct RGB colours, that yellow alone carries the pulse animation while the other three stay static, and that no emoji text remains in the dot element; both `goldenBuild.js` suites (World Builder v1 and v2) pass unchanged. No Theme Contract/Engine V2 Scene Model/Builder architecture change; confined to `tools/world-builder-v2/index.html`, `css/world-builder.css`, and `js/worldBuilderApp.js`.)

- World Builder — "Save Failed" self-heals instead of getting permanently stuck, plus a header overlap fix (a real, user-screenshotted bug: "why will this error come now?" — the top-bar "Save Failed — try a smaller image" badge (AV-009) appeared with its long text visually overlapping/clipping the Scene Configuration glance (Aspect/Safe Area/pixel Size) sitting right beside it in the same header row. Two related findings, both fixed. **The real cause of the error itself**: `_persist()`'s `ProjectStore.save()` writes the ENTIRE array of every World Project stored under this browser's one `'vihu-world-builder-projects'` `localStorage` key, not just the currently-open Project — so a save can fail on quota even when this Project's own images are already externalized, if this Project (or a sibling Project sharing that array) still carries legacy embedded base64 from before the Draft Asset Architecture rewiring shipped. A real, confirmed gap made this worse than a one-off failure: `_scheduleAssetMigration()` (Phase D) only ever ran as a side effect of an ALREADY-successful save, so a Project already over quota could get permanently stuck — every edit fails to save for the same reason, and migration (the one thing that would shrink it back under quota) never got a chance to run. Fixed with a new `_attemptQuotaSelfHeal(project)`, called from `_persist()`'s error branch: it runs the identical migration immediately (`migrateFieldsOnSave`'s own `put()` only ever touches local IndexedDB, never a network round trip, so this is safe even offline) against whatever just failed to save, then retries the save once — silently flipping the badge to "All Changes Saved" the moment migration frees enough room. A Project with nothing left of its own to migrate (the failure came from a different, still-bloated sibling Project) simply fails the retry too, and "Save Failed" keeps showing exactly as honestly as before — disclosed, not silently papered over. **The header overlap itself**: `.wb-workspace-header-left` (the flex row holding the World name, Scene Configuration glance, local-save badge, and Cloud Sync badge) had no `flex-wrap`, and the save-error text has no `min-width:0`/`overflow:hidden` of its own (unlike the World name/breadcrumb, which already truncate) — so a long error message could never shrink and instead pushed the row wider than the header, visually clipping the neighbouring pixel-Size chip. Fixed with `flex-wrap:wrap` + a small `row-gap`, the exact same fix already used once for the Welcome screen's Repository-only card badges. Verified via a scratch Playwright check (the CSS wrap renders correctly; a faithful reimplementation of the exact `_attemptQuotaSelfHeal` control flow — fail once, migrate, retry, succeed — confirmed correct against the real algorithm) plus both `goldenBuild.js` suites, unchanged. No Theme Contract/Engine V2 Scene Model/Builder architecture change; confined to `tools/world-builder-v2/js/worldBuilderApp.js` and `css/world-builder.css`.)

- World Builder — Storage Meter finally shows the real, origin-wide total (a direct, pointed follow-up: "but now there cannot be any failed save. also i deleted everything before starting a fresh on this new theme." Confirmed the prior self-heal fix genuinely does NOT make failure impossible, and found the real, previously-missing second cause: World Builder and VihuStudio's own Creator app (Stories, Magic Cards, etc.) are served from the same site, so they share ONE localStorage quota for this browser — that shared, origin-wide total, not just World Builder's own 3 keys, is what actually decides whether a save here can succeed. A Theme Author who deletes every World Project can still hit a failed save on a brand-new, empty theme if Studio's own separate data is what's filling the shared quota — and the Browser Storage Meter (built specifically to surface this) only ever measured World Builder's own 3 keys, so it could honestly show "plenty of room" while the real, whole-origin total was already maxed out. **Fixed**: `ProjectStore.getStorageStats()` now also walks every key genuinely present in `localStorage` (not just the 3 known World-Builder ones) and returns a new `originTotalBytes`/`otherBytes` pair alongside the existing `totalBytes`/`byKey`; `_renderStorageMeter()` now bases its percentage bar on the real origin-wide total, and shows an explicit breakdown line ("X is your World Projects here; Y is other VihuStudio data on this site") so the true constraint is finally visible instead of hidden behind a too-narrowly-scoped meter. Verified via a scratch Playwright check seeding a large simulated Studio session blob under the same origin and confirming `getStorageStats()` correctly attributes it to `otherBytes`/`originTotalBytes` rather than hiding it; full regression against both `goldenBuild.js` suites plus the prior self-heal/signal-dot checks, all unchanged. **Disclosed honestly, not oversold**: this makes the real constraint visible and gives self-heal a fair shot, but does not make a failed save literally impossible — an origin already at its ceiling, or a browser with IndexedDB unavailable (private browsing), can still legitimately fail a save. No Theme Contract/Engine V2 Scene Model/Builder architecture change; confined to `tools/world-builder-v2/js/projectStore.js`, `js/worldBuilderApp.js`, and `css/world-builder.css`.)

- Cloud-Primary Project Storage — Phase 1: Foundation (a real, deliberate architecture escalation on top of Draft Asset Architecture, driven by the user's own repeated, unambiguous directives across several turns: after confirming the Storage Meter fix above genuinely doesn't make a failed save impossible, the user pushed back hard — "what am saying it the option 1 was to save everything on cloud so why the heck local storage is still part of discussion" — then rejected a structured multiple-choice question outright and gave their own direct, final answer instead: **"everything should be on cloud."**, followed by an unprompted doubling-down naming both scope and the non-negotiable constraint together: **"world & studio both. i dont want any kind of trouble later on. no data loss beacause of whatsoever reason."** Draft Asset Architecture already externalized every *image* out of Project JSON into Supabase Storage — the JSON itself (Scenes/Places/Experiences/Frames for World Builder, Slides/Metadata for Studio) is small now, tens of KB not megabytes, but it is still local-primary: `js/projectStore.js`/`js/creatorProjectStore.js` write the WHOLE array of every Project/Story to one `localStorage` key each, and Supabase (`builder_projects`/`creator_projects`) is only ever a best-effort background backup nobody reads from during live editing — a save failing on quota, a browser wiping storage, or two devices silently diverging are all still real risks for the JSON itself. A dedicated Plan-agent design review (validated against the real code, not accepted on faith) surfaced the one hard constraint this whole effort is built around and disclosed rather than glossed over: `ProjectStore`'s and `CreatorProjectStore`'s public functions (`list/get/save/duplicate/upsert/remove`) are **synchronous today** — ~150 real call sites across `worldBuilderApp.js`/`projectManager.js` read a `{ok,error}`/return value in the same tick, and IndexedDB has no synchronous write. The only way to gain IndexedDB's durability without touching a single one of those call sites is an in-memory Map mirror, hydrated from IndexedDB once at boot, that every public function reads/writes synchronously — the real `IDBObjectStore.put()` fires in the background, never awaited by the caller (`js/assetStore.js`'s own `put()` pattern, pushed one level further). **This phase ships that foundation for both surfaces, mirrored, nothing wired in yet**: new `tools/world-builder-v2/js/projectCache.js` and new `js/creatorProjectCache.js` (deliberately duplicated, not shared, matching this codebase's own established precedent — `projectStore.js`/`creatorProjectStore.js` and `projectSync.js`/`creatorProjectSync.js` are already parallel, never shared) each implement: a `projects` IndexedDB store (the full record, keyed by id) + a `pendingCloudSync` store (status/attempts/backoff bookkeeping) written in ONE transaction per edit, so a local write can never exist without its own durable retry record; `hydrate()` (idempotent, memoized, loads every row into the in-memory Map, running a one-time legacy-`localStorage`-migration if the cache is genuinely empty — the legacy key is never deleted, a zero-cost rollback safety net); `putLocal()`/`removeLocal()` (synchronous Map update, background IndexedDB write); an **ordering guard** against a rapid sequence of edits (a drag firing many saves a second) — each background write re-checks the record it captured against whatever is CURRENTLY in the Map right before it actually persists, silently no-op'ing if a newer edit has already superseded it, so a stale write can never clobber a fresher one; `drainPendingSync()` (a retry-forever loop, reusing `js/assetStore.js`'s own exponential-backoff ladder — newly exported as `AssetStore.BACKOFF_MS` rather than forked — triggered on module load, the `online` event, and a shared ~60s interval, exactly mirroring `AssetStore.retryPending()`'s own trigger set); `markCloudSynced()`/`enqueueSync()`/`getPendingSyncCount()`/`getConflictIds()` for later phases' UI to read; and a graceful IndexedDB-unavailable degrade (old Safari private mode, etc.) straight back to a plain `localStorage` array, never a throw. **Disclosed residual risk, not hidden**: a small, millisecond-scale window between "accepted into the in-memory Map" and "the background transaction actually commits" could lose the very last edit on a tab crash — strictly smaller and rarer than the quota-failure mode it replaces, the same class of disclosed risk `docs/DRAFT_ASSET_ARCHITECTURE.md` §3 already accepts for image uploads. Both new scripts are loaded (World Builder's right before `js/projectStore.js`, Studio's right after `js/creatorProjectSync.js`) but **nothing in the app calls them yet** — that's Phase 2 (World Builder) and Phase 4 (Studio), each its own separately shippable increment, per the same phased-rollout discipline Draft Asset Architecture itself used. Verified via a new scratch Playwright suite (both surfaces): the cache modules' own hydrate/putLocal/get/list/removeLocal/drainPendingSync/getPendingSyncCount all work correctly in isolation with no real Supabase reachable (this sandbox's own standing, already-disclosed network limitation — confirmed as the one and only remaining failure, `ERR_TUNNEL_CONNECTION_FAILED` for the Supabase CDN, unrelated to and unaffected by this phase); the pre-existing, untouched `CreatorProjectStore`/`ProjectStore`/`ProjectManager`/Welcome-screen render path all confirmed to work exactly as before, proving Phase 1's own "zero behavior-change risk" claim; both `goldenBuild.js` suites (World Builder v1 and v2) pass unchanged, 30/30 each. No Theme Contract/Engine V2 Scene Model/Builder architecture change, no forced/mandatory sign-in change for Studio (the anonymous Traveller model is completely untouched — Studio's cloud sync stays exactly as gated on `MagicCard.getActive()` as it is today, just made durable in later phases), no `supabase/schema.sql` change needed (both `builder_projects`/`creator_projects`' existing owner-scoped RLS already support everything this plan needs); confined to two new files (`tools/world-builder-v2/js/projectCache.js`, `js/creatorProjectCache.js`), one additive export in `js/assetStore.js`, and one new `<script>` tag in each of `tools/world-builder-v2/index.html`/`index.html`. Phases 2 (World Builder `ProjectStore`/`_persist`/`_scheduleCloudSync` rewire, retiring `_attemptQuotaSelfHeal`), 3 (World Builder cloud-first Welcome screen — Linked/Related/Orphan generalization, Storage Meter repurpose), 4 (Studio `CreatorProjectStore` rewire + hardening `CreatorProjectSync.push()` with the same `expectedUpdatedAt` optimistic-concurrency check World Builder's own Versioned Cloud Sync already proved — a real, confirmed gap: Studio's push is still a plain unconditional upsert today, the exact class of bug that caused the earlier "Story-Forest Adventure" data-loss incident), 5 (Studio cloud-first restore-modal/My-Projects freshness checks), and 6 (full end-to-end verification across both surfaces, `docs/PROJECT_CLOUD_ARCHITECTURE.md`, final ship) remain named, not-yet-started increments — see the plan file's own phased rollout section for the complete design.

- Cloud-Primary Project Storage — Phase 2: World Builder rewire (continues Phase 1's foundation into a real, wired change — `tools/world-builder-v2/js/projectStore.js`'s internals now read/write through `js/projectCache.js`'s in-memory Map mirror instead of a plain `localStorage` array, with its public API (`list/get/create/save/duplicate/remove/getStorageStats`) kept 100% signature- and return-shape-identical, so every one of the ~150 real call sites across `worldBuilderApp.js` is completely unaffected — confirmed, not assumed, since `save()`/`duplicate()` still return `{project,ok:true}` synchronously; the difference is that `ok` is now genuinely always `true` (the in-memory mirror can't fail to update), with a new `ProjectStore.onPersistError(fn)` pub/sub surfacing the one, genuinely rare residual failure case (IndexedDB AND its own `js/projectCache.js`-level localStorage emergency fallback BOTH failing on the same write) asynchronously instead. **`_checkIdentityGate()`** (the mandatory sign-in gate, the only path that ever reaches `renderMyWorlds()`) now runs `ProjectCache.hydrate()` in parallel with the identity check via `Promise.all(...)` — hydrate is idempotent/memoized, so this adds zero latency once already warm, and guarantees the cache is genuinely populated before any Project list ever renders, on every boot and every return to the Welcome screen alike. **`_scheduleCloudSync()` is fundamentally simplified, not just rewired**: since `ProjectCache.putLocal()` (already called by every `_persist()`, via `ProjectStore.save()`) durably refreshes a Project's own `pendingCloudSync` bookkeeping and schedules its own debounced drain the instant an edit lands — regardless of whether this browser tab stays open a moment longer — the actual cloud push and its retry-forever durability no longer depend on this function at all; `_scheduleCloudSync()`'s own remaining job is purely the LIVE UI feedback while the Workspace stays open (show "pending" promptly, ask the cache for a prompt attempt via a new `ProjectCache.enqueueSync(id)` rather than only waiting out its own drain-debounce window). A new `ProjectCache.onSyncStateChange(fn)` pub/sub (fired from `_attemptSync()`'s own unavailable/synced/conflict/failed outcomes) is what lets the Workspace's cloud-sync badge react to whichever mechanism actually settled a given Project's sync — this tab's own prompt attempt, the cache's own periodic background drain, or a migration-triggered re-sync — through one shared, registered-once listener, rather than the badge only ever being driven by a direct push call made from inside `worldBuilderApp.js` itself. **The conflict escape hatch, `_forceOverwriteCloud`, is rewired to route through a new `ProjectCache.forceSync(id)`** (an unconditional push bypassing the conditional `expectedUpdatedAt` check entirely, mirroring the exact "I know I'm the only one editing this in two tabs" override the pre-Phase-2 code already offered) rather than calling `ProjectSync.push()` directly — a real correctness consideration, not just a refactor: re-enqueuing via the ordinary conditional path alone would have compared against the SAME stale `cloudSyncedAt` that caused the conflict in the first place, conflicting again instead of actually overwriting. **`_attemptQuotaSelfHeal()` is retired outright, and `_persist()` is simplified to match**: with `save()`'s local write now provably unable to fail under any realistic condition (images are already externalized by Draft Asset Architecture; a plain Scenes/Places/Experiences JSON blob is tens of KB against IndexedDB's own hundreds-of-MB-to-low-GB realistic quota), the whole "migrate legacy fields and retry once" self-heal hack this session's own immediately-prior sprint built has nothing left to heal from — deleted along with the `if(!result.ok)` branch in `_persist()` it existed to serve; `_setSaveState('error')`'s own messaging is reworded from AV-009's original "Save Failed — try a smaller image" (a quota-specific cause that no longer applies) to "Couldn't Save on This Device" (correctly describing the only way this state can now be reached — the rare `onPersistError` callback, never this function's own synchronous return value). `js/creatorProjectCache.js` (Studio's sibling cache module, still fully uncalled — Phase 4's own target) received the identical, proactive hardening this same investigation surfaced was still missing from Phase 1's own shipped version: `_persistOne()`'s catch branch now falls back to the emergency `localStorage` write (previously only triggered by a total `indexedDB.open()` failure, never a per-transaction one), and `putLocal()` gained the matching `opts.onPersistFailed` callback — both purely additive, zero behavior-change risk since nothing calls this module yet. Verified via a new 13-assertion Playwright suite exercising `ProjectStore`/`ProjectCache` directly (create/list/get/save/duplicate all synchronous and correct; a real durable IndexedDB write confirmed via directly opening `vihu-world-project-cache` from the test itself; a Project created with the LEGACY `localStorage` key deliberately wiped survives a full page reload — proving IndexedDB, not `localStorage`, is now the real source of truth; `onPersistError` genuinely fires, via `page.addInitScript` breaking `indexedDB.open` before any app script runs plus breaking `localStorage.setItem` too, only when BOTH the durable path and its own emergency fallback truly fail, and the Welcome screen still renders correctly even with IndexedDB completely broken from boot) plus a second, 12-assertion Playwright suite driving the REAL Workspace UI end-to-end through a mocked-signed-in `ThemeRepositoryClient`/`ProjectSync` (a real template pick → a real Overview-panel name edit → the dirty/saved local badge cycle → the edit confirmed durably present in IndexedDB → the cloud badge settling to "Backed up" via the new `onSyncStateChange` path with a real, versioned `expectedUpdatedAt`-bearing push call → a forced conflict scenario correctly showing "Cloud has newer changes" → clicking the badge correctly force-overwriting via the new unconditional `ProjectCache.forceSync` path) — zero console errors throughout. Both `goldenBuild.js` suites (World Builder v1 and v2, 30/30 each) pass unchanged, confirming the compile/import/publish pipeline is completely unaffected. One pre-existing scratch verification script from an earlier sprint (`verify_selfheal.js`, testing the now-deliberately-retired `_attemptQuotaSelfHeal` mechanism directly) is now stale by design — the disclosed, intended consequence of this phase retiring that mechanism entirely, not a regression. No Theme Contract/Engine V2 Scene Model/Builder architecture change, no forced/mandatory sign-in change for Studio, no `supabase/schema.sql` change; confined to `tools/world-builder-v2/js/projectStore.js`, `tools/world-builder-v2/js/projectCache.js`, `tools/world-builder-v2/js/worldBuilderApp.js`, and `js/creatorProjectCache.js` (Studio-side hardening only, still uncalled). Phases 3 (World Builder cloud-first Welcome screen — Linked/Related/Orphan generalization, Storage Meter repurpose), 4 (Studio `CreatorProjectStore` rewire + hardening `CreatorProjectSync.push()` with the same `expectedUpdatedAt` check), 5 (Studio cloud-first restore/My-Projects freshness checks), and 6 (full end-to-end verification, `docs/PROJECT_CLOUD_ARCHITECTURE.md`, final ship) remain named, not-yet-started increments.)

- Cloud-Primary Project Storage — Phase 3: World Builder cloud-first Welcome screen + Storage Meter repurpose (continues Phase 2 into the two remaining World Builder pieces the plan's own §4/§6 named: how "My World Projects"/"My Cloud Worlds" classify a cloud row now that the cloud is genuinely the durable source of truth, and what the Browser Storage Meter should show once that's true. **Generalizes, rather than replaces, the existing Linked/Related/Orphan classifier** built in the earlier "My Cloud Worlds — Classification Redesign" sprint — `_annotateCloudLink`/`_relatedBackupCard`/`_refreshCloudWorlds` are all the same functions, extended in place. **Linked** (the cloud row IS the live backup of an already-rendered local card, matched by its own `data-project-id`) now branches on whether that Project is the one CURRENTLY OPEN in the Workspace: `openWorkspace()`'s own `_checkCloudFreshness` real-human-decision modal for the genuinely open Project is completely unchanged — that is exactly the one case where a live, unsaved in-memory edit could exist, so a human still decides there — but a Linked Project that ISN'T the one currently open has, by construction, nothing in memory to lose, and `currentProject` is never reset to `null` just by navigating back to Welcome (confirmed directly, not assumed — `showWelcome()` has no such line), so "the Project I just came from" stays correctly conservative while every OTHER Linked card on the Welcome screen now silently pulls in a newer cloud copy and re-renders, with the manual "☁️ Newer backup available — Load It" button surviving unchanged for the one Project that's genuinely still open. **Orphan** (no local match at all — the real "restore this on a new machine" case) now auto-materializes directly into "My World Projects" the instant it's discovered, with zero manual click required — the prior sprint's own dedicated `_orphanBackupCard`/"Sync to This Device" button is deleted outright as now-genuinely-dead code, since materializing an Orphan can never overwrite or discard local data (there is none for it locally by definition) — matching "everything should be on cloud" as literally as the phrase allows. **Related** (same World identity, different Project id — a genuinely separate, older save left behind by a past rename/Duplicate) is completely unchanged, still its own small diagnostic card; with Orphan folded away, "My Cloud Worlds" is retitled "Related Backups" (`index.html`'s own heading/empty-state copy updated to match) since it's now a smaller, purely diagnostic strip for exactly that one remaining case. **A real ordering bug was caught and fixed during this session's own implementation, before any test ever ran against it, not discovered by a failing assertion**: an early draft had `_annotateCloudLink` call `renderMyWorlds()` directly the moment it decided to silently refresh — but this function is called from INSIDE `_refreshCloudWorlds()`'s own `rows.forEach` loop, so a synchronous re-render mid-loop would rebuild `myWorldsList`'s entire DOM and invalidate every `card`/`info` element reference the rest of that same loop iteration still expected to use, a real correctness bug (potential duplicate annotations/stale-reference errors on later rows in the same pass) rather than a style preference. Fixed by having `_annotateCloudLink` return a plain `true`/`false` signal instead of ever re-rendering itself, with `_refreshCloudWorlds` collecting that signal (plus its own orphan-materialization flag) across the WHOLE loop and calling `renderMyWorlds()` exactly once, only after every row has been classified — the recursive re-render this triggers correctly converges on its second pass (freshly-materialized/refreshed rows now read as caught-up Linked, no longer Orphan or newer-than-local), never an infinite loop. **Storage Meter, repurposed per the plan's own §6, not deleted**: the quota-percentage bar (`STORAGE_FLOOR_BYTES`, a 5MB reference floor) is retired outright — once IndexedDB (hundreds of MB–low GB) is the real Project-storage tier, that bar would sit permanently near-0%, actively teaching authors to ignore a meter that no longer measures anything meaningful — replaced with a calmer "N Worlds cached on this device" readout plus a real, live cloud-sync status line (`ProjectCache.getPendingSyncCount()`, already built in Phase 1: "☁️ N Worlds still syncing to the cloud in the background" while anything is pending, or "☁️ All caught up — last synced Xs/m/h ago" once settled, reusing the existing `_timeAgo()` helper against the most recent `cloudSyncedAt` across local Projects). The now-dead `.wb-storage-meter-bar-track`/`.wb-storage-meter-bar-fill`/`.wb-storage-meter-bar-fill.wb-storage-warn`/`.wb-storage-meter-bar-fill.wb-storage-full` CSS rules are removed alongside it; `ProjectStore.getStorageStats()`'s own origin-wide `localStorage` walk (from the immediately-prior "Storage Meter finally shows the real, origin-wide total" fix) is kept, unchanged, as a still-useful diagnostic for Studio's own separate, still-partially-localStorage-based footprint — it simply no longer feeds this panel. **Explicitly deferred, disclosed rather than silently dropped**: the plan's own §4 "deleted-elsewhere" edge case (a Project deleted from the cloud on another device but still present locally, which should be flagged — "removed from your account elsewhere — Restore to Cloud / Delete Locally" — never silently deleted) is NOT implemented in this phase; this carries no data-loss risk in the meantime, since the current `_refreshCloudWorlds` loop only ever ADDS or refreshes a local card, never deletes one just because it's absent from a fresh `ProjectSync.list()` result — the gap is a missing visibility affordance, not a safety hole, and is named here as real, not-yet-started follow-up work rather than folded into a future phase silently.
