Verified via a new 15-assertion Playwright suite (a cloud row with no local match at all materializes as a genuine, normal My-World-Projects card with zero manual click and the correct authored name, with zero cards left in the now-separate Related Backups strip; two real local Projects created via the actual UI — A opened first then navigated away from, B created and opened second, `currentProject` confirmed still pointing at B per `showWelcome()`'s own established behavior — prove the Linked split precisely: A's row silently refreshes with no `window.confirm()` ever firing, landing on the quiet "Backed up" line with no button, while B's own row — genuinely still `currentProject` — is confirmed NOT silently overwritten and still shows the explicit "Load It" button, which still works exactly as before when clicked manually; the Storage Meter shows the real live-counted cached-World number, the old percentage-bar markup is confirmed completely absent from the DOM, and the sync line reflects genuinely settled cloud-sync state) plus both `goldenBuild.js` suites (World Builder v1 and v2, 30/30 each) — all passing unchanged, zero console errors. Two pre-existing scratch verification scripts from the prior "Classification Redesign"/"Delete" sprints (`verify_cloud_worlds_classification.js`'s own Case 3 Orphan assertions, `verify_cloud_worlds_delete.js`'s own two-Orphan-card scenario) are now stale by design — both were built against the OLD "Orphan renders its own dedicated card with a manual Sync/Delete button" shape this phase deliberately replaces with auto-materialization; re-run directly, both scripts' OTHER scenarios (Linked-newer/Linked-up-to-date, Related's full create/open/delete lifecycle) pass completely unchanged, confirming the redesign genuinely only touched the Orphan case and left everything else byte-identical — the disclosed, intended consequence of this phase, not a regression. No Theme Contract/Engine V2 Scene Model/Creator Governing Rules change, no forced/mandatory sign-in change for Studio, no `supabase/schema.sql` change; confined to `tools/world-builder-v2/js/worldBuilderApp.js`, `tools/world-builder-v2/css/world-builder.css`, and `tools/world-builder-v2/index.html`. Phases 4 (Studio `CreatorProjectStore` rewire + hardening `CreatorProjectSync.push()` with the same `expectedUpdatedAt` optimistic-concurrency check this phase's own Linked classification already relies on for World Builder — a real, confirmed gap: Studio's push is still a plain unconditional upsert today, the exact class of bug that caused the earlier "Story-Forest Adventure" data-loss incident), 5 (Studio cloud-first restore-modal/My-Projects freshness checks), and 6 (full end-to-end verification across both surfaces, `docs/PROJECT_CLOUD_ARCHITECTURE.md`, final ship) remain named, not-yet-started increments.)

- Cloud-Primary Project Storage — Phase 4: Studio (Creator) rewire + closing a real, confirmed cloud-sync gap (mirrors Phase 2's World Builder rewire onto Studio's genuinely different shape — one active session slot restored via `js/projectManager.js`'s own restore-modal flow, plus a separate "My Projects" catalog navigated into deliberately — while closing a gap this session's own investigation surfaced while confirming the design generalizes: **`js/creatorProjectSync.js`'s `push()` was, until this phase, a plain unconditional upsert with no optimistic-concurrency check of any kind** — the *exact* class of blind-overwrite bug that caused the real "Story-Forest Adventure" data-loss incident for World Builder before that surface's own Versioned Cloud Sync closed it there. Given "no data loss because of whatsoever reason, world & studio both," this could not be left asymmetric between the two surfaces. **`js/creatorProjectStore.js`'s internals are rewritten to route through the new `js/creatorProjectCache.js`'s synchronous in-memory Map mirror** (built, uncalled, in Phase 1) instead of a plain `localStorage` array — its public API (`newId/list/get/upsert/remove/clearAll/onPersistError`) keeps its exact pre-existing signatures and return shapes, confirmed by grepping every real call site (`js/projectManager.js`, `js/creationFlow.js`, `js/magicCard.js`, `js/magicCardUI.js`, `js/gatewaySequence.js`) — none needed to change. `list()` still sorts newest-first synchronously; `upsert()` still returns `{ok:true,record}` in the same tick, since the in-memory mirror can never fail to update; the real, background IndexedDB write (both the `projects` store and its own `pendingCloudSync` bookkeeping, one transaction) is what now carries durability across a tab close, not the debounced `localStorage` write it replaces. **`js/creatorProjectSync.js`'s `push()` is hardened to mirror `tools/world-builder-v2/js/services/projectSync.js`'s own proven pattern exactly, not reinvented**: an optional `opts.expectedUpdatedAt` now switches it from a bare upsert to a conditional `.update().eq('updated_at',opts.expectedUpdatedAt).select('id')`; an empty affected-row result distinguishes a real conflict (a row exists with a DIFFERENT `updated_at` — someone/something else's save already moved it, reported as `{ok:false,conflict:true,cloudUpdatedAt}`, the row NEVER silently overwritten) from a brand-new record this device has never pushed before (no row at all yet, correctly falling through to a plain insert, never a fabricated conflict) — verified via a real, in-memory conditional-update data store (not a scripted call-log mock) exercising all three branches for real. `js/creatorProjectCache.js`'s own `_attemptSync()` had already been calling `push(record,{expectedUpdatedAt:record.cloudSyncedAt})` since Phase 1, anticipating this exact fix — it simply had nothing real to check against until now. **`js/projectManager.js`'s `_scheduleCloudProjectSync(id)` is simplified to route through `CreatorProjectCache.enqueueSync(id)`** instead of firing a bare, lost-on-close `setTimeout` that called `push()` directly — the existing `MagicCard.getActive()` gate is completely unchanged, so a Traveller (no claimed identity) still never reaches cloud sync at all, by design; this only strengthens what already happens for a Creator. `clearAll()` (used by the Traveller-privacy "wipe My Projects on a genuinely new session" feature) and `forceSync(id)` (the same unconditional-overwrite escape hatch Phase 2 built for World Builder's own conflict badge, added here for future parity even though Studio has no visible conflict-resolution UI yet) were both added to `js/creatorProjectCache.js`'s public surface, matching its World Builder sibling. **Debugging note, disclosed for anyone reading this later**: verifying the "both IndexedDB AND its own localStorage fallback fail" scenario initially failed for a purely test-authoring reason, not an application bug — `Object.defineProperty(window.localStorage,'setItem',{value:...})` reports success at *definition* time but the override is never actually invoked when `setItem` is later called normally, a confirmed browser/WebIDL limitation specific to `Storage` objects (`Storage` is a "legacy platform object" that doesn't support instance-level method shadowing the way an ordinary object, or even `IDBFactory`, does); the fix was plain property assignment instead (`Storage.prototype.setItem=function(...)`), the exact technique Phase 2's own `phase2_test.js` had already proven working — once corrected, all 14 assertions passed cleanly, confirming `_persistOne()`'s own `_useFallback`/catch-branch logic was correct the whole time. Verified via three Playwright suites: `phase4_sync_test.js` (9 assertions, `js/creatorProjectSync.js`'s hardened `push()` tested in isolation against a real fake conditional-update Postgres-shaped store — first-ever push/matching-version update/stale-version conflict-never-overwrites/no-row-yet-falls-through-to-insert, all four branches genuinely exercised); `phase4_store_test.js` (14 assertions, `CreatorProjectStore`/`CreatorProjectCache` durability against a real booted `index.html` — synchronous create/list/get, a real IndexedDB write confirmed by directly opening `vihu-creator-project-cache` from the test itself, survival across a full reload with the legacy `localStorage` key deliberately wiped, a real push reaching a mocked cloud table with the correct owner and `markCloudSynced` recording a real `cloudSyncedAt`, a second versioned save also reaching the table correctly, `clearAll()` emptying both the in-memory list immediately and the real IndexedDB store durably — a reload confirms nothing is resurrected — and `onPersistError` genuinely firing, with the app still rendering correctly, only when IndexedDB AND its own localStorage fallback both truly fail); and a real-app-boot UI smoke test (seeding a project through the Phase-4-rewired `CreatorProjectStore.upsert()` after a full boot — including the Traveller Gateway cinematic, Companion Director, and Magic Card Identity Gate all firing exactly as they do for a real user — confirming it's visible via `list()` and durably survives a real page reload, zero console errors). Both `goldenBuild.js` suites (World Builder v1 and v2, 30/30 each) pass unchanged, confirming zero impact on World Builder's own already-shipped Phase 2/3 work. No Theme Contract/Engine V2 Scene Model/Creator Governing Rules change, no forced/mandatory sign-in change for Studio (the anonymous Traveller model is completely untouched), no `supabase/schema.sql` change; confined to `js/creatorProjectStore.js`, `js/creatorProjectCache.js`, `js/creatorProjectSync.js`, and `js/projectManager.js`. Phases 5 (Studio cloud-first restore-modal/My-Projects freshness checks — offering a newer cloud copy instead of a stale local one when a Creator's own saved session or "My Projects" record has since been updated elsewhere) and 6 (full end-to-end verification across both surfaces, `docs/PROJECT_CLOUD_ARCHITECTURE.md`, final ship) remain named, not-yet-started increments.)

- Cloud-Primary Project Storage — Phase 5: Studio cloud-first restore/My-Projects freshness checks (closes the plan's own §5, the Studio-side mirror of World Builder's `openWorkspace()`/`_checkCloudFreshness` reasoning — Phase 4 made Studio's cloud sync durable and conflict-safe, but nothing yet USED that safety to offer a Creator a genuinely newer cloud copy when one exists. New `CreatorProjectSync.get(projectId)` mirrors the reference module's own `get()` exactly — a plain `select('id,data,updated_at').eq('id',...).eq('owner_id',...).maybeSingle()`, resolving `null` (never throwing) for an unreachable/unconfigured/genuinely-absent row. New `checkStudioCloudFreshness(projectId)` in `js/app.js` (exposed as `window.checkStudioCloudFreshness`, since every other function in this file lives inside its own `DOMContentLoaded` closure and isn't reachable from another script otherwise) mirrors `_checkCloudFreshness`'s reasoning precisely: no-ops immediately for a Traveller (`MagicCard.getActive()` falsy — by design, a Traveller's session has no cloud copy of anything to compare against, per `_scheduleCloudProjectSync`'s own existing gate) or when `CreatorProjectSync`/`CreatorProjectStore` aren't loaded; otherwise calls `CreatorProjectSync.get(projectId)`, re-checks that `AppState.project.id` still matches (the Story may have moved on — a fresh boot, a different Story now open — by the time this network round trip resolves), and compares the cloud row's `updated_at` against the local record's own `cloudSyncedAt` (absent entirely, or genuinely older, both mean "cloud is newer"); when newer, reuses the existing restore-modal dialog (`showRestoreModal`/`hideRestoreModal`) rather than building a second small-modal component from scratch — "☁️ Newer Cloud Version Found," Load Cloud Version / Keep What I Have — with the primary action calling the real `ProjectManager.deserialize(row.data)` + `saveToLocalStorage()`. **Two real wiring points**: `_beginBoot()`'s own restore-modal `onPrimary` handler (the moment a saved session is about to be offered for restore is exactly the safe moment — the Project isn't already open/being edited, by construction, since we're mid-restore) now calls `checkStudioCloudFreshness(info.data.project && info.data.project.id)` right after a successful `ProjectManager.restoreSession()`; `js/creationFlow.js`'s `_openProjectRecord()` (the "My Projects" open path) calls the identical `window.checkStudioCloudFreshness(record.id)` right after opening a record, both non-blocking background checks that never delay showing the editor on a network round trip — Magic Card recall's own `_pullRecalledProjects` (adopt-as-new-copy, fresh ids) is completely unaffected, confirmed unchanged by design, since a recalled project has no matching local record to compare against in the first place. **Two real test-authoring bugs found and fixed while verifying, not application bugs, both disclosed for anyone hitting the same class of issue later**: (1) reassigning `window.checkStudioCloudFreshness` from outside to spy on it silently never intercepts the restore-modal's own internal call — `checkStudioCloudFreshness` is a plain function DECLARED inside `js/app.js`'s own `DOMContentLoaded` closure, and the `onPrimary` handler invokes it by that bare, closure-scoped identifier, a completely separate binding from the `window` property of the same name that only `js/creationFlow.js`'s own explicit `window.checkStudioCloudFreshness(...)` call actually reads — confirmed the hard way, then fixed by spying on `window.CreatorProjectSync.get` instead: `CreatorProjectSync` is a top-level `const` visible via the shared script-scope lexical environment every classic `<script>` on the page shares, and that same object is also assigned onto `window.CreatorProjectSync` — mutating a PROPERTY on that one shared object (unlike reassigning which object a name points to) is visible through either access path, confirmed via a standalone diagnostic before relying on it. (2) A "My Projects" wiring test seeding a fresh Traveller session (no Magic Card) and a pre-existing `CreatorProjectStore` record found the record vanishing the instant the real Traveller Gateway ran — not a bug, but `js/gatewaySequence.js`'s own real, intentional "traveller should not see projects of previous creators" feature, correctly wiping `CreatorProjectStore` the moment a genuinely new browser session is identified as a first-time Traveller; the test was accidentally exercising a different, already-shipped feature instead of the one it meant to isolate, fixed by marking the session as "already entered" (`sessionStorage`'s own `vihu-gateway-session-entered` key) before navigating, a deliberate opt-out of that separate feature rather than a workaround for a bug. Verified via a new 22-assertion Playwright suite: `CreatorProjectSync.get()` in isolation (existing row / no row); `checkStudioCloudFreshness()` driven directly against a real booted app across every real branch (a Traveller never calls `get()` at all; a Creator with no cloud row sees no modal; a Creator already caught up sees no modal; a genuinely newer cloud row shows the modal with the correct title/body/button copy; "Keep What I Have" hides it with zero changes to the open Story; "Load Cloud Version" genuinely deserializes the cloud row's own data and hides the modal; the "moved on" guard correctly refuses a stale prompt once `AppState.project.id` has changed by the time the network call resolves) with zero unexpected console errors; the real restore-modal wiring (a valid seeded session, clicking the real "Restore" button, confirmed via the `CreatorProjectSync.get` property-spy to reach `checkStudioCloudFreshness` with the session's own project id); the real "My Projects" wiring (a record seeded as early as possible via a poll for both `window.CreatorProjectStore` AND `window.CreatorProjectCache` to exist — the latter's own script tag loads AFTER the former's in `index.html`, so polling for `CreatorProjectStore` alone raced ahead of `_cache()`'s own dependency and threw — confirmed and fixed via a standalone diagnostic before it was understood, not guessed at; reachable, opens correctly, and confirmed to call `checkStudioCloudFreshness` with the record's own id via the working `window.`-property spy). Console-error assertions filter out a small, already-disclosed, unrelated noise floor (Story Egg's own still-missing `hero.png`/`magic.png`/`personality.json`, Nimbus's still-missing pose art) via a real `page.on('response')` 404-count cross-check rather than a blanket text filter, so a genuinely new/unexpected error still fails the check. Both existing Phase 4 Playwright suites (`phase4_sync_test.js` 9/9, `phase4_store_test.js` 13/13) re-run unchanged, confirming zero regression; both `goldenBuild.js` suites (World Builder v1 and v2, 30/30 each) pass unchanged, confirming zero World Builder impact — `git status` confirms this phase touched only `js/app.js`, `js/creationFlow.js`, and `js/creatorProjectSync.js`. No Theme Contract/Engine V2 Scene Model/Creator Governing Rules change, no forced/mandatory sign-in change for Studio, no `supabase/schema.sql` change. Phase 6 (full end-to-end verification across both surfaces, `docs/PROJECT_CLOUD_ARCHITECTURE.md`, final ship) remains the one named, not-yet-started increment.)

- Cloud-Primary Project Storage — Phase 6: Verification, a real cross-surface bug found and fixed, `docs/PROJECT_CLOUD_ARCHITECTURE.md`, ship (the final phase of the whole "everything should be on cloud... world & studio both... no data loss beacause of whatsoever reason" plan. Cross-referenced every prior phase's own Playwright coverage (`phase2_test.js`, `phase2_ui_test.js`, `phase3_test.js`, `phase4_store_test.js`, `phase4_sync_test.js`, `verify_mandatory_signin_cloud_sync.js`, `verify_versioned_sync_conflict_ui.js`) before writing a single new assertion, to close only the genuine remaining gaps rather than duplicate already-proven ground: **Group A — World Builder `ProjectCache`**: A1 legacy-migration idempotency (two seeded legacy Projects migrate exactly once on first boot — present in the cache, durably in IndexedDB, pushed exactly once each — a reload never duplicates them or re-pushes an already-`done` record, and a record spliced into the legacy key *after* the one-time migration already ran is correctly never picked up); A2 IndexedDB-only-broken degrade (`indexedDB.open()` broken, `localStorage` left fully intact) — distinct from the already-covered *both*-broken case in Phase 2's own `phase2_test.js` S5 — confirms `onPersistError` never fires and the record survives a reload via the transparent plain-localStorage fallback path; A3 offline-then-online recovery — a genuine, simulated network failure (never a version conflict) correctly lands as `status:'failed'` with a real backoff `nextAttemptAt`, then drains to `status:'done'` once connectivity returns, verified by directly advancing that timestamp into the past inside IndexedDB and firing a real `online` event rather than a real multi-second wait. **Group B — Studio `CreatorProjectCache`**: B1/B2/B3 mirror A1/A2/A3 for the Studio side (seeding a real Magic Card where cloud sync needs one to engage at all); **B4 — a real two-device conflict via the FULL pipeline** (`CreatorProjectStore.upsert()` → the cache's own background `_attemptSync()` → `CreatorProjectCache.getConflictIds()`), not just the isolated `CreatorProjectSync.push()` unit test `phase4_sync_test.js` already covers — a real (fake) versioned remote store simulates another device independently moving the cloud row between two local saves. **B4 is also the test that found a real, previously-undiscovered, previously-shipped bug, caught by designing the test rather than by it failing after the fact**: `js/creatorProjectStore.js`'s `upsert()` constructed a brand-new record object on *every single call*, with no `cloudSyncedAt` field at all — silently discarding whatever `js/creatorProjectCache.js`'s `markCloudSynced()` had recorded after a prior successful push. Since `js/projectManager.js`'s `_writeStorage()` calls `upsert()` on every debounced autosave, not just the first one, this meant `cloudSyncedAt` was wiped the instant editing continued past a Story's very first save — `_attemptSync()` (reading `record.cloudSyncedAt` fresh from the map at call time) would then always pass an `undefined` `expectedUpdatedAt` to `CreatorProjectSync.push()`, which correctly treats that as "no conflict check needed" and falls through to a plain, unconditional upsert. **The entire Phase 4 versioned-push hardening — built correctly, end to end, and confirmed working in isolation by `phase4_sync_test.js` — had never actually engaged in practice past a Story's first save, for any real editing session**: a genuine two-device conflict for Studio would have silently been won by whichever device happened to save last, exactly the class of incident this whole plan exists to prevent. World Builder's own `save(project)` never had this bug, because it *mutates the caller's existing object in place* rather than constructing a fresh one — since `ProjectCache`'s own `_map` holds object references, not copies, whatever `markCloudSynced()` had written directly onto that object survives automatically; `duplicate(project)` deliberately does the opposite (`delete copy.cloudSyncedAt`), since a fresh copy under a brand-new id has genuinely never been synced and must take the unconditional first-touch path — the asymmetry between the two surfaces' own object-construction style is exactly what let this bug exist on one side and not the other. **Fixed** by carrying `cloudSyncedAt` forward from the existing record exactly like `createdAt` already was — a genuinely new record (`existing` is `null`) still gets no `cloudSyncedAt`, correctly taking the unconditional first-touch path; the fix changes nothing about a first save, only restores what every subsequent save had been silently discarding — confirmed via a minimal, isolated repro (a real second `upsert()` call after a real `markCloudSynced()`) both before the fix (the field genuinely came back `undefined`) and after (the field correctly survived). Verified via a new 43-assertion Playwright suite (`phase6_test.js`, all passing stably across 3 consecutive runs, zero unexpected console errors — the standing, disclosed `ERR_TUNNEL_CONNECTION_FAILED` sandbox-network-limitation noise closed out for Group A's own tests by mocking `ThemeRepositoryClient`'s identity check the same way `phase3_test.js` already established, rather than loosening the "zero unexpected errors" bar) plus a full re-run of every prior phase's own suite (`phase2_test.js` 13/13, `phase2_ui_test.js`, `phase3_test.js`, `phase4_store_test.js`, `phase4_sync_test.js`, `phase4_ui_smoke.js`, `phase5_test.js`, all passing unchanged — confirming the `creatorProjectStore.js` fix introduced zero regression anywhere) and both `goldenBuild.js` suites (World Builder v1 and v2, 30/30 each) unchanged. New canonical `docs/PROJECT_CLOUD_ARCHITECTURE.md` (mirroring `docs/DRAFT_ASSET_ARCHITECTURE.md`'s own structure) is now the one place this whole 6-phase effort's architecture, the hard synchronous-facade constraint, both cache modules' full IndexedDB schema and public API, the cloud-first reconciliation logic for both surfaces, this phase's own found-and-fixed bug, and the verification summary all live. No Theme Contract/Engine V2 Scene Model/Creator Governing Rules change; `tools/world-builder/` (v1) is completely untouched; confined to `js/creatorProjectStore.js` (the one real code fix) and the new doc. **This closes the entire Cloud-Primary Project Storage plan — all six phases (1: Foundation, 2: World Builder rewire, 3: World Builder cloud-first Welcome screen, 4: Studio rewire, 5: Studio cloud-first restore/My-Projects freshness, 6: verification + bug fix + docs) are now shipped**, directly satisfying the user's own governing, repeatedly-restated directive: "everything should be on cloud... world & studio both. i dont want any kind of trouble later on. no data loss beacause of whatsoever reason.")

- World Builder — "Everytime I Delete It Reappears": Local Delete Now Also Removes the Cloud Backup (a real, user-reported bug hit during real manual testing right after Cloud-Primary Project Storage's own Phase 6 shipped — the user began "testing again" by deleting an existing World and starting fresh, and reported directly, with a screenshot of two "Forest Sync" cards on the Welcome screen: **"everytime i delete it reappears."** Root-caused, not guessed, by re-reading `_deleteLocalDraft`'s own history: this function was ONCE a cascading delete (removing the local draft, the Published Personal Theme, AND the Cloud Backup together) — that cascade was deliberately removed in an earlier fix ("World Builder — Delete No Longer Cascades to a Published Theme's Cloud Copies," triggered by "a world which is published despite the warning save failed. if we delete local copy of this the cloud sync file also gets deleted on its own") because Build/Publish reads the live in-memory Project directly, so a Theme could be genuinely Published — and its Cloud Backup genuinely pushed — at a moment when this Project's own LOCAL save was actively failing (the real quota-exceeded "Save Failed" state, AV-009); cascading a local delete onto a Cloud Backup that might hold MORE real content than the failing local draft risked destroying it with no way to recover. **That reasoning's own load-bearing assumption was silently invalidated by a later sprint in the very same Cloud-Primary Project Storage effort**: Phase 3 changed "My Cloud Worlds"'s Orphan classification (a Cloud Backup row with no matching local Project) from a manual, deliberate "Sync to This Device" click into automatic, zero-click materialization — "everything should be on cloud" taken literally. Once that shipped, a plain local-only Delete (removing only `ProjectStore`'s own record, leaving the Cloud Backup row completely untouched) meant the very next `renderMyWorlds()` → `_refreshCloudWorlds()` pass would fetch `ProjectSync.list()`, find that now-orphaned backup with nothing local left to match it, and — per its own, correct-in-isolation "nothing local to overwrite, so just restore it" logic — immediately recreate the local Project from it, undoing the delete on the spot, every single time, exactly as reported. **A second, separate consideration made this fix genuinely safe rather than a silent reversion of the earlier one**: the original problematic cascade destroyed BOTH the Published Theme (a Personal Repository row, a genuinely different consumer — potentially read by Studio, or shared via a World Card recipient) AND the Cloud Backup together; under Cloud-Primary Project Storage's own now-shipped architecture, the scenario that motivated protecting the Cloud Backup specifically (a local save silently, quietly FAILING while the cloud held more complete content) is now structurally all but eliminated — Phase 2 already retired `_attemptQuotaSelfHeal()` outright, since "images are already externalized by Draft Asset Architecture; a plain Scenes/Places/Experiences JSON blob is tens of KB against IndexedDB's own hundreds-of-MB-to-low-GB realistic quota" — a local save can no longer plausibly fail the way it once could. `_deleteLocalDraft(project)` now calls `window.ProjectStore.remove(project.id)` (unchanged) AND, when available, `window.ProjectSync.remove(project.id).catch(function(){})` (a genuinely best-effort call, matching every other cloud-touching operation in this codebase — a removal that fails offline/RLS/etc. is a disclosed, honest limitation, not a promise of guaranteed success) — sequenced so the cloud removal is attempted and its result awaited (success OR failure) BEFORE the screen re-renders, closing the exact race where a premature `renderMyWorlds()` could still find and re-materialize the still-in-flight backup before the removal actually lands. The Published Theme itself — the genuinely dangerous half of the original cascade, since it can have real consumers beyond this one author's own device — is deliberately, completely untouched by this fix, exactly matching the earlier "Delete No Longer Cascades" fix's own correct half; a Cloud Backup, by contrast, is a private, single-purpose recovery copy of THIS Project's own data with no other consumer anywhere, so removing it the moment its author explicitly, deliberately deletes the Project (already gated behind a real, unchanged `window.confirm()`) can never destroy content anyone else depends on. The confirm() dialog's own copy was updated to disclose this plainly — "Delete '`<name>`' from this device (and its cloud backup)? If it's published to your Personal Repository, that copy stays published — remove it separately from its own card if you want it gone too. This cannot be undone." Verified via a new, dedicated Playwright reproduction (`verify_delete_reappear_fix.js`, scratch-only — this sandbox cannot reach the user's real Supabase project, the same standing limitation every prior Supabase-touching sprint in this codebase has disclosed) seeding a real local Project plus a matching, genuine Cloud Backup row via a mocked `ProjectSync`: clicking the local card's own Delete button correctly calls `ProjectSync.remove()` with the exact right project id, the mocked Cloud Backup row is confirmed genuinely gone afterward, the local draft does NOT reappear on the delete's own natural re-render, and — the literal reproduction of "everytime it reappears" — a further, completely independent render pass (creating a second, unrelated real Project via the actual UI, which naturally re-runs `renderMyWorlds()`/`_refreshCloudWorlds()` a second time) still shows zero trace of the deleted project, with zero console errors throughout. The existing `verify_delete_no_cascade.js` (the earlier fix's own regression test, exercising this exact function with an identical Published-Theme-plus-Cloud-Backup setup) was updated in place — not weakened, its assertions corrected — to confirm the deliberate, superseding new behavior: the Cloud Backup row IS now removed (previously asserted untouched), while the Published Theme row is STILL never touched (unchanged from before), and the now-orphaned Published Theme still correctly resurfaces as its own separately-deletable repo-only card afterward (its own dedicated Delete button, unrelated to this fix, already correctly removes both the Theme and any linked backup together). Full regression across the entire existing Cloud Worlds classification/delete Playwright suite (`verify_cloud_worlds_classification.js`, `verify_cloud_worlds_delete.js` — both scripts' own Case-3-Orphan-specific assertions confirmed, via direct re-run, to already be pre-existing, previously-documented stale failures from Phase 3's own auto-materialize ship, unrelated to and unaffected by this fix; every other scenario in both scripts — Linked-newer/Linked-up-to-date/Related's own full create-open-delete lifecycle — passes completely unchanged) and both `goldenBuild.js` suites (World Builder v1 and v2, 30/30 each, unaffected — this fix touches zero Builder-tooling compile/validate/publish code) passes unchanged. No Theme Contract/Engine V2 Scene Model/Creator Governing Rules change; `tools/world-builder/` (v1, which has no Cloud Backup mechanism of its own to carry this bug) and Studio (root `js/`) are completely untouched; confined to one function plus its confirm() dialog copy in `tools/world-builder-v2/js/worldBuilderApp.js`.)

- Decoration Image Failures Now Log a Diagnostic Instead of Failing Silently (a real, user-reported gap found investigating a live report: "authored a theme in builder this is how it shows up in studio" — a screenshot of a Studio Cover page showed only a flat, unstyled coloured rectangle, with a "Paper BG" Object Strip card present (green, editable) but nothing resembling the real uploaded image it should contain; a second screenshot of Creator's Screen 2 confirmed the same World, "Unlocked with a Card" — i.e. redeemed via a World Card, a genuinely different Supabase identity than whoever authored it in the mandatory-sign-in World Builder. **Investigation, not guessed**: a first hypothesis (the visible rectangle's rounded corners came from a Shape Decoration) was ruled out by matching its exact aspect ratio and rounding against `#previewCanvas`'s own CSS (`border-radius:var(--card-radius)`, `aspect-ratio:4/5`) — the "rectangle" is the canvas element itself, filled edge-to-edge by the theme's own base `fillStyle` (`_bgOverride||_wallTone||_frameColor`), confirming neither "Background" nor "Paper BG" was drawing any DISTINGUISHING content on top of it at all — both were, in effect, invisible. Tracing `_layerDrawDecorationImage`/`_ensureDecorationImage` in `renderer/slideRenderer.js` found the real, confirmed gap: when a Decoration image's resolved src fails to load — an expired/invalid signed URL, a cross-owner Storage access denial (a live, plausible cause for a World-Card-redeemed viewer resolving another account's Personal-repository Theme assets), or `AssetStore.resolve()` itself returning `null` — the function has always just silently `return`ed, drawing nothing, with **zero console signal of any kind**, indistinguishable from "still loading" or "correctly has no image." This made the real report undiagnosable from a screenshot alone, and would have stayed just as undiagnosable for any future report of this same shape. **Fix, deliberately additive-only, no behaviour change**: `_ensureDecorationImage` now calls `console.warn('[Decoration Image] failed to load...')` on two failure paths — `AssetStore.resolve()` resolving `null` for a `vihu-asset:` reference, and the underlying `Image`'s own `onerror` firing for any resolved src (a theme-authored relative path via `ThemeRegistry.resolveAssetRef`, a Story-Author override, or a raw `data:`/`http(s)` URL alike) — each naming the exact src that failed. A genuinely successful load or a still-in-flight one is completely unaffected; nothing about what gets drawn, or when, changed in any way. Verified via a new Playwright suite (`verify_decoration_image_diagnostic.js`, scratch-only) confirming the warning fires correctly for a Decoration Layer whose image path never resolves to a real, loadable image, and confirming zero warnings fire for a genuinely valid one, which still renders its real pixel content exactly as before. Both `goldenBuild.js` suites (World Builder v1 and v2, unaffected — this fix touches only root-Studio's `renderer/slideRenderer.js`) pass unchanged. **Disclosed, not yet resolved**: this fix makes a silent failure *diagnosable* — the actual, underlying cause for THIS user's specific "Paper BG" report (most likely, but not confirmed, a cross-owner Storage/RLS denial for the World-Card-redeemed session) still needs to be confirmed live, in the user's own browser, by checking whether the new warning now appears in the console — this sandbox cannot reach the user's real Supabase project or browser session to confirm which failure mode is actually occurring. No Theme Contract/Engine V2 Scene Model/Creator Governing Rules change; confined to one function in `renderer/slideRenderer.js`.)

- Scene Decoration Images — the Real Root Cause, Found With the Diagnostic That Just Shipped (a direct, same-session follow-up: the diagnostic added above immediately surfaced the real cause the moment the user checked their own browser console — `[Decoration Image] failed to load ("image failed to decode/load: scenes/cover/decoration.png"): scenes/cover/decoration.png`, and a second screenshot confirmed the browser was requesting `https://dexprab.github.io/vihustudio/scenes/cover/decoration.png` — the bare, unresolved compiled-asset relPath being loaded directly as an `<img src>` against the PAGE's own origin, never resolved against the Theme's own compiled `assets` map at all. **Root cause, traced to its actual source, not guessed**: `ThemeRegistry.resolveAssetRef(id,value)` — the one function every image reference resolves through — looks up `getAsset(id,value)` (a plain `rec.assets[relativePath]` map lookup) and, when nothing is found there, silently falls back to returning `value` UNCHANGED (`resolved||value`) rather than `null` — by design, so a non-image field (an emoji, a label) passes through untouched. This means a genuinely MISSING asset is indistinguishable from "this was never meant to be resolved" — the caller gets back the bare relPath string with no signal that resolution failed, and Studio's renderer then tries to load that bare string as a real image URL, which the browser resolves relative to its own page, producing exactly the 404 the user saw. **The actual bug, found one level upstream, in World Builder v2's own compile step**: `tools/world-builder-v2/js/services/builder.js`'s `externalizeSceneImage(scene,layer,package_)` — the function that's supposed to put REAL BYTES into `package_.assets['scenes/<sceneId>/<layerId>.png']` at Build time — resolved a Scene Layer's `vihu-asset:` image reference via `AssetStore.resolve(src)`, then only embedded the result if it happened to start with `data:`. But `AssetStore.resolve()` **deliberately never returns a `data:` URI** for a `vihu-asset:` reference (per `docs/DRAFT_ASSET_ARCHITECTURE.md`'s own design — it resolves to a warm `blob:` object URL from local IndexedDB, or a signed Supabase Storage `https:` URL, precisely so the Draft Asset Architecture effort never re-embeds large base64 back into a Project) — so that `data:` check has failed silently for EVERY real Scene Decoration image uploaded since Draft Asset Architecture's Phase B shipped, and the function kept returning the relPath as if externalization had succeeded regardless, leaving `package_.assets` with nothing at that key. Confirmed `tools/world-builder/` (v1) has no equivalent bug — its own `externalizeSceneImage` only ever handles raw `data:` URIs, since v1 never produces `vihu-asset:` references at all (Draft Asset Architecture's upload rewiring was v2-only). **Fix**: `externalizeSceneImage` now resolves a `vihu-asset:` reference via `AssetStore.hydrateForExport(src)` instead — the module's own existing, already-tested inverse of `put()`, purpose-built for exactly this ("resolve a ref straight back to a real, durable, embeddable `data:` URI," checking the local IndexedDB blob directly before ever falling back to a network fetch) — reused rather than reimplementing its own fetch+FileReader logic a second time inline. Verified via a new Playwright suite (`verify_scene_image_externalize_fix.js`, scratch-only) driving the REAL, unmodified pipeline: a real `AssetStore.put()` producing a genuine `vihu-asset:` reference backed by a real IndexedDB blob (exactly what a real Builder upload produces), fed into the real, unmodified `builder.convergeSceneLayer()`/`externalizeSceneImage()` — confirmed via `git stash` to reproduce the exact reported failure on the pre-fix code (`package_.assets` stays empty, the compiled Layer Pack entry's own `image` field still points at the bare relPath with nothing backing it) and to pass cleanly once the fix is restored (a real, byte-identical `data:` URI now lands at the correct relPath). Both `goldenBuild.js` suites (World Builder v1 and v2) pass unchanged, confirming zero impact on the existing compile/validate/import pipeline; the earlier diagnostic fix's own test suite (`verify_decoration_image_diagnostic.js`) still passes unchanged too, confirming the two fixes compose correctly — the diagnostic still fires for a genuinely broken image, while a real Scene Decoration image no longer becomes broken in the first place. No Theme Contract/Engine V2 Scene Model/Creator Governing Rules change; confined to one function in `tools/world-builder-v2/js/services/builder.js`.)

- Image Fit — "Stretch" Added (closes a real, confirmed gap: an author screenshot showed a Working-View-only checkerboard triangle where an Image Experience's artwork didn't fully cover its own transform rect — "adding new scene attached experience . i dont have any option to stretch the image to fill the scene." **Investigation, not guessed**: a dedicated Explore pass traced the Image content section's own Fit dropdown (`IMAGE_FIT_CHOICES` in `tools/world-builder-v2/js/worldBuilderApp.js`) and confirmed it has only ever offered `fit`/`fill`/`original` — a genuine grep across `tools/world-builder-v2/`, `renderer/slideRenderer.js`, and `js/services/engineRuntime.js` confirmed **no non-uniform-scale "Stretch" mode existed anywhere in this codebase**, matching the user's own literal words exactly. The specific gap in their screenshot (Transform X0/Y10/W100/H100, not true full-bleed) was separately confirmed to be closeable today via the existing "↔ Fill Scene" button (resets to X0/Y0/W100/H100), since `_drawImageWithFit`'s `fill` (cover) math is a genuine guaranteed-full-coverage formula regardless of aspect ratio once the rect itself is full-bleed — a real, zero-code-change fix for that specific visual symptom, disclosed to the user separately from this feature addition. **Fix — a real "Stretch" fit mode, added since none existed**: `IMAGE_FIT_CHOICES` gained a fourth `{value:'stretch',label:'Stretch'}` entry; `tools/world-builder-v2/js/services/engineRuntime.js`'s `_drawImageWithFit(ctx,img,rect,fit)` (used by both World Builder's own Working View/Runtime Preview and the isolated Working View Experience Studio) gained a `fit==='stretch'` branch drawing the image at exactly `rect.w`x`rect.h` — both axes scaled independently, never cropping and never leaving a gap, at the deliberate cost of distorting the image's own aspect ratio, exactly the "always fully fills, no matter the source image's shape" behaviour a Stretch/wallpaper mode is meant to provide. `renderer/slideRenderer.js`'s `_layerDrawDecorationImage` — the Reader-facing Studio renderer a compiled/Published Theme actually renders through — got the identical `fit==='stretch'` branch added in lockstep, the same hand-mirrored-duplicate discipline this codebase has used for every prior Engine V2/Engine V1 renderer addition (Decoration Shapes, page furniture, etc.), so a Theme Author's Stretch choice renders correctly in Studio, not just in Builder's own preview. No change was needed in `js/projectModel.js`'s `_syncUniversalContent` (an Image's `fit` field was already a plain, unrestricted string pass-through onto the mirrored Scene Layer) or `tools/world-builder-v2/js/services/builder.js`'s `convergeSceneLayer` (already carries `layer.fit` straight through into the compiled `decoration.fit` field unmodified) — confirmed by direct code read before assuming either needed touching. Verified via a new Playwright suite (`verify_stretch_fit.js`, scratch-only): the Inspector's own `IMAGE_FIT_CHOICES` source now includes `stretch` alongside the unchanged `fit`/`fill`/`original`; a real, distinctly-non-square 20×10 source image drawn via the real, unmodified `EngineV2Runtime.load`/`.paintLayer` into a genuinely non-square 432×135 rect under `stretch` draws at exactly that rect's own width/height (no gap, no crop), while the identical rect under `fill` (cover) draws a provably *different* size — confirming Stretch is genuinely non-uniform, not merely an alias for Fill; a real compiled Layer Pack entry (via `convergeSceneLayer`/`externalizeSceneImage`, the exact functions the immediately-prior fix touched) correctly carries `fit:'stretch'` through with its real image bytes still correctly embedded, confirming the two fixes compose cleanly. Both `goldenBuild.js` suites and the two immediately-prior scratch test suites (the delete-reappear fix, the Scene-Decoration-image root-cause fix) all pass unchanged. No Theme Contract/Engine V2 Scene Model/Creator Governing Rules change; confined to `tools/world-builder-v2/js/worldBuilderApp.js`, `tools/world-builder-v2/js/services/engineRuntime.js`, and `renderer/slideRenderer.js`.)

- Text Experience Words/Content — Manual Line Breaks Now Actually Render (a real, user-reported gap: "in the builder when putting up text experience, enter should put new line in the experience." **Investigation, not guessed**: pressing Enter in a real `<textarea>` (World Builder's `_textarea()` helper, used for both the legacy "Words" field and the Universal Experience Content model's "Content" field) already inserts a genuine `\n` character — the browser's own native behaviour, unmodified — so the field itself was never the problem. The real gap was downstream, in every place that string later gets *rendered*: `tools/world-builder-v2/js/services/engineRuntime.js`'s `_wrapLines(ctx,text,maxWidth)` (World Builder's own Working View/Runtime Preview/isolated Experience Studio, used by `_paintLayer`/`textFootprint` alike) split ONLY on `' '`, so an embedded `\n` was silently absorbed mid-word-wrap with zero visible line break; `renderer/slideRenderer.js`'s `_layerDrawText` (the Reader-facing Studio renderer for a compiled/Published Text Experience's Layer Pack entry) was worse — a single `x.fillText(content,drawX,drawY)` call with NO wrapping of any kind, so a manual newline (or even an ordinary long line) never broke at all once Published, a real Publish Fidelity gap this fix also closes. **Fix, kept in lockstep across both renderers, matching this codebase's established discipline**: `_wrapLines` (engineRuntime.js) and `_wrapText` (slideRenderer.js, already shared by Quote composition and Creator freeform Text stickers) both now split the input on `\n` into paragraphs FIRST, then word-wrap each paragraph independently — a blank paragraph (from `\n\n`) still pushes an empty line, preserving intentional blank-line spacing; for any text with no `\n` at all (every pre-existing single-paragraph field), this is byte-identical to the original algorithm, purely additive. `_layerDrawText` was rewritten from its original single-`fillText` call into a real multi-line renderer — reusing the now-fixed `_wrapText` for word-wrap-by-`rect.w` (a Scene-converged Text Layer always carries a real, non-zero `rect.w` per `convergeSceneLayer`'s own `rect:{x,y,w,h}` field; a legacy declarative caption falls back to the broader panel/slide/holder rect, wide enough that a short caption still renders on one line exactly as before) — with the existing anchor-based h/vAlign positioning, drag-override delta, and hit-test bbox math all generalized from the single-line case to N lines (byte-identical for N=1 except a few px of extra bbox padding, which is a hit-test/selection box only, never rendered, so a negligible, disclosed difference). **Deliberately left out of scope, disclosed rather than silently fixed**: `convergeSceneLayer`'s compiled `type:'text'` entry always hardcodes `anchor:'top-left'`, silently discarding the Scene Layer's own chosen text alignment (left/center/right, set via the Universal Text Experience's Alignment dropdown) — a real, pre-existing, separate Publish Fidelity gap found while tracing this exact code path, but unrelated to "Enter should put a new line" and left unfixed to avoid unrequested scope creep; flagged to the user as a candidate for its own future fix. Verified via a new Playwright suite (`verify_text_newline_fix.js`, scratch-only): World Builder's real `EngineV2Runtime.load`/`.paintLayer` correctly renders a manual `'First line\nSecond line'` as 2 real `fillText` calls at genuinely different Y positions, with the correct per-line text and zero regression for an ordinary single-paragraph string (still exactly 1 call); Studio's real `SlideRenderer.buildPayload`/`.render()`, driven through a real compiled Layer Pack `type:'text'` entry (matching `convergeSceneLayer`'s own output shape exactly), confirms the identical manual newline now renders as 2 real, distinctly-positioned lines instead of one squashed line. Both `goldenBuild.js` suites pass unchanged. No Theme Contract/Engine V2 Scene Model/Creator Governing Rules change; confined to `tools/world-builder-v2/js/services/engineRuntime.js` and `renderer/slideRenderer.js`.)

- Creator Governing Rules Audit — Stretch Fit + Text Newline Fixes, and a Confirmed Fidelity Violation Found and Closed (a direct, requested audit — "check for both fixes against the rules which needs to be honored always" — of the two immediately-prior fixes against the 5 permanent Creator Governing Rules. **Fidelity** — both fixes strengthen this rule: the Stretch fit addition is kept byte-identical between Builder's own preview and Studio's renderer (added in lockstep to both `engineRuntime.js`'s `_drawImageWithFit` and `renderer/slideRenderer.js`'s `_layerDrawDecorationImage`), and the newline fix directly repairs a real Fidelity violation (a Scene's own manual line breaks, correctly shown in Builder, were being silently discarded once compiled/Published — exactly "Nothing about a Scene's... content is silently discarded... on the way into Creator"). **But auditing surfaced a second, separate, CONFIRMED Fidelity violation in the same code path, left disclosed-but-unfixed in the newline fix's own entry — fixed now rather than left open, since the whole point of "rules which need to be honored always" is that a confirmed violation gets closed, not just named**: `convergeSceneLayer` (both `tools/world-builder-v2/js/services/builder.js` and its `tools/world-builder/` v1 twin, confirmed carrying the identical bug in the identical shape) always hardcoded the compiled Text Layer's `anchor` to `'top-left'`, completely ignoring the Scene Layer's own real `align` field (left/center/right, set via the Universal Text Experience's Alignment dropdown and already correctly honoured by `engineRuntime.js`'s own `_paintLayer` in Builder's Working View/Runtime Preview) — so a centred or right-aligned Text Experience rendered correctly in Builder but always came back left-aligned once compiled/Published, a direct, textbook violation of "nothing about a Scene's... content is silently discarded... on the way into Creator." **Fixed in both Builders, kept in lockstep**: the text branch now derives the compiled anchor's horizontal component from `layer.align` (`'top-center'`/`'top-right'` when set, `'top-left'` as the unchanged default) — vertical positioning stays `'top'` always, matching how both renderers already anchor a text Layer's rect at its own top edge regardless of alignment; `resolveAnchor`'s existing 9-point vocabulary (`js/layerEngine.js`) already parses these three strings correctly, no changes needed there. **Guardrails** — confirmed unaffected by all three fixes (Stretch, newline, alignment): none of them touch `moveable`/`editable`/`visible` checks or the permission-gated call sites that read them; every fix operates purely on content/positioning/drawing within an already-permission-gated render call. **Refinement** — confirmed, and found to improve for free: `js/contextPanel.js`'s Story-Author-facing "Words" edit control for a World-owned text object (`_renderWorldObjectDisclosure`'s `v.kind==='text'` branch) is itself a real `<textarea>`, and its content flows through the exact same `_layerOverride`/`_layerDrawText` path the newline fix repaired — so a Story Author personalizing a World-owned Caption's own words can now press Enter and see the real line break too, with zero additional wiring. **Personalization** — neither fix adds new Story-Author-facing capability directly (both are Theme-Author-authoring/compile correctness fixes), but the Refinement improvement above is a genuine, if incidental, Personalization win. **Publish Fidelity** — confirmed satisfied by construction for all three fixes: `js/storyDestinations.js`'s Publish export path (Story Book PDF / Instagram Carousel) calls the exact same `SlideRenderer.buildPayload()`/`.render()` pair the editor's own center-pane canvas uses, with zero second rendering implementation — since every fix lives inside `renderer/slideRenderer.js` itself, Publish and the live canvas can never diverge on any of them. Verified via a new Playwright suite (`verify_text_align_fidelity_fix.js`, scratch-only, 8 assertions): both Builders' real `convergeSceneLayer` correctly compile `align:'left'/'center'/'right'` to `'top-left'/'top-center'/'top-right'` respectively, with an absent `align` still falling back to `'top-left'` (zero regression for every pre-existing theme); a real, end-to-end check confirms a compiled `anchor:'top-center'` entry genuinely sets `ctx.textAlign='center'` while Studio's real `SlideRenderer.render()` draws it — not just a compile-step string, the actual Reader-facing pixel alignment. Full regression: both `goldenBuild.js` suites and both prior scratch suites (`verify_text_newline_fix.js`, `verify_stretch_fit.js`) all pass unchanged. No Theme Contract/Engine V2 Scene Model change; confined to `tools/world-builder-v2/js/services/builder.js` and `tools/world-builder/js/services/builder.js`.)

- Five Confirmed Bugs Fixed in One Batch — Font Fallback, Decoration Rotation/Fit-Default Mismatch, Legacy-Kind Position/Size Guardrails, a Redraw Diagnostic (five bugs collected without fixing per the standing "keep collecting the bugs for studio but dont fix... we will fix them in one go" instruction, then fixed together on "ok lets fix these bugs first." **(1) Fidelity — Comic Sans font fallback**: World Builder v2's `TEXT_FONT_OPTIONS`/`TEXT_FONT_CHOICES` (`tools/world-builder-v2/js/worldBuilderApp.js`) carried `'"Comic Sans MS", cursive'`, missing the `"Chalkboard SE"` fallback step `js/cardDesigner.js`'s own equivalent `FONT_FAMILY_OPTIONS` already has — a device lacking Comic Sans MS silently rendered a different, unintended font in Builder's own preview than Studio would show; fixed to `'"Comic Sans MS", "Chalkboard SE", cursive'` in both entries, applied identically to `tools/world-builder/js/worldBuilderApp.js` (v1), matching this codebase's own established "kept in lockstep by hand" precedent. **(2) Fidelity — Decoration rotation dropped, Fit default mismatched**: `renderer/slideRenderer.js`'s `_layerDrawDecorationImage` (a compiled Image Decoration's Studio-facing draw routine) never applied `layer.rotation` at all, unlike its own shape-kind sibling `_layerDrawShape`, which already does — and `tools/world-builder-v2/js/services/engineRuntime.js`'s own `_paintLayer` already applies `rotation` to image AND shape decorations uniformly in Builder's Working View/Runtime Preview, so a rotated Image Decoration (reachable today only via a hand-authored Layer Pack, since no current authoring UI sets rotation on an uploaded Image) would render correctly in Builder but always upright once compiled/Published. Fixed by adding the identical rotate-around-center logic already used for shapes; a `d.rotation` absent (every existing theme) is a byte-identical no-op. A second, independent mismatch found in the same code path: the compile step (`convergeSceneLayer` in both `tools/world-builder-v2/js/services/builder.js` and `tools/world-builder/js/services/builder.js`) hardcoded the compiled `decoration.fit` to `'fill'` (cover, crops) regardless of the Scene Layer's own `layer.fit`, while `engineRuntime.js`'s own default is `'fit'` (contain) — so an unset Fit choice rendered differently in Builder's own preview than in the compiled/Published Theme Studio actually shows; fixed to `layer.fit || 'fit'` in both Builder versions' compile step, matching the default engineRuntime.js already uses. v2's compile branch additionally now carries `rotation: layer.rotation || 0` through to the compiled package (v1 has no shape-kind compile branch or rotation-authoring concept for Scene Layers at all — confirmed via grep — so this field was added to v2 only). **(3) Guardrails — a `moveable:true` legacy decoration (spotlight/paperTexture/shadowWash — pre-date the Universal Experience Content model, reachable only via a hand-authored Layer Pack, e.g. Museum Gallery's real `gallery-spotlight` entry) silently never moved or resized when dragged**: `_layerDrawDecoration`'s legacy-kind branches drew against the raw, un-overridden `rect` regardless of any `SceneEngine.setPosition`/`.setSize` a Story Author had applied, unlike fill/image/shape, which already correctly draw against the position/size-adjusted `r`. Fixed by generalizing paperTexture/shadowWash to draw against `r` exactly like fill/image/shape (their whole visual — blob positions, gradient center, fill bounds — is defined purely relative to whichever rect they're handed, a safe direct swap); spotlight keeps its glow radius/fill bounds tied to `r` too, and shifts its own anchor-based hotspot (an authored point like Museum Gallery's top-center, resolved via `js/layerEngine.js`'s `resolveAnchor` — deliberately NOT the same thing as `r`'s own geometric center) by the exact delta `r` moved by, rather than recentering on `r`'s center outright, which would have silently relocated every existing theme's unmoved glow. A size override (`ov.size`, from `SceneEngine.setSize` — the exact permission-block field #335 below found completely unread anywhere) is now applied first, recentred around `r`'s own current center, so a position override immediately afterward still lands the final center exactly where the Story Author dragged it to regardless of write order; absent either override, `r===rect` and the new code paths are provably byte-identical no-ops for every existing theme, verified directly by re-importing and rendering the real, on-disk `themes/MuseumGallery.vtheme` with zero override present and confirming identical scene labels/bboxes/painted pixels to before this fix. **(4)/(5) closed by the same change — resize was "completely inert for every World-owned object" per an earlier exhaustive grep finding zero Layer Pack drawing function anywhere reading a size override** — now read by all three previously-position-only kinds (fill/image/shape already did) plus the three legacy kinds fixed in (3) above, closing both the confirmed Guardrails gap (`moveable:true` doing nothing for legacy kinds) and the resize gap (a size override existing in the model but reaching zero drawing code) in one pass — Text objects (`type:'text'`) structurally never get resize handles at all (`_supportsResize`'s own type check: `'image-holder'||'decoration'||'sticker'`), narrowing that earlier claim's true reachable scope, which this fix does not attempt to widen. **A fifth reported issue, investigated and NOT reproduced**: "editing a World-owned Text object's Words textarea updates the right panel but the center-pane canvas doesn't visibly repaint" — two realistic reproduction attempts (Story-role Free-hosted text, Cover-role Free-hosted text with a real SceneEngine blueprint) both showed the write path (`SceneEngine.setContentOverride`) and the render/redraw path (`host.redraw()`/`ObjectStrip.refresh()`) working correctly end-to-end; rather than force an unconfirmed fix, applied only the clearly-warranted defensive improvement — `js/contextPanel.js`'s `_afterWorldObjectEdit` now wraps each of `host.redraw()`/`host.markDirty()`/`ObjectStrip.refresh()` in its own try/catch with a real `console.error(...)` on failure, replacing a silent catch that could previously leave the canvas stuck on its last frame with zero signal anywhere a future debugger could see — a successful redraw is completely unaffected. Verified via both `goldenBuild.js` suites (30/30 each, unchanged), a new combined Playwright verification script exercising rotation/fit-default/legacy-kind-position/legacy-kind-size together against a real compiled+imported Theme, the real-file Museum Gallery byte-compatibility regression above, and a re-run of the existing `commitments_test.js` (Story-Author colour-edit/Decoration-Slot flows unaffected). No Theme Contract/Engine V2 Scene Model change; confined to `renderer/slideRenderer.js`, `tools/world-builder-v2/js/services/builder.js`, `tools/world-builder-v2/js/worldBuilderApp.js`, `tools/world-builder/js/services/builder.js`, `tools/world-builder/js/worldBuilderApp.js`, and `js/contextPanel.js`.)

- Cloud-Sync Companion Charm — Studio's Own Traffic Light, Told Through the Companion (a direct, user-asked question — "why i dont have red, orange, green in studio. everything is on cloud now correct?" — pointed at the exact World-Builder-only `.wb-signal-dot-*` traffic light shipped for the Cloud-Primary Project Storage effort; confirmed via investigation that Studio (Creator) had nothing equivalent, since `js/creatorProjectCache.js`'s `_attemptSync()` outcomes (`pending`/`synced`/`conflict`/`failed`) had no listener of any kind — `js/projectManager.js`'s own `_scheduleCloudProjectSync` comment explicitly disclosed this: "Studio has no cloud-sync-status badge to update... so there is no live UI feedback." Rather than port the flat dot as-is, the user's own framing — "i would love to have them but in studio style. something which kid might love. we might even use companion for this" — was taken as full creative latitude, resolved by mirroring this codebase's own established "generic capability + Director assigns meaning" pattern (`setRichness`/`boostGlow` from the Story Egg Interaction & Presence sprint is the direct precedent): `js/companionEngine.js` gains a small, purely mechanical `.companion-cloud-charm` — a floating cloud-emoji charm anchored at the companion portrait's lower-left, added once in `_ensureDom()` alongside the existing `zzz` sleep indicator — plus a matching `setSyncBadge(state)`/`getSyncBadge()` pair that does nothing but toggle a plain `data-sync-badge` attribute (`'busy'|'good'|'attention'|null`) on the widget root; the engine itself has zero idea any of this means "cloud sync," exactly matching the discipline already proven for richness/glow. **`css/style.css`** gives each state its own kid-friendly animation, all skipped under `prefers-reduced-motion`: `busy` pulses gently (an orange-tinted glow, `companion-cloud-busy`); `good` gives one satisfied pop-and-settle (a green tint, `companion-cloud-good`, `animation-fill-mode:forwards` so it settles to a quiet resting glow rather than looping); `attention` gives a brief, gentle head-shake wiggle (an amber tint, `companion-cloud-attention`+`-settle`) — never a scary red X or a blocking dialog, matching this file's own established "no scary error UI for kids" precedent (`js/travellerSaveNotice.js`). **`js/creatorProjectCache.js`** gains the actual missing signal: a small `onSyncStateChange(fn)`/`_notifySyncStateChange(id,outcome)` pub/sub, mirroring World Builder's own `projectCache.js` sibling function name-for-name, called from all four of `_attemptSync()`'s existing outcome branches (`unavailable`/`synced`/`conflict`/`failed`) — deliberately NOT also firing a `'pending'` outcome from inside this module (unlike the World Builder sibling), since `js/projectManager.js`'s own `_scheduleCloudProjectSync` already knows the exact moment a sync is first requested and is the more natural place to signal that. **`js/projectManager.js`**'s `_scheduleCloudProjectSync` gains one additive line — `CompanionDirector.notify('project-sync-pending')` right alongside its existing `CreatorProjectCache.enqueueSync(id)` call — wrapped in the same defensive `try{ if(typeof X!=='undefined') ... }catch(e){}` shape this codebase uses for every cross-module hook (PageRuntime/ObjectStrip/ContextPanel/MagicCard all already follow it). **`js/companionDirector.js`**, the one file allowed to know what any of this actually means, gains `bindCloudSyncBadge()` (called once from `bindReady()` alongside the existing `bindGlobalListeners()`/`bindOcclusionWatcher()`) — subscribes to `CreatorProjectCache.onSyncStateChange`, and for a real settled outcome belonging to the CURRENTLY OPEN project (checked against `AppState.project.id`, so a background sync for a different Story a Story Author isn't even looking at can never flash the badge) and only while in Creator mode (a Traveller has no Magic Card and therefore no cloud sync to show at all — `MagicCard.getActive()` gates the entire feature structurally, the same discipline `_scheduleCloudProjectSync`'s own pre-existing gate already established), calls `engine.setSyncBadge('good'|'attention'|null)` — `'good'` additionally fires the existing `boostGlow()` for one extra flourish, since "your Story is safe" is worth celebrating a little; `notify('project-sync-pending')` is handled at the very top of `notify()`'s own `safe(...)` body, setting `'busy'` only in Creator mode. Verified via a new Playwright suite (`sync_charm_test.js`, scratch-only, mocking `ThemeRepositoryClient`/a real, versioned fake Supabase table via `page.route`): a Traveller's own real save never shows any badge at all (`data-sync-badge` attribute genuinely absent, not just hidden); becoming a Creator via the real, production `CompanionDirector.notify('creator-born')` entry point (the same one `js/magicCard.js`'s `claim()`/`adopt()` call) shows no badge until an actual save happens; a real save genuinely transitions busy → good with the correct owner id recorded in the fake cloud table; a genuine forced push failure shows the gentle `'attention'` state (never a blocking error, confirmed Studio itself — `#app` — stays fully functional throughout); and the badge recovers to `'good'` automatically, with zero further user action, once the mock heals and the real `drainPendingSync()` retry mechanism actually fires. **Investigating a real, initially-unexplained set of 5 console 404s surfaced during this verification (not caused by the sync-charm feature)**: traced via a standalone repro to `CompanionEngine.load(id)`'s own pre-existing, documented `_preloadStates()` behaviour, which eagerly preloads every pose an entity's `companion.json` declares regardless of whether it's ever shown — Story Egg's own already-disclosed `hero.png`/`magic.png`/no-`personality.json` gap accounts for 3 of the 5, and a genuinely new (if likewise pre-existing) finding accounts for the other 2: `assets/nimbus/companion.json` declares a `think` pose whose `think.png` was never uploaded, and Nimbus (like Quill) has no `personality.json` at all — both real, pre-existing asset gaps, confirmed via direct filesystem inspection, completely unrelated to and unaffected by this session's own code changes (which touch zero image-loading code). The test's own console-error assertion now cross-checks real 404 URLs via `page.on('response')` against this disclosed, known list rather than a blanket text match, so a genuinely new/unexpected error would still fail the check. Full regression across the existing Companion/Magic-Card/Story-Egg/Cloud-Sync Playwright suite (`companion_canon_test.js`, `companion_canon_v2_test.js`, `companion_engine_test.js`, `companion_engine_test2.js`, `companion_platform_v1_test.js`, `magic_card_test.js`/`_defer_test.js`/`_phase2_test.js`, `regression.js`, `final_qa.js`, `combined_regression_check.js`, `story_egg_polish_test.js`, `verify_companion_retry.js`, `verify_companion_persistent_fail.js`) — every one of the pre-existing failures already documented across these scripts' own history (a stale `visitor`→`traveller` registry-role rename, a stale `assets/companions/lumo/` path predating the Asset Path Correction sprint, a stale Screen-1 Creation Flow card locator, a pre-existing "sticker did not move" Object Strip bug, several already-documented Ceremony-beat/legacy-card-bonding assertions) was independently reconfirmed via `git stash` to fail identically on the unmodified codebase, none of it caused by or related to this feature — plus `phase4_store_test.js`/`phase4_sync_test.js`/`phase4_ui_smoke.js`/`phase5_test.js`/`phase6_test.js` (all directly exercise `creatorProjectCache.js`, the module this feature extends) and both `goldenBuild.js` suites (World Builder v1 and v2, 30/30 each, unaffected — this feature touches zero Builder files) all passing unchanged. No Theme Contract/Engine V2 Scene Model/Builder/Creator Governing Rules change; confined to `js/companionEngine.js`, `js/companionDirector.js`, `js/creatorProjectCache.js`, `js/projectManager.js`, and `css/style.css`.)

- World-Owned Text Objects Finally Honour the Resize Grid (the bug the user picked first out of the reported list, framed directly: "we will take the biggest bug. honoring the story author can adjust this grid. lets finalize it for any text object" — the exact gap the "Five Confirmed Bugs Fixed in One Batch" entry above disclosed but deliberately left open: "Text objects (`type:'text'`) structurally never get resize handles at all... narrowing that earlier claim's true reachable scope, which this fix does not attempt to widen." A moveable World-owned Text Layer (a Museum Caption-style object) could already be *moved* on canvas (Honour World-Owned Object Commitments sprint), but selecting one never showed the 8-corner resize grid every other moveable Scene Object kind gets, and even if it had, nothing downstream would have read the resulting size. **Three-part fix, all in `renderer/slideRenderer.js`/`js/app.js`**: (1) `_supportsResize(el)` widened to include `el.type==='text'` alongside the existing `image-holder`/`decoration`/`sticker` — gated by the exact same `el.locked` check every other kind already uses, itself already correctly derived from the Theme Author's own `moveable` permission, so no new guardrail logic was needed; a locked (`moveable:false`) text object correctly still gets zero handles, unchanged. (2) `_layerDrawText` — which read a Story-Author position override but never a size override — now checks `_layerOverride(s,layer.id).size` and, when present, derives a uniform scale factor from how the override's target width compares to the text's own natural (un-resized) measured width, applies that scale to BOTH font size and wrap width together, and re-wraps/re-measures before the existing position-override logic runs; absent an override, every value is byte-identical to before this fix. (3) `js/app.js`'s resize-drag handler's aspect-lock — previously scoped to sticker corner-handles only — now locks EVERY handle to a uniform scale for a text-type element specifically, since canvas text has no sensible independent width/height "stretch" in this renderer's wrap-width-plus-font-size model (unlike an image, non-uniformly stretching glyph proportions would just look broken); a side (n/s/e/w) drag on text correctly still produces a real, visible resize via the existing aspect-derived `else` branch rather than becoming a dead handle. `SceneEngine.setSize`/`.setPosition` needed zero changes — both were already fully generic, keyed by any object id regardless of type. Verified via a new Playwright suite (`text_resize_grid_test.js`, scratch-only, mirroring `scene_object_test.js`'s own synthetic-Museum-Gallery-shaped-theme pattern with a moveable and a locked Text Layer Pack entry): the moveable text object now genuinely gets all 8 resize handles (previously `[]`) while the locked one still correctly gets zero; a real, mouse-driven drag on the "se" handle writes a genuine `size` override into `slide.metadata.elementOverrides`, visibly grows the rendered text's bbox (both width and height), and the resize survives a fresh redraw (durable, not a one-off visual artifact) — 12/12 assertions passing, zero console errors. Full regression: the existing "Five Confirmed Bugs" verification (`bug332_334_335_verify.js`) and a real Museum Gallery `.vtheme` file's own render (`museum_realfile_regression.js`) both pass unchanged, with the latter's exact scene-labels/bbox/center-pixel output confirmed byte-identical between a `git stash`-baseline run and this fix (zero visual change for any theme with no size override present); `three_rules_audit.js`/`unified_layer_order_test.js`/`merged_order_test.js`/`world_shape_reorder_test.js` all pass unchanged; `sticker_dragorder_bug2.js`/`place_guardrails_test.js`/`all_object_guardrails_test.js`/`combined_regression_check.js`/`regression.js`/`final_qa.js`/`scene_object_test.js` each hit a failure, but every one was independently reconfirmed via `git stash` to already exist identically on the unmodified baseline (a pre-existing "sticker did not move"/"place did not move" Object Strip drag bug, and several older scripts predating the Traveller Gateway that time out waiting on Creation Flow Screen 1 since they never call the now-required Gateway-skip helper) — none caused by or related to this fix. Both `goldenBuild.js` suites (World Builder v1 and v2, 30/30 each, unaffected — this fix touches zero Builder files) pass unchanged. No Theme Contract/Engine V2 Scene Model/Builder change; confined to `renderer/slideRenderer.js` and `js/app.js`.)

- Selection Confidence Sprint — ThumbnailEngine Clobber Fix + Option B (Refined) Selection Action Strip (a real bug root-caused through an extended console-diagnostic collaboration with the user — repeated reports of "I clicked the title in center pane... on centerpane I did not see any changes" and "before reimporting on the previous theme I was just randomly dragging things with no action seen on screen" — that ultimately shifted product direction, not just fixed one bug. **Investigation**: a synthetic Playwright reproduction using real `mousedown`/`mouseup` mouse events and direct canvas `getImageData` pixel-sampling confirmed the selection outline/resize-handle draw calls genuinely fired at exactly the right coordinates and colour (`#FFCB45`) — the bug was never in `_drawSelectionOutline`/`_drawResizeHandles` themselves, `_supportsResize`, or `PageRuntime`'s dispatch. The real root cause: `js/thumbnails.js`'s `ThumbnailEngine.generate()` restore-to-editor-canvas step called `SlideRenderer.render(SlideRenderer.buildPayload(...))` directly — bypassing `js/app.js`'s `draw()`, the ONLY function that stamps `selectedSceneElement`/`selectedTextElement`/`dragActiveId`/`showSafeArea` onto the render payload. Since every drag-move handler (scene/text/image-pan alike) deletes `slide.thumbnail` before calling `draw()`, and every one of `mouseup`'s own resize/scene-drag-end branches calls `ThumbnailEngine.generate(s)` once a drag actually moved something, this ran after essentially every real drag+release — silently wiping the selection outline, resize handles, and drag guides off the visible editor canvas the instant a drag completed. **Fixed**: replaced the bare restore-render call with `window.redrawPreview()` — the same real choke point every other "something changed off to the side, please repaint correctly" case in this codebase already uses (`_ensureDecorationImage`/`_ensureStickerImage`'s own onload nudge) — which reads whichever slide/selection is actually current and stamps it correctly. Confirmed via a real `git stash` A/B: the exact reported symptom (0/8 gold-painted resize-handle centers after a genuine drag+release) reproduces precisely on the pre-fix code and resolves fully (8/8) with the fix restored. **Product pivot, requested directly mid-investigation**: rather than keep chasing canvas-visual-feedback reliability, the user asked for wireframes of a more robust interaction model — "if clicks are working as per you, than lets start opening contextual menu to work on the selected option" — reviewed via a published Artifact showing 3 concepts, with the user choosing "Option B is better" plus one explicit hard constraint stated up front: "any new tool which opens up cannot be over the slide in centerpane." **Implemented, "Option B, Refined"**: (1) Chunky corner grips — `renderer/slideRenderer.js`'s `HANDLE_RADIUS` bumped `12`→`18` and `_drawResizeHandles(el)` rewritten from thin filled gold circles into bigger rounded-square grips (`x.arcTo`-based rounded-rect path, 5px corner radius) — `getHandleRadius()` already feeds `js/app.js`'s own hit-test slop (`r*1.4`), so the bigger, easier-to-grab clickable area came for free with zero separate hit-test change needed. (2) A new `js/selectionActionStrip.js` module + matching `css/style.css` rules render a small, always-reliable action strip — a friendly icon+name (mirroring `js/objectStrip.js`'s own `FRIENDLY_TYPE` icon table as a deliberate small per-module copy, not a shared import) plus the exact same ownership-status wording Object Strip's own badge already uses ("🟢 You can edit" / "🌍 Part of the World" / "🔒 Locked"), an Edit button (focuses the right panel's Refine section via the existing `_activateTab('card')` + `.right-sidebar` scroll-into-view machinery) and a Deselect button (`PageRuntime.clearSelection()`) — anchored in `index.html` as a sibling element BEFORE `.preview-wrapper` inside `.preview-area` (never a child positioned relative to the selected object's own on-canvas coordinates), so the parent's own `flex-direction:column` guarantees it can only ever occupy one fixed slot above the canvas, satisfying the "never over the slide" constraint structurally rather than by convention. Refreshed from `PageRuntime.notify()`'s own dispatch list, alongside the pre-existing `CardDesigner`/`ContextPanel`/`ObjectStrip`/`TravellerSaveNotice` refreshes — no separate wiring of its own beyond that one hook plus a `configure()`/`init()` call mirroring every other Creator module's established host-binding pattern. Reordering is deliberately NOT one of the strip's actions, matching the already-established "Object Strip's own drag-to-reorder is the ONE reorder control" precedent (Unified Layer Ordering sprint). **Verified** via a new 15-assertion Playwright suite (scratch-only): the chunky-grip radius and genuinely square (not circular) handle shape; the strip's correct show/hide/content/never-overlapping-the-canvas-region behaviour (a real test-methodology bug of my own was caught and fixed along the way — the strip taking up real layout space once visible shifts the canvas down, so click coordinates must be recomputed fresh before every interaction rather than reused from a stale pre-selection measurement); and, the actual regression proof, a real drag+release confirmed to still show 8/8 gold-painted resize-handle pixels afterward (0/8 on the pre-fix code via the same `git stash` A/B). Full regression: `text_resize_grid_test.js`/`commitments_test.js` pass unchanged; several older scratch scripts (`regression.js`/`final_qa.js`/`runtime_pass_test.js`/`publish_stages.js`/`scene_object_test.js`/`frame_variation_test3.js`) hang waiting on a Creation Flow Screen 1 locator, reconfirmed via `git stash` to already hang identically on the completely unmodified baseline — a pre-existing condition (these scripts predate the Traveller Gateway's own skip helper) already documented repeatedly in this project's history, unrelated to this fix; `canvas_click_visual_repro.js`/`paperbg_hittest_repro.js`/`sync_charm_test.js` all pass unchanged. One older script's own fixed near-corner click offset (`bx+20, by+10`) now registers as a resize instead of a move — investigated directly rather than dismissed: a dedicated A/B check confirmed this is the exact, disclosed, intended consequence of the chunky-grip fix (that offset now falls inside the widened NW-handle hit-test slop, `18*1.4=25.2` vs. the old `12*1.4=16.8`, and the offset's own distance from the corner is `~22.36`) — a genuine centre-body drag still produces a clean move-only override with zero size override, confirming ordinary move behaviour away from a corner is completely unaffected. Both `goldenBuild.js` suites (World Builder v1 and v2, 30/30 each, unaffected — this sprint touches zero Builder files) pass unchanged. No Theme Contract/Engine V2 Scene Model/Builder change; confined to `js/thumbnails.js`, `renderer/slideRenderer.js`, `js/app.js`, `js/pageRuntime.js`, `css/style.css`, `index.html`, and a new `js/selectionActionStrip.js`.)
