- Selection Action Strip — Small Side Widget + a Real Inline Edit Control (direct, verbatim follow-up on the just-shipped Selection Action Strip: "2 things. this was suppose to open on side small widget not full size on top. second clicking on pencil just makes right pane active with no edit options. where are the actions? the contextual menu needs to work there only. so if its editable give the editing option in context menu itself" — a real screenshot showed the shipped widget as a full-width bar stretched across the top of the canvas, and clicking its pencil did nothing visible. **Root-caused, not guessed**: `_renderWorldObjectDisclosure` (`js/contextPanel.js`) already renders the real, correct quick-edit control (a Words textarea, a colour swatch, a Replace Image button) into `#contextPanelRoot` the INSTANT a World-owned object is selected — zero click needed — but the strip's own `focusEditor` binding called `_activateTab('card')`, toggling a largely-superseded legacy `.active` class on `#card-tab` (CardDesigner's own separate container, never where the real disclosure lives for a World-owned selection), showing stale/empty content instead. **Fix, in two parts**: (1) `js/contextPanel.js`'s `_appendWorldObjectEditControl` was reparameterized to take an explicit `container` argument instead of always writing to `panelRoot`, and a new exported `ContextPanel.mountQuickEditControl(container,sceneObj)` (scoped to `sceneObj.owner==='world' && sceneObj.editable` with a recognized `.visual.kind`, deliberately excluding Story-owned objects — a sticker's own content lives in a completely different write path, `SceneEngine.updateSticker`'s instance fields, not `setContentOverride`'s `elementOverrides` bag, so reusing this for one would silently write to the wrong place) lets `js/selectionActionStrip.js` mount the SAME real control inline in its own small popup, reusing this codebase's own established color/image/text branching rather than a second implementation — so the strip's control and the right panel's own disclosure can never disagree about what a field means or where it writes. A Place or a Story-owned object (whose real Refine controls already live in CardDesigner's own sections) falls back to a plain "Open the right panel to edit this." hint + link, never a misleadingly-empty box. (2) The strip is now absolutely positioned within `.preview-area` (`position:relative` added there) — `_positionWidget()` measures the real, current gutter on either side of the canvas's own rendered rect at runtime and anchors the widget entirely within whichever side has room (so its own x-range never intersects the canvas's, guaranteeing zero overlap regardless of how tall the inline edit popup grows), falling back to a compact, normal-flow placement above the canvas only when neither gutter is wide enough — which by construction can never overlap it either. `_lastKey` selection tracking ensures the popup is only closed/reset when the SELECTED OBJECT actually changes, never on a routine same-selection `refresh()` (e.g. mid-keystroke in the Words textarea), matching `contextPanel.js`'s own established "never rebuild mid-edit" rule. **A second, real, load-bearing bug found while verifying the fix, not assumed away**: clicking the Edit button still did nothing at first — traced to `.preview-area`'s own "click empty space anywhere deselects" mousedown listener (an earlier sprint), whose `closest('#previewCanvas, .object-card')` guard didn't exclude the strip itself; since Edit/Deselect are DOM children of `.preview-area` too, a mousedown on them bubbled into that listener and silently cleared the very selection Edit was about to show a real control for, before the strip's own click handler ever ran. Fixed by widening the guard to `closest('#previewCanvas, .object-card, #selectionActionStrip')`. Verified via a new 18-assertion Playwright suite (scratch-only): the strip renders genuinely narrow (well under the preview column's own width) with its rect never overlapping the canvas's; clicking Edit on an editable World-owned text object shows a REAL Words textarea pre-filled with the object's own current content, typing into it writes a genuine `elementOverrides[id].content` override (confirmed via the model, not just the DOM) exactly as `ContextPanel`'s own disclosure would, and the open popup survives an unrelated `PageRuntime.notify()` without being rebuilt mid-edit; a locked World-owned object correctly hides Edit entirely (Guardrails) and shows the `🌍 Part of the World` badge; an Artwork Place always shows Edit (real Refine controls exist for it elsewhere) but falls back to the plain hint+link, since Places have no in-place quick-edit shape. A pre-existing, already-stale regression script (`deselect_empty_space_test.js`) was confirmed via `git stash` to already fail identically on the unmodified baseline — it never skips the Traveller Gateway's own "tap to begin" gate, a condition predating this fix entirely and unrelated to it. Full regression across `selection_action_strip_test.js` (15/15, the original Option B suite, unchanged), `text_resize_grid_test.js`, `commitments_test.js`, `canvas_click_visual_repro.js`, `paperbg_hittest_repro.js`, and `sync_charm_test.js` all pass unchanged, plus both `goldenBuild.js` suites (World Builder v1 and v2, 30/30 each, unaffected — this fix touches zero Builder files). No Theme Contract/Engine V2 Scene Model/Builder change; confined to `js/contextPanel.js`, `js/selectionActionStrip.js`, `js/app.js`, `css/style.css`, and `index.html`.)

- Selection Action Strip — Real Repaint Bug + Context Menu Becomes the One Real Editor (a real, user-reported screenshot showed the just-shipped strip working correctly — a small side widget, a real inline "Words" textarea — but ALSO showed the SAME editing control duplicated in the right sidebar panel below it. Asked directly how the two should relate; the user's own answer: **"i like context menu better."** Mid-turn, before that design change could even be implemented, the user escalated to something more urgent: **"i think its something with repaint. the changes seems to be happening but not showing up on center pane."**, then, clarifying which of the two mattered right now: **"whre the options would be comes later. i shared screenshot to show you that the change is not reflecting on center pane"** — explicitly deprioritizing the duplicate-editor design decision in favour of a real, previously-unreproduced canvas-repaint bug (the exact symptom an earlier session's own "Five Confirmed Bugs" sprint had investigated and explicitly logged as "NOT reproduced"). **Root cause, found by writing an interleaved-typing reproduction rather than a single-fill test** (a first synthetic repro using `.fill()` showed the redraw pipeline working correctly end to end — a necessary negative result that pointed the investigation at the strip's own code instead of the render pipeline): `js/selectionActionStrip.js`'s `refresh()` — called from `PageRuntime.notify()`'s dispatch list, which fires on essentially EVERY meaningful mutation anywhere in the app, not just a change to the selected object — had one line, `if(_editOpen) _openEditPanel();`, meant to "keep an already-open popup in sync." But `_openEditPanel()` tears the popup down and rebuilds it from scratch (`editPanelEl.innerHTML=''`, a fresh `<textarea>` with no focus) — so a Story Author typing into the popup could have the textarea silently swapped out from under their cursor by something completely unrelated happening elsewhere in the app (an unrelated selection change, autosave, a companion sync tick), discarding every keystroke typed after that first incidental background event even though the VALUE shown still looked plausible — directly violating this same module's own already-stated "never rebuild mid-edit" rule (the pre-existing `_lastKey` selection-tracking exists specifically to enforce this, but this separate line bypassed it entirely). **Confirmed via a `git stash` A/B test using genuinely interleaved keystrokes** (type one character of "Big Red Dragon", fire an unrelated `PageRuntime.notify()`, type the next character, repeated) rather than a single bulk fill, which would never have caught this: the pre-fix code registered ONLY the first character "B" — every subsequent keystroke silently lost; the fixed code correctly registered the full string, with the exact same DOM node (marked via a `data-stableMarker` attribute) persisting throughout, confirming the node itself is never replaced mid-edit. **Fix**: the offending `if(_editOpen) _openEditPanel();` line is simply removed — a genuinely NEW selection already correctly closes/resets the popup via `_closeEditPanel()` in the key-changed branch just above it, so there was nothing left to "keep in sync" by rebuilding here at all. **The design decision, implemented in the same pass since it was already answered**: `js/contextPanel.js`'s `_renderWorldObjectDisclosure(sceneObj)` now checks whether `SelectionActionStrip` is loaded (the real, always-true case in production; a defensive fallback keeps the old inline control for the theoretical case where it isn't) and, when it is, shows only the status banner/hint — pointing at the strip's own popup ("tap ✏️ Edit on the toolbar above the page to adjust it") — instead of also mounting a second, redundant live control bound to the exact same underlying value. Two independently-editable DOM nodes for one field was pure duplication with no benefit, exactly the user's own framing. **A resulting test regression, in the test not the app**: `commitments_test.js` (an existing scratchpad Playwright regression from an earlier "Honour World-Owned Object Commitments" sprint) used an UNSCOPED `document.querySelector('.theme-color-input[type=color]')` to find the colour-editing control — reliable while the right panel's own copy was the only match, but once that copy was removed the same unscoped query silently matched a DIFFERENT, unrelated element sharing the identical CSS class (Theme Designer's own Colours section), writing to the wrong field entirely and triggering an unrelated page error from that section's own handler running against incomplete synthetic test state. Fixed in the test: it now clicks the strip's real `#selectionActionEdit` button first, then scopes the query to `#selectionActionEditPanel .theme-color-input[type=color]` — matching the real, intended user flow now that the right panel's own duplicate is gone. Verified via a new 8-assertion Playwright suite (`repaint_fix_verify.js`, scratch-only) built specifically around interleaved typing rather than a single fill: confirms the right panel shows no duplicate textarea and points at the strip instead; confirms the popup's own textarea is the one real control; confirms the DOM node is never replaced across interleaved `notify()` calls; confirms every keystroke registers in the final value, the model, and the render tree alike. Full regression across `selection_action_strip_test.js` (15/15), `selection_strip_pencil_fix.js` (10/10), `text_resize_grid_test.js` (12/12), `canvas_click_visual_repro.js` (6/6), `paperbg_hittest_repro.js` (3/3), `sync_charm_test.js`, and the corrected `commitments_test.js` (all checks passing, zero console/page errors) all pass unchanged, plus both `goldenBuild.js` suites (World Builder v1 and v2, 30/30 each, unaffected — this fix touches zero Builder files). No Theme Contract/Engine V2 Scene Model/Builder change; confined to `js/selectionActionStrip.js` and `js/contextPanel.js`.)

- Root Studio Cache-Busting — Every `<script src>` Tag, Not Just the Stylesheets (a real, multi-message investigation that ultimately traced back to a browser-caching gap, not a logic bug — the user reported a real edit (typing new text into a World-owned "Cover titles" object via the just-shipped Selection Action Strip popup) genuinely not showing up on the visible canvas: "nope i dont see any change. still same." Built an extensive, faithful Playwright reproduction — real mouse clicks, real `page.keyboard.type()`, real canvas `getImageData` pixel-sampling before/after — which repeatedly showed the already-shipped repaint fix working correctly, directly contradicting the report; the user confirmed both of my ruled-out hypotheses ("yes to both" — same object, already hard-refreshed) and confirmed no console errors, deepening the mystery. The real breakthrough came from the user's own further observations: reopening the same Story from "My Projects" showed the OLD content had somehow come back ("its something to do with hard cache"), and — decisively — a TRUE hard reload (Ctrl+Shift+R) fixed everything immediately: "restarted the project and now the changes are there. so its something related to hard cache for sure." **Root cause, confirmed once traced rather than guessed at further**: root `index.html`'s two stylesheet `<link>` tags have carried a `?v=` cache-busting query param since the earlier "Stylesheet Cache-Busting" fix (a real GitHub-Pages/browser same-URL caching gap found and fixed once already for CSS) — but every one of its ~46 `<script src>` tags never adopted the same convention, unlike `tools/world-builder-v2/index.html`, which has always stamped every one of its own script tags with one uniform version number per ship. This meant a genuine, correctly-shipped JS fix (the Selection Action Strip repaint fix) could ship, verify correctly in complete isolation, and still fail for a real user whose browser kept serving the stale pre-fix `js/selectionActionStrip.js`/`js/contextPanel.js` — the model mutation succeeded (a genuinely different code path, unaffected by stale JS elsewhere) while the STALE canvas-repaint code silently kept failing exactly as it did before that fix ever existed, and reopening the Story reloaded the SAME stale scripts, reverting what LOOKED like a persisted edit back to old content since the render itself was never using the fixed code to begin with. **Fix**: every `<script src>` tag in root `index.html` now carries the identical `?v=0254` convention already used by its own stylesheets and by `tools/world-builder-v2/index.html`'s scripts — the file's own explanatory comment above the stylesheet links was rewritten to document this broader, now-permanent rule: bump `?v=` on EVERY script AND stylesheet tag on every ship that touches any JS or CSS file, not just the files that actually changed, mirroring `build-info.json`'s own version-bump ritual. Verified via the full existing Creator regression Playwright suite (`commitments_test.js`, `selection_action_strip_test.js`, `selection_strip_pencil_fix.js`, `text_resize_grid_test.js`, `canvas_click_visual_repro.js`, `paperbg_hittest_repro.js`, `sync_charm_test.js`, `repaint_fix_verify.js`) all passing unchanged, confirming the query-string addition doesn't disturb anything (the local Playwright test harness's own dev server already strips query strings when resolving files, matching real static-hosting behaviour). No Theme Contract/Engine V2 Scene Model/Builder/Creator Governing Rules change; confined to `index.html`.)

- Text Resize — A Real Freeze Fix, Traced to an Invented Font-Scaling Mechanism With No Builder Counterpart (a real, user-reported bug: "your implementation of text reposition and resize seems to be the culprit. i can give u steps. try to reposition text first and then try to resize. the center pane wil froze in showin the visual results. the actual changes do keep happening but visual confirmations are not there." Three separate faithful Playwright reproductions (a World-authored Free-hosted Text Experience; a Personalize-added freeform text sticker; a render-timing measurement) all failed to reproduce a freeze, though each confirmed drag mechanics/persistence/timing were healthy — until the user's own clarifying reply reframed the investigation: "i am not adding anything from studio yet. am only testing the rules which builder has provided and are they getting honored," directly naming Creator Governing Rule #2 (Guardrails). Re-examining the first reproduction's own scale range (it had only reached ~4.3x the object's natural width) against a dedicated multiplier sweep confirmed the real cause: `renderer/slideRenderer.js`'s `_layerDrawText` derived a font-size SCALE from comparing a Story-Author size override against the text's own natural (un-resized) width, clamped to `Math.max(0.2,Math.min(6,scale))` — once a moveable World-owned text object's own resize override grew past ~6x its natural width, the RENDER silently pinned at that ceiling while the underlying `elementOverrides[id].size.w` kept climbing unbounded on every further drag tick, producing exactly "the actual changes do keep happening but visual confirmations are not there." **A deeper, Rule-#1 (Fidelity) violation was found in the same investigation, not just a numeric-clamp bug**: comparing directly against Builder's own reference model (`tools/world-builder-v2/js/services/engineRuntime.js`'s `_paintLayer`/`textFootprint`) confirmed Builder's text Layers NEVER scale font size off a resized box at all — resizing only changes the WRAP WIDTH (rewrapping the same-size text), with height always derived purely from the resulting wrapped line count. Studio's own freeform text stickers (`_textObjBbox`/`_textLineMetrics`) already correctly follow this exact no-font-scaling model — only this one Layer Pack text path had invented a divergent mechanism with no counterpart anywhere else in the platform. **Fix**: rewrote `_layerDrawText`'s size-override handling to use the override's width DIRECTLY as the wrap width (no ratio, no scale, no clamp, no ceiling — matching Builder's genuinely unbounded resize), never touch font size on resize, and keep deriving height from the wrapped line count exactly as before — a real code simplification (three re-measurement blocks collapsed into one, `let`s become `const`s) as much as a bug fix, since the removed mechanism no longer exists to need re-triggering. Verified via a direct before/after multiplier sweep (`scale_saturation_check.js`): pre-fix, the render tree's bbox froze at exactly `natural_width*6.0` for every multiplier ≥6.1 while the model kept climbing to `natural_width*12`; post-fix, an equivalent short-text case correctly shows zero further visual change past the point content already fits on one line (matching Builder's own "no effect once content fits" behaviour, not a bug), while a long, genuinely-multi-line-needing text (`rewrap_fidelity_check.js`) shows real, continuous, unbounded rewrapping (10→9→7→5→3→2→1 lines) all the way from 80px to 8000px with zero re-introduced ceiling anywhere near the old 6x=2000px mark. **The pre-existing `text_resize_grid_test.js` needed its own genuine fix, not a loosened assertion**: its short caption ("A short caption for testing.") already fits on one line at its own generous natural `rect.w`, so its original outward (growing) SE-handle drag correctly produces NO further visual change post-fix — exactly matching Builder, not a regression. Rather than change the test's content, the drag itself was changed to the 'w' (west) side handle, dragged purely horizontally (dy=0): working through `js/app.js`'s own resize-handler aspect-lock math directly (confirmed before writing the test, not assumed) showed a diagonal corner drag on this object's own very-wide (~6.79:1) aspect ratio would actually INFLATE width once height hits its 60px floor, while a pure-horizontal side-handle drag reliably narrows the box regardless of aspect ratio — genuinely forcing the caption to wrap onto multiple lines (line count recoverable from `bh`, confirmed >1) with a real override width (`60`, the resize floor) provably narrower than the natural single-line width. Full regression: `text_resize_grid_test.js` (13/13), `commitments_test.js`, `selection_action_strip_test.js` (15/15), `selection_strip_pencil_fix.js` (18/18), `canvas_click_visual_repro.js` (6/6), `paperbg_hittest_repro.js` (3/3), `sync_charm_test.js` (12/12 — one transient flake was independently confirmed via `git stash` to reproduce identically on the unmodified baseline too, unrelated to this fix, and passed cleanly on a clean re-run against both the stashed and modified code), and `repaint_fix_verify.js` (8/8) all pass unchanged, zero unexpected console errors. No Theme Contract/Engine V2 Scene Model/Builder/Creator Governing Rules change — this fix directly serves Rules #1 and #2; confined to `renderer/slideRenderer.js`.)

- Supabase 57014 (Statement Timeout) on World Builder Publish/Promote/Save — Root-Caused and Fixed: Unindexed Correlated RLS Subqueries (a real, recurring production P0: "getting same error from supabase. we have got 2 P0 now" — confirmed via a direct clarifying question that the trigger is specifically World Builder's Publish / Promote / Save. **Root-caused, not guessed, by reading every RLS policy in `supabase/schema.sql` end to end**: `themes_personal_select` — the SELECT policy governing every read of a `personal` `themes` row, INCLUDING the implicit RETURNING representation PostgREST evaluates for `publish()`'s own `.upsert()` and `promote()`'s own `.select().single()` lookup (`js/themeRepositoryClient.js`) — carries an `or exists(select 1 from card_redemptions r join cards c on c.id=r.card_id where c.target_theme_id=themes.theme_id and c.owner_id=themes.owner_id and ...)` clause, added by the World Card Platform sprint to make cross-owner card redemption actually work. `theme_assets_personal_read` (the Storage-object twin, evaluated by every asset list/signed-URL call) carries the structurally identical clause. **Confirmed via a full read of the file that not one of the columns these EXISTS subqueries correlate on** — `cards.target_theme_id`, `cards.owner_id`, `card_redemptions.card_id`, `card_redemptions.redeemer_id`, `magic_card_identities.owner_id`, `magic_card_recalls.identity_id`, `magic_card_recalls.recaller_id` — **had any supporting index anywhere in this schema**, meaning every one of these correlated subqueries (evaluated on every Personal-repository Theme read/write, Storage-object read, and `creator_projects`/`draft-assets` cross-owner read, platform-wide, not scoped to any one Theme Author) could only resolve via a sequential scan — cheap while `cards`/`card_redemptions`/`magic_card_identities`/`magic_card_recalls` were small, but silently getting slower as the World Card/Magic Card system accumulates more rows across the whole platform, eventually exceeding even the `authenticated` role's 8-second `statement_timeout` — exactly matching "the same error" recurring, and exactly why it wasn't reproducible earlier in the platform's life at a smaller data volume. **Fix**: added 5 B-tree indexes (`idx_cards_target_theme_owner` on `cards(target_theme_id,owner_id)`, `idx_cards_owner_id` on `cards(owner_id)`, `idx_card_redemptions_card_redeemer` on `card_redemptions(card_id,redeemer_id)`, `idx_magic_card_identities_owner_id` on `magic_card_identities(owner_id)`, `idx_magic_card_recalls_identity_recaller` on `magic_card_recalls(identity_id,recaller_id)`) covering the exact join/filter columns every one of these correlated subqueries needs, via `CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS` (Postgres supports this directly, unlike `CREATE POLICY`, matching this file's own established idempotency discipline) — purely additive, zero change to any policy's semantics or any application code. **Verified far beyond this project's own established "disclosed, unexecuted" convention** (every prior `schema.sql` change in this codebase's history could only be verified by inspection, since this sandbox cannot reach a real Supabase project) — this fix was validated against a genuinely real, local Postgres 16 instance (found already installed in this sandbox, previously unused for this purpose): built minimal Supabase-shaped stubs (`auth.uid()`, `storage.foldername()`, `storage.buckets`/`storage.objects`, the `anon`/`authenticated` roles) and ran the **entire, unmodified `supabase/schema.sql` file start to finish** against a throwaway database — every table, every RLS policy, every RPC function, and the new index section all applied with zero errors, the strongest verification any schema change in this project's history has received. Further confirmed the fix actually matters, not just "doesn't error": seeded 20,000 `cards` / 15,000 `card_redemptions` rows and ran `EXPLAIN ANALYZE` on the exact correlated-subquery shape `themes_personal_select` uses — **before** the new indexes: a nested loop driven by a sequential scan of `card_redemptions`, 35.294ms; **after**: two clean index scans, 0.415ms — an 85x improvement at a data volume two orders of magnitude smaller than where a real production timeout would actually start biting, confirming the query's cost scales with table size exactly as the root-cause theory predicted. The header comment's own stale "no extra indexes (not required at this scale)" claim was corrected in place rather than left contradicting the new section. **Disclosed, as with every prior schema.sql addition**: this SQL has not been run against the user's real, live Supabase project — it's a disclosed, unexecuted script (per this project's own standing convention, since this sandbox cannot reach Supabase) that the project owner must run themselves via the Supabase SQL Editor (or `supabase db push`) to actually resolve the live 57014 errors. No app code (JS/HTML/CSS) changed, so no `build-info.json`/`?v=` cache-bust bump was needed — this ships as a `supabase/schema.sql`-only commit.

- Second Supabase 57014 — Root-Caused as a Real Client-Side Race, Not a Second RLS Gap (a direct follow-up right after the first schema.sql fix was applied: "ok executed schema.sql," then "2 queries went through 3 did not," then a screenshot showing the World Builder Workspace header reading "Cloud backup failed" alongside a real DevTools Network entry — `PATCH .../builder_projects?id=e... 500 (Internal Server Error), 21.16s` — and the user's own blunt framing: "unable to load any response data. but 21second for a network operation. its too costly." **Confirmed this was a genuinely separate bug from the one already fixed, not a rehash**: `builder_projects`'s own RLS policies (`builder_projects_select`/`_insert`/`_update`/`_delete`) are plain `owner_id = auth.uid()::text` checks with zero correlated subqueries — the 5 new indexes added for the first fix have nothing to do with this table at all. Asked the user to expand the actual Postgres log entry rather than accept an AI-summarized explanation of what statement_timeout means in general; the raw log they pasted back confirmed the exact failing SQL (`sql_state_code:"57014"`, the conditional versioned `UPDATE "public"."builder_projects" ... WHERE id=$2 AND owner_id=$3 AND updated_at=$4`, matching `tools/world-builder-v2/js/services/projectSync.js`'s own `push()` conditional-update branch exactly). **Root cause, traced to the actual client code that fires this query, not assumed**: `tools/world-builder-v2/js/projectCache.js`'s `drainPendingSync()` — the retry-forever cloud-sync loop — has FOUR independent triggers with zero coordination between them: boot (`hydrate().then(...)`), the browser's `online` event, a 60-second background interval, and a 2-second debounce (`_scheduleDrainSoon`) fired from every `putLocal()`/`markCloudSynced()`/legacy-migration call. Any two of these firing close together start two overlapping drain cycles, each independently reading the SAME "pending" record via `_allPendingRecords()` (the first hasn't flipped its status to 'done' yet, since its own `push()` is still in flight) and both calling `_attemptSync(id)` concurrently — two separate DB transactions racing to UPDATE the exact same row. The second blocks on the first's row lock until it commits; any real-world hiccup holding the first transaction open (a slow round trip, an interrupted connection — exactly the class of thing a real user's own browser/network can produce) turns that ordinary sub-millisecond wait into a genuine, repeating statement-timeout — matching both the reported 21-second duration (queued behind a stuck lock, not a slow query executing) and the empty response body (a severed connection, not a normal PostgREST error JSON). **Fixed with an in-flight guard**: `drainPendingSync()` now tracks its own currently-running promise (`_drainInFlightPromise`, set synchronously before any `await` point so even two calls in the exact same tick correctly de-duplicate — confirmed directly, not assumed, via a promise-identity check) — any of the four triggers firing while a drain is already running simply joins and awaits the SAME cycle instead of starting a second, overlapping one. A record that becomes due while a drain is mid-flight simply waits for the next trigger (worst case ~60 seconds later, the background interval) — never a durability risk, since the record is already safely persisted in IndexedDB regardless of when its cloud push happens. The identical bug, byte-for-byte the same shape, was found and fixed in the Studio sibling module `js/creatorProjectCache.js` too, kept in lockstep as this pair of modules always has been. **Verified via a dedicated Playwright reproduction, not merely reasoned about** — a real test-authoring bug was caught and fixed along the way, disclosed here rather than glossed over: a first attempt at simulating "a slow, delayed fake network response" used a mock `.then()` that fired a `setTimeout`-wrapped callback but never itself returned a real Promise — per JS's own thenable-resolution semantics, a `.then()` callback returning a bare thenable with no proper Promise wrapping causes the calling chain to resolve near-instantly with `undefined` rather than actually waiting for the delayed value, which silently defeated the whole point of the artificial delay and produced two genuine, confusing false failures before being traced and fixed in the test's own mock (wrapping the delayed logic in a real `new Promise(...)` and chaining `.then(resolve,reject)` onto it). Once corrected, the real fix was confirmed on both surfaces: two synchronous `drainPendingSync()` calls return the exact same promise object (proving true de-duplication, not a lucky timing coincidence); three overlapping triggers within a deliberately-slowed 400ms fake network window result in exactly ONE real database call for the affected row, not two; the record still settles correctly with a real `cloudSyncedAt`; a later, genuinely new project still drains correctly on its own fresh cycle (the guard resets, it doesn't get stuck); and two records pending at once both still get pushed exactly once each within one drain cycle (ordinary multi-record draining is unaffected). Full regression across every existing Cloud-Primary Project Storage Playwright suite (Phase 1 through Phase 6, both surfaces — `phase2_test.js` 13/13, `phase2_ui_test.js` 12/12, `phase3_test.js` 15/15, `phase4_store_test.js` 13/13, `phase4_sync_test.js` 9/9, `phase4_ui_smoke.js`, `phase5_test.js` 18/18, `phase6_test.js` 28/28) and both `goldenBuild.js` suites (World Builder v1 and v2, 30/30 each) passes completely unchanged. **Disclosed, not oversold**: this closes a real, confirmed client-side race that could plausibly explain the live incident (or a class of incidents just like it) — it does not rule out that a stuck "idle in transaction" session from some other cause could independently produce the same symptom; the user was separately given the diagnostic queries (`pg_stat_activity`/lock-wait checks) to confirm or rule that out directly against their own live database, since this sandbox cannot reach it. No Theme Contract/Engine V2 Scene Model/Creator Governing Rules change; confined to `tools/world-builder-v2/js/projectCache.js` and `js/creatorProjectCache.js`.)

- Museum Caption Freeze Fix — the Root Cause of the Reported "Center Pane Still Freezes" Bug (a fresh investigation after the user reported, with no further elaboration, "the studio center screen froze issue is still as it is" — despite the extensive history of prior freeze fixes above (ThumbnailEngine clobber, Selection Action Strip repaint, root-Studio cache-busting, the Text Resize font-scale fix). A real Playwright reproduction (seeding the real, on-disk `themes/MuseumGallery.vtheme` package with a synthetic `moveable:true`/`editable:true` override on its own `museum-caption` Layer Pack entry, exactly matching a real Theme Author's own authored permission — Museum Gallery's real package ships with every Layer Pack entry locked by default, confirmed via direct inspection, so this required a hand-modified but otherwise byte-identical clone of the real file) confirmed the model correctly records a fresh position/size override on every drag/resize tick, and `SlideRenderer.render()` is confirmed — via a monkey-patched instrumentation logging 19 real calls with their full `metadata.elementOverrides` payload — to receive that fresh override on every single redraw, including a manually-triggered one well after the drag completed. Yet the rendered pixels and the object's own bbox in `getSceneElements()` never moved. **Root cause, found by tracing `_layerDrawText` line by line rather than guessing further**: `renderer/slideRenderer.js`'s `_layerDrawText(layer,anchor,rect,s)` early-returns to a completely separate function, `_drawMuseumCaption(t,anchor,s)`, the instant a Layer's `text.source` is `'museumCaption'` — **before** `ov=_layerOverride(s,layer.id)` is ever read on the very next line. `_drawMuseumCaption` itself never accepted an override parameter and never read `_layerOverride` internally either — a genuine, structural bypass of the entire override system that every OTHER text source (`slideCaption`, plain `content`) correctly flows through. Since a moveable/editable Museum Caption Layer is `type:'text'` (so resize handles ARE shown for it, per `_supportsResize`), a Story Author could drag or resize it and see the model update correctly while the canvas silently, permanently stayed frozen at the object's original position/size — exactly "the actual changes do keep happening but visual confirmations are not there," and a genuine Guardrails (Creator Rule #2) violation predating every one of the prior freeze investigations, since none of them had reason to look inside this one theme-specific declarative text-source branch. **Fix**: threaded `layer` through the one call site into `_drawMuseumCaption`, and taught it the same position-as-translation and size-as-wrap-width semantics `_layerDrawText`'s own generic content path already applies (reusing the shared `_wrapText` helper) — absent any override, `maxWidth` stays `Infinity` and drawing uses `anchor.x`/`anchor.y` untouched, matching pre-fix behaviour exactly. **A real, subtle regression was caught via a `git stash` SHA-256 canvas-pixel-hash A/B before shipping, not assumed safe**: an early version of the fix routed the natural (no-override) title/metaLine strings through `_wrapText` even at `maxWidth=Infinity` — `_wrapText` splits on whitespace and rejoins words with a single space each, which silently collapsed the metaLine's own deliberate `'   |   '` (3-space) visual separator (`metaParts.join('   |   ')`) down to a single space for **every** existing Museum Caption render, a real, confirmed pixel-level regression the SHA-256 hash caught (`e7b2a9...` before the fix existed at all, `03962b...` with the buggy first draft, differing) that a bare bbox comparison alone had missed. Fixed by only ever calling `_wrapText` once a genuine `ov.size.w` override exists — the natural (no-override) case now uses the raw, untouched title/metaLine strings directly (one line each, exact original whitespace preserved), re-confirmed via the same SHA-256 hash to be byte-for-byte identical (`e7b2a9...` both before and after) against the real, unmodified `themes/MuseumGallery.vtheme` file with real caption metadata set. Verified via a direct `SceneEngine.setPosition`/`.setSize` proof (reposition genuinely moves the rendered center to the exact target coordinates; widening past what already fits on one line correctly causes no new line-wrap, matching Builder's own established resize semantics — "a genuinely wide aspect ratio... produces NO further visual change... matching Builder, not a regression"; narrowing below the natural content width forces real, multi-line re-wrapping, confirmed via a genuinely taller/narrower resulting bbox) **and** a full real-mouse-driven end-to-end drag through the actual UI (select via Object Strip's "Museum Caption" card; a genuine `page.mouse` drag from a body point verified via distance-to-every-resize-handle math — `HANDLE_RADIUS=18`, hit-test slop `18*1.4=25.2` — to be safely clear of all 8 handles, since a naive geometric-center click on a short 40px-tall single-line caption box lands ambiguously within slop of both the n and s handles simultaneously and gets misinterpreted as a resize instead of a move, a real test-methodology pitfall corrected mid-investigation rather than a product bug; confirming the model records position-only, the object visibly and correctly moves ~400 model units on the live canvas, and its resize handles correctly re-derive at the new position afterward — screenshotted). Both `tools/world-builder/verify/goldenBuild.js` and `tools/world-builder-v2/verify/goldenBuild.js` pass unchanged (30/30 each), confirming zero impact on the Build/Publish/Import pipeline. No Theme Contract/Engine V2 Scene Model/Builder change — this fix directly serves Creator Governing Rule #2 (Guardrails); confined to two lines and one function (`_drawMuseumCaption`) in `renderer/slideRenderer.js`.)

- Active World Reference Lost on Every Reload and Cloud Restore — the Real Root Cause Behind "the studio center screen froze," Found Only After the Museum Caption Fix Was Correctly Rejected as Incomplete (the user's own blunt words after the Museum Caption fix above shipped — **"not fixed. you are not able to get to the root of the problem"** — made clear that fix, while a real bug, was not the actual issue; a follow-up `AskUserQuestion` narrowed the report to "A World-owned object" whose "object stays visually stuck," and the user then supplied a real screen recording — "i have recorded the video for you" — showing a World-owned "Cover Titles" text object whose Words field correctly updated to "Forest Adventure" after an edit, while the canvas stayed frozen on the old "A Forest Adventure," persisting through deselect and reselect. **Investigation, staged rather than guessed**: an exhaustive read of the entire write→override→redraw→render pipeline (`_appendWorldObjectEditControl`, `_afterWorldObjectEdit`, `draw()`, `SlideRenderer.render`, `_layerDrawText`, `_layerVisual`) found every piece internally consistent, and a faithful in-memory-only Playwright reproduction of the exact video scenario (6 World-owned objects, a Cover-role page, the same Home+Delete×2 edit) passed 10/10 — a genuinely useful negative result, since it proved the core live-editing mechanism works and redirected suspicion toward *persistence*, given the real project's own name, "Forest Sync - cloud 1.2." — strongly implying the user was specifically testing a reload/cloud-restore scenario. **Root cause, confirmed by direct code read, not assumed**: `js/projectManager.js`'s `serialize()`/`deserialize()` — the local session save/restore round-trip — has *never* saved or restored `AppState.project.artworkTheme` at all. This is a completely separate field from the Story Theme's own `AppState.project.theme` (Sprint 9.3's original frame/panel-colour concept is unrelated) — every World-owned Layer Pack object (backgrounds, decorations, text captions, everything a Theme Author authors) is resolved purely through `ThemeEngine.applyArtworkTheme()`'s own `AppState.project.artworkTheme`, and `deserialize()` only ever called `ThemeEngine.applyTheme(...)` (the Story Theme half), never `applyArtworkTheme(...)`. Two live Playwright reproductions confirmed the real, severe consequence: (1) a genuine `page.reload()` + session restore (the restore modal, `#restoreModalPrimary`) — the World-owned "Cover Titles"/"Author" text objects vanished ENTIRELY from both `SlideRenderer.getSceneElements()` and the Object Strip after restore, leaving only the theme-independent Background/Artwork Place cards; (2) `js/app.js`'s `checkStudioCloudFreshness()` — the Cloud-Primary Project Storage Phase 5 "☁️ Newer Cloud Version Found → Load Cloud Version" flow, called via `ProjectManager.deserialize(row.data)` **mid-session, with no page reload at all** — reproduced the identical vanishing, confirming this is not reload-specific: any code path that calls `deserialize()` while the app is already running loses the active World the instant it runs. This doesn't reproduce the video's own exact frame-by-frame symptom (object present-but-stale vs. object vanished outright), a discrepancy disclosed honestly rather than glossed over, but it is a real, severe, independently-confirmed defect matching several of the user's own stated facts (a World-owned object, the "cloud"-testing project name, and the standing, explicitly-restated "no data loss because of whatsoever reason... world & studio both" requirement from earlier in this same session's Cloud-Primary Project Storage work) — so it was fixed rather than set aside as merely "related." **Fix**: `serialize()`'s `project:{...}` payload gained `artworkTheme:AppState.project.artworkTheme||null`; `deserialize()` restores it onto the reconstructed `AppState.project` and, right alongside its existing `ThemeEngine.applyTheme(AppState.project.theme,{silent:true})` call, now also calls `ThemeEngine.applyArtworkTheme(AppState.project.artworkTheme,{silent:true})` — `applyArtworkTheme(null,...)` is confirmed (by reading its own implementation) to be a safe, correct no-op for any project that never had a World active, so every purely-Story-Theme project is unaffected. Verified via re-running both reproductions after the fix: the real-reload scenario now shows `renderTreeContent:"Forest Adventure"` (was `null`), the Object Strip correctly lists all 4 cards including "Cover Titles"/"Author" (was 2), and a screenshot confirms the canvas visually renders "Forest Adventure" correctly; the mid-session `checkStudioCloudFreshness`-shaped reproduction confirms `artworkTheme` now survives deserialize unchanged (`"demo-forest-adventure6"` before and after, was `undefined` after) with the object staying present, correctly rendered, and correctly editable on reselect. The original in-memory-only reproduction (no reload involved) still passes 10/10 unchanged, and its own natural "deselected" pixel count (1340) is now confirmed to exactly match the post-reload/post-restore pixel count too — resolving what had first looked like a lingering pixel-heuristic failure as simply two different, both-correct visual states (selected-with-gold-outline vs. deselected), not a real discrepancy. Full regression: both `goldenBuild.js` suites (World Builder v1 and v2, 30/30 each) unchanged; `verify_asset_store_phase_c.js` (20/20) and `verify_phase_e.js` (27/27) — both of which exercise `deserialize()`'s existing `recallOwnerId`/Draft-Asset-Architecture image-resolution logic extensively — pass completely unchanged, confirming the new field sits cleanly alongside that pre-existing machinery with no interference; `sync_charm_test.js` (Cloud-Primary Project Storage's own companion sync-badge feature, which also drives `serialize`/`_writeStorage` repeatedly) passes unchanged. No Theme Contract/Engine V2 Scene Model/Builder change — this fix directly serves the standing "at no moment under any circumstances there should be any data loss" requirement; confined to `js/projectManager.js`. **Disclosed for the user's own confirmation**: this closes a real, severe, independently-discovered defect very plausibly connected to the reported symptom, but its exact reproduction shape (object vanishes vs. object frozen-with-stale-content) doesn't perfectly match the video's own frame-by-frame evidence — if this fix doesn't fully resolve what was recorded, the video's own precise sequence of actions (was there a reload, a "Load Cloud Version" prompt, or something else immediately before the frozen moment?) is the next thing needed to close the gap.

- "Change Look" Silently Orphans the Editor's Own Canvas — the Real, Confirmed, Byte-for-Byte Match to the Video-Reported Freeze (the previous entry's own artworkTheme fix was shipped and disclosed as possibly not matching the video's exact symptom — the user confirmed exactly that: **"still no change . bug reported in video is as it is."** Continued the investigation from that exact honest gap rather than re-guessing: re-read the entire write→override→redraw→render pipeline a second time end to end (`SceneEngine.setContentOverride`, `_layerOverride`, `PageRuntime.getActivePage`, `window.redrawPreview`/`draw()`, `SlideRenderer.buildPayload`/`.render()`, `_layerDrawText`, `_layerVisual`, `_pushLayerObject`) and confirmed, once again, that every piece is internally consistent on its own — the write always lands on the same live slide object every reader reads back from, the Words field and the canvas draw resolve content through byte-identical override logic, and `SlideRenderer.init(cv,opts)` is fully synchronous with no async gap of its own. Since the mechanism itself kept checking out, the investigation shifted to every OTHER place `SlideRenderer.init()` retargets the module's own ONE shared canvas reference away from `#previewCanvas` and back — `js/thumbnails.js` (already fixed, an earlier ThumbnailEngine-clobber sprint), `js/pageOps.js`'s `exportPage` (confirmed fully synchronous, safe), `js/publishStudio.js`'s three swap-then-restore pairs (all confirmed synchronous with an unconditional restore even on a render exception, safe) — and finally `js/creationFlow.js`, which had two independent producers of the exact same class of retarget: `paintPreview()` (Screen 2's carousel, which correctly restores via `_restoreEditorCanvas()` right after building its grid — a pre-existing, correct precedent) and `_renderChangeRepresentationScreen()`/`_repCard()` (the Context Panel's "🔄 Change Look" shortcut, reachable at any time from inside an already-open Workspace, unlike Screen 2). **The bug, confirmed by direct code read**: `_repCard(r,selected,onClick,themeId)` — used only by `_renderChangeRepresentationScreen`, which is reached only from Context Panel's real, always-present "🔄 Change Look" button in the default/Personalize view (`_appendRepresentationRow`/`_buildChangeLookTile`) — calls `_renderCarouselCanvas(canvas,theme,r)` for every card that resolves a real theme, and that function calls `SlideRenderer.init(canvas,{dpr:1,adaptiveViewport:true})`, repointing the module's one shared canvas target at THAT card's own freshly-created temp `<canvas>` element. **Nothing in this entire flow ever pointed it back** — neither `_renderChangeRepresentationScreen` itself, nor `_applyRepresentationToCurrentSlide` (fired when a card is clicked), nor `_closeChangeRepresentation` (fired by both the header's "← Back" button AND, internally, by `_applyRepresentationToCurrentSlide` itself) — even though the exact restore helper this flow needed, `_restoreEditorCanvas()`, already existed in this same file, purpose-built for precisely this, and was simply never wired into this specific screen. The consequence: the moment a Story Author opens "Change Look" on any real themed project (the overwhelmingly common, highly plausible real action a "Forest Sync"-named World would see), `#previewCanvas` is silently, permanently orphaned — `SlideRenderer.render()` keeps drawing onto whichever card's now-hidden/soon-to-be-removed temp canvas was rendered last, for the rest of the session, no matter how many times `window.redrawPreview()` fires afterward (a content edit, a selection change, an autosave tick — all of them). Every downstream reader that reads the MODEL directly (the Words textarea, `SlideRenderer.getSceneElements()`, the Object Strip) keeps showing the edit correctly; only the visible canvas element the user is actually looking at never repaints again — **an exact, byte-for-byte match to "the Words field correctly updates but the canvas stays frozen... persisting through deselect and reselect,"** and consistent rather than timing-dependent, exactly matching "bug reported in video is as it is." **Fix**: `_renderChangeRepresentationScreen` now calls the pre-existing `_restoreEditorCanvas()` immediately after building its card grid — mirroring `paintPreview()`'s own already-correct precedent exactly, so the shared canvas target is corrected the moment the grid finishes rendering rather than only whenever the screen eventually closes, which also means a background redraw triggered while the screen is still open can never be misdirected either. **Verified via a live A/B reproduction, not asserted**: a new Playwright script (seeding a real 2-Representation theme with a `cover-titles`/`author` World-owned text Layer Pack, driving the actual UI — select the sanity-check object, deselect, open the real "🔄 Change Look" button, confirm 2 real `<canvas>` Page Style cards render, back out via the real `.creation-flow-back` button, reselect the World-owned object, edit its Words field via the real Selection Action Strip popup, then sample the canvas's own title-region pixels before/after) — on the UNMODIFIED code (`git stash`), the model and Words field both correctly show "Forest Adventure" after the edit while the sampled canvas pixel count stays byte-for-byte frozen (1501 before, 1501 after — literally zero change, even after an explicit extra `redrawPreview()` call), the exact reported bug reproduced on demand for the first time in this whole investigation; with the fix restored, the identical flow shows the canvas genuinely repainting (1251 → 1010, matching the exact "shorter text after removing 'A '" pixel delta this session's own earlier reproductions established as the correct signature) — 9/9 assertions passing where the baseline scored 8/9 with the one failure being this exact symptom. Full regression: the three existing "Change Look" scratch suites (overflow/live-render/orientation) pass completely unchanged, confirming this fix is purely additive; `regression.js`/`final_qa.js` (stale, timing out on a pre-Traveller-Gateway locator, confirmed via `git stash` to already fail identically on the unmodified baseline), `combined_regression_check.js`'s own pre-existing, already-documented "sticker did not move" Object Strip drag bug (also confirmed via `git stash` to be baseline-identical, unrelated to this fix), and `museum_gallery_regression_check.js`'s own stale locator (likewise baseline-identical) are all confirmed pre-existing staleness, not caused by this change; `museum_realfile_regression.js` (a real, unmodified `themes/MuseumGallery.vtheme` render) passes cleanly. Both `goldenBuild.js` suites (World Builder v1 and v2, 30/30 each) pass unchanged, confirming zero Builder-tooling impact — this fix is confined entirely to root Studio. No Theme Contract/Engine V2 Scene Model/Builder change — this fix directly serves Creator Governing Rule #5 (Publish Fidelity, and by extension every rule that depends on the center pane actually being the live, correct view of a Scene); confined to one function, `_renderChangeRepresentationScreen`, in `js/creationFlow.js`.

- The Real Root Cause of the Video-Reported Freeze — Cross-Origin Canvas Tainting Silently Orphaning `SlideRenderer`'s Shared Canvas Target (a fifth, decisive pass on the same reported bug, closing a gap the four prior fixes above — all real, all shipped, none of them the actual cause — left open. The user's own live diagnostic run on their real "Forest Sync - cloud 1.2" project threw `Uncaught SecurityError: Failed to execute 'toDataURL' on 'HTMLCanvasElement': Tainted canvases may not be exported.` — the first genuinely new evidence in this whole investigation — followed by independent confirmation that the same freeze reproduces on a SECOND, freshly-authored theme after "removed places, added image background and a text as an experience," ruling out project-specific corruption and confirming a real, general mechanism. **Root cause**: `AssetStore.resolve(ref,opts)`'s third resolution tier (`_resolveFromStorage`/`_signedUrlFor`) can return a genuinely cross-origin Supabase Storage signed URL — reached whenever the local IndexedDB blob cache misses (a fresh device, a cleared cache, a Magic-Card-recalled project, or, newly confirmed, any Published Theme with an Experience-authored image drawn in Studio, since Publish always routes through Supabase Storage). None of the three `new Image()` constructions in the codebase that consume this resolved src (`js/projectManager.js`'s `loadImageFromDataURL`, `renderer/slideRenderer.js`'s `_ensureDecorationImage`, `js/pictureStudio.js`'s `open()`) ever set `img.crossOrigin` before assigning `.src` — confirmed via a codebase-wide grep returning zero matches for `crossOrigin` anywhere in `js/` before this fix — so drawing such an Image onto any canvas silently taints it, with zero visible error at the point of drawing (drawing/rendering continues to work; only a LATER `toDataURL()`/`getImageData()`/`toBlob()` call throws, and tainting propagates canvas-to-canvas via `drawImage`). `js/thumbnails.js`'s `ThumbnailEngine.generate()` — already fixed once for the unrelated "restore-step-nested-inside-a-risky-try-block" bug — creates its own throwaway `temp` canvas, retargets `SlideRenderer`'s ONE shared module-level canvas pointer at it via `SlideRenderer.init(temp,...)`, renders the World's own image background onto it (tainting `temp`), then `drawImage`s `temp` onto a second throwaway `thumbCanvas` (propagating the taint) and calls `thumbCanvas.toDataURL('image/png')` — which throws. Since the restore-to-`#previewCanvas` step already sits OUTSIDE the try/catch (the earlier fix), the throw itself no longer skips the restore — but the restore only re-points `SlideRenderer`'s canvas TARGET back; it does nothing about the fact that `#previewCanvas` itself becomes independently, permanently tainted the very next time that same cross-origin image is drawn directly onto it (e.g. via `window.redrawPreview()` after the image's own `onload` fires) — and while a tainted canvas continues to draw and display correctly (tainting only blocks pixel-data READS, never writes), a decisive screenshot-based reproduction proved the visible canvas genuinely stops updating in this exact scenario, matching "the actual changes do keep happening but visual confirmations are not there" precisely. **Fix**: `img.crossOrigin='anonymous'` added to all three `new Image()` construction sites, immediately after construction and before `.src` is ever assigned — matching Supabase Storage's own real, permissive `Access-Control-Allow-Origin:*` default (confirmed via a real second HTTP server in the reproduction sending genuine CORS headers), so the browser requests the image in CORS mode and the resulting canvas is never tainted at all. `js/thumbnails.js`'s `ThumbnailEngine.generate()` also had its restore-guarantee discipline reinforced with a fuller explanation of the SecurityError root cause in its own comments (no functional change beyond the prior sprint's own fix, which already moved the restore outside the try/catch). **Verified via a two-stage git-stash A/B Playwright reproduction, the first attempt of which initially produced a false pass**: a first reproduction script (`taint_freeze_repro.js`) seeded a synthetic Story theme with a Scene-hosted image-background Decoration Layer Pack entry, stubbed `AssetStore.resolve()` to return a real, second-HTTP-server-hosted cross-origin image URL, and checked for tainting — but reported "Image server received 0 request(s)" on both the fixed and unmodified code, a false negative traced to a bug in the TEST itself, not the app: the synthetic Layer Pack entry used the field name `decoration:{kind:'image', src:'...'}`, but `renderer/slideRenderer.js`'s real `_layerDrawDecorationImage` reads `d.image`, not `d.src` (confirmed against `tools/world-builder-v2/js/services/builder.js`'s own real compiled output, `decoration:{kind:'image', image:assetPath,...}`) — so the image was never resolved or requested at all, and the "not tainted" result was uninformative rather than a genuine pass. Corrected to `decoration:{kind:'image', image:'vihu-asset:...'}` and re-run: on the git-stashed UNMODIFIED baseline, the image genuinely loads (1 real HTTP request) and `canvas.toDataURL()`/`getImageData()` both throw `SecurityError: The canvas has been tainted by cross-origin data` — matching the user's own live diagnostic exactly. A second, more decisive script (`taint_freeze_repro2.js`) was built specifically because `getImageData()`/`toDataURL()` throw identically whether the canvas is "tainted but still drawing fine" or "genuinely frozen because `SlideRenderer`'s target got silently orphaned" — those two states can't be told apart via the Canvas API once tainted. Using `page.screenshot({clip:canvasBox})` instead (a browser-level CDP frame capture, immune to Canvas API tainting restrictions entirely, since it never calls `getImageData`/`toDataURL`) and comparing SHA-256 hashes of the canvas region before/after a forced content edit gave the decisive, unambiguous signal: on the unmodified baseline, the model correctly updates ("Forest Adventure") but the screenshot hash is BYTE-IDENTICAL before and after (`c898f04c2292` both times) — the canvas is genuinely, visually frozen, not merely tainted-but-still-drawing; with the fix applied, the hash changes (`c898f04c2292`→`a433aaacce24`), confirming the canvas genuinely repaints. Full regression across 9 directly-relevant existing scratch Playwright suites (`text_resize_grid_test.js`, `commitments_test.js`, `selection_action_strip_test.js`, `selection_strip_pencil_fix.js`, `canvas_click_visual_repro.js`, `paperbg_hittest_repro.js`, `sync_charm_test.js`, `repaint_fix_verify.js`, `museum_realfile_regression.js`) all pass unchanged, plus a second batch of 6 scripts (`scene_viewport_test.js`, `multi_place_test.js`, `combined_regression_check.js`, `scene_object_test.js`, `runtime_pass_test.js`, `publish_stages.js`) that fail on both the fixed AND the unmodified-baseline code (a stale Traveller-Gateway-skip helper predating several of these scripts, and the already-documented pre-existing "sticker did not move" Object Strip drag bug) — confirmed via `git stash` to be pre-existing, unrelated staleness, not a regression introduced by this fix. Both `goldenBuild.js` suites (World Builder v1 and v2, 30/30 each) pass unchanged, confirming zero Builder-tooling impact. **Disclosed honestly, given the history of four prior rejected fixes on this exact report**: this is the first fix in this whole investigation that reproduces the reported symptom on demand, on the unmodified baseline, via a technique immune to the very tainting the bug itself causes — the strongest evidence obtained so far — but per this session's own established discipline, it should only be considered fully resolved once the user has verified it against their own real project. No Theme Contract/Engine V2 Scene Model/Builder change; confined to `js/projectManager.js`, `renderer/slideRenderer.js`, `js/pictureStudio.js`, and `js/thumbnails.js`.

- Home Button — a New Theme No Longer Silently Inherits the Previous Theme's Story-Owned Content (the user's own words, right after confirming the crossOrigin freeze fix above was finally resolved — "it seems to have been fixed. finally." — followed immediately by a fresh, distinct, clearly-reproducible bug: "start working on one theme. press home button. start working on new theme. studio owned changes done on first theme reflects on second theme as well. i checked this with doodle function." **Root cause, confirmed by direct code read**: the Home button previously called `CreationFlow.start()` directly against the SAME live, in-memory `AppState` — `js/creationFlow.js`'s `_finish(type,theme,representation)` only calls `PageOps.addBefore(0)` to create a first page when `AppState.slides.length===0`, a guard designed for the genuine first-boot case; since a mid-session Home press never actually emptied `AppState.slides`, that guard silently never re-fired for the "second" theme selection — Home never actually started a NEW project, it just re-skinned the CURRENT one in place via `ThemeEngine.applyArtworkTheme`/`applyTheme`, carrying every Story-owned object (stickers, Doodles, Words edits, anything a Story Author had already added) straight over onto the newly-picked theme. `AppState` (`js/state.js`) is one scattered, module-level `const` singleton with fields set from many different files (`project.theme`/`.artworkTheme`/`.creationType`/`.representationId`/`.id`/`.bookTitle`/`.title`/`.author`/`.createdDate`/`.modifiedDate`, `slides`, `currentSlide`) and no single function anywhere resets all of them — `ProjectManager.discardSession()` only clears the `localStorage` session key, doing nothing to the live in-memory state at all. **Fix, reusing an already-proven precedent rather than inventing a fragile hand-reset**: `js/publishStudio.js`'s own `_makeAnotherStory()` hit this exact class of problem already and solved it the only reliable way — discard the saved session, then a soft `window.location.reload()` for a genuinely blank `AppState`, since no function exists that resets every scattered field reliably. The Home button now does the identical thing: `ProjectManager.discardSession()` (best-effort, wrapped in a defensive try/catch matching this codebase's own established cross-module hook discipline) followed by `window.location.reload()`. **Confirmed safe, not merely convenient**: the current project is never actually lost by this reload — `CreatorProjectStore.upsert()` (called from inside every `_writeStorage()` autosave, part of this session's own earlier Cloud-Primary Project Storage work) already durably persists a separate "My Projects" catalog entry per project id, completely independent of the single session-slot key `discardSession()` clears, so the just-abandoned project stays fully recoverable via "My Projects" — matching the Home button's own original "autosave already covers the current project" reasoning, now actually true rather than only assumed. After a discard, `js/app.js`'s `_beginBoot()` correctly routes straight to `_startCreationFlow()` with no restore-modal prompt (`ProjectManager.getSessionStatus()` returns `{state:'none'}`), landing cleanly on Creation Flow Screen 1. **Verified via a decisive git-stash A/B Playwright reproduction, not merely reasoned about**: a new script drove the real UI end-to-end — register two demo themes, pick Theme A, add a real Doodle sticker via the actual "Add Something" accordion, click the real `#homeBtn`, wait for the resulting reload and skip the Traveller Gateway (which plays on every boot), pick Theme B, and confirm zero stickers carried over with a genuinely fresh single-page project. On the git-stashed UNMODIFIED baseline, the reproduction showed the EXACT SAME sticker id (`sticker-ms0k1j9x-keh1`) present on "Theme B's fresh page" — byte-for-byte confirming the reported leak; with the fix restored, Theme B correctly shows zero stickers and exactly one fresh page. Full regression across `text_resize_grid_test.js`, `commitments_test.js`, `selection_action_strip_test.js`, and `sync_charm_test.js` all pass unchanged; `myprojects_test2.js`'s own pre-existing failure (a stale `.creation-flow-card:has-text("Showcase My Artwork")` locator, timing out) was independently confirmed via `git stash` to already fail identically on the unmodified baseline, matching this session's own extensively-documented "predates the Traveller Gateway's own skip-helper convention" staleness class — not a regression caused by this fix. No Theme Contract/Engine V2 Scene Model/Builder change; confined to one click handler in `js/app.js`.

- The Grid — Auditing Every Object Kind Against Builder's Honor Commitments (a direct, requested audit: "ok now lets work out the grid for each object for what can be done against the builder honor commitments" — Governing Rule #2, Guardrails: "Every object on Scene honors the guardrails." Read `_resolvePlacePermissions`/`getPlacePermissions`, `_supportsResize`, `_layerVisual`, `_pushLayerObject`, `_appendWorldObjectEditControl`/`mountQuickEditControl`, and the reorder-bucket functions (`_mergedReorderableIds`/`_worldBucketOrder`/`getReorderBucket`) end to end to build a real grid — 7 World-owned object kinds (Artwork Place/Frame, Decoration Colour Fill, Decoration Image, Decoration Shape, Decoration Legacy Effect [spotlight/paperTexture/shadowWash], Text Layer Pack, and the separate declarative Sticker Layer Pack kind — Wax-Seal-style theme glyphs) × 6 capabilities (Visible, Move, Resize, Reorder, Edit Content, Decoration Slot) — rather than guessing which cells were real. **Confirmed one row was structurally different and never got the same treatment as the rest**: `type:'sticker'` (a declarative theme glyph, a genuinely separate code path from `type:'decoration'`/`type:'text'`, sharing only the `type` string with Story-owned Sticker-Studio-placed stickers) surfaced two real, confirmed gaps. **(1) Resize was structurally offered but silently inert**: `_supportsResize`'s own type check has included `'sticker'` since the earlier "Resize is completely inert for every World-owned object" fix, but that fix's own scope (per its own CLAUDE.md entry) only ever extended a size-override read to fill/image/shape/legacy-decoration kinds — `_layerDrawSticker` itself never read `ov.size` at all, so a moveable Wax Seal showed real resize handles that visibly did nothing when dragged. Fixed by reading `ov.size` (averaged across w/h, since a sticker's own resize is corner-only and uniformly aspect-locked in `js/app.js`, matching the same discipline `_supportsResize`'s own comment already documents for text) into the glyph font-size / circle radius. **(2) A glyph-less colour-fallback sticker's Colour edit control was a dead end in two separate places**: `_layerVisual`'s `type==='sticker'` branch never read `ov.fillColor` back — unlike its own sibling `kind==='fill'` decoration branch right above it, which already does — so the edit popup always reopened showing the stale, original authored colour rather than whatever the Story Author last picked, and the Object Strip thumbnail swatch never reflected an edit either; separately, `_layerDrawSticker`'s own circle-fill paint never read `ov.fillColor` either, so even a correctly-displayed edit never actually changed what rendered on canvas. Both fixed to match the identical `ov.fillColor` precedence `_layerDrawDecoration`'s own `fill` kind already established. **Every other cell in the grid was confirmed already correct, not assumed**: Places get a dedicated grab-handle for Move but deliberately no resize (no size-override mechanism exists in `_placePixelRectFor`, a disclosed, intentional scope decision, not a bug); Frame Look/Style/Artwork Presentation correctly gate on `editable` while Add/Replace Artwork/Crop-Rotate stay always-available regardless (the picture itself is Story content, never Theme-authored chrome); Reorder is uniformly available across every kind including Places, gated purely on `moveable`; a glyph-bearing sticker (has a real emoji, e.g. an actual Wax Seal) correctly shows no edit control at all — `_layerVisual` resolves `kind:'glyph'`, which `_appendWorldObjectEditControl` has no branch for, matching this codebase's own established "that kind of edit isn't available in Creator yet" disclosure pattern rather than a bug; Decoration Slot ("✨ Add your own decoration here," reusing Sticker Studio end to end) flows uniformly off `layer.decorationSlot` regardless of `type`, though Builder's own authoring UI only ever sets it for decoration-kind Experiences today; there is deliberately no Story-Author-facing Show/Hide toggle anywhere — `visible:false` is a permanent, Builder-authored decision with no Creator-side override, by design. Verified via a new synthetic-theme Playwright test (a `type:'sticker'` Layer Pack entry, no glyph, `moveable:true`/`editable:true`, target `'slide'` so no picture upload is needed) driving real `SceneEngine.setSize`/`.setContentOverride` calls exactly as a real resize-drag/Colour-swatch edit would, then sampling canvas pixels with a tolerance band (a small circle's own anti-aliased stroke ring makes exact-integer pixel matching unreliable, so the decisive check is "closer to the new colour than the old one," not an exact RGB match) — 6/6 assertions confirm both fixes: the render-tree bbox genuinely grows to the real size override, `_layerVisual` reflects the fillColor override, and the canvas paint genuinely shifts to the new colour. Full regression across `text_resize_grid_test.js`, `commitments_test.js`, `bug332_334_335_verify.js`, and `museum_realfile_regression.js` passes unchanged; `scene_object_test.js`/`three_bugs_check.js` fail identically with zero Traveller-Gateway-skip handling of their own (confirmed via grep, not via a full git-stash A/B, since this fix touches only sticker-specific drawing code with no relationship whatsoever to the boot/Gateway sequence those two scripts stall on) — the same, already extensively-documented pre-existing staleness class this session's own history has confirmed dozens of times, unrelated to this fix. No Theme Contract/Engine V2 Scene Model/Builder change — this fix directly serves Creator Governing Rule #2 (Guardrails); confined to two functions, `_layerVisual` and `_layerDrawSticker`, in `renderer/slideRenderer.js`.

- World-Owned Text Objects Gain Full Story-Author Control — Rotation, Opacity, Typography (the direct follow-up to "The Grid" audit's own Text row, taken to completion: the audit found Rotation/Opacity "not built for this kind" and Font/Size/Weight/Style/Colour/Alignment "fixed by Builder as Theme chrome, never exposed to the Story Author" — presented as a review, the user answered directly, twice: "if capability is not built in we will need to build in the capability" and, once asked whether Font/Typography (a deliberate design lock, distinct wording from Rotation/Opacity's plain "not built") was in scope too, "font/typo needs to be built in." All three are now real, reachable Story-Author capabilities for a moveable/editable World-owned Text Layer Pack entry — a genuine escalation from documenting the Honor Grid to closing its gaps, per the user's own explicit direction. **A separate factual correction, resolved by code, not assumption**: the same review claimed Reorder was "uniformly gated on `moveable`" for every kind — re-verified against `_worldBucketOrder`/`_mergedReorderableIds` (`renderer/slideRenderer.js`) and confirmed TRUE for World-owned objects (a `moveable:false` Layer Pack entry is genuinely excluded from every reorder bucket) but FALSE for Story-owned ones, where the code's own comment is explicit — a locked Scene element/Sticker "stays reorderable even while its own position is frozen," honors-free by design, closing the loop on why the table's Story-Own rows needed to go fully blank. **`js/sceneEngine.js`** gains `setOpacity(slide,id,opacity)`, mirroring `setRotation`'s exact Sprint-6.6.1 "clear at the neutral default" convention (opacity 1, the value every untouched object already renders at, clears the override rather than storing a redundant 1) — `setRotation` itself already existed, generic and already proven for Frame rotation, just never wired into any Text draw path. `setContentOverride`'s own doc comment is widened from its original `'fillColor'/'content'/'image'/'color'` field list to also document `'fontFamily'/'fontSize'/'fontWeight'/'fontStyle'/'alignment'` — the underlying `entry[field]=value` was already field-name-agnostic, so no mutator logic changed, only what's now actually written through it. **`renderer/slideRenderer.js`'s `_layerDrawText`** (the generic-content branch only — `_drawMuseumCaption` is a deliberate, disclosed scope boundary: it has no in-place quick-edit popup today at all, since `_layerVisual` already returns `null` for `t.source==='museumCaption'`, so there's no UI path to reach these new fields there regardless of render-side readiness) now reads `ov.fontFamily`/`ov.fontSize`/`ov.fontWeight`/`ov.fontStyle`/`ov.alignment` (`ov.color` was already read) alongside the existing position/size overrides, and applies `ov.rotation`/`ov.opacity` as a `x.globalAlpha` set plus a translate-rotate-translate transform anchored at the already-resolved (post-position-override) `drawX`/`drawY` — both riding on the function's own pre-existing `x.save()`/`x.restore()` wrap, so neither needs its own cleanup; absent any override this is byte-identical to before, confirmed via the existing Museum Gallery regression. **Guardrail gating, a real architectural nuance found while wiring the UI, not assumed**: Rotation is a spatial transform, gated on `moveable` (Honor 2) — the SAME bucket Move/Resize already live in — genuinely independent of whether the object's CONTENT is editable; every other new control (Font/Size/Weight/Style/Colour/Alignment/Opacity) stays gated on `editable` (Honor 3), alongside Words. This meant `js/selectionActionStrip.js`'s Edit-button visibility (previously hidden whenever `!editable` for a non-Place Scene Object) had to widen to `!editable && !moveable` — a `moveable:true`/`editable:false` object now correctly still shows a reachable Edit button for its Rotation slider alone, verified directly rather than assumed reachable. **`js/contextPanel.js`**: `mountQuickEditControl`'s own gate dropped its blanket `!sceneObj.editable` check (previously mounting nothing at all for a non-editable object, Rotation included) — `_appendWorldObjectEditControl` now decides per-honor internally and reports back whether anything was actually mounted; content controls (Words plus the new Font Family/Size/Weight/Style/Colour/Alignment/Opacity block) stay wrapped in `if(sceneObj.editable)`, Rotation stands alone gated on `sceneObj.moveable && v.kind==='text'` — deliberately scoped to `v.kind==='text'` only for this pass (a real, disclosed boundary: Decoration Image/Shape's own `d.rotation`/`d.alpha` are Builder-authored COMPILED fields, not Story-Author override fields, and adding a Rotation slider for those kinds today would silently do nothing, a dead-end UI the Grid's own next-object rounds will need to resolve on their own terms, not smuggled in here). New `WORLD_TEXT_FONT_OPTIONS`/`WORLD_TEXT_WEIGHT_OPTIONS` are this module's own small copy — same option set and field-naming convention (`fontFamily`/`fontSize`/`fontWeight`/`fontStyle`/`alignment`) as `js/cardDesigner.js`'s own, separate, pre-existing fixed-Text-furniture typography system (`_buildTextControls`, Sprint 4.4/9.4 — Story Text/Footer/Page Number/Handle, writing to the completely different `cardOverrides.textElements` bag) — kept duplicated rather than cross-imported, matching this codebase's own established per-module vocabulary-table precedent (`js/objectStrip.js`'s `FRIENDLY_TYPE` vs. `js/selectionActionStrip.js`'s own `_friendlyIcon` copy), so a Story Author sees identical vocabulary in both places even though the two write to genuinely separate override bags for genuinely separate object kinds. Three small new helpers (`_makeRangeRow`/`_makeSelectRow`/`_makeIconChoiceRow`) build the new controls in this module's own plain-DOM style, reusing the already-proven `.designer-row`/`.designer-row-label`/`.text-slider-label`/`.icon-row`/`.icon-card`/`.icon-card.active` classes cardDesigner.js's own sibling controls already established — confirmed via a direct CSS read before assuming any of them were free, not guessed. **`css/style.css`** adds `.context-select`/`.context-range-input`/`.context-range-value`, matching `.context-textarea`'s own visual weight, scoped `width:100%` for the popup's own established ~200px narrow-widget convention (the same scoping `.selection-action-edit-panel .context-btn`/`.context-textarea` already needed), plus `flex-wrap` + `flex:1 1 auto` on the popup's own icon-rows so Style/Alignment's icon-card choices wrap sensibly at that width instead of overflowing. Verified via a new 26-assertion Playwright suite (`text_object_full_build_check.js`, scratch-only) driving three synthetic Layer Pack entries through the real UI end to end — a moveable+editable object shows all 9 controls (Words, Font Family, Font Size, Weight, Style, Colour, Alignment, Opacity, Rotation), every one of which genuinely writes its own override field and is confirmed via the live model afterward, with the render tree bbox confirmed to reflect the new, larger-font content; a moveable-only object correctly shows Rotation alone (Edit button reachable, content controls absent); an editable-only object correctly shows every content control but no Rotation. Full regression across 11 directly-relevant existing suites (`bug332_334_335_verify.js`, `commitments_test.js`, `sticker_layer_grid_fix_check.js`, `text_resize_grid_test.js`, `selection_action_strip_test.js`, `selection_strip_pencil_fix.js`, `repaint_fix_verify.js`, `canvas_click_visual_repro.js`, `paperbg_hittest_repro.js`, `museum_realfile_regression.js`, `three_rules_audit.js`) passes unchanged, zero console errors; two further checks (`all_object_guardrails_test.js`'s own Creation-Flow-locator timeout, `place_guardrails_test.js`'s own "place did not move" drag assertion) were confirmed via a `git stash` A/B to fail identically on the unmodified baseline — the same, already-extensively-documented pre-Traveller-Gateway-skip-helper and pre-existing Object-Strip-drag staleness classes this session's own history has repeatedly confirmed, unrelated to this change. Both `goldenBuild.js` suites (World Builder v1 and v2, 30/30 each) pass unchanged, confirming zero Builder-tooling impact — this build is confined entirely to root Studio. No Theme Contract/Engine V2 Scene Model/Builder architecture change — this directly serves Creator Governing Rules #3 (Refinement) and #4 (Personalization), on top of the Guardrails discipline (#2) the audit itself was already grounded in; confined to `js/sceneEngine.js`, `renderer/slideRenderer.js`, `js/selectionActionStrip.js`, `js/contextPanel.js`, and `css/style.css`. The Honor Grid artifact (the user's own live-edited table, republished with these three rows corrected to reflect the now-built reality) is the next-object queue's own reference going forward, per the user's own stated sequencing: "once we are done with text object we will go to next object.")

- World-Owned Text Quick-Edit Popup — Compact 2-Column Layout, No Scroll (a direct, screenshot-driven follow-up to the just-shipped Text object build: "the implementation is clean, the UI is not. all options are not visible. scroll is needed but i dont want to put scroll. need alternative way for the context menu so that it does not looks cramped, options are visible, scroll is last way out." **Root cause**: the popup's own `_appendWorldObjectEditControl` stacked all 9 controls (Words, Font Family, Font Size, Weight, Style, Colour, Alignment, Opacity, Rotation) one per row inside a 230px-max-width strip — at a realistic browser window height the popup simply ran off the bottom of the viewport, invisible with no scrollbar of its own to reveal it. **Fix, mirroring an already-established codebase convention rather than inventing a new one**: `js/contextPanel.js`'s `_makeRangeRow`/`_makeSelectRow`/`_makeIconChoiceRow` all gained an optional-append mode (pass
