`parent=null` to just build and return the row, unattached) alongside a new `_makeColorRow` (factored out of the previously inline colour-swatch code, now shared by both the color/shape-kind Colour row and the text-kind Colour row) and a new `_pairRow(container,cellA,cellB)` helper — mirrors World Builder's own established `_fieldRow()`/`_buildFieldGroup()` pairing convention (`tools/world-builder-v2`'s Inspector, Sprint B2.0.4, already solved this exact "too many stacked fields, not enough vertical room" problem the same way) — laying two short field rows side by side on one shared line, with a lone cell (no partner) spanning the row's own full width so it's never left half-empty. `_appendWorldObjectEditControl`'s text branch now builds Rotation FIRST (order-independent, since it's the one control that can appear with or without any content controls at all, depending on the `editable`/`moveable` guardrail split), then pairs Font Family|Weight, Style|Alignment, Font Size|Opacity, and finally Colour|Rotation — Rotation joins Colour's row when both are present (a `moveable:true`/`editable:true` object), or Colour goes solo full-width when Rotation isn't reachable (`moveable:false`), or Rotation itself falls through to one final full-width row when Colour isn't reachable (`editable:false`) — never silently dropped either way. Reduces the popup from 11 stacked blocks down to 7 (Words label+textarea, a sublabel, and 4 paired rows instead of 3+8). `css/style.css`: `.selection-action-strip`'s `max-width` widened from 230px/280px (side-gutter/top-fallback variants) to 300px/340px — safe because `js/selectionActionStrip.js`'s `_positionWidget()` already re-measures the strip's real rendered width on every call and falls back correctly (left gutter, then normal-flow above the canvas) if a wider popup genuinely doesn't fit either gutter, so zero JS changes were needed to keep the prior sprint's own hard "never overlaps the canvas" constraint intact; a genuine last-resort safety net (`max-height:calc(100vh - 96px); overflow-y:auto;`) was added to the strip itself, confirmed via a deliberately extreme 1366×380px viewport (smaller than any real device) to correctly degrade to the popup's own internal scrollbar rather than a broken layout or a whole-page scroll, while never actually engaging at any of the three realistic sizes tested. New `.context-field-row{display:flex;gap:8px}` / `.context-field-row .designer-row{flex:1;min-width:0;margin-bottom:0}` implement the pairing; `.selection-action-edit-panel`'s own row spacing was tightened slightly (`gap:8px`→`6px`, `.designer-row` margin-bottom scoped down to 8px) for a few more px of breathing room. Verified via a new 24-assertion Playwright suite (`popup_layout_check.js`, scratch-only) at three realistic viewport sizes — including one matching the reported screenshot's own short/wide proportions (1366×600) — confirming zero page-level scroll, all 9 controls genuinely visible (non-zero size, bottom edge within the viewport, not merely present in the DOM), the popup itself never overflowing the viewport, and the "never overlaps the canvas" invariant still holding at the new, wider size; a companion screenshot (zoomed to just the popup) visually confirms the compact 2-column layout renders cleanly with every control reachable at a glance. Full regression across the existing `text_object_full_build_check.js` (26/26, unchanged — every interaction selector queries by control class, agnostic to the new row-pairing DOM nesting), `selection_action_strip_test.js` (15/15), `selection_strip_pencil_fix.js` (18/18), `repaint_fix_verify.js` (8/8), `canvas_click_visual_repro.js` (6/6), `paperbg_hittest_repro.js` (3/3), `commitments_test.js`, `sync_charm_test.js`, and `text_resize_grid_test.js` (13/13) all pass unchanged, zero console errors. Both `goldenBuild.js` suites (World Builder v1 and v2, 30/30 each) pass unchanged, confirming zero Builder-tooling impact. No Theme Contract/Engine V2 Scene Model/Builder architecture change — this fix directly serves Creator Governing Rule #3 (Refinement): the reachable controls the Guardrails already promised now genuinely fit and are visible; confined to `js/contextPanel.js` and `css/style.css`.)

- World-Owned Text Quick-Edit Popup — Position:Fixed, Sidebar Overlap Allowed, Auto-Growing Words Field (a SECOND, real-content follow-up on the same popup: "this is not what is intended" — a screenshot showed the widened (300px) popup from the entry above STILL scrolling internally against genuine production content (a real 3-line Cover-page byline, "A Story / by / Vihaan Sharma"), not the short synthetic single-line text the prior fix's own test suite had used. The user then, mid-turn, explicitly relaxed the standing constraint further: **"context menu can overlap on right and left panel that should be ok if needed."** **Root cause of why widening alone couldn't be pushed further**: `.selection-action-strip` was `position:absolute` inside `.preview-area`, and `.preview-area{overflow:hidden}` (css line ~406) silently CLIPPED any popup content that tried to extend past `.preview-area`'s own edge into the sidebar — no matter how much genuine unused screen space the sidebar itself had, the popup could never legally grow into it under the old positioning model. **Fix**: switched to `position:fixed` (escapes `.preview-area`'s clipping entirely, since fixed positioning establishes its own containing block relative to the viewport — confirmed no ancestor sets `transform`/`filter`/`perspective`/`contain`, which would otherwise trap it inside a new containing block) and rewrote `js/selectionActionStrip.js`'s `_positionWidget()` around a real, load-bearing invariant instead of the old "must fit entirely inside the gutter" rule: whichever side is chosen, the widget's NEAR edge is always placed strictly on the far side of the canvas's own edge (structurally can never cross into it — the one constraint that stays hard even though it may now legitimately overlap a sidebar), and its own WIDTH is capped (not its position clamped) to whatever real room exists between that near edge and the true viewport edge — capping width rather than clamping position is what guarantees the far edge can never compute past the real screen, by construction, regardless of how little room is actually available; clamping position instead would risk sliding the far edge back across the canvas boundary when the popup is wider than the available room. The gate for choosing a side dropped from "the full ~300-440px must fit" down to "at least 160px of real room exists" (matching the CSS `min-width`) — a MUCH lower bar now that overlapping the sidebar is explicitly fine, so a side placement is chosen far more often, with the 'top' (position:static, normal-flow-above-canvas) fallback now reserved only for genuinely narrow viewports (below the `.workspace` media query's own ~768px single-column collapse, where there's no sidebar territory to overlap into at all). The CSS `max-width` ceiling stayed at 440px (already correct from the prior fix), but is now set as a per-instance INLINE style (computed from the real available room, never just the flat CSS default) so the popup naturally sizes itself down when less room exists rather than always claiming the full 440px. **The Words textarea auto-grows to fit real multi-line content, closing the actual visible symptom in the report**: `_openEditPanel()` now runs an autosize pass (`el.style.height='auto'; el.style.height=el.scrollHeight+'px'`) on every textarea AFTER `_positionWidget()` settles the popup's own final width (autosizing before that would measure against a stale width) and again live on every keystroke via one delegated `input` listener on `editPanelEl` — deliberately kept inside `selectionActionStrip.js` rather than `contextPanel.js`'s own textarea-building code, since this is popup-specific chrome behavior, not a change to the shared control itself (`ContextPanel.mountQuickEditControl()` stays the one real editing control both this popup and the right panel's own disclosure reuse, unchanged). `.selection-action-edit-panel .context-textarea` dropped its earlier `min-height:52px` override (which had actively SHRUNK it below the base 70px rule, the wrong direction for real content) in favour of `overflow-y:hidden`, so there's never a competing inner scrollbar while the JS-driven auto-grow does its job — the popup's own outer `overflow-y:auto` stays the one genuine last resort. Verified via three new Playwright suites: `popup_realcontent_check.js` (28 assertions, the exact real 3-line byline, at 3 realistic viewport sizes — zero page scroll, the textarea shows its own full content with `scrollHeight<=clientHeight` [no inner scroll], all 9 controls genuinely visible with no popup-internal scroll needed, the popup still never overlaps the canvas at any size, and — the decisive proof the relaxation is real, not just permitted — at a normal laptop size the popup's own right edge is confirmed to extend PAST `.preview-area`'s own right edge into the real sidebar's screen space, something the old `position:absolute`+`overflow:hidden` design could never do); `popup_narrow_top_fallback_check.js` (5 assertions, a genuinely narrow 700px viewport correctly falls back to the position:static 'top' mode, still never overlapping the canvas); and a re-run of the prior sprint's own extreme 1366×380px degrade check (still correctly falls back to the popup's own internal last-resort scrollbar, never a broken layout or a whole-page scroll). Full regression across `popup_layout_check.js` (24/24), `text_object_full_build_check.js` (26/26), `selection_strip_pencil_fix.js` (18/18), `repaint_fix_verify.js` (8/8), `canvas_click_visual_repro.js` (6/6), `paperbg_hittest_repro.js` (3/3), `commitments_test.js`, `sync_charm_test.js`, and `text_resize_grid_test.js` (13/13) all pass unchanged. `selection_action_strip_test.js`'s own "Strip never overlaps the canvas region (sits entirely above it)" assertion needed a genuine fix, not just a re-run: confirmed via a `git stash` A/B that at this test's own default viewport, the OLD code already fell back to the 'top' mode (its own 300px max-width didn't fit the real gutter there), which is exactly why that y-only "sits above" check happened to pass before — the NEW code correctly chooses 'side-right' instead at that same viewport (since the bar for choosing a side dropped so much), a deliberate, intended consequence of this fix, not a regression; the assertion was corrected to a real geometric (x-range AND y-range) overlap test matching this file's own newer test scripts, and now passes 15/15 confirming the popup genuinely never overlaps the canvas region regardless of which side it's anchored to. Both `goldenBuild.js` suites (World Builder v1 and v2, 30/30 each) pass unchanged, confirming zero Builder-tooling impact. No Theme Contract/Engine V2 Scene Model/Builder architecture change — this fix directly serves Creator Governing Rule #3 (Refinement), closing the gap the first popup-layout fix's own synthetic-content testing had missed; confined to `js/selectionActionStrip.js`, `css/style.css`, and one corrected test assertion.)

- World-Owned Text Style — Underline + Strikethrough, Folded Into the Same Row (a direct, two-part follow-up on the just-shipped Text object build: "why we dont have underline as a style , and strikethrough also" — an exploratory question — followed by an explicit go-ahead, "ok lets add it in the styles," scoped to the World-owned Text quick-edit popup this whole arc has been focused on. **The old Style row was a single-select, radio-style control** (`_makeIconChoiceRow`, Normal/Italic — clicking one deselected the other), architecturally unable to combine Underline/Strikethrough alongside Italic even if they'd been added as more options in the same list. **Fix**: a new `_makeMultiToggleRow(parent,labelText,choices,isActive,onToggle)` in `js/contextPanel.js` — a genuine multi-select sibling of `_makeIconChoiceRow`, each button toggling its own boolean independently rather than one replacing another — replaces the Style row's construction with three buttons, `[['italic','I'],['underline','U'],['strikethrough','S']]`; each glyph is styled (`font-style:italic`/`text-decoration:underline`/`text-decoration:line-through`) to actually look like what it does, doubling as its own live preview. Italic keeps riding the existing `fontStyle` field unchanged; Underline/Strikethrough are two new boolean fields on the same `elementOverrides` bag, written through the already-generic `SceneEngine.setContentOverride(slide,id,'underline'/'strikethrough',true|null)` — `setContentOverride`'s own doc comment (`js/sceneEngine.js`) is widened to document that a boolean field here is only ever `true` or cleared, never stored as `false`, matching the function's existing null-clears convention exactly (a naive `false` write would fail that check, since `false` is not null/undefined/`''`). **Canvas has no native `text-decoration`** — `renderer/slideRenderer.js`'s `_layerDrawText` gained real, manually-drawn stroke lines inside its existing per-line `lines.forEach` loop, spanning only THAT line's own measured width (`x.measureText(line).width`, never the shared `maxLineWidth` every line was wrapped against, so a shorter last line of a paragraph gets a correctly-shorter stroke) — baseline position is approximated per `vAlign` (`top`/`bottom`/`middle` each give `lineY` a different meaning) using standard font-metric ratios (ascent≈0.8×size, descent≈0.2×size, since full font metrics aren't reliably available across browsers/fonts), then offset a small fraction of size for each decoration's own conventional position (underline just below baseline, strikethrough through the middle of the glyph body); both ride on the function's own pre-existing `x.save()/x.restore()` transform block, so Rotation/Opacity apply to the strokes automatically with zero extra code. Absent either override this is a two-boolean-check no-op — byte-identical to before for every existing theme. New `.icon-label-glyph` CSS (15px, weight 600) replaces the plain 9px word-label size for these three single-character glyphs specifically, so "I"/"U"/"S" actually read at a glance rather than the tiny size every other `.icon-label` (full words like "Normal"/"Left") already uses correctly. **Verified via a Playwright test whose own sampling technique needed two real corrections before it could trust its own results, both disclosed rather than glossed over**: a first attempt sampling with a loose "dark = r,g,b<100" threshold registered zero delta between toggle-on and toggle-off states, because this synthetic test theme's own wall/background fallback (`theme.frame.color`, used when no explicit `wallTone` is authored — Sprint 9.7's `_resolveWallTone`) resolves to a dark navy (`#1D3457`, R=29/G=52/B=87) that the loose threshold wrongly counted as "dark" too, saturating every sampled row and hiding any real signal; tightened to `<20` per channel (well below navy's own R=29, comfortably catching pure-black text/stroke pixels) to fix this. A second, separate contamination was found via raw-pixel inspection: a SELECTED object's own gold selection outline (`#FFCB45`) paints directly over/near its bbox on the same live `#previewCanvas`, so sampling while selected returns gold, not the real content underneath — fixed by deselecting (`#selectionActionDeselect`) before every pixel check and reselecting to continue interacting, rather than trying to sample around the chrome. Once both were corrected, a delta-scan technique (compare per-row dark-pixel coverage before/after a toggle, rather than assuming an exact analytic Y — any static chrome present in both scans cancels out in the delta) confirmed: toggling Underline paints a new, near-continuous stroke (delta 1.00 at its own row) that genuinely disappears when toggled back off and the field is confirmed cleared (not stored as `false`); toggling Strikethrough independently paints its OWN stroke at a row 15 positions away from Underline's (confirming distinct positions, not the same line); all three (Italic + Underline + Strikethrough) can be active simultaneously with both strokes visibly coexisting, proving genuine multi-toggle rather than one replacing another — 19/19 assertions passing. Full regression across `text_object_full_build_check.js` (26/26, its one Style-row click index updated from nth=1 to nth=0 to match the new 3-button order — Italic is now first, not second, the disclosed intended consequence of the row's own restructuring, not a regression), `popup_layout_check.js` (24/24), `popup_realcontent_check.js` (28/28), `popup_narrow_top_fallback_check.js` (5/5), `selection_action_strip_test.js` (15/15), `selection_strip_pencil_fix.js` (18/18), `repaint_fix_verify.js` (8/8), `canvas_click_visual_repro.js` (6/6), `paperbg_hittest_repro.js` (3/3), `commitments_test.js`, `text_resize_grid_test.js` (13/13), and `sync_charm_test.js` all pass unchanged. Both `goldenBuild.js` suites (World Builder v1 and v2, 30/30 each) pass unchanged, confirming zero Builder-tooling impact — this build is confined entirely to root Studio. No Theme Contract/Engine V2 Scene Model/Builder architecture change — this fix directly serves Creator Governing Rules #3 (Refinement) and #4 (Personalization); confined to `js/contextPanel.js`, `renderer/slideRenderer.js`, `js/sceneEngine.js`, and `css/style.css`.)

- Lumo Voice — Real Recordings Swap In (all 21 spoken lines) ("ok i have recorded all the prompts. same file name prefixed with v." Closes the placeholder era for Lumo's spoken dialogue: every one of the 21 scripted lines this session's own "give me the prompts which lumo is speaking" request delivered as a script -- the tap-grid Gatekeeper greeting, the Traveller Gateway's 5 title+subtitle greeting pairs, the Returning Creator's recognition pair and reunion pair, the Creator Ceremony's two Guardian beats, and the sky-recognition challenge's 4 lines -- was re-recorded and delivered as `vlumo-NN-<name>.mp3` files uploaded straight to the repo, matching this codebase's own established "GitHub-web-UI upload, then `git pull`" delivery pattern for binary assets. Each real recording was `git mv`'d directly over its matching placeholder (`vlumo-01-tapgrid.mp3`->`lumo-01-tapgrid.mp3`, etc.) -- every filename `js/lumoVoice.js`'s `LINES` table already points at is unchanged, so zero code paths needed to move; only the bytes at each path changed. Every clip's real duration was re-measured via `ffprobe` (a re-recorded line rarely runs the exact same length as its placeholder, per this file's own established discipline: "if a line is ever re-recorded with a different length, this value needs a matching manual update") and the `ms:` value for all 21 corresponding `LINES` entries updated to match -- several genuinely differ from the old placeholder timing by a full second or more (e.g. `skyFresh` 3553ms->4598ms, `greeting4b` 4676ms->4362ms), meaning on-screen bubble hold times (driven by `js/gatewaySequence.js`'s `playLines()`, which stretches a beat to fit `LumoVoice.durationMs()`) now genuinely track the real spoken length instead of an approximation. `lumo-22-flying.mp3`/`lumo-23-landing.mp3` (the Gate video's own non-verbal flying/landing vocalizations) were explicitly excluded per direct instruction -- "lumo 22 and lumo 23 stays as it is. no change to them" -- confirmed no `vlumo-22`/`vlumo-23` files were ever uploaded, matching that instruction exactly. Verified via a new, dedicated Playwright suite (`lumo_recordings_verify.js`, scratch-only) confirming all 23 `durationMs()` values match the new/unchanged table exactly, `preload()`/`play()`/`playSequence()` all still run with zero throw across every id, and zero unexpected console/page errors -- plus a spot-check against two existing regression scripts (`sky_voice_test.js`, `gateway_flyland_test.js`), with `sky_voice_test.js`'s own pre-existing flaky "succeeded: false" outcome and its 3x404/1xERR_TUNNEL_CONNECTION_FAILED console noise confirmed, via a real `git stash` A/B, to reproduce identically on the unmodified baseline -- pre-existing, unrelated to this change. No Theme Contract/Engine V2 Scene Model/Builder/Creator Governing Rules change, no JS logic change of any kind beyond the duration constants; confined to `js/lumoVoice.js` and the 21 audio files under `assets/lumo/voice/`.)

- World-Owned Text Style — Bold Joins the Same Row, Weight Dropdown Retired ("weight is a very technical term, is that drop down even needed?" — a direct question on the just-shipped Underline/Strikethrough Style row, followed by a wireframed proposal ("show me the change wireframe for bold toggle style") and an explicit go-ahead ("approved make the change"). The old Font Style section (`js/contextPanel.js`'s `_appendWorldObjectEditControl`, text branch) paired Font Family with a 7-option Weight dropdown (World Default/Light/Regular/Medium/Semibold/Bold/Black) — real, jargon-heavy vocabulary a child was never going to reason through, and a whole paired row spent on a control almost nobody but Bold itself gets real use out of. **Fix**: `WORLD_TEXT_WEIGHT_OPTIONS` is retired outright — Font Family now spans its own row alone (`_pairRow`'s existing `cellB===null` branch already handles a lone, full-width cell, no new plumbing needed), and Bold joins the Style row as a fourth `_makeMultiToggleRow` button (`[['bold','B'],['italic','I'],['underline','U'],['strikethrough','S']]`, styled `font-weight:800` so the glyph itself previews the effect, matching Italic/Underline/Strikethrough's own established "the label looks like what it does" convention) — one small, legible glyph instead of a whole dropdown. Bold is the one Style-row entry that doesn't write a plain boolean field: it shares the exact same `fontWeight` field the old dropdown always wrote, toggling between `'700'` (on) and `null`/cleared (World Default, off) through the identical `SceneEngine.setContentOverride` path — a narrower vocabulary, not a new mechanism; every other Style button keeps writing its own boolean/`fontStyle` field exactly as before. Verified via a new Playwright suite (`bold_toggle_verify.js`, scratch-only, 22 assertions) against a synthetic Layer Pack Text entry (Museum Caption's own `museumCaption` source has no reachable quick-edit popup at all — a pre-existing, disclosed scope boundary — so a plain `text.content` entry was used instead): Font Family renders alone, unpaired; no Weight row exists anywhere; the Style row shows exactly 4 buttons in order Bold("B", `font-weight:800`)/Italic("I")/Underline("U")/Strikethrough("S"), none active by default; toggling Bold writes `fontWeight:'700'` (never a boolean) and clears it back to `null` (never `false`) on toggle-off; all four Style buttons combine freely and independently; a canvas bbox-scoped pixel-variance check (not a flat threshold — this test theme's own dark-navy default text colour, R29/G52/B87, would falsely register as "no content" under a naive near-black-only scan) confirms real content still paints correctly. Full regression across the existing popup-layout/real-content/text-object-build Playwright suites passes unchanged, plus both `goldenBuild.js` suites (World Builder v1 and v2, unaffected — this change is confined entirely to root Studio). No Theme Contract/Engine V2 Scene Model/Builder architecture change — this fix directly serves Creator Governing Rule #3 (Refinement); confined to `js/contextPanel.js`.)

- Context Panel — "Welcome to `<World>`" Heading Removed ([screenshot: "Welcome to [broken image glyph] Forest Sync - cloud 1.2."] "this is not required." — initially ambiguous, prompting an investigation into WHY a World's `themeIcon` rendered as a broken glyph specifically in Studio's Context Panel default view but not in World Builder's own preview (confirmed via a direct follow-up question: "Only in Studio."); traced partway through `js/themeRegistry.js`/`ThemeRepositoryClient`/font-cascade code and a self-built emoji-rendering diagnostic page before the user's own decisive clarification resolved the entire question: **"what i meant is that welcome string in the right pane of studio is not needed . we can remove it"** — the ask was never to fix the glyph, only to remove the heading it lived in; the underlying rendering-mismatch investigation is now moot and was left unresolved by design, since there's nothing left for it to explain once the heading it affected no longer exists. **Fix**: `_renderDefault()`'s `_worldIdentity()` call and its resulting `.context-welcome-heading` element are dropped outright — not replaced, not gated behind a fallback — from the Context Panel's "nothing selected" default view; `_worldIdentity()` itself (`js/contextPanel.js`, the Artwork-Theme-first/Story-Theme-fallback lookup mirroring `js/app.js`'s own `_updateHeaderContext()`) is deleted entirely, since it had exactly one caller; `.context-welcome-heading`'s own CSS rule (plus its dark-theme override) is removed from `css/style.css`, with the block comment above the still-used `.context-ownership-legend` rule updated to note the heading's removal rather than left describing a rule that no longer exists. Investigated before touching any code, using a comprehensive, real-UI-driven Playwright reproduction rather than guessing: `ProjectModel.scenes(project)`/`_ordered()` were confirmed to have zero caching and always reflect a freshly-added Scene immediately; a **Public** Experience's own "Host Here" dropdown (`_renderExperienceAttachPicker`, `tools/world-builder-v2/js/worldBuilderApp.js`) was confirmed to correctly and immediately show a newly-added Scene, with no bug of any kind in that path. The screenshot's own "Welcome to `<broken glyph>` Forest Sync - cloud 1.2." heading was investigated separately and confirmed to no longer exist anywhere in the live codebase (removed in an earlier, already-shipped Context Panel sprint) — most likely a stale/cached page, not a live regression; flagged as unresolved rather than silently assumed fixed, since this sandbox has no way to confirm what the user's own browser was actually showing at that moment. Verified via a new, comprehensive Playwright suite (`scene_dropdown_repro3.js`, scratch-only, 14/14 assertions, zero console errors) driving the real UI end to end: Create New World → Blank template → add Scene A via the real Scenes strip → seed a Public and a Personal Experience via real model calls → confirm the Public dropdown's pre-Scene-B state (one option) → add Scene B via the real "+ Add a Scene" button → confirm the Public dropdown now offers both Scenes → confirm the Personal dropdown still correctly offers only its own scoped Scene, never the new one → confirm the new disclosure note renders with the correct wording. Two pre-existing scratch regression scripts (`verify_experiences_dead_end.js`, `verify_host_here_redraw.js`) were confirmed via a `git stash` A/B to already hang identically on the completely unmodified codebase — both predate the Mandatory Sign-In gate and never mock `ThemeRepositoryClient`, so `.wb-project-card` never appears and the Welcome-screen click they depend on times out; unrelated to and unaffected by this fix. Both `goldenBuild.js` suites (World Builder v1 and v2) pass unchanged, confirming zero impact on the compile/validate/publish pipeline. No Theme Contract/Engine V2 Scene Model/Creator Governing Rules change; confined to `tools/world-builder-v2/js/worldBuilderApp.js`.)

Spin functionality of here should be in world own text objects context menu also." Three asks; investigation resolved the third immediately, before touching any code, by reading `_appendWorldObjectEditControl`'s existing `v.kind==='text'` branch (`js/contextPanel.js`) — a Rotation control (a plain 0-360° slider, gated on `sceneObj.moveable`, writing through `SceneEngine.setOpacity`'s sibling `setRotation`) and the identical Bold/Italic/Underline/Strikethrough `_makeMultiToggleRow` already ship there, both landed in an earlier sprint this same session ("World-Owned Text Objects Gain Full Story-Author Control"). "Spin" (the sticker popup's own name for rotation) and "Rotation" (World-owned Text's name for the same control) are the identical capability under two labels — no new code was needed for the third ask, only confirmation. The real implementation work was scoped entirely to the OTHER, genuinely separate popup — `_appendStickerTextEditControl(container,sceneObj)`, the quick-edit control for a Story-owned freeform Text sticker (`type:'sticker'`, `owner:'story'`, `visual.kind==='text'`, created via Personalize → Add Something → Text), never World-owned text, which already had its own Bold/Underline/Strikethrough and needed no change. **Fix, mirroring the World-owned popup's own already-proven pattern rather than inventing a new one**: the `STICKER_TEXT_WEIGHT_OPTIONS` constant (a 7-entry World-Default/Light/Regular/Medium/Semibold/Bold/Black dropdown) is deleted outright; Font Family now spans its own row alone (`_pairRow`'s existing `cellB===null` branch, no new plumbing); a `_makeMultiToggleRow` Style row replaces the old single-select Normal/Italic pair with four independent toggles — `[['bold','B'],['italic','I'],['underline','U'],['strikethrough','S']]`, each glyph styled to preview its own effect exactly like the World-owned version's row — writing `fontWeight:'700'`/`''`, `fontStyle:'italic'`/`'normal'`, and two new plain boolean fields (`underline`, `strikethrough`) directly onto the sticker instance via the existing, already field-name-agnostic `SceneEngine.updateSticker` shallow merge — zero SceneEngine changes needed, since this write path (a Story-owned sticker's own instance fields) is structurally distinct from World-owned text's `elementOverrides`/`setContentOverride` bag. **Canvas has no native text-decoration for freeform stickers either** — `renderer/slideRenderer.js`'s `_drawFreeformText(st)` gained manually-stroked underline/strikethrough lines, ported from (but a separately-maintained implementation from) the existing World-owned `_layerDrawText` technique: each wrapped line's own real stroke, sized to that line's own measured width, positioned via the same `size*0.8`/`size*0.2` ascent/descent baseline approximation, honoring the sticker's own fixed `textBaseline:'middle'` (simpler than World-owned text's `vAlign`-dependent case, since a freeform sticker always centers). Verified via a new, dedicated Playwright suite (`bold_underline_strike_verify.js`, scratch-only, 20/20 assertions, zero console/page errors) built specifically around the live canvas, not just the model: Weight dropdown confirmed gone; the Style row confirmed to be exactly 4 buttons (Bold/Italic/Underline/Strikethrough), none active until toggled; each writes its own correct field (`fontWeight`/`fontStyle`/`underline`/`strikethrough`) independently and all four combine simultaneously (genuine multi-select, not radio-style); un-toggling Bold clears `fontWeight` back to `''` (never stored as boolean `false`, matching the codebase's existing null-clears convention) while leaving the other three untouched; a real pixel scan of the live canvas confirms an actual dark horizontal stroke paints when Underline/Strikethrough are on and the same scan band is empty once they're off — genuinely painted, not just stored. Two real bugs were found and fixed in the TEST script itself, neither an app bug, both disclosed rather than glossed over: the test's own pixel-sampling code hardcoded `canvas.width/1080` assuming every page is portrait, which produced a false zero-pixels-found failure on this particular MuseumGallery "Showcase" test fixture — actually landscape (1350×1080) — fixed by querying `SlideRenderer.getCanvasSize(slide)` dynamically instead of assuming; and an unscoped `#selectionActionEditPanel .icon-card` query matched all 7 icon-style buttons in the popup (4 Style + 3 Alignment: Left/Center/Right), not just the intended 4, producing a false failure once Alignment's own correctly-inactive Left/Right buttons were folded into an "all should be active" check — fixed by scoping the query specifically to the Style row's own DOM subtree via its `.designer-row-label` text. Full regression across `sticker_text_quickedit_verify.js` (32/32, the Delete/quick-edit sprint's own suite, confirming the popup's other controls and the Delete button are unaffected), `bold_toggle_verify.js` (22/22, confirming World-owned Text's own separate Bold/Style row and Rotation are completely untouched — this fix never touches that code path), and `welcome_heading_removed_verify.js` (4/4, an unrelated area, quick sanity check since this fix also touches `js/contextPanel.js`) — 85 total assertions across all suites, zero failures, zero console/page errors. Both `goldenBuild.js` suites (World Builder v1 and v2, unaffected — this fix touches zero Builder files) pass unchanged. **Disclosed, not yet fixed**: `js/cardDesigner.js`'s own sticker Text group — the full-editor surface a Story-owned text sticker still shows on its very FIRST selection (per the prior sprint's "first-edition vs. context-menu-from-then-on" routing), before the quick-edit popup takes over on the second selection onward — still has the old Weight dropdown and single-select Normal/Italic Style row, unchanged by this fix; a real, foreseeable inconsistency (first selection shows the old controls, every later selection shows the new ones) left deliberately out of scope since the user's literal request was scoped to "here," the popup shown in the screenshot. No Theme Contract/Engine V2 Scene Model/Builder architecture change; confined to `js/contextPanel.js` and `renderer/slideRenderer.js`.)

- World Builder — Host Here Disclosure Note Reworded, "Cover" Was Never a Special Category ([screenshot: "This is a Personal Experience — it can only ever host in Cover, the Scene it belongs to..."] "what does this mean. personal experience can only ever host in cover ?? personal experience is bound to one single scene but that can be any scene." A real, immediate follow-up to the just-shipped Host Here disclosure note — confirmed to be a genuine wording ambiguity, not a data bug: `scenes[0].name` in `_renderExperienceAttachPicker` (`tools/world-builder-v2/js/worldBuilderApp.js`) is fully dynamic, always reading the real, human-given name of the ONE Scene this specific Experience's own `exp.scopeSceneId` points at (`allScenes.filter(s => s.id === exp.scopeSceneId)`) — in this World, that Scene genuinely happens to be named "Cover" (a Storybook-template starter Scene), confirmed by reading the code rather than guessing. The original phrasing — "it can only ever host in Cover, the Scene it belongs to" — read as if "Cover" were a fixed rule or reserved category every Personal Experience must obey, rather than the plain fact that THIS Experience's own binding happens to be a Scene called that. **Fix**: reworded to lead with the general rule before naming the specific instance — "Personal Experiences are permanently bound to one Scene each — whichever Scene they were created in. This one belongs to '`<name>`,' so it can never host anywhere else, even in a Scene you add later. Other Scenes won't show up here. To host it elsewhere, Graduate it to Public below." — making explicit that the binding is per-Experience and could be any Scene, not a category named "Cover." Verified via the existing `scene_dropdown_repro3.js` suite (14/14, its own disclosure-note assertion updated to match the new copy) and both `goldenBuild.js` suites (World Builder v1 and v2), all passing unchanged. No Theme Contract/Engine V2 Scene Model/Creator Governing Rules change; confined to `tools/world-builder-v2/js/worldBuilderApp.js`.)

- Collection — Theme-Scoped, Deduplicated Asset Registry, Phase 1: Foundation (implements Phase 1 of a new World Builder v2 architecture feature, per the user's own proposal: "i want to introduce concept of collection. the collection is created in builder along with theme. any asset am adding to any scene gets added into collection also. a scene always refer to the asset which is in collection. collection can have assets which are used in scenes and others which builder would want creator to have access for customization." Clarified further: "nurturing, personal, public experiences stay as it is [unchanged]. asset can be uploaded either to collection or scene. the final resting piece of an asset is collection. builder can delete from collection but not creator. when authoring an experience builder can connect with an asset available in collection or can upload a new one. the new asset again goes into collection and that is the reference used in all scenes." Designed via Plan Mode (three Explore agents plus a Plan agent, all findings independently re-verified against the real code before finalizing) and resolved the one genuinely open design fork via `AskUserQuestion` — when a Creator picks a Collection asset flagged "available for customization," should it add a new Story-owned object (reuses the existing "Add Something" mechanism) or swap an existing World-owned object's art (a new capability)? **Answered: "Both"** — ship "add new" first (Phase 6), defer "swap existing art" as its own later phase. **A corrected headline design decision, found during Plan-agent review then independently re-verified line-by-line against the real code before adopting**: my own first-draft design proposed changing `experience.properties.imageSrc`/`graphicSrc` to hold a Collection *id* instead of a directly-resolvable reference — confirmed wrong by reading the actual code (`_resolveAssetRefToSrc`, `AssetStore.resolve()`'s own `vihu-asset:`-prefix parser, `externalizeSceneImage`'s `indexOf('vihu-asset:')` check, the Draft Asset Architecture migration accessor — at minimum 9 real call sites already assume this field IS directly a resolvable string). **Corrected design: Collection is a derived, ref-indexed side table — `imageSrc`/`graphicSrc`/the mirrored `layer.image` never change shape**, still holding the exact `vihu-asset:`/`data:` string every existing reader already expects; a Collection entry's own `.ref` field IS that string, so "connecting to an existing Collection asset" (Phase 2's job) means writing that entry's `.ref` back onto a different Experience — the identical write path a fresh upload already uses. **This phase**: new Collection CRUD in `tools/world-builder-v2/js/projectModel.js` — `collectionAssets`/`findCollectionAsset`/`findCollectionAssetByRef`/`setCollectionAsset`/`registerCollectionAsset`/`retargetCollectionAssetRef`/`renameCollectionAsset`/`setCollectionAssetAvailability`/`collectionAssetUsageCount`/`deleteCollectionAsset` — mirroring the already-proven Frame CRUD pattern 1:1 (a Frame is its own file, referenced by id, deleted by nulling every dangling reference in the same operation, "AV-012"); the one real difference is Collection needs no separate Scene-Layer reference scan the way Frame's `_clearFrameReferences` does, since `layer.image` has exactly one producer today (the Experience mirror chain, `_syncUniversalContent`) — no direct-to-Scene-Layer decoration-image upload UI exists anywhere in this codebase. **The auto-registration hook — the one place "any asset added to a Scene also goes into Collection" is realized**: `updateExperienceProperty(project,id,key,value)`, already the one chokepoint every current producer (the Experience content picker's future upload branch, the Decoration glyph-rasterization path at `worldBuilderApp.js`'s DECORATION_GLYPHS click handler) funnels through, now calls `registerCollectionAsset(project,value,{kind,name})` whenever `key` is `'imageSrc'`/`'graphicSrc'` and `value` is truthy — one chokepoint covers every producer with zero per-caller changes needed. **A real correctness gap found via direct verification, not originally flagged by any agent**: Draft Asset Architecture's own lazy migration (`AssetStore.migrateFieldsOnSave`, called from `_collectMigrationAccessors`) can rewrite an Experience's `imageSrc`/`graphicSrc` from a legacy `data:` URI to a `vihu-asset:` reference for the exact same bytes, entirely independent of Collection's own ref-indexed lookup — without a fix, this would either orphan the existing Collection entry (its `.ref` pointing at a string nothing holds anymore) or spawn a wasteful duplicate the next time that string is registered. **Fixed** by teaching the migration accessor's own `set` callback (`worldBuilderApp.js:3072-3085`) to call the new `retargetCollectionAssetRef(project,oldRef,newRef)` alongside rewriting `props[key]` — repoints an already-registered entry's `.ref` to follow the field, never creates, never duplicates. Verified via a new, comprehensive Playwright suite (`collection_phase1_verify.js`, scratch-only, 27/27 assertions) driving the real UI end to end: a brand-new Project starts with zero Collection entries; the real Decoration glyph-rasterization click (a genuine UI click, not a simulated call) registers exactly one entry (kind `'graphic'`, a real `data:` URI ref, defaulting to NOT available to Creator); registering the SAME ref a second time on a different Experience — simulating Phase 2's future "connect to an existing Collection asset" picker action — is a clean no-op, never a duplicate, and the second Experience correctly holds the reused ref; a simulated `vihu-asset:` Image-picker upload registers its own distinct entry; the migration-retarget fix was proven end-to-end for REAL, not just asserted — this sandbox genuinely has IndexedDB, so triggering a real `_persist()` (via typing into the World Name field on Overview, the simplest reliable way to fire the private, debounced `_scheduleAssetMigration()`) caused the real async `AssetStore.migrateFieldsOnSave` to actually run, and the seeded legacy Experience's Collection entry was confirmed to follow the field to its new `vihu-asset:` reference with zero duplication and zero orphaning; the retarget/delete functions were also exercised directly (a no-op retarget for an unregistered ref correctly returns `null` rather than fabricating an entry; Builder-only delete correctly nulls every dangling Experience reference — never fabricates a substitute — removes the entry, and correctly reports a false/no-op for an already-deleted id). Full regression: both `goldenBuild.js` suites (World Builder v1 and v2, 30/30 each) pass unchanged, confirming this phase touches neither the compile/validate/publish pipeline; `scene_dropdown_repro3.js` (14/14, exercising Experience CRUD/graduation/attachment/Host Here dropdown heavily) passes unchanged, confirming the new `updateExperienceProperty` hook has zero effect on any pre-existing Experience behaviour. No Theme Contract/Engine V2 Scene Model/Creator Governing Rules change; `tools/world-builder/` (v1) and root Studio are completely untouched — confined entirely to `tools/world-builder-v2/js/projectModel.js` and `tools/world-builder-v2/js/worldBuilderApp.js`. Phases 2 (a Collection-aware picker for Experience Image/Graphics content, replacing the plain upload rows), 3 (a Manage Collection screen + the Builder-only delete UI, behind a confirmation dialog showing usage count), 4 (compile-time dedup in `builder.js`'s `externalizeSceneImage` — where "reduces data load" is actually realized, a shared Collection entry compiling to exactly one `collection/<id>.png` regardless of how many Layers/Experiences point at it), 5 (Creator-facing `availableToCreator` metadata added to the compiled `.vtheme`, with a matching `docs/VTHEME_PACKAGE_SPEC.md` update), and 6 (a Creator-side "🎁 From This World" browsing row in `js/contextPanel.js`'s Add Something accordion, "add new" only per the user's own answered "Both") remain named, not-yet-started increments — see `/root/.claude/plans/witty-floating-thimble.md` for the complete phased rollout.)

- Collection — Theme-Scoped, Deduplicated Asset Registry, Phase 2: Collection-Aware Picker (implements Phase 2 of the approved Collection plan — the picker itself, following directly on Phase 1's registry/auto-registration foundation. `worldBuilderApp.js`'s two Experience content sections that can hold an image — Image's "Photo" field and Graphics' "Asset" field — previously called the plain `_assetUploadRow(icon,value,onChange)` (upload/replace/remove, nothing else); both now call a new `_renderCollectionPicker(exp,key,iconFallback,accept)`, synthesizing two already-proven precedents rather than inventing a third mechanism: `_renderFramePicker`'s "grid of existing options, pick one or make new" shape, and `_assetUploadRow` itself (kept completely unchanged, still funneling every fresh upload through `_storeUploadedAsset`/`AssetStore.put()`). The picker filters `collectionAssets(project)` to entries whose `kind` matches the field (`'image'` for Photo, `'graphic'` for Asset) and renders them as a small reuse grid — shown only when at least one matching entry exists, so a brand-new World with an empty Collection shows the plain upload row alone, never an empty/confusing grid. Clicking a reuse-grid card writes that entry's own `.ref` string back onto `imageSrc`/`graphicSrc` through the exact same `updateExperienceProperty()` write path a fresh upload already uses (the picker's own `commit()` closure, shared by both the reuse-card click handler and the upload/replace callback) — the identical string, so `AssetStore.resolve()`/`ThemeRegistry.resolveAssetRef()`/`_syncUniversalContent` never need to know Collection exists at all, exactly matching the corrected "derived, ref-indexed side table" design Phase 1 already committed to. Graphics' pre-existing mutual-exclusion rule (setting an image clears `graphicShape`, since a Graphics Experience can only ever be one or the other) is preserved for the reuse path too — the clearing logic that used to live inline at the Graphics section's own `_assetUploadRow` call site now lives inside `_renderCollectionPicker`'s shared `commit()`, so all three ways a Graphics Experience can gain an image (a fresh upload, reusing a Collection entry, and — the OTHER Graphics path, Shape-picking — clearing `graphicSrc` back) stay mutually exclusive with each other, verified as three separate real UI interactions, not just the two the ticket named. **Two real bugs found and fixed during verification, neither invented for this ticket, both disclosed rather than routed around**: **(1) a genuine, pre-existing World Builder app bug** — `showTemplates()` (`worldBuilderApp.js`) called `renderTemplateGrid()` exactly once, at module boot, never again on any later visit to Screen 2; since a template card's own click handler marks itself `wb-busy` and never clears that class on its success path (the Template Rule replaces the card with the Workspace immediately, so clearing was never thought necessary), a SECOND "Create New World → pick the same template" in one page session silently did nothing at all — no new Project, the click handler's own `if(card.classList.contains('wb-busy')) return;` guard fired and Screen 2 just stayed exactly where it was, with zero visible error or console signal. Reproduced directly via Playwright (confirmed `total projects` stayed at 1, `#wb-screen-templates` stayed visible) before fixing — this is a real, user-reachable data-loss-adjacent bug (a Theme Author who authors one World, goes Home, and tries to start a second one in the same session would hit exactly this frozen screen in production), not a hypothetical. **Fixed** by calling `renderTemplateGrid()` fresh every time `showTemplates()` runs — a template card's DOM node (and its own one-shot `wb-busy` state) is discarded and rebuilt from scratch on every visit, so there is never a stale, already-clicked card left over from an earlier World to trip that guard. **(2) a verification-script bug, not an app bug** — the test's own "brand-new second World" section computed `projectId2` via `list[list.length-1].id`, silently assuming append order; `ProjectStore.list()` has always sorted newest-first (its own doc comment: "My World Projects always leads with whatever the creator touched most recently"), so that line actually grabbed the OLDEST Project (World #1, still bearing all of World #1's own seeded Experiences/Collection entries from earlier in the same test run) rather than the just-created World #2 — producing a confusing false failure ("brand-new World starts with zero Collection entries" reporting 2 existing entries) that, on inspection, traced cleanly to the test's own indexing rather than any real Collection/registration bug. Fixed to `list[0].id`. Verified via a comprehensive Playwright suite (`collection_phase2_verify.js`, scratch-only, 28/28 assertions, zero console/page errors) driving the real UI end to end: Image-section reuse (seeding a Collection entry directly, navigating to the real Experience Library tab, clicking the real "Image" Content Kind selector button since a fresh Experience's `contentKind` locks to `'text'` at creation time regardless of `type` — an existing, pre-existing behaviour this test works around via the real, always-present selector rather than assuming a creation-time default) writes the same ref via a genuine rendered-grid click and never spawns a duplicate entry; the plain Upload/Remove row still works completely unchanged (a real regression check — Remove correctly clears `imageSrc` back to `null` but is confirmed to NEVER delete the Collection registry entry itself, since deletion is Phase 3's own, separate, Builder-only action, "the final resting piece of an asset is collection... builder can delete from collection but not creator"); Graphics-section mutual exclusion holds across a real fresh-glyph-rasterization-upload → Shape-pick → reuse-existing-Collection-entry sequence, with each step correctly clearing whatever the OTHER path had set; and a genuinely brand-new second World (created via the just-fixed `showTemplates()` rebuild, confirmed via `total projects: 2` and a correctly-opened Workspace) correctly shows zero Collection entries and no reuse grid/help text at all, with the plain upload row still present. Full regression: both `goldenBuild.js` suites (World Builder v1 and v2, 30/30 each) pass unchanged, confirming this phase touches neither the compile/validate/publish pipeline; `scene_dropdown_repro3.js` (14/14, exercising Experience CRUD/graduation/attachment/Host Here dropdown heavily) passes unchanged, confirming the `showTemplates()` fix has zero effect on any unrelated Workspace behaviour. No Theme Contract/Engine V2 Scene Model/Creator Governing Rules change; `tools/world-builder/` (v1) and root Studio are completely untouched — confined entirely to `tools/world-builder-v2/js/worldBuilderApp.js`. Phases 3 (a Manage Collection screen + the Builder-only delete UI, behind a confirmation dialog showing usage count), 4 (compile-time dedup in `builder.js`'s `externalizeSceneImage` — where "reduces data load" is actually realized), 5 (Creator-facing `availableToCreator` metadata added to the compiled `.vtheme`), and 6 (a Creator-side "🎁 From This World" browsing row in `js/contextPanel.js`'s Add Something accordion, "add new" only per the user's own answered "Both") remain named, not-yet-started increments — see `/root/.claude/plans/witty-floating-thimble.md` for the complete phased rollout.)

- Collection — Theme-Scoped, Deduplicated Asset Registry, Phase 3: Manage Collection Screen + Builder-Only Delete (implements Phase 3 of the approved Collection plan — the registry's own management screen, reached from Phase 2's picker's new "🗂️ Manage Collection →" bridge link, mirroring `_renderFramePicker`'s own "Manage Frames" bridge exactly (setting `currentNav='collection'` and re-rendering, never a Global Navigation peer, exactly the pattern already established for Frame/Layer Packs/Assets). **A real, useful discovery, not a design surprise**: Phase 1's own model-layer work had already built `renameCollectionAsset`/`setCollectionAssetAvailability`/`collectionAssetUsageCount`/`deleteCollectionAsset` in full — going further than its own phase name implied — so Phase 3's actual remaining work was purely a new UI screen, `_renderCollectionPanel()`, calling those already-shipped functions; no new model-layer code was needed at all. `_renderCollectionPanel()` mirrors `_renderFramesPanel`'s own shape (a Scene-anchored bridge editor) but with no per-entry "selected" detail state — a Collection entry has far fewer fields than a Frame's eight, so rename/availability/delete all fit inline on each row rather than needing a separate detail view. Each row shows a real resolved thumbnail (`_resolveAssetRefToSrc`, reused unchanged from Phase 2), a rename text input (`renameCollectionAsset`), a live "Used by N Experiences" count (`collectionAssetUsageCount`), a "Let Creators use this too" checkbox (`setCollectionAssetAvailability`, reusing the existing `_checkboxField` helper verbatim), and a Delete button. Delete is gated behind a real `window.confirm()` naming the exact live usage count before committing ("It is currently used by N Experiences — those will lose this picture"), then calls the already-shipped `deleteCollectionAsset` (Phase 1) — which nulls every Experience's `imageSrc`/`graphicSrc` currently pointing at the deleted entry through the real `updateExperienceProperty` path, so the Engine Adapter's own existing re-sync (`_syncExperienceAttachments`) fires and Working View/Runtime Preview both correctly clear rather than showing a stale image for a reference that no longer resolves to anything — the exact AV-012 discipline already proven for Frame, now proven for Collection with two real, simultaneously-affected Experiences, not just one. Wired into the existing modal-dispatch architecture exactly like Frames/Layer Packs/Assets already are (`MODAL_NAVS`/`MODAL_TITLES`/`_renderContextPanel`'s dispatch chain/`STATE_GUIDANCE`), and deliberately left OUT of `WORKING_VIEW_PASSTHROUGH_NAVS` since it has no Working View specimen of its own, matching Layer Packs/Assets' own precedent. Verified via a comprehensive Playwright suite (`collection_phase3_verify.js`, scratch-only, 25/25 assertions, zero console/page errors) driving the real UI end to end: the modal opens with the correct "🗂️ Collection" title reached via the real bridge link; two seeded Collection entries (one shared by two real Experiences, one genuinely unused) render with correct thumbnails/kind/live usage counts; rename and the availability checkbox both persist through their real model functions via real input/checkbox interactions; deleting the shared entry (behind a real, accepted `confirm()` dialog) nulls BOTH real Experiences' `imageSrc` in one operation while leaving the unrelated unused entry completely untouched, and the panel correctly re-renders down to one row; deleting the now-unused entry is confirmed a clean no-op elsewhere (zero entries left, nothing else in the project changed); the empty state renders correctly and the bridge link stays reachable with zero entries; and a static grep confirms Collection's delete/rename/availability functions are absent from every root Studio (Creator) JS file — Creator has zero code path anywhere that can reach them, matching the plan's own "builder can delete from collection but not creator." Phases 4 (compile-time dedup in `builder.js` — where "reduces data load" is actually realized), 5 (Creator-facing `availableToCreator` metadata added to the compiled `.vtheme`), and 6 (a Creator-side "🎁 From This World" browsing row in `js/contextPanel.js`'s Add Something accordion) remain named, not-yet-started increments — see `/root/.claude/plans/witty-floating-thimble.md` for the complete phased rollout.)

- Collection — Theme-Scoped, Deduplicated Asset Registry, Phase 4: Compile-Time Dedup in builder.js (implements Phase 4 of the approved Collection plan — the actual "reduces data load" payoff, entirely inside `tools/world-builder-v2/js/services/builder.js`'s existing `convergeScenes` → `convergeScene` → `convergeSceneLayer` → `externalizeSceneImage` chain, no new UI. `packageTheme()` gains `package_.collectionAssets = await this.collectFolder('collection')` (the identical pattern already used for `frameVariations`/`layerPack`/`representations` — metadata only, never itself holding embedded bytes; `theme.collectionAssets` on the compiled `.vtheme` is a separate, later phase). `convergeScenes()` builds one ref-keyed lookup (`refToEntry`) from that array, once per Build, threaded down as a new trailing parameter through `convergeScene` → `convergeSceneLayer` → `externalizeSceneImage`. Inside `externalizeSceneImage`, before computing today's per-Layer relPath (`'scenes/<sceneId>/<layerId>.png'`), a Layer's own `layer.image` is checked against `refToEntry`: a hit converges onto that entry's OWN stable key (`'collection/<id>.png'`) instead of minting an independent relPath for every Layer — so N Experiences/Layers sharing one Collection asset compile to exactly ONE embedded image in `package_.assets`, not N duplicates, the literal realization of the user's own words: "the concept of collection allows reusable assets for creator and parallely reduces data load on builder by remapping to same asset used in different experiences." A miss (a Layer whose image was never registered in Collection — every Theme authored before this feature, or content Phase 1's auto-registration hook never saw) falls straight through to exactly today's per-Layer relPath, fully unaffected. A small memoization guard (skip re-hydrating via `AssetStore.hydrateForExport()` if `package_.assets[relPath]` is already set) avoids a redundant Storage round trip for every additional Layer sharing one Collection asset — purely an efficiency guard, since writing the identical value to the same key twice would be harmless either way. A real bug was caught and fixed mid-implementation, before any test ever ran against it: `convergeSceneLayer`'s own single call site to `externalizeSceneImage` (inside the `layer.kind==='decoration' && layer.image` branch) was updated for the new signature everywhere EXCEPT that one call itself, silently passing `undefined` for `refToEntry` and making the whole dedup path unreachable in practice — caught by a follow-up grep across every `externalizeSceneImage`/`convergeSceneLayer`/`convergeScene` reference in the file before writing the verification suite, not by a failing assertion. Verified via a new, comprehensive Playwright suite (`collection_phase4_verify.js`, scratch-only, 17/17 assertions, zero console/page errors) driving the REAL, unmodified compile pipeline end to end — `ProjectCompiler.runBuild(project)` → `validator.validate()` → `builder.build()` → `packageTheme()` — against a real Blank World Project with a real Scene: two real Experiences (both graduated Public, both Free-hosted, both mirrored onto DISTINCT Scene Layers via the real Engine Adapter) sharing the exact same Collection ref converge to EXACTLY ONE compiled `collection/<id>.png` asset (not two `scenes/.../<layerId>.png` duplicates), with BOTH compiled Layer Pack entries' `decoration.image` fields pointing at that same relPath; a third, legacy-shaped Decoration Layer authored directly (never through an Experience, never registered in Collection) alongside them still converges via exactly today's own per-Layer relPath, completely unaffected by Collection existing elsewhere in the same Theme — confirming the fallback path is genuinely untouched, not just assumed so; and two consecutive Builds of the unmodified Project produce a byte-identical compiled assets map (both keys and values), matching this codebase's own already-established Publish determinism guarantee. Full regression: both `goldenBuild.js` suites (World Builder v1 and v2, 30/30 each) pass unchanged, confirming a Theme with zero Collection entries still compiles byte-identically to before this plan; the Phase 1 (27/27), Phase 2 (28/28), and Phase 3 (25/25) suites all pass completely unchanged, confirming zero regression from this phase's own additions. No Theme Contract/Engine V2 Scene Model/Creator Governing Rules change; `tools/world-builder/` (v1) and root Studio are completely untouched — confined entirely to `tools/world-builder-v2/js/services/builder.js`. Phases 5 (Creator-facing `availableToCreator` metadata added to the compiled `.vtheme`, with a matching `docs/VTHEME_PACKAGE_SPEC.md` update) and 6 (a Creator-side "🎁 From This World" browsing row in `js/contextPanel.js`'s Add Something accordion, "add new" only per the user's own answered "Both") remain named, not-yet-started increments — see `/root/.claude/plans/witty-floating-thimble.md` for the complete phased rollout.)

- Collection — Theme-Scoped, Deduplicated Asset Registry, Phase 5: Creator-Facing Availability Metadata (implements Phase 5 of the approved Collection plan — the one part of Collection that touches the currently-locked `.vtheme` contract, so it ships with a `docs/VTHEME_PACKAGE_SPEC.md` update, not treated as "just more code." A Collection entry the Theme Author flagged `availableToCreator:true` must reach the compiled package regardless of whether any Layer currently references it — that's the whole point of the flag ("collection can have assets which are used in scenes and others which builder would want creator to have access for customization," the user's own words) — but Phase 4's own dedup path only ever embedded a Collection entry as a side effect of some Layer's own `layer.image` pointing at it. `packageTheme()` (`tools/world-builder-v2/js/services/builder.js`) now walks `package_.collectionAssets` (already collected there, carrying every entry's own internal `.ref`) right after `convergeScenes()` runs, and for every entry with `availableToCreator===true`, guarantees its bytes are embedded at its own stable `collection/<id>.png` key — a no-op via memoization if a Scene Layer already embedded it first — then builds a SEPARATE, sanitized array, `package_.creatorCollectionAssets`, holding only `id`/`name`/`kind`/`relPath`/`availableToCreator` per entry: never the internal `.ref`, a Builder-session-internal detail that must never leak into a published Theme. The hydrate-and-embed logic itself was extracted out of `externalizeSceneImage`'s own Phase 4 dedup branch into one new shared method, `_embedCollectionEntry(entry, package_)`, reused by both call sites (`externalizeSceneImage` for the "a Layer points at this entry" case, `packageTheme`'s new sweep for the "flagged for reuse but used by nothing at all" case) rather than duplicated — `externalizeSceneImage`'s own Phase 4 dedup behaviour stays byte-identical, confirmed via the unchanged 17/17 Phase 4 suite. `buildTheme()` gained the exact same "only when non-empty" pattern already used for `frameVariations`/`representations`: `theme.collectionAssets = packageData.creatorCollectionAssets` only when that array actually has entries, so a Theme with zero `availableToCreator` entries — every Theme authored before this phase, or one whose Collection assets are all used only inside Scenes and never flagged for reuse — compiles with the key simply absent, never an empty array. `docs/VTHEME_PACKAGE_SPEC.md` gained a full `theme.collectionAssets` section (both the Story Theme and Artwork Theme JSON examples, plus a dedicated field-by-field writeup covering the sanitized shape, the `relPath`-resolves-via-`ThemeRegistry.resolveAssetRef` convention every other image-bearing field already uses, and the one deliberate exception this field represents — an `availableToCreator` entry is embedded regardless of Scene usage, unlike every other asset field in the document). Verified via a new, comprehensive Playwright suite (`collection_phase5_verify.js`, scratch-only, 30/30 assertions, zero console/page errors) driving the REAL, unmodified compile pipeline end to end against a real Blank World Project with a real Scene carrying four distinct cases in one Theme: Entry A (`availableToCreator:true`, used by a real Layer) is embedded once and listed once in `theme.collectionAssets`; Entry B (`availableToCreator:true`, registered standalone via `ProjectModel.registerCollectionAsset` with zero Layer or Experience referencing it at all) still gets its bytes embedded and still appears in `theme.collectionAssets` — the literal proof of the flag's own purpose; Entry C (used by a real Layer, left at its default `availableToCreator:false`) is still embedded via Phase 4's own unaffected dedup but correctly does NOT appear in `theme.collectionAssets`, confirming the two concepts are genuinely orthogonal; a fourth, legacy-shaped Decoration Layer (authored directly, never through an Experience, never registered in Collection at all) still converges via exactly today's own per-Layer relPath; every `theme.collectionAssets` record was confirmed to carry ONLY the sanitized `id`/`name`/`kind`/`relPath`/`availableToCreator` fields with the internal `.ref` field genuinely absent; two consecutive Builds produced a byte-identical `theme.collectionAssets` array and assets map (determinism, matching this codebase's own already-established Publish guarantee); and a brand-new second World with zero Collection entries at all compiled successfully with `theme.collectionAssets` confirmed simply absent (`undefined`), never an empty array. Full regression: both `goldenBuild.js` suites (World Builder v1 and v2, 30/30 each) pass unchanged; the Phase 1 (27/27), Phase 2 (28/28), Phase 3 (25/25), and Phase 4 (17/17) suites all pass completely unchanged, confirming zero regression from this phase's own additions. No Theme Contract/Engine V2 Scene Model/Creator Governing Rules change; `tools/world-builder/` (v1) and root Studio are completely untouched — confined entirely to `tools/world-builder-v2/js/services/builder.js` and `docs/VTHEME_PACKAGE_SPEC.md`. Phase 6 (a Creator-side "🎁 From This World" browsing row in `js/contextPanel.js`'s Add Something accordion, resolving `theme.collectionAssets` via the existing, uniform `ThemeRegistry.resolveAssetRef` — "add new" only per the user's own answered "Both") remains a named, not-yet-started increment — see `/root/.claude/plans/witty-floating-thimble.md` for the complete phased rollout.)

- Collection — Manage Collection Gains Direct "Add Image"/"Add Graphic" Controls (a direct, real-usage follow-up, delivered once the user actually started using the shipped 6-phase Collection feature: "i started using it. manage collection is good way to connect through experience. manage collection should also be operatable individually without going into collection. i would like to add extra assets there." Until now, the ONLY way anything ever reached a Collection registry was indirect — Phase 1's auto-registration hook only ever fires as a side effect of an Experience's own Image/Graphics field being set, so the ONLY way to open Manage Collection at all was to first create or select an Experience, switch it to Image/Graphics content mode, and follow the picker's own "🗂️ Manage Collection →" bridge link (Phase 2/3) — a Theme Author who simply wanted to stock a World's Collection ahead of time, with no specific Experience in mind yet, had no path to do that at all. **Fix**: `_renderCollectionPanel()` (`tools/world-builder-v2/js/worldBuilderApp.js`) gained a new `.wb-collection-add-row` — two buttons, "+ 🖼️ Add Image" and "+ 🎭 Add Graphic" — inserted immediately after the existing `_stateIntro('collection')` call and, critically, immediately BEFORE the panel's own `if (!assets.length) { ...; return; }` early-return, so the controls render even on a totally empty registry rather than only appearing once at least one entry already exists via the indirect path. Each button wires a fresh `_fileInputUpload('image/*', onFile)` (the exact, unmodified upload chokepoint every existing Collection/Experience/Overview upload already funnels through — real file → FileReader → downscale-if-large → `_storeUploadedAsset` → `AssetStore.put()` → a durable `vihu-asset:` ref) whose `onFile` callback calls `window.ProjectModel.registerCollectionAsset(project, ref, {kind:'image'|'graphic'})` directly — the identical registration function the Phase 1 auto-hook already calls, just invoked straight from the panel instead of via an Experience's own property write — then `_persist()` + `_renderCollectionPanel()` to save and re-render. **No Experience is ever touched by this path** — a picture added this way sits in Collection on its own, exactly matching "add extra assets there," ready to be picked up later by the Phase 2 picker's own reuse grid or by Creator's Phase 6 "🎁 From This World" browsing (once flagged `availableToCreator`). The Image/Graphic split mirrors why `kind` exists at all: it only ever matters for the Experience picker's own reuse-grid filter (Phase 2, filters by `kind`) — Creator's own Phase 6 browsing never filters by kind — so this keeps the common case (add a picture) a single click while leaving the rarer Graphic case one click away rather than forcing an extra decision on every add. New `.wb-collection-add-row{display:flex;gap:8px;flex-wrap:wrap;margin-bottom:14px}` in `world-builder.css`. The empty-state help text was reworded from "upload a Photo or Asset while authoring an Experience" to "upload one above, or add a Photo/Asset while authoring an Experience," since there are now genuinely two ways to reach Collection content. Verified via a new, dedicated Playwright suite (`collection_directadd_verify.js`, scratch-only, 19/19 assertions, zero unexpected console/page errors) driving the real UI end to end: created a Blank World with one Scene and exactly one fresh, empty Experience (`addExperience`+`graduateToPublic`, no `imageSrc`/`graphicSrc` set, confirmed zero Collection entries beforehand) purely as a way to REACH the screen via the existing bridge link, then confirmed both new buttons render alongside the still-showing empty-state message; a real file upload via "+ Add Image" (Playwright's `setInputFiles` against a real PNG fixture) creates exactly one new entry with `kind:'image'`, with the seeded Experience's own `imageSrc`/`graphicSrc` both confirmed completely untouched — proving no Experience was involved at all; the new row renders with a real thumbnail, correct meta text ("🖼️ Image", "Used by 0 Experiences"), a working rename input, availability checkbox, and delete button — indistinguishable from an Experience-sourced entry, confirming this reuses the exact same CRUD; a second real upload via "+ Add Graphic" adds a genuinely independent second entry with `kind:'graphic'`, bringing the panel to 2 real rows. Full regression: the existing Phase 1 (27/27), Phase 2 (28/28), Phase 3 (25/25), Phase 4 (17/17), and Phase 5 (30/30) Collection suites all pass completely unchanged, plus both `goldenBuild.js` suites (World Builder v1 and v2, 30/30 each) — confirming this addition touches neither the compile/validate/publish pipeline nor any other Collection surface. No Theme Contract/Engine V2 Scene Model/Creator Governing Rules change; root Studio (Creator) and `tools/world-builder/` (v1) are both completely untouched — confined entirely to `tools/world-builder-v2/js/worldBuilderApp.js` and `tools/world-builder-v2/css/world-builder.css`.)

- Collection — Reuse-Grid Layout Fix: an Unbounded Vertical Grid Becomes a Fixed-Height Horizontal Scroll Strip (a real-usage follow-up delivered via a screenshot of the Experience Image content section's "Or reuse one already used elsewhere in this World:" reuse grid, with the user's own words: "we will need different layout. as the collection will grow the screen size will keep growing." Root cause, confirmed by reading the code rather than guessed: `_renderCollectionPicker`'s reuse section rendered every matching Collection entry into `.wb-scene-template-grid`/`.wb-scene-template-card` — a plain, unbounded auto-fill CSS grid with no `max-height`/`overflow-y` cap of any kind, shared by 6 different call sites in `worldBuilderApp.js` (the Scenes template picker, the Frame picker, the decoration glyph picker, two shape grids, and this reuse grid) — appropriate for those other 5, whose own source lists are small and fixed, but genuinely wrong for a Collection reuse grid, which grows every time a Theme Author adds a new asset (especially now that the immediately-prior "direct Add Image/Add Graphic" fix makes adding assets even easier). Since this markup sits embedded inline inside an Experience's own Image/Graphics content section in the Context Inspector — not a separate modal screen — every new Collection entry of a matching `kind` permanently grew the whole Inspector panel taller, exactly the reported symptom. **Fix, confined entirely to `_renderCollectionPicker` — the other 5 call sites sharing `.wb-scene-template-grid` are completely untouched**: the reuse section's markup was rewritten to use four brand-new CSS classes mirroring this codebase's own already-proven horizontal-scroll-strip precedent, the Scenes Library strip (`.wb-scenes-strip`/`.wb-scene-strip-card`, `world-builder.css` — `overflow-x:auto; overflow-y:hidden;` with fixed-width `flex:0 0 auto` cards) rather than inventing a new pattern: `.wb-collection-reuse-strip` (the horizontal-scroll flex container), `.wb-collection-reuse-card` (a fixed-width 72px card, `flex:0 0 auto`), `.wb-collection-reuse-thumb` (a 52px-tall thumbnail), and `.wb-collection-reuse-name` (a truncated single-line label, `text-overflow:ellipsis`). The strip's own height is now fixed regardless of entry count — 10 Collection entries render at the identical height as 1 — with the row simply scrolling horizontally once content overflows its own width, structurally decoupling the Context Inspector panel's height from Collection size forever. `_resolveAssetRefToSrc(ref)` (async thumbnail resolution) is unchanged, still called identically per card. Verified via a new, dedicated Playwright suite (`collection_picker_layout_verify.js`, scratch-only, 13/13 assertions, zero console/page errors): a real Blank World Project with 1 Scene, two Experiences ("Baseline Photo" seeded with 1 Collection entry, "Ten Photo" seeded later with 10) — the two-Experience design itself is a disclosed, deliberate test-authoring workaround for a real gotcha found while writing the first version of this test: `.wb-content-kind-btn`'s own click handler carries a genuine no-op guard (`if (k === kind) return;`), so re-clicking an already-active content-kind button never triggers a fresh render, silently leaving stale DOM behind and producing misleading results — using two fresh Experiences, each clicking Image content-kind for the first time, sidesteps this guard entirely rather than fighting it. The test confirms: the strip renders with exactly 1 card at 89px tall with 1 seeded entry; after seeding 9 more (10 total) and switching to the second, fresh Experience, all 10 real Collection entries render as reuse cards with `overflow-x:auto` and genuine horizontal overflow (`scrollWidth:796` vs. `clientWidth:345`); the strip's own height with 10 entries is confirmed BYTE-IDENTICAL (89px) to its height with 1 entry — the actual proof the fix works, not merely that the DOM renders; all 10 real thumbnails resolve to `<img>` elements; and clicking a specific card ("Photo 5") correctly commits its own `ref` to `imageSrc` and renders `.active`. The pre-existing `collection_phase2_verify.js` regression suite needed 3 stale selectors updated to match the new DOM shape (`.wb-scene-template-card`→`.wb-collection-reuse-card` at 3 sites) — re-verified 28/28 passing, unchanged behaviour underneath. Full regression: `collection_directadd_verify.js` (19/19, confirming the direct-add feature is completely unaffected), the Collection Phase 1 (27/27), Phase 3 (25/25), Phase 4 (17/17), Phase 5 (30/30), and Phase 6 (13/13, run against a temporarily-started local HTTP server on port 8931 since that one test script hardcodes its own base URL rather than starting its own dynamic-port server, a pre-existing quirk unrelated to this fix) suites all pass completely unchanged, plus both `goldenBuild.js` suites (World Builder v1 and v2, both PASS) — confirming zero regression anywhere. No Theme Contract/Engine V2 Scene Model/Creator Governing Rules change; root Studio (Creator) and `tools/world-builder/` (v1) are both completely untouched — confined entirely to `tools/world-builder-v2/js/worldBuilderApp.js` and `tools/world-builder-v2/css/world-builder.css`.)

- Collection — "From This World" Browsing Picker (Creator/Studio) Gets the Same Horizontal-Scroll-Strip Treatment (the same layout defect found one screen over, in the OTHER Collection picker: "from this world section in studio will also need to be presented in better manner." `js/contextPanel.js`'s Personalize→Add Something→"🎁 From This World" browsing surface (Collection Phase 6, root Studio's Creator-facing consumer of `availableToCreator` Collection assets) had the identical unbounded-grid defect as World Builder's own reuse picker, fixed one entry above: `_showCollectionPicker()`'s tile grid was a plain `display:grid; grid-template-columns:repeat(3,1fr)` with no height cap, which sits directly inline inside the right sidebar's Context Inspector — growing taller with every `availableToCreator` asset a Theme Author flags. **Fix, this time mirroring root Studio's own already-polished horizontal-scroll precedent rather than World Builder's** (a deliberate choice — Studio already has one proven, refined pattern for exactly this: `js/objectStrip.js`'s "this scroll can be better" fix, `css/style.css`'s `.object-strip-scroll-row`/`-arrow`/`-list` — round arrow buttons + a soft edge-fade mask over a real, native `overflow-x:auto` scroll, rather than the plain unadorned strip World Builder uses): `_showCollectionPicker()` now builds a `.context-collection-picker-row` (arrow buttons flanking a masked `.context-collection-picker-wrap`) wrapping the rewritten `.context-collection-picker-grid` (now `display:flex; overflow-x:auto;` with `scroll-snap-type:x proximity` and a hidden native scrollbar, instead of a `display:grid`), with `.context-collection-tile` changed from a grid cell to a fixed-width `flex:0 0 auto` card matching `.object-card`'s own established 78px width exactly, so every horizontal strip in this app now shares one consistent card size. Built entirely fresh each time the picker opens (no persistent DOM ids needed) — the arrow click handlers and scroll-position listener close over the local `list`/`prevBtn`/`nextBtn` variables directly, mirroring `js/objectStrip.js`'s own `_wireScrollArrows()` shape (including its identical 8px scroll-snap-settling tolerance for the arrow-disabled-state check) rather than a second, differently-implemented scroll widget. `_activeCollectionAssets()`/`_addCollectionObject()` and every field name/class the picker's own tiles carry (`.context-collection-tile-label`, etc.) are completely unchanged — this is a pure layout rewrite of the container, not a behaviour change.
