Verified via a new, dedicated Playwright suite (`collection_creator_layout_verify.js`, scratch-only, 17/17 assertions, zero unexpected console/page errors) seeding two synthetic artwork themes directly into `localStorage`'s `vihu.themeRegistry.imported.v1` key (2 and 10 `availableToCreator` entries respectively, in separate browser contexts) and driving the real UI end to end through Creation Flow→Workspace→Personalize→Add Something→From This World: confirms the strip is genuinely `overflow-x:auto` (not a grid) with real horizontal overflow at 10 entries (`scrollWidth:796` vs `clientWidth:345`... measured directly, not assumed), every tile still resolves a real `data:` URI thumbnail exactly as before, and — the decisive proof — the picker's own measured height with 10 entries (`102.59375px`) is byte-identical to its height with 2 entries, plus a genuine arrow-button-click scroll test confirming Next actually moves `scrollLeft` and Prev correctly enables/disables at the strip's own true start. The pre-existing `collection_phase6_verify.js` regression suite needed zero changes at all — its own selectors (`.context-collection-picker-grid`, `.context-collection-tile`, `.context-collection-tile-label`) were never renamed, only the container's own display/overflow behaviour changed — re-verified 13/13 passing unchanged. No Theme Contract/Engine V2 Scene Model/Builder architecture change; `tools/world-builder-v2/` and `tools/world-builder/` (v1) are both completely untouched — confined entirely to `js/contextPanel.js` and `css/style.css`.)

- Home Button — Skip the Gateway Cinematic, Land on My Projects (a real, direct report: "the press of home button from studio is taking out to very first screen tap to begin. it should be taking us to projects page as it was previously." **Root cause, confirmed by reading the code rather than guessed**: the Home button's own earlier fix (`ProjectManager.discardSession()` + `window.location.reload()`, needed to genuinely reset `AppState` so a new theme never inherits the previous one's Story-owned content — see "Home Button — a New Theme No Longer Silently Inherits the Previous Theme's Story-Owned Content" above) never distinguished a genuine fresh page load from a Home-triggered reload — both are, from the browser's point of view, plain page loads, so both replayed the full Traveller Gateway cinematic (`js/gatewaySequence.js`'s Sky/Lumo's Arrival/Identity/Gates-Open/Threshold sequence, deliberately unconditional on every launch per the "Canon Update Sprint — Traveller Gateway Rework V1.1," "every launch sees the Gateway now, known device or not") before Creation Flow ever appeared, and even once there, always landed on Screen 1's Type-choice grid rather than "Continue a Project" — exactly the two symptoms reported. **Fix**: a dedicated, one-shot `sessionStorage` flag (`HOME_RETURN_FLAG='vihu-home-return-to-projects'`), set only by the Home click handler right before `reload()` and read+consumed exactly once at the very top of the next boot's `_runBootstrap()` (`js/app.js`): when present, boot skips straight to `_beginBoot()` — bypassing both the Gateway cinematic AND `_afterGateway()`'s own standalone Identity Gate fallback, since Magic Card's active identity survives `discardSession()` completely untouched (a genuinely separate concept from the `ProjectManager` session key), so there's nothing left to re-verify — and tells `_startCreationFlow()` to call `CreationFlow.start({screen:'myProjects'})` instead of the bare, no-argument call. `js/creationFlow.js`'s `start()` function was widened to accept this optional `opts` parameter — opens `_renderMyProjectsScreen()` ("Continue a Project") when at least one real project exists, falling through to the ordinary Type-choice screen otherwise, mirroring the exact "never a dead-end" precedent `_deleteProjectRecord` already established for the last-project-deleted case; every other existing caller (`docs/journey/capture_screenshots.js`, calling `start()` with no arguments) is completely unaffected, since `opts` is optional throughout. The Gateway's own "every launch, known device or not" rule is left completely intact for every real fresh load/refresh — only this one button's own reload ever sets the flag, and it's removed the instant it's read, so it can never leak into or affect a genuine subsequent reload. Verified via two new Playwright suites: `home_button_myprojects_test.js` (10/10) — a real seeded My Projects record, pressing the real `#homeBtn`, confirming the Gateway overlay stays hidden and no "Tap to Begin" gate ever shows, the flag is genuinely consumed (`sessionStorage.getItem(...)===null` afterward), and Creation Flow lands directly on "Continue a Project" showing the real seeded project rather than the Type-choice grid; `home_button_edgecases_test.js` (5/5) — a genuine fresh page load (no flag manipulation at all) still shows the full Gateway cinematic exactly as before, and Home pressed with zero My Projects records still correctly falls back to the Type-choice screen rather than a dead-end blank grid. A fix was also needed to the pre-existing `home_button_leak_repro.js` scratch regression (the earlier theme-bleed-prevention test, confirming the `AppState`-reset guarantee that fix depends on is completely unaffected by this one) — its own second `pickThemeAndStart()` call now backs out via the My Projects screen's own real "← Back" link first, the disclosed, intended consequence of this fix (a real autosaved project now correctly redirects Home there instead of the bare Type-choice screen the test helper originally assumed) rather than a regression; re-verified 6/6 passing, zero console errors, confirming Theme B still carries zero stickers over from Theme A. `myprojects_test.js`/`myprojects_test2.js`'s own pre-existing, already-documented stale locator (predating the Traveller Gateway's own skip-helper convention) was confirmed via `git stash` A/B to fail identically on the unmodified baseline, unrelated to this fix. No Theme Contract/Engine V2 Scene Model/Builder architecture change; `tools/world-builder-v2/` and `tools/world-builder/` (v1) are both completely untouched — confined entirely to `js/app.js` and `js/creationFlow.js`.)

- Three Real, Screenshot-Reported Bugs — Companion Broken-Image Fallback, Publish Celebration Overlap, Magic Card Print Race (a batch of three independent, user-reported bugs, each investigated and fixed at its own root cause. **(1) "the companion did not loaded . check lower right corner"** (screenshot of the Magic Card First Claimed Moment screen showing a broken widget — a white circle with wrapped alt text spilling out reading "Quill —" / "dle"): confirmed `assets/quill/companion.json` declares 12 poses but only 5 files physically exist on disk, and critically `idle.png` — Quill's own `defaultState` — is genuinely missing (Nimbus, by contrast, has `idle.png` present and only lacks `think.png`, so it doesn't currently exhibit this exact symptom). `js/companionEngine.js`'s `_applyState(state)` had zero error handling of any kind, so the browser's own native broken-image glyph + wrapped alt text rendered directly inside the small circular portrait the instant a pose 404s. **Fix**: `_applyState` now installs an `onerror` handler mirroring the established fallback pattern already proven in `js/magicCardUI.js`'s `_playCeremonyBeats` — a missing requested-pose file falls back to the package's own already-uploaded `defaultState` pose file instead; if even THAT 404s (both files genuinely absent), the `<img>` gets a new `companion-portrait-img-broken` class (`css/style.css`, `visibility:hidden` — not `display:none`, which would collapse the portrait's own layout box and shift the glow ring/environment beneath it) so the widget shows a clean empty circle rather than an ugly broken-image box; the glow ring/environment around it still reads as "someone is here" either way. **(2) "top is getting overlapped"** (screenshot of Publish Studio's Celebration stage showing "🎉 Congratulations!" clipped flush against the modal header, only the bottom halves of the glyphs visible): confirmed via real Playwright-measured geometry, not guessed — reproduced at a shorter, realistic 1280×600 viewport (`headlineOverlapsHeader:true`) while the harness's own default 1500×950 showed no overlap at all, correctly redirecting the investigation toward viewport-height-dependent overflow rather than concluding the bug didn't exist. Root cause: `.publish-studio-body-celebration` combined `align-items:center`/`justify-content:center` with `overflow:hidden` — a classic CSS trap where `overflow:hidden` on a flex container whose centered content exceeds its own available height silently clips the TOP of that content, reading exactly as "overlapping" whatever sits directly above it (the header). **Fix**: `overflow-y:auto` (scroll instead of clip) plus `clamp()`-based padding/gap trims on `.publish-studio-body-celebration`/`.publish-celebration-center`/`.publish-celebration-stand` (shrinking vertical footprint at short heights so the common case never actually needs to scroll) plus, once stress-testing an even shorter 500px viewport surfaced the RELATED "safe center" scroll trap (`align-items:center`+`overflow-y:auto` on overflowing content leaves `scrollTop:0` showing the middle/bottom with the clipped top unreachable by scrolling up), `align-items:flex-start; align-items:safe center;` — the exact established fix pattern already proven once in this codebase for "Magic Card Home Scroll Fix," reused rather than reinvented. Verified via direct geometry measurement at four viewport heights (950/600/500/800px): zero overlap and the headline confirmed reachable/visible at every one. **(3) "print for magic card not working"** (screenshot of a real native Print dialog showing two blank placeholder rectangles instead of the Front/Back Magic Card art): cross-origin canvas tainting was investigated and ruled out first — confirmed `resolveCompanionPortrait()` in `magicCardArt.js` fetches portrait art via same-origin relative URLs, not cross-origin Supabase signed URLs, and confirmed `window.print()` visibly executed per the screenshot (which a thrown `SecurityError` from `toDataURL()` would have prevented) — correctly redirecting the investigation toward a decode-timing race instead. Root cause: `printCard(frontDataURL,backDataURL)` set both `<img>.src` to `data:` URIs and called `window.print()` on the very next line, with zero wait for the browser to actually decode either image into pixels first — a `data:` URI still needs real decode work (it isn't instant just because there's no network fetch), so print rendering could genuinely capture the sheet before either image finished, producing the blank placeholder rectangles the screenshot showed. **Fix**: `printCard()` now waits on `Promise.all([ready(imgFront),ready(imgBack)])` — `ready(img)` uses the real, Promise-based `img.decode()` where available (falling back to an `onload`-based wait, checking `img.complete` first, for a browser without `decode()` support) — before calling `window.print()`. The identical, byte-for-byte race was confirmed to exist in World Builder v2's sibling `_printCardArt()` (`tools/world-builder-v2/js/worldBuilderApp.js`) — `js/magicCardArt.js`'s own header comment discloses it was "ported verbatim" from that function — and was fixed there too, in lockstep, matching this codebase's own established convention for keeping sibling ported functions correct together rather than leaving one fixed and the other still broken. Verified via a new Playwright suite (`three_bug_batch_verify.js`, scratch-only, 17/17 assertions): a synthetic companion package with a missing requested pose but a present `defaultState` correctly falls back with no broken-image class and stays visible; a second synthetic package with BOTH the requested pose and `defaultState` missing correctly applies the broken-image class and hides via `visibility:hidden` (a genuine test-script bug was found and fixed along the way, disclosed rather than glossed over — `document.querySelector('.companion-portrait-img')` returns only the FIRST match in the DOM, and since an earlier `CompanionEngine` instance in the same page session had already mounted its own independent widget via `_ensureDom()`'s "fresh root per instance, never a document-wide singleton" behaviour, the unscoped query silently picked up the wrong engine's already-resolved element — fixed by scoping to the last-mounted widget); the Celebration heading shows zero overlap and stays reachable across all four tested viewport heights; `MagicCardArt.printCard()`'s `window.print()` call is confirmed, via a monkey-patched `HTMLImageElement.prototype.decode()` recording call order with an artificial delay, to fire only AFTER both images finish decoding, never before; World Builder v2's `worldBuilderApp.js` (containing the mirrored fix) loads with zero syntax errors. `publish_stages.js`/`magic_card_test.js`/`magic_card_phase2_test.js`/`mc_card_art_zoom.js` — older scratch scripts predating the Traveller Gateway's own skip-helper convention, confirmed via direct inspection to call no `skipGateway()` of any kind — were confirmed to be the same, already-extensively-documented pre-existing staleness class this codebase's history has confirmed dozens of times, unrelated to and unaffected by this fix; the new `three_bug_batch_verify.js` suite (which does call `skipGateway()`) already exercises the actual affected code paths (a real Publish Studio Celebration render through Creation Flow, direct `CompanionEngine`/`MagicCardArt` calls) end to end. No Theme Contract/Engine V2 Scene Model/Creator Governing Rules change; confined to `js/companionEngine.js`, `css/style.css`, `js/magicCardArt.js`, and `tools/world-builder-v2/js/worldBuilderApp.js`.)

- Magic Card Art — Enlarged Card View on Every Screen (a direct follow-up to a report first investigated and resolved as by-design: a screenshot of the Magic Card back face's small Guardian panel reading "LUMO" prompted "my card is showing lumo where as i got inkquill as my companion" — confirmed via two live Playwright rendering tests (a `companionId:'quill'` card fed straight into `MagicCardArt.drawFront`/`drawBack`) that Companion Canon V2's design is genuinely working as intended: the Front face's own headline always shows the Creator's real bonded companion (Quill's portrait/name/species), while the small Guardian panel on BOTH faces always shows Lumo — the fixed, never-bonded "Guardian of Story Companions/Creators" — exactly matching the screenshot; the user confirmed ("ok it matches") and immediately made a new, concrete ask: "i want to increase the size of card view on all screens where each element is easily readable." **Investigation, not guessed**: `.magic-card-art-canvas` (`css/style.css`) already had an enlarged `clamp(150px,32vw,240px)` size from an earlier "Star Traveller screen" sprint, but it was scoped to a specific ancestor pair, `.magic-card-awaken-stage .magic-card-art-view .magic-card-art-canvas` — reaching only the ceremony's First Claimed Moment, since Magic Card Home's own "View My Card" (`_buildCardArtView`, `js/magicCardUI.js`) never sits inside `.magic-card-awaken-stage`, and the nickname-prompt preview's own row (`.magic-card-nickname-preview-row`) never carries the required `.magic-card-art-view` class at all — both stayed stuck at the original flat 150px. **Fix, step 1**: generalized the enlarged clamp onto the bare `.magic-card-art-canvas` base rule, deleting the now-redundant ancestor-scoped override — every screen gets the same size with zero dependency on wrapper/ancestor structure, and `_fitAwakenStageToAvailableSpace()` (the established, generic "no scroll on any screen" shrink-to-fit function, already reading each canvas's real `getBoundingClientRect().width` fresh at call time rather than assuming any hardcoded base) needed zero JS changes to correctly handle the new default. **A real regression surfaced by a live Playwright measurement, not assumed safe**: Magic Card Home's canvases collapsed to a 90px floor instead of growing — traced to `_fitAwakenStageToAvailableSpace`'s width-shrink escalation step (`Math.max(90,naturalW-deficit*1.4)`), tuned for a smooth, single-line-height response to width changes, overshooting hard the instant the bigger 240px Front/Back pair crossed Home's own narrower panel's wrap threshold (`.magic-card-art-row{flex-wrap:wrap}`) — un-wrapping from two stacked lines back to one drops a whole line's height discontinuously, a jump the linear heuristic doesn't model, so a modest genuine deficit computed a wildly oversized correction that bottomed out at the function's own floor. **Fix, step 2, at the actual root rather than patching the shared multi-screen heuristic**: widened the room instead of shrinking the cards — `.magic-card-home-panel`'s own `max-width` bumped 460px→600px (enough to fit `2×240+14px gap=494px` of content plus its own horizontal padding on one line, comfortably avoiding the wrap threshold entirely on any normal viewport) — plus a second, deeper layering bug found only by directly inspecting computed styles rather than trusting the CSS source alone: that inner panel's `width:100%` was itself capped by ITS OWN parent, `#magicCardContent` (`.magic-card-panel`), whose base rule flat-caps every mode at 520px with no home-mode override at all (unlike gate-mode's own existing 680px override) — fixed by adding the missing `.magic-card-overlay.magic-card-mode-home .magic-card-panel{max-width:600px;}` rule, mirroring the gate-mode pattern exactly. Verified via a new Playwright suite driving the real UI (`MagicCardUI.openHome()` directly for Home; the real Awakening ceremony — reveal, Claim It, nickname prompt, ceremony beats, First Claimed Moment — for the other two screens) across 5 viewport sizes (1280×900 down to 420×700): all three screens now render genuine 240×336 canvases at typical sizes with zero scroll/overflow anywhere (`scrollHeight===clientHeight` confirmed at every size), and the shrink-to-fit safety net still gracefully engages at genuinely short viewports (240→143→90 as height drops from 900→700→600 at a fixed 1280 width) without ever reintroducing a scrollbar. Screenshots confirm Home's reveal-gated Back face still correctly blurs behind "Tap to Reveal," and the nickname-prompt preview — previously a small, barely-legible 150px pair — now shows a dramatically clearer Front/Back preview at the full 240px size. Full regression: both `goldenBuild.js` suites (World Builder v1 and v2) pass unchanged, confirming zero impact on either Builder surface (this change is confined entirely to root Studio CSS); 3 pre-existing scratch-script failures (`magic_card_test.js`/`magic_card_defer_test.js`/`magic_card_phase2_test.js`, all timing out on a Creation Flow Screen 1 locator) were confirmed via a `git stash` A/B to fail identically on the completely unmodified baseline — the same, already-extensively-documented "predates the Traveller Gateway's own skip-helper convention" staleness class this codebase's history has confirmed dozens of times, unrelated to and unaffected by this change; a grep confirmed no JS anywhere depends on the old flat 150px value or the old 460px panel width (the only numeric "150" matches nearby were an unrelated ceremony reveal-timing constant and `MagicCardArt`'s own separate internal canvas-drawing grid-layout math). No Theme Contract/Engine V2 Scene Model/Builder/Creator Governing Rules change; confined to `css/style.css`.)

- Magic Card Home — Redesigned Hero Layout, Then a Real Fix Once the Formula Was Actually Measured Against It (a two-part sprint, the first half shipped without its own CLAUDE.md entry at the time — recorded here alongside the correction it needed. **Part 1 — the redesign**: once the user actually saw Home rendered with the just-generalized `clamp(150px,32vw,240px)` size from the entry above, the ask sharpened: "give me a better screen for this. largest possible size for front and back." `openHome()` (`js/magicCardUI.js`) restructured its own DOM so the nickname/since block — previously two full lines of vertical footprint sitting stacked BELOW the card — now shares one thin header row with the Back button instead (`.magic-card-home-header`/`.magic-card-home-identity`, back on the left, name+since right-aligned on the right), directly funding a bigger hero row beneath it. `.magic-card-home-panel` (and its ancestor `#magicCardContent`/`.magic-card-panel`, kept in lockstep with the gate-mode override the same way that override was itself added) widened from 460px to 600px so a genuinely larger Front/Back pair had real room to sit side by side without wrapping, and a new `.magic-card-home-panel .magic-card-art-canvas` rule tied sizing to a flat, guessed formula — `max(90px, min(30vw,380px,calc((100vh-420px)*0.7143)))` — derived from this screen's own approximate footprint (420px) rather than a hardcoded number. The stories row was also condensed from an up-to-2-row CSS grid into a fixed-height horizontal scroll strip (fixed-width 74px thumbs, so the row's own height stays a small, predictable constant regardless of story count) — a further, deliberate reclaim of vertical space. **Part 2 — the formula didn't actually work at the user's own real viewport**: a follow-up screenshot showed the cards still rendering small, with the explicit report "the size of cards need to be increased. the front and back of magic card. they are still the same size." Investigated empirically rather than re-guessed, through three failed attempts before landing on the real fix. Attempt 1 (an ordering bug): calling the new sizing logic before the shared `_fitAwakenStageToAvailableSpace()` safety net let that function's own unconditional `c.style.removeProperty('width')` reset wipe out the just-computed size on every call. Attempt 2 (an overcorrecting heuristic): trying that same shared function's own "start wide, shrink by `deficit*1.4` on overflow" pattern for Home too made results measurably WORSE at several viewport sizes (e.g. 1280×700 regressed from 194px→90px) — the heuristic was only ever tuned for small corrections and badly overshot when starting from a large initial deficit. Attempt 3 (the real root causes, found via a dedicated debug script logging every intermediate value at the exact reported viewport shape, 1238×547): (a) the height budget was measured against `panel.clientHeight`, which only reflects however tall the panel has auto-sized itself to whatever it holds RIGHT NOW — `max-height` is a cap, not a fixed size, so measuring against it while the canvas was still small understated the real room available once the canvas was actually let to grow toward that cap; (b) `.magic-card-art-reveal-note`/`.magic-card-art-actions` (the reveal warning + Download/Print buttons, both genuinely inside `.magic-card-art-view`) had fixed-pixel margins, never made `--awaken-density`-aware like most of the rest of this screen, so the existing compression mechanism barely touched their footprint at all. **The real fix**: a new `_sizeHomeArtCards(panel)` (replacing the old CSS formula's job entirely, called from `openHome()` in place of the shared multi-screen fit function, which Home has no further use for once this one owns the job — Home has neither a sky-frame nor a ceremony-img-wrap for that function's other steps to ever act on) computes the canvas width analytically at three real, fully-applied compression scenarios — natural; chrome density-compressed with the Stories strip merely shrunk to 55% width; chrome compressed with Stories hidden outright — using `getComputedStyle(panel).maxHeight` (the resolved true ceiling) as the height budget instead of `clientHeight`, and only escalates to a heavier scenario when the current best candidate is still below a `GOOD_ENOUGH=220`px threshold — a guard added after a live screenshot at a comfortable 1440×900 viewport showed Stories being hidden even though there was no real need, since hiding it almost always buys SOME extra room regardless of how much room already exists. The two previously-fixed-pixel margins were converted to `calc(var(--awaken-density,1) * Npx)` in `css/style.css` to make them genuinely compressible under this same escalation. Verified via Playwright across 8 viewport sizes (the exact reported 1238×547 shape included): the reported shape now renders a genuine 211px card (up from the effective 90px floor it was stuck at) with Stories correctly hidden since that viewport is genuinely tight, while comfortable sizes (1280×700 through 1920×1080) now render substantially larger cards (233px–480px, hitting the ceiling at 1920×1080) with Stories correctly staying visible — zero scroll overflow confirmed at every size. Screenshots confirm both the tight-viewport shape (a large, clean card with Stories hidden) and a generous 1440×900 shape (an even larger card with a real 5-item Stories strip still showing beneath it). Full regression: the original 6-viewport-size redesign suite from Part 1 re-verified passing with zero errors and now delivering even bigger cards than that sprint's own flat 380px ceiling (e.g. 1920×1080 now reaches 456px); both `goldenBuild.js` suites (World Builder v1 and v2) pass unchanged, confirming zero impact on either Builder surface. No Theme Contract/Engine V2 Scene Model/Builder/Creator Governing Rules change; confined to `js/magicCardUI.js` and `css/style.css`.)

- Sheet Extractor — a new standalone `tools/` utility for real image segmentation, distinct from the fresh-illustration asset packs generated earlier this session (a moodboard image was analyzed and decomposed into 112 hand-illustrated matching assets across 18 categories, since the source moodboard was only ever pasted inline in chat with no file-level access available to segment it directly). The user's own follow-up made the actual gap explicit: "is it possible to create a utility which can extract the elements from the sheet like you just did" — a genuine, reusable tool doing real pixel-level object isolation from any reference sheet the user actually has as a file, not another illustration pass. Prototyped first as a Node CLI (`extract.js`, driven via Playwright/headless Chromium for canvas-based segmentation, since this sandbox has no PIL/sharp/ImageMagick), then hosted as a real, standalone browser page per the direct follow-up "can you host it in tools ?", matching this repo's own established `tools/` convention (`tools/audio-mixer/`, `tools/platform-status/`, `tools/background-remover/` — each a dependency-free, directly-openable `index.html`+`css/`+`js/` page, deletable independently of Builder/Studio). **The pipeline** (`js/extractor.js`): sample the four corners to estimate background color; classify every pixel foreground/background by color distance from it; connected-component label (BFS flood-fill, 4-connectivity) a slightly dilated copy of that mask purely to bridge tiny anti-aliasing/compression gaps before grouping pixels into objects; recompute each component's TIGHT bounding box from the original, undilated mask (`computeTightBoxes`) — a real two-part bug was found and fixed during the CLI prototype phase, not assumed correct: dilation was inflating every reported box by its own radius on all sides, and a first attempted fix left the box's own x/y origin still reading from the dilated component even after width/height became correct, root-caused via temporary debug instrumentation comparing three independent computations (the dilated component's own minX, the new tight-box function, and a brute-force scan) before finding the real one-line bug; pad each object's tight box by a caller-chosen fraction, then copy that region's real source pixels, forcing anything that isn't this object's own labeled pixel (background OR a genuinely different neighboring object) to fully transparent — verified decisively via a deliberate stress test where two objects sat close enough that their own PADDED crop rectangles geometrically extended into each other's real colored pixels (not just shared background margin, which the default settings alone can never force, confirmed by working through the exact arithmetic: at defaults, `2×dilateRadius+1` exactly equals the padding pixel count, making real-content overlap without also merging the masks mathematically impossible — a wider gap plus a higher `--pad` was needed to force a genuine test), sampled directly inside that overlap zone and confirmed each crop shows zero trace of the other's real color while still correctly showing its own; boundary pixels get a soft, color-distance-based partial alpha instead of a hard jagged edge; objects are numbered in natural reading order (top-to-bottom coarse bands, then left-to-right). **A second real bug, found specifically because hosting this as a genuine tool demanded checking it, not merely assumed away**: before wiring up the hosted UI, `tools/background-remover/`'s own README was reviewed for prior art and disclosed a real, already-fixed browser defect — `canvas.toDataURL()`/`getImageData()` reads from the canvas's own internal bitmap storage, which browsers commonly keep premultiplied by alpha for compositing performance, so converting back to straight RGBA on read is lossy at low alpha and undefined at alpha=0. Confirmed this directly and empirically for THIS tool specifically, with a genuinely revealing test case (a non-extreme, non-white RGB value at a genuinely mid-range partial alpha — my own earlier verification had happened to test only a white/255-valued pixel, for which premultiply/unpremultiply round-trips are always mathematically exact regardless of alpha, a real, self-identified gap in that prior check): writing known RGBA values via `putImageData` and reading them straight back via `getImageData` on the SAME canvas — no export involved at all — already showed real corruption at low/partial alpha (`(42,157,143,40)` came back `(45,159,140,40)`; `(42,157,143,1)` came back `(0,255,255,1)`), confirming the corruption is baked into the canvas's own backing store, which a `toDataURL()` export reading from that same store would carry straight into the file. Since this tool deliberately produces soft, partial-alpha boundary pixels by design — exactly the class of pixel this bug can corrupt — the hosted version's output path was rebuilt around a small, dependency-free hand-rolled PNG encoder (`js/pngEncoder.js`, adapted as a plain window-attached IIFE — matching this repo's own established non-module-script convention, `js/zipWriter.js` — from `tools/background-remover/js/pngEncoder.js`'s own already-verified ES-module version) that writes the PNG file format directly from the raw pixel buffer (signature, IHDR, a `CompressionStream('deflate')`-compressed IDAT chunk, hand-rolled CRC32) with zero canvas involved in the write path at all; `extractor.js`'s per-object output is now built as a bare `Uint8ClampedArray`, never a `<canvas>`+`putImageData`+`toDataURL`. **Verified this actually fixes it at the file-byte level, not merely re-reading through another canvas** (which would reintroduce the identical corruption regardless of how correctly the file itself was written — a real methodology mistake caught and corrected mid-investigation, when a first "does PngEncoder fix this" test loaded the encoded PNG back through an `<img>`+canvas and still showed drift, which turned out to be the TEST's own canvas-based readback corrupting an already-correct file, not a defect in the encoder): parsed the resulting PNG's own chunk structure directly, inflated its IDAT payload, and compared the decompressed scanline bytes to the original pixel buffer — every pixel, including `alpha=0` and `alpha=1` (the worst-corrupted cases under `canvas.toDataURL`), came back byte-identical in the actual file. **The hosted tool** (`tools/sheet-extractor/`): a real drag-and-drop/click-to-browse upload zone with a live preview; tunable Color Threshold/Padding/Min Object Size/Gap Bridging sliders plus a filename-prefix field and an auto-vs-manual background-color override, matching every option the CLI prototype offered; a results grid showing each cutout on a real checkerboard-transparency background with its own pixel-count/dimension readout and individual download link; a "Download All as ZIP" button reusing this repo's own existing `js/zipWriter.js` verbatim (already a dependency-free, STORED-only PKZip writer built for exactly this — PNGs are already compressed, so a second DEFLATE pass inside the ZIP would cost CPU for no space savings). Styled plainly and functionally, matching `tools/platform-status`'s own explicit "a developer dashboard, not a marketing page" precedent rather than Builder/Studio's warm/watercolor product identity. Verified end-to-end via a real-browser Playwright suite (26/26 assertions) driving the actual UI — a real file upload through the real `<input type="file">`, a real Extract click, confirming the exact same decisive checks the CLI prototype validated (genuine `(0,0,0,0)` transparency at every crop corner; the circle's tight bbox matching its known geometry exactly; every shape's center color exact against its known source hex value including the shadowed triangle; the same geometric-overlap-into-real-content stress test showing zero cross-contamination; the deliberate 3×3px noise speck correctly discarded) plus new UI-specific checks (a real individual PNG download link, a real "Download All as ZIP" click producing a genuine non-empty file starting with the correct PKZip signature, zero console/page errors throughout) — plus the separate, dedicated file-byte-level PNG-encoder proof described above. Purely additive — zero existing repository file was touched; `git status` before shipping confirmed only new files under `tools/sheet-extractor/`, so no `goldenBuild.js`/existing Playwright regression run was needed. No Theme Contract/Engine V2 Scene Model/Builder/Creator Governing Rules change; this tool has no relationship to Builder/Studio/the Theme Contract/Publish/Repository at all — confined entirely to the new `tools/sheet-extractor/` folder (`index.html`, `css/style.css`, `js/{app,extractor,pngEncoder,zipWriter}.js`, `README.md`).

- World Builder v2 — Rotate Functionality for the Image Content Section ("ok great utility. in the builder for images i need rotate functionality" — a direct product request landing right after the Sheet Extractor ship above. Investigated before assuming a gap: the sibling Graphics/Shape content section already had a working `graphicRotation` field and Rotation slider (0-359°), and all three consumers of a compiled decoration's `rotation` field — `EngineV2Runtime.paintLayer` (Working View/Runtime Preview/the isolated Experience Studio), `builder.js`'s `convergeSceneLayer` (the compiled Layer Pack entry's `decoration.rotation`), and root Studio's `renderer/slideRenderer.js`'s `_layerDrawDecorationImage` — were confirmed, via direct code read, to ALREADY be fully generic to a decoration layer's own `.rotation` field regardless of image-vs-shape source (the latter two already shipped in an earlier "BUG: Studio drops rotation on image-kind Decorations" fix this session). So the entire gap was purely authoring-side: no `imageRotation` field existed, no Inspector control existed, and — the real, load-bearing bug this feature's own implementation surfaced — `projectModel.js`'s `_syncUniversalContent` (the Engine Adapter mirroring an Experience's active content onto a real Scene Layer) computed its `rotation` value from a `shapeFields` fallback object that hardcoded `rotation:0` for the image slot on every single sync, since `shapeKind` computation is gated on `spec.slot==='graphic'` only — meaning even a correctly-added Rotation control would have been silently reset to 0 by the very next unrelated property edit (e.g. Opacity), never actually persisting. **Fix**: `experienceSchema.js`'s `defaultUniversalContent()` gained `imageRotation:0` alongside the existing `imageFit`/`imageOpacity` fields. `_syncUniversalContent` now computes `rotation` as its own variable — `props.imageRotation||0` for the image slot, the unchanged `props.graphicRotation||0` logic for a Graphics Shape, `0` for a plain (non-shape) Graphics image, matching this codebase's own already-established "Fit's `undefined` for non-image slots" precedent right above it — and spreads it onto BOTH the update-existing-layer `Object.assign(...)` call and the create-new-layer branch (`created.rotation=rotation`), so a rotated Image now survives repeated syncs instead of reverting to 0 on the next edit. `worldBuilderApp.js` gained a Rotation field group (`_buildFieldGroup('Rotation', _range(0,359,...))`) in the Image content section's Inspector, right after its existing Transform (Move/Resize) fields — mirroring the Graphics section's own layout exactly — plus `rotation:props.imageRotation||0` added to the isolated Experience Studio's own live-preview `paintLayer` call, so Working View/Runtime Preview reflect the rotation immediately while authoring, not only after a later Build. Verified via a new 19-assertion Playwright suite across 4 parts, each confirming a different link in the chain end to end: **(1)** the real UI — create an Image Experience via the actual "+ Add Experience" sequence (`addExperience({hostedBy:'free'})`→`graduateToPersonal`→`attachExperience`), click the real "Image" Content Kind button (confirming, along the way, that `contentKind` locks to `'text'` at creation time and no mirrored Layer exists for the image slot until this real click happens — a genuine finding about the existing content-kind-lock mechanism, not a bug), drag the real Rotation slider via a genuine DOM `input` event — confirms `props.imageRotation` persists AND the mirrored Scene Layer's own `.rotation` field reflects it (135, not hardcoded to 0 — the actual root-cause fix), with a subsequent, unrelated Opacity edit on the SAME sync pass confirmed to NOT stomp rotation back to 0; **(2)** `EngineV2Runtime.paintLayer`, called directly with a synthetic image layer and a `ctx.rotate` spy, confirms a genuine `ctx.rotate(42° in radians)` call for a rotated layer and zero `ctx.rotate` calls for `rotation:0` (byte-identical no-op for every existing theme with no rotation ever authored); **(3)** a real compile-time test through the actual Experience mirror (not a hand-built object) confirms `builder.js`'s `convergeSceneLayer` carries the real mirrored Layer's `rotation:275` through to the compiled Layer Pack entry's `decoration.rotation` unchanged, with the real image bytes still correctly embedded (Draft Asset Architecture unaffected); **(4)** root Studio's `renderer/slideRenderer.js`, driven with a mocked `ThemeEngine.getActiveArtworkTheme()` returning a synthetic theme carrying a compiled `decoration:{kind:'image', rotation:66, ...}` Layer Pack entry, confirms a genuine `ctx.rotate(66° in radians)` call — closing the loop on Creator Governing Rule #5 (Publish Fidelity): what Builder authors is exactly what Studio's Reader-facing renderer paints. Two real test-script bugs (not app bugs) were found and fixed while building this suite, both worth naming since they're the same class of gotcha this codebase's own history has hit before: a synthetic `slide.artworkTheme` set to a bare STRING id (rather than left `undefined`) silently defeats `_artworkTheme(s)`'s own `s.artworkTheme!==undefined` check, which returns the unresolved string directly instead of ever calling the mocked `ThemeEngine.getActiveArtworkTheme()` — the fix was to leave the field unset in the test fixture, letting the real fallback chain run; and a compile-time model test that sets `imageSrc` via a direct `updateExperienceProperty` call without ever calling `updateExperience(project,id,{contentKind:'image'})` first produces no mirrored Layer at all (an Experience's `contentKind` locks to `'text'` at creation and only changes via that explicit call, exactly matching what the real "Image" Content Kind button does), leaving `findMirroredSceneLayer` correctly returning `null`. Full regression: both `goldenBuild.js` suites (World Builder v1 and v2, 30/30 each, unaffected — this fix touches zero v1 files) and the existing Collection Phase 2/4/5 + scene-dropdown-repro Playwright suites all pass unchanged, confirming zero regression on any adjacent Experience/Collection machinery this feature's own fix (`_syncUniversalContent`) shares code with. No Theme Contract/Engine V2 Scene Model/Creator Governing Rules change; confined to `tools/world-builder-v2/js/services/experienceSchema.js`, `tools/world-builder-v2/js/projectModel.js`, and `tools/world-builder-v2/js/worldBuilderApp.js`.)

- World Builder v2 — Manage Collection Gains Multi-File Add ("also for collections in builder i would like to add multiple images in one go" — a direct, mid-turn follow-up request landing while the Image Rotation feature above was still being verified. The Manage Collection screen's direct "+ Add Image"/"+ Add Graphic" controls (an earlier, already-shipped sprint) each drove a plain single-file `<input type=file>` via the shared `_fileInputUpload(accept,onFile)` helper — selecting several files in the native OS picker in one go only ever registered the first, with the rest silently discarded, since `onFile` fires exactly once per `_fileInputUpload` call by design. **Fix, additive rather than a widened contract**: a new `_processUploadedFile(file,onFile)` factors out the shared read/downscale/store pipeline (FileReader → downscale-if-large via the existing `_downscaleImageDataURL` → `_storeUploadedAsset`) that `_fileInputUpload` already had inline, so both the original single-file path and the new multi-file path reuse the identical logic rather than duplicating it; `_fileInputUpload(accept,onFile)` itself is completely unchanged in behavior and signature — still calls `onFile` exactly once — so every one of its ~9 other existing callers (Identity Thumbnail/Hero, the generic Assets-screen slots, the Frame picker, the Experience Image/Graphics content picker's own `_assetUploadRow`) is untouched, deliberately preserving the established single-file contract rather than widening it for everyone. A new, separate `_fileInputUploadMulti(accept,onFile)` builds a hidden `<input type=file multiple>` and calls `onFile` once per selected file, in whatever order the browser's own `FileList` provides — each file's own upload/downscale/register pipeline runs completely independently, and `registerCollectionAsset`'s own already-idempotent, synchronous `project.files` mutation means calling it several times in a row as each file's async pipeline resolves is safe regardless of completion order (no coordination needed between the N in-flight uploads). Both Manage Collection direct-add buttons (`"+ 🖼️ Add Image(s)"`, `"+ 🎭 Add Graphic(s)"` — relabelled with the "(s)" suffix to signal the new capability) now build their hidden input via `_fileInputUploadMulti` instead of `_fileInputUpload`, with each file's `onFile(ref)` callback calling the identical, unchanged `registerCollectionAsset(project,ref,{kind})` + `_persist()` + `_renderCollectionPanel()` sequence the single-file version already used. Verified via a new, dedicated Playwright suite (`verify_collection_multifile.js`, scratch-only, 22/22 assertions, zero console/page errors): static source checks confirm `_fileInputUploadMulti`/`_processUploadedFile` exist and that both Manage Collection buttons route through the new multi-file helper while the Experience content picker's own `_assetUploadRow` is confirmed completely unaffected, still calling the original single-file `_fileInputUpload`; a real end-to-end drive of the UI (Create New World → Blank template → add a Scene + a fresh Experience purely to reach the screen via the real "Manage Collection →" bridge link, mirroring the earlier direct-add sprint's own proven navigation) selects 3 real, distinct PNG fixture files on the real "+ Add Image(s)" input in ONE native `setInputFiles()` call — simulating a genuine multi-select in the OS file picker — and confirms all 3 register as 3 distinct Collection entries (not just the first) with 3 genuinely distinct resolved thumbnails (no dedup/collision), then repeats the identical proof for "+ Add Graphic(s)", bringing the panel to 6 correctly-kinded rows total (3 image, 3 graphic). Full regression: both `goldenBuild.js` suites (World Builder v1 and v2, 30/30 each, unaffected — this fix touches zero v1 files) and the existing Collection Phase 1-5 + direct-add + picker-layout Playwright suites all pass unchanged; a Creator-side (root Studio) Collection layout test was independently confirmed, via `git stash`, to already fail identically on the unmodified baseline (a pre-existing, already-documented hardcoded-port quirk in that one scratch script, unrelated to and unaffected by this change). No Theme Contract/Engine V2 Scene Model/Creator Governing Rules change; confined to `tools/world-builder-v2/js/worldBuilderApp.js`.)

- Sheet Extractor — Per-Image Compression Slider ("in the image extractor, can we also add compressor for each image extracted," refined by a direct follow-up: "we can show the size of image on the tool itself and a slider which can show at how much compression what will be the size of image and how it will look?" — so the feature must show real file size before/after AND let the slider live-update both the resulting size and the visual thumbnail, so any quality loss is directly visible before downloading anything, never a blind trade-off. **Two techniques, layered**: (1) `js/pngEncoder.js`'s `encode()` — previously always Filter-None — now runs real per-scanline filter selection (None/Sub/Up/Average/Paeth, picked per-line via the same "minimum sum of absolute signed-byte differences" heuristic libpng's own default encoder uses) — genuinely lossless, benefiting every existing extraction for free, no slider needed; (2) a new `js/pngCompressor.js` implements from-scratch median-cut color quantization — builds a histogram of distinct RGBA colors (canonicalizing every fully-transparent pixel to `(0,0,0,0)` first), and either uses the exact colors verbatim when the real distinct count already fits the requested cap (flagged `exact:true`, a genuinely lossless re-encode, not a quality trade) or repeatedly splits the group with the widest weighted-count-scored channel range at its weighted median until the target count is reached, then maps every pixel to its nearest palette entry (squared distance, alpha weighted 4x) with per-color memoization — written out via a new `PngEncoder.encodeIndexed()` (color type 3, a real PLTE + tRNS-for-alpha PNG, still zero `<canvas>` involvement in the write path, matching this tool's own established integrity discipline). A 7-level `LEVELS` table (Lossless/256/128/64/32/16/8 colors) backs the slider; the slider's own `max` attribute is derived from `PngCompressor.LEVELS.length-1` at init time rather than hardcoded, so the two can never silently drift apart. **AV-009's established discipline, reused rather than reinvented**: quantizing never makes a download bigger — the compressor always falls back to the original lossless blob when a quantized attempt comes out larger, and the UI honestly labels a genuinely-already-low-color object as "still lossless" (`exact:true`) rather than implying a trade-off that didn't actually happen. `js/app.js` wires a debounced (150ms) `applyCompression(level)` that re-encodes every extracted item at the chosen level via `PngCompressor.compress(item.pixelBuffer, level, item.blob)` (each item's raw RGBA buffer was already kept alive from segmentation for exactly this, per `extractor.js`'s own doc comment) and swaps each result into `item.activeBlob`/a fresh thumbnail object URL, updating a real `Original: X → Y (-Z%)` size line per item plus an aggregate `Total: X (Y% smaller)` summary line — both the "Download" link per item and "Download All as ZIP" (and a fresh extraction run) all read `item.activeBlob`, so every export path respects whatever level is currently selected. Verified via a new 29-assertion Playwright suite against the real, hosted page (a genuine upload + extract + slider drag, no mocks): a high-color gradient object quantizes to a real indexed PNG whose palette — parsed directly from the file's own PLTE chunk, never inferred via canvas — never exceeds the requested color count and whose real byte size shrinks; a low-color flat rectangle object is correctly labeled "still lossless" rather than falsely implying a quality trade; reverting the slider to Lossless restores the exact original blob URL (not a re-encoded copy); ZIP download and re-running Extract both correctly respect the currently-selected level; zero console/page errors. A follow-up screenshot at compression level 5 (~16 colors) was visually inspected and confirmed real, visible color banding on the gradient object while the flat-color object stayed correctly labeled lossless — the trade-off is genuinely visible, not just reported in text. Shipped via this tool's own established convention (plain commit + push, no `build-info.json`/cache-bust ritual — this standalone page has neither). No Theme Contract/Engine V2 Scene Model/Builder/Creator Governing Rules change; this tool has no relationship to Builder/Studio/Publish/the Theme Contract at all — confined to `tools/sheet-extractor/js/{app,extractor,pngEncoder}.js`, a new `tools/sheet-extractor/js/pngCompressor.js`, `tools/sheet-extractor/{index.html,css/style.css,README.md}`.)

- World Builder v2 — Rotation Extended to Text Content ("also add rotation to text, and graphics in builder" — a direct follow-up landing right after the Image Rotation feature shipped. Investigated methodically, one link of the pipeline at a time, rather than assumed complete by analogy: Graphics (Shape variant — an author-drawn circle/star/arrow/speech-bubble/banner) already had a fully-wired `graphicRotation` field end to end (Inspector control, `_syncUniversalContent`, `EngineV2Runtime.paintLayer`, `builder.js`'s compiled `decoration.rotation`, root Studio's `_layerDrawShape`) — confirmed working via a quick sanity re-check rather than left unverified; a plain uploaded Graphics IMAGE (not a Shape) deliberately stays unrotatable, matching its own pre-existing "no Fit control either" scope boundary (Properties: Upload/Replace/Remove/Preview/Opacity only) — a disclosed design boundary, not a gap, so left untouched. Text had genuinely nothing, confirmed at every layer: no `textRotation` property existed; `_syncUniversalContent`'s text mirror block (`projectModel.js`) never read or wrote any rotation field at all; `EngineV2Runtime.paintLayer`'s `text` branch (`engineRuntime.js`) had no rotation handling whatsoever, unlike its own sibling Decoration branch immediately below it; `builder.js`'s `convergeSceneLayer` text-kind compile branch produced `{type:'text',anchor,text:{content,font,size,color}}` with no rotation field, so even an authored rotation would have been silently discarded at Build time; and — a genuinely NEW finding beyond the Image-rotation precedent, confirmed by reading the full function rather than assumed — root Studio's own `renderer/slideRenderer.js`'s `_layerDrawText` only ever read a Story-Author override (`ov.rotation`, from an earlier "Extend `_layerDrawText` for rotation/opacity/full typography overrides" sprint), never any Theme-Author-authored compiled rotation field, so even a perfectly correct compile step would have had nowhere to land in the real Reader-facing renderer. **Fix, five links, each verified against its own real mechanism rather than assumed to follow from the others**: `experienceSchema.js` gained `textRotation:0` alongside the existing `textOpacity`; `_syncUniversalContent`'s text mirror block now carries `rotation:props.textRotation||0` on both the update (`Object.assign`) and create (`created.rotation=...`) paths, mirroring the Image-slot fix exactly; `engineRuntime.js`'s `_paintLayer` text branch gained the identical translate-to-rect-centre/rotate/translate-back wrapping its own Decoration branch already used, reading `layer.rotation`; `builder.js`'s text compile branch now carries `rotation:layer.rotation||0` inside the compiled `text:{}` object (root Studio's `_layerDrawText` reads it as `t.rotation`); root Studio's `_layerDrawText` was rewritten so its rotation resolution reads `t.rotation` (the compiled, Theme-Author-authored base) as its default, with a genuine Story-Author override (`ov.rotation`) still correctly winning over it when present — the exact `ov`-overrides-`t` precedent every other field in this function already follows (fontFamily/color/etc.), byte-identical to before for any object with neither set. `worldBuilderApp.js` gained a Rotation field group in the Text content section's Inspector, appended right after its existing Transform (X/Y/Width/Height) fields — the last range slider in DOM order, matching the Image section's own layout precedent — plus `rotation:props.textRotation||0` wired into the isolated Experience Studio preview's own live `paintLayer` call for text-kind content. `tools/world-builder/` (v1) was deliberately left untouched — confirmed by reading its own `builder.js`, which has an identical Fidelity-fix-era text compile branch (kept in lockstep once, for the anchor/alignment fix only) but no rotation-authoring mechanism anywhere in its `projectModel.js` for ANY object kind, image/shape/text alike — adding a compile-time field for a capability v1 has no UI to author would be scope creep beyond what was asked, matching this codebase's own "v1 untouched" precedent. Verified via a new 22-assertion Playwright suite across 5 parts, mirroring the Image-rotation feature's own verification shape: **(1)** the real UI — create a Text Experience via the actual "+ Add Experience" sequence (Text's `contentKind` defaults to `'text'` already, so unlike Image the mirror exists the instant `textContent` is set, with no Content Kind button click needed — confirmed directly, not assumed), drag the real Rotation slider via a genuine DOM `input` event — confirms `props.textRotation` persists AND the mirrored Scene Layer's own `.rotation` field reflects it (210, not hardcoded to 0), with a subsequent unrelated Opacity edit on the SAME sync pass confirmed to NOT stomp rotation back to 0; **(2)** `EngineV2Runtime.paintLayer`, called with a synthetic text layer and a `ctx.rotate` spy, confirms a genuine `ctx.rotate(42° in radians)` call for a rotated layer and zero calls for `rotation:0`; **(3)** a real compile-time test through the actual Experience mirror confirms `builder.js`'s `convergeSceneLayer` carries the real mirrored Layer's `rotation:187` through to the compiled Layer Pack entry's `text.rotation`, with the pre-existing alignment/content Fidelity fields confirmed unaffected; **(4)** root Studio's `renderer/slideRenderer.js`, driven with a mocked `ThemeEngine.getActiveArtworkTheme()` returning a synthetic theme carrying a compiled `text:{rotation:66,...}` Layer Pack entry, confirms a genuine `ctx.rotate(66° in radians)` call when no Story-Author override exists (Publish Fidelity, Creator Governing Rule #5) — AND, driven a second time with a real `elementOverrides` bag setting `ov.rotation:15`, confirms the override genuinely wins over the compiled 66° base, never both applied together; **(5)** a quick sanity re-check confirms Graphics Shape rotation (already shipped) still persists correctly end to end, unaffected by this change. All 22 assertions passed on the first run. Full regression: both `goldenBuild.js` suites (World Builder v1 and v2, 30/30 each, unaffected — this fix touches zero v1 files) and the existing Collection Phase 2/4/5 + scene-dropdown-repro3 Playwright suites all pass unchanged, confirming zero regression on any adjacent Experience/Collection machinery this feature's own fix (`_syncUniversalContent`) shares code with. No Theme Contract/Engine V2 Scene Model/Creator Governing Rules change; confined to `tools/world-builder-v2/js/services/{experienceSchema,engineRuntime,builder}.js`, `tools/world-builder-v2/js/projectModel.js`, `tools/world-builder-v2/js/worldBuilderApp.js`, and root Studio's `renderer/slideRenderer.js`.)

- World Builder v2 — Text Rotation Was Orbiting, Not Spinning: Fixed the Rotation Pivot (a real, user-reported bug found the very same session the Text Rotation feature above shipped: "you have implemented rotation. we need spin... the current rotation is moving the object all around the canvas in circular motion. the rotation needs to be able to rotate the object 360 degree tied down at its centre. like we did for image, like we have in studio." Investigated rather than assumed — a first `AskUserQuestion` correctly ruled out "just rename it" (this was never a vocabulary ask) once the user clarified the actual visible symptom. **Root cause, confirmed by direct code read**: `engineRuntime.js`'s `_paintLayer` text branch rotated around the Layer's *declared* box (`rect`, from `rectFor()`) — the exact convention its sibling Decoration branch correctly uses, since an Image/Shape's declared box IS its visible content. But a Text Layer's declared box is only ever a wrap-width/creation-time placeholder height (`textFootprint()`'s own AV-006/AV-010 doc comment already names this precisely) — completely decoupled from where the real glyphs sit once actual content exists (World Builder's default text box is `{w:0.7,h:0.15}`, routinely far larger than a short line of real text). Pivoting on that declared box's own center swung the visible glyphs through a wide arc around empty space as the angle changed, reading exactly as "moving around the canvas" rather than spinning in place — and confirmed this ISN'T how Image/Shape or root Studio's own `_layerDrawText` behave: Studio already rotates around `drawX/drawY`, a point derived from the real rendered content's own measured bbox (`maxLineWidth`/`totalH`), never a raw declared box, which is why "like we have in studio" was a correct reference point. **Fix**: `_paintLayer`'s text branch now computes its rotation pivot from `textFootprint(ctx,layer,graph)` — the same real, measured extent this module already exports and already uses for hit-testing/dragging — instead of `rect`, so painting and interaction can never disagree about where the text's true center is; `rect` is still used unchanged for wrap-width/positioning, only the rotation pivot changed. Zero changes needed anywhere else — the isolated Experience Studio preview calls `EngineV2Runtime.paintLayer` directly and inherits the fix automatically; Image/Shape rotation (whose declared box already coincides with their visible content) and root Studio's compiled-rotation rendering (already footprint-equivalent) both needed no change. **Verified via real pixel sampling, not just a `ctx.rotate()` angle spy** (which can't distinguish "rotates in place" from "rotates around the wrong point"): rendered a short string ("Hi") in a large declared box at rotation 0° and 180°, and measured the actual painted ink's own bounding-box center at each — a stationary pivot must leave that center essentially unchanged across a 180° turn. Confirmed via a `git stash` A/B: the unmodified baseline showed a 711px center drift between the two renders (the reported bug, reproduced exactly); the fix reduces it to 22px (residual glyph-shape/alignment asymmetry, not pivot error), landing within 11.5px of the real footprint center versus 356px away from the old declared-box center. Full regression: the original 22-assertion Text Rotation Playwright suite passes completely unchanged (this fix touches only the rotation pivot, not the rotation angle/persistence/compile/Fidelity mechanics that suite covers), and both `goldenBuild.js` suites (World Builder v1 and v2, 30/30 each) pass unchanged. No Theme Contract/Engine V2 Scene Model/Creator Governing Rules change; confined to one function, `_paintLayer`, in `tools/world-builder-v2/js/services/engineRuntime.js`.)

- World Builder v2 — Working View Z-Order Fidelity Fix: Builder's Own Preview No Longer Lies About a Free-Hosted Background Image's Real Compiled Z-Order (a real bug found only after the user disputed an earlier claim with concrete evidence: two screenshots showing Builder's own Runtime Preview rendering "The Imagination Gallery" correctly — a frame, a ribbon, a heart icon, "Imagination Vault" title text, and an "@vihuPlanet" watermark all visible — while root Studio showed the SAME World as a completely blank cream/tan rectangle, even though the Object Strip beneath it still listed every object as present and editable. Two synthetic reproductions built first (a single-Place Scene with a Frame; a 6-Place Gallery-template Scene) both rendered correctly in Studio, directly contradicting the report — so, per this session's own established discipline of re-investigating honestly rather than defending a narrower test, the user's real, uploaded `.vtheme` export file was requested and traced directly. **Root cause, confirmed by decoding the actual compiled package**: the real file's `theme.layerPack` (7 entries, a zero-Holder Scene) had exactly ONE entry compiled to `target:'overlay'` (drawn dead LAST, on top of literally everything) — a full-bleed image literally named "Cover - bg - Experience," decoded and visually confirmed to be a cream/tan aged-paper texture, exactly matching the reported blank canvas; the other 6 entries (a picture frame, a tape clip, three text pieces, a heart-shaped decoration) all compiled to `target:'slide'` (drawn FIRST, underneath). Reading `tools/world-builder-v2/js/services/builder.js`'s `convergeSceneLayer` confirmed this bucketing is driven entirely by each Experience's own Hosted-By setting (`layer.hostedByScene===true` → `'slide'`; otherwise, unless it's a true full-bleed Colour fill, → `'overlay'`) — completely independent of a Layer's actual position in the authored Scene Stack. In this real Theme, the Theme Author left the ONE Experience meant to be a background as Free-hosted while leaving all 6 foreground decorations Scene-hosted — backwards from the design's own intent — but with zero warning anywhere, because `tools/world-builder-v2/js/services/engineRuntime.js`'s `render(ctx,graph)` (the one function shared by both Working View and Runtime Preview) painted `graph.stack` in pure, raw authored order with NO consideration of this bucketing rule at all — a genuine, confirmed Fidelity gap (Creator Governing Rule #1): a Theme Author who places a Free-hosted image at the bottom of their Scene Stack (the natural way to intend a background) sees it render correctly, behind everything, in Builder's own preview — then discovers, only after Publishing, that it draws dead last and buries everything else, since Free-hosted content always compiles to the overlay bucket regardless of stack position. **Fix**: a new `_isBackgroundLayer(layer)` helper mirrors `convergeSceneLayer`'s own `target` computation byte-for-byte (`layer.hostedByScene===true` OR a true full-bleed Colour fill); `render()` now buckets its OWN paint order to match — background-classified Layers paint first, Holders/Places keep their own relative order in the middle, every other Layer paints last — reordering PAINT ONLY via a local array built fresh on every call; `graph.stack` itself is never mutated, so `worldBuilderApp.js`'s own click-to-select `mousedown` handler (which reads `ProjectModel.sceneStack` directly, a completely separate, live-reconciled source) is provably unaffected. **Verified via a decisive git-stash A/B Playwright reproduction built directly from the real file's own exact configuration** (a Free-hosted full-bleed firebrick-red background Layer at the bottom of the stack, a Scene-hosted navy-blue foreground decoration on top, matching the real Theme's actual `hostedByScene` values): the UNMODIFIED baseline showed the foreground correctly on top at the overlap pixel (matching the user's own Builder screenshot, but silently diverging from what Studio would actually compile and render) — the FIXED code shows the background now correctly painting last/on top in Builder's own preview too, an honest, truthful match for Studio's real `target:'overlay'` behaviour, giving a Theme Author immediate, correct visual feedback in Builder itself to switch that one Experience's Hosted-By setting to Scene, rather than a silent surprise only discoverable after Publish. **A disclosed, important limitation, not glossed over**: this fix makes Builder's preview truthful going forward — it does NOT retroactively repair the user's own already-authored "The Imagination Gallery" Theme's actual visual output. That specific Theme's "Cover - bg - Experience" is still Free-hosted while its 6 siblings are Scene-hosted; fixing that Theme's real appearance (in both Builder's now-corrected preview and in Studio) requires the Theme Author to go into Builder and switch that one Experience's Hosted-By setting from Free to Scene, matching its siblings — Builder's newly-honest Working View will now show this problem clearly before Publish, rather than hiding it. Full regression: both `goldenBuild.js` suites (World Builder v1 and v2, 30/30 each) and every existing Rotation/Shapes/Text-fidelity Playwright suite (image rotation, text rotation, text rotation pivot, stretch fit, text alignment fidelity, text newline fix) pass completely unchanged, confirming zero regression — none of them exercise multi-layer z-order bucketing, so none were affected by this fix. No Theme Contract/Engine V2 Scene Model/Builder architecture change; `tools/world-builder/` (v1) is untouched, since v1 has no Experience/hostedByScene concept of its own to carry this bug; confined to one function, `render()`, plus one new helper, `_isBackgroundLayer()`, in `tools/world-builder-v2/js/services/engineRuntime.js`.)

- World Builder v2 — Transparent Scene Backgrounds + a Direct Answer on Multi-Asset Experiences (two independent, direct questions in one message, with no further elaboration: "1. i want option to set background color as transparent. 2. is it possible to have multiple assets within a single experience?" A clarifying `AskUserQuestion` on both went unanswered; proceeded on my own best-judgment, most conservative interpretation for each, disclosed here rather than silently assumed. **Item 1, two real, stacked gaps, both found by reading the code rather than guessed**: (a) the Colour Experience's Scene-hosted "Transparent" checkbox (`_syncUniversalContent` in `tools/world-builder-v2/js/projectModel.js`) was a documented no-op — `if(kind==='colour' && props.colorTransparent===false){setSceneBackground(...)}` only ever ran when the checkbox was NOT checked, so checking it never actually cleared or transparentized anything at all. Fixed by having it genuinely resolve an opacity every time: `props.colorTransparent ? 0 : (colorOpacity or 1)`, then always calling `setSceneBackground(project,sceneId,color,opacity)` — the checkbox now forces the background fill Layer's own opacity to genuinely `0` when checked, and correctly restores whatever `colorOpacity` was already set to when unchecked, matching this codebase's own established "an ordinary full-bleed fill Scene Layer, not a special field" design (the exact mechanism Sprint 9.5/Engine Invariant 8 already locked in — "Canvas has no background property... a special `scene.background` field would be exactly the second way to do something Elements-in-Layers already do" — reused, never a new field invented). `setSceneBackground(project,sceneId,color,opacity)` gained an optional 4th `opacity` parameter (default `1`, so every existing caller keeps its exact prior fully-opaque behaviour byte-for-byte). (b) Even with a genuinely transparent background Layer now authored, BOTH rendering engines still couldn't show it: `tools/world-builder-v2/js/services/engineRuntime.js`'s `render(ctx,graph)` and root Studio's `renderer/slideRenderer.js`'s `render(s)` each painted an UNCONDITIONAL opaque backdrop fill (`#F4F1EC`/`_wallTone||_frameColor(...)`) before any Scene Layer ever drew — so a fully-transparent background Layer's own alpha=0 pixels simply composited over an already-opaque canvas and stayed invisible, no matter how correctly the checkbox itself now worked. Fixed with a matching, mirrored guard in each engine — a new `_hasExplicitBottomFill(graph)` (Builder) checks whether `graph.stack[0]` is a genuine full-bleed (`w,h>=0.98`) fill Layer, and a new `_hasSlideFullBleedFill(pack)` (Studio) checks the active compiled Layer Pack for the equivalent `target:'slide'`/`decoration.kind==='fill'`/`rect.w,h>=0.98` entry — each skipping its own unconditional fallback fill ONLY when such a Layer genuinely exists, letting that Layer's own (possibly fully transparent) opacity become the real, honest painted result instead. Deliberately left the fallback's own default behaviour completely untouched for every Scene/theme with no such Layer authored — a purely additive, opt-in design, not a sweeping change to what an ordinary, unauthored-background theme shows by default. This directly serves Creator Governing Rule #1 (Fidelity) and #5 (Publish Fidelity): Builder's own Working View/Runtime Preview and Studio's real Reader-facing render now agree on transparency exactly, since both engines resolve it through the identical "is there an explicit full-bleed fill Layer" check mirrored against each other. **Item 2, answered directly rather than built**: confirmed via direct code reading (`experienceSchema.js`'s `_ensureExperienceDefaults`, whose own doc comment states it plainly) that "Only-one-content-type-at-a-time" is a deliberate, already-shipped Builder V3.1 product simplification — an Experience's `contentKind` ('text'|'image'|'graphics'|'colour') restricts rendering to exactly one of the four Universal Content sections at a time, a real, intentional decision reversing Builder V3.1's own earlier "every Experience holds all four simultaneously" design — so no new capability was built for this question; the real, already-available workaround (placing several separate Experiences together in one Scene, each its own content) plus an offer to build either "combine kinds within one Experience" or "multiple images in one slot" as a genuine, separately-scoped follow-up were the answer given, not code. Verified via a new 8-assertion Playwright suite spanning all three affected surfaces: Part A, World Builder's own `EngineV2Runtime.render()` called directly with synthetic Scene data (no bottom fill Layer → the exact `#F4F1EC` opaque fallback, byte-for-byte unchanged; a full-bleed fill Layer at `opacity:0` → genuinely `alpha:0`; the same Layer at `opacity:1` with an opaque colour → paints that colour correctly, confirming the fallback-skip path itself paints right, not just skips); Part B, real `ProjectStore`/`ProjectModel` calls simulating the actual Colour Experience UI flow end to end (not-Transparent honours `colorOpacity` at 0.7; checking Transparent forces opacity to genuinely `0`, not a silent no-op; unchecking restores `colorOpacity` back to 0.7); Part C, Studio's `renderer/slideRenderer.js` `render(s)` called directly with a synthetic compiled theme (no full-bleed `target:'slide'` fill Layer → the wall-tone/frame-colour fallback fully unchanged, `alpha:255`; a full-bleed fill Layer at `alpha:0` → genuinely transparent, `alpha:0`, not the opaque fallback). Full regression across every existing render-pipeline-touching Playwright suite confirmed zero regression: `verify_bg_zorder_fix.js` (the immediately-prior z-order fix, sharing the exact same `render()` functions this fix touches), `verify_stretch_fit.js`, `verify_text_align_fidelity_fix.js`, `verify_text_newline_fix.js`, `verify_image_rotation.js`, `verify_text_rotation.js`, `verify_text_rotation_pivot.js`, `verify_rotation_publish_honored.js`, `museum_regression.js`, and — the most decisive check, since it touches the exact same `render()`/base-fill code path this fix modifies — `museum_realfile_pixelhash.js`, a real, on-disk `themes/MuseumGallery.vtheme` file rendered end to end and SHA-256-hashed, confirmed byte-for-byte identical (`e7b2a9...`) to the hash this codebase's own history already recorded before this session's changes, plus `museumcaption_fix_verify.js`/`museumcaption_realdrag_verify.js` (real drag/resize interaction on a Museum Caption text object, unaffected), plus `scene_dropdown_repro3.js` (Experience Host Here dropdown/graduation flows, sharing `_syncUniversalContent` with this fix, unaffected). Both `goldenBuild.js` suites (World Builder v1 and v2, 30/30 each) pass unchanged. No Theme Contract/Engine V2 Scene Model/Builder architecture change; `tools/world-builder/` (v1) is untouched — this fix is scoped to v2's own Universal Experience Content model, which v1 never had; confined to `tools/world-builder-v2/js/projectModel.js`, `tools/world-builder-v2/js/services/engineRuntime.js`, and `renderer/slideRenderer.js`.)

- Multi-Asset Experience Parts (World Builder v2 only — implements the user's own governing request across all 6 phases: **"ok lets try to incorporate multiple assets in single experience. lets allow combinations with max number of assets in an experience not exceeding 5."** A follow-up confirmed repeats of the same kind (two Image parts, two Text parts, etc.) are genuinely allowed — any mix, up to 5 total — scoped to `tools/world-builder-v2/` only, never v1 or root Studio. Two Explore-agent investigations plus a Plan-agent design (independently re-verified against the live code before finalizing) surfaced the load-bearing finding: the compile pipeline (`builder.js`), the paint engine (`engineRuntime.js`), and root Studio's entire Reader-facing render/selection stack are ALL already fully N-parts-capable with zero code changes needed — none of them have any concept of "which Experience owns this Layer" at all, confirmed via grep that `builder.js` never even copies Experience-grouping info into a compiled Layer Pack entry. The entire feature is contained in the Engine Adapter (`projectModel.js`'s `_syncUniversalContent` and neighbors) plus the authoring UI (`worldBuilderApp.js`). **Phase 1 — data model + migration + Collection dual-write foundation**: `experience.properties.parts` holds up to 5 `{id,kind,props}` entries, reusing the exact existing flat field names (`imageX`, `textContent`, etc.) nested one level in — no kind-agnostic renaming scheme, so `_contentTransformFields` and every existing per-field helper needed zero internal changes. A live legacy mirror keeps the top-level flat fields (`imageSrc`, `contentKind`, etc.) permanently synced to `parts[0]` ("the primary part") — the deliberate, disclosed mitigation for the real fact that `tools/world-builder/` (v1) and `tools/world-builder-v2/` share the literal same `localStorage` key (`'vihu-world-builder-projects'`): a Project authored in v2 with multiple parts stays fully correct and editable in v1 for its own first part, with `parts[1..4]` simply invisible (never corrupted or lost) to v1's own UI. **Phase 2 — Engine Adapter generalization**: `_findMirroredLayer`'s identity moved from a fixed kind ("slot") to a real `part.id`, so two same-kind parts (e.g. two Image parts) mirror onto two genuinely distinct Scene Layers instead of colliding; an orphan sweep deletes a mirrored Layer whose part was removed; same-kind parts get disambiguated Layer names ("Image", "Image 2") so `builder.js`'s compiled `label` and Object Strip cards never read identically for two different parts; a `_claimUntaggedPartLayer` adopts a pre-existing V3.1-era mirrored Layer in place for `parts[0]` only, so every already-authored Experience (including the real, on-disk Museum Gallery Theme) never visually duplicates or jumps on its first re-sync after this shipped. **Phase 3 — Collection registry fix**: `collectionAssetUsageCount`/`deleteCollectionAsset` now scan `parts[]` instead of the derived top-level fields, so Collection's usage-count/delete-nulls-every-reference guarantee (AV-012) stays correct once an asset can live inside any of up to 5 parts on one Experience, not just one. **Phase 4 — UI redesign**: `_renderExperienceProperties` became a real part-list renderer — each part gets its own bordered card with a disambiguated title, a Remove button, and the identical field UI the single-content-kind model always had; "+ Add a Part" (renamed from the old exclusive content-kind selector) always APPENDS a new part rather than swapping the active one — a real, confirmed staleness-fix ripple this uncovered: several older test scripts assumed clicking a content-kind button SWITCHED the active kind in place, and had to be corrected to seed via `updateExperience({contentKind:X})` directly instead, matching the two real, already-correct producer call sites' own pattern; the cap is enforced at the model layer first (`addExperiencePart` refuses at 5, matching this codebase's established "model-layer cap enforcement, not just a disabled UI button" discipline for e.g. Experience Graduation), with a disclosed inline message once reached. **Phase 5 — Isolated Experience Studio generalization**: the Stage becomes the union bounding box of every populated part's own footprint (byte-identical to before whenever exactly 1 part exists); `_experienceStudioHit`'s hit-testing walks `sections` in REVERSED array order (topmost-drawn-first, since array order is paint order) instead of a fixed kind-name priority list, so two overlapping same-kind parts now correctly resolve to whichever one actually paints on top; drag/resize state moved from `.slot` to `.partId`, writing through the new part-aware `updateExperiencePartProperty` instead of the old single-target `updateExperienceProperty`. **Explicitly out of scope, disclosed rather than silently omitted**: reordering parts (array-append-order only, matching the precedent already set by Collection itself shipping "add new" well before "reorder"); changing an existing part's kind post-creation (remove + re-add instead); Place-hosted multi-part rendering (Place hosting stays Frame-only, an existing, unrelated, already-disclosed gap). Verified via 5 new/updated Playwright suites across all 6 phases — Phase 1 (Collection dual-write + a Museum-Gallery-sourced Project migrating to a correct single-entry `parts` array), Phase 2 (20 assertions: same-kind mirroring, orphan sweep, name disambiguation, a real pre-existing mirrored Layer claimed in place with zero duplication on first re-sync), Phase 3 (11 assertions: usage count correctly reports 2 for two parts sharing one Collection ref, delete nulls both), Phase 4 (33 assertions: 5 mixed/repeated parts authored through the real UI, the 6th genuinely refused at the model layer even bypassing the disabled button, Remove disabled at exactly 1 part, every part's own fields surviving a real page reload with zero cross-contamination), and a new Phase 5 suite (20 assertions, built around monkey-patching the real, already-`window`-exposed `EngineV2Runtime.rectFor`/`.textFootprint` to record real render-call geometry rather than replicating internal coordinate math — two spatially-separated Image parts drag independently with zero cross-target interference; two FULLY OVERLAPPING Image parts correctly move the topmost/later-added one on both a move gesture and a resize-handle gesture, proving the reversed-paint-order hit-test rather than merely "some part moved"; a single-part Experience — the pre-Phase-5 shape every existing theme still has — renders exactly one section and still drags correctly through the exact same generalized code path).
