Full regression across the complete existing suite (`goldenBuild.js` for both World Builder v1 and v2; every Collection Phase 1-6 suite; every rotation suite — image, text, text-rotation-pivot, rotation-honoured-through-real-Publish-export; the real, on-disk Museum Gallery `.vtheme` byte-for-byte pixel-hash regression plus its own Caption drag/resize suites; `scene_dropdown_repro3.js`) all pass completely unchanged throughout every phase. `git diff` confirms root Studio (`js/`, `renderer/`) and `tools/world-builder/` (v1) are byte-identical/untouched throughout — this feature is confined entirely to `tools/world-builder-v2/`.)

- Image-Typed Frame Variations + Place-Hosted Experiences of Any Type (World Builder v2, plus one root-Studio renderer file — implements two independent features, shipped together, from the user's own words: **"i would like to do two things. 1st allow frames to be type of image also. and second yes extend experiences to places."** Begun while investigating a real, user-reported bug: *"check for experiences which get attached to places. they are not rendering in builder."* **Root cause, confirmed by direct code read**: `js/services/experienceSchema.js`'s `EXPERIENCE_TYPES` table declared `renders.place: true` for exactly one type, `"frame"`, and `false` for every other type (`decoration`/`text`/`atmosphere`/`lighting`/`text-style`). Since Universal Experience Authoring (Builder V3.1) permanently retired the Type picker, every Experience an author can create through the ordinary "+ Add Experience" flow is permanently `type:'decoration'` — meaning every Experience a Theme Author could normally create rendered nothing at all when Hosted By a Place, with zero visual signal. `js/projectModel.js`'s `_syncExperienceAttachments`'s Place branch simply returned immediately once this gate failed, with `rendersWhenHosted` confirmed to have exactly one caller in the whole codebase, so widening the table was a complete, self-contained fix. **One earlier claim made while reporting this bug is itself wrong and is corrected here, not silently carried forward**: the one path that DOES set `type:'frame'` (the Place panel's own "+ Add Experience" → "📎 Create & Host" shortcut) was never broken by the Multi-Asset Experience Parts refactor above — re-reading `_mirrorFrame` and the Experience Properties panel's own `if(exp.type==='frame')` block confirmed a `type:'frame'` Experience's Frame fields (Mat Width/Frame Thickness/Border Colour/Wall Tone/Shadow) live directly on `experience.properties`, **outside** the multi-part `parts[]` array entirely, so `_mirrorFrame`'s `Object.assign({}, experience.properties)` still copies them correctly — this path worked throughout and needed no fix. **Feature 2 — Place-hosted Experiences of any type**: `EXPERIENCE_TYPES.renders.place` flips `decoration`/`text` from `false` to `true` — the two types that already render somewhere (Scene/Free hosting) via the Universal Content Layer-mirroring mechanism now also render at a Place via that same mechanism, just anchored differently; `frame` keeps its own separate, unchanged `place:true` path (the Frame-mirror shortcut above); `atmosphere`/`lighting`/`text-style` stay `false` across every hosting axis — a pre-existing, disclosed, zero-adapter reserved vocabulary this feature does not extend. `_syncExperienceAttachments`'s Place branch keeps its existing `type==='frame'` branch completely unchanged and adds an `else` calling `_syncUniversalContent(project, sceneId, experience, 'place', placeId)` — a new, additive 5th argument. Every mirrored part becomes an ordinary Scene Layer tagged `layer.hostPlaceId=placeId` (parallel to the existing `layer.hostedByScene` boolean, holding the target Place's own id instead of a bare flag), seeded `{position:{x:0,y:0},size:{w:1,h:1}}` — inert placeholder values, since the real paint rect is always resolved fresh from the Place's own live geometry at paint time (`rectFor(holder,graph)`), never copied/snapshotted, so the content correctly follows its Place through a later move/resize with zero staleness. `builder.js`'s `convergeSceneLayer` gains a third `target` branch, `layer.hostPlaceId ? 'place' : (existing slide/overlay logic)`, carrying `placeId:layer.hostPlaceId` onto the compiled entry — purely additive; every pre-existing Layer with no `hostPlaceId` compiles exactly as before. `engineRuntime.js`'s `render(ctx,graph)` excludes `hostPlaceId`-tagged entries from its existing `before`/`after` bucketing split entirely and paints each one immediately after its matching Holder inside the `middle` loop instead — giving Builder's own Working View/Runtime Preview correct, live-following-the-Place rendering, verified with a real Place move/resize confirming zero staleness. Root Studio's `renderer/slideRenderer.js` gains a new `_renderPlaceHostedLayers(pack, placeId, placeRect, s)`, called from **both** `_drawPlaceOne` (Place 1) and `_drawPlaceExtra` (Place 2+) — this is the one part of the feature that reaches Publish/Studio at all (Creator Governing Rule #5, Publish Fidelity), and the first time this new `target:'place'` scope reaches every Place on a page, not only Place 1 — the older, legacy `frame`/`holder`/`element` Layer Pack scopes remain Place-1-only, an unrelated, unchanged, disclosed limitation this feature does not lift. **Feature 1 — Image-typed Frame Variations**: a separate, genuinely different system from Experiences — a reusable, named Frame "recipe" (`frames/<id>.json`), never an ordinary content Layer. Two of its enum fields, `fields.background` and `fields.frame`, were silently defaulted by `ProjectModel._ensureFrameFieldDefaults` with **zero authoring UI anywhere** since the field was introduced (Asset Repository Transition sprint) — a real, confirmed gap, not a design choice. This feature gives both real controls on the Frames screen for the first time, and adds a genuine `"image"` option to `background`, backed by a new `fields.frameImage` field — a Collection-sourced picture that fills the Frame's own mat band in place of a flat colour. The picker reuses the exact reuse-or-upload mechanism already shipped for Experience Image/Graphics content (a small, extracted Collection-picker-core helper, since a Frame Variation has no `parts[]` of its own to key a picker off of) — Collection's own registry/dedup/delete machinery (Collection Phase 1-6, above) needed zero changes: `frameImage` is just one more producer of `vihu-asset:`/`data:` refs, exactly like `imageSrc`/`graphicSrc`. Both `engineRuntime.js`'s `_paintHolder` (Builder's own preview) and root Studio's `_drawPictureFrameFill` (the real Reader-facing renderer) gained the identical `background==='image'` draw step, painted at the same point in the concentric wall→border→mat→content fill sequence a flat mat colour would occupy — verified identically correct for both a plainly-authored Frame Variation and an Experience-mirrored one (`type:'frame'` at a Place), confirming the two authoring paths genuinely converge on one `fields` object with zero special-casing needed. The compile step (`builder.js`) gained a new `_externalizeFrameVariationImages` step, resolving a set `frameImage` exactly like every other image-bearing compiled field, reusing Collection's own compile-time dedup — a plain Frame Variation and an Experience-mirrored one sharing the same underlying image bytes converge to exactly one embedded asset, not two. **Scope**: `tools/world-builder/` (v1) is completely untouched by both features — v1 has no Multi-Asset Parts/Universal Content model of its own to extend, confirmed via `goldenBuild.js` passing unchanged; independent Transform positioning for a Place-hosted part within its own Place (always full-bleed-within-the-Place today), reordering multiple Place-hosted Experiences within one Place, and extending the legacy `frame`/`holder`/`element` scopes to Place 2+ are all explicitly out of scope, named rather than silently dropped. Verified via new scratch Playwright suites at every phase (Feature 2 Phase A — compiled-package shape, 14/14; Phase B — Builder's own Working View/Runtime Preview including the real Place move/resize proof, 8/8; Phase C — a real compiled Theme's Place-hosted Experience rendering correctly at both Place 1 and a Place 2+ in root Studio, 10/10; Feature 1 — end-to-end across compile dedup, both authoring paths, Builder's preview, and root Studio's real renderer, 18/18 — the last of these initially failed 2/5 in its Studio-render check for a real, confirmed reason that turned out to be a test bug, not a product bug: neither Place in the test scenario has an actual artwork photo placed, so `_drawArtworkPlaceholder`'s own legitimate "Tap to add your artwork" text — correct, pre-existing, unrelated behaviour — was being sampled at its own exact center point; fixed by sampling a corner instead, confirming the frame-background-image draw code itself was correct all along). Full regression across both `goldenBuild.js` suites (World Builder v1 and v2, both full PASS), `museum_realfile_pixelhash.js` (Museum Gallery's real, on-disk `.vtheme` — SHA-256 `e7b2a905613dbef3d2f9064211103d84762d7039d3bee404df90f4d90899b390`, byte-identical to this project's own recorded history, confirming zero regression for a theme that authors neither feature), `museum_regression.js`, the museumCaption drag/resize suites (`museumcaption_fix_verify.js`/`museumcaption_realdrag_verify.js`), Collection Phase 4's own compile-time-dedup suite (sharing the exact dedup mechanism Feature 1 reuses), and `scene_dropdown_repro3.js` (Experience Host Here/graduation flows, sharing code with Feature 2's own Engine Adapter changes) all pass unchanged. `docs/THEME_PROJECT_SPEC.md` (§6/§7 field tables plus a full sprint-history entry) and `docs/VTHEME_PACKAGE_SPEC.md` (a cross-reference note, since neither feature introduces a new top-level compiled-package key) both updated. No Theme Contract breaking change, no Engine V2 Scene Model redesign, no Creator Governing Rules change — this directly serves Rule #5 (Publish Fidelity); confined to `tools/world-builder-v2/js/{projectModel,worldBuilderApp,services/{builder,engineRuntime,experienceSchema}}.js` and `renderer/slideRenderer.js`.)

- Manage Frames Inline + Frame Background Image Rotation (World Builder v2, plus one root-Studio renderer file — two concrete fixes shipped together, both from the same user report: **"i think the manage frame opens up as seperate window and we are not able to see how it is affecting the frame, so we will need to open manage frames as part of same screen. also when i choose image option spin/rotate is missing."** **Fix A — Manage Frames un-modaled**: `_renderFramesPanel()` — reached only via a Place's Frame picker's "🖌️ Manage Frames →" bridge button, never Global Navigation — was routed through `_renderContextPanel()`'s `isModal = MODAL_NAVS.has(currentNav)` check, which for `currentNav==='frames'` was `true`, so its own DOM mounted inside the full-screen `#wb-modal` overlay, dimming/hiding Working View and Runtime Preview behind it — exactly the reported symptom, since a Theme Author changing a Frame's fields had no live picture of the effect until closing the modal. `MODAL_NAVS` no longer includes `'frames'`, so `_renderContextPanel()` now mounts the Frames screen into the permanent `#wb-context-panel` column instead, beside the still-live Working View/Runtime Preview specimen — `WORKING_VIEW_PASSTHROUGH_NAVS` (the separate set controlling whether Working View keeps showing a live specimen for a given nav, independent of modal-ness) already included `'frames'` and was left completely unchanged, since it already produced the correct "keep showing the Frame specimen" behaviour regardless of which set governs mounting location. `_renderFramesPanel()` itself needed zero changes — it was already mount-agnostic, writing only to a shared `contextPanel` DOM reference resolved by the caller. **Fix B — Rotation for Background=Image**: once a Frame Variation's `background` field is set to `'image'` (the compiled-package field this same feature area's own earlier "Image-Typed Frame Variations" sprint added), there was no way to spin the uploaded background picture — a genuine capability gap, not a bug in an existing control. Added `fields.frameImageRotation` (degrees, clockwise, defaults to `0` via `ProjectModel._ensureFrameFieldDefaults`, purely additive — every Frame authored before this feature existed renders byte-identically) and a real 0-359° Rotation slider on the Frames screen's Image-background section, right after the existing Collection-picker image control. Both engines that draw a Frame's background image gained the identical rotate-around-the-mat-rect's-own-centre transform (`ctx.translate(cx,cy); ctx.rotate(deg*Math.PI/180); ctx.translate(-cx,-cy);`), mirroring the exact, already-established convention this feature area's own Image/Graphics/Text Experience-content rotation already uses (`engineRuntime.js`'s `_paintLayer`) — `engineRuntime.js`'s `_paintHolder` (Builder's own Working View/Runtime Preview) rotates around the mat band's own rect; root Studio's `renderer/slideRenderer.js`'s `_drawPictureFrameFill` (the real Reader-facing renderer, Creator Governing Rule #5, Publish Fidelity) rotates around the frame-fill rect the identical way, confirmed via direct code read of `_resolveArtworkFields`'s wholesale `Object.assign(merged, variation.fields)` that the new field automatically flows through to `art`/`border._artwork` with zero additional wiring needed there — only the two actual draw functions needed the new transform. The compile step (`builder.js`'s `_externalizeFrameVariationImages`) needed zero changes — it only ever rewrites `fields.frameImage` specifically, and every other `fields` key (including the new `frameImageRotation`) rides through the compile step unfiltered since nothing whitelists individual keys. Verified via a new 16-assertion Playwright suite driving the real UI end to end (Create New World → Blank template → add a Scene → the "Place" activity tab → "Add a Place" → the real "Manage Frames" bridge button): confirms Fix A directly — `#wb-modal` stays hidden, the Frame fields render inside `#wb-context-panel` (never `#wb-modal-body`), and a real, visible Working View canvas remains present throughout; confirms Fix B's model layer — the Rotation slider appears only once Background is set to `'image'`, defaults to `0`, and a real slider drag persists `135` into the model; and, decisively, confirms rotation is genuinely applied (not a no-op) in BOTH engines via a magenta-left/cyan-right synthetic test image sampled at the same fixed point in the Frame's own mat "ring" (the band between the border's own inset and the mat's own further inset, where the background image is visibly NOT yet occluded by the later-drawn, opaque content-rect fill covering the interior — a real test-authoring bug in an earlier draft of this same script had sampled a point deep inside that occluded content area instead, which returned the content rect's own flat `#F5F2EA`/cream fallback colour with zero trace of the image at ANY rotation, a false failure traced to the sample point's own placement, not the rendering code, before being corrected) — the sampled pixel reads pure magenta at `frameImageRotation:0` and pure cyan at the SAME pixel coordinate once `frameImageRotation:180`, in both `EngineV2Runtime.render()` (Builder) and `SlideRenderer.render()` (root Studio, driven with a synthetic compiled theme carrying the same Frame Variation fields), an unambiguous, decisive proof the image is genuinely rotating around the rect's own centre in both renderers identically. Full regression: both `goldenBuild.js` suites (World Builder v1 and v2, 30/30 each), `feature1_frameimage_verify.js` (18/18, the earlier Image-Typed Frame Variations sprint's own regression suite, confirming zero interference from adding the new rotation field alongside it), the full Feature 2 Place-hosted-Experience suite (Phase A 14/14, Phase B 8/8, Phase C 10/10), and the Guardrails runtime-verify suite (10/10, confirming moveable/editable permissions on Place-hosted objects are unaffected) all pass unchanged. No Theme Contract/Engine V2 Scene Model/Creator Governing Rules change — Fix B directly serves Rule #5 (Publish Fidelity); confined to `tools/world-builder-v2/js/worldBuilderApp.js`, `tools/world-builder-v2/js/projectModel.js`, `tools/world-builder-v2/js/services/engineRuntime.js`, and `renderer/slideRenderer.js`.)

- Simplify Place & Frame Authoring (World Builder v2 only — implements the user's own governing request, unambiguous once scoped: *"designing a place/frame is really complicated. we need to simplify it."* → *"the entire concept of place and frame. we need to simplify it."* → asked "style presets + collapse advanced" vs. "reorganize/relabel" vs. both, the answer was **"Both."** Mid-implementation the user interrupted with a `"wait"` and then sent four further, more concrete requirements in one message, all delivered here: *"1st the editing view needs to show what we are editing... second where ever we are using colors an option of transparent color needs to be there. a place with no customization... it should be exactly same [as transparent]... also the ordering of manage frames section. it is showing all frames at the same time, making the look really confusing."* Two Explore agents plus a Plan agent, independently re-verified against the live code before finalizing, surfaced the actual shape of the complexity: `_renderFramesPanel` exposed 11 raw, jargon-named fields (`'Wall Tone (Background)'`, `'Padding (Mat Width)'`, `'Thickness (Frame Thickness)'`) with no "just pick a good look" path at all, several of which (`background`/`frame`/`paper`) had been silently defaulted since the Asset Repository Transition sprint with zero authoring UI ever built; `Corner Radius`/`Inset` were two more raw controls with no clear purpose (`Inset` easily confused with the sibling `Wall Margin`/`defaultMargin`, both feeding the same wall-band inset math); there was no way to set a custom solid mat colour at all; and — the fidelity gap that would have undermined the whole simplification — a Frame's `background`/`frame` (ornament) choice was read by root Studio's real Reader-facing renderer but **read nowhere in Builder's own preview** (`engineRuntime.js`'s `_paintHolder` hardcoded the mat fill to a flat `'#F5F2EA'` regardless of `background`, and never touched corner radius/ornament cues from `frame` at all), so a Theme Author picking "Wood" or a custom colour would see zero visible change while designing, only discovering it worked once Published. **A gallery of ready-made looks**: new `tools/world-builder-v2/js/services/framePresets.js` (`window.FramePresets.CATALOG`, 10 entries — Classic White/Warm Ivory/Natural Linen/Dark Gallery/Floating Frame/Black Matte/Gold Ornate/Snapshot Corkboard/Polaroid Snap/Taped Sketch — the first 7's `matWidth`/`frameThickness`/`borderColor`/`wallTone`/`shadow` values transcribed verbatim from the real, already-authored `official-worlds/MuseumGallery/frames/*.json` files, with `background`/`frame`/`paper` newly invented for each since Museum Gallery predates any UI for them; the 3 new presets round out coverage of every remaining enum value at least once) — a new `_renderFrameStyleGallery(project)`, rendered at the top of the Frames screen, reuses the existing `_frameOptionCard` swatch component verbatim; clicking a card mints a brand-new Frame (never reuses/dedupes), applies every `preset.fields` value, sets a uniquified name via a new `ProjectModel._uniqueFrameName(project,baseName)` (append `' 2'`/`' 3'`… until no existing Frame shares that exact name — neither `addFrame` nor `duplicateFrame` had ever uniquified *names*, only ids), and lands the author directly on that Frame's own field editor, already good-looking, ready to fine-tune. **Fewer, plainer-named knobs**: the field editor is reorganized and relabeled — Frame Name | Wall Colour (was "Wall Tone (Background)"), Mat Surface (was "Background," gains a genuine new `'color'`/"Solid Colour" enum option alongside the existing `'image'`) | Frame Style (was "Frame"), a conditional Solid Colour swatch (only when Mat Surface='color') or Background-Image picker+Rotation (only when Mat Surface='image', reusing the exact `_renderCollectionPickerCore` helper — newly extracted out of the Experience Image/Graphics content picker so a Frame Variation, which has no `parts[]` of its own, can reuse the identical reuse-or-upload mechanism with zero duplication), Border Color (now a lone field, Corner Radius's own control removed outright), Shadow | Paper Texture — a brand-new select for the long-silently-defaulted `paper` field (replaces the old Shadow|Inset row; Inset's control is removed, the field itself untouched in the data model/rendering, only its confusing UI is gone), Mat Width | Wall Margin (was "Padding (Mat Width)"/"Default Margin"), Border Thickness (was "Thickness (Frame Thickness)"), Description. **A real "pick any colour" mat option, plus Transparent everywhere colour is used**: `_ensureFrameFieldDefaults` (`projectModel.js`) gains `matColor` (a reasonable default burgundy) and three new booleans — `wallToneTransparent`/`borderColorTransparent`/`matColorTransparent` — mirroring the exact Colour-Experience-content convention already shipped (Builder V3.1's `colorValue`/`colorOpacity`/`colorTransparent`) rather than overloading the colour string itself with a magic "transparent" value; a new shared `_colorInputWithTransparent(value,transparentChecked,onColorChange,onTransparentChange)` renders a colour swatch plus an always-visible "Transparent" checkbox beside Wall Colour, Solid Colour, and Border Color alike. **"A Place with no customization should be exactly the same as transparent"**: a genuinely new `_defaultFrameFields()` (used only by `addFrame` — the Frame Style Gallery immediately overwrites these with a real preset's own values, so this baseline is only ever seen by a brand-new "+ Create Frame") sets every value EXPLICITLY (`background:'transparent'`, `frame:'none'`, `matWidth:0`, `frameThickness:0`, `defaultMargin:0`, `wallToneTransparent:true`, `borderColorTransparent:true`, `matColorTransparent:true`, `shadow:'none'`) rather than leaving anything `undefined` — deliberately so `_ensureFrameFieldDefaults`'s own backward-compat reconciliation (reserved for a Frame authored before one of these fields existed, which always resolves to a concrete, visible look) never overwrites this transparent baseline the first time the new Frame is read; a genuinely uncustomized Place now renders with zero visible wall/border/mat/shadow, identical to a Place with no Frame at all. **"The ordering of manage frames... showing all frames at the same time"**: the saved-Frames list is now collapsed behind a plain `<details class="wb-frames-list-details">` ("Your Frames (N)"), open by default only while there's nothing yet to be confusing about (0-1 Frames); an already-crowded World opens it back up with one click instead of every Frame always sitting in full view. **"The editing view needs to show what we are editing... it seems to be stuck on background color"** (Working View fidelity) plus the Builder-preview fidelity gap named above are closed together in `engineRuntime.js`'s `_paintHolder`: a new `MAT_MATERIAL_FILL` table mirrors root Studio's real `ARTWORK_BACKGROUND_FILL` exactly (white/cream/kraft-paper/watercolor-paper/notebook-paper/black/bulletin-board), so `background`'s chosen value now genuinely renders distinctly in Builder's own preview — `background==='color'` uses `matColor` (or is fully skipped when `matColorTransparent`), `background==='transparent'` skips the mat fill entirely (the mat's rect stays unfilled, still available for the `'image'` branch beneath it), any other recognized value uses its `MAT_MATERIAL_FILL` entry, and only a genuinely unset/unrecognized value falls back to the original, narrower `'#F5F2EA'` fallback (never reachable once `_ensureFrameFieldDefaults` has run, which it always has by the time `_paintHolder` sees a Frame in production, since the real resolver `_holderFrameFields(frameId)` always routes through `ProjectModel.findFrame()` first). A new `FRAME_ORNAMENT_PRESET` table mirrors root Studio's `ARTWORK_FRAME_PRESET`'s own `cornerRadius` values (`{none:0,'white-mat':0,floating:8,wood:6,polaroid:0,tape:0,'bulletin-board':0}`) — **the one disclosed, intentional visual-change consequence of this sprint**: corner radius is now always DERIVED from the Frame Style (`fields.frame`) choice instead of read from the now-removed raw `cornerRadius` control, so any already-authored Frame that had a manually-set nonzero `cornerRadius` will render with its ornament-derived radius going forward instead. A new, lightweight `_paintFrameOrnament(ctx,rect,insets,fields,matRect,matIsTransparent)` adds one small distinguishing visual cue per ornament value beyond corner radius alone (`wood` → 3 thin darker grain-lines across the border band; `polaroid` → a single caption-baseline line in the lower mat band; `tape` → two semi-transparent tan corner rectangles; `bulletin-board`, triggered on either `fields.frame` or `fields.background` matching, since Studio's own pin-drawing is keyed off `background` — 4 small dark corner "pin" dots; `none`/`white-mat` → no extra draw, correctly matching Studio's own identical visual parity there) — purely additive decoration, never changes geometry. Deliberately NOT added: any `fields.paper` rendering in `engineRuntime.js` (Studio's own `_drawArtworkPaper` uses real fixed-coordinate pattern-drawing code; the new Paper Texture control still persists and renders correctly in real Studio Publish, it simply shows no distinguishing effect in Builder's own simplified preview yet — a disclosed boundary, not an oversight). **De-emphasizing Experience-as-Frame**: `_renderHolderPanel`'s one Frame-related call site to `_renderContextualExperienceActions` (the full Nurturing/Personal/Public/Hosted-By/Usage/Graduate/Reuse-Existing vocabulary — a second, parallel authoring path to the exact result the plain Frame picker right above it already gives 95% of authors) is wrapped in a `<details class="wb-state-intro">`, reusing the swap-and-restore `contextPanel` idiom this file already established for exactly this purpose — collapsed by default, its summary reading `'🧵 Reuse this Frame as an Experience (Advanced)'` when nothing is attached or `'🧵 This Frame is an Experience: <name>'` once one is. **A real bug found and fixed while building this, not merely a test artifact**: the `<details>`'s own `open` computation initially considered only whether a Frame Experience was already attached — but clicking "➕ Add Experience" sets the shared, module-level `contextualQuickCreateOpen` flag and triggers a FULL `_renderContextPanel()` re-render (not a scoped one), rebuilding this `<details>` fresh with no attached Experience yet and silently re-collapsing around the very quick-create form the click had just opened — a genuine UX bug any real Theme Author using this flow would have hit, not just a test-authoring artifact; fixed by widening `details.open` to `!!attachedExperience || contextualQuickCreateOpen || contextualReuseOpen`. Explicitly out of scope, disclosed: `tools/world-builder/` (v1) and `renderer/slideRenderer.js` (root Studio) are both completely untouched — every fidelity fix is confined to `engineRuntime.js`, Builder's own preview engine; the two Decoration call sites of `_renderContextualExperienceActions` are untouched, only the Place/Frame call site is wrapped; no dedup/reuse-by-name for gallery presets, every click mints a new record; no Theme Contract/compiled-package/schema change — `matColor` rides through `builder.js`'s existing wholesale per-Frame-file compile step unfiltered, exactly like `frameImageRotation` did before it. Verified via a comprehensive 57-assertion Playwright suite (`verify_simplify_place_frame.js`) covering: Gallery creation (every `preset.fields` key matching exactly, a uniquified name, correct field-editor selection); the relabeled text confirmed present and the old labels/Corner-Radius/Inset controls confirmed absent; Solid Colour revealing/persisting correctly on `background==='color'`, Paper Texture persisting; the Experience-as-Frame `<details>` closed-by-default/"(Advanced)"-copy with nothing attached, open with the attached Experience's real name once one is hosted (this is the exact assertion that caught the re-collapse bug above); Builder-preview mat-fill fidelity across 6 distinct `background` values including `'color'`+`matColor` and `'transparent'` (pairwise-distinct sampled pixel colours matching `MAT_MATERIAL_FILL`/`matColor`/no-fill, never the old universal `#F5F2EA`); frame-style/ornament fidelity — confirmed via direct hand arithmetic on `_band()`'s own inset-compositing math (not assumed) that with `defaultMargin`/`inset` both 0, the wall band and border band draw at the identical inset and the border band (drawn second) fully overpaints the wall band, so a `frame:'none'` sharp corner correctly shows `borderColor`, not `wallTone` — genuinely rounded-off corners for `floating`/`wood` show the canvas's own `#F4F1EC` backdrop instead, and the wood grain-line overlay's own subtle-but-real ~9-unit-per-channel difference (hand-computed: `rgba(60,35,15,0.35)` composited over a flat border colour) is detected with a tightened, deliberately-proportioned tolerance rather than a loose one that would wrongly call it "the same"; and backward compatibility — a real legacy-shaped Frame (no `background`/`frame`/`paper` authored, fed through the actual `window.ProjectModel.findFrame()` reconciliation path rather than a hand-bypassed fixture, the one methodology correction this verification needed — an earlier draft handed a raw, unreconciled fields object directly to `resolveFrame`, entirely bypassing the real production code path and producing a methodologically-wrong failure against the OLD universal fallback) now correctly resolves to a true white mat + sharp zero-radius corners, Builder's preview becoming *more* accurate to what Studio already rendered, not diverging. A second, pre-existing regression suite (`feature1_frameimage_verify.js`, from the earlier Image-Typed Frame Variations sprint) needed one genuine correction, not a weakening: its own "un-imaged Frame" fixture explicitly authors `background:'white'`, and its hardcoded assertion — written before `MAT_MATERIAL_FILL` existed — still expected the OLD universal `#F5F2EA` fallback; corrected to expect real white (`#ffffff`, matching `MAT_MATERIAL_FILL.white`), with the disclosure that this is the deliberate, intended consequence of this sprint's own fidelity fix, not a regression — now passing 18/18. Full regression: both `goldenBuild.js` suites (World Builder v1 and v2, PASS unchanged, confirming zero Theme Contract/schema/compile-pipeline impact); `museum_realfile_pixelhash.js` (the real, on-disk `themes/MuseumGallery.vtheme`, rendered through root Studio's own Reader-facing pipeline and SHA-256-hashed — `e7b2a905613dbef3d2f9064211103d84762d7039d3bee404df90f4d90899b390`, byte-identical to this project's own recorded history, confirming root Studio is completely unaffected, exactly as scoped); `manageframes_inline_rotation_verify2.js` (16/16, the Manage-Frames-inline + rotation sprint's own regression, confirming the rotation transform and the mat-fill fidelity fix compose correctly with zero interference); `place_guardrails_runtime_verify.js` (10/10, Place/Decoration guardrail permission checks unaffected); `scene_dropdown_repro3.js` (14/14, Experience Host Here dropdown/graduation flows unaffected). No Theme Contract/Engine V2 Scene Model/Creator Governing Rules change; confined to `tools/world-builder-v2/js/projectModel.js`, `tools/world-builder-v2/js/worldBuilderApp.js`, `tools/world-builder-v2/js/services/engineRuntime.js`, `tools/world-builder-v2/css/world-builder.css`, and a new `tools/world-builder-v2/js/services/framePresets.js`.)

- Publish Quality — Genuine High-Resolution Exports (root Studio only — the user's own single, deliberately under-specified request: **"we need to work on publish quality. it can be high resolution."** No destination or exact degree was named; a clarifying `AskUserQuestion` ("Export scope," offering Story Carousel 2x / Print-ready PDF true 300 DPI / Digital PDF left unchanged as the recommended defaults) went unanswered, so — per this session's own standing instruction to proceed autonomously on an unanswered question rather than stall — I shipped exactly those recommended defaults, disclosed here rather than silently assumed, for the user to confirm or redirect. **Root cause, confirmed by direct code read**: `js/storyDestinations.js`'s shared `_renderSlideInto(canvas, slide, idx, total, opts)` — used by both the Story Book PDF and Story Carousel destinations — unconditionally called `SlideRenderer.init(mid, {dpr:1, adaptiveViewport:true})` regardless of how much larger the destination canvas actually was, meaning the old "Print-ready PDF" (nominally 216 DPI, 1620×2025) was never a genuinely sharper render — it was always only a 1080×1350-quality image stretched up via `_fitCompositeInto`'s own smoothing, no crisper than the Digital PDF underneath it. `SlideRenderer.init`'s `dpr` option already exists specifically to produce a genuinely higher-density NATIVE render (the canvas backing-store multiplies while `x.setTransform(_dpr,0,0,_dpr,0,0)` keeps every draw call in the same logical coordinate space) — the fix was threading a real `scale` value into it, not inventing new rendering machinery. **Fix**: `_renderSlideInto` gained an `opts.scale` parameter (default `1`, so every unspecified caller is byte-for-byte unaffected) passed straight through as `SlideRenderer.init`'s `dpr`; `BOOK_FORMATS.print` gained a `renderScale` field and its dimensions were corrected to genuinely reflect true 300 DPI (2250×2813, replacing the old, misleadingly-labeled-216-DPI 1620×2025), with `BOOK.renderPage` reading `ctx.format.renderScale` and passing it through; `CAROUSEL_RENDER_SCALE=2` was introduced and `CAROUSEL_FORMATS`' Portrait/Square dimensions doubled (2160×2700 / 2160×2160, up from 1080×1350 / 1080×1080), with `CAROUSEL.createCanvas`/`.renderPage` both using the new scale. Story Book's Digital PDF format is deliberately left completely untouched (144 DPI, scale 1) — already screen-optimized, per the unanswered question's own "Recommended" framing. **Verified via a decisive, byte-level Playwright test** (`verify_publish_quality.js`, scratch-only) driving the REAL Publish Studio UI through all 4 format combinations and decoding the actual downloaded file's own metadata directly — a PDF's `/Width N /Height N` dictionary token (the exact literal string `js/pdfWriter.js` emits before any binary JPEG stream) and a PNG's IHDR chunk (byte-parsed: signature + big-endian width/height) — rather than trusting the UI alone: Digital PDF confirmed unchanged at 1080×1350; Print-ready PDF confirmed genuinely 2250×2813 (a real 152,501-byte file, not a stretched-up smaller render); Carousel Portrait confirmed genuinely 2160×2700; Carousel Square confirmed genuinely 2160×2160 with real, non-blank rendered content (a 1.7MB PNG, far too large to be a flat/near-empty canvas). Since Studio ships with zero built-in themes today (`OFFICIAL_THEMES`/`OFFICIAL_ARTWORK_THEMES` are commented out in `js/themeRegistry.js`, and Supabase is unreachable in this sandbox), the test seeds the real, already-validated `themes/MuseumGallery.vtheme` file directly into the `vihu.themeRegistry.imported.v1` localStorage key and drives through "Showcase My Artwork" — the same, already-proven pattern this session's own `welcome_heading_removed_verify.js` established — since Publish Studio only needs a real slide to exist and is completely theme-agnostic. The public `window.PublishStudio` test-harness API (`open`/`_setStage`/`_publishedBlob`/`_publishedFilename`) let all 4 format combinations be exercised in one continuous session with no reload, `MagicCard.setFlags({awakeningOffered:true})` keeping the Awakening ceremony from interrupting the repeated `_setStage(STAGES.DESTINATION)` calls. Full regression: confirmed via `git diff --stat` that only `js/storyDestinations.js` changed (zero touch to `renderer/slideRenderer.js`/`js/publishStudio.js`); a full scratchpad grep for any other script asserting the old 1080×1350/1620×2025/216-DPI Carousel/Print values found exactly one, `verify_rotation_publish_honored.js` (the Image/Text Rotation Publish Fidelity sprint's own regression suite) — its one hardcoded `canvasW===1080 && canvasH===1350` Carousel-size assertion was the disclosed, intended consequence of this very fix, corrected to `2160×2700` and re-verified 10/10 passing, confirming Rotation-reaching-real-Publish-output is completely unaffected by the resolution change (every substantive bbox-delta/content-presence check in that suite passed both before and after). No Theme Contract/Engine V2 Scene Model/Builder architecture change; `tools/world-builder/` and `tools/world-builder-v2/` are untouched — confined entirely to `js/storyDestinations.js`.)

- Publish Quality Follow-Up — Instagram Carousel/Feed Resolution Bumped Again (root Studio only — a direct, same-day escalation on the fix above: **"the social media export size for insta crousel and feed we need to increase resolution there too."** The prior sprint's own "Story Carousel 2x" default (chosen from an unanswered clarifying question's "Recommended" option) wasn't enough — the user wanted the Instagram Carousel/Feed formats specifically pushed further. Confirmed via `CAROUSEL_FORMATS`' own existing descriptions ("Feed post (HD)"/"Classic feed (HD)") that "insta crousel and feed" refers to exactly the two formats this destination already exposes (Portrait 4:5, Square 1:1) — no separate "Feed" destination exists to build, this is the same `CAROUSEL_RENDER_SCALE` constant the immediately-prior fix introduced. **Fix**: `CAROUSEL_RENDER_SCALE` raised from `2` to `3` — Portrait now genuinely 3240×4050 (was 2160×2700/2x), Square now genuinely 3240×3240 (was 2160×2160/2x) — both real, native higher-density renders via `SlideRenderer.init`'s own `dpr` option (the same mechanism the prior fix already proved out, not new rendering machinery), never a blurred upscale. The format descriptions and every explanatory code comment (including the centre-crop trim math, confirmed scale-invariant at exactly 135 logical px each side regardless of `CAROUSEL_RENDER_SCALE`'s value) were updated to match the new real dimensions. Story Book's Digital PDF (144 DPI) and Print-ready PDF (true 300 DPI, 2250×2813) are both completely untouched — this escalation was scoped specifically to the two named formats, not a blanket re-bump of everything the prior sprint touched. **Verified via the same decisive, byte-level Playwright technique already established**: `verify_publish_quality.js` (extended, 17/17 passing) confirms Carousel Portrait/Square now decode to genuine 3240×4050/3240×3240 PNG IHDR dimensions (parsed directly from the downloaded file's own bytes, not inferred from the UI), while Digital PDF (1080×1350) and Print-ready PDF (2250×2813) are confirmed byte-for-byte unchanged; `verify_rotation_publish_honored.js`'s one dependent hardcoded Carousel-size assertion (`canvasW===2160 && canvasH===2700`, itself the disclosed consequence of the prior sprint's own fix) was updated to `3240×4050` and re-verified 10/10 passing, confirming Image/Text Rotation Publish Fidelity is completely unaffected by the further resolution bump — every substantive bbox-delta/content-presence check in that suite passed both before and after. A repo-wide grep confirmed `CAROUSEL_RENDER_SCALE`/the old `2160`-shaped Carousel dimensions exist nowhere else in the codebase besides this one file and its own two dependent scratch tests. Both `goldenBuild.js` suites (World Builder v1 and v2) pass unchanged, confirming zero Builder-tooling impact — this is root Studio's Publish pipeline only. No Theme Contract/Engine V2 Scene Model/Builder architecture change; `tools/world-builder/` and `tools/world-builder-v2/` are untouched — confined entirely to `js/storyDestinations.js`.)

- Publish Quality — Digital PDF Bumped Too (root Studio only — closes the one format the original Publish Quality pass deliberately left untouched. Right after the Carousel/Feed 3x follow-up shipped, the user repeated the exact original request verbatim: **"we need to work on publish quality. it can be high resolution."** Rather than blindly re-implement already-completed work, I gave a status summary (Digital PDF unchanged/1080×1350; Print-ready PDF true 300 DPI/2250×2813; Carousel 3x/3240×4050 & 3240×3240) and used `AskUserQuestion` to check what, if anything, was still wanted. The user's answer: **"Digital PDF too"** — with the option's own description framing the ask: "Currently deliberately left at 1080×1350/144 DPI (screen-optimized) — bump it up as well, e.g. matching Print-ready's 300 DPI or a middle ground." **Decision made and disclosed, not silently assumed**: rather than match Print-ready's 300 DPI outright, Digital PDF is bumped to a genuine, deliberate **216 DPI middle ground** — matching 300 DPI exactly would have collapsed the two formats down to nearly the same resolution, leaving only a JPEG-quality difference (0.92 vs. 0.95) between "Small file · great on screen" and "true print quality," erasing the real reason the two formats exist side by side. 216 DPI (`renderScale:216/144=1.5`) is a clean 1.5x step up from the original 144 DPI, producing a genuinely sharper `1620×2025` native render (via `SlideRenderer.init`'s own `dpr` mechanism, exactly the same real-density-not-upscale technique both prior Publish Quality passes already proved out — no new rendering machinery) while staying meaningfully smaller/lighter than Print-ready's true 300 DPI. **A small historical-comment disambiguation, disclosed rather than left confusing**: `1620×2025` happens to be the exact pixel count the OLD, since-corrected "Print-ready PDF" bug used to mislabel as 216 DPI (see the original Publish Quality entry above) — purely a coincidence of the math (144×1.5=216, and 216 DPI at this page's own fixed 540×675pt size always works out to 1620×2025 regardless of which format asks for it), not a reuse of the old bug's numbers on purpose; both of `js/storyDestinations.js`'s own explanatory comment blocks (`BOOK_FORMATS`' header comment and `_renderSlideInto`'s own historical-bug note) were updated to name this explicitly, so a future reader never mistakes the coincidence for a leftover bug. **Fix**: `BOOK_FORMATS[0]` (`id:'digital'`) — `renderScale:216/144`, `renderW:1620`, `renderH:2025`, description updated to `'216 DPI · sharp on screen, smaller file'` (mirroring the print format's own `'300 DPI · true print quality'` descriptive convention). Print-ready PDF and both Carousel formats are completely untouched — this ships as a single-format, single-line-of-reasoning change. **Verified via the same decisive, byte-level Playwright technique already established across both prior passes**: `verify_publish_quality.js` (updated, 18/18 passing) confirms Digital PDF now decodes to a genuine `1620×2025` PDF `/Width`/`/Height` token pair (parsed directly from the downloaded file's own raw bytes, not inferred from the UI), while Print-ready PDF (`2250×2813`) and both Carousel formats (`3240×4050`/`3240×3240`) are confirmed byte-for-byte unchanged; `verify_rotation_publish_honored.js` was checked and confirmed to assert nothing about Digital PDF's own dimensions at all (it exercises Carousel Portrait exclusively), so it needed no changes and re-verified 10/10 passing unchanged, confirming Image/Text Rotation Publish Fidelity is completely unaffected. Both `goldenBuild.js` suites (World Builder v1 and v2) pass unchanged, confirming zero Builder-tooling impact — this is root Studio's Publish pipeline only. No Theme Contract/Engine V2 Scene Model/Builder architecture change; `tools/world-builder/` and `tools/world-builder-v2/` are untouched — confined entirely to `js/storyDestinations.js`.)

- Coloring Kit — Crayon, Pastel, and Brush Media for Studio's Doodle Tool (root Studio only — the user's own request, delivered with no further elaboration: **"for coloring can we have wax colors , pastel colors and brush and crayons in studio."** Interpreted, disclosed rather than silently guessed and never re-confirmed: "wax colors" and "crayons" are treated as one and the same medium (crayons are wax-based), giving exactly 3 distinct drawing media — Crayon, Pastel, Brush — each with its own curated 8-colour palette and its own distinct stroke-rendering algorithm, replacing Studio's Doodle tool's single flat pen-colour/thickness picker. **Data model**: every stroke in `st.strokes` (`js/sceneEngine.js`'s `addSticker`/`updateSticker`, unchanged) now optionally carries `medium: undefined | 'crayon' | 'pastel' | 'brush'` — absent (every stroke drawn before this feature shipped) always renders through the exact original, byte-identical single-pass algorithm; a stroke drawn after this feature ships always carries a real medium string. **Three genuinely distinct rendering algorithms**, hand-mirrored between the live editing pad (`js/cardDesigner.js`'s `_drawDoodleStrokeOnCtx`) and the real Reader-facing/Publish-facing renderer (`renderer/slideRenderer.js`'s own separately-maintained copy of the identical function) — matching this codebase's own established shape-pad/real-renderer duplication discipline, since the two files share no common drawing module: **Crayon** is three offset, partially-transparent passes (a solid core plus two faint diagonal ghost strokes at ±1px) simulating a soft, textured wax-on-paper look; **Pastel** is a single stroke with `shadowBlur`/`shadowColor` glow at reduced opacity, simulating a soft, chalky, feathered edge; **Brush** varies its own `lineWidth` continuously along the stroke's own point sequence via a new `_doodleBrushTaper(t)` easing function (a narrow 0.35× width for the first/last 15% of the stroke, full width in the middle), drawn as many short per-segment `moveTo`/`lineTo` calls rather than one path, simulating a real brush's natural taper at the start and end of a stroke. **UI**: the Doodle Refine panel's pen-tools row gains a new medium-switcher row above it — three pill buttons (🖍️ Crayon / 🎨 Pastel / 🖌️ Brush, Crayon selected by default) built from a new `DOODLE_MEDIA` table pairing each medium with its own `DOODLE_PALETTE`/`DOODLE_PASTEL_PALETTE`/`DOODLE_BRUSH_PALETTE` (8 swatches each, all distinct hex values, no colour shared across palettes); switching medium rebuilds the swatch row to that medium's own palette via a new `_rebuildDoodleSwatches()` and resets the active pen colour to the new palette's own first swatch, so a Story Author is never left with a stale colour that doesn't belong to the medium they just picked. Each swatch's own original hex string is stored on a `data-color` attribute (rather than relying on a `.style.background` read-back, which browsers can re-serialize into `rgb(...)` form, breaking exact-string identity checks) for reliable active-state syncing. New `.doodle-media-row`/`.doodle-media-btn`/`.doodle-media-icon`/`.doodle-media-label` CSS — the pill buttons needed the same `!important`+explicit-width/height+`flex-shrink:0` override this codebase has fixed repeatedly for a plain `<button>` caught by the global `button{width:100%;height:var(--button-height)}` cascade rule (Object Strip cards, the Publish Studio close button, Doodle's own pre-existing pen swatches/thickness buttons all needed this fix historically, now joined by the new medium buttons). Verified via a new 22-assertion Playwright suite (scratch-only) split into two parts, both catching real test-authoring bugs before landing on a decisive proof — disclosed here since neither was an app bug: Part A (`SlideRenderer.drawObjectThumbnail`, the real exported render-path entry point, driven directly with synthetic stroke data) initially sampled a 2-point stroke's own centreline to check for brush taper — the wrong test, since a stroke's centreline is fully painted by ANY nonzero line width regardless of taper, and a 2-point stroke collapses to one constant-width segment with no taper index granularity at all; corrected to a 40-point stroke (matching what a real mouse drag actually produces) sampled 8px off the centreline near the stroke's own start, where a genuinely tapered ~3.5px-half-width brush stroke reads as background while a constant 10px-half-width legacy stroke still reads as fully painted — a decisive, geometry-correct proof of real width modulation, confirmed with a paired "legacy stays full-width at the same point" control assertion. Part B (the real UI, Story-role boot through Studio's Creation Flow → Personalize → Add Something → Doodle) initially timed out with `#previewCanvas` never becoming visible, since Studio ships with zero built-in themes and the test picked "Story" with no World card ever available to select; fixed by seeding the real, already-validated `themes/MuseumGallery.vtheme` package into `localStorage`'s `vihu.themeRegistry.imported.v1` key and picking "Artwork" instead — the exact, already-established scratch-test pattern this session's own `bold_toggle_verify.js` proved out. Once corrected: confirms exactly 3 medium buttons in Crayon/Pastel/Brush order, Crayon selected by default with its own 8-swatch palette starting at `#E63946`, switching to Pastel rebuilds the swatch row to its own distinct palette (`#F6C6D2`) and resets the active colour to it, switching to Brush does the same (`#B23A48`), and three real mouse-driven strokes drawn while Pastel/Brush/Crayon were each successively active commit to the live model (`window.PageRuntime.getActivePage()`) with exactly those three medium strings in draw order — end-to-end proof the medium selected at draw time is what actually persists. Full regression across `sticker_text_quickedit_verify.js` (32/32, the closest existing suite sharing render-tree/sticker/quick-edit machinery), `verify_text_rotation.js` (22/22), `verify_text_rotation_pivot.js` (5/5), `verify_text_align_fidelity_fix.js` (8/8), `verify_text_newline_fix.js` (7/7), and `verify_rotation_publish_honored.js` (10/10) — all exercising `renderer/slideRenderer.js`'s broader render pipeline, since the new `_drawDoodleStrokeOnCtx`/`_doodleBrushTaper` functions sit in the same file — all pass unchanged, plus both `goldenBuild.js` suites (World Builder v1 and v2), confirming zero impact on either Builder-tooling surface, both untouched by this change. No Theme Contract/Engine V2 Scene Model/Builder/Creator Governing Rules change; confined to `js/cardDesigner.js`, `renderer/slideRenderer.js`, and `css/style.css`.)

- Studio Frame Personalization — a Story Author's Own Picture as a Place's Frame (root Studio only — the user's own single governing request: **"also studio is not providing options to personalize frames. allow studio to put image as frame. and also change the size and shape of place if story author has allowed it."** This entry covers the first half; the second half (Place resize + shape, gated on Story-Author permission) is a genuinely separate, not-yet-started task. **Investigation first**: Studio already has two parallel, mutually-exclusive frame-styling systems in `renderer/slideRenderer.js` — "Picture Border"/"Frame Style" (`slide.metadata.cardOverrides.border`, Place 1, or `slide.metadata.placeContent[placeId].cardOverrides.border` for extra Places; a flat `{design,padding,fill,cornerRadius,lineEnabled,lineWidth,lineColor,shadowEnabled,shadowIntensity}` shape, managed via `_ensureBorder`/`_readBorder`/`_pruneBorder`/`_commitBorder`/`_resetBorder` in `js/cardDesigner.js`) and the separate Sprint 9.x Artwork Theme system (`cardOverrides.artwork.frameVariation`, referencing a Theme-Author-authored `theme.frameVariations[]` entry — already supports `background:'image'`+`frameImage` from an earlier World Builder feature, "Image-Typed Frame Variations"). **`_resolveBorder(s,placeId)`'s precedence is not layered — `cardOverrides.border`, if set at all, wins outright over any Artwork chrome resolution** — so the Picture Border system, not the Artwork Theme system, is the one that must gain a Story-Author-facing image option; a Theme Author's own Frame Variation stays completely untouched by this feature. **Fix**: `_resolveBorder`'s two branches (the per-Place shape and the global/Place-1 shape) both gained `image:pb.image||null` and `imageRotation:(typeof pb.imageRotation==='number')?pb.imageRotation:0` — absent for every existing project (byte-for-byte unaffected). `_drawPictureFrameFill(rect,border,theme,s)` gained an optional trailing `s` (the slide, needed for `AssetStore`'s cross-owner `recallOwnerId` fallback, matching the exact resolution a Story-Author-replaced World-owned object's own image override already uses) and a new `hasBorderImageBg` branch, resolved via `_ensureDecorationImage(border.image,s&&s.recallOwnerId)` — deliberately `_ensureDecorationImage` (the Draft Asset Architecture `vihu-asset:`/`data:` resolution path with `crossOrigin='anonymous'` already set, from an earlier session's own cross-origin-canvas-tainting fix), never `ThemeRegistry.resolveAssetRef` (reserved for Theme-authored assets — a Story Author's own upload isn't one). Cover-fit (crop to fill, matching the existing `background:'image'` Artwork-Theme convention right above it in the same function) plus an optional rotation, applied via a translate-rotate-translate transform anchored at the frame rect's own centre, clipped to the frame's own shape path (`_frameFillPath`) before drawing. Confirmed mutually exclusive with the pre-existing Feature-1 `border._artwork` image case by construction — `border._artwork` is only ever stashed by `_artworkBorder()`, a code path `_resolveBorder` never reaches once `cardOverrides.border` is set at all. `_drawPictureFrameFill`'s 4 real call sites (`_drawPlaceExtra`, the Place-1/no-Layout fallback, the Scene-converged Place-1 path, `_renderPlace`'s extra-Place loop) were all updated to pass `s` through; the one swatch-preview call site (`drawFrameSwatch`) deliberately keeps its existing no-`s` call, since it has no real slide in scope and never carries a Picture-Border image anyway. **Authoring UI** (`js/cardDesigner.js`): a new `_storeUploadedAsset(dataURL,onFile)` — the established per-module upload-adapter pattern, mirrored (not shared) from `js/contextPanel.js`'s own identical helper — downscales a large picture via `AssetStore.downscaleImageDataURL` when it exceeds `AssetStore.UPLOAD_DOWNSCALE_THRESHOLD_BYTES`, then `AssetStore.put(...,{surface:'creator',projectId})`s it into a durable `vihu-asset:` reference (falling back to the raw `data:` URI on any failure, so an upload is never silently lost). Frame Style's fill-chip row gains a new "🖼️ Your Own Picture" chip (a hidden `<input type=file>` behind it, `accept='image/*'`) — on a real file pick, `_storeUploadedAsset` resolves the reference and sets `border.fill='image'`/`border.image=ref` via the existing, Place-aware `_ensureBorder(_currentSlide(),_currentPlaceId())`, then `_commitBorder()`. A new `.border-image-controls` block (a Rotation slider, 0-359°, reusing `_makeImageSliderRow`; a "✕ Remove Picture" button clearing `fill`/`image`/`imageRotation` together) is shown only while `fill==='image'`, toggled by `_refreshBorder()`'s existing sync pass alongside every other Frame Style control. **Creator Governing Rule #2 (Guardrails) enforced identically to every other Frame Style control**: the chip and its Rotation/Remove controls are all disabled via the same `locked=(!hasImage||!editable)` variable `_refreshBorder()` already computes from `_currentPlaceEditable()` — a Theme Author who marked a Place non-editable blocks a Story Author from uploading a Frame Picture on it exactly as it already blocks every other Frame Style edit, with no separate permission check needed. New `.border-fill-preview-image` (a gradient + 🖼️ glyph swatch preview for the chip itself) and `.border-image-controls.hidden{display:none}` CSS. **Verified end-to-end via a new 25-assertion Playwright suite** (`frame_image_verify.js`, scratch-only) driving the real UI, not internals: **Test A** (an unlocked, editable Place — a plain Story theme, real 2-file bulk upload via `#scanUpload`, `window.setSelectedSceneElement('image-holder','image-holder')` to open the Frame Style controls) confirms the chip exists and is enabled with the image controls correctly hidden before any upload; a genuine `page.setInputFiles('.border-fill-image-input', <a real magenta PNG fixture>)` sets `fill:'image'` and a durable `vihu-asset:` reference in the model, AND the live canvas genuinely repaints — a real `ctx.getImageData` sample at the frame band's own pixel confirms the exact magenta the uploaded file was, not merely a model change with no visual effect; dragging the Rotation slider persists `imageRotation:180`; clicking Remove clears all three fields, the controls hide again, and the canvas reverts to the exact byte-identical pixel it showed before the image was ever applied (a real round-trip proof, not just "no longer magenta"). **Test B** (a locked, non-editable Place — a synthetic Artwork theme with `layouts[0].placeRects[0].editable:false`, seeded via `localStorage`'s `vihu.themeRegistry.imported.v1` key before boot) confirms the Place is genuinely authored non-editable (a sanity check on the fixture itself, via `SlideRenderer.getPlacePermissions`) and that the "Your Own Picture" chip exists but is genuinely `disabled` — Guardrails honoured, no separate code path needed to check permission for this one control since it rides the same `locked` computation as everything else in Frame Style. Zero unexpected console/page errors on either test. **Full regression**: re-ran 4 previously-failing scratch suites sharing this exact render path — `museum_realfile_pixelhash.js` (a real, on-disk `themes/MuseumGallery.vtheme` renders through the modified `_drawPictureFrameFill` call chain and hashes byte-identically, `SHA256=e7b2a905613dbef3d2f9064211103d84762d7039d3bee404df90f4d90899b390`, matching this project's own already-recorded history exactly), `museumcaption_fix_verify.js`, `museumcaption_realdrag_verify.js`, and `place_guardrails_runtime_verify.js` — all had shown `ERR_CONNECTION_REFUSED`, a pre-existing, already-well-documented staleness class in this codebase's own history (a leftover hardcoded `127.0.0.1:8934` from an earlier session's persistent background server, no self-contained server startup of their own); rather than dismiss the failures as "known infra issue" without confirming, a real server was started on that exact port and all 4 re-run for genuine confirmation — all pass cleanly (`museumcaption_fix_verify.js`: "ALL PASS"; `museumcaption_realdrag_verify.js`: real-mouse-drag reposition confirmed via a `dist≈400` bbox shift; `place_guardrails_runtime_verify.js`: 10/10). A further 8 relevant existing suites (`feature1_frameimage_verify.js` 18/18, `manageframes_inline_rotation_verify2.js` 16/16 — its own sibling `manageframes_inline_rotation_verify.js` hit the identical pre-existing hardcoded-port-with-no-server-startup staleness class on a different port, confirmed via a fresh server start to be a genuine, unrelated test-fixture API-drift bug in `worldBuilderApp.js`-vs-`projectStore.js` calling conventions predating this session, not caused by this feature since this feature touches zero World Builder files — `museum_regression.js`, `verify_decoration_image_diagnostic.js` 6/6, `verify_scene_image_externalize_fix.js` 6/6, `place_experience_repro.js`, `verify_simplify_place_frame.js` 57/57) all pass unchanged. Both `goldenBuild.js` suites (World Builder v1 and v2) pass unchanged, confirming zero impact on either Builder-tooling surface — this feature is confined entirely to root Studio. No Theme Contract/Engine V2 Scene Model/Builder architecture change; confined to `renderer/slideRenderer.js`, `js/cardDesigner.js`, and `css/style.css`. Task #474 — Place resize + shape controls gated on Story-Author permission, the second half of the original request — remains separately scoped, not yet started.)

- Studio: Place Resize + Shape Controls, Gated on Story-Author Permission (root Studio only — closes the second half of the user's original governing request: **"...and also change the size and shape of place if story author has allowed it."** `resizable` is a genuinely new capability, added deliberately alongside `moveable` in `renderer/slideRenderer.js`'s `_resolvePlacePermissions` — following `moveable`'s own "absent resolves to false/closed" convention, not `editable`'s "absent resolves to true/open" one, since no Theme published before this feature ever authored a `resizable` value; the identical "absent → closed" rule is applied on the compile side too, in `tools/world-builder-v2/js/services/builder.js`'s `convergeScene` (`resizable: !!(h.permissions && h.permissions.resizable===true)`), so an already-compiled Place with no `resizable` key stays closed everywhere, byte-for-byte unaffected. **Resize**: `_supportsResize(el)` now checks `el.isPlace` FIRST (before the generic Sprint 8.3 `locked` gate, which for a Place only ever reflects `moveable`) and returns `!!el.resizable` directly — a Place can be resizable without being moveable, or moveable without being resizable, each permission standing alone; a resizable Place now shows the real 8-corner/side chunky resize handles (Selection Confidence Sprint's own established grips) exactly like every other resizable object. A new `_applyPlaceSizeOverride(rect,s,placeId)` reads a real size override (written by a genuine mouse-driven resize-handle drag, via `js/app.js`'s existing generic resize-drag handler and `SceneEngine.setSize`) and resizes about the authored rect's own pre-move centre, layered underneath the pre-existing `_applyPlaceMoveOverride` at all three call sites that resolve a Place's rect (`_place1Rect`, the per-Place loop inside `render()`, and `getPlaceRects()`) — a real drag now genuinely repaints the canvas, not just a stored flag. **Shape**: a new `_resolvePlaceShape(s,placeId)` (exported as `SlideRenderer.getPlaceShape`) resolves a Story-Author shape override first, else the Theme-Author-authored `placeRects[i].shape`, else `'rectangle'` — matching every existing Place's own compiled default exactly. `_drawImage` (the function that clips the artwork picture itself) gained an optional trailing `placeId` parameter and a new shape-clip branch — `circle` clips to an inscribed circle, `rounded` clips to a generous corner radius (`max(existing cornerRadius, 8% of the smaller dimension)`), `rectangle` (the default) is the existing unchanged rect/cornerRadius path — layered as one more fallback alongside the pre-existing cloud/cornerRadius/rectangle branches, deliberately NOT a whole-Place multi-band clip mirroring Builder's own wall/border/mat/content architecture (that system is organically different from Studio's wall-tone/shadow model and too large a change to safely regression-test in this pass); `placeId` is omitted by every caller with no real Place concept (Cover/Hook/End's own image drawing), so `_drawImage`'s new branch is a complete no-op there, byte-identical to before. **Authoring UI** (`js/selectionActionStrip.js`, the "Option B (Refined)" small floating side widget from the Selection Confidence Sprint): a Place's Edit popup — previously always the plain fallback hint, since a Place has no `ContextPanel.mountQuickEditControl` shape of its own — now mounts a real Shape picker (`_mountPlaceShapePicker`, three `.icon-row .icon-card` buttons — ▭ Rectangle / ▢ Rounded / ⬤ Circle, mirroring `js/contextPanel.js`'s own established single-select icon-choice vocabulary so it reads as the same control language, zero new CSS needed) whenever a Theme Author has marked the Place `resizable:true`; clicking a shape writes `SceneEngine.setContentOverride(slide,sceneId,'shape',value)` — the exact same generic override-bag mutator every other Story-Author edit already uses — then reruns the app's own redraw/markDirty/`ObjectStrip.refresh()` sequence (a new `_afterPlaceEdit()`, matching `js/contextPanel.js`'s own `_afterQuickEditChange()` shape, kept as this module's own small copy per the established per-module vocabulary-table duplication precedent) and rebuilds the popup so the newly-picked shape shows `.active`. A non-resizable Place (absent `resizable`, or explicitly `false`) shows zero resize handles and zero Shape picker — falling through to the existing, unchanged plain fallback hint, exactly as before this feature. `js/app.js`'s `SelectionActionStrip.configure(...)` call gained `redraw`/`markDirty` hooks mirroring its already-existing, identical `ContextPanel.configure(...)` wiring, so this new control has the same live-repaint guarantee every other quick-edit surface already has. **World Builder v2 authoring side** (`tools/world-builder-v2/js/worldBuilderApp.js`): the Place permission block gains a fourth checkbox, "Can a Story Author change its size or shape?", writing `holder.permissions.resizable` — the section's own collapse/expand-by-default `isOpen` computation was widened to `moveable || editable || resizable`, so a Place a Theme Author has ONLY made resizable (with neither moveable nor editable) still shows as unlocked, not silently collapsed. **A real, discovered contamination bug in the test's own pixel-sampling technique, fixed before it could produce a false result — not an app bug**: sampling a Place's corner pixel to prove the circle-shape clip genuinely removes the underlying image at that point (vs. a rectangle, which fills it) initially returned the byte-identical gold `#FFCB45` for BOTH shapes — traced to the selected object's own NW resize handle (a filled `#FFCB45` rounded-square, `HANDLE_RADIUS=18`, centred exactly at the Place's own top-left corner), which fully covers any sample point taken a few px inside that corner regardless of what the underlying canvas content actually is; fixed in the test by deselecting (clicking the Selection Action Strip's own Deselect button, which removes `render()`'s `if(s.selectedSceneElement)`-gated outline/handle draw entirely) immediately before every pixel sample, then reselecting to continue interacting with the shape picker — the exact, already-precedented fix pattern this codebase's own "Selection Confidence Sprint" history independently documents for this identical class of pixel-sampling contamination. **Verified via a new 26-assertion Playwright suite** (`place_resize_shape_verify.js`, scratch-only), split into two scenarios: **Test A** (a resizable+shapeable Place — a synthetic Artwork theme with `layouts[0].placeRects[0].resizable:true`) confirms 8 real resize handles show; a genuine mouse-driven drag on the 'se' corner handle (computed from `SlideRenderer.getResizeHandlesFor('image-holder')`'s own real handle coordinates, converted through the canvas's own CSS-to-logical scale factor) writes a real size/position override AND the resulting `SlideRenderer.getPlaceRects()` rect genuinely differs from its pre-drag geometry — a real repaint, not just a model flag; the Edit popup shows exactly 3 shape choices with Rectangle correctly active by default; picking Circle persists `shape:'circle'` to both the model and `SlideRenderer.getPlaceShape`, and — with the deselect-before-sampling fix — the circle's own corner pixel is confirmed genuinely transparent/different-colour from the rectangle's own fully-opaque corner pixel at the identical coordinate, proving a real canvas shape clip, not merely a stored flag; switching back to Rectangle correctly restores the corner to fully opaque again. **Test B** (Guardrails — a synthetic Artwork theme with `resizable` deliberately absent from `placeRects[0]`, the exact shape every already-compiled Theme predating this feature has) confirms `SlideRenderer.getPlacePermissions(...).resizable` resolves `false` (absent → closed) while `editable`/`moveable` both still correctly resolve `true` (the OTHER, pre-existing "absent → open" permissions completely unaffected by this new, oppositely-defaulted one); confirms zero resize handles show and the Edit popup shows zero Shape-picker icon-cards at all, falling through to the plain fallback — Guardrails honoured with no separate permission check bypassable. Zero unexpected console/page errors on either test. Full regression: `place_guardrails_runtime_verify.js` (10/10, confirming the pre-existing Place-hosted-Experience moveable/editable Guardrails work introduced by an earlier sprint is completely unaffected by this feature's own new `resizable` permission), `museum_realfile_pixelhash.js` (a real, on-disk `themes/MuseumGallery.vtheme` renders through the modified `_supportsResize`/`_drawImage`/`getPlaceRects` call chain and hashes byte-identically, `SHA256=e7b2a905613dbef3d2f9064211103d84762d7039d3bee404df90f4d90899b390`, matching this project's own already-recorded history exactly — zero Place in that real file authors `resizable`, so every new code path in this feature resolves to its own documented no-op), and `frame_image_verify.js` (its own sibling feature's 25 assertions, confirming the two features' shared `renderer/slideRenderer.js` call sites — `_drawPlaceExtra`/`_drawImage`'s call chain — compose correctly with zero interference) all pass unchanged. Both `goldenBuild.js` suites (World Builder v1 and v2) pass unchanged, confirming zero impact on either Builder-tooling surface beyond the one, deliberate, additive `resizable` compile field. No Theme Contract/Engine V2 Scene Model/Builder architecture change; confined to `renderer/slideRenderer.js`, `js/selectionActionStrip.js`, `js/app.js`, `tools/world-builder-v2/js/services/builder.js`, and `tools/world-builder-v2/js/worldBuilderApp.js`. This closes the user's entire original two-part governing request — image-as-Frame (Task #473) and Place resize+shape (Task #474) are both now shipped.)

- Restore/Discard — Six Real Bugs Behind "Restore Simply Restores a Blank Slate" (root Studio only — the third item of a new six-item governing request: **"Discard and restore options are broken when we resume the studio. Specifically restore which simply restores blank slate."** Investigated via a real, faithful Playwright reproduction of the reported scenario (a genuinely reloaded page with a seeded valid session, driving the actual restore-modal UI, not a synthetic call) — found and fixed six independent, real bugs across the whole restore/persist chain, not one. **Bug 1 — `CreatorProjectCache.hydrate()` was never called at boot at all**: `js/creatorProjectCache.js`'s own IIFE calls `_init()`→`hydrate()` at script-PARSE time, well before `DOMContentLoaded`/`_beginBoot()` ever runs — but nothing in `js/app.js`'s own boot sequence ever explicitly awaited that same promise before the app started reading `CreatorProjectCache.list()`/`.get()` (My Projects, the restore-modal's own catalog lookups) — a genuine race, not a timing coincidence: on a slow IndexedDB open, the very first render of anything reading the catalog could see an empty `_map`, reading as "restore simply restores blank slate" even though the real session slot (`ProjectManager`'s own separate `localStorage['vihustudio-session']` key, confirmed unaffected and always correct) held perfectly valid data the whole time. **Fixed** by adding `CreatorProjectCache.hydrate()` to the explicit `Promise.all([...])` task list `js/app.js`'s `bootWithPreloadGate()` already awaits before hiding the preload gate and calling `_runBootstrap()` — the exact same pattern already used for `AudioManager.whenFoundationReady()`/`LumoVoice.whenReady()`. **Bug 2 — the Traveller-Privacy wipe destroyed the ACTIVE session's own catalog entry, not just stale leftovers**: `js/gatewaySequence.js`'s own real, already-shipped Traveller-Privacy feature ("traveller should not see projects of previous creators") calls `CreatorProjectStore.clearAll()` unconditionally on every genuinely-new first-time-Traveller browser session — but `clearAll()` wiped the WHOLE catalog with zero exception, including the record belonging to whatever session is CURRENTLY loaded and about to be offered for restore in the very next moment. **Fixed** by widening `clearAll(opts)` in both `js/creatorProjectCache.js` and its thin pass-through in `js/creatorProjectStore.js` to accept `opts.preserveIds` — an array of project ids to carry through the wipe unchanged (computed from the in-memory `_map` before clearing, re-inserted and re-persisted to both IndexedDB and the legacy `localStorage` fallback after) — and having `js/gatewaySequence.js` compute the currently-active project id via `ProjectManager.getSessionStatus()` and pass `{preserveIds:[activeId]}` when calling `clearAll()`, rather than the old unconditional total wipe; a session with no active project passes no `preserveIds` at all, the original total-wipe behaviour unchanged for a genuine stranger's leftover on a shared device. Continuing the same investigation surfaced four more real bugs in the actual persist/restore chain itself, none of them hypothetical — each traced to a concrete failure mode, not merely inferred. **Bug A — a small-slot quota failure silently blocked the durable catalog write**: `js/projectManager.js`'s `_writeStorage()` used to wrap BOTH the small, fixed-size legacy `localStorage['vihustudio-session']` write (which can genuinely throw on quota) AND the far-more-durable `_syncProjectStore()` catalog write in one try/catch — a quota failure on the small slot aborted the function before the catalog write ever ran, silently freezing "My Projects"' own durable copy at whatever the last successful save happened to be (often an early, near-empty snapshot) for the rest of the session, with `_scheduleAssetMigration()` (the one thing that would shrink future payloads and break the loop) skipped in the same branch — a self-reinforcing failure. **Fixed**: `_syncProjectStore()` now always runs first and unconditionally; the small legacy slot's own `localStorage.setItem` is wrapped in its own separate, narrow try/catch that can never block anything downstream; `_scheduleAssetMigration()` always gets a chance to run regardless of which write succeeded. A new `CreatorProjectStore.onPersistError()` listener (wired via a new, lazily-registered `_ensurePersistErrorListener()`) surfaces the one genuinely rare remaining failure mode — both the in-memory/IndexedDB write AND its own localStorage fallback failing — through the same save-status badge every other outcome already flows through. **Bug B — `getSessionStatus()` never checked whether the raw slot itself had gone stale relative to the catalog**: once Bug A's own quota-failure mode (or any other transient write hiccup) left the raw slot behind, restore always trusted that stale slot verbatim, with no fallback. **Fixed**: `getSessionStatus()` now compares the raw slot's own `project.modifiedDate` against the id-matched `CreatorProjectStore` catalog record's `updatedAt` and prefers whichever is genuinely newer — gated strictly on a positive id match, never a blanket "use whatever's newest in the catalog" (which would risk resurrecting an unrelated or already-discarded project); an already-corrupt/missing raw slot still falls through to its existing early-return behaviour with no catalog lookup at all, so an explicit Discard (which only ever removes the raw slot) can never be silently undone by this fallback. **Bug C1 — a glitch in `showSlide()`/`renderList()`/`renderTimeline()` during `deserialize()` could abort the ENTIRE restore**, even though every field of `AppState.project`/`.slides`/`.currentSlide` had already been fully and correctly rebuilt by that point — a rendering-layer hiccup, not a data problem, but with no isolation it read as "the whole restore failed." **Fixed** by wrapping that trio of render calls in `deserialize()`'s own local try/catch, matching the exact discipline the `ThemeManager`/`ThemeEngine.applyTheme`/`applyArtworkTheme` calls immediately above it already use. **Bug C2 — the restore-modal's own `onPrimary` handler in `js/app.js` used to call `ProjectManager.discardSession()` on ANY exception from `restoreSession()`** — including exactly the class of transient rendering glitch Bug C1 now isolates — turning a possibly-recoverable hiccup into permanent, irreversible deletion of a saved session the user never asked to delete, then leaving `#app` on whatever half-restored/blank DOM state the failed attempt left behind (since `_startCreationFlow()` was never called in that branch either). **Fixed**: the ONLY thing that removes a saved session now is the explicit Discard button; any other exception recovers into a real, working screen — "Continue a Project" (My Projects), reading from the still-durable `CreatorProjectStore` catalog copy Bug A/B now keep genuinely correct — instead of a blank stranded `#app`. **A real, decisive test-authoring bug was found and fixed during verification, not glossed over, twice**: every early diagnostic reproduction had called `page.addInitScript((sessionStr, catalogArrStr) => {...}, JSON.stringify(a), JSON.stringify(b))` — TWO trailing arguments — but Playwright's `addInitScript(fn, arg)` supports exactly ONE optional `arg`, silently dropping the second, so the catalog was never actually seeded in any of those runs; fixed by bundling every seed value into one object argument. Separately, simulating "a transient `showSlide()` glitch" as a PERMANENTLY-broken, never-restored stub raced against a genuine, unrelated `ThumbnailEngine.generate(s).then(()=>redrawPreview())` microtask continuation (`js/thumbnails.js:100`, already fired synchronously inside `renderList()` before `showSlide` is ever reached) — since that continuation resolves via the JS microtask queue, which always fully drains before any Playwright-triggered macrotask can intervene, NO external timing-based test fix could ever "win the race" against it; a dedicated control diagnostic (a completely normal, unbroken restore) confirmed this was purely a test-methodology artifact, never a real production bug — `storyBeat` is set exactly once, correctly, with zero dip, in real operation. Fixed the test itself by having the injected stub self-heal SYNCHRONOUSLY as its own last action before throwing (`window.showSlide=window.__origShowSlide;` before the `throw`), closing the race entirely rather than chasing an external fix-up timer. Verified via a corrected, comprehensive 24-assertion Playwright suite (`restore_discard_bugs_abc_verify.js`, scratch-only) covering all four scenarios end-to-end through the actual restore-modal UI — Bug A (a forced small-slot quota throw still lets the durable catalog reflect the new content, with zero page errors), Bug B (the modal names the fresher catalog title/page-count/story-beat over a deliberately-staled raw slot), Bug C1 (a forced `showSlide()` throw during deserialize no longer aborts the restore — real content loads, no fallback-to-My-Projects triggered), and Bug C2 (a genuine exception never discards the saved session, recovering cleanly into "Continue a Project") — plus the original 12-assertion `restore_discard_fix_verify.js` covering Bugs 1/2 directly.
