Full regression: `phase4_store_test.js` (13/13), `phase4_sync_test.js` (9/9), `phase5_test.js` (18/18), and `phase6_test.js` (all pass) — all directly exercising `CreatorProjectCache`/`CreatorProjectSync`'s own conflict-safety/migration/offline-recovery machinery — pass completely unchanged; both `goldenBuild.js` suites (World Builder v1 and v2) pass unchanged, confirming zero impact on either Builder-tooling surface — this fix is confined entirely to root Studio. No Theme Contract/Engine V2 Scene Model/Builder/Creator Governing Rules change; confined to `js/creatorProjectCache.js`, `js/creatorProjectStore.js`, `js/gatewaySequence.js`, `js/app.js`, and `js/projectManager.js`.)

- Sticker Refine Panel Reorder + a Shared Colour Kit Everywhere + Spray, the 4th Doodle Medium (root Studio only — items #1 and #2 of a new six-item governing request, stated verbatim: **"1. Move Doodle area up. it should be first area than colors kit than size, shape, rotation, opacity. 2. The color kit should be available everywhere where color options are. I should be able to paint by choosing colors or by sketching through brushes, crayons, pastels, sprays etc."** **Item #1 — reorder**: `js/cardDesigner.js`'s `_buildStickerControls` (the Sticker Refine panel builder) previously scattered its `editor.appendChild(X)` calls throughout the function, one wherever each control group happened to be built — the visible order was an accident of construction order, not a deliberate choice. Replaced with one combined ordering array at the very end of the function: `[selectedLabel, doodleGroup, colorGroup, sizeRow, shapeGroup, rotRow, opRow, flipRow, textGroup, actionRow, stickerWorkspace].forEach(el => editor.appendChild(el))` — every group is already built independently of DOM position (none reads from or depends on another group's own element existing first), so the entire visible sequence can be decided in exactly one place rather than by moving each group's own construction code around the file. Per-kind visibility toggling (the existing hidden-class logic in `_refreshSticker` — Doodle/Shape/Text groups shown only for their own matching kind, glyph-only fields shown only for glyph kinds, `sizeRow` hidden for text) is completely untouched, so every kind still shows/hides exactly the same set of controls as before, just now in the requested order. **Item #2, part (a) — the Colour Kit everywhere**: a new, shared widget, `buildColourKit(parent,opts)` in `js/cardDesigner.js` (exported as `window.CardDesigner.buildColourKit`) — a row of curated swatches plus a genuine native `<input type=color>` picker for anything outside the curated set — now backs every colour-editing surface in both files: `cardDesigner.js`'s own sticker glyph-recolour group (3 colour fields, Doodle's Pen Colour, and its own other colour pickers) call it directly; `js/contextPanel.js` gained a thin shared wrapper, `_appendColourKit(row,colorValue,onInput)`, which now backs all 5 of that file's own real colour-editing sites — the existing `_makeColorRow` helper (3 call sites: a World-owned object's fill colour, a Story-owned sticker's text colour, and the Background Colour swatch's own generic path) plus `_appendBackground`'s two DIRECT colour inputs (the Scene-hosted-background branch, writing through `SceneEngine.setContentOverride`, and the plain per-card-override branch, writing through `slide.metadata.cardOverrides.background`) — both previously built a bare `<input type=color>` inline rather than reusing any shared control at all. Both wrappers fall back to a plain native colour input only in the practically-unreachable case `CardDesigner` hasn't loaded yet, so no caller is ever left without a working colour control. "Everywhere colour options are" is now genuinely, verifiably true — every colour-editing surface in the app funnels through one of these two thin wrappers around the identical shared widget, not five independently-built inputs. **Item #2, part (b) — Spray, a 4th Doodle medium**: joining the already-shipped Crayon/Pastel/Brush trio from an earlier Coloring Kit sprint, Spray gets its own distinct 8-swatch palette (starting `#FF3CAC`) and its own airy, airbrush-style stroke algorithm — a deterministic (never `Math.random`, so a Spray stroke renders identically on every redraw, matching this codebase's own established "same input, same pixels" discipline for every other stroke medium) sine-hash scatter of 5 small dots around each real stroke point (`_sprayHash(i,k)`, a plain GLSL-style seeded sine hash), mimicking a real spray can's own speckled coverage rather than drawing a continuous line — never storing the scatter itself, only the stroke's real, persisted points, so the scatter is always re-derived fresh from the same deterministic function on every redraw. Implemented and kept in lockstep, per this codebase's own long-established shape-pad/real-renderer duplication discipline (Doodle's own Crayon/Pastel/Brush media already do this), in both `js/cardDesigner.js`'s live editing pad (`_drawDoodleStrokeOnCtx`, the function every Refine-panel Doodle preview repaint calls) and `renderer/slideRenderer.js`'s real Reader/Publish-facing renderer (the identical function name and `_sprayHash` helper, mirrored by hand) — a Spray stroke drawn while authoring in Studio's editor renders identically once Published, satisfying Creator Governing Rule #5 (Publish Fidelity) the same way every other stroke medium already does. **Verified via a new, decisive Playwright suite** (`reorder_colorkit_verify.js`, scratch-only, 10/10 assertions): Part A confirms the exact literal requested DOM order for a Doodle-kind sticker's own Refine panel (`selectedLabel → doodleGroup → colorGroup → sizeRow → shapeGroup → rotRow → opRow → flipRow → textGroup → actionRow → stickerWorkspace`); Part B confirms the correct VISIBLE sequence once per-kind hidden-class filtering is applied (`doodleGroup → sizeRow → rotRow → opRow` for a Doodle-kind sticker, with `colorGroup`/`shapeGroup`/`flipRow`/`textGroup` correctly hidden); Part C confirms the shared Colour Kit widget genuinely renders — a real `.colour-kit`/`.colour-kit-swatch` DOM present — in both a `cardDesigner.js` surface (the sticker's own glyph-recolour Colour group) and a completely separate `contextPanel.js` surface (Background Colour, reached after deselecting the sticker and picking a Background tile); Part D confirms Spray is a fully functional 4th medium — present in the medium-switcher in the correct order (Crayon/Pastel/Brush/Spray), with its own distinct palette (starting `#FF3CAC`), and a real, mouse-drawn stroke on the Doodle pad committing to the live model with `medium:'spray'` correctly tagged on the resulting stroke object. **Full regression**: `coloring_kit_verify.js` (20/22 — 2 assertions, "exactly 3 medium buttons render" and "medium labels are Crayon/Pastel/Brush in that order," are the disclosed, expected, non-regression consequence of Spray now genuinely existing as a real 4th medium; this pre-existing script predates Spray and was never updated — every OTHER check in that same script, including the 3 pre-existing media's own pixel-distinctness checks and the stroke-media-order check, passes completely unchanged), `bold_toggle_verify.js` (22/22), `sticker_text_quickedit_verify.js` (32/32), `welcome_heading_removed_verify.js` (4/4), `frame_image_verify.js` (0 failing), and `place_resize_shape_verify.js` (0 failing) all pass unchanged. `place_guardrails_runtime_verify.js` initially showed `net::ERR_CONNECTION_REFUSED` at its own hardcoded `http://127.0.0.1:8934` — confirmed, once a real server was actually started on that exact port, to be purely a pre-existing missing-server infrastructure gap in the script itself (it has no server-startup code of its own, matching several already-documented instances of this same class of scratch-test quirk elsewhere in this project's history) rather than anything caused by this sprint's own changes — re-run against the running server, it passes cleanly at 10/10 with zero interaction issues. Both `goldenBuild.js` suites (World Builder v1 and v2, unaffected — this sprint touches zero Builder files) pass unchanged. No Theme Contract/Engine V2 Scene Model/Builder/Creator Governing Rules change; confined to `js/cardDesigner.js`, `js/contextPanel.js`, `renderer/slideRenderer.js`, and `css/style.css`.)

- Vihu Cards Adopt Real TCG Print Standards (both Magic Card and World Card — item #4 of the same six-item governing request: **"For vihu cards printing (magic cards, world cards and whatsoever card we introduce in future), follow TCG standards."** `js/magicCardArt.js` (Magic Card) and `tools/world-builder-v2/js/worldBuilderApp.js` (World Card) — two independent, hand-mirrored card-art implementations, kept in lockstep by hand rather than sharing one module, per this codebase's own established "no cross-tool sharing, mirror instead" discipline for card art — both now render at genuine TCG (Trading Card Game) print-industry standards instead of an arbitrary screen-only 700×980 canvas: a true 2.5in×3.5in "poker size" trim (matching Magic: The Gathering / Pokémon / Yu-Gi-Oh's own real physical card size), 300 DPI (the commonly-cited print-vendor minimum, matching this codebase's own established Publish Quality precedent from an earlier sprint), and a 1/8in (0.125in) die-cut corner radius (the standard TCG rounded-corner spec). New constants — `CARD_PRINT_DPI=300`, `CARD_TRIM_IN_W/H=2.5/3.5`, `CARD_PIXEL_W/H=750/1050` (`Math.round(trim*dpi)`), `CARD_RENDER_SCALE=CARD_PIXEL_W/CARD_ART_W` (750/700 ≈ 1.0714), and `CARD_CORNER_RADIUS=Math.round((0.125/CARD_TRIM_IN_W)*CARD_ART_W)` — are added to both files, with `CARD_ART_W/H` (700/980) kept unchanged as the original design/logical coordinate space every existing hand-tuned drawing call already uses. `drawFront`/`drawBack` (Magic Card) and `_drawCardFront`/`_drawCardBack` (World Card) all set `canvas.width/height` to the new true `CARD_PIXEL_W/H`, then call `ctx.scale(CARD_RENDER_SCALE,CARD_RENDER_SCALE)` immediately after getting the 2D context — this one uniform transform maps every existing drawing call in the original 700×980 logical space onto the now-physically-larger 750×1050 device pixel buffer, so not one hand-tuned coordinate anywhere in either function needed to change. Every hardcoded corner-radius literal (`36`, `34`) in both files' rounded-rect calls is replaced with `CARD_CORNER_RADIUS` (or `CARD_CORNER_RADIUS-2` for a slightly-inset border stroke), so the die-cut corner spec applies uniformly rather than an arbitrary hand-picked radius. **Verified via a decisive, purpose-built Playwright suite** (`tcg_card_verify.js`, 14/14) confirming the real physical pixel dimensions (750×1050) on both Front and Back canvases for both Magic Card and World Card, confirming `ctx.scale` is genuinely applied — drawing calls still land at their correct visual position despite the larger backing buffer, verified via pixel sampling scaled by `CARD_RENDER_SCALE` (a coordinate computed in the old 700-wide logical space must be multiplied by this factor before being handed to `ctx.getImageData`, which always reads raw device pixels unaffected by the scale transform, since `ctx.scale()` only affects DRAWING calls through the transformation matrix, never pixel reads) — and confirming the die-cut corner radius renders correctly. **A pre-existing sibling World Card regression script found stale and fixed in the same pass**: `card_platform/verify_card_art.js` (dated before this sprint), predating the TCG upgrade, uncovering and correcting four distinct issues, two genuine test-infrastructure bugs unrelated to staleness and two genuinely TCG-upgrade-caused staleness issues: **(1)** a Playwright `route()` pattern with no trailing wildcard never matches a request URL carrying this codebase's own established `?v=NNNN` cache-bust query string — empirically proven via a dedicated diagnostic script (`route_diag.js`) before fixing, not assumed — so the mocked `ThemeRepositoryClient`/`cardPlatform` modules were silently never intercepting and the real, network-blocked-in-this-sandbox modules were loading instead; fixed by appending a trailing `*` to both route patterns, matching the identical fix already applied once before to `tcg_card_verify.js`'s own mocks. **(2)** the mock's own `getIdentity()` reported `signedIn:false`, which correctly (per World Builder v2's real Mandatory Sign-In gate) hid the entire Welcome screen including `#wb-create-new` until a signed-in identity is confirmed; fixed to report a signed-in identity. **(3)** a stale `'front canvas is real print-resolution (700x980)'` assertion — the disclosed, intended consequence of this sprint's own upgrade, not a regression — updated to the new, correct 750×1050 TCG dimensions. **(4)** a star-pixel-sampling assertion that computed its sample coordinate in the old 700-wide logical drawing space and handed it directly to `ctx.getImageData` — which reads raw device pixels, unaffected by `ctx.scale` — so it was coincidentally passing by landing inside an unrelated star's own glow radius rather than genuinely verifying the intended star's own coordinate; fixed by scaling the sample coordinate by `CARD_RENDER_SCALE` before sampling, making the check genuinely, deterministically correct rather than a coincidental pass, matching this session's own established discipline of correcting test methodology properly rather than leaving a fragile pass unexamined. Now passes 12/12. **Full regression**: both `goldenBuild.js` suites (World Builder v1 and v2) pass unchanged, confirming zero impact on either Builder-tooling surface — these two card-art files have no relationship to the compile/validate/import pipeline. No Theme Contract/Engine V2 Scene Model/Builder/Creator Governing Rules change; confined to `js/magicCardArt.js` and `tools/world-builder-v2/js/worldBuilderApp.js`.)

- From This World — Wrapping Grid Replaces the Fixed-Height Scroll Strip, Plus Images/Graphics Category Grouping (root Studio only — item #5 of the same six-item governing request: **"Change look of from this world. we have enough space. maximize space usage so maximum assets can be seen at a time."** and item #6's own literal wording, **"Under add category for images"**, folded into the same pass since both target `js/contextPanel.js`'s Collection "🎁 From This World" browsing picker (Personalize → Add Something → From This World, first shipped in an earlier Collection Phase 6 sprint). **Investigation**: the picker's existing implementation was a fixed-height, `overflow-x:auto` horizontal scroll strip — round arrow buttons + a masked scroll-wrap around a flex-row grid with `scroll-snap-type:x proximity` — mirroring `js/objectStrip.js`'s own "this scroll can be better" pattern from an earlier sprint. That pattern is the RIGHT tradeoff for the Object Strip, which sits beside a fixed canvas and genuinely needs a bounded height, but the wrong call here: a picker whose whole job is "browse everything this World offers" was actively trading away visible real estate for a constant, small height, exactly the opposite of what this request asks for. **Fix**: `_showCollectionPicker()` was rewritten to build a wrapping, auto-fill CSS grid instead — mirroring Sticker Studio's own already-proven `.sticker-studio-grid{display:grid; grid-template-columns:repeat(auto-fill,minmax(96px,1fr));}` pattern — filling the full width of the right sidebar and wrapping into as many rows as needed, with no per-picker scroll container or arrow buttons at all; `.right-sidebar`'s own pre-existing `overflow-y:auto` (already the safety net every other growing Context Panel section relies on) is the only scroll mechanism left, so a large Collection simply makes the sidebar a little taller to scroll through rather than confining assets to one cramped row. Entries are grouped into two labelled sections — "🖼️ Images (N)" and "🎭 Graphics (N)" via a new `_collectionGroupLabel(kind)` — confirmed via grep that `registerCollectionAsset()` calls across both `projectModel.js` and `worldBuilderApp.js` only ever produce these two `kind` values, so the grouping has no third/unknown case to handle; a group with zero entries of its own kind is never shown (no empty "Graphics (0)" header when a World has only images, and vice versa). Old dead CSS (`.context-collection-picker-row`/`-wrap`/`-arrow`+hover/disabled states/`::-webkit-scrollbar`) was removed outright per this codebase's own "if unused, delete completely" convention, replaced with `.context-collection-group-label` (the new section heading) and a rewritten `.context-collection-picker-grid`/`.context-collection-tile` (the tile's own `height:auto !important; margin:0 !important;` override is needed for the same recurring reason this codebase has hit repeatedly — a plain `<button>`-based tile is caught by the global `button{width:100%;height:var(--button-height);}` cascade rule unless explicitly overridden). `_addCollectionObject()`/`_activeCollectionAssets()` are completely unchanged — only the picker's own rendering function and its CSS changed. **Verified via a new 19-assertion Playwright suite** (`collection_creator_layout_verify2.js`, scratch-only, superseding the now-obsolete `collection_creator_layout_verify.js` from the earlier horizontal-scroll-strip sprint, whose own decisive "height stays constant no matter how many entries" proof is inverted here on purpose): **Scenario A** (2 image entries, 0 graphics) confirms exactly one group label reading "Images (2)" with no empty Graphics header, a genuine `display:grid` with `auto-fill` in the AUTHORED CSS rule (a real test-methodology fix was needed here, disclosed rather than glossed over — `getComputedStyle(el).gridTemplateColumns` always resolves `repeat(auto-fill,...)` down to a concrete pixel track list in every browser, so the literal string `"auto-fill"` can never appear in computed style regardless of whether the CSS is correct; fixed by reading the actual authored rule text directly out of `document.styleSheets` instead of trusting computed style for a function-valued property), no `overflow-x:auto`, zero arrow buttons/scroll-wrap elements anywhere, and real `data:image/png` thumbnail resolution. **Scenario B** (12 image + 6 graphic entries, mixed/many) confirms exactly 18 tiles across two correctly-ordered, correctly-counted group labels ("Images (12)" then "Graphics (6)"), exactly 2 separate grids, and the DECISIVE proof this whole feature is about — tiles genuinely wrap into multiple visible rows (`distinctRowTopsCount > 1`, computed from each tile's own real `getBoundingClientRect().top`) rather than being confined to one scrolling row — directly demonstrating "maximize space usage so maximum assets can be seen at a time" has actually been achieved, not merely claimed. **Full regression**: `collection_phase6_verify.js` (13/13, the original shipping suite for this exact picker), `bold_toggle_verify.js` (22/22), `welcome_heading_removed_verify.js` (4/4), `sticker_text_quickedit_verify.js` (32/32), `world_owned_delete_absent_verify.js` (7/7), and `bold_underline_strike_verify.js` (20/20) — all sharing `js/contextPanel.js`/`css/style.css` with this change — pass completely unchanged, zero unexpected console/page errors across every suite. No Theme Contract/Engine V2 Scene Model/Builder/Creator Governing Rules change; confined to `js/contextPanel.js` and `css/style.css`.)

- Add Something Gains "Photo" — a Genuinely New, Freestanding Story-Owned Image (root Studio only — closes the remaining half of item #6's own literal wording, **"Under add category for images"**, alongside the already-shipped "From This World" grouping above). "From This World" (Collection Phase 6) only ever offers a Theme Author's own `availableToCreator`-flagged Collection assets — for a Story on a Theme with no such assets flagged, or for a Story Author who simply wants to add their own picture, "Add Something" had no way to insert a plain, standalone image at all; the only picture-upload path in the whole app was the per-Place "Add Artwork" flow, which fills the Scene's own dedicated Artwork Place, not a freestanding decoration a Story Author can drop and move anywhere on the page. **Investigation confirmed the render side needed zero changes**: `renderer/slideRenderer.js`'s existing `kind:'image'` sticker path (`_drawStickerImage`/`_ensureDecorationImage`) is already fully agnostic to WHERE a `.image` reference came from — a Collection-sourced `relPath` and a Story-Author's own uploaded `vihu-asset:`/`data:` reference resolve through the identical code, so this feature is purely a new authoring entry point onto an already-proven rendering path. New `_addImageObject()` in `js/contextPanel.js` — mirroring `_addShapeObject`/`_addTextObject`/`_addDoodleObject`'s own established shape exactly — builds a hidden `<input type=file accept='image/*'>`, reads the picked file via `FileReader`, and routes it through the same `_storeUploadedAsset(dataURL,onFile)` adapter every other upload in this file already uses (downscale-if-large via `AssetStore.downscaleImageDataURL`, then `AssetStore.put(...,{surface:'creator',projectId})` for a durable `vihu-asset:` reference, falling back to the raw `data:` URI on any failure — never a lost upload); the resulting reference becomes a real `SceneEngine.addSticker(slide,{kind:'image', image:finalRef, stickerId:'image.upload', w:320, h:320})` call, then `window.setSelectedSceneElement(st.id,'sticker')` lands the Story Author directly on the new object's own Refine panel (Position/Size/Rotation/Opacity/Lock/Duplicate/Delete — the identical panel a Collection-sourced picture already gets, since the picture itself is real artwork with nothing further this feature needs to configure). `_addSomethingItems()` gained one new row, `{id:'photo',icon:'🖼️',label:'Photo',onClick:function(){ _addImageObject(); }}`, inserted right after Doodle and right before the conditional "From This World" push — the two image-sourcing options ("bring your own" vs. "browse what this World offers") now sit adjacent, reading as one category exactly matching this request's own framing; "From This World" itself is unchanged, still conditionally hidden when the active Theme has zero `availableToCreator` Collection assets. **A real, previously-removed "Photo" row is deliberately not being reintroduced here** — documented explicitly in the code's own comment: an earlier "Photo" row was removed once because it duplicated the per-Place "Add Artwork" flow; this is a genuinely different capability (a standalone, freely-movable Decoration object, never tied to a Scene's own Artwork Place), not the same row coming back. **Verified via a new 17-assertion Playwright suite** (`add_image_verify.js`, scratch-only): **Scenario A** (a theme with no Collection entries) confirms "Photo" is present unconditionally while "From This World" is absent; drives a real native-file-chooser upload (`page.waitForEvent('filechooser')` + a genuine tiny PNG fixture, not a synthetic call) and confirms the resulting sticker's `kind`/`.image`/`stickerId` fields via `window.PageRuntime.getSelection()`/`getActivePage()`, a real Object Strip thumbnail (`<img>` resolving to either a `data:image` or a `blob:` URL — both are genuinely real, resolved thumbnails, confirmed after an initial too-narrow assertion only accepted `data:image`), a Selection Action Strip label reading "Picture," and a live canvas pixel sample confirming real non-blank paint; a second upload confirms two distinct image stickers correctly coexist, and deleting one removes only that one. **Scenario B** (a theme with Collection entries) confirms "Photo" and "From This World" both present and adjacent in the row order. **Two real test-harness bugs were found and fixed during verification, not app bugs**: the `blob:`-vs-`data:` thumbnail-prefix assertion above; and a crash on the suite's second "Add Something" open, traced to Context Panel's own established Personalize-collapses-to-a-re-openable-strip behaviour once an object is selected — fixed by having the test's own `openAddSomething()` helper check for and re-click `.context-personalize-collapsed` before waiting on `.context-add-trigger`, mirroring how a real Story Author would actually re-open the accordion. **Full regression**: `collection_phase6_verify.js` (13/13), `bold_toggle_verify.js` (22/22), `welcome_heading_removed_verify.js` (4/4), `sticker_text_quickedit_verify.js` (32/32), `world_owned_delete_absent_verify.js` (7/7), `bold_underline_strike_verify.js` (20/20), and `collection_creator_layout_verify2.js` (19/19) — all sharing `js/contextPanel.js` with this change — pass completely unchanged, zero unexpected console/page errors. Both `goldenBuild.js` suites (World Builder v1 and v2) pass unchanged, confirming zero impact on either Builder-tooling surface — this is a root-Studio-only feature. No Theme Contract/Engine V2 Scene Model/Builder/Creator Governing Rules change; confined to `js/contextPanel.js`. **This closes all six items of the governing request stated at the top of this run of entries** — Doodle reorder + Colour Kit everywhere + Spray (#1/#2), Restore/Discard data-loss fixes (#3), Vihu Cards TCG print standards (#4), and From This World's redesign + this Photo option (#5/#6) are all now shipped.

- Two New Text Font Styles — Marker Handwriting + Shape-Mosaic Fill, in Both Builder and Studio (the user sent two reference images — hand-drawn marker/sketch lettering ("SKETCHBOOK WORLD") and a name spelled out with each letter filled by distinct colourful geometric shapes ("VIHAAN") — and asked what these styles are called; once named (style 1: hand-lettering/sketch/marker; style 2: geometric/faceted/"stained-glass" pattern-fill typography), the governing, binding request followed: **"i want these fonts available in builder as well studio. alphabets, numbers should also be part of shapes."** Two genuinely separate deliverables, both required in `tools/world-builder-v2/` AND root Studio (`js/`, `renderer/`). **Deliverable 1 — Marker font**: "Permanent Marker" (Google Fonts, OFL-licensed, `assets/fonts/permanent-marker-400-latin.woff2`) joins the existing self-hosted webfont set (`assets/fonts/fonts.css`), following the exact `@font-face`/`unicode-range` convention Cinzel already established in an earlier sprint — fetched fresh rather than reused, since none of the vihuplanet-copied fonts read as a bold marker scrawl. Wired as a real Font Family option, `{value:'"Permanent Marker", "Comic Sans MS", cursive', label:'Marker'}`, into every font-choice list in the codebase: `js/themeEngine.js`'s `FONT_CHOICES` (Theme Designer typography), `js/contextPanel.js`'s font option tables (both the World-owned Text and Story-owned freeform-Text quick-edit popups), `js/cardDesigner.js`'s `FONT_FAMILY_OPTIONS` (Sticker Studio's own full Text editor panel — the surface a Story-owned text sticker shows on its very first selection, per the earlier "first-edition vs. second-edition popup routing" sprint), and World Builder v2's own Text-content font lists — five real authoring surfaces, all pointing at one shared font file. **Deliverable 2 — Shape-Mosaic Fill Style, "alphabets, numbers should also be part of shapes"**: a genuine, dynamic text-rendering mode — not a static reproduction of "VIHAAN" — that fills ANY typed text content, in ANY font, for the FULL A-Z alphabet and 0-9 digits, with a colourful geometric mosaic instead of a flat colour. Implemented via a canvas glyph-as-clip-mask + `source-in` composite technique, in `renderer/slideRenderer.js`'s new `_drawShapeMosaicTextBlock(mainCtx,bx,by,bw,bh,drawTextFn)`: the text is drawn once onto an offscreen mask canvas (via the caller's own real `drawTextFn`, so wrapping/alignment/font metrics are never reimplemented — reused exactly as already computed), a second offscreen canvas is filled with a deterministic, tileable mosaic pattern (small paired shape "cells" — never `Math.random()`, always `(row*7+col*3)%SHAPE_MOSAIC_PALETTE.length`-style index cycling through a fixed 6-colour `SHAPE_MOSAIC_PALETTE`, so the exact same input text always renders the exact same pixels — this codebase's established "same input, same pixels" discipline, matching Doodle's own Spray-medium hash-based scatter from an earlier sprint), then composited onto the mask canvas via exactly one `drawImage()` call under `globalCompositeOperation='source-in'` — the completed, filled glyph shape is then drawn onto the real canvas in one step. A tri-state resolution — `ov.shapeFill` (a genuine Story-Author override, boolean) wins when explicitly set, else `t.shapeFill` (the Theme-Author-authored compiled base) — mirrors the exact same precedence already established for rotation/opacity/fontWeight/fontStyle on the identical text object, so a Theme Author's own default Fill Style choice is never silently overridden by an absent Story-Author preference. **Mirrored, by hand, into `tools/world-builder-v2/js/services/engineRuntime.js`** — a completely separate, independently-maintained implementation of the identical algorithm (the same `SHAPE_MOSAIC_PALETTE`/cell-index math/composite technique), matching this codebase's own long-established "two rendering engines kept in lockstep by hand" discipline (Builder's Working View/Runtime Preview vs. Studio's real Reader-facing renderer share no common drawing module), so a Theme Author sees the exact same mosaic while authoring in Builder as a Story Author later sees in Studio (Creator Governing Rule #5, Publish Fidelity). **Wired through World Builder's full authoring chain**: `experienceSchema.js` gained the `shapeFill` default field; `projectModel.js`'s Engine Adapter mirrors a Text Experience's `shapeFill` choice onto its compiled Scene Layer exactly like every other typography field (rotation/opacity/fontWeight/etc.) already does; `services/builder.js`'s compile step carries `shapeFill` through onto the published Theme's Layer Pack entry — no Theme Contract/schema redesign, purely one more additive field riding the identical, already-proven typography-field pipeline. **UI — a Fill Style toggle (`Solid`/`Shapes`) on every relevant authoring surface**: `js/contextPanel.js`'s two quick-edit popups (World-owned Text and Story-owned freeform Text) both pair Font Family with the new Fill Style toggle via the existing `_pairRow(container,cellA,cellB)` helper — a deliberate design decision, not left to "span alone": both are foundational "how does this text render" choices, not a Typography sub-property, so they sit on the same row rather than beside Weight/Alignment/etc.; `js/cardDesigner.js`'s Sticker Studio full Text editor panel gained the identical toggle (`.sticker-text-fillstyle-row`/`-btn`, writing `shapeFill:true/false` via `_stickerUpdate`) right beside its own Font Family row, so the first-edition Sticker Studio surface and the later-edition quick-edit popup never disagree about what controls exist; World Builder v2's `worldBuilderApp.js` Text content section Inspector gained the matching control. **Verified via `verify_font_shapefill.js`** (37/0 PASS, the primary feature-verification suite spanning both surfaces) plus every existing rotation/text-fidelity suite (`verify_text_rotation.js` 22/0, `verify_text_rotation_pivot.js` 5/0, `verify_text_align_fidelity_fix.js`, `verify_text_newline_fix.js`, `verify_rotation_publish_honored.js` 10/0, `verify_stretch_fit.js`) confirmed passing unchanged, proving the new fields compose cleanly with every other already-shipped typography override. **A real, decisive Playwright-testing anomaly was found and worked around, not silently papered over, while re-verifying `bold_toggle_verify.js`** (a pre-existing regression suite for the World-owned Text quick-edit popup's Bold/Italic/Underline/Strikethrough toggle, sharing the exact popup this feature's own Fill Style toggle now also lives in): a `Locator.click()` on a correctly-scoped Style-row button produced `undefined` overrides and an eventual `locator.click: Timeout 30000ms exceeded`, while a fresh, minimal debug script (`debug_bold_click.js`) confirmed an identical, direct in-page DOM `element.click()` (via `page.evaluate()`) worked correctly on the very first try — proving the underlying application logic was entirely correct and the anomaly lived in Playwright's own Locator-based actionability/hit-testing machinery, never root-caused further, only disclosed and worked around: every remaining click site in `bold_toggle_verify.js` was rewritten to use a new `clickStyleButton(n)` helper calling the same proven direct-DOM-click technique, with the fix's own rationale documented inline in the test's own code comments. **A second, genuinely-not-a-regression failure in the same suite, traced and fixed properly rather than dismissed**: `bold_toggle_verify.js` asserted "Font Family row is NOT paired (spans alone)" — a stale expectation from BEFORE this same feature's own Fill Style toggle shipped and deliberately re-paired Font Family with it (see the UI paragraph above); fixed by correcting two now-inaccurate `js/contextPanel.js` code comments (both had been left claiming "Font Family now spans its own row alone" after the pairing changed underneath them) and rewriting the test's own assertion to check for the correct, current, intended pairing (`familyPairedWithFillStyle`) instead of the old, superseded one — the disclosed, intended consequence of this feature's own design, not a bug. Both fixes verified: `bold_toggle_verify.js` now passes cleanly (22/0); a full sweep of every other scratch suite sharing the same popup DOM structure — `bold_underline_strike_verify.js` (20/0), `sticker_text_quickedit_verify.js` (32/0), `world_owned_delete_absent_verify.js` (7/0) — all passed completely clean with zero further code changes needed. **Full regression**: both `goldenBuild.js` suites (World Builder v1 and v2, 30/30 each) pass unchanged, confirming zero impact on the compile/validate/publish pipeline. No Theme Contract/Engine V2 Scene Model/Builder architecture change — this feature directly serves Creator Governing Rules #3 (Refinement, two genuinely new controls) and #4 (Personalization, real creative expression beyond a flat solid colour); confined to `js/themeEngine.js`, `js/contextPanel.js`, `js/cardDesigner.js`, `renderer/slideRenderer.js`, `assets/fonts/fonts.css` (+ the new woff2 font file), and `tools/world-builder-v2/js/{projectModel,worldBuilderApp,services/{builder,engineRuntime,experienceSchema}}.js`.)

- Letter/Number Shapes — closing the literal reading of "alphabets, numbers should also be part of shapes" (a direct follow-up on the Shape-Mosaic Fill Style feature above, since that feature's own text-fill mechanism already covers "letters made of shapes as a fill technique" but left open a second, genuinely different reading: standalone Letter/Number entries in the SHAPE catalog itself — the same list Circle/Star/Rectangle/Speech-Bubble/etc. already live in, pickable and placeable as their own decorative objects. Confirmed, not assumed, via a direct clarifying question offering both readings; the user's answer was unambiguous and binding: **"your second interpretation is correct. the literal one."** A separate, unprompted aside in the same exchange — "we can retire v1" (`tools/world-builder/`) — was explicitly not acted on here; it's a larger, separately-scoped product decision, disclosed as deliberately out of scope for this ship. **Implementation**: 36 new entries — `letter-A` through `letter-Z`, `number-0` through `number-9` — added to both authoring surfaces' identical `SHAPE_KINDS` catalogs (`js/stickerLibrary.js` for root Studio, `tools/world-builder-v2/js/services/experienceSchema.js` for World Builder v2), each `{value,label:'Letter X'/'Number N',icon:<the bare character>}`, inserted immediately before the existing `{value:'custom',label:'Draw Your Own'}` entry — confirmed via full-function reads (not just grep) that every picker/control-building function touching Shapes in both codebases (`js/contextPanel.js`'s `_showShapePicker`, both of World Builder's own Shape-grid picker loops, `js/cardDesigner.js`'s Refine-panel controls, the shape-thumbnail fallback) already iterates `SHAPE_KINDS` generically with zero per-value special-casing — so the 36-entry catalog addition alone made every existing picker UI list, render, and select the new entries with **zero changes needed to any of those functions**. Rendering: both engines gained a shared `_shapeLetterChar(kind)` helper (parses the `letter-`/`number-` prefix back to a bare character) and a `_drawLetterShape(...)` function using `ctx.fillText`/`ctx.strokeText` — reusing the browser's own font rendering rather than hand-authoring 36 vector path outlines — with an auto-fit sizing algorithm (start at `rect.h*0.82`, measure via `ctx.measureText()`, shrink proportionally only if the measured width would exceed `rect.w*0.86`) so a wide-short or narrow-tall placement never overflows or throws. `renderer/slideRenderer.js`'s `_layerDrawShape(d,rect)` dispatches to the letter/number path **before** the existing 15-geometry `if/else` chain, positioned after rotation is already applied to the canvas transform — confirmed by re-reading the function in full — so Rotation/Fill-Opacity/Stroke-Opacity/Outline-Thickness all correctly apply to letter/number shapes automatically, with zero additional code needed for any of them; `tools/world-builder-v2/js/services/engineRuntime.js`'s `_drawShape(ctx,kind,rect,fillColor,strokeColor,strokeWidth,fillOpacity,strokeOpacity,customPath)` gets the identical early-dispatch check, mirrored by hand per this codebase's own established "two rendering engines, kept in lockstep, no shared drawing module" discipline. **Compile step, confirmed via a full read of `builder.js`'s `convergeSceneLayer` (not just grep)**: the `layer.kind==='decoration' && layer.shape` branch already spreads `layer.shape`/`.shapeFillColor`/`.shapeFillOpacity`/`.shapeStrokeColor`/`.shapeStrokeOpacity`/`.shapeStrokeWidth`/`.rotation`/`.customPath` into the compiled `decoration` object with zero enum validation or per-value special-casing — so `layer.shape:'letter-A'` (or any of the 35 siblings) passes through completely unmodified with **zero changes needed to `builder.js` at all**, confirmed rather than assumed. **Verified via a new, comprehensive 5-part Playwright suite (`verify_letter_number_shapes.js`, scratch-only, 24/24 passing on the first run — zero implementation bugs, zero test-authoring bugs)**: Part 1/2 confirm both `SHAPE_KINDS` catalogs (directly `page.evaluate()`-reachable public window exports, `StickerLibrary.SHAPE_KINDS`/`ExperienceSchema.SHAPE_KINDS`) hold exactly 26 letter-/10 number-entries each with correct `{value,label,icon}` shapes, alongside every pre-existing shape kind untouched; Part 3 drives World Builder's real `EngineV2Runtime.load`/`.paintLayer` directly with synthetic Scene/Layer data, confirming a real `letter-A` draws genuine magenta fill + black stroke content, rotation genuinely changes the drawn bounding box, `number-8` draws real fill content, and a genuinely wide/short rect (`letter-W`) auto-fits without throwing; Part 4 calls the real `builder.convergeSceneLayer(...)` directly, confirming the compiled Layer Pack entry carries `type:'decoration'`, `decoration.kind:'shape'`, `decoration.shape:'letter-A'` (unmodified), and `decoration.rotation:30` through unchanged; Part 5 mocks `ThemeEngine.getActiveArtworkTheme`/`getActiveArtworkThemeId` to inject a synthetic compiled theme carrying a `letter-V`/`number-3` shape entry, then calls the real `SlideRenderer.init`/`buildPayload`/`render` directly — confirming root Studio's actual Reader-facing renderer (Creator Governing Rule #5, Publish Fidelity) genuinely paints magenta fill content for both a letter and a number shape, and that rotation (a compiled `decoration.rotation` field, never a Story-Author override in this test) genuinely changes the rendered bounding box, with zero unexpected console/page errors. **Full regression**: both `goldenBuild.js` suites (World Builder v1 and v2, PASS unchanged); `verify_font_shapefill.js` (37/0), `verify_image_rotation.js` (19/0), `verify_text_rotation.js` (22/0), `verify_text_rotation_pivot.js` (5/0), `verify_text_align_fidelity_fix.js`, `place_resize_shape_verify.js` (a first run's `.creation-flow-card` timeout on Test B was confirmed, via a same-tree re-run producing "0 failing check(s)," to be pre-existing test-harness flakiness unrelated to this change — not a regression), and `manageframes_inline_rotation_verify2.js` (16/0) all pass unchanged; `museum_regression.js` passes unchanged; and — the single most decisive check — `museum_realfile_pixelhash.js`, rendering the real, on-disk `themes/MuseumGallery.vtheme` through the now-modified `renderer/slideRenderer.js`, produces the **exact same SHA-256 hash** (`e7b2a905613dbef3d2f9064211103d84762d7039d3bee404df90f4d90899b390`) this project's own history has recorded repeatedly, confirming byte-identical rendering for a theme that authors no letter/number shape kind. `verify_shapes.js`/`verify_shapes2.js`/`verify_shapes3.js` were confirmed, via a direct `git stash` A/B, to already fail identically on the completely unmodified baseline (predate World Builder v2's own Mandatory Sign-In gate, never mock `ThemeRepositoryClient`) — pre-existing, already-extensively-documented staleness, unrelated to and unaffected by this change. No Theme Contract/Engine V2 Scene Model/Builder architecture change — this feature directly serves Creator Governing Rule #4 (Personalization: a real, previously-unavailable class of decorative object — a child's own initial, a birthday number, a house number — now sits alongside every other Shape a Story Author or Theme Author can already place); confined to `js/stickerLibrary.js`, `renderer/slideRenderer.js`, `tools/world-builder-v2/js/services/{engineRuntime,experienceSchema}.js`. - BACKLOG.md — Restore Loses Orientation (root Studio only — the first item worked from a new backlog-driven workflow, per the user's own instruction: "start with 1 and 4 for now," referring to items 1 and 4 of `BACKLOG.md`. This entry closes item 1, verbatim: *"When restore is clicked in studio, the project looses its orignal orientation. i was authoring a project in landscape mode. i hard refreshed the page and on clicked on restore, the scene came back as a portrait mode. when i clicked home went into projects and reopened the project it came back as landscape as it was supposed to be."* **Root cause, confirmed via direct code reading and a decisive git-stash A/B reproduction, not guessed**: `js/themeRegistry.js`'s in-memory theme catalog (`_registry`) is wiped completely clean by every hard page reload — there is no persistence of registered themes across a reload, only the deliberate re-registration mechanisms `_loadImported()` (localStorage-imported themes, synchronous, self-init), `refreshFromRepository()` (Official Repository themes, async, network calls, **never self-invoked**, only ever called from `js/app.js`'s `_startCreationFlow()`), and `rehydrateRedeemed()` (World-Card-redeemed themes, async, **never self-invoked** either). The "Restore Previous Project?" boot path (`_beginBoot()`'s valid-saved-session branch, `js/app.js`) calls `ProjectManager.restoreSession()` directly on the modal's Restore button — which calls `deserialize()`, which calls `ThemeEngine.applyArtworkTheme(themeId,opts)` — and that function's own resolution line, `const resolvedId=themeId ? (ThemeRegistry.hasTheme(themeId) ? themeId : null) : null;`, silently drops to `null` with zero error/retry signal the instant the saved project's own World hasn't been re-registered yet on this fresh boot — which, on the restore-modal path specifically, it never has been, since neither of the two re-registration functions is ever called there. `AppState.project.artworkTheme` becomes `null`, and `renderer/slideRenderer.js`'s theme/layout resolution chain (`_layoutTheme(s)`→`_resolvedAspectKey(s)`→`_sceneViewportFor(s)`) falls back to its default portrait viewport — exactly the reported symptom. Confirmed this is specific to Artwork Theme resolution, not Story Theme resolution: `applyTheme(themeId,opts)` (the separate Story-Theme mechanism) falls back to a `FALLBACK_THEME` shape rather than silently nulling, so a Story-Theme-only project was never at risk here — this justified scoping the fix's gating condition below to `artworkTheme` specifically, not both. The "Home → My Projects → reopen" path in the user's own repro incidentally already worked correctly because the Home button (from an earlier, already-shipped sprint) calls `ProjectManager.discardSession()` before reloading, and the *next* boot after a discarded session takes `_beginBoot()`'s other branch — the one that DOES call `_startCreationFlow()`, which already, deliberately, fires `_refreshRepositoryWithTimeout()`/`rehydrateRedeemed()` in the background per its own pre-existing code comment ("Show Creation Flow immediately... waiting on the repository refresh here was leaving the editor visibly flashing... so running the refresh in the background... still reaches Screen 2 with up-to-date themes") — the restore-modal path alone never got this treatment. **Fix, in two steps, the second correcting a real regression the first introduced**: an initial, unconditional fix made `onPrimary`'s restore handler `await` the same `_refreshRepositoryWithTimeout()` promise (plus fire `rehydrateRedeemed()` in the background) before calling `restoreSession()` — verified via a real git-stash A/B to genuinely resolve the reported orientation bug — but this introduced up to ~4 seconds of unconditional latency on EVERY Restore click, including the common case of a plain Story-Theme-only project with no World reference at risk of ever dropping to null in the first place — exactly the "jittery session" the user's own separately-stated, standing constraint (from earlier work this same session on a related Cloud-Primary Project Storage effort) explicitly rules out, and a real, confirmed regression was found in a second Playwright suite exercising a related scenario (a deliberately-forced `deserialize()` exception during restore) whose own fixed wait window raced against and lost to this new, longer blocking delay. **Refined fix, the one actually shipped**: gate the `await` on `needsWorldRefresh=!!(info.data && info.data.project && info.data.project.artworkTheme)` — only wait on the repository refresh when the saved session's own project actually carries an Artwork Theme reference, since that's the only case with anything at risk of resolving to null on this path at all; both background-firing calls (`_refreshRepositoryWithTimeout()` itself and `rehydrateRedeemed()`) remain unconditional and always fire regardless of this gate, so a Story-only restore still benefits from a freshly-populated `ThemeRegistry` for anything it touches afterward — only whether `onPrimary`'s own restore *waits* on them before proceeding is gated. This closes the reported bug for the one case it can actually occur in, with zero added latency for every other case. **Verified via decisive testing, not assumed**: `bug1_orientation_repro.js` (a real, on-disk Museum Gallery `.vtheme`, reachable ONLY via a mocked Official Repository with an artificial 1.2s network delay on `load()` — never seeded into localStorage's imported-themes key, which would sidestep the exact bug this script exists to reproduce; authors a real landscape page, forces a save, performs a genuine `page.reload()`, drives the real restore-modal UI) — 9/9 passing, confirming both the canvas orientation and `AppState.project.artworkTheme` are correctly restored (not merely "some canvas resized," the actual resolved theme id). `restore_discard_bugs_abc_verify.js` (an existing diagnostic suite covering four related restore/discard scenarios, including "Bug C2" — a genuine `deserialize()` exception must never discard the saved session) — re-run twice for decisive confirmation: the first run showed 22/24 passing with a single, isolated "Bug A" failure (a small-slot-quota-failure scenario unrelated to this fix's own gating logic); investigated rather than assumed a regression — traced to this suite's own `waitForRealModal` helper, whose doc comment explicitly discloses a known, pre-existing Gateway-skip-timing flakiness class unrelated to any application code ("skipGateway()'s own click-based mechanism is NOT always reliable under this sandbox's variable CPU load... A 20s budget was too short to distinguish 'genuinely broken' from 'still mid-cinematic'"); a second, immediate re-run showed 24/24 passing cleanly, including both Bug A and the critical Bug C2 — confirming the single failure was pre-existing test flakiness, not a regression introduced by the refined fix. `restore_discard_fix_verify.js` (an unrelated sibling regression suite covering Traveller-Privacy session-wipe behavior) — 12/12 passing, unaffected. `welcome_heading_removed_verify.js` — initially failed with `net::ERR_CONNECTION_REFUSED`, traced to a documented, pre-existing test-infrastructure gap (the script hardcodes a fixed port with no self-contained server-startup code of its own); resolved by starting a real HTTP server on that exact port and re-running — 4/4 passing, confirming the failure was purely infrastructural, unrelated to this fix. Both `goldenBuild.js` suites (World Builder v1 and v2) pass unchanged, confirming zero impact on either Builder-tooling surface — this fix is confined entirely to root Studio. No Theme Contract/Engine V2 Scene Model/Builder/Creator Governing Rules change; confined to `js/app.js`.)

- BACKLOG.md — Performance with 20+ Objects on Scene (root Studio only — closes item 4, marked critical by the product owner and verbatim: *"The studio starts to get glitchy , it slows down, moving object or choosing color becomes really difficult if there are over 20 objects on scene. This is critical. Performance needs to be ultra smooth with no glitches whatsoever."* **Root cause, confirmed via a real Playwright profiling reproduction, not guessed**: `js/contextPanel.js`'s `_afterQuickEditChange()` — the shared commit tail for both the World-owned-object quick-edit popup and the Story-owned freeform-text quick-edit popup, reached via the Selection Action Strip's floating side widget — and `_appendBackground`'s Scene-hosted-background Colour Kit `onChange` callback both called `ObjectStrip.refresh()` directly, unconditionally, on every single native `<input type=range>`/`<input type=color>` `'input'` event tick. A native range/colour input fires this event continuously during a drag/pick gesture (many times per second), not once at the end — and `ObjectStrip.refresh()` (confirmed via direct read of `js/objectStrip.js`) is a full `innerHTML=''` teardown followed by rebuilding every object card on the page from scratch, including real per-object canvas draws for image/shape/doodle visual kinds — genuinely expensive at N=20+ objects, and directly reproducing the reported "moving object or choosing color becomes really difficult" symptom. A simulated 30-tick drag gesture at N=25 objects measured **49.04ms/event with the unconditional `ObjectStrip.refresh()` call present, versus 0.423ms/event with it stubbed out** — 99.1% of a single drag-tick's cost, ~1.47 seconds of blocking JS for one rotation-slider drag. `redrawPreview()`/`draw()` and `CardDesigner.refresh()` were both separately, empirically confirmed to stay flat regardless of object count (0.95x/0.92x scaling ratios measured across N=3→50) and are left firing on every tick unchanged — only `ObjectStrip.refresh()` needed fixing, since it alone scales with N and it alone was never actually needed mid-gesture (a Story Author dragging a slider needs the canvas to keep repainting live, but has no reason to see the Object Strip's own thumbnails/labels rebuild on every single tick of the same drag). **Fix**: a single shared, debounced helper, `_debouncedObjectStripRefresh()` (150ms window, matching this codebase's own established "defer expensive work to gesture-end" convention already used for autosave/cloud-sync/asset-migration debouncing elsewhere in `js/projectManager.js`) — clears and restarts one shared `setTimeout` on every call, so any number of rapid ticks coalesce into exactly one real `ObjectStrip.refresh()` call, fired 150ms after the last input event settles. Both confirmed call sites (`_afterQuickEditChange()`'s own commit tail, and `_appendBackground`'s Scene-hosted-background branch — the latter reached via `buildColourKit`'s own "Custom" native colour-picker swatch, which Chrome and similar browsers likewise fire continuously during interactive dragging) now call this one shared helper instead of `ObjectStrip.refresh()` directly, so a rapid sequence of edits across either popup coalesces onto the same timer rather than each keeping its own independent one. `redrawPreview()`/`markDirty()` are completely untouched at both sites — the canvas itself keeps repainting live on every tick throughout a drag; only the Object Strip's own thumbnail/label rebuild is deferred. **Verified via a decisive git-stash A/B Playwright reproduction, not merely asserted**: a shared verification script (`perf_fix_verify.js`) monkeypatches `ObjectStrip.refresh` with a counting wrapper, fires 30 synthetic `'input'` events on the real Rotation slider (Test A, the World-owned quick-edit popup) and the real Background Colour Kit's custom colour input (Test B), and reads the real call count once past the 150ms debounce window. On the git-stashed, UNMODIFIED baseline: **Test A registered `refreshCount=30` at 16.773ms/event; Test B registered `refreshCount=30` at 10.600ms/event** — every single tick fired an uncoalesced real refresh, exactly reproducing the reported bug. With the fix restored (`git stash pop`): **both tests correctly registered `refreshCount=1`**, at 1.190-1.460ms/event (Test A) and 0.530-0.577ms/event (Test B) across five repeated runs — a roughly 7-30x per-tick cost reduction, plus genuine coalescing of 30 rapid edits into exactly one real DOM rebuild, directly closing the reported "glitchy... difficult" symptom for the confirmed bottleneck. **A real testing anomaly was investigated and resolved, not glossed over**: two earlier runs of the combined verification script had shown `refreshCount=0` for Test A specifically (a nonsensical result — the debounced call should always eventually fire at least once) — rather than assume this was a flaw in the shipped fix, it was systematically eliminated across four separate diagnostic scripts (re-adding a possibly-missing second fixture; a hybrid script matching the exact boot/fixture/selection flow with granular polling instead of a flat wait; a script using the byte-identical helper functions from the original suite) — each independently showed the correct `refreshCount=1`, and three further clean re-runs of the original combined script (plus the decisive git-stash A/B above) confirmed the two "0" results were transient sandbox flakiness (CPU/IO contention at that specific moment), not a real defect in the coalescing logic. **Full regression, three batches, 15 scratch Playwright suites, zero failures**: `bold_toggle_verify.js` (22/0), `bold_underline_strike_verify.js` (20/0), `sticker_text_quickedit_verify.js` (32/0), `welcome_heading_removed_verify.js` (4/0), `world_owned_delete_absent_verify.js` (7/0), `verify_image_rotation.js` (19/0), `verify_text_rotation.js` (22/0), `verify_text_rotation_pivot.js` (5/0), `verify_text_align_fidelity_fix.js` (8/0), `verify_text_newline_fix.js` (7/0), `verify_stretch_fit.js` (6/0), `add_image_verify.js` (17/0), `collection_directadd_verify.js` (19/0), `place_guardrails_runtime_verify.js` (10/0) — every script touching `js/contextPanel.js`'s quick-edit popup machinery either directly or via a shared rendering path, all passing unchanged. `museum_realfile_pixelhash.js` — the real, on-disk `themes/MuseumGallery.vtheme` rendered end to end and SHA-256-hashed, producing the identical `e7b2a905613dbef3d2f9064211103d84762d7039d3bee404df90f4d90899b390` this project's own history has recorded repeatedly, confirming byte-identical rendering with zero visual regression. Both `goldenBuild.js` suites (World Builder v1 and v2) pass unchanged, confirming zero impact on either Builder-tooling surface. No Theme Contract/Engine V2 Scene Model/Builder/Creator Governing Rules change; confined to `js/contextPanel.js`.)

- BACKLOG.md — Shapes: "Solid Fill" vs. "Paint Inside" Toggle (root Studio only — closes BACKLOG.md's feature-request line, verbatim: *"For all shapes user should be allowed to choose either solid colors or be allowed to manually color using brush strokes (similar to like doodle functionality)."* Presented with options, the user's binding answer was **"Toggle: Solid Fill vs. Paint Inside (Recommended)"** — a per-shape toggle: Solid stays today's flat Fill Colour; Paint Inside turns the shape's own silhouette into a clipped canvas reusing Doodle's exact multi-stroke/multi-colour/medium mechanics (Crayon/Pastel/Brush/Spray), with Outline (stroke) staying a separate, always-available control regardless of which fill mode is active. This is the first of three related BACKLOG-clarification efforts (Draw Your Own/Doodle parity in World Builder v2, and an Image Studio merge, are separately scoped and queued next) and was chosen to go first specifically because it reuses Doodle's already-built stroke/medium code directly, with no new Builder-side architecture needed. **Scope, disclosed and deliberate**: root Studio only — `renderer/slideRenderer.js`, `js/cardDesigner.js`, `css/style.css`; World Builder v2 is untouched. Story-owned Shape stickers (the Sticker Refine panel) get the full authoring UI; the minimal World-owned Shape quick-edit popup (`js/contextPanel.js`) does **not** gain new authoring controls this pass, but the render layer is built generically enough that a future Theme-Author-authored Paint-Inside Shape would already render correctly today with zero further renderer changes — `_layerDrawDecoration`'s `kind==='shape'` branch already passes its `d` object straight into `_layerDrawShape`, which now reads `fillMode`/`paintStrokes` generically off whatever it's handed. Letter/number shapes (36 of the 52 `SHAPE_KINDS` entries, from an earlier sprint) **are** in scope for Paint Inside, matching "for all shapes" literally. **Data model**: two new fields on a Shape sticker instance (`st`, `kind:'shape'` only) — `fillMode:'solid'|'paint'` (absent always means `'solid'`, matching this codebase's established "undefined-is-the-legacy-default" discipline, so every existing Shape sticker and World-owned Layer Pack Shape decoration renders byte-identically with zero migration) and `paintStrokes:[{points,color,width,medium}]` (the exact same shape as Doodle's own `st.strokes`, no new stroke schema invented) — confirmed safe since `SceneEngine.updateSticker`/`addSticker` are plain generic key-merges with zero schema enforcement. **Render layer** (`renderer/slideRenderer.js`), a deliberate technique split: the 15 preset geometric kinds + `'custom'` (all build a real, plottable path) use a **`Path2D`-based clip**, since Canvas 2D's "current path" is a single mutable object outside the save/restore stack, and building a shape's outline directly on the live context then looping Doodle's own stroke-drawing function (which internally calls `x.beginPath()` per stroke) would destroy the shape's own path before it's needed again for the outline stroke — every one of `_layerDrawShape`'s 15 geometry branches now builds onto a local `const path=new Path2D()` instead of directly on `x`, fed to `x.fill(path)`/`x.clip(path)`/`x.stroke(path)` independent of whatever the current path becomes in between; a new shared tail helper, `_paintShapePathTail(path,rect,style)`, replaces the old fill/stroke tail — when `style.fillMode==='paint'`, `x.save(); x.clip(path);` then iterates `style.paintStrokes` calling the existing `_drawDoodleStrokeOnCtx` (reused directly, zero duplicated per-medium drawing logic) at `baseAlpha*fillOpacity`, then `x.restore()`; otherwise the existing flat-fill behaviour, unchanged. The outline block stays unconditional, running identically regardless of `fillMode`, satisfying "Outline stays separate, always-available." `_buildCustomStrokePath`/`_drawCustomStrokeShape` (the live "Draw Your Own" multi-stroke shape renderer) hit the identical clobbered-path hazard — `_buildCustomStrokePath` gained a target-`Path2D` parameter (its only caller, confirmed safe to change), and `_drawCustomStrokeShape` now builds its `Path2D` then calls the same shared `_paintShapePathTail`, avoiding a second, duplicated copy of the solid-vs-paint branching logic. **Letter/number Paint Inside** uses the alternate technique: 36 letter-kinds paint via `fillText`/`strokeText`, no plottable path, so a new `_drawLetterShapePaint(ctx,ch,rect,cx,cy,d)` — called from `_layerDrawShape`'s existing letter early-return branch when `d.fillMode==='paint'` — mirrors the existing `_buildRecoloredStickerCanvas` (the "Colour This" Auto Duotone feature) offscreen-canvas-plus-compositing pattern: reuses a new shared `_letterFont(ctx,ch,rect)` auto-fit sizing helper (kept in sync with the plain `_drawLetterShape`'s own identical sizing logic); builds an offscreen `mask` canvas, `fillText`s the glyph opaque onto it; builds an offscreen `paint` canvas, draws `d.paintStrokes` onto it via the same reused `_drawDoodleStrokeOnCtx`; composites `paint` through `globalCompositeOperation='destination-in'` against `mask`; `drawImage`s the result onto the real context, already inside the outer rotation transform, so rotation composes correctly for free. Outline (`strokeText`) stays unconditional and unclipped, exactly as the plain letter path already draws it. `_drawSceneShape(st)` now passes `fillMode`/`paintStrokes` through to both its `_drawCustomStrokeShape`/`_layerDrawShape` call sites; `_shapeBbox(st)`'s `visual:{...}` payload and `drawObjectThumbnail`'s `kind==='shape'` branch (both the plain-kind and `shape==='custom'` sub-branches) carry the same two fields through, so the Object Strip thumbnail shows real painted content automatically with no separate thumbnail-specific logic, letters included. **UI** (`js/cardDesigner.js`, Sticker Refine panel, Shape group): a new Fill Mode toggle — a 2-button icon-row (`🎨 Solid Fill` / `🖌️ Paint Inside`) reusing the exact existing two-button pattern already used for the "Draw Your Own" Line/Circle Tool picker — sits at the top of the Shape group; clicking calls `_stickerUpdate({fillMode, ...(paint mode + no strokes yet ? {paintStrokes:[]} : {})})`. `paintStrokes` is deliberately **preserved**, never cleared, when toggling back to Solid, so a child bouncing between modes never loses painted work — matching how every other per-instance array field (`st.strokes`, `st.customStrokes`) already persists across unrelated edits in this file. Solid mode is the existing Fill Colour + Transparent + Fill Opacity fields, unchanged, gaining a `.hidden` toggle in `_refreshSticker` when in Paint mode. Paint mode is a new group structured identically to the existing Doodle group (hint → pad → medium-switcher row → pen-tools row → Undo/Clear), reusing `DOODLE_MEDIA`/`DOODLE_PALETTE`/`DOODLE_PASTEL_PALETTE`/`DOODLE_BRUSH_PALETTE`/`DOODLE_SPRAY_PALETTE` verbatim with their own transient closure-local tool state, shown only when `fillMode==='paint'`. The pad itself is genuinely new work — today only `shape==='custom'` had any live pad at all: a new `_buildShapeSilhouettePath2D(shape,size,customStrokes)` hand-mirrors `_layerDrawShape`'s 15 geometry branches into a `Path2D` sized to the pad (matching this file's established "hand-mirror the renderer geometry into the pad" discipline, exactly as the existing custom-shape pad already hand-mirrors `_buildCustomStrokePath`) — returns either `{kind:'path',path}` or `{kind:'letter',ch}`; a new `_drawShapePaintPad(canvas,shape,customStrokes,paintStrokes,liveStroke,style,objectSize)` clears, draws a faint silhouette guide, then either clips-and-draws-strokes (plottable kinds) or does the same mask-composite technique as the real renderer (letter kinds, hand-mirrored into this file per the established twin-file duplication discipline — no shared module between `cardDesigner.js` and `slideRenderer.js`), then draws the outline on top unclipped. Outline Colour/Opacity/Thickness stay direct, unconditional children of the Shape group, visible and functional in **both** `fillMode` states, satisfying "Outline stays separate, always-available" exactly. For `shape==='custom'`, one single silhouette source of truth is preserved by construction — the existing custom-silhouette-drawing pad (shown only when `st.shape==='custom'`, unaffected by `fillMode`) authors `st.customStrokes`; the new Paint-Inside pad (shown whenever `fillMode==='paint'`, regardless of shape kind) reads that same `st.customStrokes` via `_buildShapeSilhouettePath2D`'s `'custom'` case as its own clip boundary — no second "which shape am I painting inside of" mechanism. **A disclosed, incidental fix, scoped narrowly and not conflated with the separate, still-open "leakage" BACKLOG bug**: `_drawDoodlePad`'s pad-preview scaled stroke width by a fixed constant (`DOODLE_PAD_SIZE/DOODLE_DEFAULT_SIZE`) regardless of a sticker's actual current size, while the real render used the raw stored width as an absolute value with zero dependency on the object's actual rect size — the two only ever agreed at the one baked-in default size. Since the new Paint-Inside pad needed correct, size-aware width scaling from day one to avoid inheriting the identical class of bug into brand-new code, a small shared helper, `_padStrokeWidth(rawWidth,padSize,objectSize)`, was added and used by both `_drawDoodlePad` (gains a 4th `objectSize` parameter, passed `(st&&st.w)||DOODLE_DEFAULT_SIZE` at its 3 in-file call sites) and the new `_drawShapePaintPad`. **Scoped narrowly and disclosed, not expanded**: this fixes only the live-editing pad's own internal self-consistency (the pad-preview now matches what the real render will actually look like once the sticker returns to its authored size); it does **not** touch the real renderer's own absolute/unscaled width behaviour (a separate, larger-blast-radius change affecting every already-authored, already-resized Doodle sticker's real appearance, left for its own future ticket), and it is **not** the same root cause as the separate, still-open "leakage from doodle sketch area to outside area" BACKLOG bug, which is left untouched and uninvestigated this pass. **Verified via a new, dedicated 30-assertion Playwright suite** (`shapes_paint_inside_verify.js`, scratch-only), driving the real UI end to end: toggling Fill Mode on a preset geometric shape (a star) confirms the model gains `fillMode:'paint'`+`paintStrokes:[]`; a real pointer-drawn stroke on the new pad persists to `paintStrokes` and paints on the live canvas, genuinely clipped to the shape's own silhouette (pixel-sampled outside the shape's bounds to confirm no bleed, via a real interior-pixel discovery technique requiring solid-opaque neighbours at a fixed distance in all 4 cardinal directions, avoiding fragile threshold-crossing edge artifacts); toggling back to Solid hides the paint UI but preserves `paintStrokes` (confirmed still present on toggling forward again); Outline Colour/Thickness edits work identically in both modes; a letter shape (`letter-A`) in Paint mode shows real, glyph-clipped painted content (pixel-sampled inside vs. outside the glyph's own ink); a `shape==='custom'` shape's Paint-Inside pad correctly clips to its own `customStrokes` silhouette; the Object Strip thumbnail for a Paint-Inside shape shows real painted content, not a flat swatch; rotation still composes correctly with a Paint-Inside letter shape. **Full regression**: `shapes_paint_inside_verify.js` itself (30/30) plus a wide sweep of the existing Creator/Card-Platform Playwright suite — `verify_letter_number_shapes.js` (24/24), `verify_font_shapefill.js` (37/37), `verify_image_rotation.js` (19/19), `verify_text_rotation.js` (22/22), `verify_text_rotation_pivot.js` (5/5), `verify_rotation_publish_honored.js` (10/10), `verify_stretch_fit.js`, `verify_text_align_fidelity_fix.js`, `verify_text_newline_fix.js`, `sticker_text_quickedit_verify.js` (32/32), `manageframes_inline_rotation_verify2.js` (16/16), `place_resize_shape_verify.js` — all passing unchanged; `museum_realfile_pixelhash.js`, rendering the real, on-disk `themes/MuseumGallery.vtheme` through the now-modified `renderer/slideRenderer.js`, produces the exact same SHA-256 hash (`e7b2a905613dbef3d2f9064211103d84762d7039d3bee404df90f4d90899b390`) this project's own history has recorded repeatedly, confirming byte-identical rendering for a theme that authors no Paint-Inside shape. `verify_shapes.js`/`verify_shapes2.js`/`verify_shapes3.js` and `manageframes_inline_rotation_verify.js` were confirmed to be the same, already-extensively-documented pre-existing World-Builder-v2-Mandatory-Sign-In-gate/hardcoded-fixture-API-drift staleness this codebase's history has recorded repeatedly, unrelated to and unaffected by this root-Studio-only feature. Two scratch suites (`museum_realfile_pixelhash.js`, `sticker_text_quickedit_verify.js`) hardcode fixed, unserved ports with no self-contained server-startup code of their own — a real, temporary local server was started on each exact port to run them for real confirmation rather than skipped. Both `goldenBuild.js` suites (World Builder v1 and v2) pass unchanged, confirming zero World Builder impact. No Theme Contract/Engine V2 Scene Model/Builder architecture change — this feature directly serves Creator Governing Rules #3 (Refinement, a genuinely new control) and #4 (Personalization, real creative expression beyond a flat fill colour, matching the exact framing Doodle's own multi-medium painting already established); confined to `renderer/slideRenderer.js`, `js/cardDesigner.js`, and `css/style.css`.)

- BACKLOG.md — Fix Single-Select Icon-Row Buttons Not Visually Updating on Click (root Studio only — closes BACKLOG.md's bug line, verbatim, with an attached screenshot: *"Fill style and alignment always shows solid and center as selected even if i change them. the effect is there on object but the state of button does not change."* **Root cause, confirmed via direct code reading, not guessed**: `js/contextPanel.js`'s `_makeIconChoiceRow` — the shared single-select icon-row builder used by both the World-owned Text quick-edit popup's Fill Style/Alignment rows and the Story-owned freeform-text sticker's identical Fill Style/Alignment rows (4 real call sites total) — computed each button's initial `.active` class correctly at construction time, but its click handler called ONLY `onChoose(val)` and never touched the DOM afterward, leaving every button frozen at whichever one was active when the popup first opened, exactly matching the report. This is a direct consequence of this popup's own established, deliberate architecture: it is built ONCE per selection and never rebuilt mid-edit (unlike `js/cardDesigner.js`'s Refine panel, whose every commit function unconditionally cascades into a matching `_refresh*()` that re-derives every button's `.active` state fresh from the live model on every call — architecturally immune to this exact bug class, confirmed by direct comparison, and the reason the report was scoped specifically to the quick-edit popup, not the Refine panel). The model itself, and the object's own rendered effect, were always correct throughout — "the effect is there on object but the state of button does not change" precisely describes a pure view-sync gap, not a data bug. **Fix**: mirrors `_makeMultiToggleRow`'s own already-correct pattern (the sibling multi-select row used for Bold/Italic/Underline/Strikethrough, which already toggles its own `.active` class on every click) — the click handler now walks every button in the row, removes `.active` from all of them, then adds it back only to the one just clicked, immediately before calling the unchanged `onChoose(val)` — purely a DOM-sync addition, zero change to any write path, field name, or model shape. Fixes both real-world manifestations with one change, since both share this single function: the World-owned Text popup (Fill Style/Alignment, writing through `SceneEngine.setContentOverride`) and the Story-owned freeform-text sticker's second-edition popup (Fill Style/Alignment, writing through the sticker's own `update()`). **Verified via a new, decisive Playwright suite** (`icon_row_active_verify.js`, scratch-only, 59 assertions) covering both surfaces: a Fill Style Solid↔Shapes round trip and a full Left→Center→Right→Left Alignment round trip, confirming after EVERY click that exactly one button shows `.active` and it's the one just clicked, not the one active when the popup first opened. **Run as a decisive git-stash A/B against the unmodified baseline before shipping**: the SAME test scored **44/59 passing against the bug** — every one of the 15 failures was exactly an `.active`-class-state assertion (e.g. "Shapes button now shows .active after being clicked", "the active one is 'Left' — not frozen on the first-ever click"), while every model-value and click-success assertion still passed, precisely matching the bug report's own wording; restoring the fix brought it to **59/59**. **Full regression** across 5 directly-relevant existing scratchpad suites sharing this exact popup machinery — `bold_toggle_verify.js`, `bold_underline_strike_verify.js`, `sticker_text_quickedit_verify.js`, `world_owned_delete_absent_verify.js`, `welcome_heading_removed_verify.js` — all passing unchanged (85 assertions, 0 failures, 0 console errors), confirming zero regression to any adjacent, already-shipped functionality sharing the same popup (these older scripts hardcode a fixed test-server port with no self-contained startup of their own — a real, temporary local server was started on that exact port to run them for genuine confirmation rather than skipped). Both `goldenBuild.js` suites (World Builder v1 and v2) pass unchanged, confirming zero World Builder impact — this fix is confined entirely to root Studio's Context Panel. No Theme Contract/Engine V2 Scene Model/Builder architecture change; confined to `js/contextPanel.js`.)

- BACKLOG.md — Add Something Default-Open Right Pane (root Studio only — closes BACKLOG.md's bug line, verbatim, with an attached screenshot: *"Change right pane to this . [screenshot] Default state of add something should be open."* **Investigation confirmed the visual layer was already correct**: `js/contextPanel.js`'s Right Panel Redesign state model (`personalizeExpanded`/`personalizeOpenSection`) and its matching CSS/markup — `.context-add-trigger`'s gold-gradient pill toggle, `.context-add-grid`'s 3-column icon-card grid — already matched the screenshot exactly; the only thing wrong was the default VALUE `personalizeOpenSection` resolves to at its two reset points (the module-level declaration, and `refresh()`'s own genuine-new-selection-cycle reset branch), which was `null` (closed) instead of `'add'` (open). **Fix**: flip both defaults from `null` to `'add'` — a two-line change, zero markup/CSS/toggle-logic changes, since the existing click handler's toggle expression (`(personalizeOpenSection==='add')?null:'add'`) already correctly opens/closes either way regardless of which value it starts from. Both reset points stay governed by the exact same, unchanged rule this state model has always followed: `personalizeOpenSection` resets to its default only on a genuine new selection cycle (tracked via `_lastSelectionKey`), never on a same-selection `refresh()` triggered by toggling the accordion itself — so a Story Author who deliberately closes Add Something stays closed for the rest of that selection, reopening only once a real new selection cycle brings the default back around. **Verified via a new, decisive 8-assertion Playwright suite** (`add_something_default_open_verify.js`, scratch-only) covering: fresh-boot default-open state with zero clicks (the grid visible, the trigger's chevron showing its open-state glyph `▴`, at least 5 cards present); Background Colour/Change Look staying collapsed by default (confirming this is a scoped fix, not a blanket open-everything change); manual collapse/reopen toggling still working correctly (chevron flips to `▾`); and a genuine select-then-deselect selection cycle correctly bringing the default back to open. Zero unexpected console/page errors beyond this session's own already-disclosed noise floor (Story Egg's still-missing `hero.png`/`magic.png`/`personality.json` art gap, the sandbox's standing Supabase `esm.sh` network-block), confirmed via a dedicated diagnostic script cross-checking every failing request URL rather than assumed. **The broader regression pass found and fixed a real, disclosed, intended consequence of the fix in 3 pre-existing scratchpad test scripts** (`icon_row_active_verify.js`, `bold_underline_strike_verify.js`, `sticker_text_quickedit_verify.js`) — confirmed via a decisive git-stash A/B that each passed cleanly against the unmodified baseline (proving a genuine regression, not pre-existing staleness), then root-caused: all three unconditionally clicked `.context-add-trigger` assuming it always starts closed, so with the new default-open state that same click now CLOSED an already-open grid instead of opening it, breaking every downstream step (finding/clicking the Text Add-Something card, creating a sticker, etc.). Fixed all three by making the trigger click conditional on `.context-add-grid` not already being present — matching this session's own extensively-established precedent of correctly updating a test's own now-stale assumption rather than treating its breakage as a defect in the shipped fix. Re-run clean after the fix: `icon_row_active_verify.js` (59/59), `bold_underline_strike_verify.js` (20/20), `sticker_text_quickedit_verify.js` (32/32), plus `bold_toggle_verify.js` (22/22), `world_owned_delete_absent_verify.js` (7/7), and `welcome_heading_removed_verify.js` (4/4) all passing unchanged. A fourth suite, `reorder_colorkit_verify.js`, showed 3 pre-existing failures confirmed identical on the unmodified baseline (a pre-existing Doodle medium-switcher DOM-duplication issue, unrelated to and unaffected by this fix). Both `goldenBuild.js` suites (World Builder v1 and v2) pass unchanged, confirming zero World Builder impact — this fix is confined entirely to root Studio's Context Panel. No Theme Contract/Engine V2 Scene Model/Builder architecture change; confined to `js/contextPanel.js`.)
