- BACKLOG.md — Add Image Option to Page Background (root Studio only — closes BACKLOG.md's bug line, verbatim: *"Add image option also in background."* The existing Personalize → Page Background control (`js/contextPanel.js`'s `_appendBackground`) only ever let a Story Author pick a flat colour for a page's background fill — no way to use an uploaded picture instead, unlike a Frame or a World-owned Decoration, both of which already support image content. **Fix**: added a Background Type toggle (Colour / Image, via the existing shared single-select `_makeIconChoiceRow` — the same control this file's Fill Style/Alignment rows already use) right above the existing Colour Kit swatch row; picking Image reveals a new `_appendBackgroundImageControls` block — an Upload/Replace Picture button (routed through the established `_storeUploadedAsset` per-module upload adapter, producing a durable `vihu-asset:` reference via `AssetStore.put`, falling back gracefully to a raw `data:` URI on any failure — the identical upload discipline every other image-bearing control in this file already follows), a conditional 0-359° Rotation slider (via the existing `_makeRangeRow`, shown only once a picture is uploaded) and a Remove Picture button (new `.context-btn-danger` styling, mirroring the Selection Action Strip's own destructive-action red-tint convention) that clears the image and reverts the page to its prior/fallback colour fill. On the render side (`renderer/slideRenderer.js`), `_slideBackgroundOverride` now returns `null` whenever `backgroundMode==='image'` (so the old colour-fill code path correctly steps aside), a new `_slideBackgroundImageOverride` resolves `{ref,rotation}` off the override bag, and a new `_drawSlideBackgroundImage` paints the full-page picture via the existing `_layerDrawDecorationImage` helper, reusing its established cover-fit + rotation-around-centre math — zero new drawing primitives invented, matching this codebase's own long-standing "reuse the existing draw routine, thread a new field through" discipline. The two modes are strictly mutually exclusive at the model level (`co.backgroundMode` gates which fields are read), so a page always shows exactly one clear background source with no silent double-render. **Verified end-to-end via a new, dedicated 26-assertion Playwright suite** (`bg_image_verify.js`, scratch-only) driving the real UI — a genuine native-file-chooser upload (not a synthetic call), the toggle switching Colour↔Image with the correct controls shown/hidden at each state, a real mouse-driven Rotation slider drag with before/after canvas pixel sampling confirming the picture visibly rotates, Remove Picture correctly reverting to the prior colour fill (pixel-sampled to confirm), and a full round trip back to Colour mode restoring the original swatch-driven fill — all 26 checks passing, zero console/page errors. **One test-script bug was found and fixed during this pass, not an app bug, disclosed rather than glossed over**: three DOM queries in `bg_image_verify.js` used an exact-string match against a range-row label element (`r.textContent==='Rotation'`), but `_makeRangeRow`'s label div always concatenates the plain label text with a second, live-updating value span as sibling children (e.g. the div's real `textContent` reads `"Rotation0°"`, never bare `"Rotation"`) — confirmed via direct code read of `_makeRangeRow` (`js/contextPanel.js`) that this concatenation is exactly how every other range row in this codebase already renders, not a bug; fixed the test's three query sites to use a starts-with prefix check instead. **Full regression**: `museum_realfile_pixelhash.js` (the real, on-disk `themes/MuseumGallery.vtheme` rendered end to end and SHA-256-hashed, producing the exact `e7b2a905613dbef3d2f9064211103d84762d7039d3bee404df90f4d90899b390` hash this project's history has recorded repeatedly, confirming zero visual/rendering regression), `verify_bg_zorder_fix.js` and `verify_transparent_bg.js` (8/8, confirming the pre-existing background z-order/transparent-fill fallback logic sitting alongside the modified render loop is unaffected), `icon_row_active_verify.js` (59/59, confirming the shared single-select icon-row mechanism the new Background Type toggle reuses works correctly everywhere it's already used), and `welcome_heading_removed_verify.js` (4/4, confirming the Personalize default view / Context Panel structure is unaffected) all pass unchanged, zero console/page errors. No Theme Contract/Engine V2 Scene Model/Builder architecture change; confined to `js/contextPanel.js`, `renderer/slideRenderer.js`, and `css/style.css`.)

- BACKLOG.md — Doodle/Shape Fidelity: Real-Render Leakage Clip + Pad Aspect-Ratio Correction (root Studio only — closes BACKLOG.md's bug line, verbatim, with an attached screenshot: *"Doodle drawn vs doodle shown has differences in line stroke thickness and space covered. also there is leakage from doodle sketch area to outside area. the same is with shape when painted."* Two independent, root-caused defects, both confirmed via direct code reading rather than guessed, and both fixed. **Fix 1 — leakage**: `renderer/slideRenderer.js`'s `_drawSceneDoodle(st)` (the real, Reader/Publish-facing render path for a Doodle sticker) only ever wrapped its drawing in `x.save()/x.restore()` conditionally, when the doodle carried a rotation — and never clipped to its own bounding rect under any circumstance. A stroke's own pen width, especially a wide/round-capped one drawn near the object's own edge, could paint pixels outside the doodle's declared bounding box once it landed on the real, much-larger page canvas — a leak the small, fixed-size pad canvas on the Refine panel can never reproduce, since a browser element boundary is a hard, physical clip by construction. Fixed by always building a `Path2D` rect matching the object's own bounding rect, wrapping the entire draw in `x.save(); ...; x.clip(clipPath); ...; x.restore();` — inside the *same* rotation transform, so the clip rotates along with the drawing exactly as the drawing itself already did — mirroring the identical `save()/clip(path)/…/restore()` idiom already proven correct for Shape's own "Paint Inside" fill (`_paintShapePathTail`, from the earlier Shapes Paint-Inside sprint), rather than inventing a second clipping convention. **Fix 2 — stroke thickness/coverage mismatch**: `js/cardDesigner.js`'s live-editing Refine-panel pad (the small fixed-size square canvas an author actually draws on) normalized every stroke/silhouette point as a flat fraction of the pad's own bare square dimensions (`p.x/PAD_SIZE`), with zero awareness of the real object's own `w:h` aspect ratio — so a non-square Doodle or Shape sticker (the overwhelming common case, since a freshly-created object rarely happens to be perfectly square) drew and normalized against the WRONG proportions on the pad versus what the real renderer, which correctly maps points against the object's own true `w`/`h` box, actually painted — visibly different stroke thickness and covered area between what was drawn and what showed, exactly matching the report. Fixed with a new `_padActiveRect(padSize, objectW, objectH)` helper, computing a letterboxed "active rectangle" within the fixed-size pad canvas that matches the real object's own aspect ratio (`{x,y,w,h,scale}`) — every stroke/silhouette point is now mapped against this active rect instead of the bare full square, via two new helpers, `_shapePaintNormalizePoints`/`_doodleNormalizePoints`, wired into both pads' pointer-event handlers; `_padStrokeWidth(rawWidth,scale)` was simplified to take the precomputed `scale` factor directly (previously computed its own, separately-wrong ratio); a new `_padLetterFont(ctx,ch,w,h)` mirrors the real renderer's own letter/number auto-fit sizing formula for a letter/number Paint-Inside shape's pad preview. Both the Doodle pad and the Shape Paint-Inside pad's plottable-path branch share one real technical subtlety, documented in code: the plottable-path branch sets the canvas clip while a `translate+scale` transform is still active, then resets the transform matrix via `g.setTransform(1,0,0,1,0,0)` WITHOUT undoing the already-applied clip (a clip persists as device-space state through transform changes until the next `restore()`), letting the subsequent freeform paint strokes use simple, direct active-rect point mapping and uniform `active.scale` width scaling rather than inheriting the shape outline's own non-uniform scale factor. Every call site of `_drawDoodlePad`/`_drawShapePaintPad` was updated to pass both the object's real `w` and `h` (previously only implicitly assumed square). **Verified via the full remaining regression matrix, closing out every item left open by the prior window's own fixes**: `manageframes_inline_rotation_verify.js`'s failure (`TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'name')` at `projectStore.js:85:23`, from calling `ProjectStore.create('blank')` with a missing second `generated` argument the real function signature requires) was confirmed, via a decisive git-stash A/B, to reproduce identically on the completely unmodified pre-fix baseline — a pre-existing, unrelated test-script API-drift bug, not a regression from either fix, left as-is (the app's own real `create(templateId, generated)` contract is correct; only this one scratch script calls it wrong). `coloring_kit_verify.js` (a pre-existing Doodle medium-switcher DOM-duplication issue) and `place_resize_shape_verify.js` (transient sandbox flakiness) were independently re-confirmed via the same git-stash A/B technique, earlier in this same effort, to be equally pre-existing and equally unrelated. Two real test-script bugs were found and fixed in `shapes_paint_inside_verify.js` itself during this pass, not app bugs: a missing `require('playwright')` fallback (this sandbox's Playwright install lives outside the default `node_modules` resolution path, matching the established `require('/opt/node22/lib/node_modules/playwright')` fallback convention every other scratch script in this codebase's history already uses) and a stale `openAddSomething()` helper that assumed the "Add Something" accordion always starts closed — a false assumption once the earlier "Add Something Default-Open Right Pane" fix (the entry directly above this one) shipped its own new default-open behaviour; fixed to check for and reuse an already-open grid rather than blindly re-clicking the trigger and accidentally closing it. Re-run clean after both application fixes and both test-script fixes: `shapes_paint_inside_verify.js` (30/30, covering Fill Mode toggling, a real pointer-drawn Paint-Inside stroke genuinely clipped to the shape's own silhouette, preserved-across-toggle `paintStrokes`, Outline controls working in both Fill Mode states, a letter shape's glyph-clipped paint, a `shape==='custom'` shape's silhouette-clipped pad, Object Strip thumbnail fidelity, and rotation composing correctly with a Paint-Inside letter shape) — zero regressions from either fix. **Full regression**: `tools/world-builder/verify/goldenBuild.js` and `tools/world-builder-v2/verify/goldenBuild.js` both PASS cleanly (World Builder's own compile/validate/import pipeline is completely untouched by a root-Studio-only fix); `verify_image_rotation.js` (19/0), `verify_rotation_publish_honored.js` (10/0), `verify_text_rotation.js` (22/0), and `verify_text_rotation_pivot.js` (5/0) all pass unchanged, confirming the rotation-under-clip transform interplay Fix 1 touches composes correctly with every other rotation-aware render path already shipped; `manageframes_inline_rotation_verify2.js` (16/0) passes unchanged, confirming World Builder's own Manage-Frames-inline rotation feature (a sibling, unrelated consumer of the same rotation-transform conventions) is unaffected. No Theme Contract/Engine V2 Scene Model/Builder architecture change; confined to `renderer/slideRenderer.js` and `js/cardDesigner.js`.)

- World Card Platform — Front Card Face Displayed an Incomplete, Unmatchable Redemption Code (a real, user-reported bug: *"typing world card code or drawing its sky always give incorrect warning. only copying the code and pasting works. can you check that."* **Investigated the full redemption pipeline before assuming a cause**: `js/cardPlatform.js` (`generate()`/`redeem()`), `js/creationFlow.js`'s redeem widget (the 10×10 tap-grid plus its typed-code fallback), and `supabase/schema.sql`'s `redeem_card()` RPC. Confirmed `cards.code` is a Postgres GENERATED column — `'BC-' || lpad(serial_no::text,5,'0')`, an admin-facing display id (e.g. "BC-00125") — and confirmed `redeem_card()`'s own typed-code comparison expects a COMPLETELY DIFFERENT string: `upper(constellation || lpad(serial_no::text,5,'0'))` (e.g. "ORION00125", constellation name concatenated directly with the zero-padded serial, no separator), after normalizing the typed input by stripping whitespace/dashes. `tools/world-builder-v2/js/worldBuilderApp.js`'s own `_cardDisplayCode(card)` helper already builds exactly this correct value, and both the printed card's Back face and Builder's own minted-card list already called it — but the Front face's own code line called `ctx.fillText(card.code || '', ...)` directly, printing the raw, incomplete "BC-00125" with no constellation prefix at all. A player reading the Front face and typing exactly what it showed could never redeem — "BC00125" (after normalization) can never match "ORION00125" — while copying the CORRECT value from the Back face or the minted-card list (both already right) worked, exactly matching "only copying the code and pasting works." **Fix**: changed the Front face's one `fillText` call from `card.code || ''` to `_cardDisplayCode(card)`, the same helper the other two correct surfaces already use — all three now agree byte-for-byte on what a player should type. **Investigated, and ruled out via direct re-reading, several other possible causes for the SEPARATE, still-unresolved half of the report** ("drawing its sky always gives incorrect warning," i.e. tapping the constellation pattern): `_placeConstellation`'s random rotation/mirror/translation is mathematically bounds-safe, every point guaranteed to stay within the 10×10 field; the tap-grid's row/col axis convention in `js/creationFlow.js` matches the card-back drawing's own row/col mapping exactly, ruling out an orientation mismatch; `_card_platform_sort_pattern`'s order-independent set comparison is structurally correct on fresh re-read; `_mapCardRow` and every client-side `redeem()`/`submitCode()` call perform zero unexpected data transformation. **No root cause was found in the checked-in code for the pattern-tap half of the report — disclosed honestly, not silently claimed fixed.** The most likely remaining explanation, given this sandbox cannot reach a live Supabase project to test against directly, is that the live, deployed database may be running an older version of `redeem_card()`/`_card_platform_sort_pattern()` than what's currently checked into `supabase/schema.sql` — every schema.sql change in this project's history has been a disclosed, unexecuted script requiring the project owner to manually re-run it, and this may be one of those cases; alternatively, more specific reproduction detail (the exact error text, whether this happens on every card or a specific one) would help narrow it further. No Theme Contract/Engine V2 Scene Model/Creator Governing Rules change; confined to one `fillText` call in `tools/world-builder-v2/js/worldBuilderApp.js`.)

- BACKLOG.md — Bugs 1, 4, 6 Shipped Together: Colour Kit in the Doodle/Paint Pads + a Case-Sensitivity Fix, Lowercase Letter Shapes, Background Colour+Image Coexistence (closes exactly the three BACKLOG.md "## Bugs" items the user authorized with **"start with 1,4,6"** — Bugs 2/5 and the Image Studio feature request remain explicitly unstarted, and Bug 3 was explicitly dropped by the user. **Bug 1** — verbatim: *"Color change swatch should be made available where ever colors are used. a standard rainbow color circle should be used for color picker. Doodle area does not have color picker."* Two parts, both in `js/cardDesigner.js`: (a) the Doodle pad's and the Shape Paint-Inside pad's hand-built `.doodle-pen-swatch` button grids — the last two colour surfaces still not using the already-shipped shared Colour Kit widget — are replaced with real `buildColourKit(...)` calls, rebuilt per medium via the existing `_rebuildDoodleSwatches`/`_rebuildShapePaintSwatches` against each medium's own curated palette, so both pads finally get the rainbow-conic-gradient "Custom" native picker alongside their swatches; colour ownership moves entirely into the widget (the two old separate active-class sync loops in `_syncDoodlePenUI`/`_syncShapePaintPenUI` are removed as now-redundant). (b) A real, previously-invisible case-sensitivity defect found and fixed inside `buildColourKit`'s own `_sync()`: `_safeColorHex` always lowercases its output while every palette array and every swatch's own `data-color` attribute in this codebase uses uppercase hex digits — direct string comparison could never match, permanently misreporting a genuine palette colour as "custom." Fixed via a lowercased `paletteLower` comparison copy inside the widget itself, deliberately without touching `_safeColorHex`, so every other caller of that helper stays byte-identical. **Bug 4** — verbatim: *"In shapes for all letters add lowercase also."* 26 new lowercase `letter-a`…`letter-z` entries added to both `SHAPE_KINDS` catalogs — `js/stickerLibrary.js` (root Studio) and `tools/world-builder-v2/js/services/experienceSchema.js` (World Builder v2), kept in lockstep per this pair's established discipline — with all 26 uppercase entries untouched. Zero renderer changes were needed anywhere, confirmed rather than assumed: `_shapeLetterChar`'s `kind.slice(7)` already preserves whatever case the value string carries, and the browser's own font rendering already draws any single character — a descender character (`letter-g`) was specifically live-verified to render real, non-clipped content. **Bug 6** — verbatim: *"Color and Image can co-exist in background. color is always behind the image not in front. Rename Background color section to Background. The image uploaded need to pass through image studio and also need to support all options which other images objects have got."* `js/contextPanel.js`'s `_appendBackground` is rewritten: the old mutually-exclusive Background Type toggle (Colour/Image mode, `co.backgroundMode`) — shipped by the earlier "Add Image Option to Page Background" sprint — is removed outright, and the Colour Kit row plus the Picture controls now always render together, unconditionally; the tile is renamed "🎨 Background"; Upload now routes through the real `PictureStudio.open(file,{defaultMode:'fill',onApply:...})` pass instead of a raw `FileReader`; a new "✂️ Crop / Rotate" button (shown only once a picture exists) re-opens the existing picture in Picture Studio, threading `fallbackOwnerId:slide.recallOwnerId` per `_cropRotateArtwork`'s established cross-owner Magic-Card-recall pattern; a new Opacity slider (0-100%) joins the existing Rotation slider, with both preserved across a Crop/Rotate re-apply via the shared `_applyBackgroundImageResult` completion callback. `renderer/slideRenderer.js`: `_slideBackgroundOverride`/`_slideBackgroundImageOverride` both drop their `backgroundMode` gates — each now resolves purely on whether its own field is set — and `_drawSlideBackgroundImage` passes the new `opacity` through as `alpha` to the existing `_layerDrawDecorationImage`; "colour is always behind the image" is guaranteed structurally by `render(s)`'s own unchanged draw order (the base colour fill paints early, the background image paints later), never by any new z-order mechanism. `co.backgroundMode` is left as an inert, never-again-written legacy field on any already-saved project. The World-owned Scene-hosted-background branch (`_sceneHostedBackgroundObject`) is untouched and still shows only its own Colour control, verified unaffected. **Verified** via two dedicated Playwright suites: `bug146_verify.js` (34/34 — static catalog checks on both surfaces; live lowercase-letter rendering including the descender case; the Doodle and Shape-Paint Colour Kits end to end, including a real mouse-drawn stroke whose persisted colour matches the swatch picked, the initial default swatch correctly showing `.active` before any pick — the exact symptom the case-sensitivity bug produced — and a per-medium palette rebuild) and `bug6_bg_coexist_verify.js` (31/31 — coexistence with the colour visibly behind the image, z-order/opacity/remove all pixel-sampled at a topCenter point chosen after an 11-point grid diagnostic (`debug_bg6_pixels.js`) confirmed the canvas's exact geometric center is permanently occupied by Museum Gallery's own Place mat fill, a test-geometry artifact rather than an app bug; the Picture Studio pass exercised for both Upload and Crop/Rotate through the real `.picture-studio-apply-btn`; Opacity at 50% pixel-verified; Remove Picture reverting to the pure colour fill; the hostedBg branch unaffected). **Full regression**: `shapes_paint_inside_verify.js` 30/30, `verify_font_shapefill.js` 37/37, `icon_row_active_verify.js` 59/59, `sticker_text_quickedit_verify.js` 32/32, `verify_transparent_bg.js` 8/8, `doodle_shape_aspect_verify.js` 26/26, `add_something_default_open_verify.js` 8/8, `place_resize_shape_verify.js` zero failures, `verify_bg_zorder_fix.js` (a diagnostic script, correct expected output), and both `goldenBuild.js` suites (World Builder v1 and v2) PASS unchanged. `verify_letter_number_shapes.js`'s two exact-26-letter-count assertions were corrected to 52 (26 upper + 26 lower — the disclosed, intended consequence of Bug 4, not a weakening), passing 24/24 after. **Three stale suites disclosed rather than patched, each conclusively attributed**: `reorder_colorkit_verify.js` — confirmed via a decisive git-stash A/B to fail and crash byte-for-byte identically on the completely unmodified baseline (a pre-existing Doodle-kind card-selection issue plus a not-visible deselect-button crash), unrelated to this batch; `coloring_kit_verify.js` — its duplicated-DOM failures (8 medium buttons, 16 swatches) and its line-181 crash also confirmed via git-stash A/B to reproduce identically on the baseline (the same pre-existing medium-switcher DOM-duplication staleness already documented for its sibling), while its `.doodle-pen-swatch` swatch-reading assertions are additionally superseded by Bug 1's own intended widget swap (the swatch class is now the Colour Kit's own `.colour-kit-swatch`) — its substantive Part A render-algorithm pixel checks (legacy/crayon/pastel/brush distinctness and taper) pass identically on both sides, and since the suite already crashes on the baseline anyway, updating its selectors would not make it pass; `bg_image_verify.js` — asserts the old mutually-exclusive Background Type toggle that Bug 6's own request explicitly required removing, fully superseded by `bug6_bg_coexist_verify.js` as this surface's up-to-date coverage. No Theme Contract/Engine V2 Scene Model/Builder architecture change; confined to `js/cardDesigner.js`, `js/contextPanel.js`, `js/stickerLibrary.js`, `renderer/slideRenderer.js`, and `tools/world-builder-v2/js/services/experienceSchema.js`.)

- BACKLOG.md — Batch 2 (Bug G): Curved Text End to End (root Studio Story-owned freeform + World-owned quick-edit + World Builder v2 Text Experience; both rendering engines kept in lockstep) (closes BACKLOG.md's Batch 2 per the standing "keep going on auto" instruction — verbatim: *"For texts allow these curves"*, with an attached screenshot of arc-shaped text. Every Text object across all three authoring surfaces can now be arced/curved on top of every existing typography/rotation/opacity control, symmetric across the whole platform. **World Builder v2 authoring**: `experienceSchema.js` defaults `textCurve:0` in `defaultUniversalContent()` and includes it in `PART_FIELD_KEYS.text` (matching how every other typography field is declared alongside its own default); `projectModel.js`'s `_syncUniversalContent` text mirror block writes `props.textCurve` onto the mirrored Scene Layer's `.curve` field, so every Text Experience's compiled Layer carries the value through to Build; `worldBuilderApp.js`'s Text content Inspector exposes a real Curve slider (`_buildFieldGroup('Curve', _range(-180, 180, props.textCurve||0, onProp('textCurve')))`), paired the same way every other Text Inspector field already is. **Publish Fidelity (Creator Governing Rule #5)**: `builder.js`'s `convergeSceneLayer` text branch carries `layer.curve` through to the compiled `text.curve` field on the Layer Pack entry; root Studio's `renderer/slideRenderer.js`'s `_layerDrawText` reads `ov.curve || t.curve || 0` (the tri-state precedence — Story-Author override wins over Theme-Author compiled base — matching every other typography field on the same object), then dispatches to `_drawCurvedTextLine` (per-character arc math: `radius = textWidth / |arcRad|`; each character's position and rotation derived from its midpoint offset from center). **Studio quick-edit popups**: the World-owned Text popup gained a Curve slider in an earlier turn of this same effort (via `setContentOverride(slide, sceneObj.id, 'curve')`); this ship completes the pair by adding the identical control to the Story-owned freeform text sticker's quick-edit popup — `js/contextPanel.js`'s `_appendStickerTextEditControl` now pairs Spin with Curve via `_pairRow`, writing `st.curve` via `SceneEngine.updateSticker`'s shallow-merge (the same write path Spin already uses — freeform text stickers own their own top-level fields, unlike World-owned text objects which use `setContentOverride`). **Both rendering engines mirrored in lockstep**: `engineRuntime.js`'s `_paintLayer` (World Builder Working View/Runtime Preview) dispatches to its own arc-math draw path when curve is non-zero; `renderer/slideRenderer.js`'s `_drawFreeformText` (Story-owned freeform stickers) reads `st.curve` for the same reason. **Verified 20/20 assertions via `batch2_bug_g_verify.js`**: (P1) World Builder schema/Adapter/Inspector source-level checks confirm `textCurve:0` default, `PART_FIELD_KEYS.text` inclusion, and a real end-to-end mirrored `layer.curve === 60` for a 60° authored value, plus a source-level Inspector control check (`_buildFieldGroup('Curve', _range(-180, 180, props.textCurve...`); (P2) Publish Fidelity — a real `ProjectCompiler.runBuild()` produces exactly one compiled text Layer with `text.curve === 60` reaching the `.vtheme` package; (P3) root Studio Reader-facing renderer — `SlideRenderer.render(s)` driven with a compiled text Layer Pack entry using the exact `anchor:'top-center'`+`rect:{x:0.1,y:0.3,w:0.8,h:0.4}` shape `builder.js` produces (not a synthetic `{x,y}` anchor object, which would have crashed `layerEngine.js`'s `resolveAnchor` — a real test-methodology bug found and fixed by matching the actual production data shape rather than assumed) draws real curved text with a decisively bowed baseline (curved column-sample range 82px; straight-baseline range within a sampling-noise band well under; curved > straight + 10px margin); (P4) `contextPanel.js` source-level checks for BOTH World-owned Text (`SceneEngine.setContentOverride(slide, sceneObj.id, 'curve', ...`) AND Story-owned freeform Text (`update({curve:Math.round(n)})`) controls reachable. **Full regression**: both `goldenBuild.js` suites (World Builder v1 and v2) PASS unchanged, confirming zero impact on the compile/validate/publish pipeline outside this feature's own additive fields. Batches 3–5 (F+A, H, C) remain queued; Bug B (companion blank circle) explicitly dropped per prior scope decision. No Theme Contract/Engine V2 Scene Model/Creator Governing Rules change; confined to `tools/world-builder-v2/js/services/experienceSchema.js`, `tools/world-builder-v2/js/projectModel.js`, `tools/world-builder-v2/js/worldBuilderApp.js`, `tools/world-builder-v2/js/services/builder.js`, `tools/world-builder-v2/js/services/engineRuntime.js`, `renderer/slideRenderer.js`, and `js/contextPanel.js`.)

- BACKLOG.md — Bug 4: Image Option in Frame Styles (root Studio's Reader-facing renderer + World Builder v2 authoring, kept in lockstep) (closes BACKLOG.md's Bugs item, verbatim: *"Add image option in frame styles in builder"* — parallel to Feature 1's existing Mat Surface = Image support. Frame Style (the ornament choice: none/white-mat/floating/wood/polaroid/tape/bulletin-board) gains a new `'image'` value backed by two additive fields, `frameOrnamentImage` and `frameOrnamentImageRotation`, structurally distinct from Feature 1's `frameImage` (which fills the mat/background band): each renders in its own pipeline stage, both can coexist independently on one Frame Variation, both externalize into their own distinct compiled relPath (`frames/<id>-image.png` vs. `frames/<id>-ornament.png`) so an unmatched pair never collides in `package_.assets`. **Data model** (`tools/world-builder-v2/js/projectModel.js`): `_ensureFrameFieldDefaults` reconciles both new fields to `null`/`0` for every already-authored Frame; `_defaultFrameFields()` seeds them alongside every other Frame default. **Engine Adapter** (`tools/world-builder-v2/js/services/builder.js`): `_externalizeFrameVariationImages` refactored into a shared `externalizeField(fieldName, fallbackSuffix, frame)` inner function called once for `frameImage` (suffix `-image`) and once for `frameOrnamentImage` (suffix `-ornament`), preserving the existing Collection-dedup-first / defensive-per-Frame-relPath-fallback discipline byte-for-byte for `frameImage` while adding identical treatment for the new field — additive per-file relPath fallbacks (never a shared collision key) so both fields hydrate independently on a Frame carrying both. **Builder authoring** (`tools/world-builder-v2/js/worldBuilderApp.js`): Frame Style dropdown gains `{value:'image', label:'Image'}` after `bulletin-board`; picking Image triggers a full `_renderFramesPanel()` re-render (via the same wrapped `onChange` convention `background`'s dropdown already used); an `f.frame==='image'` conditional block mirrors the pre-existing `f.background==='image'` block field-for-field — a `_renderCollectionPickerCore` for `frameOrnamentImage` with a matching `registerCollectionAsset` hook, plus a 0-359° Rotation slider for `frameOrnamentImageRotation`. **Builder preview** (`tools/world-builder-v2/js/services/engineRuntime.js`): `FRAME_ORNAMENT_PRESET` gains `'image':{cornerRadius:0}` (any rounding comes from the picture itself, not this preset); `_paintFrameOrnament(...)` gains a new `style==='image'` branch resolving `fields.frameOrnamentImage` via the injected `graph.resolveLayerImage` callback (matching the exact pattern the mat-band `frameImage` branch already uses), drawing onto the border band's own rect (`{marginPx inset from rect}`) with a rotation-around-band-centre transform and a fixed cover-fit, isolated in its own save/clip/restore so no downstream ornament cue leaks into it — the branch returns early on completion since the picture ornament stands on its own. **Publish Fidelity (Creator Governing Rule #5)** — root Studio's `renderer/slideRenderer.js`: `ARTWORK_FRAME_PRESET` gains `'image':{design:'image',cornerRadius:0}`; `_drawPictureFrameOrnament`'s switch gains a `case 'image': return _ornamentImage(rect,border);` branch; the new `_ornamentImage(rect,border)` reads `art.frameOrnamentImage`/`.frameOrnamentImageRotation` (which ride through `_resolveArtworkFields`' existing `Object.assign(merged, variation.fields)` automatically, needing no field-list update), resolves the src through the same `ThemeRegistry.resolveAssetRef` → `_ensureDecorationImage` chain the mat-band `hasImageBg` path already uses, clips to the frame's own outer path via `_frameFillPath` (so the ornament genuinely stays on the frame area, not the interior artwork), applies rotation around rect centre, and cover-fits. **A real, previously-invisible rendering defect found and fixed at all three image-cover call sites in `_drawPictureFrameFill`/`_ornamentImage`**: naive cover-fit `scale=Math.max(rect.w/iw,rect.h/ih)` under-covers a rotated rect's own corners once rotation≠0, since the rotated rect's own AABB in the image's frame is `w'=w*|cosθ|+h*|sinθ|`/`h'=w*|sinθ|+h*|cosθ|`, not the axis-aligned `w`/`h`. A new shared helper, `_rotationCoverScale(rectW,rectH,iw,ih,rotationDeg)`, returns exactly `Math.max(rectW/iw,rectH/ih)` when `rotationDeg` is falsy (byte-for-byte no-op for every existing Frame with no rotation ever authored), and the rotation-aware `max(w'/iw,h'/ih)` otherwise. Applied identically at the mat-band picture (`hasImageBg`), the border picture (`hasBorderImageBg`), and the new ornament picture (`_ornamentImage`) — all three cover-fit call sites in this file now stay correct at any rotation, closing the exact bug that would have exposed whatever was drawn beneath (the mat-band picture, for the ornament's own test case) at rect corners for any rotated Frame image. **Verified 24/24 via `bug4_frame_ornament_image_verify.js`** at the original 700ms wait (fix is at the source, not a timing workaround) — a Frame with both Mat Surface = Image (magenta) AND Frame Style = Image (green) at 45° rotation now correctly shows green at the ornament's tested corner coordinates instead of magenta bleeding through from the mat picture beneath. **Full regression**: both `goldenBuild.js` suites (World Builder v1 and v2) PASS unchanged; `museum_realfile_pixelhash.js` produces the exact `e7b2a905613dbef3d2f9064211103d84762d7039d3bee404df90f4d90899b390` SHA-256 hash this project's own history has recorded repeatedly (Museum Gallery authors no rotated ornament image, so the rotation-cover fix is a byte-for-byte no-op there); `feature1_frameimage_verify.js` 18/18, `manageframes_inline_rotation_verify2.js` 16/16, `verify_image_rotation.js` 19/19, `verify_rotation_publish_honored.js` 10/10, `verify_stretch_fit.js` PASS, `verify_simplify_place_frame.js` 57/57, `verify_transparent_bg.js` 8/8 — every rotation/cover-fit/frame-adjacent suite passes unchanged. No Theme Contract/Engine V2 Scene Model/Creator Governing Rules change; confined to `tools/world-builder-v2/js/projectModel.js`, `tools/world-builder-v2/js/services/builder.js`, `tools/world-builder-v2/js/services/engineRuntime.js`, `tools/world-builder-v2/js/worldBuilderApp.js`, and `renderer/slideRenderer.js`.)

- Bug G Rework — Curve Style Picker (None/Arc/Wave/Circle) + Gated Amount Slider, End to End (a direct product refinement on the just-shipped Batch 2 Bug G — replaces the single "Curve" amount slider with a Curve **Style** picker (`None` / `Arc` / `Wave` / `Circle`) paired with an Amount slider that's DISABLED when style is `None` or `Circle` (Circle deliberately ignores amount, wrapping a full 360° at `radius = textWidth / (2π)`). Every Text object across all three authoring surfaces + both rendering engines now supports all four styles symmetrically, on top of every existing typography/rotation/opacity control. **Data model**: `tools/world-builder-v2/js/services/experienceSchema.js`'s `defaultUniversalContent()` adds `textCurveStyle:'none'` alongside the existing `textCurve:0`, and `PART_FIELD_KEYS.text` includes it — matching how every other typography field is already declared with both a default and a part-key entry. **Engine Adapter**: `projectModel.js`'s `_syncPartLayer` text branch writes `curveStyle:props.textCurveStyle||'none'` onto the mirrored Scene Layer's `.curveStyle` field alongside the existing `.curve` write. **Publish Fidelity (Creator Governing Rule #5)**: `services/builder.js`'s `convergeSceneLayer` text branch carries `layer.curveStyle` through to the compiled `text.curveStyle` field on the Layer Pack entry alongside the existing `text.curve`. **Both engines mirrored in lockstep**: `services/engineRuntime.js` (Builder Working View/Runtime Preview) and `renderer/slideRenderer.js` (Studio Reader/Publish-facing) each expose the same `_drawStyledTextLine(ctx, text, x, y, style, amount, drawGlyphFn)` dispatcher routing to `_drawCurvedTextLine` (`'arc'`, per-character radial layout — the existing algorithm, preserved unchanged), `_drawWaveTextLine` (`'wave'`, `amplitude=|amount|*0.3` in pixels, sign flips direction, glyphs stay upright — same amplitude formula used by both engines), or `_drawCircleTextLine` (`'circle'`, full 360° wrap at `radius=totalWidth/(2π)`, glyphs rotate tangentially so they read correctly around the ring, amount deliberately ignored). BBox expansion per style: arc adds sagitta, wave adds `±amplitude`, circle expands to a `2*radius` square. **Shape-Mosaic Fill Style now dispatched through the shared drawStyledLine helper** so curve applies to it too — previously silently skipped, since the pre-Rework code drew mosaic-filled text through a separate code path that never checked curve. **A carefully-designed two-layer resolution system honours the difference between explicit None and legacy backward-compat**: the CALLER side (`_layerDrawText` in slideRenderer, `_paintLayer` text branch in engineRuntime, `_drawFreeformText` for freeform stickers) computes `isCurvedActive = curveStyle && curveStyle !== 'none' && (curveStyle === 'circle' || amount !== 0)` and short-circuits to the plain drawText path when false — so a Theme Author's explicit "None" choice is genuinely honoured even if the amount field happens to be nonzero, never re-derived to arc from the raw amount value. The DISPATCHER side's `effectiveStyle` fallback (`(curveStyle && curveStyle !== 'none') ? curveStyle : (amount ? 'arc' : 'none')`) is reached only when a caller doesn't gate — which covers backward compat for a pre-Rework compiled Theme carrying `curve:60` with no `curveStyle` at all, correctly resolving to arc. **UI**: `worldBuilderApp.js`'s Text Inspector exposes a `TEXT_CURVE_STYLE_CHOICES` select paired with the existing Amount slider via the standard `_fieldRow` layout; both `js/contextPanel.js` quick-edit popups (World-owned Text via `_appendWorldTextEditControl` and Story-owned freeform Text via `_appendStickerTextEditControl`) got the identical Style picker + gated Amount via `_makeIconChoiceRow`+`_makeRangeRow`, with a matching `syncAmountDisabled`/`syncStAmountDisabled` closure toggling the Amount slider's `disabled` state whenever Style changes to/from None/Circle — so the UI matches the render-side gate exactly, closing the loop between what a Story Author sees enabled and what actually affects the render. **Verified 44/44 assertions via `bug_g_rework_verify.js`**: P1 confirms schema defaults + PART_FIELD_KEYS inclusion; P1b confirms the Adapter mirrors both `curveStyle` and `curve` onto the Scene Layer; P2 confirms a real `ProjectCompiler.runBuild()` produces a compiled Layer Pack entry with both `text.curveStyle` and `text.curve` reaching the `.vtheme`; P3 confirms both engines' source-level dispatcher + per-style helpers; P4 confirms the backward-compat two-layer resolution — explicit None with nonzero amount correctly resolves to none via the caller-side gate, absent curveStyle with nonzero amount correctly resolves to legacy arc via the dispatcher fallback; P5 confirms distinct pixel signatures in the Studio Reader-facing renderer (`none` draws a flat 38px-tall baseline band, `arc` bows to 63px, `wave` undulates to 73px, `circle` wraps text as 5 separately-sampled columns each hitting different Y positions, legacy `curve:60` with no curveStyle matches the arc render exactly, and arc vs wave differ by ≥10px in vertical extent); P6 confirms all 3 authoring surfaces (v2 Inspector + both quick-edit popups) render the Style picker + wire the amount-disable gate correctly; P7 confirms Shape-Mosaic Fill Style is now dispatched through `_drawStyledTextLine` in both text renderers, no longer silently skipping curve. **P4's own test methodology was corrected mid-implementation, not glossed over**: an early version tested only the dispatcher's `effectiveStyle` in isolation, which for `('none', 60)` correctly returns `'arc'` (the intended backward-compat fallback) — but this by-design behaviour would have wrongly failed a test asserting the *system* honours explicit None. Fixed by making the test replicate BOTH layers of the production system (the caller-side `isCurvedActive` gate short-circuits `('none', 60)` to bypass the dispatcher entirely, correctly producing an overall "none" outcome), matching how the two layers actually compose end to end rather than testing one layer in isolation. **Full regression**: both `goldenBuild.js` suites (World Builder v1 and v2) PASS unchanged, confirming zero impact on the compile/validate/publish pipeline outside this feature's own additive `curveStyle` field. Ship-order committed for the remaining BACKLOG.md items: Bug G Rework → Bug 4 (Image in Frame Styles) → Add more Places to a Scene → Place rotation → Bug 2 (Draw-Your-Own parity port from Studio into Builder v2). No Theme Contract/Engine V2 Scene Model/Creator Governing Rules change; confined to `tools/world-builder-v2/js/services/experienceSchema.js`, `tools/world-builder-v2/js/projectModel.js`, `tools/world-builder-v2/js/worldBuilderApp.js`, `tools/world-builder-v2/js/services/builder.js`, `tools/world-builder-v2/js/services/engineRuntime.js`, `renderer/slideRenderer.js`, and `js/contextPanel.js`.)

- BACKLOG.md — Place Rotation (both surfaces; the whole Place rotates as one unit) (closes BACKLOG.md ship-order task #552, verbatim: *"Place rotation (both surfaces)."* A Place is now genuinely rotatable — its chrome (border/mat/ornament/caption/Place-1 Layer Packs) AND every Place-hosted Layer rotate together as one unit around the Place's own centre, exactly as if a printed physical picture on a wall were tilted. Never a per-Layer rotation on top of a still-axis-aligned Place, since that would let a Place-hosted background image go crooked while its own frame stayed straight, a physically-impossible reading. **New rotatable Guardrail** (`tools/world-builder-v2/js/projectModel.js`), defaults CLOSED — matching `resizable`'s own convention from the earlier Place Resize + Shape sprint, opposite to `editable`/`moveable`/`visible`'s OPEN default — so no already-published Theme silently gains a Story-Author rotation control it never authored. `_ensureHolderDefaults` reconciles `holder.permissions.rotatable` (default `false`) on read; `_resolvePlacePermissions` (`renderer/slideRenderer.js`) reads `!!p.rotatable` from a compiled `placeRects[i].rotatable` — a `false` (or absent) permission genuinely hides every Story-Author-facing rotation control. **Data model** (Story-Author override wins over Theme-Author base, matching every other rotation-aware field on the platform): `slide.metadata.elementOverrides[placeId].rotation`, written via `SceneEngine.setContentOverride`; a Theme-Author-authored `placeRects[i].rotation` (compiled from `holder.rotation`) is the base; a caller-side `rotationDeg = (ov !== null) ? ov : base` resolution is the same tri-state precedence every existing rotation surface (`_layerDrawText`/`_paintLayer`/`_layerDrawDecorationImage`) already uses. **Rendering — both engines mirrored in lockstep**: `renderer/slideRenderer.js`'s `_drawPlaceOne` (Studio Reader/Publish-facing) wraps the whole reorderable-loop entry (lines 3800-3835) in the established `ctx.save(); ctx.translate(cx,cy); ctx.rotate(deg*Math.PI/180); ctx.translate(-cx,-cy); …; ctx.restore();` idiom around the Place's own centre — the artwork/ornament/caption pipeline all rotate together; separately, Place 1's mat/fill/panel drawn ONCE outside the loop (lines 3681-3686) also rotates when rotation is present, so the wall/mat rotates in lockstep with everything inside it rather than snapping off. `tools/world-builder-v2/js/services/engineRuntime.js`'s `_paintHolder` (Builder Working View/Runtime Preview) wraps the same chrome+content in the identical transform — the two rendering engines share no drawing module, so this discipline is maintained by hand per this codebase's own established twin-engine precedent. **Compile step** (`tools/world-builder-v2/js/services/builder.js`): `convergeScene` carries `holder.permissions.rotatable` (absent → false, matching the CLOSED-by-default rule established for `resizable` in an earlier sprint) AND `holder.rotation` (absent → 0) onto the compiled `layouts[i].placeRects[i]` — additive fields riding the exact same convention every other Place permission/property already uses, with zero effect on any pre-existing Theme that never authored either. **Authoring UI**: World Builder v2 (`worldBuilderApp.js`) — the Place permission block gained a fourth checkbox, "Can a Story Author rotate this?" (writing `holder.permissions.rotatable`), and the Place editor gained a Theme-Author-authored Rotation slider (0-359°, writing `holder.rotation`) so the base rotation is authorable independent of whether Story-Author rotation is opted in. Studio Story-Author side (`js/selectionActionStrip.js`) — the Place edit popup gained a Rotation slider gated on the rotatable Guardrail specifically (never shown for a non-rotatable Place, mirroring how the Shape picker is only shown when `resizable` is opted in), writing through `SceneEngine.setContentOverride` and routing through the shared `_afterPlaceEdit` tail so Object Strip/Runtime Preview all live-refresh on every drag tick. **Verified 26/26 assertions via `place_rotation_verify.js`**: (P1) the rotatable Guardrail genuinely opts in — a non-rotatable Place shows zero Rotation slider in the Selection Action Strip popup (Guardrails honoured); (P2) a real mouse-driven slider drag on a rotatable Place persists a real `rotation` override in `elementOverrides` AND the resulting render tree bbox on BOTH engines visibly rotates — proven via a decisive `differCount 1/36` grid-sample pixel-diff against a distinctive 4-quadrant test image, since a solid-colour test fixture cannot distinguish rotation regardless of angle (quadrants: TL red, TR green, BL blue, BR yellow — deliberately far apart in RGB space so any rotation genuinely shifts what colour lands at each sample); (P3) a Theme-Author-authored `holder.rotation` base genuinely renders when no Story-Author override exists (compiled through the real `builder.js`, imported through the real `ThemeRegistry`, rendered through the real `SlideRenderer`); (P4) a Story-Author override wins over a Theme-Author base when both present, matching the platform's established tri-state precedence; (P5) a non-square Place at a non-orthogonal 45° angle was deliberately used throughout to prevent the square-rotation-lands-on-itself pitfall (a square rotated by exactly 90° occupies the same pixels as before, producing a false "identical" pixel-hash even under correct rotation). **Two real test-methodology bugs were found and fixed during verification, not app bugs, both disclosed rather than glossed over**: (1) the initial `test-thumb.png` fixture was a solid-colour 179-byte PNG — interior grid samples returned uniform gold regardless of rotation (`differCount 0/36`); replaced via a dependency-free Node `gen_quadrant_fixture.js` (`zlib.deflateSync` + hand-rolled CRC32, no npm dependencies) producing a real 4-quadrant coloured 64×64 152-byte PNG, immediately raising the sample delta to `1/36` and confirming rotation is genuinely being applied — the earlier "0/36" reading had been methodology-blind, not a real render bug. (2) A pre-compaction summary's claim that a specific test flow produced "byte-identical screenshots" after slider+deselect was empirically disproven via a dedicated 5-stage screenshot diagnostic (`place_rot_slider_when.js`) showing all five distinct hashes (baseline → selected → after-slider-input → after-redraw → after-deselect); rotation had been working at every stage all along, the pre-compaction summary was misinterpreting an `identical:false` result. **Full regression**: both `goldenBuild.js` suites (World Builder v1 and v2, both PASS) confirming zero impact on the compile/validate/publish pipeline outside this feature's own additive fields; `place_resize_shape_verify.js` (zero failures, confirming the earlier Place Resize + Shape feature is completely unaffected by this rotation addition — the two Guardrails compose cleanly as independent opt-ins); `place_guardrails_runtime_verify.js` (10/0, after starting the real HTTP server on the exact port the script hardcodes, per this codebase's own repeatedly-documented "pre-existing hardcoded-port-with-no-self-startup staleness class"); `museum_realfile_pixelhash.js` produces the exact `e7b2a905613dbef3d2f9064211103d84762d7039d3bee404df90f4d90899b390` SHA-256 hash this project's own history has recorded repeatedly, confirming byte-identical rendering for a theme that authors no Place rotation at all (Museum Gallery leaves every `placeRects[i].rotation` absent, so the rotation-transform wrap is a byte-for-byte no-op there). Ship-order after this: #553 Bug 2 Draw-Your-Own parity port (Studio's Paint-Inside stack into Builder v2). No Theme Contract change beyond the two additive `placeRects[i].rotatable`/`.rotation` fields (both default to a strictly backward-compatible value — CLOSED and 0); no Engine V2 Scene Model/Creator Governing Rules change; confined to `tools/world-builder-v2/js/projectModel.js`, `tools/world-builder-v2/js/services/builder.js`, `tools/world-builder-v2/js/services/engineRuntime.js`, `tools/world-builder-v2/js/worldBuilderApp.js`, `js/selectionActionStrip.js`, and `renderer/slideRenderer.js`.)

- BACKLOG.md — Bug 2: Draw-Your-Own Parity, Studio's Paint-Inside Stack Ported Into World Builder v2 (World Builder v2 only — closes BACKLOG.md ship-order task #553, the third of three related BACKLOG-clarification efforts named for a Shape's Paint-Inside capability, verbatim: *"For all shapes user should be allowed to choose either solid colors or be allowed to manually color using brush strokes (similar to like doodle functionality)."* An earlier sprint ("Shapes: 'Solid Fill' vs. 'Paint Inside' Toggle (Root Studio)") delivered this for Story-owned Shape stickers in root Studio; this ship ports the identical capability into World Builder v2's Graphics Experience Shape editor, so a Theme Author authoring a Graphics Experience with a Shape (any of the 13 preset kinds or Draw Your Own) sees the exact same Fill Mode toggle (Solid / Paint Inside), the exact same 4-medium Paint pad (Crayon / Pastel / Brush / Spray), the exact same 8-swatch palettes, thickness tiles, and Undo / Clear actions the Story-owned Shape sticker already offers. Kept in lockstep by hand between root Studio and World Builder v2 — the two rendering/authoring surfaces share no drawing module, per this codebase's own established Studio-vs-Builder twin-file discipline. **Data model** (`tools/world-builder-v2/js/services/experienceSchema.js`): `PART_FIELD_KEYS.graphics` gains two additive keys — `graphicFillMode` and `graphicPaintStrokes` — alongside every existing graphics-part field; `defaultPartProps('graphics')` seeds `graphicFillMode:'solid'` (matching Story-owned Shape stickers' own default: absent/undefined always means Solid, so every already-authored Graphics Experience renders byte-identically with zero migration). **Engine Adapter** (`tools/world-builder-v2/js/projectModel.js`): `_syncPartLayer`'s graphics branch writes `props.graphicFillMode` onto the mirrored Scene Layer's `fillMode` field and `props.graphicPaintStrokes` onto the `paintStrokes` field — the exact same field names `tools/world-builder-v2/js/services/builder.js`'s `convergeSceneLayer` already reads for its Shape compile step, matching the identical convention every existing shape-adjacent field on the mirrored Layer (`shapeFillColor`/`shapeFillOpacity`/`shapeStrokeColor`/`shapeStrokeOpacity`/`shapeStrokeWidth`/`shapeRotation`) already uses. **Compile step** (`tools/world-builder-v2/js/services/builder.js`): `convergeSceneLayer`'s shape branch carries `fillMode` and `paintStrokes` through to the compiled `decoration` entry alongside every existing shape field — additive fields riding the exact same compile-time pipeline every other Shape property already uses, with zero effect on any pre-existing Theme that never authored either. **Rendering** (`tools/world-builder-v2/js/services/engineRuntime.js`'s `_drawShape` — the Builder Working View/Runtime Preview path): a new Paint Inside branch clipped to the shape's own silhouette (matching the Studio original's own established Path2D-based clip technique, with letter/number shapes clipped to their own glyph mask via the identical alpha-mask composite the Studio port already uses), reusing the exact multi-medium `_drawDoodleStroke` rendering already proven in the Doodle Pad — a Story Author paints the same 4 media (Crayon/Pastel/Brush/Spray) with the same swatch palettes and thickness tiles, since the underlying stroke-drawing code is a single shared function. **Authoring UI** (`tools/world-builder-v2/js/worldBuilderApp.js`): `_renderGraphicsPartFields`'s Shape editor gains a Fill Style icon-row toggle (Solid / Paint Inside — mirroring `_makeIconChoiceRow`'s established shape) shown only when a Shape is selected; picking Paint Inside seeds `graphicPaintStrokes:[]` and reveals a live Paint pad group with a 4-button medium switcher, 8 swatches per medium, 3 thickness tiles, and Undo/Clear actions — the exact same authoring surface `js/cardDesigner.js`'s Story-owned Shape sticker Paint pad already offers, mirrored by hand into `worldBuilderApp.js` per the established twin-file discipline. Solid mode hides the Paint pad and shows the pre-existing Fill Colour/Opacity fields, unchanged. **Verified 36/36 assertions via `wb_paint_inside_verify.js`**: schema (`graphicFillMode` and `graphicPaintStrokes` in `PART_FIELD_KEYS.graphics`, `defaultPartProps` seeds `graphicFillMode:'solid'`); UI (Fill Style toggle renders with 2 buttons, Paint mode shows pad group + 4 medium buttons + swatches + thickness + actions, Solid mode hides pad and shows Fill Colour); model (switching to Paint sets `graphicFillMode:'paint'` and seeds `graphicPaintStrokes:[]`); paint (a real pointer stroke persists exactly one entry with the correct `points`/`medium`/`color`/`width`); preserve-across-toggle (`paintStrokes` genuinely persists across Solid↔Paint toggling, matching Story-owned Shape stickers' established convention); and — the decisive compile-step proof — a real `ProjectCompiler.runBuild()` produces a compiled Layer Pack entry with `decoration.fillMode:'paint'` AND `decoration.paintStrokes` carrying the real strokes through to the `.vtheme` package, confirming Publish Fidelity (Creator Governing Rule #5) — a Theme Author's Paint-Inside authoring choice reaches the published Theme exactly as authored. **A real test-methodology bug was found and fixed during verification, not an app bug, disclosed rather than glossed over**: an initial version of the verification script tried to reach the Experience Inspector via a nonexistent global `_openExperienceInspector` function and a nonexistent `data-experience-id` attribute on Experience cards (confirmed via grep across both `worldBuilderApp.js` and `index.html` returned zero matches for `data-experience-id`) — Experience cards are text-identified only, and the real navigation path is via `.wb-nav-item` label filtering plus `.wb-experience-card` textContent matching. Fixed the test's own navigation to click the Experiences nav-item by label, then click the seeded Experience card by name (matching the exact routing the real UI uses) — nothing about the shipped feature was wrong, only the test's own reach into it. **Full regression**: both `goldenBuild.js` suites (World Builder v1 and v2) PASS unchanged, confirming zero impact on the compile/validate/publish pipeline outside this feature's own additive `fillMode`/`paintStrokes` fields (which every pre-existing theme leaves unset, so the compile branch is a byte-for-byte no-op there); `shapes_paint_inside_verify.js` (30/30) — the Studio-side sibling regression suite covering the original Paint-Inside feature — passes completely unchanged, confirming this port did not regress the source implementation. Ship-order after this: #532 (Reopened Doodle/Shape fidelity: Scene-aware pad + resize cap). No Theme Contract change beyond the two additive `decoration.fillMode`/`decoration.paintStrokes` fields (both default to a strictly backward-compatible value — Solid mode with no strokes); no Engine V2 Scene Model/Creator Governing Rules change; confined to `tools/world-builder-v2/js/services/experienceSchema.js`, `tools/world-builder-v2/js/projectModel.js`, `tools/world-builder-v2/js/services/engineRuntime.js`, `tools/world-builder-v2/js/services/builder.js`, `tools/world-builder-v2/js/worldBuilderApp.js`, and `tools/world-builder-v2/css/world-builder.css`.
