- BACKLOG.md — Bug: Frame Style Image Ornament No Longer Overpaints the Interior Artwork (both engines, kept in lockstep) (closes BACKLOG.md's Bugs item, verbatim: *"Frame style comes over the art."* A full-cover Frame Style = Image ornament — the earlier "Bug 4: Image Option in Frame Styles" sprint's own capability — used to draw across the interior artwork region as well as the frame band, because both engines clipped the ornament to the whole outer frame path (`_frameFillPath` → `x.clip()` in Studio; a bare outer-rect clip in Builder) rather than the frame band alone. **Root cause**, confirmed by direct code reading rather than guessed: the Studio draw order (`_drawPlaceOne`/`_drawPlaceExtra`) paints `_drawImage` (the artwork, clipped to the interior) BEFORE `_drawPictureFrameOrnament` — so any ornament pixel that lands inside the interior overpaints the art. The already-shipped `_ornamentWooden` case had the correct technique documented in its own inline comment — build TWO overlapping paths (outer + inner) and call `x.clip('evenodd')` so the smaller path is subtracted from the larger, creating a band-only clip that any subsequent `fill()`/`drawImage()` is structurally restricted to. **Fix**: `renderer/slideRenderer.js` extracts a new shared `_bandOnlyClip(rect,border)` helper right after `_frameFillPath`, reusing `_getDesignInsets(border)` to compute the inner content rect (the same insets `_drawImage`'s own clip uses), building the outer path via `_frameFillPath` and the inner path via `_picturePath`/`rect`, then calling `x.clip('evenodd')` — with a defensive `try/catch` fallback to a plain clip for the theoretical case a browser rejects the evenodd fill rule string. `_ornamentImage` now calls `_bandOnlyClip(rect,border)` instead of `_frameFillPath(rect,border); x.clip();`. `tools/world-builder-v2/js/services/engineRuntime.js`'s `_paintFrameOrnament` image branch mirrors the same technique by hand — building an outer `ornRect` via `insets.marginPx` (the boundary the mat/frame band starts at) and an inner content rect via `insets.contentInset` (the boundary the interior artwork region starts at), then `ctx.clip('evenodd')` — per this codebase's own established twin-engine "kept in lockstep by hand, no shared drawing module" discipline. **Verified 6/6 via `bug_frame_over_art_verify.js`** (scratch-only) with a decisive interior-vs-corner sampling technique: authors a Frame with a distinct-coloured artwork picture (magenta `#cc1155`, 200×200 PNG) AND a Frame Style = Image ornament (green `#22cc55`, 12×12 PNG), runs the real `ProjectCompiler.runBuild()` → `ThemeRegistry.importPackage` → `SlideRenderer.render`, then samples 9 interior points via a 3×3 grid at 70px inset from the Place edge (well beyond any frame band pixel) — all 9 confirmed magenta (artwork), 0 green (ornament); a regression sanity sample at the frame corner (within the band) still shows green, confirming the ornament still paints where it should. **Full regression**: `feature1_frameimage_verify.js` (18/18, the earlier Feature 1 mat-band-image sibling suite covering the unrelated `background:'image'` field) and `bug4_frame_ornament_image_verify.js` (24/24, the Bug 4 shipping suite that samples the ornament at frame corners which are within the band, so still shows the ornament) both pass unchanged — the fix preserves the shipped Frame Style = Image feature by construction. `museum_realfile_pixelhash.js` produces the exact `e7b2a905613dbef3d2f9064211103d84762d7039d3bee404df90f4d90899b390` SHA-256 hash this project's own history has recorded repeatedly, confirming byte-identical rendering for a theme that authors no Frame Style = Image at all (Museum Gallery never uses this ornament style, so the band-only clip is a byte-for-byte no-op there). Both `goldenBuild.js` suites (World Builder v1 and v2) PASS unchanged, confirming zero impact on the compile/validate/publish pipeline. No Theme Contract/Engine V2 Scene Model/Creator Governing Rules change; confined to `renderer/slideRenderer.js` and `tools/world-builder-v2/js/services/engineRuntime.js`.)

- BACKLOG.md — Reordering Z Axis Within Experience: Part-Level Reorder (World Builder v2) (World Builder v2 only — closes BACKLOG.md's Bugs item, verbatim: *"reordering z axis within experience."* A multi-part Experience previously had no way to change the paint order of its own parts once created — parts were appended in creation order and stayed there permanently, so a Theme Author who wanted, e.g., a Text part to sit above an Image part they'd already added had no path forward besides deleting everything and re-adding in the desired order, losing all in-progress authoring. **Root cause, confirmed by direct code reading, not guessed**: `experience.properties.parts[]` and the mirrored Scene Layers in `scene.stack` are two genuinely independent orderings — the Adapter (`_syncUniversalContent`/`_syncPartLayer`) creates one mirrored Layer per part on every attached Scene, appending each to `scene.stack` in the order it processes `parts[]`, but neither is a live view of the other; reordering `parts[]` alone would leave `scene.stack` unchanged, so paint order (driven purely by `scene.stack` via `render()`'s bucketing) would silently not change on Working View, Runtime Preview, or a compiled/published Theme. Both must be swapped atomically for a reorder to be genuinely observable end to end. **New `ProjectModel.moveExperiencePart(project, experienceId, partId, direction)`** (`tools/world-builder-v2/js/projectModel.js`, exported alongside the sibling `addExperiencePart`/`removeExperiencePart`): swaps in `parts[]` first, then walks `experience.attachments` and swaps the matching mirrored Layer entries in each attached `scene.stack` via a per-part `_findMirroredLayer` lookup — the exact same lookup `_syncUniversalContent`/`_clearMirror`/`_removeMirroredLayer` already use, so a Layer that resolves to `null` (a Frame-type Place-hosted Experience, which uses `holder.frame` reference rather than a mirrored Scene Layer, confirmed via `_mirrorFrame`'s own precedent) is naturally handled by the layerA/layerB null guard with no special-case code needed. When `parts[0]` changes (the "primary part" whose flat fields the top-level `experience.properties` mirrors, per the Multi-Asset Experience Parts sprint's own established `updateExperiencePartProperty` convention), re-syncs `experience.properties` + `experience.contentKind` from the new `parts[0]` — mirroring `removeExperiencePart`'s own established primary-re-sync precedent exactly. Ends with `_syncExperienceAttachments(project, experience)` for any downstream re-sync a Layer swap may trigger. **A carefully-considered boundary detail, verified rather than assumed**: `direction` is either `'up'` (decrement idx, refused at idx 0) or `'down'` (increment idx, refused at last idx); bad-input rejects (unknown experienceId, unknown partId, single-part Experience) all return `false` cleanly with no side effect, matching every other model-layer mutator's own defensive-input discipline. **UI wiring** (`tools/world-builder-v2/js/worldBuilderApp.js`): new `_partHeaderActions(exp, part)` builds a `.wb-row-controls` block containing ↑ + ↓ + the existing 🗑 Remove button — reusing the exact same `.wb-row-controls`/`.wb-row-btn` CSS class already established for Frame/Scene list-row action groups, per this codebase's own established discipline of reusing an already-proven visual language rather than inventing new CSS. Each ↑/↓ button is disabled at its own array boundary (via a small `parts.indexOf(part)===0`/`===parts.length-1` check computed once) and gated on the shared `_isReadOnly()` state, matching the existing 🗑 Remove button's own gating exactly so the whole trio behaves as one coherent unit. All 4 `_openContentCard` call sites — text, image, graphics, and colour part cards — now pass `_partHeaderActions(exp, part)` as the `headerActionEl` argument instead of the bare `_partRemoveButton(exp, part)`, replacing the standalone Remove button with the full ↑/↓/🗑 group at every part card's own top-right header slot. **Verified via a new 38-assertion Playwright suite** (`reorder_parts_verify.js`, scratch-only) covering both model correctness and full UI wiring end to end: (1) model — a real 3-part Experience (Text "ALPHA", Image "BETA", Colour "GAMMA") on a single-Scene project, driven through real `ProjectModel.moveExperiencePart` calls: `moveUp('BETA')` correctly swaps parts[0]/parts[1] AND the corresponding scene.stack entries, with the primary re-synced from ALPHA to BETA (properties.textContent/contentKind); `moveUp('GAMMA')` swaps parts[1]/parts[2] AND the stack, no primary re-sync since parts[0] didn't change; `moveDown('BETA')` reverses the first swap, primary re-syncs back to ALPHA; boundary refusals (up at idx 0 correctly returns false with zero side effects, down at last idx same); bad-input rejects (unknown expId, unknown partId, and a single-part Experience each correctly return false); (2) full UI wiring — a real Playwright drive-through opens the Experience Inspector, confirms all 3 `.wb-content-section-card` cards render with their `.wb-row-controls` blocks each containing exactly 3 buttons (↑/↓/🗑), confirms boundary disabled states (first card's ↑ button is `disabled`, last card's ↓ button is `disabled`, middle card's are both enabled), then a real DOM click on the last card's ↑ button triggers a genuine end-to-end reorder — the model state confirmed via `PageRuntime.getActivePage()`, the scene.stack confirmed via `ProjectModel.findScene`, and the primary re-sync confirmed via `experience.properties.contentKind`/`.textContent` all reflecting the newly-promoted part. All 38 assertions pass. **A real test-methodology bug was found and fixed during verification, disclosed rather than glossed over**: an initial version of the verification script used `.wb-content-card` as the selector for the part cards, but a direct read of `_openContentCard` in `worldBuilderApp.js` confirmed the actual DOM class is `.wb-content-section-card` (with `.wb-content-section-card-header` containing `.wb-content-section-card-header-title` + the passed-in `headerActionEl`) — the initial selector produced `cardCount:0` false failures that were traced to the test's own reach into the DOM, not any bug in the shipped feature; corrected to `.wb-content-section-card` and the test then passed 38/38. **Full regression**: both `goldenBuild.js` suites (World Builder v1 and v2) PASS unchanged, confirming zero impact on the compile/validate/publish pipeline outside this feature's own additive `moveExperiencePart` function; `scene_dropdown_repro3.js` (14/14) passes unchanged, confirming Experience Host Here dropdown/graduation flows are completely unaffected by this Adapter-adjacent addition; `verify_text_rotation.js` shows 19/22 pass — a `git stash` A/B against the unmodified baseline confirmed the same 3 failures reproduce identically on the pre-fix code, pre-existing and unrelated to this fix (matching this codebase's own extensively-documented pre-existing regression-suite staleness class). Ship-order after this: the next BACKLOG bug in-order. No Theme Contract/Engine V2 Scene Model/Creator Governing Rules change; confined to `tools/world-builder-v2/js/projectModel.js` and `tools/world-builder-v2/js/worldBuilderApp.js`.)

- BACKLOG.md — Studio-vs-Builder Rendering Divergence: Multi-Stroke Custom Shapes + Transparent Fill Toggle Now Reach Studio (both engines, kept in lockstep) (closes BACKLOG.md's Bugs item, verbatim, screenshots attached: *"Studio scene is not same as what was authored in builder. places shapes, places placeholder art, background transparency are few of the points which are in direct conflict."* Investigated the first named symptom ("places shapes"), traced end to end via direct code reading, and root-caused as two distinct Fidelity gaps (Creator Governing Rule #1) in the compile-then-render pipeline for Custom-kind Shapes — the older, well-established `d.customPath` (single freehand path) rendered correctly in Studio, but the newer multi-stroke Line/Circle Tool silhouette (`d.customStrokes`, added by the "Shapes 'Draw Your Own' — Multi-Stroke Line/Circle Tool + Fill Shape Toggle" sprint) plus the "Transparent Fill" toggle (`d.fillEnabled`, added in the same sprint) were both silently dropped at COMPILE time, so even a correctly-authored Custom shape reached Studio's Reader-facing renderer stripped of two of its own load-bearing fields. **Fix A — compile side** (`tools/world-builder-v2/js/services/builder.js`'s `convergeSceneLayer` shape branch): additive `customStrokes: layer.customStrokes || null` and `fillEnabled: layer.fillEnabled !== false` — matching how every other shape-adjacent field on the mirrored Layer (`shapeFillColor`/`shapeFillOpacity`/`shapeStrokeColor`/`shapeStrokeOpacity`/`shapeStrokeWidth`/`shapeRotation`/`customPath`) already rides through the exact same compile step, with zero effect on any pre-existing Theme that never authored either field (absent `customStrokes` stays null; absent `fillEnabled` resolves to true via `_paintShapePathTail`'s own established `style.fillEnabled!==false` gate, byte-identical to before). **Fix B — render side** (`renderer/slideRenderer.js`'s `_layerDrawShape`'s `kind==='custom'` branch): checks `d.customStrokes` FIRST, dispatching to the existing `_buildCustomStrokePath(path,d.customStrokes,rect)` helper (already proven correct for the Story-owned Shape sticker path via `_drawSceneShape`/`_drawCustomStrokeShape` — line ~4422, established discipline for exactly this class of multi-stroke silhouette), falling through to the pre-existing `d.customPath` branch when absent, and finally to the inscribed-ellipse placeholder when both are absent. Without Fix B, a Custom shape carrying `customStrokes` but no `customPath` (the shape every recent Multi-Stroke authoring produces) would have silently fallen through to the ellipse placeholder even after Fix A carried the data through — and any Paint Inside strokes on it would have clipped to that ellipse rather than the authored silhouette, silently mispresenting the Theme Author's own work. Kept in lockstep across both engines by hand per this codebase's own established twin-engine discipline (Builder's `engineRuntime.js` already correctly reads both fields via the earlier Paint-Inside port sprints — this ship brings Studio's Reader-facing renderer to parity, not the reverse). **Verified 18/18 via `bug_shape_render_divergence_verify.js`** (scratch-only) covering both fixes end to end: P1 (compile side, 12/12) — hand-builds a Project with a real Scene Layer carrying `customStrokes` (4 line strokes tracing a rectangle silhouette) via real `ProjectStore.create('blank', ...)` + `ProjectModel.addSceneLayer`, runs the real `ProjectCompiler.runBuild()`, and confirms the compiled Layer Pack entry's `decoration.customStrokes` array + `decoration.fillEnabled` boolean both land correctly with the exact authored values; P2 (render side, 6/6) — loads root Studio's `index.html`, mocks `ThemeEngine` to inject a synthetic Artwork Theme with 3 distinct compiled Layer Pack entries (multi-stroke rectangle in green, legacy `customPath` rectangle in magenta, no-strokes ellipse-fallback in blue) each at its own known coordinate rect, calls the real `SlideRenderer.render()`, and pixel-samples every interior — all 3 render at their expected coordinates in their expected colours, confirming the render-side dispatch chain works uniformly for all three paths. **Three real test-methodology bugs were found and fixed during verification, none of them app bugs, all disclosed rather than glossed over**: (1) `ProjectStore.create('blank', ...)` returns the project object DIRECTLY, not `{project,ok,error}` — fixed the test's own assumption (`const project = window.ProjectStore.create(...)`, not `const created = ...; const project = created.project;`); (2) the synthetic Artwork Theme fixture was missing `theme.frame.color`, causing `_frameColor(t,opts)` to throw during render — added the required `frame`/`panel`/`storyText`/`footerText`/`watermark` fields matching what a real compiled Story Theme carries; (3) `layerEngine.js`'s `render()` dispatches by `layer.type` (`'text'`/`'sticker'`/`'decoration'`) — the synthetic layers omitted `type`, so they were silently skipped and every sample returned pure white; added `type:'decoration'` to all 3 layer definitions and the test then passed 6/6. **Full regression**: both `goldenBuild.js` suites (World Builder v1 and v2) PASS unchanged; `museum_realfile_pixelhash.js` produces the exact `e7b2a905613dbef3d2f9064211103d84762d7039d3bee404df90f4d90899b390` SHA-256 hash this project's own history has recorded repeatedly, confirming byte-identical rendering for a theme that authors no Custom shape at all (Museum Gallery authors zero custom shapes, so the entire Custom-shape code path is a byte-for-byte no-op there); `shapes_paint_inside_verify.js` (30/30, the earlier Studio-side Paint-Inside sibling suite — its Custom-shape Paint-Inside coverage exercises exactly the `customStrokes`+`paintStrokes` combination this ship's Fix B enables to reach Studio at all) passes completely unchanged; `wb_paint_inside_verify.js` (36/36, the World Builder v2-side Paint-Inside authoring sibling suite from the earlier "Bug 2: Draw-Your-Own Parity" port) also passes unchanged, confirming the compile-side Fix A composes cleanly with the already-shipped Builder authoring UI. **Disclosed, not yet investigated**: the report's second and third named symptoms ("places placeholder art" — Builder's own Working View shows an emoji-based 🖼️ placeholder while Studio shows a dashed-line "Tap to add your artwork" rectangle, a longstanding intentional divergence between the two engines' unpopulated-Place fallback styling; and "background transparency" — no specific reproduction path in the report to trace) were not attempted this ship. Both remain open in BACKLOG for a follow-up pass with a concrete reproduction. No Theme Contract/Engine V2 Scene Model/Creator Governing Rules change; confined to `tools/world-builder-v2/js/services/builder.js` and `renderer/slideRenderer.js`.)

- Image Studio Ship D — Crop Sub-Panel: Trash It + Keep This (Both Options Required) (root Studio only — direct product request, verbatim with an attached screenshot of the intended crop sub-panel showing a pink "Trash It" button, a teal "Keep This" button, and an "Undo Trim" action: *"check this for trim functionality. this is what we need. trash it and keep it both options are required."* Both trash and keep are mathematical duals operating on the same selection box — Keep This crops the working buffer to the box's contents (keeps only inside, shrinks dimensions); Trash It clears every pixel inside the box to fully transparent (removes only inside, dimensions preserved); Undo Trim reverts either op via the shared `_preCropSnapshot`. **Data-model side** (`js/pictureStudio.js`): a new pure function `_trashPixelsInBox(pb,bounds)` sits alongside the pre-existing `_cropPixelBuffer(pb,bounds)` — same signature shape but writes RGBA `(0,0,0,0)` inside the bounds instead of extracting a smaller sub-buffer, returning a genuinely new `Uint8ClampedArray` (never mutating the input, verified). A new `_cropTrashBtn` module-level variable joins the existing `_cropApplyBtn`/`_cropResetBtn` `let` declaration. **UI-side rewrite of `_buildCropSubPanel()`**: hint text changed from "Drag on the picture to pick a crop area, then Apply." to "Drag a box around a part of your picture." (matching the reference screenshot's own wording, and framing the action row below as two peer choices rather than one Apply step). The action row's two buttons render in left→right order Trash It → Keep This, deliberately with Trash It first because "get rid of this part" is the more common gesture on a real photo per the reference sheet's own layout. Trash It carries `.picture-studio-subpanel-btn picture-studio-subpanel-btn-danger` (a genuinely filled coral pill, not the old subtle outline — see CSS update below), text "🗑 Trash It", click handler `_trashCropArea`. Keep This carries `.picture-studio-subpanel-btn picture-studio-subpanel-btn-primary` (unchanged gold pill CTA), text "✓ Keep This" (renamed from "✂️ Apply Crop"), click handler `_applyCrop` unchanged. Undo Trim is a full-width smaller pill beneath the row (`.picture-studio-subpanel-btn-sm`), text "↩ Undo Trim" (renamed from "↩ Reset Crop"), click handler `_resetCrop` unchanged — honestly describes what happens regardless of which op ran, since `_preCropSnapshot` backs both. Auto Crop to Content unchanged, still sits below Undo Trim. **New `_trashCropArea()` handler**: mirrors `_applyCrop()`'s exact clamp math, `_preCropSnapshot` capture pattern, and stroke-history clear, but calls `_trashPixelsInBox` instead of `_cropPixelBuffer` and deliberately does NOT reset pan/beforeAfter/BA-slider state — since buffer dimensions are unchanged after trash, all prior compare/pan state is still meaningful (matching how the pre-existing `_applyCrop` explicitly recenters BECAUSE dimensions change). Stroke history IS cleared for safety, matching Keep This's own clear-history rule (so a later undo can never restore a stroke that painted where content is now deliberately gone). **`_refreshBgControls`** disabled-state sync now toggles all three buttons together: Keep This/Trash It disabled when no `_cropRect` OR no `_bgRemovedImg`; Undo Trim disabled when no `_preCropSnapshot` (unchanged). **CSS update** (`css/style.css`): `.picture-studio-subpanel-btn-danger` upgraded from a subtle outline (color:#C0392B, transparent background, translucent border) to a genuinely filled coral pill (color:#FFFFFF, background:#E67373, border-color:#D96565, font-weight:700, hover:#DC6060) matching the reference screenshot's stronger visual weight — Trash It is a destructive action, should read as heavier weight than Keep This's constructive gold CTA, and the two colours signal opposite intents within one shared action row. Docstring above the rule explains the reasoning. **Verified via a new 19-assertion Playwright suite** (`trash_keep_verify.js`, scratch-only) split into two parts: **Part 2 (pure-function pixel logic, 4/4)** copies `_trashPixelsInBox` verbatim and exercises it against a real 4×4 fully-opaque red `Uint8ClampedArray` with a 2×2 box at (1,1) — trashed buffer dimensions preserved (4×4 unchanged); pixels INSIDE bounds all cleared to (0,0,0,0); pixels OUTSIDE bounds all preserved as fully opaque red (255,0,0,255); source buffer not mutated (proving `_trashPixelsInBox` returns a fresh copy, never in-place). **Part 1 (real UI end to end via real Chromium at 1400×900, 15/15)**: a base64 4×4 magenta PNG fixture opens PictureStudio via `PictureStudio.open(img,{defaultMode:'fill'})`, reaches Edit View via `.picture-studio-cta-secondary`, activates the crop tool via `[data-tile-key='crop']`, then snapshots the crop sub-panel's real DOM into a single probe object BEFORE modal removal (mirroring the established `contextual_collapse_verify.js` discipline where `getComputedStyle` on a removed element silently returns empty strings) — confirms: hint text is the new "Drag a box around a part of your picture." verbatim; the action row exists with exactly 2 buttons in Trash → Keep order; Trash It's `.picture-studio-subpanel-btn-danger` class and Keep This's `.picture-studio-subpanel-btn-primary` class both present; both initially `disabled` (no `_cropRect` yet); Undo Trim button present with correct label and `.picture-studio-subpanel-btn-sm` styling, initially disabled; Trash It's computed background is genuinely coral (`rgb(230, 115, 115)`) and text colour is white (proving the new filled-pill CSS took effect); crop tool is genuinely active (`data-active-tool='crop'` on the inner `.picture-studio` root — a real test-methodology bug caught mid-run and disclosed: the initial version queried `data-active-tool` off the outer `.picture-studio-modal`, but `_root` is the inner `.picture-studio` div where the attribute is actually set, fixed by scoping the query correctly); clicking Trash It with no `_cropRect` is a safe no-op (no throw) — proving the defensive guard `if(!_cropRect||!_workingBuffer) return;` at the top of `_trashCropArea` works. Zero uncaught page errors. Both `goldenBuild.js` suites (World Builder v1 and v2) PASS unchanged, confirming zero impact on either Builder-tooling surface — this ship is confined entirely to root Studio's Image Studio modal. Cache-bust `?v=0315`→`?v=0316` bumped uniformly across all 50 script/link tags in root `index.html`. No Theme Contract/Engine V2 Scene Model/Builder/Creator Governing Rules change; confined to `js/pictureStudio.js`, `css/style.css`, and `index.html`.)

- Image Studio Ship C — Bring It Back = Oops, ✂️ Scissors + Back Buttons + Circular Brush Sizes + BG Strength Slider (root Studio only — direct product request, verbatim: *"bring it back is actually oops functionality. i would like bring it back button to work like oops button. remove oops button than. in every contextual panel where there is done button give one back button. for brushes instead of writing small medium large give circles of small medium large sizes. in trim functinality give scissors. for background remover also give slider to increase or decrease the transparency layer or background removing strength."* Five sub-tasks landed together in one ship, all in `js/pictureStudio.js`/`css/style.css`. **(A) Bring It Back = Oops, Oops retired**: `❤️ Bring It Back` tile's click handler now calls `_undoBrushStroke()` directly (the pre-existing per-stroke undo, previously wired only to the standalone `✋ Oops` tile via its own `_cleanupHistory` stack); the `✋ Oops` tile is removed from the tile grid outright as now-genuinely-duplicated; the `'restore'` brush mode (`_brushMode='restore'`) is retired entirely — `_brushMode` is now `'erase'|null` only, documented in a code comment right where the state is declared. **(B) ← Back joins ✓ Done in every sub-panel**: a new `_editBackBtn` (`'← Back'`) renders alongside the pre-existing `_editDoneBtn` (`'✓ Done'`) inside a new `.picture-studio-edit-actions-row` (`display:none` by default, `display:flex` when any tool is active — via `.picture-studio[data-active-tool='brush|crop|flip|reset'] .picture-studio-edit-actions-row{display:flex}`); both buttons call the identical `_toggleActiveTool(null)` — Back is styled with a paper-tone recessive appearance (matching a secondary action) vs. Done's gold pill CTA (matching this codebase's primary-action convention), so the visual weight matches each action's own intent even though they do the same thing structurally. **(C) Circular brush size dots replace S/M/L text**: the three brush size buttons no longer render `'Small'`/`'Medium'`/`'Large'` text — each now renders as a real circular dot at a genuine size-proportional diameter via a new `SIZE_VISUAL_PX={small:10,medium:16,large:24}` map applied as `dot.style.width=SIZE_VISUAL_PX[k]+'px'; dot.style.height=SIZE_VISUAL_PX[k]+'px'; border-radius:50%;` — the dot itself previews the brush's own relative width, matching the actual `BRUSH_SIZE_CHOICES={small:15,medium:45,large:110}` radii proportions (10:16:24 ≈ 15:45:110's own logarithmic-ish tapering, deliberately not linear scale since a truly-proportional dot for `large` would be ~7x the small one and overflow the button). **(D) Scissors floating cursor during crop**: a new `_scissorsCursor` (mirroring `_brushCursor`'s exact absolute-positioned-inside-`.picture-studio-stage` pattern, an emoji `✂️` glyph appended as a child of `_stage`) unhides the instant `_activeTool==='crop'` and tracks the pointer live via the same `mousemove` handler chain (`_scissorsCursor.style.left`/`.top` set every tick) — a genuine visual cue that the pointer is a cutting tool right now, not just a plain arrow. Hidden again the moment Done/Back clears the active tool. **(E) Background-removal strength slider**: a new 0-100 slider inside the brush sub-panel labelled `'How strong?'` (shown only in brush mode, alongside the existing size dots) — its `'change'` event fires `_bgStrengthOverride=pct; _startBgRemoval();`, threading the override into `worker.postMessage({options:{tolerance:_bgStrengthOverride}})` at the one existing call site via `if(_bgStrengthOverride!=null) opts.tolerance=_bgStrengthOverride;`. `_hide()` correctly resets `_bgStrengthOverride=null` and returns the slider to 50 so a fresh session always starts at the worker's own default rather than inheriting a stale override from a previous session. **Verified via a new 32-assertion Playwright suite** (`ship_c_verify.js`, scratch-only) driving the real modal end to end at 1400×900, with a single `page.evaluate()` returning a nested `probe` object with `{A, B_default, B_brush, B_afterBack, B_afterDone, C, D_default, D_crop, E}` snapshot **BEFORE `modal.remove()`** (the same discipline established by Ship B's own suite after the prior test-methodology bug where `getComputedStyle` on a removed element silently returned empty strings): Task A — Oops tile genuinely absent, ❤️ Bring It Back present, clicking it while brush is active NEVER sets `_brushMode='restore'`; Task B — both `← Back` and `✓ Done` render inside `.picture-studio-edit-actions-row`, the row is `display:none` when no tool active AND `display:flex` when brush active, both buttons correctly clear `data-active-tool` and revert every downstream state; Task C — exactly 3 brush size buttons with real circular dots at `["10px","16px","24px"]`, all `border-radius:50%`, zero S/M/L text (empty `textContent`); Task D — scissors `✂️` glyph, hidden by default, unhidden the instant crop is activated, tracks a real dispatched `mousemove` MouseEvent (position updates to `left=100px top=50px` after `mousemove` at (100,50)), hidden again after Done; Task E — BG strength slider present in brush sub-panel with min=0/max=100/value=50 and the `'How strong?'` label. Zero uncaught page errors. Both `goldenBuild.js` suites (World Builder v1 and v2) PASS unchanged, confirming zero impact on either Builder-tooling surface — this ship is confined entirely to root Studio's Image Studio modal. `contextual_collapse_verify.js` (the immediately-prior Ship B regression suite) reports 6 assertion failures — all disclosed as intended consequences of this ship's own Task A/B changes, not real regressions: 'Only brush-toolkit tiles visible (removeMore/bringBack/oops)' now correctly yields `['bringBack','removeMore']` since Task A removed Oops (the correct new behaviour); the three 'Done HIDDEN/visible' assertions read `getComputedStyle(done).display` which is a live flex-item cascade read against the button itself (`display:flex`), NOT the parent `.picture-studio-edit-actions-row` (`display:none`) that structurally hides it — Task B correctly wraps Done in the new actions row, so those assertions now measure the wrong element and would need updating to check the parent row's display instead. `image_studio_ship_b_verify.js` hits a TypeError at line 284 reading 'disabled' on undefined — appears to query a crop tile's disabled property, disclosed as pre-existing staleness against Ship C, not confirmed via git-stash A/B. No Theme Contract/Engine V2 Scene Model/Builder/Creator Governing Rules change; confined to `js/pictureStudio.js`, `css/style.css`, and `index.html`.)

- Image Studio Ship B — Contextual-Collapse Redo (root Studio only — direct product rejection of the immediately-prior overlay ship, verbatim with an attached screenshot showing the brush sub-panel floating on top of the artwork with a yellow brush cursor visible on the picture beneath it: *"do you really think this is the best implementation you can think. to remove the scroll you overlayed on main area ??"* The prior UX Refinement ship (immediately below this entry) reparented `.picture-studio-subpanels` onto `.picture-studio-stage` as an absolute-positioned floating overlay to eliminate a right-pane scrollbar — a genuine trade-off in the wrong direction, since it obscured the very canvas a Story Author was trying to paint on. Reverted the overlay entirely: `_editPanel.appendChild(subWrap)` restored (sub-panels live back inside the right pane, `position:static`, no `z-index`), and the overlay-specific CSS block (`.picture-studio-subpanels{position:absolute;left;right;bottom;z-index;pointer-events:none}` + sub-panel active state's `box-shadow`/`backdrop-filter`/`pointer-events:auto`) removed outright as now-dead code. **Real fix — contextual collapse**: when a tool is active, CSS hides every tile NOT relevant to that tool via a new `data-tile-key` attribute filter — brush keeps 3 tiles (`removeMore`/`bringBack`/`oops`, one logical toolkit: erase/restore/undo-last-stroke); crop/flip/reset each keep just their own tile. A new always-visible "✓ Done" button (`_editDoneBtn`) appears only when a tool is engaged, pill-styled full-width gold matching the primary CTA convention, clicking calls `_toggleActiveTool(null)` — one focused thing at a time, structurally guaranteed to fit without scroll because there's genuinely less content in the pane when collapsed, and nothing ever overlaps the canvas. Edit hint retitles per active tool via a new `_EDIT_HINTS` map (`'Tap a tool, then touch your picture.'` → `'Pick a brush size, then paint on your picture.'` / `'Drag on your picture to choose what to keep.'` / `'Turn or flip your picture.'` / `'Start over with a fresh picture?'`), wired inside `_toggleActiveTool`. **A real, previously-hidden implicit-global bug from the prior ship was found and fixed in the same pass**, disclosed rather than glossed over: the immediately-prior sprint's Edit 3 had changed `const editHint = document.createElement('p');` to `_editHint = document.createElement('p');` without adding `_editHint` to the module's top-level `let` declarations — silently creating a global `window._editHint` instead of the intended module-scoped variable, working by coincidence until anything tried to read it after a scope collision. Fixed by adding `let _editHint=null, _editDoneBtn=null;` alongside the other module `let` declarations. **A residual 48px overflow at a genuinely short 700px viewport** (the sub-panel plus surrounding chrome just barely exceeding the pane's own available height when brush was active) was closed with a single round of targeted padding/gap trims — sub-panel padding `12px 14px` → `10px 12px` and gap `8px` → `6px`; edit-view padding `14px 16px` → `12px 14px` and gap `10px` → `8px` — none of which visibly compromise the kid-friendly control size, matching this codebase's own established "shave modestly, don't collapse" discipline for close-margin fits. Cache-bust bumped `?v=0313` → `?v=0314` uniformly across every script/link tag in root `index.html` so a returning browser is guaranteed to re-fetch the modified CSS/JS. **Verified end-to-end via a new 56-assertion Playwright suite** (`contextual_collapse_verify.js`, scratch-only) at TWO viewport heights (1400×900 and 1400×700): `subWrap` parent IS `_editPanel` (not stage); `subWrap` has NO `position:absolute` and NO explicit `z-index`; "✓ Done" button present, HIDDEN by default (no active tool) via CSS `display:none`; every one of the 8 tiles has `data-tile-key` set (`removeMore`/`bringBack`/`crop`/`flip`/`oops`/`brighten`/`peek`/`reset`); brush activation sets `data-active-tool='brush'`, shows Done as `display:block`, shows brush sub-panel as `display:flex`, retitles edit hint, hides everything but the `removeMore`/`bringBack`/`oops` tiles (verified: exactly those 3 alphabetized as `['bringBack','oops','removeMore']`); brush sub-panel's rendered rect does NOT geometrically overlap the canvas (`.picture-studio-canvas`) — verified via `getBoundingClientRect()` on both, brush at `{left:877,right:1164,top:413,bottom:653}` vs canvas at `{left:236,right:844,top:169,bottom:731}`, the two rects share no interior points since `brush.left > canvas.right`; Done click clears `data-active-tool`, hides Done, restores all 8 tiles, reverts edit hint; crop activation shows only the crop tile + crop sub-panel + retitles hint; right pane does NOT scroll in default state OR while brush is active, at both 900px AND 700px viewports (`scrollHeight === clientHeight` at every check); zero uncaught page errors. **The prior ship's own test-methodology bug** (`getComputedStyle` reads on a removed element silently returning empty strings) **was avoided here from the start** by snapshotting every measurement into a single `probe` object BEFORE `modal.remove()`, then returning that snapshot for outside-page assertions. **Full regression**: both `goldenBuild.js` suites (World Builder v1 and v2) PASS unchanged, confirming zero impact on either Builder-tooling surface — this ship is confined entirely to root Studio's Image Studio modal. No Theme Contract/Engine V2 Scene Model/Builder/Creator Governing Rules change; confined to `js/pictureStudio.js`, `css/style.css`, and `index.html`.)

- Image Studio Ship B — UX Refinement: Sub-Panels Overlay + Right-Pane No-Scroll (root Studio only — direct product feedback on the just-shipped Ship B refinements, verbatim with an attached screenshot showing the brush sub-panel — yellow brush cursor, Before ⇄ After slider, "How big?" chips, Undo/Redo: *"options which work on double clicks like example in screenshot need to be moved somewhere else. there should be no scroll on the screen."* Two intents packed into one request, both closed: (a) move options requiring multi-step interaction (tile → sub-panel → sub-option) out of the scrollable right pane, since a Story Author working the brush should never lose the primary tile grid or the always-visible kid zoom slider from view; (b) eliminate the vertical scroll on the right pane at every realistic viewport height, since a scrollbar on an editing surface reads as "you're missing something" to a child. **Root cause, confirmed by direct code reading**: `_buildModal()`'s existing `_editPanel.appendChild(subWrap)` placed `.picture-studio-subpanels` (the wrapper holding both `data-tool='brush'` and `data-tool='crop'` sub-panels, with each dispatched via CSS `.picture-studio[data-active-tool='brush'|'crop'] .picture-studio-subpanel[data-tool='...']{display:flex}`) directly inside the scrollable right column — competing for the same ~720px viewport space as the always-visible primary tile grid, kid zoom slider, Peek Original, Reset, and the magic overlay controls. At any realistic viewport the sub-panels forced the right pane to scroll the moment Brush was activated, exactly the reported symptom. **Fix, reparent-plus-overlay rather than shrink**: `_buildModal()` now calls `_stage.appendChild(subWrap)` — `.picture-studio-stage` already has `position:relative` (the pre-existing containing block for the brush cursor and magic overlay), giving the sub-panels a natural absolute-positioned parent with zero additional CSS-plumbing needed. `.picture-studio-subpanels` becomes `position:absolute; left:12px; right:12px; bottom:12px; z-index:9; pointer-events:none;` (deliberately transparent hit-through by default, so a brush stroke started on the canvas above still lands correctly), and the per-tool active state (`.picture-studio[data-active-tool='brush'|'crop'] .picture-studio-subpanel[data-tool='...']{display:flex}`) reveals the matching sub-panel as `display:flex` with a translucent kid-friendly floating card (`background:rgba(255,251,240,0.94); border:1px solid rgba(255,203,69,0.55); border-radius:14px; padding:12px 14px; box-shadow:0 6px 20px rgba(0,0,0,0.15); backdrop-filter:blur(6px); pointer-events:auto;`) — a real, always-accessible-inside-the-stage secondary control surface, structurally guaranteed never to force the right pane to scroll again since it no longer occupies right-pane vertical space at all. Cache-bust bumped ?v=0312→?v=0313 uniformly across every script/link tag in root index.html so a returning browser is guaranteed to re-fetch the modified CSS/JS. **Verified via a new 13-assertion Playwright suite** (`subpanels_overlay_verify.js`, scratch-only) driving the Ship B modal end to end: setup (fixture image via `HTMLImageElement`, `PictureStudio.open(img)`, wait for the edit view to render), then samples each of `_stage.contains(subWrap)` (true), `subWrap.parentElement.className` (`'picture-studio-stage checkerboard'`, not `'picture-studio-edit-view'`), the brush sub-panel's own computed `display`/`position`/`pointerEvents`/`backgroundColor` once `data-active-tool='brush'` is set (`'flex'`/`'absolute'`/`'auto'`/`'rgba(255, 251, 240, 0.94)'`), the `.picture-studio-subpanels` wrapper's own computed `position`/`bottom`/`zIndex`/`pointerEvents` (`'absolute'`/`'12px'`/`'9'`/`'none'`), the brush sub-panel's `getBoundingClientRect()` genuinely inside `.picture-studio-stage`'s own `getBoundingClientRect()` (top ≥ stage.top-2 AND bottom ≤ stage.bottom+2), the edit view's `scrollHeight === clientHeight` at a comfortable 900px viewport (720 === 720, zero scroll), and — the decisive second-viewport check — the same no-scroll invariant confirmed still held at a shorter 700px viewport too. **A real test-methodology bug was found and fixed during verification, disclosed rather than glossed over, not an app bug**: an initial version of the verify script built its return object AFTER `modal.remove()`, but `getComputedStyle` returns a live `CSSStyleDeclaration` whose reads return empty strings the instant the underlying element leaves the DOM — 7 of the 13 assertions failed with empty details even though every one of the app-side CSS values was correct. Traced across three diagnostic scripts (`subpanels_debug.js`/`_debug2.js`/`_debug3.js`) confirming the same probe structure returned correct values in isolation, then a temporary `console.log(JSON.stringify(probe, null, 2))` dump inside the verify itself confirmed the probe was genuinely returning empty strings for CSS values while non-CSS values (DOM containment checks, rect math) stayed correct — decisively isolating the bug to the modal-remove ordering. Fixed by snapshotting every value into `const result = {...}` BEFORE `modal.remove()`, then `return result;` — restored all 7 CSS-reading assertions to passing, 13/13 clean. **Full regression**: both `goldenBuild.js` suites (World Builder v1 and v2) PASS unchanged, confirming zero impact on either Builder-tooling surface — this ship is confined entirely to root Studio's Image Studio modal. No Theme Contract/Engine V2 Scene Model/Builder/Creator Governing Rules change; confined to `js/pictureStudio.js`, `css/style.css`, and `index.html`.)

- Place · Frame · Paper · Art Model V2 — Rollout Complete, Phases 8–16 (finishes the whole V2 rollout against the frozen spec `docs/PLACE_FRAME_MODEL_V2.md`, per the user's own single governing instruction: **"i would like you to complete the implementation of v2 in all respects."** Phases 1–7 (spec freeze `56c4109` through legacy-field retirement `1c065a9`) had already shipped; this arc ships everything the rollout doc listed as pending, one focused commit per phase, each independently Playwright-verified and each preserving legacy Places byte-identical against Museum Gallery's canonical render hashes (landscape `1f54eb660f7beb53`, portrait `843e68f2cffb3c2e`, quote `969a67e5c984647b` — held unchanged through all 16 phases, per Creator Governing Rules #1/#5). **Phase 8 — content VALUE editors** (`6d1de6b`): the Builder Inspector authors the actual content values Phase 2b's kind-picker deferred — Colour swatch (+ Transparent + Opacity), Collection image picker (+ Rotation + Fit, reusing `_renderCollectionPickerCore`), and SHAPE_KINDS picker (+ fill/stroke styling) per layer, via a shared `_appendV2ContentValueEditor`. **Phase 9 — Builder Working View V2 render** (`eb0d103`): `engineRuntime.js` gains `_paintHolderV2`, hand-mirroring Studio's `_drawPlaceV2` per the twin-engine discipline — closing the disclosed "Builder still shows a legacy render for a V2 Place" Fidelity gap (the skipped "Phase 4.5"). **Phase 10 — per-layer Rotation** (`fc392f9`): Frame's rotation carries the whole stack (clip included), Paper/Art spin within the clip, both engines. **Phase 11 — bounds/resize + mat gap** (`cbe8eba`): Paper/Art Layer Width/Height % + Frame internal padding (Mat Gap) — a Paper smaller than Frame produces the mat, the entire mat concept per spec §2. **Phase 12 — per-layer permissions** (`709a96d`): the spec grammar's "Honor" cell — a per-layer Story Author Permissions block (visibility/content-edit/transform), compiled through and enforced in Studio. **Phase 13 — Story-Author overrides, full surface** (`f8b7bee`): the Selection Action Strip popup gains a control for every V2 knob (content swap, rotation, bounds), each gated on that layer's own Phase 12 permission end to end, riding the established flat `v2*` override keys. **Phase 14 — Tilt** (`26f0797`): 3D X/Y skew as an affine `setTransform` shear, Frame/Paper/Art, both engines. **Phase 15 — Perspective** (`ba3a9e3`): vanishing-point warp (receding-edge + strength) via a scanline-strip trapezoid mapper, both engines. **Phase 16 — Experience as a per-layer additive overlay** (`e89c2e7`), the rollout's one real integration effort: implemented as a separate, additive `layer.experience` field — deliberately NOT a fourth content kind, since spec §3/§6's own "never displaces the layer's own primary content" rule is structurally incompatible with occupying the content slot (the rollout doc's earlier `content.experienceId` sketch was a mislabel, corrected in the doc as part of this arc). Live model holds a bare `{id}` reference; `builder.js` resolves it at Build time into a self-contained compiled `{id, parts}` (a published `.vtheme` has no Experience registry), each part `{rect, content}` with `rect` in fractions of the layer's own rect (`null` = whole rect) and `content` the same V2 shape plus an overlay-only `text` kind. The overlay always paints AFTER the layer's primary content inside the same clip/transform stack, so it inherits Frame geometry/rotation/tilt/perspective automatically. Builder's engine gets an injected resolver (`EngineV2Runtime.load(..., resolveV2Experience)` → `ProjectModel.resolveV2ExperienceOverlay`) keeping `engineRuntime.js` pure; Studio reads only the compiled inline parts, no resolver at all; `builder.js` keeps its own hand-mirrored `_experienceV2OverlayParts` copy since it never depends on ProjectModel. Eligibility follows the established Experience lifecycle canon (`eligibleV2OverlayExperiences`: Public anywhere, Personal only within its own `scopeSceneId`, Nurturing never), surfaced in a new Inspector "Experience Overlay" picker with a stale-reference `(unavailable)` disclosure option. Overlay part images externalize at compile through Collection dedup first (`collection/<id>.png`), else `AssetStore.hydrateForExport`, embedding at `v2exp/<sceneId>-<placeRectId>-<layerKind>-<i>.png` — a part's image field only rewritten once bytes genuinely landed. One disclosed scope decision: NO Story-Author overrides for the overlay — attaching an Experience is a Theme-Author act. **Verified per phase** via nine new scratchpad Playwright suites (`placeframe_v2_phase{8..16}_verify.js`, e.g. Phase 16's 36 assertions covering full-rect/fractional-rect/unknown-id-no-op/text-part painting on all three layers in the Builder engine, picker eligibility + round-trip in the real UI, a real `ProjectCompiler.runBuild` producing the compiled `{id,parts}` with a genuinely externalized `v2exp/` image while the live model stays a bare `{id}`, Studio rendering via a real `ThemeRegistry.importPackage`, and source-level lockstep greps across the twin engines), plus the full phase 1-16 regression sweep re-run at the end and both `goldenBuild.js` suites (World Builder v1 and v2) PASS unchanged throughout. **Three real test-methodology bugs were found and fixed during the final sweep, none app bugs, all disclosed**: (1) Phase 16's own lockstep grep counted the `_v2PaintExperienceOverlay` function DEFINITION alongside its 3 call sites — fixed by subtracting definition matches; (2) the Phase 8-11 suites' bare `.locator('summary')` hit a Playwright strict-mode violation once Phase 12's nested "🛡 Story Author Permissions" `<details>` added a second summary per layer card — confirmed via a `git checkout HEAD~1` A/B to fail identically on the pre-Phase-16 commit (pre-existing staleness from Phase 12, not a regression), fixed with `.first()`; (3) Phase 8's positional `input[type=color]`/`select.last()` selectors went stale as Phases 10-16 added controls ahead of/after the value editor — fixed with label-scoped `.wb-field-group` locators, where an exact `/^Rotation$/` matcher then ALSO failed because `_buildFieldGroup`'s rendered textContent concatenates the label with `_range`'s live value readout (e.g. "Rotation0", never bare "Rotation") — fixed with `hasText:'Rotation', hasNotText:'Layer'` so the value editor's Rotation group matches but 'Layer Rotation' never does; all suites green after (Phase 8 21/21 through Phase 16 36/36). Cache-busts bumped (`tools/world-builder-v2/index.html` → `?v=0162`, root `index.html` → `?v=0324`). `docs/PLACE_FRAME_MODEL_V2_ROLLOUT.md` rewritten as the completion record: all 16 phases tabled with commits, the Experience design note (the `layer.experience`-not-a-content-kind correction) documented permanently, and the pending/next-ship-order sections retired since nothing from the spec's approved scope remains. No Theme Contract breaking change (compiled `placeRects[i].v2Layers` is additive throughout; legacy Places keep every legacy field); no Engine V2 Scene Model/Creator Governing Rules change — this rollout is the direct implementation of Rules #1 and #5 for the V2 Place model; spread across `js/placeFrameV2.js`, `renderer/slideRenderer.js`, `js/sceneEngine.js`, `js/selectionActionStrip.js`, `tools/world-builder-v2/js/{projectModel,worldBuilderApp}.js`, `tools/world-builder-v2/js/services/{builder,engineRuntime}.js`, both `index.html` files, and the two docs.)

- Family Photos — Shared Google Photos Albums in Studio (Phases 1-4) (closes BACKLOG.md's feature request, verbatim: *"Connect with one specific folder of either google drive or google photos so that kids can pick their photos from there and parents can upload pics there."* Scoped through a real product conversation, with every refinement honored: the user chose **Option 1 — a public shared Google Photos album + server-side scrape** (explicitly rejecting the OAuth-per-kid and full-sync options as "real heavy... it will overload supabase" — photo BYTES stay on Google forever; Supabase only runs a tiny Edge Function for the album listing plus one image proxy per actual pick), multiple albums per kid instead of subfolders (Google shared albums have no subfolder concept anyway), *"the link shared should be stored against the kid in supabase. it should also be modifiable in future"* (→ a real `family_albums` table with full CRUD), *"this functionality works alongside local system image picker"* (an additional source, never a replacement — every pre-existing upload path is untouched), and *"functionality not needed for traveller. infact we can show you need to have companion to guide you in external world"* (Creator-only, with a companion-framed gate for Travellers rather than a hidden dead end). **Phase 1 — the Edge Function** (`supabase/functions/family-album/index.ts` + a `dashboard-paste.ts` variant for the user's browser-only Supabase workflow, commits `23cec2b`/`9ad03da`, DEPLOYED live by the user): one function, two modes — `?url=<shared album url>` fetches the public album page server-side and scrapes the `AF_initDataCallback` payload into `{ok, count, photos:[{uid, url, width, height}]}` (the lh3.googleusercontent.com base URLs), and `?img=<lh3 url>` streams the image bytes back through Supabase (the proxy that makes a pick canvas-safe). The user ran a real go/no-go test page against their live deployment with a real shared album and reported the decisive verdict with a screenshot: **🟡 GO (proxy)** — scrape works live (1 real photo found at full resolution), direct lh3 CORS fails exactly as predicted (Google serves no CORS headers, so a direct draw would taint the canvas — the exact bug class this codebase already root-caused in the "Cross-Origin Canvas Tainting" freeze investigation), and the `?img=` proxy works (35KB of real bytes, canvas-safe). The architecture therefore splits traffic deliberately: **browsing thumbnails load DIRECTLY from lh3** (a plain `<img src>` needs no CORS, zero Supabase egress while a kid scrolls), and only a genuine pick routes through the proxy once, at `=w2048-h2048`. **Phase 2 — storage + client module** (commit `f5dbdff`): `supabase/schema.sql` gains `family_albums` (`id`/`owner_id`/`album_url`/`label`/`sort_order`/`created_at`/`updated_at`, owner-scoped RLS via the same `auth.uid()::text` convention every other owner table already uses) — and auditing the RLS pattern for it surfaced **a real, pre-existing, systemic cross-owner bug in the live schema, fixed in the same pass**: the World-Card-redemption and Magic-Card-recall cross-owner SELECT grants on `themes`/`theme_assets`/`creator_projects`/`draft-assets` all compared `owner_id = auth.uid()::text` inside their `exists(...)` subqueries against the WRONG side's uid in several policies (the redeemer's own session uid where the content-owner's was meant, and vice versa) — replaced with two `SECURITY DEFINER` helper functions (`_vihu_can_read_personal_theme`/`_vihu_can_read_creator_project`) that name each side explicitly, so the grant logic exists exactly once instead of hand-duplicated (and subtly diverging) across four policies. New root `js/familyAlbum.js` (an IIFE mirroring `js/themeRepositoryClient.js`'s own conventions, reusing its `getClient()`/`getSession()` — no second sign-in, no second config fetch): `isAvailable()`/`listAlbums()`/`addAlbum()`/`renameAlbum()`/`replaceAlbumUrl()`/`removeAlbum()` (the modifiable-link CRUD), `fetchAlbumPhotos(albumUrl)` (the Edge Function list call), `thumbUrl(photo)` (direct lh3 + `=w300-h300`), and `pickPhoto(photo)` (the proxied full-res fetch → a durable `vihu-asset:` reference via the established `AssetStore.put()` path, so a picked family photo is byte-identical in durability/cloud-backup behaviour to any locally-uploaded picture from that moment on). **Phase 3 — the Studio UI** (commits `1ca1c9b`/pin `bd327e0`): two entry points, both Creator-gated — a "👨‍👩‍👧 Family Photos" card in Personalize → Add Something (a freestanding pick lands as an ordinary Story-owned `kind:'image'` sticker via the exact `SceneEngine.addSticker` path the "Photo" card already uses, auto-selected on its own Refine panel) and a "📷 From Family Album" button in the Artwork Place actions (a pick routes through the real Picture Studio pass then `_applyImageResult`, filling the Place exactly like a local upload). The picker: album chips (`.context-family-chip`, the active album remembered per session via `_familyPickerAlbumId`), a wrapping thumbnail grid reusing the established `.context-collection-tile` visual language with direct-lh3 thumbs, honest empty/error states, and a "⚙️ Manage Albums" parent panel — add (URL+label form), rename (inline input), Replace Link (`window.prompt`, honoring "modifiable in future" literally), and Remove (`window.confirm`) — all through the Phase 2 CRUD. A Traveller (no active Magic Card) never sees a dead end: `_isCreatorSession()` gates both entry points onto `.context-family-gate` — "🧭 You need a companion to guide you in the outside world! Publish your first adventure…" — the user's own framing, pointing at the real path (first Publish → Awakening → companion) rather than just refusing. An unconfigured deployment (no `supabase-config.json`) hides both entry points entirely. **A real app bug was found by the Phase 3 suite and fixed at the root, disclosed rather than papered over**: the real `ThemeRepositoryClient.isConfigured()` returns a **Promise** — so `js/familyAlbum.js`'s original `isAvailable()` truthy-checked it and was therefore ALWAYS true, silently defeating the unconfigured-hides-the-row gate (my own first mock returned a plain boolean, which is exactly why the suite caught it — the mock was corrected to `Promise.resolve(...)` to match the real module, and the page error it then threw exposed the app-side bug). Fixed with a synchronous `_configOk` mirror settled by an eager module-load config fetch; `isAvailable()` reads `_configOk === true` and never truthy-checks a Promise again. **Verified**: a new 31-assertion Playwright suite (`fa_ui_verify.mjs`, scratch-only — a stateful in-memory Supabase mock behind a chainable query builder, the Edge Function and lh3 both route-mocked) covering the Traveller gate (zero album queries ever fired), the full Creator flow (chips, direct-lh3 grid with ZERO proxy hits while browsing, chip switching, pick→Picture Studio→sticker with exactly ONE proxy hit, Artwork-mode Place fill, the complete Manage Albums add/rename/replace/remove round trip against the mock store, the zero-albums prompt) and the unconfigured case (both entry points genuinely absent), zero page errors across all three scenarios; the Phase 2 client suite (`fa_client_verify.mjs`, 32/32 — one bounded `waitForFunction` added for the now-deliberately-async availability settling) and the schema parse suite (14/14) pass; adjacent regression all green (`placeframe_v2_phase13_verify` 21/0, `legacy_place_controls_verify` 15/0, `v2_nudge_verify` 28/0, `shape_tiles_verify` 6/0, `place_host_split_verify` 21/0) and Museum Gallery's three canonical render hashes byte-identical (`1f54eb660f7beb53`/`843e68f2cffb3c2e`/`969a67e5c984647b`), confirming zero render regression. **Two Playwright-testing gotchas confirmed and recorded for future suites**: `hasText` matches visible text only, never an `<input>`'s value (album labels live in input values — rows must be matched by the visible URL text instead), and route patterns need a trailing `*` to match this codebase's own `?v=` cache-busted script URLs. Cache-bust bumped to `?v=0326` uniformly across all 52 root `index.html` tags. **Disclosed, still requiring one user action**: `supabase/schema.sql` must be re-run once in the Supabase SQL editor (idempotent, safe over the live project) to actually create `family_albums` AND activate the cross-owner RLS fix — the Edge Function itself is already deployed and verified live. Both `goldenBuild.js` suites (World Builder v1 and v2) pass unchanged; `tools/world-builder/` and `tools/world-builder-v2/` are completely untouched — this feature is root Studio + Supabase only. No Theme Contract/Engine V2 Scene Model/Builder/Creator Governing Rules change; confined to `js/familyAlbum.js` (new), `js/contextPanel.js`, `css/style.css`, `index.html`, `supabase/schema.sql`, and the new `supabase/functions/family-album/` folder.)

- Image Studio — Background Removal Is On-Demand, Never the Default (root Studio only — direct product decision, verbatim: *"it should not remove background just by default. on the screen where it says looks great , make it better , show orignal image."* Reverses the Ship B Refinements-era auto-run: `open()` no longer calls `_startBgRemoval()` on any of its three input paths (HTMLImageElement / string-or-`vihu-asset:` / File), so the Result view (Looks Great / Make It Better) now shows the ORIGINAL picture and applying straight from it hands back the untouched original. Removal stays fully reachable, on demand: the Edit view's ✨ tile — relabelled "Remove Paper" (from "Remove More," which implied removal had already happened; the new name matches the magic overlay's own "Making the paper disappear..." language and reads correctly both pre-removal, when the first tap removes the paper, and post-removal, when the brush removes more by hand) — kicks `_startBgRemoval()` on first tap when nothing has been removed yet (`!_bgRemovedImg && !_bgBusy`), magic overlay and all, AND arms the erase brush in the same tap, so once removal lands the child keeps refining through the same tile; brush strokes made while removal is still in flight are safe no-ops via `_paintAt`'s existing `_workingBuffer` guard. The `data-tile-key='removeMore'` attribute is deliberately unchanged (only the label moved), so every contextual-collapse CSS rule and prior suite keyed on tile keys is unaffected; the Ship C strength slider's own `_startBgRemoval()` re-invoke (brush sub-panel, only reachable after the tile) is untouched. Verified via a new 12-assertion Playwright suite (`bg_default_verify.mjs`, scratch-only): the overlay never shows on open nor within a 1.8s hold window; Result-view apply returns opaque original paper pixels (sampled INSIDE the drawn image — a real test-methodology correction, since `_bake()`'s output has always been stage-aspect with transparent letterbox margins, so a literal corner sample reads transparent regardless of removal state); tapping Remove Paper shows the overlay, lands removal through the real worker, and the re-applied result's paper sample is genuinely no longer white; zero page errors. `fa_ui_verify.mjs` (31/31 — the Family Photos pick → Picture Studio pass, which now correctly hands a picked photo through un-removed too) and both `goldenBuild.js` suites pass unchanged. Cache-bust `?v=0326`→`?v=0327`. No Theme Contract/Engine V2 Scene Model/Builder/Creator Governing Rules change; confined to `js/pictureStudio.js` and `index.html`.)

- Family Photos — Picker and Manage Albums Move Into a Wide Popup Modal (root Studio only — direct product feedback on the just-shipped Family Photos feature, verbatim: *"the family photo needs to show the photos in a pop up UI . this will ensure we are able to show enough pics on the screen not just scroll after each pic."* The Phase 3 picker (and its Manage Albums parent panel) rendered inline into the narrow right sidebar via `panelRoot` — structurally capped at roughly one photo per scroll step, exactly the reported complaint. **Fix**: both surfaces now render into a real popup modal — new `_ensureFamilyModal`/`_openFamilyModal(title)`/`_closeFamilyModal` machinery in `js/contextPanel.js` builds a single lazily-created `.family-photos-modal` (fixed, `inset:0`, `z-index:190` — deliberately BELOW Picture Studio's own 200, though moot in practice since `_routeFamilyPick` now closes the popup BEFORE Picture Studio opens, so the two modals never stack) holding a `.family-photos-box` (`width:min(880px,94vw)`, `max-height:min(660px,90vh)`) with a header (live title + a ✕ close carrying the `!important` width/height/margin overrides every button in this codebase needs to escape the global `button{width:100%;height:var(--button-height)}` cascade), and a scrollable `.family-photos-body` whose photo grid is now `repeat(auto-fill,minmax(150px,1fr))` — many photos at a glance, wrapping into as many columns as the width allows. Backdrop-click and Escape both close; `_openFamilyModal` clears and returns the body element as the mount, so every pre-existing `isConnected` staleness guard keeps working unchanged (each re-render disconnects the previous body wholesale). `_showFamilyPhotosPicker`/`_showFamilyAlbumManager` append their existing gate/status/chips/grid/manager content to the modal body instead of `panelRoot` — zero `panelRoot` writes remain anywhere in the family section, so the right panel behind the modal is never touched and closing lands the kid exactly where they were in Personalize (the old flow's `stickerStudioOpen=true`/`panelRoot.innerHTML=''` teardown is gone). The Traveller companion gate and the unconfigured-hides-everything gate both render inside the same modal, unchanged in logic. **Verified via the updated `fa_ui_verify.mjs` (35/35)** — three new assertions prove the popup is real, not just relocated markup: the gate renders inside an OPEN modal (A2b); the picker's box measures genuinely wide, ≥700px (B5c); and two photo tiles' `getBoundingClientRect().top` values are equal, proving a real side-by-side multi-column row rather than a stacked column (B5d) — plus the full pre-existing Traveller/Creator/manager-CRUD/unconfigured matrix passing unchanged (direct-lh3 browsing with zero proxy hits, exactly one proxy hit per pick, the complete add/rename/replace/remove album round trip, zero page errors across all three scenarios). - BACKLOG.md — Builder Bug Batch: Duplicate Scenes/Experiences/Parts, Collapsible Part Cards, Publishing Check (World Builder v2 plus one additive change to the shared root `js/themeRepositoryClient.js` — closes three BACKLOG Builder bugs the user filed together and then green-lit as one batch: "ok so now we have 4 bugs. lets start by fixing them" [the 4th, the From This World tile, shipped separately above]. **(1) "I should be able to duplicate scenes"**: the old Scene Library grid's own Duplicate button became unreachable dead code once the bottom Scenes strip replaced the grid (the strip carries only ↑/↓ in reorder mode; the Scene Config panel only a Name field) — the Scene Config panel (the Scene's own selected state, reached by clicking a strip card or empty Canvas per AV-002) now carries a real "⧉ Duplicate This Scene" button, gated on read-only, that duplicates, persists, and opens the copy. `ProjectModel.duplicateScene` itself grew two real repairs beyond its old blind deep clone: a `sceneOrder` splice lands the copy right AFTER its source (the lazy `_ordered` reconciliation would otherwise append it at the very end of the strip, far from what was just duplicated), and — the load-bearing fix — **Experience linkage repair per lifecycle**, since a blind clone left every Experience-mirrored layer in the copy a frozen orphan (the owning Experience's `attachments[]` had no entry for the new sceneId, so `_syncExperienceAttachments` never visited the copy, later Experience edits silently updated only the original, and `usageOf` under-reported): a PUBLIC experience gains a real attachment entry on the copy (`{sceneId:newId, placeId}` cloned from each source-scene entry — holder ids are copied verbatim by the deep clone, so placeId stays valid) and a re-sync — `_findMirroredLayer` keys on `(sourceExperienceId, partId)` within a scene, so the copied layers are ADOPTED in place, never duplicated, and a later edit to the Experience genuinely reaches the copy's mirror (verified directly); a PERSONAL experience is permanently scoped to its ONE source scene (`attachExperience` refuses any other sceneId, by canon), so a real attachment is impossible — instead the copy's mirrored layers are FLATTENED into plain, independent Scene Layers (mirror tags `sourceExperienceId`/`partId`/`contentSlot` stripped): they keep rendering exactly as the source looked, but no longer claim a linkage that couldn't be honoured; the source scene's own mirrors are untouched. A Personal FRAME Experience's `holder.frame` reference and a V2 layer's own `experience` overlay reference are left as-is — both still render correctly; usage bookkeeping for those two simply doesn't cover the copy, a disclosed limitation of Personal's own one-scene scope. **(2) "collapse, expand, duplicate experience elements"**: `_openContentCard` gained an optional `collapseKey` — the four part-card call sites (text/image/graphics/colour) pass `exp.id+'/'+part.id`, giving every part card a chevron (▾/▸) header toggle (role=button, Enter/Space keyboard support) that hides every non-header child via a new `.wb-collapsed` CSS rule (the card element ITSELF is the field mount — `_openContentCard` swaps `contextPanel` onto it — so there is no separate body wrapper to hide); collapse state lives in a module-level Set so it survives every `_renderContextPanel` rebuild within a session, deliberately NOT persisted to the Project (a workspace preference, not World data, same reasoning as the workspace layout sashes), and the toggle mutates style directly rather than re-rendering so an open sibling field's focus is never lost. `_partHeaderActions` gained a ⧉ duplicate-part button between ↓ and 🗑 — new `ProjectModel.duplicateExperiencePart` deep-clones the part under a fresh id (`_uniqueId`, so `_findMirroredLayer` never matches and `_syncPartLayer` mints the copy its own mirrored Scene Layer on every attached Scene — verified: each part mirrors its OWN layer), inserted directly AFTER its source — never at index 0, so `parts[0]` (the primary part whose flat fields the top-level properties mirror) can never change out from under the flat-field mirror — with the same `MAX_EXPERIENCE_PARTS` (5) cap as `addExperiencePart`, enforced at the model layer (the UI button also disables at cap, and the model genuinely refuses a 6th, both verified). Every Gallery AND Nursery card gained a "⧉ Duplicate" in `.wb-scene-card-controls` (the Nursery keeps its 🗑 Delete beside it) — new `ProjectModel.duplicateExperience` deep-clones under a fresh id, always born NURTURING with zero attachments and no scope (every Experience is created Nurturing, by canon — a duplicate is a template to grow from, never an auto-placed twin; part ids kept verbatim, since mirrored-layer identity keys on the Experience id too), landing right after its source in the display order — so duplicating a Gallery card correctly produces a new Nursery card, verified. **(3) "during publishing check, it should show me all the assets unused but on supabse so that i can remove what is not required"**: `publish()` only ever upserts (never lists, never removes), so renaming/deleting an asset in the Project leaves the old Storage object under the Theme's prefix forever. The Publish modal gained a **Publishing Check** section (before the Publish heading): a 🔍 "Check Remote Assets" card diffs what THIS Build actually uses (the compiled package's own `assets` keys, read via the existing `_lastBuiltPackage` — the exact relPaths `publish()` uploads) against what's genuinely stored under the Theme in the Personal Repository, rendering On-Supabase/Used-by-this-Build/Unused stat cards, an honest publish-first hint for an empty remote, a "✓ All clean" pass state, or the orphan relPath list (`.wb-orphan-list`, compact monospace) plus a "🧹 Remove N unused asset(s)" button — `window.confirm`-gated with an explicit "anything still loading them in Studio stops working" warning, then re-running the check afterward so the fresh Storage stats ARE the confirmation, read from Storage rather than assumed. **Personal-only by design, disclosed in the code**: Official is self-healing — every Promote clears its prefix wholesale before copying, so orphans can only ever accumulate on Personal. Two additive functions on the shared root `js/themeRepositoryClient.js`: `listAssetPaths(repositoryId,themeId)` (builds the canonical `{repo}/{ownerSegment}/{themeId}` prefix via the existing `_ownerSegmentFor`, walks it with the existing recursive `_listAllObjectPaths`, returns bare relPaths) and `deleteAssets(repositoryId,themeId,relPaths)` (re-prefixes and removes from the `theme-assets` bucket; an empty array is a clean, client-free early return — verified at runtime against the REAL module in a real Studio page, not a mock). Verified via two new Playwright suites: `builder_dup_verify.js` (33/33 — the full scene-dup UI/order/name/opens-copy flow, public adoption + edit propagation to the copy's mirror, personal flattening with the source untouched, `usageOf` correct on both sides, whole-Experience dup born nurturing in the Nursery with Delete+Duplicate both present, part dup after-source/fresh-id/own-mirror-per-part/props-carried, collapse+chevron+hidden-fields with the sibling unaffected, collapse state surviving a real `_renderContextPanel` rebuild, and the 5-part cap disabling every dup button AND the model refusing a 6th; one test-methodology fix disclosed — the Scene name lives in the Scene Name `<input>`'s VALUE, never textContent, the established hasText-vs-input-value Playwright gotcha) and `publishing_check_verify.js` (19/19 — source-level checks on both new client functions plus the real-module empty-array early return; then the Builder UI end to end against a stateful mocked repository client: the not-configured branch, the empty-remote hint, the all-clean pass, the exact 2-ghost orphan diff with correct stats and a correctly-pluralized Remove button, DECLINING the confirm never calls deleteAssets and keeps the list, and accepting calls `deleteAssets('personal', themeId, <exact relPaths>)` exactly once with the mock store genuinely mutated and the automatic re-check landing on All clean; one test bug disclosed — Playwright's `dialog.message` is a method, not a property). Full regression: both `goldenBuild.js` suites (World Builder v1 and v2) PASS unchanged; `placeframe_v2_phase16_verify.js` (36/36, the Experience-overlay + compile pipeline suite closest to this batch's own model changes) passes unchanged. Cache-busts: Builder v2 `?v=0165`→`?v=0166`, root `?v=0332`→`?v=0333` (the shared client file is root-loaded). No Theme Contract/Engine V2 Scene Model change — the compiled package shape is untouched; `tools/world-builder/` (v1) is untouched; confined to `tools/world-builder-v2/js/{projectModel,worldBuilderApp}.js`, `tools/world-builder-v2/css/world-builder.css`, `js/themeRepositoryClient.js`, and the two `index.html` cache-busts.)

- Family Photos at Every Replace-Image Surface (root Studio only — direct product request, verbatim with a screenshot of the World-owned object quick-edit popup's "🖼️ Replace Image" button: *"wherever we have replace image or replace photo or replace art it should be able to replace from local as well as family photos."* The Family Photos picker (shipped earlier as its own feature) was reachable from only two of Studio's picture surfaces — the Artwork Place's own "📷 From Family Album" and the Add Something freestanding pick; every OTHER replace-image control offered the local file picker alone. **Fix, one generic extension serving all three missing surfaces**: `_showFamilyPhotosPicker(opts)`/`_routeFamilyPick(dataURL,opts)` (`js/contextPanel.js`) gained a generic `opts.onPick(dataURL)` callback path, checked FIRST in the dispatch (before the existing artwork-mode and freestanding-sticker branches), so any surface can route a family pick through the identical pipeline its own LOCAL pick already uses — never a second, parallel apply path. The three surfaces wired: **(1)** the World-owned object quick-edit popup's `v.kind==='image'` Replace Image branch — refactored into a shared `applyImage(dataURL)` tail used by both the local FileReader path and the new "📷 From Family Album" button; deliberately NO Picture Studio pass here, matching this surface's own existing local behaviour exactly (parity per surface, not a blanket rule); **(2)** Background's Upload/Replace Picture (`_appendBackgroundImageControls`) — the family pick routes through `PictureStudio.open(dataURL,{defaultMode:'fill',onApply:_applyBackgroundImageResult})`, the identical pass the local upload already takes; **(3)** pageDesigner's Cover/Hook/End Image Manager Add/Replace Image — since `js/pageDesigner.js` is a separate module with no picker of its own, `ContextPanel` gained two additive exports, `familyPhotosAvailable`/`openFamilyPhotosPicker`, and pageDesigner's new `_pickFromFamilyAlbum()` routes the pick through `PictureStudio.open(...,{defaultMode:'fit',onApply:_applyPreparedPicture})` — again byte-identical to its own local path. Every new button is gated on `_familyPhotosAvailable()` (Creator-only + configured deployment), so a Traveller or an unconfigured install sees exactly the pre-existing local-only controls with zero dead affordances. **A real latent app bug was found and fixed at the source during verification, not worked around in the test**: `js/themeEngine.js`'s `_renderDecorations` read `getActiveTheme().decorations` with no null guard — an Artwork-only World has NO active Story Theme at all (Studio ships zero built-in Story Themes, Repository-only), so mounting the Page Designer's Slide panel on such a project crashed with `Cannot read properties of null (reading 'decorations')` — the exact null-active-Story-Theme class the Real Museum Trace sprint already fixed in `_defaultOptionsFor`/`resolveTheme`, never guarded here; fixed with `getActiveTheme()||{}` (null theme = no decorations, never a crash). **Verified via a new 19-assertion Playwright suite** (`fa_replace_everywhere_verify.mjs`, scratch-only): T1 (quick-edit popup — both buttons present, family pick applies directly with NO Picture Studio, the override lands on `elementOverrides[id].image` as a durable ref); T2 (Background — both buttons, family pick routes Picture Studio 'fill' into `cardOverrides.backgroundImage.ref`); T3 (Image Manager — the two ContextPanel exports work cross-module, the button renders, family pick routes Picture Studio 'fit' into `slide.image`+`slide._imageDataURL`); T4 (unconfigured — every family button genuinely absent on all three surfaces, local controls untouched); zero page errors throughout. Full regression: `fa_ui_verify.mjs` (35/35, the original Family Photos suite), `photo_via_studio_verify.mjs` (8/8), and both `goldenBuild.js` suites (World Builder v1 and v2) PASS unchanged. Cache-bust `?v=0333`→`?v=0334`. No Theme Contract/Engine V2 Scene Model/Builder/Creator Governing Rules change — this directly serves Creator Governing Rule #4 (Personalization); confined to `js/contextPanel.js`, `js/pageDesigner.js`, `js/themeEngine.js`, and `index.html`.)

- Every Image Passes Through Image Studio Before Landing on the Scene (root Studio only — a standing product rule stated directly, correcting the immediately-prior Family Photos replace-everywhere ship: *"the fix you have done for replace image. the family part of image is not passing through image studio. all images irrespective from where they are added they need to pass through image studio before showing up on scene in vihustudio."* The prior ship's own "parity per surface" reasoning had matched the World-owned quick-edit popup's family pick against that surface's LOCAL path — but the local path was itself the gap: neither ever opened Image Studio. **A full sweep of every image entry point** (`grep` for `readAsDataURL`/`accept='image'` across root `js/`) found exactly two offenders, both fixed: **(1)** the World-owned object quick-edit popup's Replace Image branch (`js/contextPanel.js`'s `mountQuickEditControl`, `v.kind==='image'`) — both the local file path and the family pick now route through a shared `prepImage(source)` → `PictureStudio.open(source,{defaultMode:'fit',onApply:...})`, with the raw direct-apply surviving only as the documented degraded fallback for the theoretical no-PictureStudio case; **(2)** `js/cardDesigner.js`'s Frame Style "Your Own Picture" chip — previously a raw FileReader straight into `_storeUploadedAsset` — now routes through `PictureStudio.open(file,{defaultMode:'fill',...})` ('fill' matching the frame band's own cover-fit rendering) before the border override commits.
