Every other surface was confirmed already compliant (Artwork Place, Background, pageDesigner Image Manager, Add Something Photo, the family picker's own artwork/freestanding branches); Collection "From This World" picks are deliberately out of scope — those are Theme-Author-prepared World assets, not raw uploads needing prep. **Verified via the updated 22-assertion suite** (`fa_replace_everywhere_verify.mjs`): T1 was REWRITTEN to assert the exact opposite of its prior "no Picture Studio at this surface" check — the family pick must open the real Picture Studio pass, with a no-premature-apply check confirming the override only lands after Image Studio's own Apply; a new T5 drives the frame chip end to end via a real native filechooser (picture seeded onto the Place first, since the Frame Style controls gate on hasImage), confirming no premature apply and the border's `fill:'image'`+durable ref landing only after the pass. Full regression: `fa_ui_verify.mjs` (35/35), `photo_via_studio_verify.mjs` (8/8), both `goldenBuild.js` suites PASS unchanged. **Disclosed staleness**: `frame_image_verify.js` (the frame chip's original suite) was already stale before this ship — its fixture drives the removed `#scanUpload` bulk importer — and its direct-apply expectation is additionally superseded by this rule; T5 is that surface's current coverage. Cache-bust `?v=0334`→`?v=0335`. No Theme Contract/Engine V2 Scene Model/Builder change — this rule serves Creator Governing Rule #1's spirit (one consistent prep pipeline for every picture); confined to `js/contextPanel.js`, `js/cardDesigner.js`, and `index.html`.)

- Voice MVP Ship 1 — Per-Page Narration (Record + Import, Creator-Only, 60s Cap) (root Studio only — the first real slice of Locked Product Decision #4 (Audio Studio: "per-card narration, record/import audio, audio linked to cards"), turning the Personalize → Add Something Voice tile — the last remaining Coming Soon card — into a real feature. Scoping decisions locked by the product owner via an answered AskUserQuestion, all four honored exactly: attach model **"Both" — per-page narration FIRST, voice-note OBJECTS on the canvas as the agreed follow-up ship (Ship 2, explicitly not started)**; sources **record + import**; gating **Creator-only** (a Traveller sees the companion-framed gate — "You need a companion before you can leave your voice on a page! Publish your first adventure…" — the exact discipline Family Photos already established, never a hidden dead end); length cap **60 seconds** (auto-stop at the cap, the timer gaining a warning style in the last 10s). **Data model, deliberately minimal**: `slide.metadata.narration = {ref, durationMs}` — metadata rides `ProjectManager.serialize()` wholesale, so save/restore/cloud-sync/duplicate-page all needed ZERO persistence changes; the audio blob itself goes through the established `AssetStore.put(blob,{surface:'creator',projectId})` path (confirmed audio-fit with zero AssetStore changes: `put()` is MIME-agnostic via `_toBlob`, the `draft-assets` bucket has no MIME/size restriction, `resolve(ref,{ownerId})` already supports the recallOwnerId cross-owner fallback for a Magic-Card-recalled project, and `hydrateForExport` round-trips audio losslessly), producing a durable `vihu-asset:creator:` reference that syncs to cloud backup exactly like every picture already does; `js/projectManager.js`'s `_collectExportAssetAccessors` gained one narration accessor so a portable `.vihu` file hydrates the audio back to a self-contained data URI on export. **New `js/voiceRecorder.js`** — a pure MediaRecorder engine with NO UI of its own, mirroring the AudioManager/gatewayAudio "module = engine, caller = UI" convention: `start({maxMs,onTick,onAutoStop})`/`stop()`/`cancel()`/`isSupported()`/`isRecording()`; duration measured by wall clock, never blob metadata (Chrome's MediaRecorder webm famously reports Infinity duration — the wall clock is the honest source); mime preference `audio/webm;codecs=opus` → `audio/webm` → `audio/mp4`; permission-denied detection via err.name (NotAllowedError/PermissionDeniedError/SecurityError) so the panel shows an honest, kid-friendly per-cause message ("😕 I couldn't hear you — check your microphone and try again."); `DEFAULT_MAX_MS` deliberately mutable so tests exercise the auto-stop without a real 60-second wait; `cancel()` nulls `onstop`/`ondataavailable` before stopping so a discarded take can never resolve into anything. **The Voice panel** (`js/contextPanel.js`'s `_showVoicePanel`, reusing the family-gate/collection-picker-heading visual language): an idle/recording/preview state machine — idle-empty offers "🎤 Start Recording" + "📁 Import Audio" (import stays available even on a device with no mic support, disclosed honestly); recording shows a pulsing dot + a live "M:SS / 1:00" timer (`voice-timer-ending` red style in the last 10s, `prefers-reduced-motion` kills the pulse) + Stop/Cancel; preview plays the take back ("Here's what you said (M:SS) — keep it?") with Play / "✓ Keep It" (stores the blob, sets narration) / "↩ Try Again"; idle-with-voice offers "▶ Listen" / "🎤 Record Again" / "📁 Import Audio" / "🗑 Remove Voice" with the duration shown in the hint. Import measures duration via an Audio-element metadata probe (best-effort — a webm/opus import can legitimately report Infinity, 0 then just means "no time shown"). Playback resolves through `AssetStore.resolve(ref,{ownerId:slide.recallOwnerId})` so a recalled project's narration plays correctly on the new device. **Playback in Publish is deliberately out of scope, disclosed**: PDF/PNG structurally can't carry audio — narrated exports remain the "foundation for" future Locked Decision #4 anticipates; narration playback is Studio-only today. **Verified via a new 16-assertion Playwright suite** (`voice_verify.mjs`, scratch-only) using Chromium's REAL fake-mic flags (`--use-fake-ui-for-media-stream`/`--use-fake-device-for-media-stream` + `grantPermissions(['microphone'])`) so recording is genuinely real end to end — real getUserMedia, real MediaRecorder producing real webm/opus bytes through the real engine and the real AssetStore, no mocks anywhere in the recording pipeline: V1 Traveller gate (tile real/enabled/not-Coming-Soon, gate shows, no recorder); V2 the full Creator record flow (idle → live timer showing "/ 1:00" with `VoiceRecorder.isRecording()` genuinely true → Stop → preview → Keep It → a durable `vihu-asset:creator:` ref with real duration >500ms on `slide.metadata.narration` → the panel flips to Listen/Record Again/Remove with the duration shown → Listen produces no error); V3 auto-stop at a shortened cap (no Stop click — the cap lands the take in preview on its own, recorder released; Try Again + Cancel returns to idle with the FIRST take still kept); V4 `serialize()` carries narration; V5 importing a real WAV via the native filechooser replaces the narration with a finite metadata-probed duration; V6 Remove Voice clears it; zero page errors throughout. **One test-methodology bug found and fixed in the suite itself, not the app, disclosed**: V5's replaced-ref predicate originally compared refs truncated to 30 chars — but the first 30 chars of every `vihu-asset:creator:proj_…` ref are the SHARED project-id prefix, identical for every asset in one project, so the predicate could never become true; a minimal debug reproduction confirmed the import pipeline itself worked perfectly (probe metadata 0.3s, AssetStore.put resolving a durable ref) before the test's own comparison was corrected to full refs. Full regression: `fromworld_tile_verify.mjs` (13/13 — its "Voice tile still has its Soon pill" assertion updated to assert the exact opposite, the disclosed intended consequence of Voice becoming real, not a regression), `fa_replace_everywhere_verify.mjs` (22/22), `fa_ui_verify.mjs` (35/35), `photo_via_studio_verify.mjs` (8/8), and both `goldenBuild.js` suites (World Builder v1 and v2) PASS unchanged. Cache-bust `?v=0335`→`?v=0336` across all 53 root `index.html` tags (a new `voiceRecorder.js` script tag joins, inserted after `familyAlbum.js`). No Theme Contract/Engine V2 Scene Model/Builder change — `tools/world-builder/` and `tools/world-builder-v2/` are completely untouched; confined to a new `js/voiceRecorder.js`, `js/contextPanel.js`, `js/projectManager.js`, `css/style.css`, and `index.html`.)

- Voice MVP Ship 2 — Voice-Note Objects on the Canvas (🔊 Badges, Tap-to-Play) (root Studio only — the agreed follow-up to Ship 1's per-page narration, and the first half of the user's own directive for this arc: **"lets go for reel publication than. so first add voice object and than second lets do story reel publication feture"** — Ship 3, Story Reel publication, is the immediately-queued second half. A Creator can now drop little 🔊 voice bubbles ANYWHERE on a page — several per page, each carrying its own clip — record one through the real mic or import an audio file, and a clean TAP on the badge right on the canvas plays it. **A sixth sticker kind, riding the shared machinery end to end**: `kind:'voice'` joins glyph/shape/text/doodle/image — the instance carries `voiceRef` (a durable `vihu-asset:` reference via the same `AssetStore.put()` path every picture already uses, so cloud backup/recall behave identically) and `voiceDurationMs` (the wall-clock measured length), created via the existing generic `SceneEngine.addSticker` (`stickerId:'voice.note'`, extra init fields land verbatim — zero SceneEngine changes) — so move/resize/rotate/opacity/lock/duplicate/delete/Object Strip/render-tree selection all work with zero changes to any of those mechanisms, the exact reuse discipline the Shapes/Text/Doodle/Image kinds each already proved. **Renderer** (`renderer/slideRenderer.js`): `_drawSceneVoice(st)` paints a coral disc (`#E67373`, matching the Voice panel's own record-button coral) with a white ring and a centered 🔊 glyph, honoring opacity/rotation — deliberately painting in EVERY render including Publish (Creator Governing Rule #5: a printed badge is an honest "this page has sound in Studio" marker, the same way the audio itself is disclosed as Studio-only until Story Reel); `_stickerBbox` labels the object "Voice Note" and carries `visual:{kind:'glyph',glyph:'🔊'}` — Object Strip's existing glyph-visual dispatch renders the card with ZERO ObjectStrip changes needed. **Capture flow, parameterized rather than duplicated** (`js/contextPanel.js`): the Ship 1 Voice panel's record/preview/import machinery gained one `commit(ref,durationMs)` parameter deciding where a finished clip LANDS — `_setNarration` (page narration, unchanged) or the new `_addVoiceNoteSticker` (mirrors `_addImageStickerFromDataURL`'s own create-and-auto-select shape, landing the kid straight on the new note's Refine panel) — one recording pipeline serving both, never a second implementation; the panel gained a "🔊 Voice Notes" section beneath the narration half (divider, heading, a live per-page count hint, ➕ Add a Voice Note, 📁 Import a Voice Note), all inside the same Creator-only companion-framed gate Ship 1 already established. **Tap-to-play** (`js/app.js`): the scene-drag mouseup branch captures elementId/type before nulling `_sceneDragState`; a CLEAN tap (`wasMoved===false`) on a voice sticker plays it via a new exported `CardDesigner.playVoiceNote` — selection already fired on mousedown, so the tap only adds sound, never rerouting; dragging never plays (verified directly). **Refine panel** (`js/cardDesigner.js`): a "Voice Note" group with a big ▶ Play button showing the clip length; playback lives in one module-level `_playVoiceNote(st,statusEl)` (a shared Audio element, so a canvas tap and the panel's Play stop each other instead of overlapping; resolves through `AssetStore.resolve(ref,{ownerId:slide.recallOwnerId})` — the Magic-Card-recall cross-owner fallback — exactly like narration playback), exported on the CardDesigner api for app.js's tap. **Portable export gap closed, plus a disclosed pre-existing one** (`js/projectManager.js`): `_collectExportAssetAccessors` gained a `md.stickers` loop hydrating `st.voiceRef` AND `st.image` — the latter closes the previously-disclosed gap where image-kind stickers (uploads/Family picks) shipped un-hydrated `vihu-asset:` refs in a portable `.vihu` file. Verified via a new 22-assertion real-fake-mic Playwright suite (`voice_note_verify.mjs` — genuine getUserMedia/MediaRecorder through Chromium's fake audio device, no mocks anywhere in the recording pipeline): the Voice Notes section renders; a real recorded note lands with a durable ref + real duration and auto-selects onto its Refine panel showing "▶ Play (0:01)"; the render tree + Object Strip both carry the 🔊 card; the badge genuinely PAINTS (pixel-sampled coral after deselecting, per the established outline-contamination discipline); a clean canvas tap starts exactly one real playback (an Audio-constructor spy confirms a `blob:` URL resolved from the local cache) while also selecting the note; a second note imported via the real native filechooser coexists independently with the count hint reading 2; DRAGGING the badge moves it ~(160,120) model px with zero playback starts (the wasMoved gate proven directly); the Refine Play button plays through the same shared path; Duplicate/Delete ride the generic sticker machinery (the copy shares the source clip's ref); and a real `saveProjectAs()` download carries every note's clip hydrated to a `data:` URI. **Two test-logic bugs found and fixed in the suite itself, not the app, disclosed**: both notes spawn at the default center (540,675), STACKED — the drag's own hit-test correctly grabs the TOPMOST (last in array), so asserting the FIRST note moved could never pass; and Duplicate copies whichever note is SELECTED (the one just dragged), so the shared-ref check had to compare against the selected note's ref, not `notes[0]`'s. Full regression: `voice_verify.mjs` (16/16, Ship 1's own suite — the parameterized capture flow is byte-equivalent for narration), `fromworld_tile_verify.mjs` (13/13), `fa_ui_verify.mjs` (35/35), `photo_via_studio_verify.mjs` (8/8), and both `goldenBuild.js` suites (World Builder v1 and v2) PASS unchanged, zero page errors throughout. Cache-bust `?v=0336`→`?v=0337`. No Theme Contract/Engine V2 Scene Model/Builder change — `tools/world-builder/` and `tools/world-builder-v2/` are completely untouched; confined to `renderer/slideRenderer.js`, `js/contextPanel.js`, `js/cardDesigner.js`, `js/app.js`, `js/projectManager.js`, `css/style.css`, and `index.html`.)

- Voice MVP Ship 3 — Story Reel Publication (Narrated Slideshow Video) (root Studio only — the second half of the user's own directive for this arc: **"lets go for reel publication than. so first add voice object and than second lets do story reel publication feture"** — and the direct answer to the question that started the whole voice arc: "if a page has narration how can it be published... if multiple pages of a book has narration how will it publish." The Publish flow's LAST Coming Soon destination becomes real: Story Reel is now a genuine narrated slideshow VIDEO — every page renders through the exact same `SlideRenderer.buildPayload`+`render` pipeline the editor/Book/Carousel already use (Creator Governing Rule #5, Publish Fidelity — never a second rendering path), holds on screen for its own narration's REAL length (a 3-second default beat when silent), and the narrations stitch in as the audio track; the child downloads a real 1080×1920 webm ready to post as an Instagram Reel, composed entirely client-side with zero server involvement. **New `js/reelComposer.js`** — a pure composition engine with no UI of its own (the exact module discipline `js/voiceRecorder.js` established: module = engine, caller = UI): `canvas.captureStream(fps)` supplies the video track, with a rAF repaint loop keeping frames flowing (a canvas nobody draws to may stop emitting frames entirely — the load-bearing gotcha the investigation flagged up front); the codebase's FIRST AudioContext (confirmed — nothing else constructs one) + `createMediaStreamDestination()` supplies the audio track, each page's narration an `AudioBufferSourceNode` started the moment its page appears; `MediaRecorder` stitches both into one file, mime preference `vp9,opus`→`vp8,opus`→`webm`→`mp4` (webm in practice), started with a 250ms timeslice so chunks flow and relying on the spec's own dataavailable-before-stop guarantee for the final chunk. Under autoplay policy the context may start suspended — the publish flow's own clicks give the page sticky activation, so `resume()` during Publishing works; if it somehow stays suspended the video still records, with silence, never a crash. `decodeAudio(arrayBuffer)` (callback-form `decodeAudioData`, the broadest-compat signature) resolves narration bytes — the recorder's own webm/opus or whatever a Story Author imported — to a real AudioBuffer, resolving null on any failure so an undecodable clip means a silent page, never a broken publish. **Composition records in REAL TIME** (MediaRecorder records a live stream — a reel carrying 30 seconds of narration takes ~30 seconds to film), disclosed in the module's own header and owned by PublishStudio's messaging. **`js/storyDestinations.js`**: REEL's `comingSoon:true` stub (a deliberate architecture placeholder since Sprint 9.0.4, its interface left in place for exactly this day) is replaced with real hooks — `createCanvas` mints a fresh 1080×1920 canvas per page (which then IS the page bitmap, no copy needed); `renderPage` reuses the shared `_renderSlideInto` (no transparency — video has no meaningful alpha; letterbox bars fill from the page's own background-colour proxy, same as the PDF path); `encodePage` returns a THENABLE payload when the page has narration — `AssetStore.resolve(narration.ref,{ownerId:slide.recallOwnerId})` (the Magic-Card-recall cross-owner fallback) → `fetch(url).arrayBuffer()` → `ReelComposer.decodeAudio` — with the decoded buffer's own real duration driving the page hold (`max(1500ms, duration+450ms tail)` — `narration.durationMs` can legitimately be 0 for an imported clip whose metadata probe failed, Ship 1's own disclosed case, so the decode is the honest source); `finish()` returns a Promise composing every page via `ReelComposer.compose` and naming the file `<title>_reel.webm`. Three OPTIONAL, additive presentation fields join the destination contract — `publishMessages` (Reel's own 'Painting your scenes… / Warming up the camera… / Filming your story… / Adding movie magic…' beats replace the book-shaped 'Binding your book…'), `finishingMessage` ('Filming your story… this takes a minute 🎥', shown for the whole real-time compose), and `progressNoun` ('Scene X of Y' instead of 'Page X of Y') — Book/Carousel don't carry them and fall back to the classic copy. **`js/publishStudio.js`** — the smallest honest change to a fully-synchronous state machine, exactly as the investigation scoped it: `_renderNextPage`'s loop and `_finalizePublish` now AWAIT a thenable when a hook returns one (the synchronous Book/Carousel path is byte-identical — verified by their own suites passing unchanged); `ctx` gains `slide` (additive — the encode step needs `slide.metadata.narration`, Book/Carousel ignore it); `_finalizePublish` split into itself plus `_completePublish(out)` so the async finish shows the destination's finishingMessage while filming runs, with cancel still honored at completion — a cancelled publish never hands a file over, preserving the locked cancel-honesty principle; the hardcoded 'Story Reel is coming soon — check back after we film it. 🎬' banner text is genericized ('This one is coming soon — check back later! ✨') since no built-in destination is Coming Soon anymore — the banner machinery stays for any future `register()`-ed destination that ships inert, and the generic `dest.comingSoon` gates (format-pick disable, the Publishing-entry bounce) are untouched, simply never triggering now; Celebration gains reel-aware copy ('Your story is now a movie!', '✓ Your reel is ready. Download again any time.', a 🎬 'Download My Reel' button via finish()'s own celebrateLabel/celebrateGlyph). **`index.html`**: `reelComposer.js` loads immediately BEFORE `storyDestinations.js` (which references it); cache-bust `?v=0337`→`?v=0338` uniformly across all 54 tags. Verified via a new 15-assertion real end-to-end Playwright suite (`reel_verify.mjs` — the actual Publish Studio flow, a real imported WAV narration, zero mocks anywhere in the composition pipeline): the Reel destination card renders with NO Coming Soon chip/class and its format pick genuinely enables Continue; a full 2-page publish (page 1 narrated, page 2 silent) runs the real ~5s of filming and reaches Celebration with a real blob; the blob is a genuine video (>20KB, `video/webm` mime, `_reel.webm` filename, and — decisively — the EBML magic bytes `0x1A45DFA3` byte-checked on the actual blob's own first four bytes, not inferred from the UI); the Publishing stage genuinely showed 'Scene X of Y'; the Celebration copy reads 'Your story is now a movie!' with the 'Download My Reel' button; zero page errors across the whole session. One test-authoring fix disclosed (not an app bug): `AppState` is a top-level classic-script `const` — visible to `page.evaluate` through the global lexical scope but never a `window` property, so `window.AppState` reads undefined. Full regression: `voice_note_verify.mjs` (22/22), `voice_verify.mjs` (16/16), `fromworld_tile_verify.mjs` (13/13), `fa_ui_verify.mjs` (35/35), `photo_via_studio_verify.mjs` (8/8), and both `goldenBuild.js` suites (World Builder v1 and v2) PASS unchanged. **Disclosed scope boundaries**: composition is real-time by nature (no WebCodecs fast-path this ship — a future optimization, not a gap); the container is webm (Instagram accepts uploads via the app/site which transcode server-side; a true in-browser mp4 would need WebCodecs or a wasm muxer, named as possible future work); voice-note STICKERS (Ship 2's 🔊 badges) deliberately do NOT play in the reel this ship — the reel's audio track is the per-page narration, the model the user's own publish question was about; mixing badge clips in is a clean future extension of the same compose pipeline. This closes the whole three-ship voice arc — Ship 1 (narration), Ship 2 (voice-note objects), Ship 3 (Story Reel) — and with it the last Coming Soon destination in the Publish flow, plus Locked Product Decision #5's own second priority (Instagram Reel) gains its first real implementation. No Theme Contract/Engine V2 Scene Model/Builder change — `tools/world-builder/` and `tools/world-builder-v2/` are completely untouched; confined to a new `js/reelComposer.js`, `js/storyDestinations.js`, `js/publishStudio.js`, and `index.html`.)

- Story Reel — Blurred Backdrop Replaces the Flat Letterbox Bars (root Studio only — a direct bug report against the just-shipped Story Reel, verbatim: **"the exported reel has blank spaces on top and bottom."** Root-caused by geometry rather than guessed: a 1080×1350 (4:5) authored page contains into the 1080×1920 (9:16) reel frame BY WIDTH — `Math.min(dw/sw, dh/sh)` — leaving ~285px of bar above and below, which `_fitCompositeInto` filled with a single flat colour sampled from the page's own top-left pixel. Correct as far as it went (never crop or stretch a Scene to reach a platform's frame edges, Creator Governing Rule #1) but it reads as unfinished padding rather than a composed frame. **Fix — the same treatment Reels/Shorts themselves apply to a non-9:16 upload**: a new `_drawBlurredBackdrop(dctx, srcCanvas, dw, dh)` pre-shrinks the page onto a tiny 64px-wide canvas so the browser's OWN image smoothing does the averaging (the bed is genuinely soft even where `ctx.filter` is unavailable — the filter is applied on top when present, never depended on), draws that back up past cover with a 1.14 overscan so the blur's own soft edge falls off-frame rather than showing as a visible seam, then lays a light `rgba(0,0,0,0.18)` scrim so the sharp page stays the focal point; `_fitCompositeInto` gains an additive `opts.backdrop==='blur'` branch that paints the bed and then draws the contained page on top with a soft drop shadow (`shadowBlur` ≈3.5% of the frame's smaller dimension) so the page reads as sitting ON the bed rather than pasted into it. Every authored pixel stays visible and undistorted — nothing is re-laid-out, stretched, or cropped. **Scoped additively**: only REEL's `renderPage` passes `backdrop:'blur'`; Story Book and Story Carousel never pass it and their composite is byte-identical (confirmed by their own suites passing unchanged). Verified via a new 10-assertion Playwright suite (`reel_backdrop_verify.mjs`, scratch-only) rendering a real page through the real REEL destination at 1080×1920 with the page background forced to `#E63946`, then sampling `topBar`/`bottomBar`/`barNearPageEdge`/`pageTop`/`pageBottom`/`cornerTL`/`cornerBR`: the bars are NOT a flat copy of the page colour (they differ by >15) but genuinely carry the page's own colour through the scrim (r≈`230*0.82`, and r>g and r>b — a real derived bed, not a fabricated fill); the page area itself is untouched; the drop shadow is measurable at the page edge (`barNearPageEdge.r < topBar.r - 8` — added deliberately after the shadow proved hard to judge by eye on a flat-colour fixture, so the assertion is numeric rather than a screenshot opinion); every frame corner is fully opaque (no empty video pixels). Full regression: `reel_verify.mjs` (15/15), `voice_note_verify.mjs` (22/22), `voice_verify.mjs` (16/16), and both `goldenBuild.js` suites (World Builder v1 and v2) PASS unchanged. Cache-bust `?v=0338`→`?v=0339`. No Theme Contract/Engine V2 Scene Model/Builder change; confined to `js/storyDestinations.js` and `index.html`.)

- Story Reel — Page-Turn Transitions Between Scenes (+ a real fix for an empty reel when no page carries narration) (root Studio only — direct product request, verbatim: **"lets add page turning animations also."** Scenes no longer hard-cut: a storybook leaf sweeps right-to-left off the spine, bowing as it goes, darkening where it angles away from the light, catching a bright band along its curved free edge, and casting a shadow onto the page it uncovers. **The technique, and why**: canvas 2D has no perspective transform, so the turn is deliberately a 2D illusion sold entirely by LIGHT rather than by geometry — a genuine 3D page flip would need WebGL, a whole second rendering stack for one transition. `paintPageTurn(g, from, to, raw, W, H)` (exported on the api, pure, so it is measurable rather than a judgement call) eases progress via `_easeInOutSine`, fills black, draws the incoming page full-frame, computes `foldX = W*(1-t)`, and compresses the outgoing leaf into `[0,foldX]` as 48 vertical strips — each drawn 1px wider than its slot, which is what kills the seams a naive strip mapper leaves — with a `H*(1+0.05*sin(πt)*u0^1.5)` bulge so the free edge bows outward the way a real page does mid-lift. Two gradients do the rest: one over the leaf (darkest at the spine, lifting toward the fold, a white highlight band at 0.86 of the way across) and one past the fold casting the leaf's own shadow onto the page being revealed. **Sequencing — the part that had to be right**: the rAF draw loop now OWNS turn progress, read from `_nowMs()` — the same clock the sequencer's `setTimeout` uses — so the two can never disagree about what should be on screen; `nextPage()` starts the turn and defers `settlePage(p)` (which sets `currentBitmap`, starts narration, and schedules the hold) until the turn completes, so a clip is never spoken over a half-turned page and no page loses screen time to the transition. `js/storyDestinations.js`'s REEL_FORMATS declares `transition:'page-turn'` and `finish()` passes it through, so a future format can opt out with `'none'` and still hard-cut. **ALSO FIXED in the same ship — a real defect that shipped with Story Reel, found by this feature's own verification rather than caused by it**: `createMediaStreamDestination()`'s audio track reports `readyState:"live"` even when nothing is ever connected to it, but delivers no samples — the muxer waits for audio that never arrives and finishes with a single empty `dataavailable` chunk, so a reel where NO page carries voice composed to a 0-byte file. That is the ordinary case for a child who simply hasn't recorded anything, and Ship 3's own verification only ever tested WITH narration, so it could not have caught it. Diagnosed rather than assumed a test artifact: canvas size, media-device launch flags, duration, user activation and AudioContext state were each ruled out in turn; an instrumented run (compose kicked WITHOUT awaiting inside `page.evaluate`, so the page's own event loop ran freely, with `MediaRecorder` monkeypatched to count chunks and bytes and rAF ticks counted independently) reported `rafTicks:112, chunks:1, bytes:0, tracks:["audio:live","video:live"]` — a healthy repaint loop, both tracks live, one empty chunk. Adding a real 1-second AudioBuffer to page 1 flipped it to `chunks:5, bytes:82793`, isolating the cause exactly. **Fix at the source**: the destination is now fed real silence for the whole recording — a `ConstantSourceNode` with `offset.value=0` (fallback: a looping half-second silent BufferSource for a browser without it) connected the moment `audioDest` is created and stopped on both `rec.onstop` and `rec.onerror`. Verified decisively: the same all-silent-pages reel composes to **0 bytes before the fix and 64,739 bytes after**. Verified via a new 12-assertion Playwright suite (`reel_pageturn_verify.mjs`, scratch-only) driving `paintPageTurn` directly with flat red/blue 400×700 pages and walking the middle row to locate the fold numerically: at t=0 the outgoing page still covers the frame, at t=1 the incoming one does, mid-turn the frame is genuinely SPLIT (leaf left of the fold, next page right of it); the fold travels leftward as t grows (it is motion, not a crossfade) and the leaf stays fully opaque throughout (a crossfade would show it fading); the leaf darkens toward the spine (`spine.r < nearFold.r - 10`) and casts a real shadow past the fold (`justPastFold.b < farPastFold.b - 10`); the Reel format declares its transition; both `'none'` and `'page-turn'` compose real non-empty video; and the turn adds its own real time to the reel (~520ms per turn, bounded 300–900ms). Full regression: `reel_verify.mjs` (15/15), `reel_backdrop_verify.mjs` (10/10), `voice_note_verify.mjs` (22/22), `voice_verify.mjs` (16/16), and both `goldenBuild.js` suites (World Builder v1 and v2) PASS unchanged. Cache-bust `?v=0339`→`?v=0340`. No Theme Contract/Engine V2 Scene Model/Builder change — `tools/world-builder/` and `tools/world-builder-v2/` are completely untouched; confined to `js/reelComposer.js`, `js/storyDestinations.js`, and `index.html`.)

- Four Studio Bugs, Shipped Together — Moveable Means Rotatable + Resizable, "Start Something New", the My Projects Placeholder, and Naming Your Project (root Studio only — four bugs the product owner filed in one batch, each root-caused separately and verified together. **(1) "world own image when marked as movable by author means not just repositioning but also rotation and resizable. currently its not happening."** Traced rather than guessed: Move and Resize already worked at the render layer — `_supportsResize` already returns true for a `decoration`/`sticker`/`text` object whose `locked` is false (and `locked = !layer.moveable` since the Honour World-Owned Object Commitments sprint), and `_layerDrawDecoration` already applied a Story-Author `ov.size` and `ov.position`. The real gap was ROTATION, in two places at once: `renderer/slideRenderer.js`'s `_layerDrawDecorationImage` read only the Theme-Author's compiled `d.rotation` and never a Story-Author `ov.rotation`, so an override had nowhere to land; and `js/contextPanel.js`'s quick-edit Rotation slider was gated on `v.kind==='text'` only — a boundary disclosed honestly at the time precisely BECAUSE image/shape rotation was a compiled-only field no override could reach, so a slider there would have been a dead-end control. Both closed together: `_layerDrawDecorationImage` now resolves `ov.rotation` with precedence over `d.rotation` (the exact tri-state ov-beats-compiled precedence every other overridable field on these objects already follows, byte-identical when neither is set), the shape branch of `_layerDrawDecoration` merges `ov.rotation` alongside the `ov.fillColor` it already merged (still building a copy only when an override genuinely exists, so `d` passes through untouched otherwise), and the slider's gate widens to `text|image|shape`. Colour is deliberately still excluded — a full-bleed background fill has no meaningful orientation, and rotating one only ever exposes its own corners. **(2) "Change new idea story world category to start something new in which a blank page with no world association is started."** The old `more` ("More Ideas") entry in `js/creationFlow.js`'s `CREATION_TYPES` had no themes of its own and only ever led to an empty World screen; it becomes `{id:'blank', title:'Start Something New', desc:'A blank page — no world, just your ideas.', blank:true}` — the ONE branch on Screen 1, skipping Screen 2 entirely into a new `_finishBlank(type)` that creates the first page and sets `AppState.project.theme`/`.artworkTheme` to `null`. **The load-bearing detail, confirmed by reading `js/themeEngine.js` rather than assumed**: `_finishBlank` deliberately never calls `applyTheme(null)` — `getTheme(id)` does `if(id){...} return ThemeRegistry.get(DEFAULT_THEME_ID);`, so `applyTheme(null)` silently INSTALLS `storybook-classic`, the exact opposite of "no world association"; `applyArtworkTheme(null)` IS a genuine, supported clear (it resolves an absent/unknown id to `null` by design) and is called purely for its side effects — thumbnail invalidation, UI refresh, and stopping any World ambience already playing. Rendering with no Theme at all is safe and already exercised: `renderer/slideRenderer.js` carries `FALLBACK_THEME`/`FALLBACK_OPTIONS` and `js/themeEngine.js` carries `_NO_THEME_FALLBACK` precisely because a Repository-only Studio boots with zero registered Story Themes (the Real Museum Trace sprint) — a blank page is that same already-handled state, reached on purpose. **(3) "The project view shows very big placeholder for any project. its not beautiful."** Root cause was a CSS cascade-order bug, not a sizing choice: `_renderMyProjectsScreen`'s grid div carried BOTH `creation-flow-grid` and `creation-flow-project-grid`, and `.creation-flow-grid` is defined LATER in `css/style.css` at equal specificity — so its `repeat(auto-fill,minmax(200px,1fr))` + flat 20px gap silently WON and `.creation-flow-project-grid`'s own intended 4-column + `clamp()` gaps were dead code the whole time. Dropping the generic class lets the project grid's own rule apply; separately `.creation-flow-project-thumb` changed from an uncapped `aspect-ratio:4/5` (which on a ~225px card grew a ~281px-tall slab of near-empty cream whenever a project has no thumbnail yet) to `height:clamp(78px,10vh,110px)` with a soft gold-tinted gradient and a smaller glyph — compact and uniform whether or not a real thumbnail exists, image still covering, glyph still centered. **(4) "allow creator to name their project."** `#bookTitle` — the SAME element that has sat hidden inside `#story-tab` since Locked Decision #1 — is relocated into `.header-center` and un-hidden, styled (`.header-project-name`) as a quiet click-to-type title rather than a boxed form field: transparent until hovered/focused, capped at `min(320px,26vw)` so it can never crowd out the World readout beside it. Deliberately a relocation, not a second field: it names the project (it is what My Projects labels a card with, via `ProjectManager._syncProjectStore`) and, if a World chooses to show a book title on the page, it is that too — one name, one source of truth, and every `getElementById('bookTitle')` consumer (`js/app.js`, `js/projectManager.js`, `js/publishStudio.js`, `js/pageOps.js`, `js/storyDestinations.js`, `js/previewStudio.js`, `js/thumbnails.js`) is untouched. `serialize()` already prefers the DOM over `AppState` and `markDirty` was already wired, so PERSISTENCE was never the gap — the gap was every in-memory reader (`js/pageDesigner.js`, `js/publishStudio.js`, `js/publishValidator.js`) that reads `AppState.project.bookTitle` directly and would otherwise show a stale name until the next deserialize; `js/app.js` now mirrors the field into `AppState` on `input`. **This amends Locked Product Decision #1**, which had hidden the editable Book Name — see the amendment note there rather than leaving the contradiction silent. **Verified via a new 36-assertion Playwright suite** (`four_bugs_verify.mjs`, scratch-only) across three scenarios: S1 seeds a synthetic Artwork theme carrying a moveable+editable image decoration (a 16×16 four-quadrant PNG, chosen deliberately so a rotation is decisively readable from a single sampled pixel rather than judged by eye) and a moveable+editable shape decoration — confirms both land in the render tree unlocked, the image gets all 8 resize handles, a real `SceneEngine.setSize` genuinely grows the rendered bbox, the quick-edit popup now offers a Rotation control for BOTH image and shape kinds, a real slider drag writes `elementOverrides['deco-img'].rotation === 180`, and — the decisive check — the same canvas pixel that paints RED (the image's top-left quadrant) at 0° paints YELLOW (its bottom-right quadrant) at 180°, so the canvas genuinely rotates rather than merely storing a value; S2 confirms the "Start Something New" card exists, "More Ideas" is gone, clicking it never shows a World grid, the editor opens with `theme===null`/`artworkTheme===null`/`getActiveArtworkThemeId()` cleared and exactly one page, and a theme-less page still paints; S3/S4 confirm `#bookTitle` is visible in the header with exactly one instance, typing updates both `AppState.project.bookTitle` and `serialize()`, the saved project shows up in My Projects under the typed name, and the grid no longer carries the generic class, genuinely resolves 4 columns, and caps its thumbnail below 115px (and shorter than it is wide). Zero page errors in every scenario. **Full regression**: both `goldenBuild.js` suites (World Builder v1 and v2) PASS unchanged; Museum Gallery's three canonical render hashes are byte-identical (`1f54eb660f7beb53`/`843e68f2cffb3c2e`/`969a67e5c984647b`), confirming zero render regression for a theme that authors no rotation override; `fromworld_tile_verify.mjs` (13/13, Creation Flow Screen 1 — the file whose `CREATION_TYPES` changed), `photo_via_studio_verify.mjs` (8/8), `bg_default_verify.mjs` (12/12), `fa_replace_everywhere_verify.mjs` (22/22, the quick-edit popup this ship's Rotation gate lives in), `placeframe_v2_phase13_verify.js` (21/21), `legacy_place_controls_verify.js` (15/15), `v2_nudge_verify.js` (28/28), and `place_host_split_verify.js` (21/21) all pass unchanged (the last four hardcode port 8940 with no self-startup — the already-documented staleness class — so a real server was started on that exact port to run them for genuine confirmation rather than skipped). Cache-bust `?v=0340`→`?v=0341`. No Theme Contract/Engine V2 Scene Model/Builder change — `tools/world-builder/` and `tools/world-builder-v2/` are completely untouched; confined to `renderer/slideRenderer.js`, `js/contextPanel.js`, `js/creationFlow.js`, `js/app.js`, `css/style.css`, and `index.html`.)

- Image Studio Gains the Full Draw Your Own Stack — By Reusing Studio's, Not Rebuilding It (root Studio only — closes BACKLOG's "Image Studio: draw + rotate" bug's draw half, whose own clarification was *"not just draw, draw shapes, add colors to them, draw lines — the complete doodle func. should be there as part of beautifying image."* The product owner then framed the approach itself, and that framing is the whole shape of this ship: **"we already have a a draw your own functionality in studio why cant we add that into image studio ?"** — a directive to REUSE what already works rather than author a second doodle implementation. **The join surface is five additive exports on `js/cardDesigner.js`'s own api and nothing else** — `DOODLE_MEDIA` (the four `{id,icon,label,palette}` entries: Crayon/Pastel/Brush/Spray), `drawDoodleStroke` (`_drawDoodleStrokeOnCtx`), `buildShapeSilhouettePath` (`_buildShapeSilhouettePath2D`), `shapeLetterChar`, and `padLetterFont`. Nothing about cardDesigner's own pads or panels changes: `_drawDoodleStrokeOnCtx` was ALREADY pure — no module state, no `AppState`, deterministic, needing only that the caller sets `lineCap`/`lineJoin` to `'round'` first and supplies its own normalized-point `mapPt` mapper — and the three shape helpers are likewise pure geometry, so the reuse needed zero refactor of the source. **Data model — vector, in image-fractional coordinates**: `_state.doodle` holds strokes (`{points,color,width,medium}`, points in 0..1 of the SOURCE image) and shapes (`{shape,x,y,w,h,fill,fillOn,stroke,strokeOn,strokeW}`), assigned in `open()` rather than in `DEFAULT_STATE` — a real bug avoided by design, since `Object.assign` copies an array by REFERENCE, so a `doodle:[]` sitting in `DEFAULT_STATE` would be the SAME array for every session and one picture's drawing would bleed into the next. This shape also sidesteps both of the blockers a raster layer would have hit: it never depends on `_workingBuffer` (null until background removal actually runs) and never needs `_cleanupHistory` (which stores alpha-byte deltas — unusable for colour). **One shared painter, composited inside the existing transform**: `_paintDoodleLayer(g,dx,dy,dw,dh,srcW)` is called immediately after the `drawImage` in BOTH `_paintOne` (preview, where the image is drawn at `-iw*z/2 … iw*z` for preview zoom `z`) and `_bake` (output, drawn 1:1 at `-iw/2 … iw` because the whole output canvas is already rescaled by `1/z`) — inside the same already-applied translate/rotate/flip, so pan, zoom, rotation, flip and fit-scaling all carry the drawing automatically and preview and output structurally cannot disagree. It clips to the picture rect (nothing paints onto the surrounding stage — which also cleanly handles a stroke left partly outside by a later crop) and resets `ctx.filter='none'` (Enhance's colour filter belongs to the photograph, not to the child's drawing). **Pointer mapping**: a new `_screenToImageFraction` genuinely inverts translate → rotate → flip in order — deliberately NOT reusing the existing `_screenToContent`, which only ever runs post-background-removal (a step that resets rotation and flip to 0) and so correctly ignores both; drawing is available at ANY time, so the full inverse is required. **Crop**: Keep This remaps every fraction onto the new frame (`_remapDoodleForCrop`) and snapshots the layer into `_preCropSnapshot`, so Undo Trim restores the drawing too — chosen over clearing the doodle (data loss) or disabling Trim (awkward); Trash It leaves dimensions unchanged and needs no remap at all. **Shapes** place by drag (a plain tap stamps a comfortable 0.25×0.25 default centred on the tap), with fill and outline each independently toggleable through the shared colour kit; outline width stays uniform via a DOMMatrix-transformed `Path2D` (`placed.addPath(built.path, new DOMMatrix().translate(x,y).scale(w/1000,h/1000))`) rather than a scaled context, which would stretch a stroke anisotropically — with a scaled-context fallback in a try/catch, disclosed in the code as approximate. The `'custom'` shape kind is deliberately excluded from the picker: it needs its own silhouette-drawing pad, and freehand mode already covers "draw any line". **Adding a tool to Image Studio needs four touch points and all four are wired** — the `_buildTile` call, `_subPanels.draw`, `_EDIT_HINTS.draw` ("Pick a colour, then draw right on your picture."), and the three CSS selector lists (subpanel-show, contextual tile-collapse, edit-actions-row). **Verified 26/26** via a new Playwright suite (`image_studio_draw_verify.mjs`, scratch-only) driving the REAL modal on a real inline-generated PNG: the Draw tile exists and contextually collapses the others while showing Back/Done and the retitled hint; all four media genuinely paint and render distinctly; a stroke lands under the pointer, and STILL does after a real 90° turn (the decisive check on the rotation-aware inverse — the same point samples the stroke's colour afterward); shapes stamp a real filled silhouette; Undo and Clear behave; and the baked output carries the drawing. **One test-methodology bug found and fixed, disclosed rather than glossed over — not an app bug**: the "all four media paint" check initially FAILED for Spray with a pure-white sample, because Spray is deliberately a deterministic scatter of separate dots and an exact single-pixel probe can legitimately land between them; fixed by counting non-white pixels in a small region (`inkInRegion`) instead of probing one pixel. A separate harness fix: the boot-time Creation Flow overlay intercepted every pointer event, so the test hides it before opening the modal. **Full regression**: both `goldenBuild.js` suites (World Builder v1 and v2) PASS unchanged; Museum Gallery's three canonical render hashes are byte-identical (`1f54eb660f7beb53`/`843e68f2cffb3c2e`/`969a67e5c984647b`) — structurally guaranteed, since `git diff --stat` confirms `renderer/slideRenderer.js` was never touched, but verified anyway; `photo_via_studio_verify.mjs` (8/8), `bg_default_verify.mjs` (12/12), `fa_replace_everywhere_verify.mjs` (22/22), `four_bugs_verify.mjs` (36/36), `fromworld_tile_verify.mjs` (13/13), `voice_note_verify.mjs` (22/22), `shape_tiles_verify.js` (6/6), `v2_nudge_verify.js` (28/28), and `legacy_place_controls_verify.js` (15/15) all pass unchanged (the last three hardcode port 8940 with no self-startup — the already-documented staleness class — so a real server was started there for genuine confirmation rather than skipping them). Cache-bust `?v=0341`→`?v=0342`. **Disclosed scope**: this is Task #29's DRAW half only — rotation in Image Studio stays 90°-step as it was, its own separate remaining item. No Theme Contract/Engine V2 Scene Model/Builder change — `tools/world-builder/` and `tools/world-builder-v2/` are completely untouched; confined to `js/cardDesigner.js` (+15, exports only), `js/pictureStudio.js`, `css/style.css`, and `index.html`.)

- Move Pad + Spin Dial for Every Moveable Object (root Studio only — a direct product request, verbatim: **"whenever there is a moveable flag true with any object i need the 8 direction mover like we did in builder along with 360 degree rotation spinner."** Two clarifications answered by the product owner via AskUserQuestion, both honored exactly: the spinner is **"A real circular dial"** (a round widget you drag the handle around, with a degree readout — deliberately NOT another 0-359 range slider; Builder has no dial at all, its rotation is a plain slider) and the scope is **"Every moveable object"** (World-owned Layer Pack objects, Story-owned stickers, and Places alike — one consistent control everywhere `moveable` is true, replacing whatever partial control already existed there). **The Move pad is a faithful port of Builder's own `_v2NudgePad`**, not a re-invention — same `HOLD_DELAY_MS=350`/`HOLD_REPEAT_MS=80` press-and-hold timing, same 118px orbit with 30px buttons at radius 44, same `√2` diagonal normalization, and critically the same deliberately dumb contract that made the original reusable: it emits ONLY `(dx,dy)` unit steps in `{-1,0,1}` and the caller decides what a step MEANS. The full press-and-hold mechanism came across intact — `pointerdown` → `preventDefault()` → `setPointerCapture` (try/caught, since release still lands via `pointerup`) → fire once synchronously → a 350ms `setTimeout` installs an 80ms `setInterval`, with `stop()` bound to `pointerup`, `pointercancel` AND `lostpointercapture` so a capture that gets stolen can never leave the timer running; the keyboard path uses a `click` listener that fires exactly once only when `e.detail===0` (Enter/Space), so a pointer click never double-steps; the centre reset button is deliberately NOT hold-wired. `touch-action:none` + `user-select:none` on every button are load-bearing rather than cosmetic — without them a long-press on a touch device triggers native text selection and the context menu instead of repeating the nudge. **The Spin dial is genuinely new**: a 104px circle carrying a gold needle (pivoting on the dial's own centre — an 8px top offset plus a 44px height puts its base at exactly 52px, half the dial) and a draggable handle, with 0° at 12 o'clock growing clockwise so the handle's position always matches which way the object actually ends up facing (the same sense a positive canvas `rotate()` turns); `angleFromEvent` reads `atan2(dy,dx)*180/π+90` to move the origin from the +x axis to 12 o'clock; announced as `role="slider"` with live `aria-valuenow` and full keyboard support (arrows ±1, Shift ±10, Home → 0) so neither control is pointer-only. **One `_spatialAdapter` dispatches on ownership**, mirroring the dispatch `js/app.js`'s own drag handler already makes (`elementType==='sticker'` → `updateSticker`, else `setPosition`) rather than re-deriving it per control: a Story sticker's position and rotation are instance fields on `slide.metadata.stickers[]` (`SceneEngine.updateSticker`); everything else lives in `slide.metadata.elementOverrides[id]` (`setPosition`/`setRotation`) — except a Place's rotation, which uses `setContentOverride(...,'rotation',...)`, its own established 0..359 convention and the one the renderer's permission-gated `_resolvePlaceRotation` actually reads back. Both position paths are absolute canvas pixels at the object's CENTRE, clamped to the real canvas size resolved via `SlideRenderer.getCanvasSize(slide)` (which varies by aspect — never a hardcoded 1080×1350). Rotation range differs across bags (−180..180 for World objects and Story stickers, 0..359 for Places), but a dial has no ends, so normalizing everything to 0..359 is visually identical (270° IS −90°). **Three existing rotation sliders are DELETED rather than duplicated**, per the codebase's own "if unused, delete completely" convention — the World-object `rotationCell` in `_appendWorldObjectEditControl`, the sticker `Spin` range row in `_appendStickerTextEditControl`, and `js/selectionActionStrip.js`'s whole `_mountPlaceRotationSlider` plus its call site — since each wrote to the exact same override bag the dial now writes to, so leaving them would have put two controls on one field. A `const` reassignment bug was caught proactively in the same edit: after replacing `let rotationCell=null` with a `const`, the two downstream `rotationCell=null` reassignments would have thrown, so both were removed along with the now-dead append. **`mountQuickEditControl` was restructured to OR its results** instead of early-returning per branch — that early return is exactly what would have made a `moveable:true`/`editable:false` object fall through to the plain "open the right panel" hint with no controls at all; content controls and spatial controls are independent concerns and an object can legitimately have either, both, or neither. Places reach this function for real, confirmed by reading `renderer/slideRenderer.js` rather than assumed: a Place is pushed into the render tree with `isPlace:true`/`type:'image-holder'`/`owner:'story'`, so `_currentSceneObject` finds it and the adapter's Place branch (gated on `sceneObj.rotatable`) fires. **A real renderer gap was found and closed in the same ship**: `_layerDrawSticker` never read `ov.rotation` at all, so for a World glyph sticker the new dial would have written a value nothing ever painted — it now rotates around the sticker's own anchor `(ax,ay)`, exactly where both the glyph and the circle fallback are already centred, so no extra offset bookkeeping was needed; absent an override no `save`/`rotate`/`restore` runs at all, byte-identical to before. **Three deliberate exclusions, disclosed rather than left implicit**: a colour/fill-kind object never gets a dial (a full-bleed background fill has no meaningful orientation — rotating one only ever exposes its own corners, the same reasoning already recorded when image/shape rotation shipped); the V2 per-layer Rotation sliders on Frame/Paper/Art stay sliders (those are sub-layer transforms sitting beside Tilt and Perspective, not "an object with `moveable` true"); and `js/cardDesigner.js`'s own Refine-panel Spin slider is left completely unchanged — a separate, older surface with its own `_refreshSticker` plumbing, while the quick-edit popup reached by tapping an object is the surface this request is actually about and it now covers every moveable object exactly as asked. **Verified 40/40 via a new Playwright suite** (`spatial_controls_verify.mjs`, scratch-only) across five scenarios: S1 drives a World-owned moveable image end to end — pad geometry, a single-click step, a REAL press-and-hold repeat (`page.mouse.down()` → 750ms → `up()`, proving the interval genuinely fires rather than just the initial step), the centre reset, a real dial drag, the keyboard path, and a canvas pixel check confirming the repaint; S2 confirms the Guardrail holds — a `moveable:false` object gets no pad and no dial while its colour control still mounts; S3 confirms a Story sticker writes `st.x`/`st.y`/`st.rotation` with nothing leaking into `elementOverrides`; S4 confirms the closed renderer gap for a World glyph sticker; S5 statically confirms all three old sliders are genuinely gone with no remaining call sites. **Three test-methodology bugs were found and fixed along the way, none of them app bugs, all disclosed**: an `h`/`half` parameter typo in the suite's own region helper; a fixture using nested `offset:{x,y}` when `js/layerEngine.js` reads FLAT `layer.offsetX`/`layer.offsetY` (confirmed by grep — the seal was rendering off-canvas at `{bx:-60,by:1290}`, which an ASCII grid dump of the bbox made obvious); and a pixel-brightness check that could never have worked, because `_layerDrawSticker`'s glyph branch never sets `x.fillStyle` so the glyph paints in whatever colour the context happened to carry, indistinguishable from the background — a pre-existing quirk, deliberately out of scope, worked around by replacing the brightness sample with a `CanvasRenderingContext2D.prototype.rotate` spy that proves the renderer genuinely rotates (zero calls at 0°, exactly one call of π at 180°). **Full regression**: both `goldenBuild.js` suites (World Builder v1 and v2) PASS unchanged; `four_bugs_verify.mjs` 36/36 — four of its assertions were updated from the removed range slider to the new dial (S1.7 now checks for the Spin dial AND the Move pad, S1.8 drives a real pointer press at 6 o'clock on the `.rot-dial`, S1.9 accepts the resulting ~180° within a 2° tolerance since a real pointer lands where it lands, S1.12 checks the shape object's own dial), the intended and disclosed consequence of deleting the duplicate control rather than a regression; `fa_replace_everywhere_verify.mjs` 22/22, `legacy_place_controls_verify.js` 15/15, and `v2_nudge_verify.js` 28/28 all pass unchanged (the last two hardcode port 8940 with no self-startup — the already-documented staleness class — so a real server was started on that exact port for genuine confirmation rather than skipping them). Cache-bust `?v=0342`→`?v=0343`. This directly serves Creator Governing Rules #2 (Guardrails — the pad and dial appear if and only if `moveable` is true) and #3 (Refinement — what the guardrails allow now has one real, consistent, reachable control everywhere). No Theme Contract/Engine V2 Scene Model/Builder change — `tools/world-builder/` and `tools/world-builder-v2/` are completely untouched; confined to `js/contextPanel.js`, `js/selectionActionStrip.js`, `renderer/slideRenderer.js`, `css/style.css`, and `index.html`.)

- Voice Notes Can Finally Be Placed (root Studio only — a direct bug report, verbatim and with no further elaboration: **"bug regarding voice object there is no way to place it on slide."** Reproduced rather than guessed at, and the literal complaint turned out to have TWO real causes stacked on top of each other, neither of which is "dragging is broken" — a real mouse-driven canvas drag was confirmed working throughout, and is untouched by this ship. **Cause 1 — every note landed in the same, worst possible spot.** `_addVoiceNoteSticker` passed no `x`/`y`, so `SceneEngine.addSticker` applied its own dead-centre default (540,675) — which on a real page is squarely on top of the Artwork Place, so the badge lands buried in the middle of the picture, and a SECOND note lands EXACTLY on the first, making neither individually grabbable. New `_voiceNoteSpawn(slide)` (`js/contextPanel.js`) places the first note low-left (18% x / 80% y of the page's OWN resolved size via `SlideRenderer.getCanvasSize` — never a hardcoded 1080×1350, which is only one of several aspects a Scene can declare), then cascades diagonally by `min(w,h)*0.07` per voice note already on the page, wrapping into a fresh column every 5 steps so the cascade can never walk off the page. **Cause 2 — the panel a kid lands on has no position control at all.** After creating a note the selection hand-off correctly opens cardDesigner's sticker Refine panel — which for a voice note offers ▶ Play / Size / Spin / See Through / Lock / Duplicate / Delete and *nothing* that moves it; the Move pad + Spin dial shipped one build earlier live in the Selection Action Strip's own popup, reachable only by discovering an unlabelled ✏️. `js/selectionActionStrip.js` gains a new exported `openEdit()` — deliberately just the existing toggle's own open half, so the caller decides WHEN while this module still decides WHAT the popup holds — and `_addVoiceNoteSticker` calls it one `requestAnimationFrame` after selecting (deferred so `setSelectedSceneElement`'s own `PageRuntime.notify()` has already rebuilt the strip for THIS object before the popup opens against it). The pad is now simply *there* the moment a note exists. `_addVoiceNoteSticker` also now calls `host.redraw()` rather than relying on the selection notify alone. **A small accessibility fix in the same pass**, since this change is precisely what hands a kid the pad: the 8 nudge buttons carried only an arrow glyph plus a `title`, so a screen reader announced them as nothing useful — each now carries a real `aria-label` (the dial beside them already had `role="slider"`/`aria-valuenow`, so one half of the pair was labelled and the other wasn't). A clean tap on a badge still PLAYS the clip, unchanged from Ship 2. **Verified 16/16 via a new Playwright suite** (`voice_place_verify.mjs`, scratch-only, driving the real UI through Creation Flow → Add Something → Voice → Import a Voice Note): the spawn is genuinely not the centre default and sits low-left within the page's own resolved size; the note auto-selects and the strip's edit popup opens by itself with all 9 pad buttons AND the dial present; a real `page.mouse.click` on the labelled Right control moves the note right and ONLY right (x increases, y unchanged); a second note cascades a visible distance away rather than stacking, and both appear at distinct spots in the render tree; zero page errors. One test-methodology fix disclosed rather than glossed over: the suite's first pass located the Right button by regex over `textContent`, which for these buttons is a bare `→` glyph — that failure is exactly what surfaced the missing `aria-label` above, so the test was re-pointed at the (now real) label rather than at the glyph. **Full regression**: `voice_note_verify.mjs` 22/22 (Ship 2's own suite — its drag test grabs the topmost note, so it is unaffected by where notes now spawn), `voice_verify.mjs` 16/16, `spatial_controls_verify.mjs` 40/40, `four_bugs_verify.mjs` 36/36, `fa_replace_everywhere_verify.mjs` 22/22, and both `goldenBuild.js` suites (World Builder v1 and v2) PASS unchanged. Cache-bust `?v=0343`→`?v=0344`. This directly serves Creator Governing Rule #3 (Refinement — a capability the guardrails already allowed now has a real, reachable control at the moment it is needed); confined to `js/contextPanel.js`, `js/selectionActionStrip.js`, and `index.html`.)

- Move and Spin Become One Widget (root Studio only — a direct product request, verbatim and accompanied by a design mockup: **"we can combine spin and move panel into one. something like this."** The mockup shows a single circle: an outer MOVE ring holding 8 arrow buttons, a SPIN disc nested at its centre with a needle and a draggable handle, a knob on the hub, and a legend naming both gestures. The Move pad and Spin dial had shipped two builds earlier as two separate rows stacked in the quick-edit popup; this collapses them into one object exactly as drawn. **Structure**: `js/contextPanel.js`'s `_makeNudgePadRow` and `_makeRotationDial` are both retired (single-use each, so deleted rather than left dangling, per the codebase's own "if unused, delete completely" convention) and replaced by `_makeSpatialWidget`, which assembles three now-single-purpose builders — `_makeNudgePad(onNudge)` (the ring: 8 arrows, no hub), `_makeDial(opts)` (the disc alone, no row or label of its own, reporting its reading back through a new `onDisplay` callback), and `_makeCenterButton(onCenter,title)` (the hub) — into ONE row with one shared label ("Move & Spin", carrying the live degree readout) and a two-line legend. The disc is appended INSIDE the ring; the hub is appended inside the disc, and its own `pointerdown` calls `stopPropagation()` so tapping reset can never also start a rotate drag (the dial's drag handler is on the dial itself, so that one guard is the whole fix). **Geometry moved from fixed pixels to percentages**, which is what makes the nesting safe: the Selection Action Strip sizes itself to whatever gutter room it finds (`MIN_USABLE=160`, `js/selectionActionStrip.js`), so a fixed ~150px widget could overflow the narrowest popup — the ring is now `width:min(150px,100%); aspect-ratio:1`, every absolutely-placed child carries `transform:translate(-50%,-50%)` so its percentage `left`/`top` means "centre here", and the whole widget scales as one. Buttons went 30px → 28px so the disc has room inside the orbit, and the disc derives its own 52% from that same ring geometry (`DIAL_PCT_OF_PAD`, computed from `COMBO_PAD_PX`/`NUDGE_BTN_PX` rather than hardcoded), with the CSS `width:52%` commented as kept in step with it. **A real cascade trap was avoided by construction**: `.nudge-btn:active` must restate the centring translate before `scale(0.88)` — a bare `scale()` would have replaced the whole transform and snapped every pressed button a half-width up and left. The needle keeps its proven `margin-left:-1px` + plain `rotate()` (so its own `50% 100%` origin lands exactly on the disc's centre) rather than switching to a translate-based centring, whose composition order with `rotate()` is correct but far subtler to reason about. **Visual separation**: the ring gets a faint warm wash (`rgba(255,203,69,0.07)`) and the disc a gold rim (`rgba(255,203,69,0.7)`) tying it to its own needle and handle — a first pass with the disc on `var(--bg)` inside a `var(--panel)` ring rendered the disc almost invisible, caught by screenshotting the widget rather than assuming the markup implied the look. **The non-rotating case keeps its own shape, not a disabled disc**: a moveable-but-not-rotatable object (a full-bleed colour fill has no meaningful orientation; a non-rotatable Place is guardrailed off) gets the ring with the hub in its OWN centre and no `.rot-dial` element rendered at all, its label reading just "Move" with no degree readout and its legend naming only the arrows — Guardrails behave exactly as before, and the existing suite's own "a non-moveable object gets NO pad and NO dial" checks still hold. **Verified 27/27 on the first run** via a new Playwright suite (`combined_widget_verify.mjs`, scratch-only): exactly one spatial row (not two); one ring and one disc, with the disc genuinely `pad.contains(dial)` and the hub genuinely `dial.contains(centre)`; still 8 arrows + 1 hub; the shared label and the two-gesture legend; the disc centred within 1px of the ring's own centre and genuinely smaller than it; all 8 arrows measured at the same orbit radius (spread ≤2px, so the `√2` diagonal normalization survived the percentage rewrite); no arrow overlapping the disc (each arrow's inner edge ≥ the disc's radius); the widget fitting inside the popup's own width; the hub clearing the position override while leaving rotation untouched (proving the `stopPropagation` guard); a real `page.mouse.click` on the labelled Right arrow moving the object right and only right; a real drag at 6 o'clock on the disc spinning to ~180° with the shared readout following; and the full ring-only shape for the non-rotating object. **Full regression**: `spatial_controls_verify.mjs` 40/40 — two of its assertions were updated as the intended, disclosed consequence of the combine (S1.5's button size 30px→28px, and S1.13's readout lookup, which walked `dial.parentElement` back when the dial's parent WAS the row and now correctly scopes to `.context-spatial-row` since the dial's parent is the ring); `four_bugs_verify.mjs` 36/36 — two assertions likewise updated, since the two separate "Move"/"Spin" row labels are now one "Move & Spin"; `voice_place_verify.mjs` 16/16, `fa_replace_everywhere_verify.mjs` 22/22, `voice_note_verify.mjs` 22/22, `fromworld_tile_verify.mjs` 13/13, `photo_via_studio_verify.mjs` 8/8, `bg_default_verify.mjs` 12/12, and both `goldenBuild.js` suites (World Builder v1 and v2) PASS unchanged. Cache-bust `?v=0344`→`?v=0345`. This serves Creator Governing Rule #3 (Refinement — the same two capabilities, now one control a child can find and understand at a glance) with Rule #2 (Guardrails) unchanged in behaviour. No Theme Contract/Engine V2 Scene Model/Builder change — `tools/world-builder/` and `tools/world-builder-v2/` are completely untouched; confined to `js/contextPanel.js`, `css/style.css`, and `index.html`.)

- Three Voice Note Badges — and None of Them Is a Solid Backfill (root Studio only — a direct product note, verbatim: **"i like the voice icon, but its overpowering with backfill can you allow creator to choose from 3 different voice note icons."** The glyph was never the problem; the fixed coral disc behind it was. A voice note's payload is audio, so the badge IS the only thing a silent surface can show — which makes its LOOK the one thing a kid can genuinely style on this object kind. **One catalogue, two consumers**: `js/stickerLibrary.js` gains `VOICE_ICONS` (`{value,label,glyph}`), `DEFAULT_VOICE_ICON`, and a `getVoiceIcon(id)` that falls back to the first entry rather than throwing on an unknown value — the renderer and the picker both read it through the same `typeof StickerLibrary!=='undefined'` guard the file's own `getById`/`getShapeKind` consumers already use, so a fourth look is one catalogue entry plus one draw branch, never a change in two hand-synced places. **The three looks, all deliberately lighter than what they replace**: `speaker` — the glyph alone on a soft white halo (`shadowColor`/`shadowBlur` on the one `fillText`), legible over a dark photo with no disc behind it, and the default; `bubble` — the glyph inside a drawn speech bubble with a little tail (thin coral outline over a 14% coral tint), so it reads as "someone is talking here"; `mic` — a 🎤 glyph inside a thin coral ring, nothing inside it. `renderer/slideRenderer.js`'s `_drawSceneVoice` dispatches on `st.voiceIcon` via a new `_voiceIconDef(st)` helper, and `_stickerBbox`'s `visual:{kind:'glyph',glyph:…}` now follows the chosen glyph too, so the Object Strip card shows 🎤 for a mic badge with zero ObjectStrip changes (its glyph-visual dispatch already existed). **The picker sits beside Play** in the Refine panel's `.sticker-voice-group` — where this kind's own controls already live — reusing the shared `.icon-row`/`.icon-card`/`.icon-label` vocabulary, with only the preview swatch voice-specific (`.voice-icon-preview-speaker|-bubble|-mic`) so each tile genuinely SHOWS the look it picks rather than three identical glyphs in three identical boxes; `_refreshSticker` syncs the active card, resolving an absent `voiceIcon` through the catalogue's own default so a note placed before this picker existed still shows the right card as active. **One deliberate, disclosed appearance change**: an absent `voiceIcon` resolves to `speaker`, so an already-placed note picks up the lighter default rather than keeping the heavy disc — which is exactly what was reported as overpowering, and voice notes are only a few builds old. **Verified 20/20 on the first run** via a new Playwright suite (`voice_icon_verify.mjs`, scratch-only, driving the real Add Something → Voice → Import flow): the catalogue and its unknown-value fallback; three cards labelled Speaker/Bubble/Mic with the default showing active on a note that genuinely stores no `voiceIcon` yet; each pick persisting to the instance and flipping the active card; the Object Strip glyph following to 🎤 for mic; and — the decisive check on the actual complaint — a coral-pixel census over the badge's own bbox rather than a single sample: **0%** for speaker (no backfill at all), ~10% for bubble and ~11% for mic (a real outline, not a fill), where the old solid disc would have been most of the box; plus all three looks hashing to genuinely different pixels. All three were also screenshotted side by side on a dark backdrop rather than trusting the numbers alone. **Full regression**: `voice_note_verify.mjs` 22/22 — one assertion updated, the intended and disclosed consequence of this ship rather than a regression: it sampled a single pixel expecting the solid coral disc, and now checks the badge box carries real ink against the page's own background, which is the honest question once the look is the kid's choice; `voice_place_verify.mjs` 16/16, `voice_verify.mjs` 16/16, `combined_widget_verify.mjs` 27/27, `spatial_controls_verify.mjs` 40/40, `four_bugs_verify.mjs` 36/36, `image_studio_draw_verify.mjs` 26/26, Museum Gallery's three canonical render hashes byte-identical (`1f54eb660f7beb53`/`843e68f2cffb3c2e`/`969a67e5c984647b` — structurally guaranteed, since every changed renderer line sits behind `kind==='voice'` and that theme has none, but run anyway), and both `goldenBuild.js` suites PASS. Cache-bust `?v=0345`→`?v=0346`. This serves Creator Governing Rule #4 (Personalization — a real creative choice on an object that previously had exactly one fixed look). No Theme Contract/Engine V2 Scene Model/Builder change — `tools/world-builder/` and `tools/world-builder-v2/` are completely untouched; confined to `js/stickerLibrary.js`, `renderer/slideRenderer.js`, `js/cardDesigner.js`, `css/style.css`, and `index.html`.)

- Companion Intelligence — Discovery & Architecture Proposal (`docs/COMPANION_INTELLIGENCE_ARCHITECTURE.md`) — an investigation-and-design-only deliverable, **no code changes**, answering a direct product brief: *"study the VihuStudio codebase and documentation... Do not assume architecture. Do not begin implementation."* Follows the precedent of `docs/ENGINE_V2_PROMOTION_STRATEGY.md` / `docs/SCENE_ADAPTER_ARCHITECTURE_ANALYSIS.md` — both no-code strategy documents gated behind this project's standing "architecture changes require explicit approval" rule. **Two premises in the brief were corrected up front rather than silently worked around**: (a) the brief states the platform is React — verified false (no `package.json`, no `node_modules`, `grep -c 'type="module"' index.html` → 0, zero React references; it is 55 classic `<script>` tags loading `window`-attached IIFE modules with no build step), which materially changes what "extends the existing stack" means — the recommendation is new IIFE modules, not a toolchain; (b) the codebase had already *reserved* this extension point — `js/companionEngine.js`'s own header and `docs/COMPANION_ENGINE.md`'s "Future Ready" section both describe `personality.json`'s `neverSays` as *"authored policy data for a future AI-driven speech feature to respect, disclosed as currently inert,"* and document `speak()` as written so a later version can grow TTS behind the same signature. **The central finding**: most of the "intelligence" a Companion needs already exists as structured data and is simply never routed to it — `renderer/slideRenderer.js`'s `_sceneObject()` normalizer (line 3596) already gives every rendered object a uniform `{id,type,label,owner,moveable,editable,visible,visual,bbox}` shape; `js/pageRuntime.js` already owns *"what page is active, what's rendered, what's selected"* with one `notify()` dispatch every mutation already fires; `js/publishValidator.js` is already a pure rules-over-project-state engine returning friendly, ordered, non-blocking nudges with a `fixHint` routing key (its own header: *"Friendly language only. Never 'error', never 'warning'. Never blocks publishing"*) — a miniature of exactly the engine this proposal argues for, so the recommendation is to **call it, not reimplement it**; and `docs/THEME_TO_CREATOR_MAP.md` / `worldBuilderApp.js`'s `STATE_GUIDANCE` / `objectStrip.js`'s `FRIENDLY_TYPE` / `contextPanel.js`'s `_renderWorldObjectDisclosure` already supply capability, how-to, vocabulary and guardrail-explanation copy. **Proposed shape — four additive modules, each extending an existing seam, nothing replaced**: `js/companionContext.js` (read-only situation snapshot projected from PageRuntime/SlideRenderer/PublishValidator/ThemeRegistry — owns no state), `js/companionBrain.js` (situation + event → an *intent* `{pose?,say?,offer?,action?,source,confidence}`; deterministic rules first, model call an opt-in escalation), `js/companionActions.js` (a whitelist of named actions mapped onto existing `SceneEngine`/`PageOps` calls, gated three ways — whitelisted / guardrail-re-checked against the LIVE render tree at execution time per Creator Governing Rule #2 / child-initiated), and a Model Gateway (`supabase/functions/companion-chat/` + `js/companionModel.js`) as the **only** place a provider is ever named, following the `family-album` Edge Function's own proven conventions (host-restricted, `200 {ok:false,error}` for expected failures, client never holds a key — the source is public on GitHub). `js/companionEngine.js` stays frozen and generic; `js/companionDirector.js` stays the ONE Studio-aware file, its static `MODES` table becoming the Brain's fallback rather than the whole decision. **Ten capabilities mapped, and six of them need no AI at all** (situational reaction, noticing absence, guardrail explanation, capability discovery, pointing, wayfinding) — the direct answer to the brief's *"Do not assume every interaction requires an LLM"*; a model is warranted today for exactly one thing, answering an unanticipated question in the companion's own voice, always grounded in an authored knowledge corpus rather than asked to recall how Studio works. **Knowledge splits three ways** — Package (per-companion `personality.json`, extended additively with `voice`/`topics`/`lines`), Platform (a new authored `assets/companions/knowledge/*.json` corpus derived from the four existing sources above), Situation (runtime, ephemeral, never persisted) — and that split is what keeps "add a companion" a zero-code act. **The single hardest constraint, stated plainly rather than glossed**: there is **no global undo/redo** anywhere in the codebase (only local per-tool stacks — doodle strokes, Picture Studio brush strokes, `_preCropSnapshot`), so the action model is tiered Point / Offer / **Perform**, with Point and Offer shippable today and Perform explicitly gated on global undo existing first. **Ten risks named**, headed by children's creative content leaving the device — recommended to require its own explicit, recorded Locked Product Decision before any model escalation ships — followed by canon drift (`docs/COMPANION_CANON.md:17`: *"A companion is not an assistant, a chatbot, a teacher, or an AI tutor"*), guidance contradicting Guardrails, two-brains duplication, and breaking the Traveller's canonical silence (`MODES.traveller.speaks:false` — the Story Egg never speaks, so the mode gate sits at the TOP of `decide()`, before any rule evaluation). **Five-phase roadmap, each phase independently shippable**: Phase 0 Awareness and Phase 1 Noticing and Phase 2 Pointing/Offering involve **no AI, no backend, no new dependency, and no privacy question at all** — and Phase 1 is identified as the phase that most changes how the Companion *feels*; Phase 3 (the Gateway) is gated on the privacy decision, Phase 4 (Perform) on global undo. Creative suggestion, multi-turn chat UI, persistent cross-session memory, and voice input are explicitly out of scope. No code was written; this is a proposal awaiting approval.

- Story Replay — Discovery & Architecture Proposal (`docs/STORY_REPLAY_ARCHITECTURE.md`) — an investigation-and-design-only deliverable, **no code changes**, answering a direct product brief: *"Do not begin implementation. Do not write code. Do not assume Story Replay is the correct solution... Challenge the idea if the current architecture suggests a better approach."* Follows the precedent of `docs/ENGINE_V2_PROMOTION_STRATEGY.md` / `docs/SCENE_ADAPTER_ARCHITECTURE_ANALYSIS.md` / `docs/COMPANION_INTELLIGENCE_ARCHITECTURE.md`, gated behind the standing "architecture changes require explicit approval" rule. **The brief's own hypothesis was tested and found half false, which changed the whole architecture**: it proposed that *"VihuStudio already understands the author's work through structured data... Replay should be generated from semantic authoring events rather than captured pixels."* The first half is true and then some — `ProjectManager.serialize()` already returns the ENTIRE project (every page's `pageType`/`image`/`storyBeat`/full `metadata` bag, plus `theme`/`artworkTheme`/`themeOptions`) in one call, which IS a replay frame. The second half rests on a premise verified false: **there are no semantic authoring events — VihuStudio has state, not events.** No `eventBus.js`/`history.js`/`undo.js` exists anywhere in `js/` or `tools/world-builder-v2/js/`; zero application-level `new CustomEvent`/`dispatchEvent` (the two hits are `emojiPicker`/`pageDesigner` firing a DOM `input` event so a textarea's own handler runs); and the one dispatch that fires on every mutation, `PageRuntime.notify()` (`js/pageRuntime.js:125`), **takes zero arguments** — it calls refresh on five panels and returns, saying *"something changed, everyone refresh,"* never what changed, to which object, from what, or by whom. **So the recommendation is neither "wire up the events" nor "you need a screen recorder": Replay should be a snapshot timeline with events *derived by diffing*, not captured at the call site** — and that is argued as genuinely better here, not a compromise. **The decisive evidence is `markDirty()`**: 47 call sites across 11 files, with `js/sceneEngine.js` — the actual mutation API — calling it **zero** times.
