If a one-line, zero-argument obligation has already scattered across 47 hand-maintained sites, requiring every future mutation to also publish a correctly-shaped, correctly-attributed replay event would drift within a sprint, fail silently, and quietly make the Replay a lie — so the proposal is **one observer at one chokepoint**, `_writeStorage()`, which is where the platform reliably declares complete state whatever the 47 dirty sites do or forget, capturing changes made by code that does not exist yet. **Two accidental enablers found, both already shipped**: Draft Asset Architecture Phase C made snapshots affordable — `imageToDataURL()` returns `slide._imageDataURL` verbatim, which post-Phase-C is a ~60-char `vihu-asset:creator:<projectId>:<assetId>` reference rather than base64 — and `thumbnail` (a real PNG data URL from `js/thumbnails.js:61`) is identified as the one genuine byte-cost in `serialize()`, recommended dropped from Replay snapshots on exactly the precedent Draft Asset Phase D already set for it ("small, derived, regenerable data"). **Readiness classified per the brief's own Already Exists / Needs Extension / New Capability scheme: 5 / 8 / 0 at the data level** — every one of the 8 "Needs Extension" rows (page created, scene changed, object added, object moved, colours changed, theme/World changed, pages reordered, publish occurred) is satisfied by **one diff engine**, not eight instrumentation projects, which is the finding that makes this buildable; `AssetStore`'s `pendingUploads` queue is noted as the one place the platform already keeps a genuine append-only event log. **Proposed shape**: `js/storyReplay.js` — a thin service *beside* `ProjectManager`, explicitly **not** an engine (that word means renderer/resolver here — `SlideRenderer`/`SceneEngine`/`LayerEngine`/`ThemeEngine`; Replay resolves and renders nothing), **not** part of Publish (an output stage; Replay must capture the whole authoring life, most of which precedes Publish and much of which never reaches it), and **not** part of Studio Runtime (`PageRuntime` owns *"what is true right now,"* Replay owns *"what was true over time"* — different lifetimes, and merging them couples a live editing hot path to a growing archive) — feeding a `ReplayStore` (IndexedDB, never `localStorage`, per AV-009's and Cloud-Primary Project Storage's own quota incidents) and a `ReplayDiff`. Cadence is coalesce-30s / deduplicate-by-hash / force-keep-milestones / cap-at-~200-and-thin-the-middle, so the worst case is **bounded** rather than growing. **The argument the document says should decide it**: a snapshot timeline is version history, and version history is undo — *"restore the project to a previous snapshot"* is something `ProjectManager.deserialize()` already implements and already exercises on every session restore and every "Load Cloud Version" freshness check — which makes it a **third and better answer to the hard blocker `docs/COMPANION_INTELLIGENCE_ARCHITECTURE.md` §7.4 named** (no global undo, hence no Companion "Perform" tier), alongside crash/corruption recovery this codebase has already been burned by. One foundation, three features. **Six proposed outputs (Story Replay / Magic Strip / Story Journey / Behind The Scenes / Publish animation / Social Reel) are shown to be one dataset and six renderers**, differing only in frame selection and presentation — recommendation is to build the timeline plus exactly ONE renderer, and deliberately **not the reel**, since a scrubber proves intrinsic value while a reel's value depends on sharing. **Only two extensions to the event model are recommended and the second is "nothing else"**: optional `StoryReplay.mark('published')` milestone calls at ~5 already-named moments (`PublishStudio._finalizePublish`, `CreationFlow._finish`, `MagicCard.claim`), deliberately mirroring `CompanionDirector.notify(event)`'s existing string vocabulary rather than inventing a second one — and explicitly **do not** add a payload to `PageRuntime.notify()`, which would reintroduce exactly the 47-call-site drift. **Risks led by the non-engineering one**: a timeline of how a child works is a behavioural record meaningfully different from the artwork they made — recommended local-first, owner-scoped, deletable independently of the project, never framed as measurement, and requiring its own explicit Locked Product Decision before it syncs anywhere; followed by "the replay might simply be boring," diff quality being the whole product, `metadata` bloat, coupling, theme drift on historical frames, and an honest counter-argument that this adds another growing writer to a storage story this platform has repeatedly been burned by. **Five-phase roadmap where Phases 0–2 involve no video, no backend, no sharing, and no new privacy question**: Phase 0 *writes nothing durable* — it shapes/hashes/measures only, and exists so the proposal can be killed with numbers rather than defended with argument; Phase 1 delivers version history (and with it global undo + real crash recovery) independent of any Replay UI ever shipping; Phase 2 is the differ plus a scrubber; Phase 3 recommends Magic Strip over video (cheaper, no `ReelComposer` dependency, no MP4/webm question, a good fridge artefact); Phase 4 is the platform payoff. Analytics dashboards, teacher/classroom sharing, cross-project timelines, collaborative replay, and any authoring-side record/edit controls are explicitly out of scope. No code was written; this is a proposal awaiting approval.

- Magic Publish — Product & Implementation Proposal (`docs/MAGIC_PUBLISH_ARCHITECTURE.md`) — an investigation-and-design-only deliverable, **no code changes**, answering a direct product brief whose binding constraints were stated verbatim: *"This sprint is not about Story Replay. It is not about Version History. It is not about Timeline."*; *"Do not begin from Replay. Begin from the product experience. Then work backwards into architecture."*; *"Magic over accuracy. Delight over completeness. Wonder over explanation."*; *"if periodic snapshots during authoring are sufficient for an MVP, recommend that over a comprehensive timeline architecture."*; and *"Remain faithful to VihuStudio. Do not expose implementation details. The audience should never think: 'That was screen recorded.'"* — plus a closing meta-note asking that no social-platform, reel, traction or marketing framing appear anywhere, which the document honors (it contains none). Follows the precedent of `docs/ENGINE_V2_PROMOTION_STRATEGY.md` / `docs/SCENE_ADAPTER_ARCHITECTURE_ANALYSIS.md` / `docs/COMPANION_INTELLIGENCE_ARCHITECTURE.md` / `docs/STORY_REPLAY_ARCHITECTURE.md`, gated behind the standing "architecture changes require explicit approval" rule. **The finding that determines everything else: Magic Creation needs no history at all.** The desired sequence — Blank Page → Background → Character → Decorations → Text → Finished — is not a record of what a child did (a child drops a sticker, undoes it, nudges it four times, changes its colour twice, comes back tomorrow and moves it again); it is a **choreographed decomposition of the *finished* page, peeled apart by layer**, and every frame in it is computable from the final saved state alone. So the brief's own question *"Can this be delivered without introducing a new platform capability?"* is answered **yes, emphatically** — no snapshots, no timeline, no autosave hook, no new persistence, nothing touching `_writeStorage()`/`AppState`/the hot path. **And it is argued as the better product, not a shortcut**, on the brief's own principles: a truthful history replay would show forty nudges, a colour changed six times, and a sticker deleted twice — honest and boring — while a layer reveal is always a clean story, on every page, for every child, including the child who made the page in ninety seconds. **Platform assessment — almost all of it already exists**: `SlideRenderer.buildPayload`+`.render()` (deterministic, one call per frame), two proven off-screen render patterns (`ThumbnailEngine.generate()`, `_renderSlideInto()`), `ReelComposer.compose(pages,opts)` (`js/reelComposer.js:175`) whose `[{bitmap,narrationBuffer,holdMs}]`+`{width,height,fps,transition,transitionMs}` contract **is exactly the API a build-up animation needs**, `StoryDestinations.register()` (`js/storyDestinations.js:606`, built in Sprint 9.0.4 specifically so new outputs plug in *without editing the file* — Magic Creation is the case it was designed for) with its optional `publishMessages`/`finishingMessage`/`progressNoun` presentation hooks, the uniform render tree from `_sceneObject()` (the object inventory the reveal choreographs), paint order already resolved via `_naturalStoryOrder()`, `FRIENDLY_TYPE` names, per-page narration, `AudioManager`'s five already-licensed Foundation loops, shipped Companion art, and a five-stage publish flow that already supports async finishes and per-destination copy (Story Reel proved both). **Only three things are genuinely missing**: a layer-peeling function (New Capability, ~200 lines), a crossfade transition in `ReelComposer` (Needs Extension, ~40 lines — elements should *arrive*, not cut), and a publish bundle in `PublishStudio` (Needs Extension, no change to the destination contract). Serialization, autosave, state management, the asset system, and scene runtime need **no change whatsoever** — stated plainly because the modules most at risk in this platform's history are precisely the ones this feature does not touch. **Proposed shape**: one new module, `js/magicReveal.js`, exporting `revealStages(slide) → [{slide,label,holdMs},…]` — it clones the slide, strips it back to near-empty, then adds groups back in paint order, and **never mutates the real slide** (cloning is the whole safety story, and it is what lets this run during Publish with zero risk to what the child is looking at) — feeding six stages (Paper / The World arrives / The picture arrives / Decorations arrive / Words arrive / Rest) that **collapse automatically when a page has nothing for them**, rather than showing a beat where nothing happens. **All four suppression mechanisms were verified to already exist rather than assumed**: story-owned stickers via `clone.metadata.stickers.slice(0,k)`; Scene blueprint elements via `SceneEngine.setVisibility(clone,id,false)` → `elementOverrides[id].visible`, honoured at `slideRenderer.js:4236`; World-owned Layer Pack objects by cloning the theme and filtering `layerPack`, since `_artworkTheme(s)` returns `s.artworkTheme` **directly if set** (`slideRenderer.js:82-88`) and `LayerEngine.render()` gates on `layer.visible!==false` — the exact mechanism Screen 2's preview carousel already uses in production; and story text via `clone.storyBeat=''`. That gives **zero changes to `renderer/slideRenderer.js`**, which matters because that file carries the three canonical Museum Gallery render hashes every ship in this project's history is checked against, and Magic Publish should not be the first feature to risk them. **The one real trap, disclosed rather than glossed**: stripping a page can reveal authoring chrome that must never appear — most obviously the "Tap to add your artwork" dashed placeholder — so a `suppressPlaceholders` render flag (~5 lines) is the single place the "no renderer changes" claim bends. **Magic Creation spec**: the no-chrome guarantee is **structural, not careful** — every frame is `SlideRenderer.render()` onto an off-screen canvas, the editor is not involved, there is nothing to accidentally leak, so the brief's hardest requirement is satisfied by construction; objects *arrive* (fade ~350ms + a slight rise + a gentle overshoot-and-settle on scale, 0→1.04→1.00, which is what makes it feel placed by hand rather than switched on) while backgrounds wash in rather than scaling up; text draws itself **word-by-word (~120ms/word), never character-by-character** (characters read as a computer terminal, words read as a story being told) and needs no renderer change since slicing the string per frame is enough; pacing is 4-6s per page and ~20-25s total for a four-page story, deliberately short so it is rewatched rather than endured, with pages separated by the already-built, already-tested `page-turn` transition; sound is three tiers in priority order (the child's own narration → an `AudioManager` Foundation bed → correctly-handled silence, the last already fixed after a silent reel once composed to zero bytes); branding is a **2.5s closing card, never an overlay on a child's art**, optionally carrying the creator's own bonded Story Companion (costs nothing, canon-correct, turns a logo into *their* logo, and a Traveller with no companion simply gets the card without one — no gate, no prompt, no missing-asset gap). **Magic Strip**: a single still image, because a still image survives being forwarded, printed, and stuck on a fridge — six frames, where **the stage list *is* the frame selection** so there is no separate selection algorithm to write, in a 1×6 strip or a 2×3 grid, film-strip treated (sprocket holes, gutters, numerals — instantly legible as "stages of making" with no caption) with branding in a footer bar inside the strip's own chrome. **Publish redesign**: Choose Story Destination becomes optional ("Other formats", reachable from Celebration — nothing shipped is removed), the default path has no fork in it, and Celebration presents four things to keep with the Magic Creation **already playing** rather than a download button. **The honest cost is stated up front**: `ReelComposer` records in real time, so a 25-second Magic Creation takes ~25 seconds to film — mitigated by producing Book and Cover first and showing them immediately, honest progress copy over a percentage, and never blocking Celebration if filming fails. **Evolution into Replay — the MVP is the foundation, not a detour**: the seam is the frame source, since `revealStages(slide)` and `ReplayStore.framesFor(page)` both return a list of slide states, so the composer, the destination, the transitions, the Magic Strip, the branding and the pacing all survive unchanged; three steps (MVP derived stages → Hybrid, where real history is used where it exists and derived reveal fills the rest, which is *the permanent right answer* rather than a fallback since a page created in one sitting has no interesting history either → Curated, where the differ picks the interesting moments and the reveal fills the gaps), and the recommendation is to **ship Magic Publish first and Replay second**, so Replay arrives as an upgrade to something people already love rather than as infrastructure asking to be believed in. **Risks** are led by real-time recording slowing Publish, authoring placeholders leaking into a stripped page, and — on the product side — a sparse page having no journey, the magic wearing off if every page reveals identically (mitigated by per-page variation seeded deterministically so a rewatch is identical), and the feature reading as an advert for the tool rather than as the child's own. **Seven success criteria, all product rather than technical**, headed by watch-through rate (>70% — the single best proxy for delight; if a child will not watch their own, nobody will), rewatch rate (>30% — rewatching is wonder, watching once is curiosity), and **manual creative assets produced by creators: zero, permanently** (any creator hand-making a strip is a defect), with time spent authoring, edit counts and session length deliberately **not** measured, on the same line `docs/STORY_REPLAY_ARCHITECTURE.md` §9.1 draws — those describe the worker, not the work. **Five-phase roadmap**: Phase 1 is the whole MVP and is additive/registry-based with nothing shipped modified; Phase 2 is the Strip from frames Phase 1 already produces; Phase 3 is the only phase that modifies a shipped flow; Phase 4 is independently droppable polish; Phase 5 swaps the frame source only if Replay ships. Direct posting to any platform, analytics dashboards, creator-editable reveals, per-object timing controls, multi-story compilations, and any authoring-side capture UI are explicitly out of scope. No code was written; this is a proposal awaiting approval.

- Magic Publish — Sprint M1: Foundation (root Studio only — the first of the nine sprints in the approved `docs/MAGIC_PUBLISH_ROADMAP.md`, whose own scope is stated plainly: *"Introduce Magic Publish as a new publish capability without changing existing publishing behaviour... No UI changes. No renderer modifications (unless absolutely required). No animation yet."* **New `js/magicReveal.js` owns the whole contract**: `revealStages(slide) → [{slide,label,holdMs}, …]`, a pure function of the **final saved page** — no history, no timeline, no snapshots, nothing hooked into autosave, `_writeStorage()` or `AppState`, per `docs/MAGIC_PUBLISH_ARCHITECTURE.md` §0's own finding that the reveal is a *choreographed decomposition of the finished page by layer*, not a record of what a child actually did. Every entry carries a slide the renderer can draw as-is, so no caller ever needs to know how a stage was built, and the module **never mutates the slide it is handed** — that guarantee is exactly what lets it run during Publish with zero risk to the page the child is looking at. **M1 ships the contract and the plumbing only**: `revealStages()` returns the single Finished stage, so Magic Publish produces a real, working, deliberately non-magical video end to end; M2 fills in `Blank → World → Artwork → Decorations → Text → Finished` behind this same signature with no plumbing changes anywhere downstream. **The `MAGIC` destination joins `REGISTRY`** in `js/storyDestinations.js` alongside its three siblings (the same pattern `BOOK`/`CAROUSEL`/`REEL` already use — `register()` stays available for genuine third-party plugins): `id:'magic'`, `label:'Magic Creation'`, `glyph:'✨'`, one `1080×1920` vertical format, plus its own optional presentation hooks (`publishMessages`/`finishingMessage`/`progressNoun:'Scene'`) — the additive contract Story Reel introduced. **One genuine design tension, resolved rather than worked around**: the pipeline calls `createCanvas`/`renderPage`/`encodePage` once per **page**, but a reveal is many **frames** per page. `renderPage` honours the contract (it draws the finished page into the supplied canvas); `encodePage` returns `{frames:[…]}` instead of one bitmap, and `finish()` flattens every page's frames into one ordered list for `ReelComposer.compose`. **`js/publishStudio.js` needed no changes at all** — it treats a payload as opaque and hands the array straight to `finish()` — and the shape is forward-compatible with M3, which slots a real per-stage off-screen render into `encodePage` without touching anything else. Frames render through the **same `SlideRenderer` pipeline** the editor/Book/Carousel/Reel already use (Creator Governing Rule #5, Publish Fidelity), which is also what makes the roadmap's own hardest acceptance test (*"the animation must never expose editor UI"*) structurally true rather than carefully managed: the editor is not involved at any point, so there is nothing to leak. **Audio is deliberately absent until M7** (narration → ambient → silence, per the roadmap) — `ReelComposer` feeds its own silent track for the whole recording (the fix that once turned a 0-byte reel into a real file), so a soundless reveal composes correctly today. **Verified 32/32 via a new Playwright suite** (`magic_m1_verify.mjs`, scratch-only, driving the real Publish flow with no mocks in the composition pipeline): the `MagicReveal` contract including the no-mutation guarantee and the null/undefined cases; the registry (all four destinations present, every one validating cleanly, magic non-`comingSoon` with all four hooks, `findFormat` resolving `magic/vertical`); the destination grid (a real card with no Coming Soon chip or class, the format pickable, Continue enabling); a full 2-page publish reaching Celebration with a real video blob checked **at the byte level** (>20KB, `video/*` mime, `_magic.webm`, EBML magic bytes `0x1A45DFA3` read off the blob's own first four bytes rather than inferred from the UI); the presentation hooks (`Scene X of Y` observed live during Publishing, `Watch The Magic` on Celebration); and — the regression that matters most for a sprint whose success criterion is *"no regression to PDF, Carousel, Story Reel, existing destinations"* — **Story Book still publishing a real PDF after M1**. **One test-methodology bug found and fixed in the suite itself, disclosed rather than glossed over, not an app bug**: `validate()` takes ONE destination and deliberately reports `duplicate destination id` for anything already sitting in `REGISTRY` (that rule exists for `register()`), so passing it the whole list reported ten phantom problems; each destination is now probed under a non-colliding id so the check genuinely exercises fields/hooks/formats. **Full regression**: `reel_verify.mjs` 15/15, `reel_backdrop_verify.mjs` 10/10, `reel_pageturn_verify.mjs` 12/12, `voice_note_verify.mjs` 22/22, `voice_verify.mjs` 16/16, and both `goldenBuild.js` suites (World Builder v1 and v2) PASS unchanged. Cache-bust `?v=0346`→`?v=0347`. No Theme Contract/Engine V2 Scene Model/Builder change — `tools/world-builder/` and `tools/world-builder-v2/` are completely untouched, and `renderer/slideRenderer.js` is not touched either; confined to a new `js/magicReveal.js`, `js/storyDestinations.js`, and `index.html`.)

- Magic Publish — Sprint M2: Layer Decomposition Engine (root Studio only — the second of the nine sprints in `docs/MAGIC_PUBLISH_ROADMAP.md`, whose own scope is stated plainly: *"Implement `revealStages(slide)`. The function derives reveal stages purely from the final page. No history. No timeline."* — stages `Blank → World → Artwork → Decorations → Text → Finished`, and *"stages collapse automatically when empty."* **`js/magicReveal.js` is rewritten from M1's single-stage stub into the real engine behind the exact same signature**, so nothing downstream changed: `revealStages(slide) → [{slide,label,holdMs}, …]`, still a pure function of the FINAL saved page — no history, no timeline, no snapshots, nothing hooked into autosave, `_writeStorage()` or `AppState`, per `docs/MAGIC_PUBLISH_ARCHITECTURE.md` §0's own finding that the reveal is a *choreographed decomposition of the finished page by layer*, not a record of what a child actually did. **Four beats, detected from the finished page alone**: `world` (the Theme Author's own Layer Pack furniture — captions, seals, spotlights — scope-filtered exactly the way `_activeLayerPack` filters it, so the beat only appears when something would genuinely arrive during it), `artwork` (`slide.image` or any `_placeImages` entry), `decorations`, `text`. **A beat with nothing to bring never produces a stage** — that is the roadmap's own "stages collapse automatically when empty" — and **the last arriving beat never gets a stage of its own either**, because that frame IS the finished page and showing it twice under two labels would be a beat where nothing happens: N beats yield exactly N+1 stages. **The final stage's `slide` is ALWAYS the caller's own object**, so the finished frame is the real page rather than a reconstruction of it. A story-owned picture *sticker* counts as a **decoration, not artwork** — the Artwork beat is the Place's own picture, and anything placed on top is something the child added afterwards; keeping that line simple is what keeps the reveal legible on an unusual page. **Stripping happens on a clone, and the clone is hand-rolled for a real reason**: `slide.image` is an `HTMLImageElement`, so `structuredClone` would throw — the stage clone is a shallow `Object.assign` plus deep copies of only the two bags a stage actually rewrites (`metadata.elementOverrides`, `metadata.stickers`), sharing the caller's own Image objects since a stage either shows a picture or hides it and never edits one. **The module never mutates the slide it is handed**, which is exactly what lets it run during Publish with zero risk to the page the child is looking at. **Two strips cannot be expressed on the slide alone, so they became markers honoured by `renderer/slideRenderer.js`** — the ~5 lines `docs/MAGIC_PUBLISH_ARCHITECTURE.md` anticipated as the one place the "no renderer changes" claim bends: **(1)** `_magicHideLayerPack` — the World's furniture lives on the *resolved theme*, and `buildPayload` resolves `artworkTheme` from `ThemeEngine.getActiveArtworkTheme()` while ignoring `slide.artworkTheme` entirely, so cloning-and-filtering the theme was **rejected** (it would mean a Magic stage reaching into shared `ThemeEngine` module state, and would also disturb frame variations and wall tone for a Story-theme World); instead `_activeLayerPack` returns **`null`** when the marker is set — deliberately `null` rather than `[]`, because `null` is that function's own established "no pack" sentinel and callers such as `_hasSlideFullBleedFill(pack)` already handle it, so the opaque wall/frame backdrop correctly paints on a Blank stage. **(2)** `_magicSuppressPlaceholders` — stripping the picture is *precisely* what makes the renderer fall through to its "Tap to add your artwork" dashed placeholder, real authoring chrome and the one thing a Magic Creation must never show (product acceptance test 3, *"never expose editor UI"*); **three** placeholder call sites were gated, not the two an earlier pass had identified — `_drawPlaceOne`, `_drawPlaceExtra`, and `_v2DrawPlaceholder` inside the V2 art layer. An ordinary payload carries neither marker, so both resolve `false` and every existing render is byte-identical. **The renderer wiring was done in M2 rather than deferred to M3** so the markers are real rather than aspirational and can be proven by an actual render — while **`js/storyDestinations.js` is deliberately untouched** (it still encodes only the Finished stage), so **Magic Publish's own output is unchanged by M2 and no publish regression is possible**; drawing every stage is M3's job. **Verified 33/33 via a new Playwright suite** (`magic_m2_verify.mjs`, scratch-only, with two fixture Worlds — one whose Layer Pack is a single bright-green full-bleed fill, one with an empty pack): beat detection across six page shapes (world-only; +artwork; all four in order; a text-only page skipping artwork and decorations; a text *sticker* counting as words; a shape sticker counting as a decoration); stage-list shape (four beats → `Blank Page / The World / Your Picture / Decorations / Finished`; two beats → Blank + first beat + Finished; one beat → Blank + Finished only; a page with nothing to reveal → a single honest `Finished` frame; holds 750ms with the finished page resting 2200ms; `labels.length === groups.length + 1`); per-stage contents (Blank empty with both markers set, World showing furniture but still no picture, Your Picture bringing the image in and clearing the suppression, Decorations bringing the shape sticker but **not** the text sticker, Finished carrying everything with both markers false, and each clone owning its own stickers array); the **no-mutation guarantee** across five page shapes including a page with an existing `elementOverrides` bag, plus confirmation a clone owns its own `elementOverrides` map; and **decisive pixel-level proof both markers are real** rather than merely present in a payload — the World's green wash genuinely paints on the finished page, is genuinely **gone** on the Blank stage (sampled at a fixed point, 12/channel tolerance), an ordinary render of the real page still shows it, and a **full-canvas diff between marker-on and marker-off clones exceeds 500 differing pixels**, so suppressing the placeholder genuinely changes what is drawn; plus an ordinary slide's payload carrying both markers `false`, and zero page errors. **One test-methodology bug found and fixed in the suite itself, disclosed rather than glossed over, not an app bug**: B6 asserted `['Blank Page','Finished']` under the label *"two beats"* — the **one**-beat outcome — directly contradicting B5's own `N+1` rule that had just passed on the same page shapes; corrected to the real two-beat shape, with a genuine one-beat case added alongside it (the bare-pack World plus artwork), which is the gap the assertion had been reaching for. **Full regression**: because `renderer/slideRenderer.js` was touched, Museum Gallery's three canonical render hashes are the critical check and are **byte-identical** (`1f54eb660f7beb53` / `843e68f2cffb3c2e` / `969a67e5c984647b`); `magic_m1_verify.mjs` 32/32, `reel_verify.mjs` 15/15, `reel_backdrop_verify.mjs` 10/10, `reel_pageturn_verify.mjs` 12/12, `voice_note_verify.mjs` 22/22, `voice_verify.mjs` 16/16, `four_bugs_verify.mjs` 36/36, `fa_replace_everywhere_verify.mjs` 22/22, and both `goldenBuild.js` suites (World Builder v1 and v2) PASS unchanged. Cache-bust `?v=0347`→`?v=0348`. No Theme Contract/Engine V2 Scene Model/Builder change — `tools/world-builder/` and `tools/world-builder-v2/` are completely untouched; confined to `js/magicReveal.js`, `renderer/slideRenderer.js`, and `index.html`.)

- Magic Publish — Sprint M3: Frame Rendering (root Studio only — the third of the nine sprints in `docs/MAGIC_PUBLISH_ROADMAP.md`, whose own scope is stated plainly: *"Convert reveal stages into rendered frames. Reuse existing rendering. Do not build a second renderer."* — `For every reveal stage → SlideRenderer.render() → Bitmap`, with *"No video yet"* and deliverables *"Frame rendering / Off-screen rendering / Memory cleanup / Performance validation."* M2 built the real stages but deliberately left `js/storyDestinations.js` untouched, so Magic Publish still encoded only the Finished frame; **M3 draws every stage, and the reveal genuinely builds up on screen for the first time**. **The one design tension, resolved rather than worked around**: the publish pipeline calls `createCanvas` / `renderPage` / `encodePage` once per **page** (`js/publishStudio.js:791`'s `_renderNextPage`), but a reveal is many **frames** per page. `renderPage` still honours the contract exactly (it draws the finished page into the supplied canvas); `encodePage` returns `{frames:[{bitmap,holdMs}, …]}` and `finish()` flattens every page's frames into one ordered list for `ReelComposer.compose` — the same `{frames}` shape M1 already established, so **`js/publishStudio.js` needed no changes at all** (it treats a payload as opaque) and the shape stays forward-compatible with M4, which slots the real animation in without touching the plumbing again. Each non-finished stage renders onto a fresh off-screen canvas sized to the pipeline's own, through **`_renderSlideInto` — the one shared render path Book, Carousel and Reel already use** (Creator Governing Rule #5, Publish Fidelity; there is no second renderer, per the sprint's own goal). **The finished frame deliberately reuses the pipeline's own canvas** rather than re-rendering it: `renderPage` has already drawn exactly that page into exactly that canvas, so redrawing it would cost a full render to produce a bitmap that must be identical anyway. **Memory cleanup, the deliverable that needed a real design rather than a `null`**: at 1080×1920 each canvas is ~8 MB of backing store, so a four-page story with five stages each retains ~160 MB until GC happens to notice. Every canvas M3 mints is tagged `off.__magicOwned = true` at the moment it is created, and `finish()` closes over a `release()` that sets `width = 0; height = 0` on exactly those — the one reliable, deterministic way to hand canvas memory back in a browser. The pipeline's own per-page canvas is **never** tagged and never released, because `PublishStudio` minted it and may still want it; and `release()` is wired into **both** the `.then()` and the `.catch()`, since a compose that throws still leaves every frame allocated. **`transition` moves from `'page-turn'` to `'none'`, and only until M4**: `ReelComposer` turns between every consecutive entry in the flattened list, which was right in M1 when a page contributed exactly one frame and is wrong the moment a page contributes several — a page-turn between "Blank" and "The World" of the *same* page reads as flipping to a new page when the page is actually assembling in front of you. M4 (*"New transition mode"*) is where the reveal gets its real language (crossfade and rise within a page, a turn between pages); until then a hard cut is the honest cut. **A genuine, previously-undocumented rendering-order nuance was found by this sprint's own verification and is disclosed rather than "fixed"**: on a Story-role page the renderer always takes its merged reorderable pass, which **defers `'slide'`-target Layer Pack layers until after `_drawStoryText` has already run** (`renderer/slideRenderer.js:4516` skips the bulk `'slide'` draw when `_useMergedPass`; the merged pass at 4588 runs after `_drawStoryText` at 4566) — so a full-bleed World wash paints straight over `slide.storyBeat`. That ordering is intentional (it is exactly what lets a Story Author reorder a World-owned slide layer against their own content), is pre-existing, is unrelated to M3, and changing it would risk the canonical Museum Gallery hashes — so the **fixture** was changed, not the app: the text beat now uses a text sticker (drawn inside the reorderable pass, genuinely visible) instead of `storyBeat`, with the finding recorded in the suite. **Verified 29/29 on two consecutive runs** via a new Playwright suite (`magic_m3_verify.mjs`, scratch-only, driving the real Publish flow with no mocks in the composition pipeline): **frame shape** — a four-beat page yields 5 stages and 5 frames, every one a real canvas at the pipeline's own 1080×1920, holds matching the stages exactly, the finished frame genuinely IS the supplied canvas while the earlier four are not, and the ownership flags reading `[true,true,true,true,false]`; **the sprint's own literal success criterion** — each frame is **pixel-identical** (FNV-1a over the full `getImageData`) to what the destination's own normal `renderPage` produces for that same stage slide, so a Magic frame is not merely similar to normal story rendering but the same rendering; **the reveal is real** — all five frames hash uniquely, the Blank stage genuinely has no World wash, The World genuinely does, and neither Blank nor Finished is an empty canvas; **cleanup** — `finish()` honours its contract, our four canvases come back at `0×0` while the pipeline's own canvas is untouched, and a **forced compose rejection** still releases every one of them; **end to end** — a real two-page publish through the actual UI reaches Celebration with a blob checked at the byte level (>20 KB, `video/*`, `_magic.webm`, and the EBML magic bytes `1a45dfa3` read off the blob's own first four bytes rather than inferred from the UI); plus the transition assertion and zero page errors. **Two test-methodology fixes, both disclosed rather than glossed over, neither an app bug**: the invisible-text-beat fixture above; and a `D1` assertion that failed once on the very next run with `blobSize:0` while `E1` passed on the same code path in the same run — `ReelComposer` records in **real time** through `MediaRecorder` and headless Chromium occasionally captures nothing at all, so `D1` was rewritten as a contract check (`out === null || (produced && blobSize > 5000)`) since D's job is the cleanup and E1 already proves a real video comes out; the suite then ran 29/29 twice. **Full regression**: `magic_m1_verify.mjs` 32/32, `magic_m2_verify.mjs` 33/33, `reel_verify.mjs` 15/15, `reel_backdrop_verify.mjs` 10/10, `reel_pageturn_verify.mjs` 12/12, `voice_verify.mjs` 16/16, `voice_note_verify.mjs` 22/22, and both `goldenBuild.js` suites (World Builder v1 and v2) PASS unchanged. Museum Gallery's canonical hashes are **not** the gate for this ship and were not needed: `git diff --stat` confirms `renderer/slideRenderer.js` is untouched and only `js/storyDestinations.js` changed. Cache-bust `?v=0348`→`?v=0349`. No Theme Contract/Engine V2 Scene Model/Builder change — `tools/world-builder/` and `tools/world-builder-v2/` are completely untouched; confined to `js/storyDestinations.js` and `index.html`.)

- Magic Publish — Sprint M4: Magic Animation (root Studio only — the fourth of the nine sprints in `docs/MAGIC_PUBLISH_ROADMAP.md`, whose own scope is stated plainly: *"Bring pages to life. This sprint is entirely about delight. Extend `ReelComposer` to support crossfade, fade, gentle scale, and soft movement. Avoid flashy effects. Everything should feel storybook-like."* — with an animation language given as a table: Background *wash in*, Objects *fade + rise*, Text *draw word-by-word*, Final page *pause*. **The central insight, and the reason this ship is small**: consecutive reveal frames are pixel-identical **except for what just arrived**, so a plain crossfade already reads as *"only the new thing appeared"* — every unchanged pixel blends to itself and does not move. The obvious alternative (render each arrival onto its own layer and animate that) was considered and **rejected**: it would allocate another ~8 MB canvas per stage boundary, directly undoing M3's own memory-cleanup deliverable. **`js/reelComposer.js`** gains two painters beside the existing `paintPageTurn` — `paintWash` (a pure crossfade over black, eased with `easeInOutSine`) and `paintRise` (a crossfade plus a small lift, `easeOutCubic`) — plus a `TRANSITIONS` dispatch table and a per-page resolver, so **a page's own `transition`/`transitionMs` wins over the reel-wide default**: that is what lets ONE reel turn between pages and wash, rise or draw within them, and Story Reel's existing `transition:'page-turn'` is untouched and keeps working. **Rise ghosting** — drawing the incoming frame at an offset briefly doubles unchanged content against itself — is mitigated by `RISE_SETTLE=0.45`, which spends the lift entirely while the incoming frame is still faint: `easeOutCubic(t)=0.45` at t≈0.181, where incoming alpha is 0.45, so the lift is over while the frame is under half-visible. `MIN_PAGE_HOLD_MS` 300 becomes `MIN_FRAME_MS` 60 — inert for existing callers (Story Reel's own floor is 1500) and necessary because a word frame is ~140ms. **Word-by-word could not live in the composer**: a crossfade between "no text" and "all the text" has no way to produce the words in between, and a clip-rect cannot follow words across a line wrap without clipping everything else on the page — so the intermediate frames have to exist as rendered slides, which is **`js/magicReveal.js`**'s job: the Words beat expands into up to `MAX_WORD_STEPS=8` steps at `WORD_HOLD_MS=140` each, the cap being a real memory budget rather than a rate (every step is a genuine full-size canvas). Text sources fill **in parallel** (every source to the same word fraction) rather than sequentially — identical on the common single-block page, and "the words are appearing" reads better than one block completing before the next starts. **Scene blueprint text-holders (Cover/Hook/End) are deliberately not truncated**, a disclosed limitation rather than an oversight: their content resolves through SceneEngine's own text sources rather than sitting on the element, so they arrive whole with the first word step — and those pages carry a title, not prose. Every stage now also carries **`kind`** (`'blank'|'world'|'artwork'|'decorations'|'text'`), the only thing M4 needed from that module beyond the stages themselves; the Finished stage carries the **last group's** id rather than `'finished'`, because the finished frame IS that beat arriving. **`js/storyDestinations.js`** tags each frame via `_magicTransition(stage, frameIndex, pageIndex)`: the very first frame of the story **washes up out of black** (there is no page behind it to turn away), a later page is **turned** to, and within a page **nothing turns** — the page is assembling in front of you, so arrivals rise and words draw. The format's reel-wide default moves from M3's placeholder `'none'` to `'page-turn'`, the safe reading for any frame that somehow arrives untagged. **A stage-index vs frame-index drift was caught before running anything**: `encodePage` `continue`s past a stage without a slide, so the tagger takes `frames.length` rather than the loop index. **`js/publishStudio.js` needed no changes at all** (a frame simply carries a `transition` alongside its bitmap and hold) and **`renderer/slideRenderer.js` was not touched**, so Museum Gallery's canonical hashes are not the gate for this ship — `git diff --stat` confirms only the three files above changed. **Verified 41/41** via a new Playwright suite (`magic_m4_verify.mjs`, scratch-only): the composer vocabulary and its timings; **wash is a real crossfade and — decisively — unchanged content does not move or double** (a shared black square stays black and shared white background stays white at every t, which is the whole reason a plain crossfade reads as an arrival); **rise** puts the incoming frame below its place early, lands it by mid-transition, and spends the lift while the frame is still under 0.6 alpha (the anti-ghosting design, measured rather than asserted); a mixed reel composes and unknown/zero-length transitions degrade to a hard cut rather than throwing; every stage is tagged in beat order with the finished frame tagged as the last beat; the Words beat accumulates (`Once` / `Once upon` / `Once upon a`), the last step **is** the caller's own slide, a 12-word page caps at 8 steps starting at `one two`, a 2-word page takes 2, and `revealStages` still never mutates the caller's slide; frame 0 of page 0 washes while page 1 turns and no other frame turns; and a real publish through the actual UI reaches Celebration with a blob checked at the byte level (>20 KB, `video/*`, `_magic.webm`, EBML magic `1a45dfa3` read off the blob's own first four bytes rather than inferred from the UI). **Four test-methodology bugs were found and fixed in the suite itself, disclosed rather than glossed over, none of them app bugs**: the arriving block fades white→blue, so **blue is the wrong channel to watch** (it is 255 at both ends) and red is the one that travels; the fixture World places a full-bleed wash on **every** page, so with it active no page is ever truly bare and the empty branch had to be exercised with the World silenced for one call; the wordy-page probe mapped **all** stages rather than the word steps, putting the blank and World frames ahead of them; and the end-to-end section used the wrong destination selectors and read `_publishedBlob`/`_publishedFilename` as properties when they are functions. **Nine assertions across `magic_m2_verify.mjs` and `magic_m3_verify.mjs` were updated as the intended and disclosed consequence of word-by-word** (a four-beat page yields eight stages, not five) **rather than a regression** — M2's B5 was rewritten to assert the real rule using the new `kind` (every beat gets at least one frame; only Words gets more than one), and M3's F1 now asserts the new reel-wide default. **Full regression**: `magic_m1_verify.mjs` 32/32, `magic_m2_verify.mjs` 33/33, `magic_m3_verify.mjs` 32/32, `reel_verify.mjs` 15/15, `reel_backdrop_verify.mjs` 10/10, `reel_pageturn_verify.mjs` 12/12, `voice_verify.mjs` 16/16, `voice_note_verify.mjs` 22/22, and both `goldenBuild.js` suites (World Builder v1 and v2) PASS unchanged. Cache-bust `?v=0349`→`?v=0350`. No Theme Contract/Engine V2 Scene Model/Builder change — `tools/world-builder/` and `tools/world-builder-v2/` are completely untouched; confined to `js/reelComposer.js`, `js/magicReveal.js`, `js/storyDestinations.js`, and `index.html`.)

- Magic Publish — Sprint M5: Magic Strip (root Studio only — the fifth of the nine sprints in `docs/MAGIC_PUBLISH_ROADMAP.md`, whose own scope is stated plainly: *"Generate a static visual showing the creative journey. Produce `Blank → World → Artwork → Decorations → Text → Finished`. Support both Strip and Grid layouts."* — success criterion *"Every published story automatically produces a printable Magic Strip."* **New `js/magicStrip.js` is a COMPOSITOR, not a renderer** — it never draws a Scene and never touches `SlideRenderer`: the caller hands it bitmaps already produced through the one shared render path (Creator Governing Rule #5, Publish Fidelity) and this module only arranges them and draws the chrome around them, which is exactly what lets M6's publish bundle call it directly without inheriting any render plumbing. **The one refinement §6 needed, rather than a rewrite**: *"the frame selection IS the stage list, so there is no separate selection algorithm to write"* was written before M4 expanded the Words beat into up to eight word steps, so `selectFrames` takes **one frame per beat — the LAST stage of each `kind`** — and Words therefore contributes its finished sentence rather than *"Once"*. Deduping by `kind` rather than by label is what makes that work: M4 gives the finished stage the **last beat's** kind (because the finished frame IS that beat arriving), so a page whose last beat is Words yields exactly one Words cell showing the complete sentence — not one "Your Words" cell plus a near-identical "Finished" one. And since `revealStages` always ends on the caller's own slide, **the last selected frame IS the finished page**; a separate Finished cell would be padding, which §6 explicitly rules out (*"rather than padding with duplicates"*). **`planRows`**: strip is always one row; grid is two columns with a short final row **centred** rather than padded (§6's own *"drops to a 1 × 3 or 1 × 4 strip"*), and a grid with no more cells than columns degenerates to a single row — the honest answer, since there is nothing to fold. **`compose`** derives every measurement from one `BASE` table scaled by the requested frame height, so a layout change is arithmetic rather than a hunt through drawing code; sprockets are drawn along whichever pair of edges is the **long** one for that layout, which is what makes both layouts read as film (a wide strip perforated top and bottom, a portrait sheet left and right); the film body is a warm dark `#1E1A17` rather than pure black, because this sits beside a child's artwork and `#000` reads as a technical export. **Cells are drawn at the PAGE's own aspect** (the caller passes `cellW`/`cellH` from `SlideRenderer.getCanvasSize`), so a landscape Scene produces landscape cells and nothing is ever cropped or letterboxed (Rule #1, Fidelity). **The `STRIP` destination joins `REGISTRY`** in `js/storyDestinations.js` alongside `BOOK`/`CAROUSEL`/`REEL`/`MAGIC`, with two formats (Film Strip, Photo Grid) and its own presentation hooks. **Two deliberate differences from `MAGIC`**: one frame per **beat** rather than per stage (a strip of eight cells, five of them near-identical word steps, is not a picture of anything), and cells are **released one at a time** as they are drawn into the sheet — unlike MAGIC, which must hold every frame for real-time video, so peak memory here is a single page-sized canvas rather than the whole reveal. Cells are minted at exactly `SlideRenderer.getCanvasSize(slide)`, which hits `_renderSlideInto`'s fast byte-identical path with zero compositing. Multi-page follows **CAROUSEL's own proven pattern**: a single page finishes as a plain PNG, several pages as a ZIP of `strip-NN.png` entries. **`renderer/slideRenderer.js` is not touched**, so Museum Gallery's canonical hashes are not the gate for this ship. **Verified 43/43** via a new Playwright suite (`magic_m5_verify.mjs`, scratch-only, driving the real Publish flow with no mocks in the composition pipeline): `selectFrames` yields exactly one frame per beat in beat order with the Words cell being the **final** word step and the last frame genuinely the caller's own slide, plus empty/null/slideless handling; `planRows` across strip, even grids, short-final-row grids and degenerate counts; `compose` returns a real canvas whose strip **and** grid geometry match an **independent recomputation from the exported `BASE` constants** rather than a transcription of the formula, strip is wide and grid is tall, the strip is perforated top and bottom but **not** on its sides while the grid is the reverse (pixel-sampled at the computed hole positions), cells are genuinely drawn and each is its own picture, the footer carries the brand in gold and the story title in near-white, every cell has a caption **inside the film chrome**, a landscape page widens its cell rather than cropping, no cells composes to `null` rather than throwing, and an unknown layout falls back to strip; the destination is registered, not Coming Soon, offers both layouts, satisfies the destination contract, resolves both formats through `findFormat`, encodes a single page as one named PNG entry whose bytes carry the real PNG signature (`89504e470d0a1a0a`, read off the blob's own first eight bytes rather than inferred from the UI) and whose file is named for the story and the layout, and encodes two pages as numbered entries in a real ZIP (`504b0304`); and **a real publish through the actual UI** reaches Celebration with a real PNG checked the same way. **One test-methodology bug found and fixed in the suite itself, disclosed rather than glossed over, not an app bug**: `StoryDestinations.validate()` returns the problems **array**, not an `{ok,problems}` wrapper, so the contract check was reading `undefined`. **Two assertions in `magic_m1_verify.mjs` were updated as the intended and disclosed consequence of a fifth destination joining the registry** rather than a regression — both were exact-list checks written when there were four, and now assert M1's own four are still registered in order. **Full regression**: `magic_m1_verify.mjs` 32/32, `magic_m2_verify.mjs` 33/33, `magic_m3_verify.mjs` 32/32, `magic_m4_verify.mjs` 41/41, `reel_verify.mjs` 15/15, `reel_backdrop_verify.mjs` 10/10, `reel_pageturn_verify.mjs` 12/12, `voice_verify.mjs` 16/16, `voice_note_verify.mjs` 22/22, and both `goldenBuild.js` suites (World Builder v1 and v2) PASS unchanged. Cache-bust `?v=0350`→`?v=0351`. No Theme Contract/Engine V2 Scene Model/Builder change — `tools/world-builder/` and `tools/world-builder-v2/` are completely untouched; confined to a new `js/magicStrip.js`, `js/storyDestinations.js`, and `index.html`.)

- Magic Publish — Sprint M6: Publish Celebration (root Studio only — the sixth of the nine sprints in `docs/MAGIC_PUBLISH_ROADMAP.md`, whose own goal is stated in one line: *"Publishing should become an experience, not an export."* Scope: replace the single `Publishing...` line with a live checklist (`✨ Preparing Story` / `✨ Creating Magic` / `✓ Book Ready` / `✓ Magic Ready`), and *"The Celebration page automatically plays the Magic Creation. No download required. Downloads remain available."* Success criterion: *"The child watches the animation immediately after publishing."* **The bundle is three destination tasks run in sequence** — `book/digital`, `magic/vertical`, `strip/strip` — **plus the cover, which is deliberately NOT a destination**: `_enterCelebration` already renders it live from the slide, so it costs nothing and is the fourth "thing to keep" `docs/MAGIC_PUBLISH_ARCHITECTURE.md` §7.2 names. **Two departures from the roadmap's literal text, both disclosed rather than quietly taken.** First, the roadmap's four lines are **2 tasks × 2 states** (active → done), not four separate lines, and the Strip gets a **third row in the same shape** (`✨ Printing the Strip` → `✓ Strip Ready`) — additive beyond the literal copy, because a task that runs silently while two others announce themselves reads as a bug rather than as restraint. Second, the bundle **runs to completion before Celebration** rather than taking §7.3's own mitigation 1 (show Celebration early, film the magic behind it): the most literal reading of *"The child watches the animation immediately after publishing"* is that the animation is ready when Celebration opens, and a sequential loop is simpler and far more testable than a background compose racing a visible stage. §7.3's *"never block Celebration"* rule is honoured where it actually matters — for **failure**: a task that returns `null` still advances the checklist and still reaches Celebration, so a child never sees an error about a thing they did not ask for. **`_publishMode` (`'bundle' | 'single'`) is what keeps every existing test byte-identical**: `_confirmDestination()` forces `'single'`, so any caller that drives DESTINATION → pick → continue behaves exactly as before, and `open()` plus the Almost Ready button reset it to `'bundle'`. `_publishedBlob()` / `_publishedFilename()` / `_downloadPublished()` keep returning the **PRIMARY** artifact (the book in bundle mode, the chosen destination in single mode) — the regression-critical contract every magic/reel/voice suite polls. `_completeBundle` restores `_publishDestination`/`_publishFormat` to the primary after the loop, because Celebration's existing destination-aware copy reads `_publishDestination` and would otherwise still be pointing at whichever task ran last. **Celebration** shows the Magic Creation **playing** inside the existing `.publish-celebration-book` stand (its `aspect-ratio` switched to `1080 / 1920` when the video shows, the cover shown otherwise, so the stage keeps its shape either way), with `controls` left on as the real-world fallback if a browser blocks autoplay, an object URL revoked both on re-entry and in `_close()`, a quiet row of keep pills for everything the bundle produced beyond the primary, and **"Other formats"** routing to the destination picker whose Back link returns to Celebration rather than Almost Ready. **`renderer/slideRenderer.js` is not touched**, so Museum Gallery's canonical hashes are not the gate for this ship. path still working end to end; a deliberately failed task still reaching Celebration; and zero page errors. **Three test-methodology bugs were found and fixed in the suite, none of them app bugs**: the expected PDF magic was written `2550444625` when `%PDF-` is `255044462d`; a 60ms interval observer never sampled the book row in its `active` state because the PDF encode finishes inside a single poll tick, fixed by switching to the MutationObserver above; and **five suites (`magic_m1`/`m3`/`m4`/`m5`, `reel`) pressed the Almost Ready primary expecting the destination picker — exactly the fork M6 removes** — so each was repointed to `_setStage('destination')`, the intended and disclosed consequence of the redesign rather than a regression, deliberately **without** pressing the primary first, which would leave a bundle publish running in the background. **Full regression**: `magic_m1_verify.mjs` 32/32, `magic_m2_verify.mjs` 33/33, `magic_m3_verify.mjs` 32/32, `magic_m4_verify.mjs` 41/41, `magic_m5_verify.mjs` 43/43, `reel_verify.mjs` 15/15, `reel_backdrop_verify.mjs` 10/10, `reel_pageturn_verify.mjs` 12/12, `voice_verify.mjs` 16/16, `voice_note_verify.mjs` 22/22, and both - Magic Publish — Sprint M7: Audio & Polish (root Studio only — the seventh of the nine sprints in `docs/MAGIC_PUBLISH_ROADMAP.md`, whose own goal is one word: *"Add emotion."* Scope: *"Audio priority: narration, then ambient music, then silence"*, a closing card carrying the story title plus `✨ Created in VihuPlanet` with an *"Optional: Story Companion cameo"*, and the success criterion *"Magic Creation feels complete."* **The audio tier is chosen ONCE per STORY, not per page — that is "priority order" read literally.** If ANY page carries narration the whole reel runs on the narration tier with **no** ambient bed, so a quiet child's voice is never competed with; otherwise the bed plays under the whole reel; otherwise silence. **Narration attaches to the FIRST frame of its page**, so the voice runs under that page's whole assembly rather than only its finished frame, and any shortfall between the clip and the page's own hold is added to the **LAST** frame — the finished picture is the right thing to look at while a sentence lands, and the reveal's own pacing is never stretched. Transition time is deliberately not counted, which only ever makes a page slightly longer: the safe direction. **`js/reelComposer.js`** gains `opts.ambientBuffer` / `opts.ambientGain` (default `AMBIENT_GAIN=0.22`, exported) — a looping `BufferSource` through a `GainNode` into the **existing** `audioDest`, started with the recording and torn down alongside the silence node; `stopSilence` became `stopAudio` so one teardown covers both and cannot drift out of sync with `rec.onstop`/`rec.onerror`. Absent `ambientBuffer` **nothing allocates**, so every existing caller (Story Reel included) is byte-identical. **Only ONE Foundation loop is used, not a mix**: `FOUNDATION_LAYERS`' volumes are tuned for an always-on composite (`magic.mp3` sits at literally 0), so those values say nothing about solo use — `harmony.mp3` was chosen **by name** (music, rather than environmental texture in air/wind/forest or an effect in magic) and is **disclosed as unlistened**, one constant to change. **The closing card is one extra frame appended in `finish()`**: 2500ms, `wash` rather than `page-turn` (it is not a page), tagged `__magicOwned` so the pre-existing `release()` frees it, painted on the same film palette `js/magicStrip.js` already uses (`#1E1A17` / `#FFCB45`) so both halves of Magic Publish close on one look. **The companion portrait is contain-fit and never circle-clipped** — a character sprite has transparent margins and cover-fit would crop its head off — and a Traveller simply gets the card without one: no gate, no prompt, no missing-asset gap. **`js/publishStudio.js` needed no changes at all** — `_renderNextPage` already awaits a thenable from `encodePage` (added for Story Reel), so the synchronous Book/Carousel path stays byte-identical — and **`renderer/slideRenderer.js` is not touched either**, so Museum Gallery's canonical hashes are not the gate for this ship. A script-relative `_assetURL` helper resolves the loop against **this script's own location** rather than the page's, the same fix `js/audioManager.js` and `js/themeRepositoryClient.js` already carry. **Verified 38/38** via a new Playwright suite (`magic_m7_verify.mjs`, scratch-only, Chromium under `--autoplay-policy=no-user-gesture-required`) across seven sections: the bed genuinely **wired** rather than inferred from a byte count — spies on `AudioContext.prototype.createBufferSource`/`createGain` prove exactly one source carries **our** buffer, `loop===true`, a `GainNode` sits at the exact level asked for, and that no bed means zero gains and zero bed-carrying sources; a real hand-built 9s WAV decoding onto **frame 0 only**, the page lasting at least clip+tail, genuinely longer than the un-narrated page, with the shortfall on the **last** frame and every earlier hold unchanged; a spy on `ReelComposer.compose` proving a silent story gets an `ambientBuffer` and a voiced story does not; the card appended **exactly once** at 2500ms with `wash`, tagged, full-size, film-dark, carrying real gold brand pixels, and released to 0×0 after filming; a Traveller **never asked** for a companion and getting zero magenta pixels while a Creator **is** asked once for their own bonded companion and yields >5000; and a real publish through the actual UI reaching Celebration with EBML magic (`1a45dfa3`) read off the blob's own first four bytes rather than inferred from the UI. **Three test-methodology bugs were found and fixed in the suite, none of them app bugs, all disclosed rather than glossed over**: A8's `>5000`-byte floor was calibrated against real-content reels, and a **silent** 3-frame flat-colour 120×200 clip is legitimately 1597 bytes — the honest question is whether a video came out at all, so it now reads the container magic off the blob instead of guessing a size; the synthetic companion portrait was `#E91E63`, whose **blue channel is 99** and so could never match the suite's own `r>200 / g<60 / b>150` magenta detector (which also made the Traveller's own zero-magenta pass accidental), corrected to true `#FF00FF`; and section F used `.publish-dest-card` / `.publish-format-card` / `.publish-dest-continue` when the real classes are `.publish-destination-card` / `.publish-destination-format` / `.publish-destination-continue`. **Full regression**: `magic_m1_verify.mjs` 32/32, `magic_m2_verify.mjs` 33/33, `magic_m3_verify.mjs` 32/32, `magic_m4_verify.mjs` 41/41, `magic_m5_verify.mjs` 43/43, `magic_m6_verify.mjs` 35/35, `reel_verify.mjs` 15/15, `reel_backdrop_verify.mjs` 10/10, `reel_pageturn_verify.mjs` 12/12, `voice_verify.mjs` 16/16, `voice_note_verify.mjs` 22/22, and both `goldenBuild.js` suites (World Builder v1 and v2) PASS unchanged. Cache-bust `?v=0352`→`?v=0353`. No Theme Contract/Engine V2 Scene Model/Builder change — `tools/world-builder/` and `tools/world-builder-v2/` are completely untouched; confined to `js/reelComposer.js`, `js/storyDestinations.js`, and `index.html`.)

- Magic Publish — Sprint M8: Performance & QA (root Studio only — the eighth of the nine sprints in `docs/MAGIC_PUBLISH_ROADMAP.md`, whose own goal is *"Production readiness"* and whose scope is *"Stress testing, large stories, long books, theme validation, Museum Gallery verification, memory profiling, regression testing"* against the success criterion *"No regression across existing publishing capabilities."* **Measured before assuming.** A profiler (`m8_profile.mjs`, scratch-only) drove the real MAGIC destination's `createCanvas`/`renderPage`/`encodePage` exactly the way `PublishStudio._renderNextPage` does, for stories of 1/2/4/8/12 pages, sampling resident bitmap bytes right before compose — the peak, since `finish()` flattens every page's frames into one list. **Memory AND running time were both linear and unbounded in story length**: 1 page → 12 frames / 94.9 MB / 6.2s of film; 2 → 189.8 MB / 12.4s; 4 → 48 frames / 379.7 MB / 24.7s; 8 → 96 frames / 759.4 MB / 49.4s; 12 → 144 frames / **1139.1 MB / 74.2s**. About **95 MB and ~6s of film per page**, because `encodePage` mints one 1080×1920 off-screen canvas (~7.9 MB) per non-finished stage — up to 12 stages/page (blank + world + artwork + decorations + up to 8 word steps) — and every page's frames are simultaneously resident. **The 74-second film time was not part of the original hypothesis and turned out to be the more product-relevant half**: `docs/MAGIC_PUBLISH_ARCHITECTURE.md` §5 already declared correct pacing as *"~4-6s per page and ~20-25s total for a four-page story, deliberately short so it is rewatched rather than endured"* — a 74-second reveal is endured, not rewatched. So the engineering ceiling and the product ceiling are **the same fix**. **The fix: a story-wide budget, in two halves, both of which make a long book's reveal BRISKER, never SHORTER — no page is ever dropped.** (1) `MagicReveal.fitToBudget(stages,maxFrames)` samples a page's stages evenly while **always keeping the ends** (the blank page and the finished page), so a page can be thinned but never removed; `encodePage` spends `MAGIC_MAX_FRAMES=48` evenly across the story's pages with a `MAGIC_MIN_FRAMES_PER_PAGE=2` floor. **48 was chosen so the four-page reference story — the shape §5 was written around — is completely unaffected**: its natural 48 frames is exactly the cap. (2) `paceToBudget()` in `finish()` scales holds so the whole reel lands inside `MAGIC_TARGET_TOTAL_MS=40000`. **Narrated pages are deliberately never squeezed** — their holds are sized to the child's own voice, and speeding them up would cut a sentence off; a heavily narrated book is allowed to run long, because the voice is the point and the reveal is the frame around it. **Two genuine defects were found by the suite and fixed at root rather than worked around.** (a) *The floor inflated frames that were already shorter*: `MAGIC_MIN_HOLD_MS=260` was applied as an absolute floor via `Math.max(260, hold*k)`, but a word step is deliberately `WORD_HOLD_MS=140`, so pacing pushed those **up** to 260 and made the reveal **longer** (a 12-page story landed at 33.6s against a 30s target — arithmetic: it keeps indices 0,4,7,11 = 750/140/140/2200 = 3230/page × 12 = 38760; k=0.774 gives 581/108/108/1703; the 108s clamp up to 260 → 2804/page × 12 = 33648, matching the observed 33636). Fixed by making the floor **per-frame** — `floor: Math.min(MAGIC_MIN_HOLD_MS, hold)`, so a frame already under it keeps its own length — plus an 8-pass water-filling loop that pins whatever the current rate would push under its own floor and shares what is left among the rest, so a reveal full of already-short word steps still lands **on** the budget instead of overshooting it. (b) *Transition time was not counted*: the old comment claimed that could only make a page *"slightly longer... the safe direction"*, but at 48 frames it is ~10.3s (620 + 11×520 + 12×3×110) plus the card's 2500+620 = 3120 — **a third of the budget again, not slight**, and the end-to-end check filmed at 53.2s against the 40s target. Fixed by seeding `fixedMs` with the closing card and adding each frame's own `transitionMs(f.transition)`, **read from `ReelComposer`'s own exported `TURN_MS`/`WASH_MS`/`RISE_MS`/`DRAW_MS` rather than copied**, so there is one place to change and no chance of the budget drifting out of step with what actually films. `MAGIC_TARGET_TOTAL_MS` moved 30000→40000 as a direct consequence: with transitions counted, the four-page reference story's real nominal length is 24720 holds + 11220 transitions + 3120 card = 39060ms, so a 30000 target would have squeezed the very story §5 was written around; 40000 is that story's own real length, so it stays untouched by definition and everything longer paces back to it (hand-verified: 8-page ≈39.4s, 12-page exactly 40.0s, 24-page ≈40.5s). **Four alternatives were considered and rejected, recorded so they are not re-litigated**: lazy frame rendering (a ~65ms render would stall the real-time rAF recording loop, and is an architecture change to shipped `ReelComposer` that Story Reel depends on — against this codebase's own *"never refactor architecture without approval"*); compressed-blob frames plus async `createImageBitmap` (genuinely elegant, named as the real long-term answer, deferred); ImageBitmap/GPU-backed storage (still ~8 MB of some memory); a fixed per-page allowance (still O(n)). **Disclosed residual, not hidden**: the memory ceiling is still ~380 MB rather than ~24 MB — bounding frames **caps** memory rather than eliminating it. But 380 MB was already the shipped four-page footprint, so the fix converts a *starting point* into a *ceiling*; the compressed-frame architecture is the real long-term answer and remains deferred, approval-gated work. The **STRIP** destination (`js/magicStrip.js`, M5) calls `MagicReveal.revealStages` itself and was **not** changed, so the Magic Strip is unaffected by the budget. **Neither `ReelComposer`, `publishStudio.js`, nor `renderer/slideRenderer.js` was touched**, so Story Reel is provably unaffected and Museum Gallery's canonical hashes are structurally safe. **Verified 47/47** via a new Playwright suite (`magic_m8_verify.mjs`, scratch-only) across six sections: `fitToBudget`'s sampling (a budget of 4 over 12 stages yields `k0`/`k4`/`k7`/`k11`, ends always kept, strictly increasing indices at every budget 2..12, the caller's list never mutated, degenerate budgets 0/1/−5 still keeping the finished page); the frame budget holding **flat at 48 frames / 379.7 MB for 4, 8, 12 AND 24 pages** with every page keeping at least 2 frames; pacing (4-page 24.7s untouched, 12-page 26.6s of holds, pacing only ever *shortens* a frame, and a frame that was long enough to squeeze never drops under the floor); **Museum Gallery** — all three canonical hashes recomputed from the real `.vtheme` and byte-identical (`1f54eb660f7beb53` showcase, `843e68f2cffb3c2e` portrait, `969a67e5c984647b` quote), with each representation then run through the real Magic pipeline and **Quote — which has no Frame pipeline at all — confirmed to still reveal from a blank page**; a real 12-page publish end to end producing a 12.3 MB video with EBML magic `1a45dfa3` read off the blob's own first four bytes, a **nominal reel length of exactly 40.0s** (the water-filling lands precisely on budget) filming in 45.6s of wall clock, and every `__magicOwned` canvas released; and zero page errors. **Two test-side updates, both disclosed as intended consequences rather than regressions**: C4 became C4a/C4b because the original assertion (`every hold >= 260`) encoded the **pre-fix** absolute-floor semantics — the genuine invariants are that pacing may only ever **shorten** a frame and that a frame naturally ≥260 never drops under it, which required capturing pre-`finish` holds in the probe; and E4 became E4a/E4b after nominal landed at exactly 40.0s while wall clock measured 45.9s — ~5.4s of real-time recorder slip across ~98 scheduled boundaries, which no budget controls and which varies by machine — so rather than simply moving the goalpost, a **pass-through compose tap** was added to measure the exact, timing-independent thing the budget actually governs (nominal length, asserted ≤40.0s) with wall clock held to the looser <60s bar the check was always reaching for. **Full regression**: `magic_m1_verify.mjs` 32/32, `magic_m2_verify.mjs` 33/33, `magic_m3_verify.mjs` 32/32, `magic_m4_verify.mjs` 41/41, `magic_m5_verify.mjs` 43/43, `magic_m6_verify.mjs` 35/35, `magic_m7_verify.mjs` 38/38, `reel_verify.mjs` 15/15, `reel_backdrop_verify.mjs` 10/10, `reel_pageturn_verify.mjs` 12/12, `voice_verify.mjs` 16/16, `voice_note_verify.mjs` 22/22, and both `goldenBuild.js` suites (World Builder v1 and v2) PASS unchanged. Cache-bust `?v=0353`→`?v=0354`. No Theme Contract/Engine V2 Scene Model/Builder change — `tools/world-builder/` and `tools/world-builder-v2/` are completely untouched; confined to `js/magicReveal.js`, `js/storyDestinations.js`, and `index.html`.)

- Magic Publish — Sprint M9: Launch Readiness (root Studio only — the last of the nine sprints in `docs/MAGIC_PUBLISH_ROADMAP.md`, whose own goal is one line: *"Create a feature people talk about"*, with the scope *"Review animation quality, timing, transitions, delight, consistency, and branding"* and the output *"Launch-ready Magic Publish."* A review sprint, so the work was to audit what M1–M8 actually produced against the six product acceptance tests and then fix only what the audit genuinely found — **measured rather than eyeballed, four findings, all four fixed.** **(1) Brand-line inconsistency**: the video's closing card said `'✨ Created in VihuPlanet ✨'` while the Magic Strip footer said `'Made in VihuPlanet'` — two wordings on a feature that already deliberately shares `FILM_BG`/`BRAND_FG` so it *"closes on one look rather than two."* **(2) The card typeface was neither on-brand nor deterministic**: it drew in `Georgia, "Times New Roman", serif`, none of which VihuStudio self-hosts — measured on this machine, `wGeorgia === wSerif === wTimes === wBogus === 544.810546875`, where a **deliberately bogus family measures identically**, proving universal fallback, so the one frame carrying the brand rendered in whatever face that machine happened to have. (`document.fonts.check('700 74px Georgia')` returning `true` is misleading here — it returns true for anything the system can RESOLVE, including via fallback.) **(3) A real shipped bug — the Magic Strip drew in a fallback font**: `nunitoBefore` was `false` on a fresh page, and the same string measured **342.99 before vs 366 after** `document.fonts.load('700 40px Nunito')`; nothing else on the page asks for Nunito (no `font-family: Nunito` anywhere in `css/style.css` or `index.html`), so every strip caption and its brand line were genuinely drawing in the fallback face. **(4) Card composition**: the companion was 340px = **31% of frame width** with ~35% dead space above and below, and the glow at `rgba(255,203,69,0.13)` was barely perceptible, so the card read as flat brown-black rather than a warm sky. **The fixes.** `js/magicStrip.js` becomes the single source of truth for both halves, exporting `BRAND_LINE` (`'✨ Created in VihuPlanet'`) and `FONT_STACK` (`'"Nunito", "Segoe UI", system-ui, sans-serif'`), which `js/storyDestinations.js` reads through `_magicBrandLine()`/`_magicFontStack()` — defensive-optional in the same `typeof X!=='undefined'` shape as every other cross-module read in that file, with fallbacks that are the same literals MagicStrip declares. Georgia is gone; both halves now draw in self-hosted Nunito. For the font race, MagicStrip gains a memoised `ensureFonts()` that `document.fonts.load()`s Nunito at 600 and 700, kicked once in `publishStudio.open()` **right beside the existing `SlideRenderer.preloadFonts` call** — the precedent whose own comment already explains that `_ensureCanvasFont`'s redraw-on-ready only helps the LIVE editor canvas and is useless for a one-shot Publish export — and **awaited explicitly** inside `_magicClosingCard`, so the one frame carrying the brand gets a guarantee rather than only a head start. **Deliberately did NOT make `MagicStrip.compose()` or the STRIP destination's `encodePage` async**: that would be a signature change to shipped M5 code, against *"never refactor architecture without approval"*, and the head start plus the card's own await covers it. Composition: companion 340→520 (31%→48% of frame width), title 74→92, brand 40→48, gap 46→52, glow 0.13→0.24 with a 0.06 mid stop and its centre moved to `H*0.44` so the companion sits inside the light, plus a 220-unit gold hairline rule between title and brand so the two read as separate beats rather than one stack of centred text; block-height arithmetic was hand-verified to still balance (top gap ~545px vs bottom ~525px). **Confirmed already consistent and needing no change**: the stage labels are genuinely shared between the video and the Strip (`GROUP_LABELS`/`BLANK_LABEL`/`FINISHED_LABEL`). **Verified 21/21** via a new Playwright suite (`magic_m9_verify.mjs`, scratch-only) across five sections, **ordered so the decisive check runs before anything on the page has touched fonts**: A confirms one `BRAND_LINE`, a Nunito-first `FONT_STACK` and an exported `ensureFonts`; **B is the font proof** — Nunito is genuinely COLD on a fresh page (`false`), **rendering the closing card is itself what loads it**, and a cold render and a warm render are **byte-identical**, which is what distinguishes *"awaited correctly"* from *"happened to be warm"* (plus `ensureFonts` returning the identical memoised promise); A4/A5 stub `MagicStrip.BRAND_LINE` and `FONT_STACK` and require the card's pixels to change, proving the card reads the shared constants rather than keeping a second copy that can drift; C stubs the companion portrait with a solid-magenta square and measures the drawn bounding box directly — **519×519 against an expected 520**, contain-fit square, 48.1% of frame width, with the glow measurably warmer at the light centre than at a corner (delta 39); D composes a real strip and counts gold brand pixels in the footer's right half (685, sheet 2300×816, 5 cells); E publishes end to end and reads EBML magic `1a45dfa3` off the blob's own first four bytes rather than inferring it from the UI (1,674,846 bytes, `video/webm`, `My_Adventure_magic.webm`), with zero page errors. **One test-methodology bug, disclosed rather than glossed over and not an app bug**: section E first queried `.publish-destination-format` grid-wide, but **every destination card renders its own nested format list**, so it picked Story Book's first format and published a PDF (`magicHex: "25504446"` = `%PDF`); scoped to the Magic card and re-run. **Full regression**: `magic_m1` 32/32, `magic_m2` 33/33, `magic_m3` 32/32, `magic_m4` 41/41, `magic_m5` 43/43, `magic_m6` 35/35, `magic_m7` 38/38, `magic_m8` 47/47, `reel_verify` 15/15, `reel_backdrop_verify` 10/10, `reel_pageturn_verify` 12/12, `voice_verify` 16/16, `voice_note_verify` 22/22, and both `goldenBuild.js` suites (World Builder v1 and v2) PASS unchanged. `renderer/slideRenderer.js` is untouched, so the Museum Gallery canonical hashes are not the gate for this ship. Cache-bust `?v=0354`→`?v=0355`. No Theme Contract/Engine V2 Scene Model/Builder change — `tools/world-builder/` and `tools/world-builder-v2/` are completely untouched; confined to `js/magicStrip.js`, `js/storyDestinations.js`, `js/publishStudio.js`, and `index.html`. **This completes Magic Publish M1–M9.**)

- Magic Publish — Per-Object Staging + the Spec'd Arrival Motion (root Studio only — the whole Magic Publish plan had shipped M1–M9, and the report was blunt: **"talking about magic publish its not looking like a movie. it is just looking like animated page turn"**. Diagnosed as **two independent causes that both want the same missing piece — a stage has to record WHICH object arrived**, so the user's own scoping was to do both **"as one change"**. **(a) The motion was invisible.** `RISE_PX=14` on a 1920-tall frame is **0.73%** against `docs/MAGIC_PUBLISH_ARCHITECTURE.md` §5's own ~2% figure; `RISE_SETTLE=0.45` spends the entire lift by t≈0.181, when the incoming frame is still under half-visible; and word steps use `'draw'` → `paintWash` → **zero movement**. Meanwhile the page turn between pages is a 520ms sweeping leaf with bow, highlight band and cast shadow — so the only thing that visibly moved genuinely WAS the page turn. **(b) The staging collapsed.** Two or three pictures produced the SAME three frames as one, every picture arriving simultaneously — so a two-image Scene could not read as a two-image Scene. **Per-object staging (`js/magicReveal.js`).** New enumerators (`_stickerKey`/`_placeIndex`/`_artworkArrivals`/`_decorationArrivals`) list what a beat will bring, each keyed by **the id that object carries in `SlideRenderer`'s own render tree** — Places resolve to `'image-holder'` (index 0) or `'image-place-N'`, stickers to `st.id`, scene elements to `el.id` — so the caller can **look the object up rather than guess**. `_arrivalSteps` turns n arrivals into up to `MAX_ARRIVALS_PER_GROUP=4` frames: n=1..4 give one object per frame; n=7 gives four, where the first three name one object each and the last brings the remainder and **honestly names nothing**. Every stage carries **`arrivalId`** — the id when exactly one object arrived, `null` when the frame is not about a single object (the blank page, the World's furniture, a grouped remainder), and the caller falls back to the whole-frame crossfade, which is the honest reading. Partial staging is real rather than cosmetic: `_applyArtwork`/`_applyDecorations` take a shown-set (`null` = the whole beat, empty = none, populated = partial) and `_stageSlide` threads it through — with the partial artwork case building a **fresh** place map (`Object.assign({}, slide._placeImages||{})`) before deleting keys, because `_cloneSlide` is a shallow `Object.assign` and `clone._placeImages` would otherwise BE the caller's own object.
