The no-mutation guarantee holds: the caller's `_placeImages`, `image` and `_magicSuppressPlaceholders` are all untouched, and the final stage is still the caller's own slide. **The spec'd arrival motion (`js/reelComposer.js`).** A new `'arrival'` transition beside `page-turn`/`wash`/`rise`/`draw`: `ARRIVAL_MS=560`, `ARRIVAL_RISE_PX=38` (**~2% of 1920 — the spec's own figure**, against rise's 14), `ARRIVAL_START_SCALE=0.94`, `ARRIVAL_OVERSHOOT=1.04`, `ARRIVAL_PEAK_AT=0.62`, `ARRIVAL_CLIP_PAD=0.08`. `_arrivalScale(p)` takes **raw** progress (so a caller cannot double-ease it) and runs grow → overshoot → settle. `paintArrival` crossfades everything **outside** the arriving object's rect via an evenodd two-rect clip — so the rest of the page is pixel-identical to a plain crossfade and **does not move at all** — while **inside** a padded clip it scales and lifts the incoming frame about that rect's own centre; without a usable rect it degrades to `paintRise`, exactly. One collision resolved rather than papered over: `paintArrival` wants ~38px and `paintRise` must keep 14, so `compose()`'s `risePx` default changed `RISE_PX` → `null` and **each painter falls back to its own constant** (`paintRise` already read `typeof risePx==='number'?risePx:RISE_PX`, so `null` correctly falls through); an explicit `opts.risePx` still overrides both, and every existing caller is byte-identical. **Joining the two (`js/storyDestinations.js`).** MagicReveal names WHICH object arrived; the render tree knows WHERE it is, in the slide's own logical pixels. `_magicFrameMap` reproduces `_fitCompositeInto`'s own contain-fit centred arithmetic — which also gives the right answer on the fast path (scale 1, both offsets 0), so there is no branch — `_magicArrivalRect` maps the object's bbox into output-frame pixels, and `_magicTransition` gained a fourth argument: an object frame gets `'arrival'` when a rect resolved and `'rise'` when it did not. **The finished frame's tree was the one real problem**: `encodePage`'s finished stage reuses the pipeline's own canvas and skips `_renderSlideInto`, so by the time the loop reaches it `getSceneElements()` describes stage n-2. Re-rendering the finished page purely to refresh the tree (~65ms/page) was **rejected**; instead the tree is snapshotted at the **top** of `encodePage`, where `PublishStudio`'s own `createCanvas` → `renderPage` → `encodePage` order means it already describes the finished page and is **free**. Every other stage reads the tree straight after its own render, so a rect always describes the frame it is attached to; a stage without a slide is skipped, so the transition tag uses `frames.length` rather than the loop index. **One defect found by inspection rather than by a failing test**: `fitToBudget` hands back the same stage objects, so `arrivalId` survived trimming — but a kept frame whose predecessor was dropped now brings everything the dropped stages would have while still claiming one object. Reachable in practice (`MAGIC_MAX_FRAMES=48` gives a 4-page story 12 frames per page; a page with world + 2 places + 2 decorations + 8 words is 14 stages). Fixed with gap detection (`idx-prev>1`) that pushes a **copy** with `arrivalId:null`, never editing the caller's own objects. **Verified 48/48** via a new Playwright suite (`magic_arrival_verify.mjs`, scratch-only) on a fixture theme authoring **two Places**, so the render tree genuinely yields `image-holder` and `image-place-2`: **A** — two/three Places give two/three frames in Place order, seven decorations cap at four with the last honestly `null`, and the enumerator agrees with the stage list; **B** — a partial stage shows P1 and **not yet** P2, suppresses the authoring placeholder, writes to its own place map, and leaves the caller's slide untouched; **C** — a tight budget keeps the ends **and** nulls the claims it can no longer support, while an untrimmed list hands back the very same object references; **D** — the motion is **measured rather than eyeballed**: the lift is 30-45px, the scale starts under 1 and overshoots past it, the object is genuinely **wider** at `ARRIVAL_PEAK_AT` than at t=1 and settles within 2px of its own width, and outside the rect the frame is **pixel-identical to `paintWash`** at six sample points; **E** — a 4:5 page letterboxes with scale 1 and oy 285, and Place 1 lands at exactly `{x:64.8, y:420, w:432, h:405}`, within 1px of `getPlaceRects` mapped through the frame map, with no rect-less frame ever claiming `'arrival'`; **F** — a real publish reads EBML magic `1a45dfa3` off the blob's own first four bytes rather than inferring it from the UI; **G** — zero page errors. **One test-methodology bug, disclosed rather than glossed over and not an app bug**: E8/E9 first compared the whole **frame** object against the expected rect (the app's own value was already exactly right), fixed to read `frame.arrivalRect`. **One stale assertion updated as the intended and disclosed consequence of this ship rather than a regression**: `magic_m4`'s G4 required object frames to be `'rise'`, which is precisely what this change replaces — split into **G4a** (a word frame draws, an object frame arrives **or** rises, never the other way round and never a page turn) and **G4b** (the arrival path is genuinely live, not merely permitted). **Full regression**: `magic_m1` 32/32, `m2` 33/33, `m3` 32/32, `m4` 42/42, `m5` 43/43, `m6` 35/35, `m7` 38/38, `m8` 47/47, `m9` 21/21, `reel_verify` 15/15, `reel_backdrop_verify` 10/10, `reel_pageturn_verify` 12/12, `voice_verify` 16/16, `voice_note_verify` 22/22, and both `goldenBuild.js` suites (World Builder v1 and v2) PASS unchanged. `renderer/slideRenderer.js` is untouched, so the Museum Gallery canonical hashes are not the gate for this ship; `js/publishStudio.js` needed no change (payloads are opaque to it) and `js/magicStrip.js` needed none either (`selectFrames` dedupes by `kind` keeping the last, so it still picks the all-pictures-present frame, which is the right still for a static image). Cache-bust `?v=0355`→`?v=0356`. No Theme Contract/Engine V2 Scene Model/Builder change — `tools/world-builder/` and `tools/world-builder-v2/` are completely untouched; confined to `js/magicReveal.js`, `js/reelComposer.js`, `js/storyDestinations.js`, and `index.html`.)

- Sheet Extractor — Scan Mode for Photographed Line Art (`tools/sheet-extractor/` only — a standalone dev tool, so no Studio, Builder, Theme Contract, renderer, or publish surface is touched at all. The ask, with a photo of a child's notebook page attached: **"can we fine tune sheet extractor to extract elements from pages like this"**, and then the real goal — the drawing needs to reach **Studio**, because Image Studio gives "blurred, thin or too black" results, and the child wants to colour and resize the objects individually. **Where the existing tool goes wrong on that page, diagnosed rather than assumed — four separate failures at once, and each one drove a specific part of the fix**: (1) sheet mode samples the four corners for its background, and on a phone photo the corners are the *table*, so the background is wrong before anything else runs; (2) lighting falls off across the page, and there is no single global threshold that keeps the lit corner clean *and* still finds pencil in the shaded one — the threshold low enough to catch the shadowed drawing has already turned half the paper into one giant object; (3) pencil is mid-grey, not black, and photographed at an angle it is often only a pixel or two of real darkness; (4) the previous page bleeds through, and that bleed-through is *genuine* contrast, not noise an area filter can drop. **The deeper point, and the reason this is a mode rather than a slider tweak**: background *removal* — what both sheet mode and Image Studio's own worker do — preserves the original pixel values and softens the boundary, which is exactly backwards for line art. That single fact explains all three of the user's own symptoms at once: **blurred** is the feather step; **thin** is keeping mid-grey graphite with soft camera edges; **too black** is what raising tolerance buys, because it starts catching shadowed paper, paper tooth and bleed-through. Line art wants the opposite ending: discard the values, keep only the shape, redraw it as solid ink. **So scan mode changes both ends of the pipeline and reuses the whole middle.** The shared core is untouched — dilate for labelling only, iterative-BFS connected components, min-area discard, tight boxes recomputed from the **undilated** mask, natural reading order, and `PngEncoder` writing bytes with **zero `<canvas>` in the write path** (the premultiplied-alpha corruption this tool exists to avoid). **The front: a local-mean mask instead of a global one.** Convert to perceptual grayscale (transparent ⇒ 255 = paper, so it can never read as ink), take a **separable sliding-window box blur** for a per-pixel local mean — "what is the paper right *here*" — and call a pixel ink when it is darker than its own local mean by more than **Ink Sensitivity**. The blur is O(w·h) regardless of radius, which matters because a phone photo wants a large one. That one change is what lets a single setting span a lit corner and a shaded one, and it is also why bleed-through and sensitivity are deliberately the **same knob**: bleed-through is faint *relative to its own local paper*, so raising sensitivity drops it while leaving real strokes alone. **The back: fresh anti-aliasing, not a faded copy of a blurry photo.** The traced shape is optionally thickened by **Ink Weight** (for the pixel-or-two-of-darkness case), filled with a chosen **Ink Colour**, and its soft edge is generated by blurring the **coverage** — the binary mask — rather than the colour, with `AA_GAIN = 1.35` so a radius-1 box blur's 1.0 interior / 0.667 straight edge / 0.333 outside becomes a solid interior and a still-nearly-solid edge with a genuine partial-coverage ring beyond it. Because the output is a clean single-colour mask rather than photographic pixels, **recolouring it later is nearly free** — a `fillStyle` plus `source-in` — rather than needing the tone-mapping hack Studio's own Auto Duotone (`_buildRecoloredStickerCanvas`) exists to work around precisely *because* it is stuck with original pixel values. **Two supporting additions**: a **crop** tool (drag a box on the preview, `box-shadow: 0 0 0 9999px` dimming everything outside it) — which matters most on a phone photo, where the page rarely fills the frame and whatever else is on the table is otherwise just another object to find — with every reported coordinate crop-relative and an oversized crop clamped rather than throwing; and a **"What was traced"** black-on-white mask preview, so a broken result can be *seen* rather than guessed at. **Sheet mode is byte-identical and still the default** — this is purely additive, because the existing path is right for a clean reference sheet and wrong only for a photographed page. **Verified 47/47** (`scan_mode_verify.mjs`, scratch-only, self-hosting Node server on a dynamic port + Playwright, driving the real UI). The fixture is a synthetic notebook photo built to carry all four hazards at once: paper shading 245→155 left-to-right with seeded per-pixel grain, a fabric-coloured strip standing in for the table, a 3.5%-opacity bleed-through line, and two drawings placed so that no global threshold can reach both. **The load-bearing section is B**, which tests the mode's own premise as a claim rather than asserting it: sweeping the sheet-mode threshold 30→70 over that fixture, no value yields two clean objects one per region, low values swallow the shaded half into a blob covering **88%** of the page, and raising the threshold never escapes it — at 60 and 70 the largest object is still **73%** and **57%**. **B3 was originally written wrong and the failure was mine, not the product's**: I predicted from per-channel arithmetic that a threshold of 70 would lose the ring, but `colorDist` is **Euclidean** (√3 ≈ 1.73× larger), so the ring's real distance is ≈110 and it survives comfortably. Diagnosed by dumping each sweep step's actual boxes rather than trusting the prediction — which also surfaced that at T=70 a 27×7 fragment of the bleed-through line crosses over and becomes its own "object", so pushing higher changes *what* is wrong, not *whether*. The assertion was replaced with the stronger claim the data actually supports. Elsewhere: **C** proves the redraw is real — with ink set to `(220,30,30)`, *every* visible pixel across every cutout is **exactly** that colour, none of the photo's greys survive anywhere, and the fresh AA is genuine (fully-opaque interior present, partial alpha present, more than two distinct alpha levels); **D** Ink Weight 2 lays down 3408 opaque pixels against 1278 at 0 without merging the drawings; **E** sensitivity 4 finds the bleed-through (11 components) and the default 18 does not (2); **F** crop is honoured with every coordinate crop-relative and an oversized rect clamped to `{x:400,y:100,w:200,h:300}`; **G** sheet mode still hands back the **actual source colours** `(200,50,30,255)`/`(30,94,200,255)`, still samples a background, and still runs by default; **H** the mask preview is a real PNG by signature read off the blob itself; **J** an impossible sensitivity returns nothing rather than throwing and still hands back a mask so you can see why, with zero page errors. **Disclosed rather than glossed**: it does **not** dewarp — a page shot at an angle or bowed near a spine comes out at that angle and that bow, and that is deliberately out of scope; Paper Radius is wrong in both directions if pushed (too small and thick strokes hollow out, since the middle of a fat stroke *is* its own local mean; too large and it degenerates back into the global threshold this mode exists to avoid); bleed-through versus faint pencil is a genuine judgement call on one knob, since they are the same kind of signal differing only in degree; the mode throws tone away on purpose, so anything shaded or coloured wants sheet mode instead; and **the fixture is synthetic** — the user's real notebook photo was pasted into chat, never written to disk, so there is no file to test against and whether *their* page comes out right is still their own eyes to judge. Hand-off to Studio is manual for now (download the PNGs, then Add Something → Photo); if it works on real pages, the follow-on question is whether this belongs as a Line Art mode inside Image Studio itself. `tools/sheet-extractor/README.md` restructured around the two modes throughout. This tool carries neither the build-info pin nor the cache-bust ritual — its own script tags have no `?v=` and it has no build-info reference — so this ships as a plain commit; confined to `tools/sheet-extractor/{index.html,README.md,css/style.css,js/extractor.js,js/app.js}`.

- Image Studio — Trim Picture Was Locked Behind Background Removal (root Studio only — a direct bug report, verbatim: **"ok while we wait the crop functionality of image studio seems to have broken can you check that."** Reproduced first rather than guessed at: a fresh `PictureStudio.open()` renders ✂️ Trim Picture with `disabled === true`, so a child who simply wants to crop a photo cannot, ever, without first tapping ✨ Remove Paper. **Root cause is a stale gate left behind by a shipped ship, not a broken crop.** `_refreshBgControls` carried `_cropTile.disabled = !_bgRemovedImg`, written back when background removal ran automatically on every `open()` — so a working buffer always existed by the time anyone reached for a tool. The later "Background Removal Is On-Demand, Never the Default" ship removed that auto-run without revisiting the gate, and since `_workingBuffer`/`_bgRemovedImg` were set **only** by `_onBgResult`, every pixel tool silently inherited a dependency on a removal the child never asked for. Trimming a photo has nothing to do with removing its paper. **The fix is a flag split plus lazy materialization, not merely a loosened gate.** `_bgRemovedImg` keeps meaning *"the canvas currently displayed and edited"* — but a new, narrower `_bgRemovalDone` answers *"did the worker actually run?"*, and that is what the Remove Paper tile, the Before/After compare wrap and the erase brush sub-panel key off, since none of the three mean anything without a genuine removal. Simply overloading `_bgRemovedImg` was considered and **rejected**: it would have made Remove Paper refuse to run after a plain trim, and un-hidden both the compare slider (where "before" and "after" would be the same picture) and the alpha-erase brush (with no removed alpha to erase). New `_ensureWorkingBuffer()` materializes a mutable buffer on demand via the existing `_bakeSourceForBg()`, mints the matching canvas, and — deliberately — **bakes rotation and flip exactly as `_startBgRemoval` already does**, resetting `_state.rotation`/`_state.flipH`, because `_screenToContent` (which converts a drag box into buffer pixels) has always assumed an un-rotated buffer and carries the comment saying so. Two alternatives were rejected here too: making `_screenToContent` rotation-aware (a screen-drawn box on a rotated picture is **not** axis-aligned in buffer space, so inverse-transforming its corners gives a wrong rectangle rather than a rotated one), and adding a doodle-remap-through-rotation subsystem (scope creep — the same drift is pre-existing on the removal path, so baking introduces no *new* class of bug; disclosed in the code comment rather than papered over). The bake is triggered from `_toggleActiveTool` on **entering** crop rather than on the first drag, so the picture never visibly changes mid-gesture. `_startCropDrag` and `_autoCrop` swap their `if(!_workingBuffer) return;` guards for `_ensureWorkingBuffer()`, so both Auto Crop and a hand-drawn box work from a cold open; `_finishCropDrag` now resolves coordinates against `_workingBuffer` (the space `_cropPixelBuffer` actually operates in — `_bgRemovedImg` is drawn *from* that buffer, so the dimensions match, but the buffer is the source of truth) with a null guard, and its clamp fallback was **simplified rather than extended**: the original re-called `_screenToContent` with identical arguments when the first call returned null, which could only ever return null again. Crop gates become `_cropTile.disabled = !_origImg` and the Keep This / Trash It pair `!(_cropRect && _workingBuffer)`, so the actions arm exactly when there is genuinely something to act on. **Verified 23/23, zero page errors**, via a new Playwright suite (`crop_fix_verify.mjs`, scratch-only) driving the real modal with real `page.mouse` drags across six sections: **A** — Trim is enabled on open with **no removal ever run**, and the compare slider and erase brush correctly stay hidden while its own sub-panel opens and Keep This / Trash It / Undo Trim all start disabled; **B** — a real drag arms both actions, Keep This crops, Undo Trim becomes available, and still no removal was triggered; **C** — Trash It arms Undo the same way, likewise with no removal; **D** — Undo Trim reverts and disables itself, Trim stays enabled, and ✨ Remove Paper afterwards still runs a **genuine** removal that wakes the removal-gated UI; **E** — the round trip works on a **rotated** picture end to end, which is the bake proving itself; **F** — zero uncaught page errors. **Three test-side fixes, all disclosed, none of them app bugs**: the four boot overlays (preload gate, Traveller Gateway's tap-to-begin, Creation Flow, Magic Card) are *removed* rather than class-hidden, because Playwright hit-tests real drags against them; two selectors of my own were wrong against source (`.picture-studio-ba-compare`, and `.picture-studio-brush-panel` — the child that `_refreshBgControls` toggles — rather than the `[data-tool="brush"]` wrapper the active-tool CSS shows); and two places had to tap `← Back` before reaching another tile, since Ship B's contextual collapse correctly hides every non-active tool's tile. **Full regression**: `bg_default_verify.mjs` 12/12 (the on-demand-removal ship's own suite — the one this fix is most at risk of undoing, confirming removal still never auto-runs), `image_studio_draw_verify.mjs` 26/26, `photo_via_studio_verify.mjs` 8/8, `fa_replace_everywhere_verify.mjs` 22/22, and both `goldenBuild.js` suites (World Builder v1 and v2) PASS unchanged. `renderer/slideRenderer.js` is untouched, so the Museum Gallery canonical hashes are not the gate for this ship. Cache-bust `?v=0356`→`?v=0357`. **One pre-existing quirk noted and deliberately left alone**: `_bgRemovedDataURL` is write-only (nulled at four sites, read nowhere). No Theme Contract/Engine V2 Scene Model/Builder change — `tools/world-builder/` and `tools/world-builder-v2/` are completely untouched; confined to `js/pictureStudio.js` and `index.html`.)

- Sheet Extractor — Ink Fill Works in Both Modes (`tools/sheet-extractor/` only — a standalone dev tool, so no Studio, Builder, Theme Contract, renderer, or publish surface is touched at all. The ask, in one line: **"use ink mode in both scan and sheet if possible"**. **The insight is that the single "mode" switch was conflating two genuinely independent things**, and once separated the answer was mostly *deletion of a coupling* rather than new capability: **detection** — how objects are FOUND — is either `buildMask` (one global Euclidean colour distance from a corner-sampled background: right for a clean reference sheet) or `buildScanMask` (local contrast against a per-pixel box-blur local mean: right for a photographed page where lighting falls off across it); **render** — how each object is DRAWN — is either `renderSheetObject` (copy the real source pixels, soften the outermost ring) or `renderInkObject` (throw the pixels away, redraw the traced shape as solid ink with fresh anti-aliasing). Scan mode had been shipped with both ends bolted together, so ink was reachable only on a photo. But ink is the right answer for **anything meant to be recoloured later** — a clean sheet of flat-colour shapes very much included — because a single-colour mask recolours with a `fillStyle` + `source-in`, while photographic pixels need the tone-mapping hack Studio's own Auto Duotone (`_buildRecoloredStickerCanvas`) exists precisely to work around. **`renderInkObject` turned out to already be fully mode-agnostic** — it reads only `labels`, `origMask`, `w`, `id`, the box, `inkWeight` and `ink`, every one of which both detection paths already populate identically in `rctx` — so ink-in-sheet-mode needed **zero new rendering code**: `extractSheet` gained an `inkFill` option (defaulting to `mode === 'scan'`, so every existing caller is byte-identical) and one line became `var od = inkFill ? renderInkObject(rctx) : renderSheetObject(rctx);`. The only arithmetic that had to follow was `minPad`, which is keyed on `inkFill` rather than on the mode, because Ink Weight dilates the traced shape in either mode and a percentage of a three-pixel-tall box is zero. **The UI is now two switches rather than one**, with the CSS visibility split to match: `data-mode` + `data-only` hide the *detection* fields (Color Threshold and Background belong to sheet; Ink Sensitivity and Paper Radius to scan) while a separate `data-ink` + `data-ink-only` pair hides the *render* fields (Ink Weight, Ink Colour) — deliberately two independent rules rather than one combined one, since an ink field is valid in either mode and so cannot hang off `data-mode` at all. `MODE_DEFAULTS` carries a per-mode `ink` value so the defaults keep the obvious pairing (Scan inks, Sheet doesn't) while either can be flipped, and `rememberModeState`/`applyModeState` carry it so flipping back and forth doesn't lose the choice. Ink Weight is disclosed in its own help text as applying *after* tracing, so it can never change what gets found. **A real product bug was found by the new suite and fixed at source**: the previously-unreachable **scan detection + ink OFF** combination crashed — `renderSheetObject` dereferences `bg[0..2]` for its soft-edge blend, and scan detection sets `bg = null` by design, because "there is no single background" is the entire point of a local-mean mask. Fixed with a null guard (`if (bg && isBoundary(...))`) rather than by inventing a fallback background: with nothing to measure a boundary pixel against, the honest answer is to keep that pixel's own source alpha and accept a hard cutout edge — a softening factor conjured from a `null` would be a guess wearing a number. Disclosed in the README rather than left to be discovered. **A second finding was deliberately NOT fixed, and is now documented instead**: a sheet cutout carries a thin fully-opaque halo of background, because `renderSheetObject` gates on the **dilated** `labels` while only the outermost ring is softened, so at `dilateRadius = 2` the inner ring is copied at full opacity. It is pre-existing, unrelated to this change, absent from ink fill (which reads the undilated `origMask`), and — since `computeTightBoxes` recomputes every box from the undilated mask — it never affects what is actually cropped. Changing it would alter every existing sheet cutout's edges in the default, working mode nobody asked about, so it is disclosed in the limitations rather than quietly changed. **Verified 32/32** (`ink_both_modes_verify.mjs`, scratch-only, self-hosting Node server on a dynamic port + Playwright, driving the real UI), across six sections: **A** — the two switches are genuinely independent (ink visible and flippable in sheet mode, mode fields still switching correctly, ink fields hidden entirely when ink is off); **B** — sheet + ink OFF is unchanged, handing back the fixture's own actual source colours `(200,30,30)` and `(30,94,200)`; **C** — sheet + ink ON genuinely redraws, with **every** fully-opaque pixel across **every** cutout exactly the chosen magenta and none of the source's reds or blues surviving anywhere; **D** — sheet + ink honours a manual background override, so the two axes compose rather than one silently overriding the other; **E** — scan + ink OFF (the crash) now yields real objects carrying the photographed page's own mid-grey pixels; **F** — the API is backward compatible, an `extractSheet` call with no `inkFill` at all still inking in scan and not in sheet. Every colour probe filters on `d[i+3] === 255`, because a partial-alpha pixel round-trips through premultiplied canvas storage and picks up ±2 per-channel rounding — the same reason `PngEncoder` keeps `<canvas>` out of the write path entirely. **One test-side bug, disclosed and not an app bug**: the spy installer kept the original `extractSheet` only in a closure-local `const`, so section F's bypass had nothing to call; fixed by also stashing it on `window`. `README.md` was restructured around the two axes throughout — the two mode sections became four (Finding objects: Sheet / Finding objects: Scan / Drawing each object: ink off / Drawing each object: ink on), Ink Weight and Ink Colour moved into their own "Ink fill only (either mode)" table, and the limitations gained the two disclosures above. **Full regression**: `scan_mode_verify.mjs` 47/47 and `ink_color_verify.mjs` 12/12, both PASS unchanged. This tool carries neither the build-info pin nor the root cache-bust ritual — it has its own, already bumped to `?v=0002` — so this ships as a plain commit; confined to `tools/sheet-extractor/{index.html,README.md,css/style.css,js/extractor.js,js/app.js}`.

- Magic Publish — The World Stages Per Object Too (root Studio only — a one-line directive: **"magic publish should stage world owned objects."** Artwork and Decorations had staged per object since the arrival ship — two pictures are two moments — but the World beat still arrived as one whole backdrop, so every Theme-authored layer on a page (the wall, the frame that hangs on it, a caption, a seal) snapped in together in a single frame. That reads as a slide template appearing, not as a place being built. `js/magicReveal.js`'s own `revealStages` doc comment even asserted the opposite of this directive in prose, so it was rewritten rather than left to contradict the code beneath it. **The World beat now enumerates its own arrivals and stages them exactly like the other two beats**: new `_worldLayers(slide)` reproduces `renderer/slideRenderer.js`'s own `_activeLayerPack` — same theme source, same scope filter against `slide.metadata.layout`, same order — and `_worldArrivals` turns it into the `{id,index}` list `_arrivalSteps` already splits into up to `MAX_ARRIVALS_PER_GROUP=4` steps; `_hasWorldFurniture` is now a thin wrapper over it, so beat detection and beat staging can never disagree about what the World has to bring. Layer pack array order IS paint order, so a full-bleed backdrop naturally arrives first and whatever hangs on it follows. **The one genuinely new decision: a partial World stage names its layers by INDEX into the scope-filtered pack, not by id.** Ids are optional on a Layer Pack entry, and — the deciding reason — an id-based marker would force `js/magicReveal.js` and `renderer/slideRenderer.js` to agree on a keying scheme, which is exactly the drift both files' own comments already warn against; an index into the array `_activeLayerPack` itself returns needs no agreement at all beyond the array, which is a single line in each file. That contract only holds if both files resolve the SAME pack, so the resolution chain was traced end to end rather than assumed: `_worldLayers` tries `ThemeEngine.getActiveArtworkTheme()` then `getActiveTheme()`; `_activeLayerPack` goes through `_layoutTheme(s)` → `s.layoutTheme` → `_artworkTheme(s)` → `ThemeEngine.getActiveTheme()`, where `_artworkTheme(s)` returns `s.artworkTheme` directly when set and `buildPayload` sets that from `ThemeEngine.getActiveArtworkTheme()` — the same object, in the same order — and `buildPayload` carries `metadata` verbatim, so `layoutId` matches too. **Marker discipline is unchanged from M2**: a stage still sets `_magicHideLayerPack` (whole beat hidden) or, new, `_magicLayerPackShown` (a list of indices) on its own CLONE, and `_activeLayerPack` honours both — never a filtered theme, because the resolved theme is shared `ThemeEngine` module state a Magic stage must never reach into. `_stageSlide`'s existing `setFor(group)` tri-state (empty Set = hide all, `null` = show all, populated = partial) drove the World with no new mechanism. An ordinary payload carries neither marker, so both resolve false/null and every existing render is byte-identical. **One real consequence had to be handled rather than inherited: a full-bleed layer's bbox IS the page**, so the `'arrival'` transition would scale and lift the entire frame — the camera moving, not an object arriving. `docs/MAGIC_PUBLISH_ROADMAP.md`'s own animation table already says a background *washes in*, so `js/storyDestinations.js` gained `_magicRectIsFullBleed` and `_magicTransition` routes such a frame to `'wash'` with its `arrivalRect` deliberately dropped (handing `paintWash` a rect it ignores would only invite a later reader to think it mattered). The fullness test measures against the page's own MAPPED extents rather than the canvas, because a 4:5 page inside a 9:16 frame is letterboxed — a genuinely full-bleed layer fills the page and leaves the bars alone, and comparing it to the canvas would answer "no" for exactly the case it exists to find. `_magicArrivalRect` needed no change at all (it already matches `els[i].id === arrivalId` generically), and `js/publishStudio.js`, `js/magicStrip.js` and `js/reelComposer.js` were not touched. **Verified 35/35, zero page errors**, via a new Playwright suite (`magic_world_stage_verify.mjs`, scratch-only, self-hosting on a dynamic port) against a fixture theme with one Place and a 4-entry Layer Pack — a full-bleed green wash, a magenta badge bottom-left, a cyan seal bottom-right, and a deliberately `visible:false` fourth — across six sections: **A** enumeration order and indices with the invisible layer skipped and an ordinary payload carrying both markers as false/null; **B** three World frames in paint order, blank leading, World before Artwork, and a bare World producing no beat at all; **C** the marker progression `[0]` → `[0,1]` → `[0,1,2]` with the caller's own slide untouched and each stage its own object; **D** the decisive part — a real `SlideRenderer.init`+`render` per stage, pixel-sampling the wash, badge and seal positions (all deliberately clear of the Place) at 18/channel tolerance, so the renderer is proven to honour the index list rather than merely to receive it; **E** the full-bleed frame tagged `'wash'` with no rect while badge and seal tag `'arrival'` with rects, and no wash frame carrying a stray one; **F** zero page errors. **Two test-side items, both disclosed and neither an app bug**: the suite's own "bare World" fixture first tried `slide.layoutTheme = {layerPack:[]}`, which is inert — grepping confirmed that field is written only by `js/creationFlow.js`'s Screen 2 preview carousel onto a *payload* and read only by `_layoutTheme`, and `buildPayload` never carries it off a slide — so the case is now exercised by stubbing the two `ThemeEngine` accessors `_worldLayers` actually calls, with try/finally restore, which is sound because `js/themeEngine.js`'s top-level `const` and its `window.ThemeEngine` are the same object and property mutation is visible through both; and `magic_m4_verify.mjs`'s G4a required an object frame to be `'rise'` or `'arrival'`, which a full-bleed World frame now correctly is neither — the intended, disclosed consequence of this ship rather than a regression, so the assertion was **widened, not weakened**, keeping both real invariants (a word frame only ever draws; no frame past the first turns a page). **Because `renderer/slideRenderer.js` is touched, the Museum Gallery canonical hashes ARE the gate for this ship and all three are byte-identical**: showcase `1f54eb660f7beb53`, portrait `843e68f2cffb3c2e`, quote `969a67e5c984647b`. **Full regression**: `magic_m1` 32/32, `m2` 33/33, `m3` 32/32, `m4` 42/42, `m5` 43/43, `m6` 35/35, `m7` 38/38, `m8` 47/47, `m9` 21/21, `magic_arrival` 48/48, `reel_verify` 15/15, `reel_backdrop_verify` 10/10, `reel_pageturn_verify` 12/12, and both `goldenBuild.js` suites (World Builder v1 and v2) PASS unchanged. Cache-bust `?v=0357`→`?v=0358`. No Theme Contract/Engine V2 Scene Model/Builder change — `tools/world-builder/` and `tools/world-builder-v2/` are completely untouched; confined to `js/magicReveal.js`, `renderer/slideRenderer.js`, `js/storyDestinations.js`, and `index.html`.)

- Sheet Extractor — Per-Asset Editing Tools on Every Result Tile (`tools/sheet-extractor/` only — a standalone dev tool, so no Studio, Builder, Theme Contract, renderer, or publish surface is touched at all. The ask, verbatim: **"hey i like this sheet extractor, can we add tools to each asset tile. i would need , crop, eraser, color outline, shape draw, color fill, rotate, flip."** Every result card gains an **✏️ Edit** button opening that one cutout in its own modal with all seven. **The architectural decision that shaped everything else: an edit rewrites `item.pixelBuffer` and re-encodes — it deliberately does NOT re-run extraction.** Extraction is *global* (one background sample, one threshold, one min-area filter for the whole sheet), while fixing one asset is *local*; re-running it would re-derive every other object from a global setting the user is not currently arguing with, and would make a per-tile fix able to change tiles nobody touched. `applyCompression` in `js/app.js` already does exactly this shape of work (edit the buffer, re-encode, refresh the card), so the pattern was extended rather than invented. **New `js/tileEditor.js` exports `window.TileEditor` with all seven operations as PURE functions** — each takes a pixel buffer and returns a new one, never mutating its input — exported individually alongside `open`/`close` specifically so each can be exercised on its own, without a browser or a modal, which is what made 22 of the 38 assertions possible as direct calls. `open(item, onApply)` calls `onApply(buf)` with the edited buffer, or `null` when nothing actually changed, and does not call it at all on cancel. Notable op behaviours, all verified rather than assumed: `crop` **clamps** an out-of-bounds rect rather than rejecting it; `outline` **grows the buffer by `width` on every side**, since an outline drawn on a tight cutout would otherwise have nowhere to go, and stamps only from boundary pixels so an interior hole is not filled in; `drawShape` deliberately never fills a `line`; `rotate90` swaps dimensions on odd turns; `bucketFill` treats anything under alpha 8 as "the same transparent region", so filling the empty space around a shape works as expected. Undo is 20 steps. **The subtle bug this shape avoids, and why `applyItemEdit` encodes through `PngEncoder` rather than leaning on the compressor**: `PngCompressor.compress()` short-circuits at the lossless level — `if (!level.maxColors) return { blob: originalBlob, ... }` — and hands back the ORIGINAL blob untouched. An edit that only updated `pixelBuffer` would therefore appear correctly at every compression level *except the default one*, since levels above 0 quantize from `pixelBuffer` and would pick it up. A bug that hides itself at exactly one setting, and the one setting most people never move. Encoding the edited buffer explicitly also keeps the picture off a `<canvas>` on its way to bytes, which is this tool's own founding discipline (canvas export silently corrupts RGB at partial alpha — measured: `(42,157,143,1)` came back `(0,255,255,1)`). There is a dedicated regression check for exactly this, B9. **Verified 38/38** (`tile_editor_verify.mjs`, scratch-only, self-hosting Node server on a dynamic port + Playwright): section **A** is 22 pure-op assertions covering crop clamping and non-mutation, erase coverage, outline growth and boundary-only stamping, shape fill/stroke and the line exception, bucket fill across transparent regions, rotate dimension swap in both directions, and flip on both axes; section **B** is a 15-step real-UI round trip — open the editor from a real card, rotate, save, and then confirm the card reports its new dimensions, the compression level is still the default lossless one, **the downloadable bytes genuinely changed at that level** (B9, the check that would have caught the `PngCompressor` short-circuit), a fresh object URL was minted, the thumbnail points at the new bytes, the encoded PNG itself carries the rotated size, the *other* card is untouched, Cancel discards an edit entirely, and saving with no changes is a no-op; section **C** is zero page errors. **Two bugs found during verification were both in the TEST, not the app, and are disclosed in the README rather than quietly fixed**: an erase assertion sampled a point the brush genuinely reaches — the brush measures from pixel *centres* (`dx = x + 0.5 - cx`) with coverage `radius + 0.5 - d`, so radius 2 reaches 2.5px, while the fixture's 4×4 square has corners only 2.121px from its own middle (the predicted alpha of 158 matched the observed value exactly, confirming the app was right and the premise was mine and wrong); and a wait hung for 30s because Playwright's `waitForSelector` defaults to `state:'visible'`, which an element carrying `hidden` can never become — the Playwright log itself (`64 × locator resolved to hidden <div hidden class="se-te-overlay">`) proved the app was correct, fixed with a `waitForFunction` on the property instead. **Full regression**: the tool's three existing suites all PASS unchanged — `scan_mode_verify.mjs` 47/47, `ink_both_modes_verify.mjs` 32/32, `ink_color_verify.mjs` 12/12. `README.md` gained a full `## Editing an individual asset` section (a per-tool table, `### Two things this deliberately does *not* do`, and `### A subtle bug this shape avoids, worth knowing about`), a `js/tileEditor.js` entry in `## Files`, and a `### The per-asset editor` verification subsection recording all 38 assertions and the erase arithmetic. This tool carries neither the build-info pin nor the root cache-bust ritual — it has its own, bumped to `?v=0003` across all 7 versioned tags — so this ships as a plain commit; confined to `tools/sheet-extractor/{index.html,README.md,css/style.css,js/app.js}` and the new `js/tileEditor.js`.)

- Image Studio — Sheet Extractor Inside It (root Studio only — the standalone `tools/sheet-extractor/` app is completely unchanged. The ask was to bring the sheet extractor's own capability into Image Studio, so a child never has to leave Studio, download PNGs and re-upload them just to pull the objects out of a photographed page. Three new tools join the Edit view: **✂️ Cut Out Objects** (`extract`), **🖊 Outline** (`outline`) and **🪣 Colour Fill** (`fill`). **The governing decision is reuse, not reimplementation**: `index.html` now loads `tools/sheet-extractor/js/extractor.js` and `js/tileEditor.js` directly, so Image Studio calls the very same `extractSheet` and `TileEditor` those tools' own suites (47 + 32 + 12 + 38 assertions) already cover — not one line of detection, tracing, ink-fill, outline or bucket-fill logic was copied into `js/pictureStudio.js`. Cut Out Objects runs `extractSheet` on the current picture and renders a grid of everything it found: tapping one cutout replaces the picture with it, and **Use All** sends every cutout back to the caller at once. Both detection modes are offered, with the **render** axis (ink fill on/off) kept independent of the **detection** axis exactly as the standalone tool separates them — sheet detection with ink off keeps the photo's own pixels, scan detection with ink on redraws the traced shape as solid colour. **The one new contract, and it is deliberately optional**: `PictureStudio.open(src, opts)` gains `opts.onApplyMany(dataUrls)`; only `js/contextPanel.js`'s Add Something → Photo call site opts in, and the other ten `open()` call sites pass just `onApply` and are completely unaffected. Use All reads each cutout from **its own `PngEncoder` blob via `FileReader`** rather than re-drawing it through a `<canvas>`, because canvas export corrupts RGB at partial alpha (premultiplied backing store) — which is the same reason the standalone tool keeps `<canvas>` out of its write path at all, measured there as `(42,157,143,1)` coming back `(0,255,255,1)`. **One test bug, fixed properly and never weakened**: the suite's `seen()` helper checked `classList.contains('hidden')` on the **input**, but the app toggles `hidden` on the row **wrapper**, so `seen()` always returned `true` and four B assertions were passing for the wrong reason. Rewritten to `el.offsetParent !== null` — real rendered visibility, which additionally proves the `.picture-studio-subpanel-row.hidden{display:none}` rule genuinely exists (`css/style.css:4908`); that matters because this codebase has **no global `.hidden` utility**, only component-scoped rules, and has shipped a bug of exactly that class before (`.text-empty`, a `hidden` toggle with no matching rule). B: 5/9 → **9/9**. **Four genuine app bugs, every one found by instrumenting or reading the real code path rather than guessing.** **(1)** `_runExtract` read `(res && res.objects)` while `extractSheet` resolves `{items:[…]}`, so the grid was always empty and C2 timed out. **(2)** `PngEncoder` **was never loaded in Studio at all**, even though `extractor.js` calls it at two sites — after fixing (1) the extraction still failed, and a six-probe diagnostic with `page.on('pageerror')` surfaced `ReferenceError: PngEncoder is not defined`, which `_runExtract`'s own `.catch` had been quietly converting into the friendly "Couldn't find anything this time."; one script tag fixed it, C: 1/7 → **7/7**. This is the classic-script failure mode: a missing `<script>` tag is a silent `ReferenceError` at call time, never a load-time failure. **(3)** `_hide()` left `_workingBuffer` stale — `_workingBuffer` and `_bgRemovedImg` are a matched pair (`_ensureWorkingBuffer` mints them together, `_syncCanvasFromBuffer` needs both) and the other two reset sites (`_undoBgRemoval`, "Yes, start over") correctly null the pair, but `_hide()` nulled only `_bgRemovedImg`, so on a **re-open** `_ensureWorkingBuffer` early-returned on the stale buffer and never re-minted the canvas: **every** pixel tool (extract, crop, outline, fill, erase) silently operated on the *previous* picture's pixels and painted nothing. Isolated by comparing the three reset sites and noticing `_hide()` was the sole outlier on that pair; far broader than extract, and the reason D2 timed out. Fixed by nulling the pair plus the five companion fields describing the picture that just went away, so a re-open can never offer an Undo Trim that would restore a completely different picture. **(4)** `_applyAllExtracted` read `_onApplyMany` **after** `_hide()` had already nulled it, so Use All threw "not a function" straight into a silent `catch` and dropped every cutout on the floor — `_hide()` nulls `_onApplyMany` but not `_onApply`, which is precisely why the single-picture path never hit this; fixed by capturing the callback before teardown. Both (3) and (4) were masked by swallowed-exception sites that turned hard errors into friendly no-ops. **Verified 46/46, zero failures**, across sections A–H (`image_studio_extract_verify.mjs`, scratch-only, self-hosting Node server on a dynamic port + Playwright): **A** engines reachable and all three tiles present; **B** both detection modes with their own field sets — the two sensitivity sliders carry the *identical* label, so they are told apart by range (sheet 6–90, scan 4–60), never by label text; **C** a real extraction finding both fixture objects and rendering two tiles; **D** tapping a tile replaces the picture and Use All returns both cutouts through `onApplyMany`; **E** outline grows the shape with working undo; **F** bucket fill applied by tapping the canvas (no apply button); **G** contextual tile collapse and the back button; **H** zero page errors. **Full regression**: both `goldenBuild.js` suites (World Builder v1 and v2) PASS, `bg_default_verify.mjs` 12/12, `image_studio_draw_verify.mjs` 26/26, `crop_fix_verify.mjs` 23/23, `photo_via_studio_verify.mjs` 8/8, `fa_replace_everywhere_verify.mjs` 22/22. `renderer/slideRenderer.js` is untouched, so the Museum Gallery canonical hashes are not the gate for this ship. Cache-bust `?v=0358`→`?v=0359` across all 59 tags. No Theme Contract/Engine V2 Scene Model/Builder change — `tools/world-builder/` and `tools/world-builder-v2/` are completely untouched; confined to `js/pictureStudio.js`, `js/contextPanel.js`, `css/style.css` and `index.html`.)

- A Page Carrying Voice Narration Says So On Its Own Card (root Studio only — a one-line ask: **"if a slide has a voice narration , i want some hint that its there"**. Voice MVP Ship 1 stored per-page narration at `slide.metadata.narration = {ref, durationMs}`, and the Voice panel already said *"This page has your voice on it (M:SS)"* **inside** the panel — so the gap was purely discoverability from outside it: to tell which pages carried a clip you had to open Personalize → Add Something → 🎤 Voice on each page in turn. Both page strips now show a small 🔊 badge on any page whose `narration.ref` is set, driven by one shared `_hasNarration(s)` predicate in `js/app.js` so `window.renderList` (the sidebar `#slideList .thumb` cards) and `window.renderTimeline` (`#timelineList .timeline-thumb` cards) can never disagree about which pages have one. **Three placements were rejected before writing any code.** The **canvas** is out because Creator Governing Rule #5 (Publish Fidelity) means whatever the centre pane shows is exactly what Publish produces, so a badge drawn there would land in the published book, reel and strip. **Baking into `s.thumbnail`** is out because narration is not a rendered property of the page — DOM chrome keeps thumbnails pure renders and avoids regenerating them. **An Object Strip entry** is out because narration is page-level, not an object: the strip's two synthetic entries (Background, Artwork Place) each map to a real selection, and narration has none. **`pointer-events:none` on the badge is load-bearing rather than tidy** — the sidebar `.thumb` is itself both the click target (`d.onclick = () => showSlide(i)`) and the HTML5 drag handle wired by `_wireSlideListDnD`, so a badge that could receive a pointer would eat both. `.timeline-thumb` gained `position:relative` deliberately: it has `overflow:hidden` and no positioned children of its own, so establishing a containing block changes nothing else, and the badge is inset (`right:3px, bottom:3px`) so nothing clips. **Refresh**: `js/contextPanel.js`'s `_setNarration`/`_removeNarration` call a shared `_refreshPageStrips()`, which invokes `window.renderList()`/`window.renderTimeline()` through the `try{ if(typeof …==='function') }catch(e){}` guard this codebase already uses at six other cross-module call sites (`js/pageOps.js`, `js/projectManager.js`, `js/themeEngine.js`, `js/creationFlow.js` ×2, and inside `contextPanel` itself). `host.markDirty()` only flags the project dirty — it does not re-render — and `PageRuntime.notify()` would be **wrong** here, because it calls `ContextPanel.refresh()` and would rebuild the Voice panel out from under the flow the child is in. **Two test-side fixes, both disclosed, neither an app bug, and no assertion weakened** — the app code was correct throughout; both failures were false premises in my own assertions. (1) B3b/B5b failed with the timeline badge present in the DOM but `offsetParent === null` and 0×0; grepping found `<div class='timeline' hidden>` at `index.html:288` and nothing in `js/` that ever un-hides it, so the test removed the attribute before measuring — and that was insufficient. (2) The same two still failed. Rather than guess, a throwaway diagnostic walked the ancestor chain and reported `.timeline` with `hidden:false` but `display:"none"` — CSS was hiding it too: `css/style.css:1280` is `.timeline{ display:none !important; }`, sitting immediately above the strip's own retained-but-unreachable styling at 1281. An author-stylesheet `!important` can only be beaten by an **inline** `!important`, so both checks now use `wrap.style.setProperty('display','block','important')` and restore afterward; the retirement check was **strengthened, not dropped**, asserting both halves (`hasAttribute('hidden') && computed display === 'none'`). **A finding worth recording: the timeline strip is retired-but-maintained** — hidden twice over with no revival path anywhere in `js/`, yet `renderTimeline()` still runs and still builds its cards, which is why the badge is present in the DOM there at all. Both strips were badged anyway, so whichever one a future layout revives already carries the hint. **Verified 21/21, zero page errors**, via `voice_badge_verify.mjs` (scratch-only) across eight sections: **B1** no badge before narration in either strip and the page genuinely carrying none; **B2** both badges appearing after a real WAV import through the native filechooser with **no manual `renderList()`/`renderTimeline()` call from the test**, which is what proves `_refreshPageStrips()` is genuinely wired in rather than the test doing the work; **B3** rendered visibility, `pointer-events`, absolute positioning, glyph and title, plus the retirement finding; **B4** monkeypatching `window.showSlide` and clicking the badged thumb still yielding `showSlide(0)`; **B5** the timeline badge sitting inside its own `overflow:hidden` thumb with real size; **B6** a second page via the real `#addPageBtn` with only page 1 badged in both strips; **B7** Remove Voice clearing both badges with no manual re-render; **B8** zero page errors. **Full regression**: `voice_verify.mjs` 16/16, `voice_note_verify.mjs` 22/22, `voice_place_verify.mjs` 16/16, `voice_icon_verify.mjs` 20/20, and both `goldenBuild.js` suites (World Builder v1 and v2) PASS unchanged. `renderer/slideRenderer.js` is untouched, so the Museum Gallery canonical hashes are not the gate for this ship. Cache-bust `?v=0359`→`?v=0360` across all 59 tags. No Theme Contract/Engine V2 Scene Model/Builder change — `tools/world-builder/` and `tools/world-builder-v2/` are completely untouched; confined to `js/app.js`, `js/contextPanel.js`, `css/style.css` and `index.html`.)

- Image Studio — Mark Out Where To Look, Compose One Picture From What You Find, and a Grid You Can Actually Read (root Studio only — three asks in one message, delivered as one change because all three share the same extraction pass and the same results grid: **"1. for finding objects can i also have a way to mark out area from where i want object extraction. this will reduce the number of stray objects. 2. I should be able to compose a new image from the objects. 3. the view showing objects is not easy to traverse."** **Ask 1 — the search area — needed no extractor change at all.** `extractSheet(imgSrc, opts)` has always accepted `opts.crop = {x,y,w,h}` in **source pixels** (`tools/sheet-extractor/js/extractor.js:414`, clamped to bounds at 443-446, echoed back at 534), so the work was a marker UI and one option passed through. The crop-drag machinery is already tool-agnostic — `_startCropDrag(clientX,clientY)` and `_screenToContent(clientX,clientY,imgW,imgH)` never read `_activeTool` — so both are reused unchanged and mousedown simply routes to them while Cut Out Objects is active. **`_extractArea` is deliberately a separate field from `_cropRect`**: `_refreshBgControls` arms the destructive Keep This / Trash It pair off `_cropRect`, so marking out where to *look* must never arm a control that *trims*; `_finishCropDrag` was rewritten around a `forExtract`/`commit` split so one gesture can land in either place, and A9 asserts the trim pair stayed disabled through the whole marking flow. No coordinate translation was needed downstream, because `_useExtracted` consumes `item.pixelBuffer` and `_applyAllExtracted` consumes `item.blob` — neither reads a source-relative box. **Ask 2 — compose.** Every result card carries a tick; picking two or more reveals **Make One Picture**, which shelf-packs the picked cutouts into a single new picture and replaces the one on screen. The compositor works by hand in a raw `Uint8ClampedArray` and **never through a `<canvas>`**, because canvas backing stores are premultiplied and round-tripping a cutout at partial alpha corrupts its RGB — the same reason `_applyAllExtracted` already reads each cutout from its own `PngEncoder` blob via `FileReader`. **Ask 3 — the grid.** `_renderExtractGrid` was a flat wall of unlabelled `<img>` tiles with no ordering aid and no size readout. Each result is now a card carrying its number, its pixel size and a pick tick, on a wider grid (`minmax` 56→84px, gap 6→8px, `max-height` 180→260px). The tick calls `stopPropagation` so unticking can never double as "use this one" (B6 proves it), and B9 confirms tapping the tile image itself still replaces the picture exactly as before. **One deletion**: `_lastMouseClientX()` was orphaned by the `_finishCropDrag` rewrite — verified via `grep -rn` (one hit, the definition itself) and removed, per this codebase's own "if unused, delete completely" convention. **Four test-side fixes, all disclosed, none an app bug, and every one strengthened rather than weakened.** **(1)** A3 asserted `.picture-studio-crop-box` existed *before* any drag, but `_ensureCropBox()` builds it lazily inside `_startCropDrag` and so cannot exist yet; relocated after the drag and grown from one condition to three (`exists && shown && width > 10`), which is a stronger claim — it proves marking an area genuinely goes through the same crop-drag machinery. **(2)** C8 clicked the Result view's `😊 Looks Great`, but `_composeExtracted` calls `_toggleActiveTool(null)` and never `_setView`, so the modal is still in the **Edit** view — the correct target is the footer's own `.picture-studio-save-btn`. **(3)** C8 and D4 both expected a bare data-URL **string**; the long-established contract for **both** `onApply` and `onApplyMany` is `{dataURL, width, height, imageView}` (`_bake` line 3208; `_applyAllExtracted` line 1874), so both now assert the whole shape. **(4)** D4 additionally read `m.dataUrl` (lowercase `rl`) where the real field is `m.dataURL`. **One flake investigated rather than papered over**: `image_studio_draw_verify.mjs` timed out once on `page.click('.picture-studio-cta-secondary')`, and a `git stash` A/B showed the baseline passing — which looked like a real regression. Rather than accept that, a dedicated in-page diagnostic probed all four Playwright actionability conditions **with the changes applied**: the button exists, is visible (`offsetParent !== null`), is enabled (`disabled === false`), has real geometry (180×44 at 702,746), is genuinely the top hit-target at its own centre (`document.elementFromPoint` returns the button itself), and is stable (byte-identical rects across two consecutive animation frames). The suite then passed **26/26 twice**. Transient sandbox CPU-load flakiness; no code changed and no assertion weakened. **Verified 35/35, zero page errors**, via `image_studio_extract_v2_verify.mjs` (scratch-only, self-hosting Node server on a dynamic port + Playwright) across five sections: **A** (12) the search area, where **A7 is decisive** — with red marked out, exactly one object was found and blue was never looked at — plus A10/A11 confirming reset restores whole-picture search and A12 that leaving the tool clears the area; **B** (9) the grid, its card structure, numbering, size readout, pick toggle and the two proofs above; **C** (8) compose — the button appears only at two or more picked and withdraws at one, both colours appear in the composed canvas, the picture genuinely changed, the tool closed itself, the grid cleared, and the result applies back in the usual payload shape; **D** (5) the existing contracts — `Use All` is still exactly one button, `Make One Picture` cannot be mistaken for it, `window.__many` is an array of 2 in the usual shape, and the single-picture callback was not also fired; **E** (1) zero page errors. The suite cannot reach closure-private `_stageRect`/`_state`/`_canvas` to drag a box, so `screenBoxOf()` scans the **rendered canvas** for a target colour's bounding box and converts through the element's own `getBoundingClientRect()` — a truer test anyway, since it drags where a child would actually see the thing. **Full regression, all eight suites green**: `image_studio_extract_verify.mjs` **46/46** (the most at-risk, since this ship rewrites both `_renderExtractGrid` and `_finishCropDrag`), `bg_default_verify.mjs` 12/12, `image_studio_draw_verify.mjs` 26/26 (twice), `crop_fix_verify.mjs` 23/23, `photo_via_studio_verify.mjs` 8/8, `fa_replace_everywhere_verify.mjs` 22/22, and both `goldenBuild.js` suites (World Builder v1 and v2) PASS. `renderer/slideRenderer.js` is untouched, so the Museum Gallery canonical hashes are not the gate for this ship. - Image Studio — Mark Out Several Areas, in Any Shape, and Start With Nothing Picked (root Studio only — two asks shipped as one change because they live in the same tool: **"u can go with 1 but the area marker should be rectangle, circle as well as free hand draw"** (multiple search areas for Cut Out Objects, with three marker shapes) and **"issue with make one picture. 1. all tiles are selected by default"** (extraction results must start with ZERO tiles picked). Ask B — the compose side panel — is deliberately its own next commit, per the owner's own sequencing: "Finish Ask A first, get the file running and green, ship it. Then do Ask B as its own commit." **The settled design, and the alternative it rejected**: the shared `tools/sheet-extractor/js/extractor.js` is NOT modified — `extractSheet` only understands a rectangular `opts.crop`, so a circle or freehand shape runs as a pass cropped to the shape's own BOUNDING BOX (real pixels, so the extractor's corner-sampled background estimation still samples genuine paper) and objects whose CENTRE falls outside the shape are dropped afterwards via a new `_pointInArea` (bbox reject first; circle as the normalized-ellipse test `dx*dx+dy*dy<=1`, which is per-axis affine-invariant so screen-space drag calibration preserves computed margins; freehand as ray-casting over ≥3 clamped points; rect returns true — a no-op filter, so the already-shipped single-rect behaviour is byte-identical). Pre-masking the source to the shape before extraction was REJECTED: the corner-sampled background would then be fabricated mask pixels rather than the photo's own paper. **Several areas at once**: `_extractArea` became `_extractAreas[]` (`[]` = whole picture, hint reads "Looking inside your N marked areas only."), each `{kind:'rect'|'circle'|'free', bbox, points?}` in working-buffer pixels; drags under 4px are ignored; out-of-bounds freehand points are clamped. `_runExtractPasses` runs one sequential `extractSheet` pass per area (per-area `.catch`, so one bad area never kills the rest), maps every result back into source space, and de-dupes overlapping areas' finds by source-space centre/size within 4px — revoking dropped duplicates' object URLs rather than leaking them. A three-button shape picker (▭ Box / ◯ Circle / ✎ Draw) sits in the tool's sub-panel, and a lazily-created SVG overlay (`.picture-studio-area-svg`, pointer-events:none, on the stage) draws every registered marker plus the in-flight drag as a dashed draft. `_areaShape` deliberately survives `_hide()` — the shape you like is a preference, not per-picture state — while `_extractAreas`/`_areaDrag` are correctly torn down. **Ask C is two lines with real consequences**: `_extractPicked` initializes to an EMPTY Set after every extraction (was: everything picked), the compose button stays hidden until 2+ are genuinely picked (`🧩 Make One Picture (N)`), and Use All shows only at 2+ results (`✓ Use All N`). **A real app bug found by the fresh suite, not by inspection**: `_runExtractPasses` read `it.box` with `width`/`height` fields — neither exists; the extractor's real fields are `bboxOriginal` with `w`/`h` (`extractor.js:513`). Rect areas MASKED it (their filter is a no-op, so undefined geometry was never consulted) while circle areas dropped everything and de-dup degenerated to identical centres — the exact class of silent classic-script failure this codebase keeps finding behind friendly `.catch`es. **Verification was rebuilt fresh, disclosed rather than glossed**: every prior scratchpad Playwright suite was lost with the old container (scratch-only, never committed — the only committed suites are the two `goldenBuild.js`), so a NEW 60-assertion suite (`image_studio_areas_verify.mjs`, scratch-only, self-hosting on a dynamic port, boot overlays removed, `page.on('pageerror')` throughout) covers sections A–H: A rect-restricted search (A8 decisive — with red marked out, exactly 1 object found; A10 proves Ask C's zero-picked default; A13 whole-picture still finds all 3), B circle & freehand centre-filtering, C multiple areas/merge/de-dupe/tiny-drag rejection (C6 decisive — overlapping areas still yield 2 tiles, not 4), D picking/compose gating/Use All contracts (all 3 cutouts via `onApplyMany` in the `{dataURL,width,height,imageView}` shape, single-picture `onApply` NOT also fired), E compose end to end, F teardown/re-open, G the Trim crop drag unaffected (Keep This genuinely crops — red kept, blue gone — proving the forExtract/commit split still routes correctly), H zero page errors — **60/60**. **Four test-side items, all disclosed, every one STRENGTHENED rather than weakened**: (1) `clickShapeBtn` matched internal kind names when the rendered labels are Box/Circle/Draw — fixed with the mapping; (2) Section C inherited `_areaShape:'free'` from Section B (the deliberate persistence above), fixed with an explicit re-select plus its own C0a check; (3) D8 asserted the modal was REMOVED from the DOM after Use All, but `_hide()` (pictureStudio.js:3642) only ever class-hides it — rewritten to assert the modal exists AND carries `hidden`, which verifies the real teardown contract instead of an impossible one; (4) **the old B5 was a false positive**: it "passed" 0 tiles on the main fixture only because the then-unfixed `it.box` bug dropped everything — once fixed, the same drag legitimately found 1 tile (the circle genuinely contained green's centre). Replaced with a dedicated FIXTURE_B5 rect-vs-circle differential — the SAME bbox dragged twice, once as rect (keeps both squares) and once as circle (drops the corner square at normalized ellipse distance ≈1.13) — growing one assertion into five (B5a–B5d + B5 decisive), a strictly stronger claim that the ellipse test is genuinely live. **Full regression**: both `goldenBuild.js` suites (World Builder v1 and v2) PASS unchanged. `renderer/slideRenderer.js` is untouched, so the Museum Gallery canonical hashes are not the gate for this ship. - Image Studio — A Compose Side Panel, So the Edit Underneath Survives (root Studio only — the deliberately-deferred "Ask B" from the previous ship, quoted verbatim: **"to draw a composite image open a side panel. this way the orignal edit is not lost."** That ship's **Make One Picture** shelf-packed the ticked cutouts and immediately overwrote the picture on screen — one shot, no arranging, and whatever was being edited underneath it gone. Now Make One Picture opens a new **`js/composePanel.js`** (`window.ComposePanel`) as a flex sibling of the stage, where each cutout can be moved, resized and bucket-filled, and the destructive apply runs only from that panel's own **Use This Picture** button. **Shipped in five commits, one per stage, each syntax-checked before the next**: skeleton (`c0ab42c`) → wiring (`55198ad`) → paint + drag (`0808573`) → scale, fill and the bake (`0a79e3d`) → a real bug the suite caught (`5b345a0`). **Dependencies are handed over, never reached for**: `configure({mount, tileEditor, onUsePicture})` at boot, mirroring the `contextPanel`/`objectStrip` host-binding convention, so `composePanel.js` never touches `pictureStudio.js`'s closure. `PngEncoder` is a **bare global** in this codebase (never `window.PngEncoder` — see the sheet extractor's own call sites), so its `typeof` guard matters: a missing script tag is a silent `ReferenceError` at call time, a repeat failure mode here. It was **dropped again at Stage 6** once it turned out to be configured, stored and never read — `_applyComposedPicture` takes the raw buffer straight into `_swapWorkingBuffer`, so no PNG is ever encoded; the header and `configure()` comments that claimed otherwise were corrected rather than left to mislead the next reader. **Painting** keys a per-tile offscreen canvas cache on the pixel-buffer **object** rather than an index, which is what lets a drag redraw every frame without re-uploading anything; the cache is dropped in both `open()` and `close()`, since a stale entry could never be mis-read (the keys are distinct identities) but every one of those canvases is real memory nobody can reach again. Hit testing walks tiles topmost-first and is **alpha-aware** — after the bbox reject it reads the source pixel's own alpha byte, so tapping the hole in a ring falls through to whatever is behind it instead of grabbing the ring's box. Pointer coordinates convert through `getBoundingClientRect` because the canvas lays out at `width:100%;height:auto`. **Scale is about the tile's own TOP-LEFT** — the corner `_tileRect()` measures from and `_surfaceSize()` grows around — so a growing tile pushes the surface out and x/y stay non-negative with no extra clamping. **Fill was written but unreachable**: `_fillTile` read `_state.fillPoint`, which nothing ever wrote, so its guard returned every time; the pointerdown handler already had the canvas-space point in hand and was dropping it, so it is passed as an argument rather than smuggled through a state field that exists for one call. **The bake composites by hand in a raw `Uint8ClampedArray` and NEVER through a canvas readback**, because a canvas backing store is premultiplied and mangles RGB wherever alpha is partial — which is exactly what a cutout's edges are made of. Sampling is **nearest-neighbour on purpose**: bilinear would invent partial alpha along every edge and soften the boundaries the extractor worked to keep clean; at the default scale of 1 the mapping is exactly 1:1 and nothing is resampled. The preview uses `drawImage` and so reads slightly smoother than the bake at other scales — disclosed in the comment rather than papered over. **One real app bug, found by the suite rather than by inspection**: every fill came out pure black. `TileEditor.bucketFill` indexes `col[0..2]` straight into the output buffer; handed the hex string `'#ff00ff'` it wrote the **characters** `'#'`,`'f'`,`'f'`, each coerced to `NaN` and then stored as `0` by the clamped array — so the call succeeded, the tile repainted, and the result was silently wrong. `hexToRgb` lives in `tileEditor.js` but is **not** on its export list, so the fix carries its own converter, the same per-module adapter convention `js/pictureStudio.js` already follows for this exact call. **Verified 71/71, zero page errors**, via `compose_panel_verify.mjs` (scratch-only, self-hosting server on a dynamic port): **A** (17) panel structure, lazy DOM, scoped `.hidden` rules and the button-cascade overrides; **B** (6) open/close/isOpen and idempotency; **C** (6) shelf-pack layout and surface growth; **D** (11) drag, alpha-aware hit testing, clamping, and the Move/Fill mode switch — D6/D7/D8 are the fill checks that caught the bug; **E** (15) scale about top-left, fill on a copy, and the bake's own pixel content — E8 is the fill check; **F** (6) Use This Picture end to end, including that the panel auto-closes through `_toggleActiveTool`'s existing hook rather than a close call of its own; **G** (8) teardown across both routes (leaving the tool, and `_hide()`, since a modal dismissal never routes through `_toggleActiveTool` — `close()` is idempotent, so the overlap is harmless); **H** (2) zero page errors. **The error collector was split rather than loosened**: genuine `pageerror`s are separated from failing-resource console noise, the ignored set is cross-checked against a `KNOWN_BAD` list and **printed**, so the filter cannot quietly grow to cover a real problem — confirmed the ignored set is exactly the four documented entries (Story Egg's `hero.png`/`magic.png`/`personality.json` and the sandbox's Supabase block). **Full regression**: both `goldenBuild.js` suites (World Builder v1 and v2) PASS unchanged. `renderer/slideRenderer.js` is untouched, so the Museum Gallery canonical hashes are not the gate for this ship. Cache-bust `?v=0362`→`?v=0363` across all 60 tags. No Theme Contract/Engine V2 Scene Model/Builder change — `tools/world-builder/`, `tools/world-builder-v2/` and `tools/sheet-extractor/` are completely untouched; confined to a new `js/composePanel.js` plus `js/pictureStudio.js`, `css/style.css` and `index.html`.)

## Companion v1 Foundation — Canon V3 & Guide Proposal (docs only)

Product owner locked the publishing roadmap (Publish → Motion Publishing →
Magic Publish, with Story Journey scoped but intentionally postponed) and made
**Companion v1 — platform guidance** the next capability. Six findings changed
the brief: `docs/COMPANION_CANON.md` already existed and was frozen at V2, and
its line *"a companion is not an assistant, a chatbot, a teacher, or an AI
tutor"* actively forbade the Guide responsibility being requested — so the
canon was **amended to V3** (Canon 5, the Guide responsibility, plus a
Companion version table) rather than a second canon being created;
`docs/COMPANION_INTELLIGENCE_ARCHITECTURE.md` already specified the
context/brain/actions/gateway architecture, so the new work became its Phase
0–2 slice rather than a rival design; there is **no Activity architecture** in
the codebase (only `onActivity()`, an idle-timer reset) and **no command
system or global undo**; and the Companion widget is **output-only** — it has
no way to receive a question at all. `docs/COMPANION_V1_PROPOSAL.md` maps all
nine goal questions to deterministic sources and shows **none of them needs an
LLM**: `PublishValidator.run()` already computes *"what should I do next?"*,
and `_sceneObject`'s `owner/moveable/editable/visible` already carries the
guardrail truth behind *"why can't I move this?"*. Two decisions carry the
design: the ask surface is **tap-first contextual question chips, not a text
box** (better for young children, and the single choice that removes any need
for NLU), and the two commands — *add another page*, *duplicate this* — ship as
**Offers that point at existing controls, not Performs**, delivering the goals
with no global-undo prerequisite and nothing mutated. Docs only; no
implementation code. `CLAUDE.md` gained Locked Product Decision 7.

## Studio Rite — Vision Challenge & Architecture Proposal (docs only)

User testing found children's first question inside VihuStudio was *"Who is a
Traveller?"*, not "how do I resize this" — an entry-experience gap, not a
usability one. Product owner locked a mandatory **Studio Rite** before Studio
Home and explicitly asked for the vision to be challenged against canon rather
than implemented straight. Seven conflicts found, three of them blocking.
**The Story Egg cannot guide the Rite**: Canon 1 states it has no face, no
limbs and *never speaks*, and Visitor Behaviour forbids speech bubbles,
onboarding dialogue and tutorials outright — so the brief's "Story Egg / Lumo"
resolves to **Lumo guides, the Egg accompanies in silence**, costing one
widened clause in Canon 2 (Lumo appears at *the two thresholds*) and leaving
Canon 1 intact. **The Rite must not publish**: `shouldOfferAwakening()` fires
at most once ever, so a Rite ending in publish would spend the child's Creator
Ceremony — their permanent Companion bonding — on a practice story. **The
platform has two words for the same person**: the Gateway's literal first line
is `'Welcome, Traveller.'` and the code/registry agree, but `COMPANION_CANON.md`
says Visitor ×8 and `KID_JOURNEY.md` says Visitor ×14 — the word that broke user
testing is one the canon docs do not even use. Also found: the Gateway already
does part of the Rite's job (Lumo already introduces himself and Story
Companions), so the Rite extends an existing entry experience rather than
filling an empty slot; "locked" must mean Studio Home is gated, not the editor,
since steps 4–9 need the real canvas; and existing Creators should be
grandfathered by their claimed Magic Card. The architecture is deliberately
tiny — one new IIFE (`js/studioRite.js`) and **two call sites in `js/app.js`**,
wrapping `GatewaySequence.begin(_beginBoot)` as
`GatewaySequence.begin(function(){ StudioRite.gate(_beginBoot); })`; unlock is
one localStorage flag OR'd with `MagicCard.list().length > 0`, so migration
needs no backfill and no schema change. `detectMode()` already implements
"the guide depends on lifecycle". Docs only; no implementation code. Canon 6
records the locked decision and names the three open questions rather than
resolving them silently. `CLAUDE.md` gained Locked Product Decision 8.

## Studio Rite — Script & Phase Plan (docs only)

Approved direction restated with two additions: a fourth question (*Why do
stories matter?*) and Decision 10's scope lock. Nothing contradicted frozen
canon, so no stop-and-report was needed. Wrote `docs/STUDIO_RITE_SCRIPT.md` —
the screenplay, before code, as directed: four acts plus completion, **18 Lumo
lines, 5 blocking child actions, 5 Egg poses**, every beat waiting indefinitely
with no timeout, skip or auto-advance. One real blocker was found and removed
during the technical design: Studio ships with **zero built-in Worlds**
(Repository-only), so a Rite requiring a World would hard-fail on a first
offline launch — on a mandatory gate that blocks the Studio. `CREATION_TYPES`
already ships `{id:'blank', blank:true}`, documented as the one branch that
"skips Screen 2 entirely and lands straight in the editor on a page with no
World at all", and `StickerLibrary`'s `characters` category is built-in emoji
glyphs — so the Rite reuses a shipped, offline, World-free path and needs no new
content pipeline. Also caught a stale Canon 6 bullet that still described a
Companion-guided variant for returning Creators; that case cannot occur under
Decision 8 (grandfathering) and was withdrawn. Phase plan R1–R4 written with
per-phase file/anchor lists so each phase is implementable in a fresh session
without re-exploring the codebase, and the three largest files in the repo
(`slideRenderer.js`, `cardDesigner.js`, `contextPanel.js`) are touched by no
phase. The Rite observes `PageRuntime.notify()` as a sixth subscriber rather
than driving the editor. Docs only; no implementation code.

## Studio Rite — Implemented (R1–R4)

Built the Rite in four reviewable phases against the approved plan and script.
**R1** added `js/studioRite.js` as a thin gate plus `_riteThenBoot()` at the
three post-Gateway continuations in `js/app.js`; unlock is one localStorage flag
OR'd with `MagicCard.list().length > 0`, so existing Creators are grandfathered
with no migration. **R2** played Act I on a full-screen stage reusing the
Gateway's literal `.gateway-greeting-bubble` vocabulary — the ceremony's own
beat player is module-private to `magicCardUI.js` and is a poor fit anyway
(the Rite blocks on child actions, not timers), so the pattern was reused
rather than the internals exported, and `js/gatewaySequence.js` was never
touched. **R3** hands off to the Studio part way through — at the moment the
child says yes — because Acts III–IV need the real editor; the stage becomes a
pointer-events:none band over the live canvas. Two additive seams were needed:
`PageRuntime.observe(fn)` (the Rite as a sixth subscriber, observers wrapped so
one that throws can't break the panel refreshes) and `CreationFlow.startBlank()`
(exposing the existing `_finishBlank()` rather than duplicating it). **R4**
added Act IV, completion, and the single place the flag is ever written.
Verification in headless Chromium caught a real bug before ship: `js/state.js`
seeds `bookTitle:'My Adventure'`, so "the story has a name" was true before the
child typed anything and Act IV's *"What is this one called?"* was being skipped
every run — deleting the emotional peak of the Rite. The condition became "the
child changed it from what it said when the beat began." An earlier R3 test
also passed while silently skipping a prompt whose condition was already
satisfied; re-run waiting for the prompt to render first. Final run: all 18
beats in order, completion written once, second launch skips the Rite, and
`shouldOfferAwakening()` still true afterwards — the Creator Ceremony was not
consumed. Zero page errors.

## Studio Rite — Conversation Pacing (product feedback)

Testing reported "the prompts are moving too fast." Investigation found two
faults, one worse than the complaint: beat durations were hand-picked constants
of 3–5s regardless of length, so a 23-word beat and a 6-word beat got nearly
the same time on screen; and `_reducedMotion()?900` collapsed **every** beat to
900ms, so anyone with `prefers-reduced-motion` set had the entire Rite flashed
past unreadably — an accessibility defect, not a pacing preference. A first fix
derived each beat's duration from its own word count and added tap-to-continue.
The product owner then gave a better direction: *don't remove the prompts —
